papers.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often contain misleading content, emphasizing the need to align them with human values to ensure secure AI systems. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has been employed to achieve this alignment. However, it encompasses two main drawbacks: (1) RLHF exhibits complexity, instability, and sensitivity to hyperparameters in contrast to SFT. (2) Despite massive trial-and-error, multiple sampling is reduced to pair-wise contrast, thus lacking contrasts from a macro perspective. In this paper, we propose Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO) as an efficient SFT algorithm to directly fine-tune LLMs for human alignment. PRO extends the pair-wise contrast to accommodate preference rankings of any length. By iteratively contrasting candidates, PRO instructs the LLM to prioritize the best response while progressively ranking the rest responses. In this manner, PRO effectively transforms human alignment into aligning the probability ranking of n responses generated by LLM with the preference ranking of humans towards these responses. Experiments have shown that PRO outperforms baseline algorithms, achieving comparable results to ChatGPT and human responses through automatic-based, reward-based, GPT-4, and human evaluations.
papers.summary_en: Existing RLHF methods for aligning LLMs with human values are complex, unstable, and rely on limited pair-wise comparisons. This paper proposes Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO), an efficient supervised fine-tuning approach that extends pairwise contrast to full preference rankings, training the model to prioritize the best response and rank others accordingly. Evaluated via automatic metrics, reward models, GPT-4, and human judges, PRO outperforms baseline alignment methods and achieves performance comparable to ChatGPT and human responses. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有基于RLHF的LLM人类对齐方法复杂、不稳定，且仅依赖有限的成对比较。本文提出偏好排序优化（PRO），一种高效的监督微调方法，将成对对比扩展为完整偏好排序，训练模型优先最佳响应并对剩余响应排序。通过自动化指标、奖励模型、GPT-4和人工评估，PRO优于基线对齐方法，性能堪比ChatGPT和人类响应。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Perception-Guided Jailbreak Against Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: In recent years, Text-to-Image (T2I) models have garnered significant attention due to their remarkable advancements. However, security concerns have emerged due to their potential to generate inappropriate or Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) images. In this paper, inspired by the observation that texts with different semantics can lead to similar human perceptions, we propose an LLM-driven perception-guided jailbreak method, termed PGJ. It is a black-box jailbreak method that requires no specific T2I model (model-free) and generates highly natural attack prompts. Specifically, we propose identifying a safe phrase that is similar in human perception yet inconsistent in text semantics with the target unsafe word and using it as a substitution. The experiments conducted on six open-source models and commercial online services with thousands of prompts have verified the effectiveness of PGJ.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the security vulnerability of text-to-image models that can be manipulated to generate NSFW content. It proposes PGJ, an LLM-driven black-box jailbreak method that substitutes unsafe words with safe phrases that are perceptually similar but semantically different, creating natural-looking attack prompts. Evaluated on six open-source models and commercial services with thousands of prompts, PGJ effectively bypasses safety filters. This work reveals a fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing it can be circumvented through perceptual-semantic mismatch.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对文本到图像模型可能被操纵生成不当内容的安全漏洞。提出一种由大语言模型驱动的黑盒越狱方法 PGJ，通过将不安全词替换为感知相似但语义不同的安全短语，生成自然的攻击提示。在六个开源模型和商业服务上对数千提示进行实验，PGJ 有效绕过安全过滤。该研究表明，后训练安全对齐在面对感知-语义错配时存在脆弱性。

papers.title: MoralReason: Generalizable Moral Decision Alignment for LLM Agents Using Reasoning-Level Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract:
Large language models are increasingly influencing human moral decisions, yet current approaches focus primarily on evaluating rather than actively steering their moral decisions. 
We formulate this as an out-of-distribution moral alignment problem, where LLM agents must learn to apply consistent moral reasoning frameworks to scenarios beyond their training distribution. 
We introduce Moral-Reason-QA, a novel dataset extending 680 human-annotated, high-ambiguity moral scenarios with framework-specific reasoning traces across utilitarian, deontological, and virtue ethics, enabling systematic evaluation of moral generalization in realistic decision contexts.
Our learning approach employs Group Relative Policy Optimization with composite rewards that simultaneously optimize decision alignment and framework-specific reasoning processes to facilitate learning of the underlying moral frameworks. 
Experimental results demonstrate successful generalization to unseen moral scenarios, with softmax-normalized alignment scores improving by +0.757 for utilitarian and +0.450 for deontological frameworks when tested on out-of-distribution evaluation sets. 
The experiments also reveal training challenges and promising directions that inform future research.
These findings establish that LLM agents can be systematically trained to internalize and apply specific moral frameworks to novel situations, providing a critical foundation for AI safety as language models become more integrated into human decision-making processes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of steering LLM agents to make consistent moral decisions, formulating it as an out-of-distribution moral alignment challenge. It proposes a learning approach using Group Relative Policy Optimization with composite rewards, trained on a novel dataset that includes framework-specific reasoning traces for utilitarian, deontological, and virtue ethics. Experiments demonstrate successful generalization to unseen moral scenarios, with softmax-normalized alignment scores improving by +0.757 and +0.450 for utilitarian and deontological frameworks, respectively. The work advances alignment methodology by integrating moral reasoning but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了引导大语言模型智能体在分布外道德场景中做出一致道德决策的问题，将其形式化为分布外道德对齐挑战。提出了一种使用分组相对策略优化与复合奖励的学习方法，并在包含功利主义、义务论和美德伦理学推理轨迹的新数据集上进行训练。实验表明，模型能成功泛化到未见过的道德情景，功利主义和义务论框架的softmax归一化对齐分数分别提高了+0.757和+0.450。该工作通过结合道德推理推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Multi-Reference Preference Optimization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: How can Large Language Models (LLMs) be aligned with human intentions and values? A typical solution is to gather human preference on model outputs and finetune the LLMs accordingly while ensuring that updates do not deviate too far from a reference model. Recent approaches, such as direct preference optimization (DPO), have eliminated the need for unstable and sluggish reinforcement learning optimization by introducing close-formed supervised losses. However, a significant limitation of the current approach is its design for a single reference model only, neglecting to leverage the collective power of numerous pretrained LLMs. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel closed-form formulation for direct preference optimization using multiple reference models. The resulting algorithm, Multi-Reference Preference Optimization (MRPO), leverages broader prior knowledge from diverse reference models, substantially enhancing preference learning capabilities compared to the single-reference DPO. Our experiments demonstrate that LLMs finetuned with MRPO generalize better in various preference data, regardless of data scarcity or abundance. Furthermore, MRPO effectively finetunes LLMs to exhibit superior performance in several downstream natural language processing tasks such as HH-RLHF, GSM8K and TruthfulQA.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the limitation of single-reference Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which does not leverage multiple pretrained LLMs. The paper proposes Multi-Reference Preference Optimization (MRPO), a closed-form formulation for direct preference optimization using multiple reference models to incorporate broader prior knowledge. Evaluated on diverse preference data and downstream tasks like HH-RLHF, GSM8K, and TruthfulQA, MRPO significantly improves generalization and performance over single-reference DPO. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该工作针对单参考模型直接偏好优化（DPO）的局限性，即未能利用多个预训练大语言模型。提出多参考偏好优化（MRPO），一种使用多个参考模型的封闭形式直接偏好优化方法，以融入更广泛的先验知识。在多种偏好数据以及 HH-RLHF、GSM8K 和 TruthfulQA 等下游任务上进行评估，MRPO 相比单参考 DPO 显著提升了泛化能力和性能。本文改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: SafeInfer: Context Adaptive Decoding Time Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Language models aligned for safety often exhibit fragile and imbalanced mechanisms, increasing the chances of producing unsafe content. In addition, editing techniques to incorporate new knowledge can further compromise safety. To tackle these issues, we propose SafeInfer, a context-adaptive, decoding-time safety alignment strategy for generating safe responses to user queries.
safeInfer involves two phases: the 'safety amplification' phase, which uses safe demonstration examples to adjust the model’s hidden states and increase the likelihood of safer outputs, and the 'safety-guided decoding' phase, which influences token selection based on safety-optimized distributions to ensure the generated content adheres to ethical guidelines. Further, we introduce HarmEval, a novel benchmark for comprehensive safety evaluations, designed to address potential misuse scenarios in line with the policies of leading AI technology companies.
papers.summary_en: Existing safety-aligned LLMs exhibit fragile mechanisms, making them prone to generating unsafe content, especially after model editing. The paper proposes SafeInfer, a context-adaptive decoding-time strategy that amplifies safety through demonstration examples and guides token selection using safety-optimized distributions. It is evaluated on the newly introduced HarmEval benchmark, demonstrating improved safety. By explicitly addressing the fragility of safety alignment and offering a decoding-time hardening method, the paper suggests that post-training alignment alone may not be robust, though it does not directly study adversarial bypassing.
papers.summary_zh: 现有的安全对齐大语言模型展现出脆弱的机制，尤其在模型编辑后容易生成不安全内容。本文提出 SafeInfer，一种上下文自适应的解码时安全对齐策略，通过安全示例放大安全性并利用安全优化分布指导 token 选择。在新引入的 HarmEval 基准上评估，表明安全性的提升。本文通过直接应对安全对齐的脆弱性并提出解码时加固方法，暗示仅靠训练后对齐可能不够鲁棒，但未直接研究对抗性绕过。

papers.title: Aligning Language Models Using Follow-up Likelihood as Reward Signal
papers.abstract: In natural human-to-human conversations, participants often receive feedback signals from one another based on their follow-up reactions. These reactions can include verbal responses, facial expressions, changes in emotional state, and other non-verbal cues. Similarly, in human-machine interactions, the machine can leverage the user's follow-up utterances as feedback signals to assess whether it has appropriately addressed the user's request. Therefore, we propose using the likelihood of follow-up utterances as rewards to differentiate preferred responses from less favored ones, without relying on human or commercial LLM-based preference annotations. Our proposed reward mechanism, ``Follow-up Likelihood as Reward" (FLR), matches the performance of strong reward models trained on large-scale human or GPT-4 annotated data on 8 pairwise-preference and 4 rating-based benchmarks. Building upon the FLR mechanism, we propose to automatically mine preference data from the online generations of a base policy model. The preference data are subsequently used to boost the helpfulness of the base model through direct alignment from preference (DAP) methods, such as direct preference optimization (DPO). Lastly, we demonstrate that fine-tuning the language model that provides follow-up likelihood with natural language feedback significantly enhances FLR's performance on reward modeling benchmarks and effectiveness in aligning the base policy model's helpfulness.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of obtaining reward signals for aligning language models without costly human or LLM annotations. It proposes using the likelihood of follow-up utterances as a reward signal (FLR) and automatically mining preference data from online model generations for direct alignment. Evaluated on 8 pairwise-preference and 4 rating-based benchmarks, FLR matches the performance of strong reward models trained on large-scale human or GPT-4 annotated data, and fine-tuning the likelihood model with natural language feedback further improves alignment. This work advances automatic alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在不依赖昂贵的人工或大语言模型标注的情况下，获取对齐语言模型所需奖励信号的问题。提出使用后续话语的可能性作为奖励信号（FLR），并从在线模型生成中自动挖掘偏好数据用于直接对齐。在8个成对偏好基准和4个评分基准上评估，FLR与在大规模人工或GPT-4标注数据上训练的强奖励模型性能相当；用自然语言反馈微调可能性模型进一步提升了对齐性能。这项工作推进了自动对齐方法的发展，但未直接研究训练后对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: AURA: Affordance-Understanding and Risk-aware Alignment Technique for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Present day LLMs face the challenge of managing affordance-based safety risks—situations where outputs inadvertently facilitate harmful actions due to overlooked logical implications. Traditional safety solutions, such as scalar outcome-based reward models, parameter tuning, or heuristic decoding strategies, lack the granularity and proactive nature needed to reliably detect and intervene during subtle yet crucial reasoning steps. Addressing this fundamental gap, we introduce AURA, an innovative, multi-layered framework centered around Process Reward Models (PRMs), providing comprehensive, step level evaluations across logical coherence and safety-awareness. Our framework seamlessly combines introspective self-critique, fine-grained PRM assessments, and adaptive safety-aware decoding to dynamically and proactively guide models toward safer reasoning trajectories. Empirical evidence clearly demonstrates that this approach significantly surpasses existing methods, significantly improving the logical integrity and affordance-sensitive safety of model outputs. This research represents a pivotal step toward safer, more responsible, and contextually aware AI, setting a new benchmark for alignment-sensitive applications.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses affordance-based safety risks where LLM outputs inadvertently facilitate harmful actions due to overlooked logical implications. It proposes AURA, a framework that combines Process Reward Models for step-level evaluation with introspective self-critique and adaptive safety-aware decoding to dynamically guide reasoning. Evaluated empirically, AURA significantly improves logical integrity and affordance-sensitive safety, outperforming existing methods. This work directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment by introducing granular, proactive intervention mechanisms, demonstrating that alignment can be strengthened against subtle reasoning-level vulnerabilities.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型因忽略逻辑含义而无意中辅助有害行为的可提供性安全风险。提出AURA框架，通过过程奖励模型进行步骤级评估，结合自省式自我批评和自适应安全解码，动态引导安全推理。实验证明该方法在逻辑完整性和可提供性敏感安全方面显著超越现有方法。该研究直面训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，通过引入细粒度主动干预机制，表明对齐可在推理层面得到强化，应对微妙的漏洞。

papers.title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in Large Language Model Alignment Reveals Trade-offs in Safety, Inclusivity, and Model Behavior
papers.abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained using human feedback for safety and alignment with human values, alignment decisions often overlook human social diversity. This study examines how incorporating pluralistic values affects LLM behavior by systematically evaluating demographic variation and design parameters in the alignment pipeline. We collect alignment data from US and German participants (N = 1,095 participants, 27,375 ratings) who rated LLM responses across five dimensions: Toxicity, Emotional Awareness (EA), Sensitivity, Stereotypical Bias, and Helpfulness. We fine-tuned multiple Large Language Models and Large Reasoning Models using preferences from different social groups while varying rating scales, disagreement handling methods, and optimization techniques. The results revealed systematic demographic effects: male participants rated responses 18% less toxic than female participants; conservative and Black participants rated responses 27.9% and 44% higher on EA than liberal and White participants, respectively. Models fine-tuned on group-specific preferences exhibited distinct behaviors. Technical design choices showed strong effects: the preservation of rater disagreement achieved roughly 53% greater toxicity reduction than majority voting, and 5-point scales yielded about 22% more reduction than binary formats; and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) consistently outperformed Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) in multi-value optimization. These findings represent a preliminary step in answering a critical question: How should alignment balance expert-driven and user-driven signals to ensure both safety and fair representation?
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of social diversity in LLM alignment by incorporating pluralistic human values. The authors collected preference ratings from 1,095 US and German participants on five dimensions and fine-tuned multiple LLMs and reasoning models using group-specific feedback while varying rating scales, disagreement handling, and optimization methods. Key findings include significant demographic effects (e.g., male raters perceived less toxicity, conservative and Black raters gave higher emotional awareness scores) and technical insights (preserving disagreement reduced toxicity 53% more than majority voting, 5-point scales outperformed binary, and DPO was more effective than GRPO). This work advances alignment methodology by surfacing trade-offs but does not directly study the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过纳入多元人类价值观，解决大语言模型对齐中社会多样性被忽视的问题。作者收集了1095名美国和德国参与者对五个维度的偏好评分，并使用基于不同社会群体的反馈微调多个大语言模型和推理模型，同时变化评分尺度、分歧处理方式和优化技术。关键发现包括显著的人口统计学效应（如男性评估毒性较低，保守派和黑人参与者的情绪感知评分较高）和技术选择的影响（保留分歧比多数投票降低毒性多53%，5点量表优于二元量表，DPO比GRPO更有效）。该工作在揭示权衡方面推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: ALPHA: Action-Based Learning for Pluralistic Human Alignment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models are widely used, but aligning them with societal values remains challenging. Current approaches often rely on human annotations, which are hard to scale, or synthetic data produced by models that may themselves be misaligned, making it difficult to capture genuine public opinion. This limits scalability and introduces demographic biases that reduce the representativeness and fairness of model behavior. We introduce a novel approach to pluralistic alignment through behavioral learning, grounded in the psychological principle that actions (behavior) have strong consistency with opinions. Specifically, we present ALPHA50M, a dataset of over 50 million samples derived from 1.5 million real-world advertisements, incorporating rich behavioral signals inferred from demographic engagement patterns. Models trained on this data achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on diverse alignment benchmarks spanning cultural reasoning, political views, and social values. We also propose two new benchmarks: OpinionQA-XL, which covers surveys across 100+ societal topics, and GSS, which evaluates temporal opinion shift modeling over decades. Our results demonstrate that learning from behavioral signals, derived from observed human actions, enables models to align with diverse demographic opinions, capture underlying social and cultural norms, and generalize to new topics and surveys beyond training data. This behavioral learning paradigm offers a scalable and demographically broad alternative to existing alignment techniques.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the scalability and bias issues in aligning LLMs with diverse societal values by proposing a behavioral learning paradigm. It introduces ALPHA50M, a dataset of 50M samples derived from real-world advertisements, leveraging demographic engagement patterns to infer opinions. Models trained on this data achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across alignment benchmarks, and two new benchmarks (OpinionQA-XL, GSS) are presented. The work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment; it offers an alternative data-driven approach rather than probing modular stability.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过提出行为学习范式解决大语言模型与多元社会价值观对齐的可扩展性和偏差问题。它引入ALPHA50M数据集，包含超过5000万个来自真实广告的样本，利用人口统计学参与模式推断观点。基于此数据训练的模型在多个对齐基准上达到最先进的零样本性能，并提出了两个新基准（OpinionQA-XL和GSS）。这项工作推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或稳健性；它提供了一种数据驱动的替代方案，而非探究模块的稳定性。

papers.title: Rethinking Deep Alignment Through the Lens of Incomplete Safety Learning
papers.abstract: Large language models exhibit systematic vulnerabilities to adversarial attacks despite extensive safety alignment through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback. These vulnerabilities manifest as differential safety behavior across token positions, with safety modifications concentrating in early positions while later positions show minimal distributional changes from base models. We provide a mechanistic analysis of safety alignment training dynamics, revealing that gradient concentration during autoregressive training creates signal decay across token positions. This leads to incomplete distributional learning where safety training fails to fully transform model preferences in later response regions. We introduce base-favored tokens as computational indicators of incomplete safety learning. Analysis reveals that while early positions undergo substantial distributional changes, later positions retain concerning base model preferences in safety-critical contexts, indicating systematic incomplete learning due to insufficient training signals. We develop a targeted completion method that addresses these undertrained regions through adaptive penalties and hybrid teacher distillation. Experimental evaluation across Llama and Qwen model families demonstrates remarkable improvements in adversarial robustness, with dramatic reductions in attack success rates across multiple attack types while fully preserving general capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the systematic vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial attacks despite safety alignment, attributing it to incomplete safety learning that leaves later token positions undertrained. It proposes a targeted completion method using adaptive penalties and hybrid teacher distillation to reinforce safety in undertrained response regions. Experiments on Llama and Qwen models show dramatic reductions in attack success rates across multiple attack types while maintaining general capabilities. This paper provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile due to incomplete distributional learning, particularly in later response tokens, and offers a hardening approach to mitigate this fundamental weakness.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型在安全对齐后仍存在对抗攻击系统脆弱性的问题，发现其根源在于安全学习不完整，导致响应后段标记训练不足。它提出了一种目标补全方法，通过自适应惩罚和混合教师蒸馏来强化未充分训练区域的安全性。在Llama和Qwen模型上的实验表明，该方法显著降低了多种攻击类型的成功率，同时完全保持了通用能力。该论文直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：由于后期响应标记学习不完整，对齐是脆弱的，并提供了强化方法以应对这一根本缺陷。

papers.title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
papers.short_title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
papers.abstract: LLMs produce harmful and undesirable behavior when trained on datasets containing even a small fraction of poisoned data. We demonstrate that GPT models remain vulnerable to fine-tuning on poisoned data, even when safeguarded by moderation systems. Given the persistence of data poisoning vulnerabilities in today's most capable models, this paper investigates whether these risks increase with model scaling. We evaluate three threat models—malicious fine-tuning, imperfect data curation, and intentional data contamination—across 24 frontier LLMs ranging from 1.5 to 72 billion parameters. Our experiments reveal that larger LLMs are significantly more susceptible to data poisoning, learning harmful behaviors from even minimal exposure to harmful data more quickly than smaller models. These findings underscore the need for leading AI companies to thoroughly red team fine-tuning APIs before public release and to develop more robust safeguards against data poisoning, particularly as models continue to scale in size and capability.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to data poisoning, where even a small fraction of poisoned fine-tuning data can induce harmful behaviors. It investigates whether this vulnerability scales with model size by testing three threat models—malicious fine-tuning, imperfect data curation, and intentional data contamination—on 24 frontier LLMs (1.5B to 72B parameters). Experiments reveal that larger LLMs are significantly more susceptible, learning harmful behaviors from minimal exposure more quickly than smaller models. This directly shows that post-training safety alignment is fragile: data poisoning can bypass alignment, and the risk increases with scale, highlighting a fundamental weakness in current alignment methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了LLM对数据投毒的脆弱性，即便微调数据中只包含少量有毒样本，也能诱导有害行为。通过测试三种威胁模型——恶意微调、不完美数据筛选和故意数据污染——在24个前沿LLM（1.5B到72B参数）上，探究了脆弱性是否随模型规模扩大而增加。实验表明，更大规模的LLM更容易受到影响，从极少的有害数据中更快地学习有害行为。这直接证明训练后安全对齐是脆弱的：数据投毒可以绕过对齐，且风险随规模增加而上升，揭示了当前对齐方法的一个根本性弱点。

papers.title: Approximated Variational Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: Approx. Variational BIRL for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract:
The alignment of large language models (LLMs) is crucial for generating helpful and harmless content.
Existing approaches leverage preference-based human feedback data to learn the reward function and align the LLM with the feedback data.
However, these approaches focus on modeling the reward difference between the chosen and rejected demonstrations, rather than directly modeling the true reward from each demonstration.
Moreover, these approaches assume that the reward is only obtained at the end of the sentence, which overlooks the modeling of intermediate rewards.
These issues lead to insufficient use of training signals in the feedback data, limiting the representation and generalization ability of the reward and potentially resulting in reward hacking.
In this paper, we formulate LLM alignment as a Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning (BIRL) problem and propose a novel training objective, Approximated Variational Alignment (AVA), to perform LLM alignment through Approximated Variational Reward Imitation Learning (AVRIL). 
The BIRL formulation facilitates intermediate reward modeling and direct reward modeling on each individual demonstration, which enhances the utilization of training signals in the feedback data.
Experiments show that AVA outperforms existing LLM alignment approaches in reward modeling, RL fine-tuning, and direct optimization.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses insufficient training signal utilization in LLM alignment from human feedback, where existing methods only model reward differences and overlook intermediate rewards, limiting generalization and risking reward hacking. It proposes Approximated Variational Alignment (AVA), which formulates alignment as Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning (BIRL) to enable direct reward modeling per demonstration and intermediate reward modeling. Experiments show AVA outperforms existing approaches in reward modeling, RL fine-tuning, and direct optimization. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了现有基于人类反馈的LLM对齐方法中训练信号利用不足的问题，这些方法仅建模奖励差异且忽略中间奖励，导致泛化能力有限和可能发生奖励破解。作者提出了近似变分对齐（AVA）方法，将LLM对齐建模为贝叶斯逆强化学习（BIRL），从而实现对每个示范的直接奖励建模和中间奖励建模。实验表明，AVA在奖励建模、RL微调和直接优化方面均优于现有方法。本文改进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: When Safe Unimodal Inputs Collide: Optimizing Reasoning Chains for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are susceptible to the implicit reasoning risk, wherein innocuous unimodal inputs synergistically assemble into risky multimodal data that produce harmful outputs. We attribute this vulnerability to the difficulty of MLLMs maintaining safety alignment through long-chain reasoning.To address this issue, we introduce Safe-Semantics-but-Unsafe-Interpretation (SSUI), the first dataset featuring interpretable reasoning paths tailored for such a cross-modal challenge.A novel training framework, Safety-aware Reasoning Path Optimization (SRPO), is also designed based on the SSUI dataset to align the MLLM's internal reasoning process with human safety values. Experimental results show that our SRPO-trained models achieve state-of-the-art results on key safety benchmarks, including the proposed Reasoning Path Benchmark (RSBench), significantly outperforming both open-source and top-tier commercial MLLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of multimodal LLMs to cross-modal safety risks where individually safe unimodal inputs combine into harmful outputs due to failures in safety alignment during long reasoning chains. It proposes SSUI, the first dataset with interpretable reasoning paths for this challenge, and SRPO, a training framework that aligns the model’s internal reasoning with human safety values. SRPO-trained models achieve state-of-the-art results on safety benchmarks including the new RSBench, outperforming leading open-source and commercial MLLMs. This work advances alignment by targeting a specific fragility in multimodal reasoning but does not directly investigate the overall robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型中安全单模态输入组合产生有害输出的跨模态安全风险，归因于模型在长链推理中难以保持安全对齐。提出首个针对该挑战的可解释推理路径数据集SSUI，以及基于该数据集的训练框架SRPO，将模型内部推理过程与人类安全价值观对齐。SRPO训练的模型在包括新提出的RSBench在内的安全基准上达到最优，超越领先的开源和商业多模态大语言模型。该研究通过优化推理加固了对齐，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的整体鲁棒性问题，而是针对多模态推理中的特定脆弱性。

papers.title: Failures to Surface Harmful Contents in Video Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) are increasingly deployed on numerous critical applications, where users rely on auto-generated summaries while casually skimming the video stream. We show that this interaction hides a critical safety gap: if harmful content is embedded in a video, either as full-frame inserts or as small corner patches, state-of-the-art VideoLLMs rarely mention the harmful content in the output, despite its clear visibility to human viewers. A root-cause analysis reveals three compounding design flaws: (1) insufficient temporal coverage resulting from the sparse, uniformly spaced frame sampling used by most leading VideoLLMs, (2) spatial information loss introduced by aggressive token downsampling within sampled frames, and (3) encoder-decoder disconnection, whereby visual cues are only weakly utilized during text generation. Leveraging these insights, we craft three zero-query black-box attacks, aligning with these flaws in the processing pipeline. Our large-scale evaluation across five leading VideoLLMs shows that the harmfulness omission rate exceeds 90\% in most cases. Even when harmful content is clearly present in all frames, these models consistently fail to identify it. These results underscore a fundamental vulnerability in current VideoLLMs' designs and highlight the urgent need for sampling strategies, token compression, and decoding mechanisms that guarantee semantic coverage rather than speed alone.
papers.summary_en: This paper reveals that state-of-the-art Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) systematically fail to surface harmful visual content embedded in videos, even when it is clearly visible to humans. The authors identify three design flaws—insufficient temporal coverage from sparse frame sampling, spatial information loss from aggressive token downsampling, and weak encoder-decoder connection during generation—and craft zero-query black-box attacks exploiting these flaws. Evaluated on five leading VideoLLMs, the harmfulness omission rate exceeds 90%, demonstrating a fundamental vulnerability. This work directly supports the fragility thesis of post-training safety alignment, exposing how architectural weaknesses enable easy bypass of safety mechanisms in multimodal contexts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了顶尖视频大语言模型（VideoLLM）的一项系统性缺陷：即便视频中嵌入了人类清晰可见的有害内容，模型也极少在输出中提及。作者定位了三个设计缺陷——由稀疏均匀采样导致的时序覆盖不足、帧内激进令牌降采样导致的空间信息丢失，以及生成时视觉线索利用薄弱的编码器-解码器脱节，并据此设计了零查询黑盒攻击。在五个主流模型上的评估显示，有害内容遗漏率超过90%，揭示了根本性漏洞。该研究直接印证了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性命题，即多模态场景下架构弱点可轻易绕过安全机制。

papers.title: Adaptive KL Control for Direct Preference Optimization in Instruction-Following LLMs
papers.abstract: The scaling parameter β in Direct Preference Optimization governs a fundamental trade-off: low β produces weak gradients that fail to learn from ambiguous preferences, while high β amplifies updates and causes excessive drift from the reference policy. Prior work treats β as fixed or scheduled throughout training. We introduce DualLoop-DPO, which modulates β via dual feedback: a fast loop raises β temporarily on high-uncertainty batches to enforce stronger preference margins, while a slow loop uses EMA-smoothed KL tracking to regulate policy drift. Experiments on preference alignment benchmarks show consistent improvements over existing static-β, β-scheduling, and dynamic-β baselines. These findings suggest that dual-loop β control—responding to uncertainty for learning and divergence for stability—offers a promising direction for preference-based fine-tuning.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of setting the scaling parameter β in Direct Preference Optimization, where improper values cause weak gradients or excessive policy drift. It proposes DualLoop-DPO, which adaptively controls β via a dual feedback loop: a fast loop increases β on high-uncertainty batches to enforce stronger preference margins, while a slow loop uses EMA-smoothed KL tracking to regulate divergence. Evaluated on preference alignment benchmarks, DualLoop-DPO consistently outperforms static-β, β-scheduling, and existing dynamic-β baselines. While this work advances alignment methodology by improving DPO stability, it does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is robust or fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接偏好优化中缩放参数β的选择难题，不当取值会导致梯度弱或策略漂移。提出DualLoop-DPO方法，通过双环反馈自适应调控β：快环在高不确定性批次上临时提升β以强化偏好边界，慢环利用EMA平滑的KL跟踪调节发散。在偏好对齐基准上的实验表明，该方法一贯优于静态、调度及其他动态β基线。该研究提升了DPO稳定性，推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: SCANS: Mitigating the Exaggerated Safety for LLMs via Safety-Conscious Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Safety alignment is indispensable for Large language models (LLMs) to defend threats from malicious instructions. However, recent researches reveal safety-aligned LLMs tend to reject benign queries due to the exaggerated safety issue, limiting their helpfulness. In this paper, we propose a Safety-Conscious Activation Steering (SCANS) method to mitigate the exaggerated safety concerns in aligned LLMs. First, SCANS extracts the refusal steering vectors within the activation space and utilizes vocabulary projection to anchor some specific safety-critical layers which influence model refusal behavior. Second, by tracking the hidden state transition, SCANS identifies the steering direction and steers the model behavior accordingly, achieving a balance between exaggerated safety and adequate safety. Experiments show that SCANS achieves new state-of-the-art performance on XSTest and OKTest benchmarks, without impairing their defense capability against harmful queries and maintaining almost unchanged model capability.
papers.summary_en: Aligned LLMs often reject benign queries due to exaggerated safety, limiting helpfulness. The paper proposes SCANS, which extracts refusal steering vectors from activation space, anchors safety-critical layers via vocabulary projection, and steers behavior by tracking hidden state transitions to balance safety. Experiments on XSTest and OKTest show state-of-the-art performance in reducing over-refusal while preserving defense against harmful inputs and maintaining general capability. While SCANS improves the precision of safety alignment, the paper primarily focuses on calibration and does not directly examine the fragility of safety mechanisms under adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 针对对齐后大语言模型因过度安全而拒绝良性查询的问题，本文提出SCANS方法，通过从激活空间中提取拒绝转向向量，利用词汇投影定位影响拒绝行为的关键安全层，并跟踪隐藏状态转变以引导模型行为，从而平衡过度安全与适度安全。在XSTest和OKTest基准上，SCANS实现了新的最优性能，在降低过度拒绝的同时保持了对有害查询的防御能力和模型通用能力。虽然该方法提升了安全对齐的精确性，但主要关注校准问题，并未直接探究安全机制在面对对抗攻击时的脆弱性。

papers.title: ALTER: Asymmetric LoRA for Token-Entropy-Guided Unlearning of LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have advanced to encompass extensive knowledge across diverse domains. Yet controlling what a LLMs should not know is important for ensuring alignment and thus safe use. However, effective unlearning in LLMs is difficult due to the fuzzy boundary between knowledge retention and forgetting. This challenge is exacerbated by entangled parameter spaces from continuous multi-domain training, often resulting in collateral damage, especially under aggressive unlearning strategies. Furthermore, the computational overhead required to optimize State-of-the-Art (SOTA) models with billions of parameters poses an additional barrier. In this work, we present ALTER, a lightweight unlearning framework for LLMs to address both the challenges of knowledge entanglement and unlearning efficiency. ALTER operates through two phases: (I) high entropy tokens are captured and learned via the shared A matrix in LoRA, followed by (II) an asymmetric LoRA architecture that achieves a specified forgetting objective by parameter isolation and unlearning tokens within the target subdomains. Serving as a new research direction for achieving unlearning via token-level isolation in the asymmetric framework. ALTER achieves SOTA performance on TOFU, WMDP, and MUSE benchmarks with over 95% forget quality and shows minimal side effects through preserving foundational tokens. By decoupling unlearning from LLMs' billion-scale parameters, this framework delivers excellent efficiency while preserving over 90% of model utility, exceeding baseline preservation rates of 47.8-83.6%.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of efficient unlearning in LLMs, where knowledge entanglement leads to collateral damage during forgetting. It proposes ALTER, a two-phase lightweight framework that first captures high-entropy tokens via a shared LoRA matrix, then isolates and unlearns target subdomain tokens using an asymmetric LoRA architecture. Evaluated on TOFU, WMDP, and MUSE, ALTER achieves over 95% forget quality and preserves over 90% model utility, outperforming baselines. This paper advances unlearning methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型高效遗忘的难题，其中知识纠缠会导致遗忘过程中的附带损伤。它提出了 ALTER，一个两阶段的轻量级框架：首先通过共享的 LoRA 矩阵捕获高熵 token，然后利用非对称 LoRA 架构隔离并遗忘目标子域内的 token。在 TOFU、WMDP 和 MUSE 基准上评估，ALTER 实现了超过 95% 的遗忘质量，并保留了超过 90% 的模型效用，超越了基线方法。本文推进了遗忘方法论，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: MetaCipher: A Time-Persistent and Universal Multi-Agent Framework for Cipher-Based Jailbreak Attacks for LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face persistent vulnerability to jailbreak attacks despite their increasing capabilities. While developers deploy alignment finetuning and safety guardrails, researchers consistently devise novel attacks that circumvent these defenses. This dynamic mirrors a strategic game of continual evolution. However, two challenges hinder jailbreak development: the high cost of querying top-tier LLMs and the short lifespan of effective attacks due to frequent safety updates. These factors limit cost-efficiency and impact. To address this, we propose MetaCipher, a low-cost, multi-agent jailbreak framework that generalizes across LLMs with varying safety measures. Using reinforcement learning, MetaCipher is modular and adaptive, supporting extensibility to future strategies. Within as few as 10 queries, MetaCipher achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates on recent malicious prompt benchmarks, outperforming prior jailbreak methods. We conduct a large-scale empirical evaluation across diverse victim models, demonstrating its robustness and adaptability.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the persistent vulnerability of LLMs to jailbreak attacks, noting that existing attacks are costly and have short lifespans due to frequent safety updates. It proposes MetaCipher, a low-cost multi-agent framework that uses reinforcement learning to generate adaptive cipher-based jailbreak prompts, supporting extensibility and requiring only 10 queries. Evaluated on recent malicious prompt benchmarks, MetaCipher achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates across diverse victim models, outperforming prior methods. This work provides clear evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as a novel attack surface can efficiently bypass defenses with minimal queries, demonstrating that alignment can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型在安全对齐后仍存在的越狱攻击脆弱性问题，指出现有攻击成本高且因模型频繁更新而寿命短暂。提出MetaCipher，一种基于强化学习的低成本多智能体框架，能生成自适应的密文越狱提示，仅需10次查询即可攻击不同安全措施的大模型。在近期恶意提示基准测试中，MetaCipher取得了针对多种受害模型的最优攻击成功率，超越了先前方法。该研究清晰表明，后续训练的安全对齐是脆弱的，新型攻击面可通过极少查询高效绕过防御，证实对齐可被轻易打破。

papers.title: Preference Optimization via Contrastive Divergence: Your Policy Is Secretly an NLL Estimator
papers.abstract:
Existing studies on preference optimization (PO) have been focused on constructing pairwise preference data following simple heuristics, such as maximizing the margin between chosen and rejected responses based on human (or AI) ratings. 
In this work, we develop a novel PO framework that provides theoretical guidance to effectively sample rejected responses.
To achieve this, we formulate PO as minimizing the negative log-likelihood (NLL) of a probability model and propose a sampling-based solution to estimate its normalization constant via contrastive divergence. 
We show that these estimative samples can act as rejected responses in PO. 
Leveraging the connection established between PO and NLL estimation, we propose a novel PO algorithm, called Monte-Carlo-based PO (MC-PO), that applies a MC kernel to sample *hard negatives* w.r.t.~the log-likelihood of the target policy. 
Intuitively, these hard negatives represent the rejected samples that are most difficult for the current policy to differentiate.
We show that MC-PO outperforms existing SOTA baselines on popular alignment benchmarks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of theoretical guidance in sampling rejected responses for preference optimization (PO). It proposes a novel framework that formulates PO as minimizing the negative log-likelihood of a probability model and uses contrastive divergence to estimate its normalization constant, turning estimative samples into effective rejected responses. The resulting Monte-Carlo-based PO (MC-PO) algorithm samples hard negatives most difficult for the current policy, and it outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines on popular alignment benchmarks. This paper advances preference optimization methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了偏好优化中如何有效采样被拒回应时缺乏理论指导的问题。提出了将偏好优化形式化为最小化概率模型的负对数似然，并利用对比散度估计归一化常数的新框架，从而将估计样本转化为有效的被拒回应。由此产生的蒙特卡洛偏好优化（MC-PO）算法能够采样对当前策略最难区分的难负例，并在主流对齐基准上超越了现有最优基线。该研究推进了偏好优化方法，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Can Editing LLMs Inject Harm?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a new information channel. Meanwhile, one critical but under-explored question is: Is it possible to bypass the safety alignment and inject harmful information into LLMs stealthily? In this paper, we propose to reformulate knowledge editing as a new type of safety threat for LLMs, namely Editing Attack, and conduct a systematic investigation with a newly constructed dataset EditAttack. Specifically, we focus on two typical safety risks of Editing Attack including Misinformation Injection and Bias Injection. For the first risk, we find that editing attacks can inject both commonsense and long-tail misinformation into LLMs, and the effectiveness for the former one is particularly high. For the second risk, we discover that not only can biased sentences be injected into LLMs with high effectiveness, but also one single biased sentence injection can degrade the overall fairness. Then, we further illustrate the high stealthiness of editing attacks. Our discoveries demonstrate the emerging misuse risks of knowledge editing techniques on compromising the safety alignment of LLMs and the feasibility of disseminating misinformation or bias with LLMs as new channels.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether knowledge editing can be weaponized as a new safety threat to bypass LLM alignment and inject harmful content stealthily. The authors propose the concept of Editing Attack and systematically evaluate it using a custom dataset EditAttack, focusing on misinformation and bias injection. Experiments show that editing attacks effectively inject both commonsense and long-tail misinformation, with commonsense being particularly vulnerable, and that a single biased edit can significantly degrade overall fairness. These findings expose knowledge editing as a stealthy attack surface that undermines post-training safety alignment, highlighting its fragility and ease of bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究知识编辑技术是否可被武器化为一种新的安全威胁，从而绕过大型语言模型的对齐机制并隐蔽地注入有害内容。作者提出编辑攻击概念并利用自建数据集EditAttack进行系统评估，重点关注错误信息和偏见的注入。实验发现，编辑攻击能高效注入常识性和长尾错误信息，尤其前者更为脆弱；而单次偏见编辑即可显著降低模型整体公平性，且攻击具有高隐蔽性。这些发现揭示了知识编辑作为一种隐蔽攻击面，能够破坏训练后安全对齐，凸显其脆弱性与易绕过性。

papers.title: Security Attacks on LLM-based Code Completion Tools
papers.short_title: Jailbreak & Data Extract on Code LLMs
papers.abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has significantly advanced code completion capabilities, giving rise to a new generation of LLM-based Code Completion Tools (LCCTs). Unlike general-purpose LLMs, these tools possess unique workflows, integrating multiple information sources as input and prioritizing code suggestions over natural language interaction, which introduces distinct security challenges. Additionally, LCCTs often rely on proprietary code datasets for training, raising concerns about the potential exposure of sensitive data.  This paper exploits these distinct characteristics of LCCTs to develop targeted attack methodologies on two critical security risks: jailbreaking and training data extraction attacks. Our experimental results expose significant vulnerabilities within LCCTs, including a 99.4% success rate in jailbreaking attacks on GitHub Copilot and a 46.3% success rate on Amazon Q. Furthermore, We successfully extracted sensitive user data from GitHub Copilot, including 54 real email addresses and 314 physical addresses associated with GitHub usernames. Our study also demonstrates that these code-based attack methods are effective against general-purpose LLMs, highlighting a broader security misalignment in the handling of code by modern LLMs. These findings underscore critical security challenges associated with LCCTs and suggest essential directions for strengthening their security frameworks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in LLM-based code completion tools (LCCTs), focusing on jailbreaking and training data extraction attacks. It proposes attack methodologies specifically tailored to exploit the unique workflows of LCCTs, such as their integration of multiple information sources and emphasis on code suggestions over natural language. Experiments show a 99.4% jailbreak success rate on GitHub Copilot and a 46.3% success rate on Amazon Q, and successfully extracted real sensitive data like email and physical addresses from Copilot. These findings reveal that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed through code-based attack vectors, indicating a broader security misalignment in how LLMs handle code.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于LLM的代码补全工具（LCCTs）的安全漏洞，重点关注越狱攻击和训练数据提取攻击。提出了专门利用LCCTs独特工作流程（如整合多种信息源、以代码建议而非自然语言交互为主）的攻击方法。实验结果显示，对GitHub Copilot的越狱攻击成功率高达99.4%，对Amazon Q的成功率为46.3%，并成功从Copilot中提取出真实敏感用户数据（包括54个邮箱和314个地址）。这些发现表明，后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过基于代码的攻击向量被绕过，揭示了现代LLM处理代码时更广泛的安全对齐不足。

papers.title: AMaPO: Adaptive Margin-attached Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: AMaPO: Adaptive Margin PO for Alignment
papers.abstract: Offline preference optimization offers a simpler and more stable alternative to RLHF for aligning language models. However, their effectiveness is critically dependent on ranking accuracy, a metric where further gains are highly impactful. This limitation arises from a fundamental problem that we identify and formalize as the Overfitting-Underfitting Dilemma: current margin designs cause models to apply excessive, wasteful gradients to correctly ranked samples (overfitting) while providing insufficient corrective signals for misranked ones (underfitting). To resolve this dilemma, we propose Adaptive Margin-attached Preference Optimization (AMaPO), a simple yet principled algorithm. AMaPO employs an instance-wise adaptive margin, refined by Z-normalization and exponential scaling, which dynamically reallocates learning effort by amplifying gradients for misranked samples and suppressing them for correct ones. Extensive experiments on widely used benchmarks demonstrate that AMaPO not only achieves better ranking accuracy and superior downstream alignment performance, but targeted analysis also confirms that it successfully mitigates the core overfitting and underfitting issues.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overfitting-underfitting dilemma in offline preference optimization for language model alignment, where fixed margins waste gradients on correctly ranked samples and under-correct misranked ones. It proposes AMaPO, which uses an instance-wise adaptive margin with Z-normalization and exponential scaling to dynamically reallocate learning effort. Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved ranking accuracy and downstream alignment, with analysis confirming the mitigation of the dilemma. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决离线偏好优化中对齐语言模型时的过拟合-欠拟合困境，即固定边界对正确排序样本施加无效梯度，而对错误排序样本校正不足。提出AMaPO方法，采用实例级自适应边界，结合Z标准化和指数缩放动态调整学习重点。在常用基准上的实验表明，该方法不仅提升排序准确性和下游对齐性能，且分析证实其缓解了核心困境。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: On Effects of Steering Latent Representation for Large Language Model Unlearning
papers.abstract:
Representation Misdirection for Unlearning (RMU), which steers model representation in the intermediate layer to a target random representation, is an effective method for large language model (LLM) unlearning. Despite its high performance, the underlying cause and explanation remain underexplored. In this paper, we theoretically demonstrate that steering forget representations in the intermediate layer reduces token confidence, causing LLMs to generate wrong or nonsense responses. We investigate how the coefficient influences the alignment of forget-sample representations with the random direction and hint at the optimal coefficient values for effective unlearning across different network layers. We show that RMU unlearned models are robust against adversarial jailbreak attacks. Furthermore, our empirical analysis shows that RMU is less effective when applied to the middle and later layers in LLMs. To resolve this drawback, we propose Adaptive RMU---a simple yet effective alternative method that makes unlearning effective with most layers.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that Adaptive RMU significantly improves the unlearning performance compared to prior art while incurring no additional computational cost.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates why steering latent representations in intermediate layers enables unlearning in large language models (LLMs) via Representation Misdirection for Unlearning (RMU). It theoretically shows that RMU reduces token confidence for forget samples, leading to erroneous outputs, and identifies optimal coefficient ranges. The authors propose Adaptive RMU, which extends effective unlearning to middle and later layers, significantly improving performance over prior RMU with no extra cost. RMU models are shown to resist jailbreak attacks, contributing to robust unlearning; however, the initial layer-specific fragility underscores that unlearning methods require careful design to avoid bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究了通过中间层潜在表示转向（RMU）实现大语言模型遗忘的底层机制。从理论上证明了RMU通过降低遗忘样本的token置信度导致错误输出，并给出了最优系数范围，进而提出了自适应RMU，使遗忘在多数层上有效，克服了原有方法在中后层的不足。实验表明，自适应RMU无需额外计算即可显著提升遗忘性能，且RMU模型对越狱攻击具有鲁棒性。该研究展示了通过操纵内部表示可构建鲁棒的遗忘机制以抵御越狱绕过，但初始的层级脆弱性提示遗忘方法需精心设计以避免被攻破。

papers.title: Persistent Backdoor Attacks Under Continual Fine-Tuning of LLMs
papers.abstract: Backdoor attacks embed malicious behaviors into Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling adversaries to trigger harmful outputs or bypass safety controls. However, the persistence of the implanted backdoors under user-driven post-deployment continual fine-tuning has been rarely examined. Most prior works evaluate the effectiveness and generalization of implanted backdoors only at releasing and empirical evidence shows that naively injected backdoor persistence degrades after updates. In this work, we study whether and how implanted backdoors persist through a multi‑stage post-deployment fine‑tuning. We propose P‑Trojan, a trigger‑based attack algorithm that explicitly optimizes for backdoor persistence across repeated updates. By aligning poisoned gradients with those of clean tasks on token embeddings, the implanted backdoor mapping is less likely to be suppressed or forgotten during subsequent updates. Theoretical analysis shows the feasibility of such persistent backdoor attacks after continual fine-tuning. And experiments conducted on the Qwen2.5 and LLaMA3 families of LLMs, as well as diverse task sequences, demonstrate that P‑Trojan achieves over \textbf{99\%} persistence while preserving clean‑task accuracy. Our findings highlight the need for persistence-aware evaluation and stronger defenses in realistic model adaptation pipelines.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the persistence of backdoor attacks in LLMs under post-deployment continual fine-tuning, where prior attacks degrade after updates. It proposes P-Trojan, an algorithm that aligns poisoned gradients with clean task gradients on token embeddings to prevent the backdoor from being forgotten. Experiments on Qwen2.5 and LLaMA3 models across diverse tasks show over 99% backdoor persistence with minimal clean accuracy loss. This work demonstrates that safety alignment can be fragile, as persistent backdoors introduce a novel attack surface that survives continual tuning.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了大语言模型在部署后持续微调下后门攻击的持久性问题，发现简单注入的后门会随更新退化。提出P-Trojan算法，通过将有毒梯度与干净任务在嵌入层的梯度对齐，使后门映射不易被遗忘。在Qwen2.5和LLaMA3系列模型及多种任务序列上，实现了超99%的持久率且保持干净任务性能。该工作揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，持续微调可使后门鲁棒存留，构成新的攻击面。

papers.title: When Smiley Turns Hostile: Interpreting How Emojis Trigger LLMs' Toxicity
papers.abstract: Emojis are globally used non-verbal cues in digital communication, and extensive research has examined how large language models (LLMs) understand and utilize emojis across contexts. While usually associated with friendliness or playfulness, it is observed that emojis may trigger toxic content generation in LLMs. Motivated by such a observation, we aim to investigate: (1) whether emojis can clearly enhance the toxicity generation in LLMs and (2) how to interpret this phenomenon.* We begin with a comprehensive exploration of emoji-triggered LLM toxicity generation by automating the construction of prompts with emojis to subtly express toxic intent.  Experiments across 5 mainstream languages on 7 famous LLMs along with jailbreak tasks demonstrate that prompts with emojis could easily induce toxicity generation. To understand this phenomenon, we conduct model-level interpretations spanning semantic cognition, sequence generation and tokenization, suggesting  that emojis can act as a heterogeneous semantic channel to bypass the safety mechanisms. To pursue deeper insights, we further probe the pre-training corpus and uncover potential correlation between the emoji-related data polution with the toxicity generation behaviors.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how emojis, typically friendly non-verbal cues, can unexpectedly trigger toxic content generation in large language models (LLMs). The authors propose an automated method to construct prompts with emojis subtly expressing toxic intent, and evaluate across 5 languages and 7 LLMs including jailbreak tasks. Experiments show emojis easily induce toxicity; model-level interpretations reveal emojis act as a heterogeneous semantic channel that bypasses safety mechanisms, potentially linked to emoji-related data pollution in pre-training. This finding demonstrates a new attack surface that directly exposes the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as innocuous emojis can circumvent safety filters.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究表情符号（通常与友好相关的非言语线索）如何意外触发大型语言模型生成有毒内容。作者提出自动化构建含表情符号的提示以微妙表达有毒意图，并在5种语言和7个主流LLM上（包括越狱任务）进行实验评估。结果表明表情符号极易诱导毒性生成；模型层面的分析揭示表情符号充当异构语义通道绕过安全机制，且可能与预训练数据中的表情符号相关污染有关。这一发现揭示了新的攻击面，直接暴露了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性——无害的表情符号即可绕过安全过滤。

papers.title: EigenShield: Inference-Time, Model-Agnostic Jailbreaking Defense via Causal Subspace Filtering
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) remain highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks despite widespread adoption. Existing defenses typically require retraining, rely on heuristics, or fail under adaptive and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions. We introduce EigenShield, a principled, inference-time, architecture-agnostic defense that leverages Random Matrix Theory (RMT) to suppress adversarial noise in high-dimensional embeddings. EigenShield uses spiked covariance modeling and a Robustness-based Nonconformity Score (RbNS) with quantile thresholding to isolate and preserve causal eigenvectors, filtering out adversarial components without model access or adversarial training. We develop a theoretical framework establishing conditions for asymptotic noise suppression and demonstrate effectiveness in both unimodal and multimodal settings. Empirically, EigenShield consistently improves robustness across threat models, reducing attack success rates (ASR) by up to 48% over state-of-the-art defenses, including adversarial training, UNIGUARD, CIDER, and input transformations. On jailbreak attacks, EigenShield lowers LLM ASR by up to 92.9% relative to undefended models. Under multimodal adversarial attacks, it reduces VLM ASR by up to 76.5%. Against adaptive attacks on LLMs, it achieves ASR reductions of up to 77.7%. In OOD settings, EigenShield maintains strong performance, reducing ASR by up to 88.4% for LLMs and 80.4% for VLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs and VLMs to jailbreaking and adversarial attacks, where existing defenses often require retraining or heuristics and fail under adaptive and out-of-distribution conditions. EigenShield proposes an inference-time, model-agnostic defense that uses Random Matrix Theory and spiked covariance modeling with a robustness-based nonconformity score to filter out adversarial components while preserving causal embeddings. Evaluated across various threat models, EigenShield reduces attack success rates by up to 48% over state-of-the-art defenses, achieving up to 92.9% relative ASR reduction on jailbreaks and maintaining strong robustness in adaptive and OOD settings (up to 88.4% ASR reduction). This work advances alignment hardening by showing that inference-time filtering can bolster post-training safety, offering a complementary approach to address the fragility of alignment without directly resolving whether alignment is inherently fragile or robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型和视觉语言模型在越狱和对抗攻击下的脆弱性，现有防御多需重训练或启发式方法，且在自适应和分布外场景中失效。EigenShield提出一种推理时、模型无关的防御方法，利用随机矩阵理论和尖峰协方差建模，结合基于鲁棒性的非一致性评分与分位数阈值化，隔离因果特征向量以滤除对抗成分。实验表明，在多种威胁模型下，EigenShield将攻击成功率最高降低48%（相比其他先进防御），在越狱攻击上ASR相对降低达92.9%，并在自适应与分布外条件下保持强鲁棒性（ASR降低达88.4%）。该研究通过推理时过滤增强了后期安全对齐的鲁棒性，从防御角度回应了脆弱性问题，但未直接证明对齐本质是否脆弱。

papers.title: SEAS: Self-Evolving Adversarial Safety Optimization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to advance in capability and influence, ensuring their security and preventing harmful outputs has become crucial. A promising approach to address these concerns involves training models to automatically generate adversarial prompts for red teaming. However, the evolving subtlety of vulnerabilities in LLMs challenges the effectiveness of current adversarial methods, which struggle to generate diverse, complex prompts and dynamically explore the weaknesses of these models. To tackle these challenges, we introduce the Self-Evolving Adversarial Safety (SEAS) optimization framework, which includes both a SEAS dataset and a SEAS pipeline. The SEAS dataset comprises complex adversarial prompts, while the SEAS pipeline operates through three stages: Initialization, Attack, and Adversarial Optimization. This framework generates a diverse range of adversarial prompts and dynamically explores the model's vulnerabilities to enhance its security. Our contributions include a novel adversarial framework, a comprehensive safety dataset, and empirical evidence demonstrating the effectiveness of SEAS.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of current adversarial methods in generating diverse, complex prompts to dynamically explore LLM vulnerabilities for red teaming. It proposes the SEAS framework, comprising a dataset and a three-stage pipeline (Initialization, Attack, Adversarial Optimization) that evolves adversarial prompts to uncover weaknesses. Empirical evaluation demonstrates the framework's effectiveness in enhancing LLM security through adversarial training. This work advances adversarial alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有对抗方法难以生成多样化、复杂提示并动态探索LLM漏洞的问题，提出SEAS优化框架，包含数据集和三阶段流程（初始化、攻击、对抗优化），以生成多样对抗提示并动态探索弱点。实证评估表明该框架能有效增强LLM安全性。该研究推进了对抗训练对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Alleviating Shifted Distribution in Human Preference Alignment through Meta-Learning
papers.short_title: MetaRM: Alleviating Shifted Distribution in RLHF
papers.abstract: The capability of the reward model (RM) is crucial for the success of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in aligning with human preferences. However, as training progresses, the output space distribution of the policy model shifts. The RM, initially trained on responses sampled from the output distribution of the early policy model, gradually loses its ability to distinguish between responses from the newly shifted distribution. This issue is further compounded when the RM, trained on a specific data distribution, struggles to generalize to examples outside of that distribution. These two issues can be united as a challenge posed by the shifted distribution of the environment. To surmount this challenge, we introduce MetaRM, a novel method leveraging meta-learning to adapt the RM to the shifted environment distribution. MetaRM optimizes the RM in an alternating way, by preserving both the preferences of the original preference pairs, as well as maximizing discrimination power over new examples of the shifted distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MetaRM can iteratively enhance the performance of human preference alignment by improving the RM's capacity to identify subtle differences in samples of shifted distributions.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the degradation of reward models in RLHF due to the policy model's shifting output distribution. It proposes MetaRM, which uses meta-learning to adapt the reward model to new distributions by alternating between preserving original preferences and maximizing discrimination on shifted samples. Experiments show iterative improvement in alignment performance by enhancing the RM's ability to spot subtle differences. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中因策略模型输出分布偏移导致奖励模型性能退化的问题，提出MetaRM方法，通过元学习使奖励模型自适应偏移分布，交替保持原始偏好并增强对新样本的区分力。实验表明该方法能迭代提升奖励模型对细微差异的识别能力，从而改善人类偏好对齐效果。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: ACID Test: A Benchmark for Cultural Safety and Alignment in LALMs
papers.short_title: ACID: Cultural Safety Benchmark for LALMs
papers.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) are transforming AI by processing and generating human language directly from audio. As these models proliferate in real-world applications, it becomes critical to evaluate their performance to ensure equitable and safe use across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. We present the first comprehensive study of cultural bias in LALMs, extending text-based harm frameworks to the audio modality to analyze how linguistic diversity influences model behavior and uncover challenges in interpreting audio nuances. To address this, we introduce the Audio Cultural Intelligence Dataset (ACID), a multilingual audio–text benchmark spanning 1,315 hours across diverse languages and cultural contexts, and we conduct a systematic evaluation of 10 open-source and two closed-source models. Our results reveal substantial performance disparities across languages and cultural settings and show that biases manifest distinctly when models process audio inputs. These findings highlight the need to evaluate LALMs not only for technical accuracy but also for fair and culturally sensitive behavior, motivating the development of inclusive datasets and culturally aware training practices for safer and more equitable audio language models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of cultural safety evaluation in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs). It proposes the Audio Cultural Intelligence Dataset (ACID), a multilingual audio-text benchmark, and evaluates 10 open-source and 2 closed-source LALMs. The evaluation reveals substantial performance disparities across languages and cultures, with biases manifesting distinctly in audio processing. While this work provides a benchmark to improve cultural alignment, it does not directly test the fragility of post-training safety alignment; it instead lays groundwork for more robust and inclusive models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型音频语言模型（LALMs）中文化安全评估的缺失问题。提出了多语言音频文本基准数据集ACID，并对10个开源和2个闭源模型进行系统评估。评估发现不同语言和文化背景下性能存在显著差异，且音频处理时偏见表现独特。尽管该基准有助于提升文化对齐，但并未直接检验后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，而是为构建更稳健和包容的模型奠定了基础。

papers.title: Multi-Turn Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Attention Shifting
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved significant performance in various natural language processing tasks but also pose safety and ethical threats, thus requiring red teaming and alignment processes to bolster their safety. To effectively exploit these aligned LLMs, recent studies have introduced jailbreak attacks based on multi-turn dialogues. These attacks aim to prompt LLMs to generate harmful or biased content by guiding them through contextual content. However, the underlying reasons for the effectiveness of multi-turn jailbreaks remain unclear. Existing attacks often focus on optimizing queries and escalating toxicity to construct dialogues, lacking a thorough analysis of the inherent vulnerabilities of LLMs. In this paper, we first conduct an in-depth analysis of the differences between single-turn and multi-turn jailbreaks and find that successful multi-turn jailbreaks can effectively disperse the attention of LLMs on keywords associated with harmful behaviors, especially in historical responses. Based on this, we propose ASJA, a new multi-turn jailbreak approach by shifting the attention of LLMs, specifically by iteratively fabricating the dialogue history through a genetic algorithm to induce LLMs to generate harmful content. Extensive experiments on three LLMs and two datasets show that our approach surpasses existing approaches in jailbreak effectiveness, the stealth of jailbreak prompts, and attack efficiency. Our work emphasizes the importance of enhancing the robustness of LLMs' attention mechanism in multi-turn dialogue scenarios for a better defense strategy.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the mechanisms behind multi-turn jailbreaking attacks on LLMs, revealing that successful attacks disperse the model's attention away from harm-related keywords in historical responses. To exploit this, the authors propose ASJA, a novel jailbreak method that uses a genetic algorithm to iteratively fabricate dialogue history, thereby shifting the LLM's attention and inducing harmful outputs. Evaluated on three LLMs and two datasets, ASJA surpasses existing approaches in effectiveness, stealth, and attack efficiency. By uncovering a fundamental vulnerability in the attention mechanism, this work strongly supports the view that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be readily bypassed through sophisticated multi-turn interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了针对大语言模型的多轮越狱攻击机制，发现成功攻击能够将模型注意力从历史回答中的有害关键词上分散开。基于此，作者提出ASJA方法，利用遗传算法迭代构造对话历史，通过转移注意力诱导模型生成有害内容。在三个大模型和两个数据集上的实验表明，ASJA在攻击有效性、隐蔽性和效率上均超越现有方法。该研究揭示了注意力机制的内在脆弱性，有力证明了后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过精心设计的多轮交互轻易攻破。

papers.title: Disentangling Adversarial Prompts: A Semantic-Graph Defense for Robust LLM Security
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly vulnerable to adversarial prompts that exploit semantic ambiguities
to bypass safety mechanisms, resulting in harmful or inappropriate outputs. Such attacks, including jailbreaking and
prompt injection, pose significant risks to the integrity and
availability of LLMs in security-critical applications. This paper proposes the Adversarial Prompt Disentanglement (APD)
framework, a novel defense mechanism that proactively identifies and neutralizes malicious components in input prompts
before they are processed by the LLM. The APD framework
integrates three key innovations: (1) a mutual information-
based semantic decomposition method to isolate adversarial and benign prompt components, ensuring statistical in-
dependence; (2) a graph-based intent classification approach
that leverages spectral analysis to detect malicious patterns
in prompt semantics; and (3) a lightweight transformer-based
classifier trained on real-world datasets of toxic and jailbreaking prompts, enabling efficient and accurate adversarial intent detection. Evaluated on diverse datasets containing adversarial prompts, APD demonstrates superior robustness, reducing harmful output generation by over 85% while maintaining negligible impact on model performance. The framework’s computational efficiency supports real-time deploy-
ment, making it a practical solution for securing LLMs. Our
work addresses critical challenges in machine learning security on novel attacks and integrity methods for ML systems,
and offers a scalable, ethically grounded defense against
prompt-based adversarial threats.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety mechanisms to adversarial prompts, including jailbreaking and prompt injection, which exploit semantic ambiguities to bypass alignment. It proposes the Adversarial Prompt Disentanglement (APD) framework, which uses mutual information-based decomposition to separate benign and adversarial components, graph-based spectral analysis for intent classification, and a lightweight transformer classifier for detection. Evaluation on toxic and jailbreaking prompt datasets shows APD reduces harmful outputs by over 85% with minimal performance overhead, enabling real-time deployment. This work highlights the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that adversarial prompts can systematically circumvent it, but provides a robust defense layer that suggests alignment alone is insufficient and must be complemented by proactive filtering mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全机制易受对抗性提示攻击的问题，包括越狱和提示注入，这些攻击利用语义模糊性绕过对齐。提出了对抗提示解耦（APD）框架，采用基于互信息的语义分解分离良性与对抗成分，基于图的谱分析进行意图分类，并使用轻量级Transformer分类器检测。在毒性和越狱提示数据集上的评估显示，APD将有害输出减少85%以上，对模型性能影响极小，支持实时部署。该工作揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明对抗攻击可系统性绕过，但通过主动防御层加固，说明仅靠对齐不足，需结合过滤机制。

papers.title: The Alignment Game: A Theory of Long-Horizon Alignment Through Recursive Curation
papers.abstract: In self-consuming generative models that train on their own outputs, alignment with user preferences becomes a recursive rather than one-time process. In this paper, we provide the first formal foundation for analyzing the long-term effects of such recursive retraining on alignment. Under a two-stage curation mechanism based on the Bradley–Terry (BT) model, we model alignment as an interaction between two factions: the Model Owner, who filters which outputs should be learned by the model, and the Public User, who determines which outputs are ultimately shared and retained through interactions with the model. Our analysis reveals three structural convergence regimes: consensus collapse, compromise on shared optima, and asymmetric refinement, depending on the degree of preference alignment. We prove a fundamental impossibility theorem: no recursive BT-based curation mechanism can simultaneously preserve diversity, ensure symmetric influence, and eliminate dependence on initialization. Framing the process as dynamic social choice, we show that alignment is not a static goal but an evolving equilibrium shaped by power asymmetries and path dependence.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of alignment drift in generative models that recursively train on their own outputs, where alignment becomes a dynamic process. It proposes a game-theoretic model using a two-stage curation mechanism based on the Bradley–Terry model, featuring a Model Owner and a Public User. Analysis reveals three convergence regimes and proves an impossibility theorem: no recursive BT-based curation can preserve diversity, symmetric influence, and initialization independence simultaneously. This paper advances theoretical understanding of long-term alignment dynamics but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks or bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了生成模型在自身输出上递归训练时对齐漂移的问题，其中对齐成为一个动态过程。它提出了一个基于 Bradley-Terry 模型的两阶段策展机制的博弈论模型，包含模型所有者与公共用户。分析揭示了三种收敛模式，并证明了一个不可能定理：任何基于递归 BT 的策展都无法同时保持多样性、对称影响和初始化独立性。本文推进了对长期对齐动态的理论理解，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐在面对对抗攻击或绕过机制时的脆弱性。

papers.title: Investigating the Security Threat Arising from "Yes-No" Implicit Bias in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained significant attention for their exceptional performance across various domains. Despite their advancements, concerns persist regarding their implicit bias, which often leads to negative social impacts. Therefore, it is essential to identify the implicit bias in LLMs and investigate the potential threat posed by it. Our study focused on a specific type of implicit bias, termed the ''Yes-No'' implicit bias, which refers to LLMs' inherent tendency to favor ''Yes'' or ''No'' responses to a single instruction. By comparing the probability of LLMs generating a series of ''Yes'' versus ''No'' responses, we observed different inherent response tendencies exhibited by LLMs when faced with different instructions. To further investigate the impact of such bias, we developed an attack method called Implicit Bias In-Context Manipulation, attempting to manipulate LLMs' behavior. Specifically, we explored whether the ''Yes'' implicit bias could manipulate ''No'' responses into ''Yes'' in LLMs' responses to malicious instructions, leading to harmful outputs. Our findings revealed that the ''Yes'' implicit bias brings a significant security threat, comparable to that of carefully designed attack methods. Moreover, we offered a comprehensive analysis from multiple perspectives to deepen the understanding of this security threat, emphasizing the need for ongoing improvement in LLMs' security.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the security threat from 'Yes-No' implicit bias in LLMs, where models inherently favor 'Yes' or 'No' responses. It proposes an attack method, Implicit Bias In-Context Manipulation, that exploits this bias to manipulate LLM outputs. Evaluation shows that by leveraging the 'Yes' bias, the attack can turn safe 'No' responses into harmful 'Yes' responses for malicious instructions, posing a threat comparable to carefully designed attacks. This work reveals a new attack surface based on inherent model biases, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be fragile and easily bypassed through subtle manipulation of response tendencies.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨了大语言模型中“是-否”内隐偏见的安全威胁，即模型固有地倾向于“是”或“否”响应。提出了一种名为“内隐偏见上下文操纵”的攻击方法，利用该偏见操控模型输出。评估表明，利用“是”偏见能将恶意指令的安全“否”响应转为有害的“是”响应，其威胁程度与精心设计的攻击相当。这一发现揭示了基于固有模型偏见的新攻击面，表明安全对齐可能脆弱且易被绕过，直接回应了对齐稳健性问题。

papers.title: Preference-Oriented Supervised Fine-Tuning: Favoring Target Model over Aligned Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Alignment, endowing a pre-trained Large language model (LLM) with the ability to follow instructions, is crucial for its real-world applications. 
Conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) methods formalize it as causal language modeling typically with a cross-entropy objective, requiring a large amount of high-quality instruction-response pairs.
However, the quality of widely used SFT datasets can not be guaranteed due to the high cost and intensive labor for the creation and maintenance in practice.
To overcome the limitations associated with the quality of SFT datasets, 
we introduce a novel preference-oriented supervised fine-tuning approach, namely PoFT. 
The intuition is to boost SFT by imposing a particular preference: favoring the target model over aligned LLMs on the same SFT data.
This preference encourages the target model to predict a higher likelihood than that predicted by the aligned LLMs, incorporating assessment information on data quality  (i.e., predicted likelihood by the aligned LLMs) into the training process. 
Extensive experiments are conducted, and the results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
PoFT achieves stable and consistent improvements over the SFT baselines across different training datasets and base models.
Moreover, we prove that PoFT can be integrated with existing SFT data filtering methods to achieve better performance, and further improved by following preference optimization procedures, such as DPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for LLMs suffers from noisy or low-quality instruction-response data.
