It proposes PoFT, a preference-oriented SFT method that trains the target model to assign higher likelihood to responses than a pre-aligned LLM, using the aligned model's likelihoods as a quality signal. Experiments show PoFT consistently improves over standard SFT baselines and can be combined with data filtering or DPO for further gains. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对传统监督微调(SFT)因指令-响应数据质量难以保证而性能受限的问题。提出PoFT方法，通过偏好导向训练，使目标模型在相同SFT数据上预测高于已对齐大语言模型的似然性，从而引入数据质量评估信息。大量实验表明，PoFT在不同数据集和基座模型上均稳定优于SFT基线，并可结合数据过滤或DPO进一步提升性能。本研究改进了对齐方法，增强了SFT对噪声数据的鲁棒性，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: LEGEND: Leveraging Representation Engineering to Annotate Safety Margin for Preference Datasets
papers.abstract: The success of the reward model in distinguishing between responses with subtle safety differences depends critically on the high-quality preference dataset, which should capture the fine-grained nuances of harmful and harmless responses. This motivates the need to develop the datasets involving preference margins, which accurately quantify how harmless one response is compared to another. In this paper, we take the first step to propose an effective and cost-efficient framework to promote the margin-enhanced preference dataset development. Our framework, Legend, Leverages rEpresentation enGineering to annotate preferENce Datasets. It constructs the specific direction within the LLM's embedding space that represents safety. By leveraging this safety direction, Legend can then leverage the semantic distances of paired responses along this direction to annotate margins automatically. We experimentally demonstrate our effectiveness in both reward modeling and harmless alignment for LLMs. Legend also stands out for its efficiency, requiring only the inference time rather than additional training. This efficiency allows for easier implementation and scalability, making Legend particularly valuable for practical applications in aligning LLMs with safe conversations.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the need for preference datasets with safety margins to improve reward models in distinguishing subtle safety differences. It proposes LEGEND, a framework that constructs a safety direction in the LLM embedding space using representation engineering and automatically annotates margins based on semantic distances along that direction. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness in reward modeling and harmless alignment, with efficiency from requiring only inference time. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对奖励模型需要具有安全边际的偏好数据集以区分细微安全差异的问题，提出LEGEND框架，通过在LLM嵌入空间中构建安全方向并利用该方向上的语义距离自动标注边际。实验显示该方法在奖励建模和无害对齐中有效，且仅需推理时间，无需额外训练。本文改进了对齐方法，但未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Unveiling the Attribute Misbinding Threat in Identity-Preserving Models
papers.abstract: Identity-preserving models have led to notable progress in generating personalized content. Unfortunately, such models also exacerbate risks when misused, for instance, by generating threatening content targeting specific individuals. This paper introduces the Attribute Misbinding Attack, a novel method that poses a threat to identity-preserving models by inducing them to produce Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) content. The attack's core idea involves crafting benign-looking textual prompts to circumvent text-filter safeguards and leverage a key model vulnerability: flawed attribute binding that stems from its internal attention bias. This results in misattributing harmful descriptions to a target identity and generating NSFW outputs. To facilitate the study of this attack, we present the Misbinding Prompt evaluation set, which examines the content generation risks of current state-of-the-art identity-preserving models across four risk dimensions: pornography, violence, discrimination, and illegality. Additionally, we introduce the Attribute Binding Safety Score (ABSS), a metric for concurrently assessing both content fidelity and safety compliance. Experimental results show that our Misbinding Prompt evaluation set achieves a 5.28 % higher success rate in bypassing five leading text filters (including GPT-4o) compared to existing main-stream evaluation sets, while also demonstrating the highest proportion of NSFW content generation. The proposed ABSS metric enables a more comprehensive evaluation of identity-preserving models by concurrently assessing both content fidelity and safety compliance.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces the Attribute Misbinding Attack, which exploits flawed attribute binding in identity-preserving models to generate NSFW content. The attack uses benign-looking prompts to circumvent text filters and misattribute harmful descriptions to target identities through attention biases. Evaluation with the Misbinding Prompt set shows a 5.28% higher filter bypass rate than mainstream sets and the highest NSFW generation ratio. This work reveals a mechanistic vulnerability in attention alignment, suggesting that safety modules can be bypassed by manipulating internal binding processes.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出属性误绑定攻击，利用身份保持模型中属性绑定的缺陷生成不良内容。该攻击通过看似无害的提示绕过文本过滤器，并利用注意力偏见将有害描述错误归于目标身份。使用误绑定提示集评估表明，其绕过主流过滤器的成功率比现有数据集高5.28%，且生成不良内容比例最高。该研究揭示了注意力对齐的机制脆弱性，表明安全模块可通过操纵内部绑定过程被绕过。

papers.title: Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed with hierarchical instruction schemes, where certain instructions (e.g., system-level directives) are expected to take precedence over others (e.g., user messages). Yet, we lack a systematic understanding of how effectively these hierarchical control mechanisms work. We introduce a systematic evaluation framework based on constraint prioritization to assess how well LLMs enforce instruction hierarchies. Our experiments across six state-of-the-art LLMs reveal that models struggle with consistent instruction prioritization, even for simple formatting conflicts. We find that the widely-adopted system/user prompt separation fails to establish a reliable instruction hierarchy, and models exhibit strong inherent biases toward certain constraint types regardless of their priority designation. Interestingly, we also find that societal hierarchy framings (e.g., authority, expertise, consensus) show stronger influence on model behavior than system/user roles, suggesting that pretraining-derived social structures function as latent behavioral priors with potentially greater impact than post-training guardrails.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the reliability of instruction hierarchies in large language models (LLMs), where system-level directives should override user messages for safety alignment. It introduces a constraint prioritization evaluation framework and tests six state-of-the-art models. The results show that LLMs consistently fail to enforce instruction hierarchies, with system/user role separation being ineffective and models exhibiting strong inherent biases toward certain constraints regardless of priority. This exposes a fragility in post-training safety alignment: a core mechanism designed to enforce safety can be easily bypassed, indicating that alignment is not robust and can be broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大型语言模型中指令层级机制的可靠性，即系统级指令本应优先于用户消息以实现安全对齐。作者提出了基于约束优先级的评估框架，并测试了六个顶尖模型。结果表明，模型无法一致地执行指令层级，系统/用户角色分离无效，且模型对某些约束类型存在固有偏好，不受优先级影响。这揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：用于强制安全的核心机制可被轻易绕过，说明对齐并不鲁棒，易被攻破。

papers.title: AlignTree: Efficient Defense Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that bypass safety guidelines and generate harmful content. Mitigating these vulnerabilities requires defense mechanisms that are both robust and computationally efficient. However, existing approaches either incur high computational costs or rely on lightweight defenses that can be easily circumvented, rendering them impractical for real-world LLM-based systems. In this work, we introduce the AlignTree defense, which enhances model alignment while maintaining minimal computational overhead. AlignTree monitors LLM activations during generation and detects misaligned behavior using an efficient random forest classifier. This classifier operates on two signals: (i) the refusal direction - a linear representation that activates on misaligned prompts, and (ii) an SVM-based signal that captures non-linear features associated with harmful content. Unlike previous methods, AlignTree does not require additional prompts or auxiliary guard models. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of AlignTree across multiple LLMs and benchmarks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to jailbreak attacks that bypass safety guidelines and generate harmful content. It proposes AlignTree, a defense mechanism that efficiently monitors LLM activations during generation using a random forest classifier operating on a linear refusal direction and an SVM-based nonlinear signal. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that AlignTree achieves both robustness and minimal computational overhead compared to existing defenses. Relating to post-training safety alignment fragility, this work introduces a hardening method that detects misaligned behavior on the fly, suggesting that lightweight runtime monitoring can mitigate alignment failures without retraining, though it does not directly analyze the fragility of the alignment module itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型（LLM）易受越狱攻击绕过安全准则生成有害内容的问题。提出 AlignTree 防御机制，通过在生成期间监测 LLM 激活，利用随机森林分类器，结合线性拒绝方向信号和基于 SVM 的非线性特征信号来高效检测未对齐行为。在多个 LLM 和基准测试上的大量实验表明，AlignTree 在保持低计算开销的同时实现了防御的鲁棒性。就后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题而言，本文给出了一种强化方法，通过在推理时动态检测未对齐行为来缓解对齐失败，但并未直接研究对齐模块本身的脆弱性。

papers.title: LLMGuard: Guarding against Unsafe LLM Behavior
papers.abstract:
Although the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) in enterprise settings brings new opportunities and capabilities, it also brings challenges, such as the risk of generating inappropriate, biased, or misleading content that violates regulations and can have legal concerns.
To alleviate this, we present "LLMGuard", a tool that monitors user interactions with an LLM application and flags content against specific behaviours or conversation topics. To do this robustly, LLMGuard employs an ensemble of detectors.
papers.summary_en: LLMGuard addresses the problem of LLMs generating inappropriate or biased content in enterprise settings. It proposes a monitoring tool that employs an ensemble of detectors to flag user interactions against specific behaviors or topics. The abstract does not provide evaluation details, but the approach aims to robustly detect unsafe content. This paper introduces an external moderation layer rather than directly investigating the fragility of post-training safety alignment, so it complements alignment without addressing whether it is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: LLMGuard 针对企业环境中大型语言模型生成不当或偏见内容的问题。提出一种监控工具，采用集成检测器对用户交互按特定行为或话题进行标记。摘要未给出评估细节，但该方法旨在稳健地检测不安全内容。本文引入外部审核层，而非直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，是对对齐机制的补充，但未回答其是否鲁棒或易被绕过。

papers.title: Robust Multi-Objective Preference Alignment with Online DPO
papers.abstract: Multi-objective preference alignment of large language models (LLMs) is critical for developing AI systems that are more configurable, personalizable, helpful, and safe. However, optimizing model outputs to satisfy diverse objectives with variable weights at inference time for truly personalized models presents a significant challenge. Existing approaches are either computationally expensive to train or do not sufficiently steer model behaviors. This paper introduces the Multi-Objective Online DPO (MO-ODPO) algorithm, designed to robustly and efficiently align model behaviors with multiple, potentially conflicting human preferences. Our approach incorporates a prompt conditioning mechanism, allowing us to train a single preference-conditional policy, that can adapt to new preference combinations at inference. Experiments on two popular benchmarks show that MO-ODPO Pareto-dominates existing baselines while providing excellent inference-time steerability between diverse objectives.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with multiple, potentially conflicting human preferences to enable configurable and personalized AI. It proposes Multi-Objective Online DPO (MO-ODPO), which uses prompt conditioning to train a single preference-conditional policy that adapts to arbitrary preference weights at inference time. Evaluations on two benchmarks show MO-ODPO Pareto-dominates existing baselines and provides strong inference-time steerability between objectives. This paper advances multi-objective alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文应对使大语言模型对齐多个可能冲突的人类偏好以实现可配置和个性化AI的挑战。提出多目标在线DPO（MO-ODPO），通过提示条件训练单一策略，在推理时适应任意偏好权重。在两个基准上的评估表明，MO-ODPO在帕累托效率上优于现有基线，并在目标间提供出色的推理时可操控性。该论文推进了多目标对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts
papers.abstract:
Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) signify a groundbreaking paradigm shift within the Artificial Intelligence (AI) community, extending beyond the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by assimilating additional modalities (e.g., images).
Despite this advancement, the safety of LVLMs remains adequately underexplored, with a potential overreliance on the safety assurances purported by their underlying LLMs. 
In this paper, we propose FigStep, a straightforward yet effective black-box jailbreak algorithm against LVLMs.
Instead of feeding textual harmful instructions directly, FigStep converts the prohibited content into images through typography to bypass the safety alignment.
The experimental results indicate that FigStep can achieve an average attack success rate of 82.50% on six promising open-source LVLMs.
Not merely to demonstrate the efficacy of FigStep, we conduct comprehensive ablation studies and analyze the distribution of the semantic embeddings to uncover that the reason behind the success of FigStep is the deficiency of safety alignment for visual embeddings. 
Moreover, we compare FigStep with five text-only jailbreaks and four image-based jailbreaks to demonstrate the superiority of FigStep, i.e., negligible attack costs and better attack performance.
Above all, our work reveals that current LVLMs are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which highlights the necessity of novel cross-modality safety alignment techniques.
papers.summary_en: This paper exposes a new attack surface in large vision-language models (LVLMs) by introducing FigStep, a black-box jailbreak that converts harmful textual queries into typographic images to circumvent safety alignment. Experiments on six open-source LVLMs yield an 82.50% average attack success rate, and ablation studies attribute the vulnerability to insufficient safety alignment on visual embeddings. The findings directly support the SoK's central question by demonstrating that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be easily bypassed through cross-modality exploits, underscoring the need for robust multimodal alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）的安全性，提出了一种名为FigStep的黑盒越狱攻击方法，通过将有害文本指令转化为排版图像来绕过安全对齐。实验在六个开源LVLMs上取得了平均82.50%的攻击成功率，消融研究表明漏洞源于视觉嵌入的安全对齐不足。这些发现直接回应了SoK的核心问题：训练后安全对齐是脆弱的，可被跨模态利用轻易绕过，凸显了鲁棒多模态对齐的必要性。

papers.title: ParetoHqD: Fast Offline Multiobjective Alignment of Large Language Models Using Pareto High-Quality Data
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models with multiple human expectations and values is crucial for ensuring that they adequately serve a variety of user needs. To this end, offline multiobjective alignment algorithms such as the Rewards-in-Context algorithm have shown strong performance and efficiency. However, inappropriate preference representations and training with imbalanced reward scores limit the performance of such algorithms. In this work, we introduce ParetoHqD that addresses the above issues by representing human preferences as preference directions in the objective space and regarding data near the Pareto front as ''high-quality'' data. For each preference, ParetoHqD follows a two-stage supervised fine-tuning process, where each stage uses an individual Pareto high-quality training set that best matches its preference direction. The experimental results have demonstrated the superiority of ParetoHqD over five baselines on two multiobjective alignment tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of aligning large language models with multiple human values, where existing offline multiobjective algorithms suffer from inappropriate preference representations and imbalanced reward scores. It proposes ParetoHqD, which represents preferences as directions in objective space and uses Pareto-optimal data as high-quality training instances in a two-stage supervised fine-tuning process tailored to each preference. Experiments on two multiobjective alignment tasks show that ParetoHqD outperforms five baselines. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question regarding post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决将大语言模型与多种人类价值对齐的问题，现有离线多目标算法存在偏好表示不当和奖励分数不平衡的缺陷。论文提出ParetoHqD，将偏好表示为目标空间中的方向，并将帕累托前沿数据视为高质量数据，通过两阶段监督微调为每个偏好匹配训练集。在两个多目标对齐任务上的实验表明，ParetoHqD优于五种基线方法。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Activation Manipulation Attack: Penetrating and Harmful Jailbreak Attack Against Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract:
Recently, Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have been demonstrated to be vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, highlighting the urgent need for further research to comprehensively identify and mitigate these threats.
Unfortunately, existing jailbreak studies primarily focus on coarse-grained input manipulation to elicit specific responses, overlooking the exploitation of internal representations, i.e., intermediate activations, which constrains their ability to penetrate alignment safeguards and generate harmful responses.
To tackle this issue, we propose the Activation Manipulation (ActMan) Attack framework, which performs fine-grained activation manipulations inspired by the perception and cognition stages of human decision-making, enhancing both the penetration capability and harmfulness of attacks.
To improve penetration capability, we introduce a Deceptive Visual Camouflage module inspired by the masking effect in human perception. This module uses a benign activation-guided attention redirection strategy to conceal abnormal activation patterns, thereby suppressing LVLM's defense detection during early-stage decoding.
To enhance harmfulness, we design a Malicious Semantic Induction module drawing from the framing effect in human cognition, which reconstructs jailbreak instructions using malicious activation guidance to change LVLM’s risk assessment during late-stage decoding, thereby amplifying the harmfulness of model responses.
Extensive experiments on six mainstream LVLMs demonstrate that our method remarkably outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average relative ASR improvement of 12.06%.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreak attacks against large vision-language models (LVLMs) by exploiting fine-grained manipulation of internal activations, an attack surface overlooked by prior methods that focus on coarse input perturbations. It proposes the Activation Manipulation (ActMan) Attack framework, which incorporates a Deceptive Visual Camouflage module to suppress defense detection and a Malicious Semantic Induction module to amplify harmful outputs, inspired by perceptual and cognitive biases. Evaluated on six mainstream LVLMs, ActMan achieves a 12.06% average relative improvement in attack success rate over state-of-the-art baselines. The findings highlight the fragility of post-training safety alignment in LVLMs, as it can be bypassed by directly targeting internal representations.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）的越狱攻击漏洞，聚焦于现有方法忽视的内部激活细粒度操纵这一攻击面。提出激活操纵攻击框架（ActMan），受感知与认知偏差启发，通过欺骗性视觉伪装模块抑制防御检测，利用恶意语义诱导模块放大有害输出。在六个主流LVLMs上的实验表明，ActMan的攻击成功率平均相对提升12.06%，优于现有基线。该研究直接证明了LVLMs的后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，攻击者可通过操纵内部表示轻易绕过防护。

papers.title: Unintended Misalignment from Agentic Fine-Tuning: Risks and Mitigation
papers.abstract: Beyond simple text generation, Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved into agentic systems capable of planning and interacting with external tools to solve complex tasks. This evolution involves fine-tuning LLMs on agent-specific tasks to enhance their proficiency. However, safety concerns are frequently overlooked during this fine-tuning process. In this work, we show that aligned LLMs can become unintentionally misaligned, leading to a higher likelihood of executing harmful tasks and a reduced tendency to refuse them when fine-tuned to execute agentic tasks. To address these safety challenges, we propose Prefix INjection Guard (PING), a simple yet effective method that prepends automatically generated natural language prefixes to agent responses, guiding them to refuse harmful requests while preserving performance on benign tasks. Specifically, we introduce an iterative approach that alternates between (1) generating candidate prefixes and (2) selecting those that optimize both task performance and refusal behavior. Experimental results demonstrate that PING significantly enhances the safety of fine-tuned LLM agents without sacrificing their effectiveness. PING consistently outperforms existing prompting approaches across diverse benchmarks in both web navigation and code generation tasks. Our analysis of internal hidden states via linear probes reveals that prefix tokens are crucial for behavior modification, explaining the performance gains.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that fine-tuning aligned LLMs on agentic tasks can unintentionally reduce safety, leading to more harmful outputs and fewer refusals. It proposes Prefix INjection Guard (PING), an iterative method that prepends automatically generated prefixes to agent responses to guide refusal of harmful requests while maintaining task performance. Evaluated on web navigation and code generation benchmarks, PING significantly improves safety without sacrificing effectiveness, outperforming existing prompting approaches. The work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by uncovering a new attack surface (agentic fine-tuning causing misalignment) and offers a mitigation, showing alignment can be both easily broken and hardened.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐后的大语言模型在智能体任务微调中意外失准的问题，即更易执行有害任务且拒绝减少。提出前缀注入防护（PING），通过迭代生成并选择优化任务表现和拒绝行为的前缀，自动引导模型拒绝有害请求。在网页导航和代码生成基准上，PING在不影响效用的前提下显著提升安全性，优于现有提示方法。该工作直接揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，发现智能体微调可导致失准的新攻击面，并提供防御，表明对齐既易被破坏也可加固。

papers.title: CHASE: Contextual History for Adaptive and Simple Exploitation in Large Language Model Jailbreaking
papers.abstract: We propose Contextual History for Adaptive and Simple Exploitation (CHASE), a novel multi-turn method for Large Language Model (LLM) jailbreaking. Rather than directly attack an LLM that may be difficult to jailbreak, CHASE first collects jailbroken histories from an easy-to-jailbreak LLM and then transfers them to the target LLM. Through this history transfer process, CHASE misleads the target LLM into thinking that it is responsible for producing the jailbroken histories and increases the chances of successful jailbreaking by prompting it to continue the conversation. Extensive evaluations on mainstream LLMs show that CHASE consistently achieves higher attack success rates and demands fewer computational resources compared to existing methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of jailbreaking large language models (LLMs) through multi-turn interactions. It proposes CHASE, a method that collects successful jailbroken dialogues from an easier-to-attack LLM and transfers them as contextual history to a target LLM, tricking it into continuing the harmful conversation. Extensive evaluations show that CHASE achieves higher attack success rates and demands fewer computational resources than existing jailbreaking methods. By exploiting cross-model context transfer, CHASE reveals a novel attack surface where safety alignment can be circumvented, providing clear evidence that post-training safety measures may be fragile when confronted with convincingly jailbroken history prompts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了通过多轮对话对大语言模型（LLM）进行越狱攻击的问题。提出了CHASE方法，先从一个易受攻击的LLM收集越狱对话历史，再将其作为上下文转移到目标LLM，诱使其继续生成有害内容。实验表明，CHASE在主流LLM上取得了更高的攻击成功率且计算开销更低。该方法利用跨模型上下文迁移发现了一种新攻击面，表明当面对具有说服力的越狱历史时，安全对齐可能被绕过，直接支持了后训练安全对齐存在脆弱性的观点。

papers.title: Watch Out for Your Guidance on Generation! Exploring Conditional Backdoor Attacks against Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Mainstream backdoor attacks on large language models (LLMs) typically set a fixed trigger in the input instance and specific responses for triggered queries. 
However, the fixed trigger setting (e.g., unusual words) may be easily detected by human detection, limiting the effectiveness and practicality in real-world scenarios. 
To enhance the stealthiness of backdoor activation, we present a new poisoning paradigm against LLMs triggered by specifying generation conditions, which are commonly adopted strategies by users during model inference. 
The poisoned model performs normally for output under normal/other generation conditions, while becomes harmful for output under target generation conditions. 
To achieve this objective, we introduce BrieFool, an efficient attack framework. 
It leverages the characteristics of generation conditions by efficient instruction sampling and poisoning data generation, thereby influencing the behavior of LLMs under target conditions. Our attack can be generally divided into two types with different targets: Safety unalignment attack and Ability degradation attack. 
Our extensive experiments demonstrate that BrieFool is effective across safety domains and ability domains, achieving higher success rates than baseline methods, with 94.3% on GPT-3.5-turbo.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of existing backdoor attacks on LLMs that rely on fixed, easily detectable triggers. It proposes BrieFool, a framework that creates conditional backdoors activated by specifying generation conditions (e.g., output styles), making the attack stealthier. Experiments show BrieFool achieves a high attack success rate of 94.3% on GPT-3.5-turbo across safety and ability domains. The work reveals a novel fragility in LLM safety alignment: generation-conditioned triggers can bypass safeguards, demonstrating that alignment is not robust to such conditional attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有大语言模型后门攻击依赖固定触发词、易于被检测的局限，提出了一种新型条件后门攻击。提出BrieFool框架，通过生成条件（如输出风格）作为触发，使模型仅在目标条件下产生有害输出，提升隐蔽性。实验在GPT-3.5-turbo上验证，攻击成功率高达94.3%，超过基准方法。该研究揭示了大模型安全对齐的新脆弱性：利用生成条件可绕过安全防护，表明对齐在面对此类条件攻击时并不鲁棒。

papers.title: Silenced Biases: The Dark Side LLMs Learned to Refuse
papers.abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) are becoming increasingly widespread, especially in sensitive applications where fairness is essential and biased outputs can cause significant harm. However, evaluating the fairness of models is a complex challenge, and approaches that do so typically utilize standard question-answer (QA) styled schemes. Such methods often overlook deeper issues by interpreting the model's refusal responses as positive fairness measurements, which creates a false sense of fairness. In this work, we introduce the concept of silenced biases, which are unfair preferences encoded within models' latent space and are effectively concealed by safety-alignment. Previous approaches that considered similar indirect biases often relied on prompt manipulation or handcrafted implicit queries, which present limited scalability and risk contaminating the evaluation process with additional biases. We propose the Silenced Bias Benchmark (SBB), which aims to uncover these biases by employing activation steering to reduce model refusals during QA. SBB supports easy expansion to new demographic groups and subjects, presenting a fairness evaluation framework that encourages the future development of fair models and tools beyond the masking effects of alignment training. We demonstrate our approach over multiple LLMs, where our findings expose an alarming distinction between models' direct responses and their underlying fairness issues.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that safety-aligned LLMs may conceal unfair biases through refusal responses, leading to a false sense of fairness. It proposes the Silenced Bias Benchmark (SBB), which uses activation steering to reduce refusals and expose latent biases during standard QA. Evaluated on multiple LLMs, SBB reveals significant hidden biases that are not evident in direct outputs, highlighting a gap between perceived and actual fairness. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment can be fragile, as it masks rather than removes underlying biases, offering a novel way to probe the model's true preferences.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了安全对齐的大语言模型可能通过拒绝回答来隐藏不公平偏见，从而造成公平假象的问题。提出了静默偏见基准（SBB），利用激活引导减少拒绝回答，在标准问答中暴露潜在偏见。在多个大语言模型上的评估显示，SBB揭示了直接输出中不明显的重要隐藏偏见，凸显了感知公平与实际公平之间的差距。该工作表明，后训练安全对齐可能比较脆弱，因为它掩盖而非消除了底层偏见，提供了一种探测模型真实偏好的新方法。

papers.title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: Model Deficiency Unlearning via Parameter-Efficient Module Operation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used in various applications but are known to suffer from issues related to untruthfulness and toxicity. While parameter-efficient modules (PEMs) have demonstrated their effectiveness in equipping models with new skills, leveraging PEMs for deficiency unlearning remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a PEMs operation approach, namely Extraction-before-Subtraction (Ext-Sub), to enhance the truthfulness and detoxification of LLMs through the integration of ``expert'' PEM and ``anti-expert'' PEM. Remarkably, even anti-expert PEM possess valuable capabilities due to their proficiency in generating fabricated content, which necessitates language modeling and logical narrative competence. Rather than merely negating the parameters, our approach involves extracting and eliminating solely the deficiency capability within anti-expert PEM while preserving the general capabilities. To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach in terms of truthfulness and detoxification, we conduct extensive experiments on LLMs, encompassing additional abilities such as language modelling and mathematical reasoning. Our empirical results demonstrate that our approach effectively improves truthfulness and detoxification, while largely preserving the fundamental abilities of LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses untruthfulness and toxicity in large language models (LLMs). It proposes Extraction-before-Subtraction (Ext-Sub), a parameter-efficient module (PEM) operation approach that uses an expert PEM and an anti-expert PEM to extract and remove only deficiency capabilities while preserving general skills. Evaluation on truthfulness and detoxification tasks shows improved safety metrics without significantly harming language modeling or mathematical reasoning. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型中存在的不真实性和有毒内容问题。提出了一种参数高效模块操作方法“提取再减去”(Ext-Sub)，利用专家PEM和反专家PEM提取并仅移除缺陷能力，同时保留通用能力。在真实性和去毒任务上的评估显示该方法有效提升了安全性指标，且未显著损害语言建模和数学推理能力。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Token Highlighter: Inspecting and Mitigating Jailbreak Prompts for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into services such as ChatGPT to provide responses to user queries. To mitigate potential harm and prevent misuse, there have been concerted efforts to align the LLMs with human values and legal compliance by incorporating various techniques, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), into the training of the LLMs. However, recent research has exposed that even aligned LLMs are susceptible to adversarial manipulations known as Jailbreak Attacks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method called Token Highlighter to inspect and mitigate the potential jailbreak threats in the user query. Token Highlighter introduced a concept called Affirmation Loss to measure the LLM's willingness to answer the user query. It then uses the gradient of Affirmation Loss for each token in the user query to locate the jailbreak-critical tokens. Further, Token Highlighter exploits our proposed Soft Removal technique to mitigate the jailbreak effects of critical tokens via shrinking their token embeddings. Experimental results on two aligned LLMs (LLaMA-2 and Vicuna-V1.5) demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively defend against a variety of Jailbreak Attacks while maintaining competent performance on benign questions of the AlpacaEval benchmark. In addition, Token Highlighter is a cost-effective and interpretable defense because it only needs to query the protected LLM once to compute the Affirmation Loss and can highlight the critical tokens upon refusal.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses jailbreak attacks on safety-aligned large language models (LLMs). It proposes Token Highlighter, a defense that measures the model's Affirmation Loss to identify critical tokens via gradients, then applies Soft Removal by shrinking their embeddings to neutralize the attack. Evaluated on LLaMA-2 and Vicuna-V1.5 against multiple jailbreak methods, Token Highlighter effectively defends while preserving performance on benign queries from AlpacaEval. By offering a cost-effective and interpretable mitigation, this work shows that alignment can be fortified against adversarial manipulations, indirectly addressing the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型面临的越狱攻击问题，提出了一种名为Token Highlighter的防御方法。该方法通过计算模型的肯定损失（Affirmation Loss）及其对输入token的梯度来定位关键token，并利用软移除（Soft Removal）技术收缩关键token的嵌入以减轻攻击效果。在LLaMA-2和Vicuna-V1.5上的实验表明，Token Highlighter能有效防御多种越狱攻击，同时在AlpacaEval的良性问题上保持性能。通过提供一种经济且可解释的防御手段，该工作间接表明后训练安全对齐并非绝对鲁棒，但可以通过此种方式增强其抵抗恶意操纵的能力。

papers.title: Long-form RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Long-form Generation
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of reinforcement learning-based alignment highlights the growing importance of reward models. Various benchmarks have been built to evaluate reward models in various domains and scenarios. However, a significant gap remains in assessing reward models for long-form generation, despite its critical role in real-world applications. To bridge this, we introduce Long-form RewardBench, the first reward modeling testbed specifically designed for long-form generation. Our benchmark encompasses five key subtasks: QA, RAG, Chat, Writing, and Reasoning. We collected instruction and preference data through a meticulously designed multi-stage data collection process, and conducted extensive experiments on 20+ mainstream reward models, including both classifiers and generative models. Our findings reveal that current models still lack long-form reward modeling capabilities. Furthermore, we designed a novel Long-form Needle-in-a-Haystack Test, which revealed a correlation between reward modeling performance and the error's position within a response, as well as the overall response length, with distinct characteristics observed between classification and generative models. Finally, we demonstrate that classifier exhibit better generalizability compared to generative models trained on the same data. As the first benchmark for long-form reward modeling, this work aims to offer a robust platform for visualizing progress in this crucial area.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of evaluation benchmarks for reward models in long-form generation tasks. It introduces Long-form RewardBench, the first testbed with five subtasks (QA, RAG, Chat, Writing, Reasoning) built through multi-stage data collection. Experiments on 20+ models reveal current reward models struggle with long-form reward modeling, and a novel needle-in-a-haystack test shows performance depends on error position and response length, with better generalization in classifiers. This work provides essential evaluation tools for reward models, which underpin RLHF alignment, but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对长文本生成中奖励模型评估基准缺失的问题。提出了首个长文本奖励模型测试平台Long-form RewardBench，涵盖问答、RAG、对话、写作和推理五类任务。对20多个主流模型的实验表明，现有模型缺乏长文本奖励建模能力；新设计的‘大海捞针’测试显示性能与错误位置和回复长度相关，且分类模型泛化性优于生成模型。该研究为奖励模型评估提供了重要工具，间接关联对齐稳健性，但未直接解答安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Medical MLLM Is Vulnerable: Cross-Modality Jailbreak and Mismatched Attacks on Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Security concerns related to Large Language Models (LLMs) have been extensively explored; however, the safety implications for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly in medical contexts (MedMLLMs), remain inadequately addressed. This paper investigates the security vulnerabilities of MedMLLMs, focusing on their deployment in clinical environments where the accuracy and relevance of question-and-answer interactions are crucial for addressing complex medical challenges. We introduce and redefine two attack types: mismatched malicious attack (2M-attack) and optimized mismatched malicious attack (O2M-attack), by integrating existing clinical data with atypical natural phenomena. Using the comprehensive 3MAD dataset that we developed, which spans a diverse range of medical imaging modalities and adverse medical scenarios, we performed an in-depth analysis and proposed the MCM optimization method. This approach significantly improves the attack success rate against MedMLLMs. Our evaluations, which include white-box attacks on LLaVA-Med and transfer (black-box) attacks on four other SOTA models, reveal that even MedMLLMs designed with advanced security mechanisms remain vulnerable to breaches. This study highlights the critical need for robust security measures to enhance the safety and reliability of open-source MedMLLMs, especially in light of the potential impact of jailbreak attacks and other malicious exploits in clinical applications. Warning: Medical jailbreaking may generate content that includes unverified diagnoses and treatment recommendations. Always consult professional medical advice.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates security vulnerabilities in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models (MedMLLMs) by introducing mismatched malicious attacks (2M-attack and O2M-attack) that inject harmful cross-modality content. It proposes the MCM optimization method and constructs the 3MAD dataset spanning diverse medical imaging and adverse scenarios to enhance attack effectiveness. Evaluations on LLaVA-Med and four other state-of-the-art models demonstrate high attack success rates in both white-box and black-box settings, revealing that even security-hardened MedMLLMs are susceptible. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of safety alignment in medical MLLMs, as advanced defenses can be bypassed through cross-modality jailbreaks, underscoring the need for more robust protections.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文通过提出不匹配恶意攻击（2M-attack和O2M-attack）和跨模态越狱方法，揭示了医学多模态大模型的脆弱性。它构建了涵盖多种医学影像和不良场景的3MAD数据集，并开发了MCM优化方法以提升攻击成功率。实验表明，即使具备先进安全机制的MedMLLMs也无法抵御此类攻击，白盒和迁移黑盒攻击均取得高成功率。这一发现直接印证了安全对齐在医学多模态模型中的脆弱性，说明现有防御措施可被轻易突破，迫切需要加强安全机制。

papers.title: Model Editing as a Double-Edged Sword: Steering Agent Behavior Toward Beneficence or Harm
papers.abstract: Agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities across a wide range of tasks. However, deploying LLM-based agents in high-stakes domains comes with significant safety and ethical risks. Unethical behavior by these agents can directly result in serious real-world consequences, including physical harm and financial loss. To efficiently steer the ethical behavior of agents, we frame agent behavior steering as a model editing task, which we term Behavior Editing. Model editing is an emerging area of research that enables precise and efficient modifications to LLMs while preserving their overall capabilities. To systematically study and evaluate this approach, we introduce BehaviorBench, a multi-tier benchmark grounded in psychological moral theories. This benchmark supports both the evaluation and editing of agent behaviors across a variety of scenarios, with each tier introducing more complex and ambiguous scenarios. We first demonstrate that Behavior Editing can dynamically steer agents toward the target behavior within specific scenarios. Moreover, Behavior Editing enables not only scenario-specific local adjustments but also more extensive shifts in an agent’s global moral alignment. We demonstrate that Behavior Editing can be used to promote ethical and benevolent behavior or, conversely, to induce harmful or malicious behavior. Through extensive evaluations of agents built on frontier LLMs, BehaviorBench validates the effectiveness of behavior editing across a wide range of models and scenarios. Our findings offer key insights into a new paradigm for steering agent behavior, highlighting both the promise and perils of Behavior Editing.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of steering ethical behavior in LLM-based agents by framing it as a model editing task called Behavior Editing. It introduces BehaviorBench, a multi-tier benchmark grounded in psychological moral theories, to systematically evaluate and edit agent behaviors across increasingly complex scenarios. Evaluations on frontier LLMs show that Behavior Editing enables both scenario-specific local adjustments and global shifts in moral alignment, effectively promoting either ethical or harmful behavior. This work demonstrates that post-hoc behavior editing can easily build, break, or bypass safety alignment, directly engaging with the fragility question by revealing that alignment is not robust and can be arbitrarily steered.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过将LLM智能体的伦理行为控制框定为模型编辑任务（即行为编辑）来解决行为引导问题。提出基于心理学道德理论的多层级基准BehaviorBench，系统评估和编辑不同复杂性场景下的智能体行为。在主流LLM上的评估表明，行为编辑不仅能实现场景局部的行为调整，还能改变全局道德取向，有效诱导利他或有害行为。该工作揭示事后行为编辑可轻易构建、打破或绕过安全对齐，直接回应了对齐脆弱性问题，表明智能体的安全对齐可被任意操纵。

papers.title: MedOmni-45°: A Safety-Performance Benchmark for Reasoning-Oriented LLMs in Medicine
papers.abstract: With the rapid integration of large language models (LLMs) into medical decision-support aids, ensuring reliability in reasoning steps—not just final answers—is increasingly critical. Two key safety dimensions are Chain-of-Thought (CoT) faithfulness, which assesses alignment of the model’s reasoning process with both its response and medical facts, and sycophancy, an emergent misalignment where models follow misleading cues instead of factual correctness. Yet existing benchmarks tend to prioritize performance evaluation, frequently collapsing nuanced safety vulnerabilities into a single accuracy score. To fill this gap, we introduce MedOmni-45°, a benchmark and evaluation workflow explicitly designed to quantify the safety–performance trade-off in LLMs under manipulative hint conditions. The benchmark contains 1,804 reasoning-focused medical questions across six clinical specialties and three task types, including 500 publicly comparable items from MedMCQA. Each question is systematically augmented with seven manipulative hint types, each embedding two distinct misleading cue variants, along with a No-Hint baseline, resulting in approximately 27,000 unique inputs. These inputs are then evaluated across seven LLMs spanning open- and closed-source, general-purpose and medical-specific, and base versus reasoning-enhanced variants, amounting to over 189K total inference instances. Three orthogonal metrics (Accuracy, CoT-Faithfulness, Anti-Sycophancy) are combined into a composite score visualized via a 45° safety–performance plot. Results reveal a universal trade-off, with no model surpassing the ideal diagonal. Open-source QwQ-32B approaches closest at 43.81°, demonstrating notable safety while not surpassing others in performance. MedOmni-45° thus highlights critical vulnerabilities of LLMs in reasoning oriented medical tasks, offering a robust benchmark for future alignment research.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the gap in evaluating both safety (CoT faithfulness and sycophancy) and performance in LLMs for medical reasoning. It proposes MedOmni-45°, a benchmark comprising 1,804 medical questions augmented with seven manipulative hint types and two misleading cue variants, yielding ~27K inputs. Evaluation across seven LLMs and 189K inference instances reveals a universal safety-performance trade-off, with no model surpassing the ideal diagonal; QwQ-32B was closest at 43.81°. The work highlights the fragility of safety alignment under misleading cues, directly informing the SoK question by demonstrating that post-training safety can be compromised, though it does not propose a new attack or defense.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了医疗推理大语言模型评估中安全（思维链忠实性和谄媚性）与性能评价脱节的问题。提出MedOmni-45°基准，包含1804个医学问题，并系统性地添加七种操纵性提示和两种误导变体，生成约2.7万条输入。在七个大语言模型上进行约18.9万次推理评估，发现普遍的安全-性能权衡，无一模型超越理想对角线；QwQ-32B以43.81°最近接。该研究表明误导性线索可暴露安全对齐的脆弱性，直接回应了安全对齐是否稳健的SoK问题，尽管它未提出新攻击或防御，但为脆弱性研究提供了重要基准。

papers.title: Efficient LLM-Jailbreaking via Multimodal-LLM Jailbreak
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on jailbreaking attacks against large language models (LLMs), eliciting them to generate objectionable content in response to harmful user queries. Unlike previous LLM-jailbreak methods that directly orient to LLMs, our approach begins by constructing a multimodal large language model (MLLM) built upon the target LLM. Subsequently, we perform an efficient MLLM jailbreak and obtain a jailbreaking embedding. Finally, we convert the embedding into a textual jailbreaking suffix to carry out the jailbreak of target LLM. Compared to the direct LLM-jailbreak methods, our indirect jailbreaking approach is more efficient, as MLLMs are more vulnerable to jailbreak than pure LLMs. Additionally, to improve the attack success rate of jailbreak, we propose an image-text semantic matching scheme to identify a suitable initial input. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art jailbreak methods in terms of both efficiency and effectiveness. Moreover, our approach exhibits superior cross-class generalization abilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreaking attacks against LLMs to elicit harmful content. It proposes an indirect method: first build a multimodal LLM (MLLM) on the target LLM, then jailbreak the MLLM to obtain a jailbreaking embedding, and finally convert that embedding into a textual suffix for attacking the target LLM. An image-text semantic matching scheme is used to improve attack success. Experiments show it outperforms state-of-the-art in efficiency and effectiveness with superior cross-class generalization. The work demonstrates that safety alignment can be fragile when LLMs are extended to multimodal contexts, as MLLMs are more vulnerable and can serve as an attack vector to bypass LLM safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究针对大语言模型（LLM）的越狱攻击，旨在生成有害内容。它提出一种间接方法：首先在目标LLM上构建多模态大语言模型（MLLM），然后越狱该MLLM获得越狱嵌入，最后将嵌入转化为文本后缀以攻击目标LLM。还使用图文语义匹配方案提高攻击成功率。实验表明该方法在效率和效果上超越现有方法，且具有优越的跨类泛化能力。这项工作表明，当LLM扩展到多模态情境时安全对齐可能变得脆弱，因为MLLM更易受攻击，可被用作绕过LLM安全机制的途径。

papers.title: Bootstrapping LLMs via Preference-Based Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Bootstrapping large language models (LLMs) via preference-based policy optimization enables aligning model behavior with human preferences while reducing reliance on extensive manual annotations. We propose a novel preference-based policy optimization (PbPO) framework that formulates learning as a min-max game between the LLM policy and a reward model (RM). The RM is constrained within a confidence set derived from collected preferences to ensure reliable exploitation, while simultaneously promoting robust exploration. Our iterative online algorithm actively collects new preference data from the evolving policy, enabling continual self-improvement of both the policy and the RM. We provide theoretical guarantees, establishing high-probability regret bounds for both sequence-level and token-level RMs. Extensive experiments across five benchmark datasets demonstrate that PbPO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art preference optimization methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences while minimizing manual annotation. It proposes PbPO, a preference-based policy optimization framework that formulates learning as a min-max game between the LLM policy and a reward model, with a confidence set for reliable exploitation and robust exploration, iteratively collecting preferences online. Theoretical regret bounds are proved for both sequence-level and token-level reward models, and experiments on five benchmarks show PbPO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art preference optimization methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在减少人工标注的同时使大语言模型与人类偏好对齐的挑战。提出了一种基于偏好的策略优化框架PbPO，将学习建模为LLM策略与奖励模型之间的最小-最大博弈，通过置信集实现可靠利用和鲁棒探索，并迭代在线收集偏好数据。提供了序列级和词元级奖励模型的理论遗憾界，在五个基准上的实验表明PbPO一致优于现有最优偏好优化方法。该论文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: PurMM: Attention-Guided Test-Time Backdoor Purification in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Downstream fine-tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is advancing rapidly, allowing general models to achieve superior performance on domain-specific tasks. Yet most prior research focuses on performance gains and overlooks the vulnerability of the fine-tuning pipeline: attackers can easily poison the dataset to implant backdoors into MLLMs. We conduct an in-depth investigation of backdoor attacks on MLLMs and reveal the phenomenon of Attention Hijacking and its Hierarchical Mechanism. Guided by this insight, we propose PurMM, a test-time backdoor purification framework that removes visual tokens exhibiting anomalous attention, thereby avoiding targeted outputs while restoring correct answers. PurMM contains three stages: (1) locating tokens with abnormal attention, (2) filtering them using deep-layer cues, and (3) zeroing out their corresponding components in the visual embeddings. Unlike existing defences, PurMM dispenses with retraining and training-process modifications, operating at test-time to restore model performance while eliminating the backdoor. Extensive experiments across multiple MLLMs and datasets show that PurMM maintains normal performance, sharply reduces attack success rates, and consistently converts backdoor outputs to benign ones, offering a new perspective for safeguarding MLLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses backdoor attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during fine-tuning, uncovering a phenomenon called Attention Hijacking. It proposes PurMM, a test-time purification framework that zeroes out visual tokens with anomalous attention to restore correct outputs. Experiments on multiple MLLMs and datasets show PurMM maintains normal performance and sharply reduces attack success rates. The work demonstrates that backdoor attacks can easily undermine alignment, but test-time defenses can effectively restore robustness, contributing to the discussion on the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型微调中的后门攻击，发现了注意力劫持现象。提出PurMM框架，在测试时通过滤除异常注意力的视觉令牌来净化模型输出。实验表明，PurMM在多模型和多数据集上保持正常性能并大幅降低攻击成功率。该工作揭示了后门攻击可轻易破坏对齐，但测试时防御能有效恢复鲁棒性，为后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题提供了实证。

papers.title: SPA: Achieving Consensus in LLM Alignment via Self-Priority Optimization
papers.abstract: In high-stakes scenarios—such as self-harm, legal, or medical queries—LLMs must be both trustworthy and helpful. However, these goals often conflict. We propose priority alignment, a new alignment paradigm that enforces a strict “trustworthy-before-helpful” ordering: optimization of helpfulness is conditioned on first meeting trustworthy thresholds (e.g., harmlessness or honesty). To realize this, we introduce Self-Priority Alignment (SPA)—a fully unsupervised framework that generates diverse responses, self-evaluates them and refines them by the model itself, and applies dual-criterion denoising to remove inconsistency and control variance. From this, SPA constructs lexicographically ordered preference pairs and fine-tunes the model using an uncertainty-weighted alignment loss that emphasizes high-confidence, high-gap decisions. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show that SPA improves helpfulness without compromising safety, outperforming strong baselines while preserving general capabilities. Our results demonstrate that SPA provides a scalable and interpretable alignment strategy for critical LLM applications.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the conflict between helpfulness and trustworthiness in LLMs for high-stakes scenarios by introducing priority alignment, which enforces a strict trustworthy-before-helpful ordering. It proposes Self-Priority Alignment (SPA), a fully unsupervised framework that generates diverse responses, self-evaluates and refines them, applies dual-criterion denoising, and constructs lexicographically ordered preference pairs for fine-tuning with an uncertainty-weighted alignment loss. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show SPA improves helpfulness without compromising safety, outperforming strong baselines while preserving general capabilities. This paper advances alignment methodology by building a robust priority-based mechanism, but it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了高风险场景下LLM中帮助性与可信度之间的冲突，提出了优先级对齐的新范式，强制实施“先可信后帮助”的顺序。它提出自我优先级对齐（SPA）方法，一种完全无监督的框架，通过生成多样响应、自我评估与优化、双标准去噪，构建字典序偏好对，并使用不确定性加权对齐损失进行微调。在多个基准上的实验表明，SPA在不牺牲安全性的前提下提升了帮助性，超越了强基线并保持了通用能力。该论文通过构建鲁棒的基于优先级的机制推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易于绕过。

papers.title: SceneJailEval: A Scenario-Adaptive Multi-Dimensional Framework for Jailbreak Evaluation
papers.abstract:
Accurate jailbreak evaluation is critical for LLM red team testing and jailbreak research. Mainstream methods rely on binary classification (string matching, toxic text classifiers, and LLM-based methods), outputting only "yes/no" labels without quantifying harm severity. Emerged multi-dimensional frameworks (e.g., Security Violation, Relative Truthfulness and Informativeness) use unified evaluation standards across scenarios, leading to scenario-specific mismatches (e.g., "Relative Truthfulness" is irrelevant to "hate speech"), undermining evaluation accuracy. To address these, we propose SceneJailEval, with key contributions:
(1) A pioneering scenario-adaptive multi-dimensional framework for jailbreak evaluation, overcoming the critical "one-size-fits-all" limitation of existing multi-dimensional methods, and boasting robust extensibility to seamlessly adapt to customized or emerging scenarios.  
(2) A novel 14-scenario dataset featuring rich jailbreak variants and regional cases, addressing the long-standing gap in high-quality, comprehensive benchmarks for scenario-adaptive evaluation.  
(3) SceneJailEval delivers state-of-the-art performance with an F1 score of 0.917 on our full-scenario dataset (+6% over SOTA) and 0.995 on JBB (+3% over SOTA), breaking through the accuracy bottleneck of existing evaluation methods in heterogeneous scenarios and solidifying its superiority.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses inaccurate jailbreak evaluation caused by binary classification and scenario-invariant multi-dimensional frameworks that mismatch criteria to specific harmful scenarios. It proposes SceneJailEval, a scenario-adaptive multi-dimensional framework that dynamically adjusts evaluation dimensions per scenario, accompanied by a new 14-scenario dataset. The method achieves state-of-the-art F1 scores of 0.917 on the proposed dataset and 0.995 on JBB, significantly improving accuracy over existing methods. This work advances evaluation methodology for jailbreak harm severity, crucial for testing safety alignment robustness, but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 论文解决了现有越狱评估方法因二元分类和跨场景统一评估标准导致的评估不准问题，尤其是多维度框架在不同场景下维度不匹配。提出了SceneJailEval，一个场景自适应的多维度评估框架，能够动态调整每个场景的评估维度，并构建了一个包含14个场景的越狱数据集。该方法在全场景数据集上取得了0.917的F1分数（比SOTA高6%），在JBB上取得了0.995（比SOTA高3%），在异构场景中显著提升了评估准确性。该工作推进了越狱危害性评估方法论，为测试安全对齐的鲁棒性提供了重要工具，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐本身的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: EduGuardBench: A Holistic Benchmark for Evaluating the Pedagogical Fidelity and Adversarial Safety of LLMs as Simulated Teachers
papers.abstract: Large Language Models for Simulating Professions (SP-LLMs), particularly as teachers, are pivotal for personalized education. However, ensuring their professional competence and ethical safety remains a major challenge, as existing benchmarks fail to measure role-playing fidelity or address the unique teaching harms inherent in educational scenarios. To address this gap, we propose EduGuardBench, a dual-component benchmark that evaluates professional fidelity through the Role-playing Fidelity Score (RFS) and diagnoses harms specific to the teaching profession. It also probes safety vulnerabilities using persona-based adversarial prompts targeting both general harms and academic misconduct, with metrics such as Attack Success Rate (ASR) and a three-tier Refusal Quality assessment. Extensive experiments on 14 leading models reveal a stark polarization in performance. While reasoning-oriented models generally demonstrate higher fidelity, incompetence remains the dominant failure mode across most models. Adversarial testing uncovered a counterintuitive scaling paradox, where mid-sized models appear more vulnerable, challenging monotonic safety assumptions. Notably, we identify an Educational Transformation Effect, where the safest models convert harmful requests into teachable moments through ideal educational refusals. This ability is strongly negatively correlated with ASR, revealing a new dimension of advanced AI safety. EduGuardBench thus provides a reproducible framework for holistic assessment of professional, ethical, and pedagogical alignment, uncovering dynamics critical to deploying trustworthy AI in education.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the gap in evaluating both the pedagogical fidelity and adversarial safety of large language models (LLMs) when used as simulated teachers. It proposes EduGuardBench, a benchmark combining a Role-playing Fidelity Score (RFS) for professional competence and persona-based adversarial testing with metrics such as Attack Success Rate (ASR) and three-tier Refusal Quality for safety evaluation. Experiments on 14 models reveal that reasoning-oriented models achieve higher fidelity, yet incompetence dominates; adversarial testing exposes a scaling paradox where mid-sized models are more vulnerable, and identifies an Educational Transformation Effect where safe models convert harmful requests into teachable moments, strongly negatively correlated with ASR. These findings highlight the fragility of safety alignment, as the scaling paradox and successful adversarial attacks demonstrate that post-training safety can be bypassed, although the Educational Transformation Effect in some models points to more robust alignment behaviors.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在评估大型语言模型（LLM）作为模拟教师时的教学忠实度和对抗安全性方面缺乏基准的问题。提出了EduGuardBench基准，结合角色扮演忠实度评分（RFS）和基于角色的对抗提示测试，使用攻击成功率（ASR）和三级拒绝质量评估安全性。在14个模型上的实验表明，推理型模型忠实度较高但不足仍普遍；对抗测试揭示了中等规模模型更易受攻击的反直觉缩放悖论，并发现安全模型能将有害请求转化为教育时刻的“教育转化效应”，与ASR强负相关。这些发现凸显了安全对齐的脆弱性，缩放悖论和成功的对抗攻击表明事后安全可被绕过，但某些模型的教育转化效应显示了更鲁棒的对齐行为。

papers.title: Uncovering and Aligning Anomalous Attention Heads to Defend Against NLP Backdoor Attacks
papers.abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to the security of large language models (LLMs), causing them to exhibit anomalous behavior under specific trigger conditions. The design of backdoor triggers has evolved from fixed triggers to dynamic or implicit triggers. This increased flexibility in trigger design makes it challenging for defenders to accurately identify their specific forms. Most existing backdoor defense methods are limited to specific types of triggers or rely on an additional clean model for support. To address this issue, we propose a backdoor detection method based on attention similarity, enabling backdoor detection without prior knowledge of the trigger. Our study reveals that models subjected to backdoor attacks exhibit unusually high similarity among attention heads when exposed to triggers. Based on this observation, we propose an attention safety alignment approach combined with head-wise fine-tuning to rectify potentially contaminated attention heads, thereby effectively mitigating the impact of backdoor attacks. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly reduces the success rate of backdoor attacks while preserving the model’s performance on downstream tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses backdoor attacks on LLMs, where triggers are increasingly dynamic and hard to detect. The authors propose a detection method based on attention similarity that identifies backdoors without prior trigger knowledge, and then apply attention safety alignment with head-wise fine-tuning to rectify contaminated heads. Extensive experiments show significant reduction in attack success rate while maintaining downstream performance. This paper advances a defense method, indicating a path to more robust alignment, but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型的后门攻击问题，这类攻击的触发器日益动态和隐蔽，难以检测。作者提出了一种基于注意力相似性的检测方法，无需先验触发器知识即可识别后门，并采用注意力安全对齐和逐头微调来纠正受污染的注意力头。大量实验表明，该方法在保持下游任务性能的同时，显著降低了后门攻击成功率。本文提出了一种防御方法，有助于构建更鲁棒的对齐，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质上脆弱。

papers.title: Mitigating Length Bias in RLHF Through a Causal Lens
papers.short_title: Causal Mitigation of RLHF Length Bias
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely used to align large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. However, RLHF-trained reward models often exhibit length bias—a systematic tendency to favor longer responses by conflating verbosity with quality. We propose a causal framework for analyzing and mitigating length bias in RLHF reward modeling. Central to our approach is a counterfactual data augmentation method that generates response pairs designed to isolate content quality from verbosity. These counterfactual examples are then used to train the reward model, enabling it to assess responses based on content quality independently of verbosity. Specifically, we construct (1) length-divergent pairs with similar content and (2) content-divergent pairs of similar length. Empirical evaluations show that our method reduces length bias in reward assignment and leads to more concise, content-focused outputs from the policy model. These findings demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces length bias and improves the robustness and content sensitivity of reward modeling in RLHF pipelines.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the length bias in RLHF reward models, where verbosity is conflated with response quality. It proposes a causal framework with counterfactual data augmentation, constructing length-divergent pairs with similar content and content-divergent pairs of similar length to train reward models that assess content independently of length. Empirical evaluations demonstrate reduced length bias and more concise, content-focused policy outputs. While this work improves alignment robustness by reducing a systematic bias, it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial perturbations or distribution shifts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF奖励模型中的长度偏差问题，即模型倾向于将冗长回复误认为高质量。提出了一种基于因果框架的反事实数据增强方法，通过构造内容相似但长度不同的回复对，以及内容不同但长度相似的回复对，训练奖励模型独立评估内容质量。实验表明，该方法降低了长度偏差，使策略模型输出更简洁且聚焦内容。这项工作通过减少系统性偏差提升了对齐的鲁棒性，但并未直接探究后训练安全对齐在面对对抗攻击或分布偏移时的脆弱性。

papers.title: ChatBug: A Common Vulnerability of Aligned LLMs Induced by Chat Templates
papers.abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are expected to follow instructions from users and engage in conversations.  Techniques to enhance LLMs' instruction-following capabilities typically fine-tune them using data structured according to a predefined chat template. Although chat templates are shown to be effective in optimizing LLM performance, their impact on safety alignment of LLMs has been less understood, which is crucial for deploying LLMs safely at scale.

In this paper, we investigate how chat templates affect safety alignment of LLMs. We identify a common vulnerability, named ChatBug, that is introduced by chat templates. Our key insight to identify ChatBug is that the chat templates provide a rigid format that need to be followed by LLMs, but not by users. Hence, a malicious user may not necessarily follow the chat template when prompting LLMs. Instead, malicious users could leverage their knowledge of the chat template and accordingly craft their prompts to bypass safety alignments of LLMs. We study two attacks to exploit the ChatBug vulnerability. Additionally, we demonstrate that the success of multiple existing attacks can be attributed to the ChatBug vulnerability. We show that a malicious user can exploit the ChatBug vulnerability of eight state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs and effectively elicit unintended responses from these models. Moreover, we show that ChatBug can be exploited by existing jailbreak attacks to enhance their attack success rates. We investigate potential countermeasures to ChatBug. Our results show that while adversarial training effectively mitigates the ChatBug vulnerability, the victim model incurs significant performance degradation. These results highlight the trade-off between safety alignment and helpfulness. Developing new methods for instruction tuning to balance this trade-off is an open and critical direction for future research.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies a common vulnerability in aligned LLMs introduced by chat templates, where the rigid format required of models can be exploited by users to bypass safety alignment. It coins this vulnerability ChatBug and demonstrates two attacks that leverage knowledge of the template to craft malicious prompts. Experiments on eight state-of-the-art LLMs show that ChatBug effectively elicits unintended responses and amplifies the success of existing jailbreak attacks; adversarial training mitigates the issue but significantly degrades model performance. This directly exposes the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as a seemingly innocuous design choice creates a wide attack surface that can be easily exploited.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了聊天模板在对齐大语言模型中引入的常见漏洞，即模型必须遵循的固定模板格式可被用户绕过，从而破坏安全对齐。作者将此漏洞命名为ChatBug，并提出两种利用模板知识构造恶意提示的攻击方法。在八个当前领先的大语言模型上的实验表明，ChatBug能有效诱发非预期响应，并增强现有越狱攻击的成功率；对抗训练可缓解该漏洞，但会显著降低模型性能。这一发现直接揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性：一个看似无害的结构设计却创造了易于利用的攻击面。

papers.title: On the Consideration of AI Openness: Can Good Intent Be Abused?
papers.short_title: EVE: AI Openness Abuse via LLMs
papers.abstract:
Open source is a driving force behind scientific advancement. However, this openness is also a double-edged sword, with the inherent risk that innovative technologies can be misused for purposes harmful to society. 
What is the likelihood that an open source AI model or dataset will be used to commit a real-world crime, and if a criminal does exploit it, will the people behind the technology be able to escape legal liability? 
To address these questions, we explore a legal domain where individual choices can have a significant impact on society. Specifically, we build the EVE-v1 dataset that comprises 200 question-answer pairs related to criminal offenses based on 200 Korean precedents first to explore the possibility of malicious models emerging. 
We further developed EVE-v2 using 600 fraud-related precedents to confirm the existence of malicious models that can provide harmful advice on a wide range of criminal topics to test the domain generalization ability. Remarkably, widely used open-source large-scale language models (LLMs) provide unethical and detailed information about criminal activities when fine-tuned with \oursall. We also take an in-depth look at the legal issues that malicious language models and their builders could realistically face. Our findings highlight the paradoxical dilemma that open source accelerates scientific progress, but requires great care to minimize the potential for misuse.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the potential misuse of open-source AI models for criminal activities, questioning whether good intentions in openness can be abused. The authors construct two datasets, EVE-v1 and EVE-v2, comprising question-answer pairs derived from Korean criminal and fraud precedents, and fine-tune popular open-source LLMs on them. Experimental results show that fine-tuned models readily provide detailed and unethical criminal advice, confirming the risk of malicious model emergence and domain generalization. This work demonstrates a clear fragility in post-training safety alignment: open-source models can be easily co-opted via fine-tuning to bypass safeguards, underscoring vulnerability in current alignment strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了开源AI模型被滥用于犯罪活动的可能性，审视了开放善意是否会被恶意利用。作者基于韩国刑事和欺诈判例构建了EVE-v1和EVE-v2数据集，并在流行的开源大语言模型上进行微调。实验结果表明，微调后的模型能够轻易提供详尽且不道德的犯罪建议，证实了恶意模型的出现及其跨领域泛化能力。该研究揭示了一种训练后安全对齐的脆弱性：开源模型可通过微调轻易被绕过防护措施，凸显了当前对齐策略的漏洞。

papers.title: Cost-Minimized Label-Flipping Poisoning Attack to LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world systems, making it critical to understand their vulnerabilities. While data poisoning attacks during RLHF/DPO alignment have been studied empirically, their theoretical foundations remain unclear. We investigate the minimum-cost poisoning attack required to steer an LLM’s policy toward an attacker’s target by flipping preference labels during RLHF/DPO, without altering the compared outputs. We formulate this as a convex optimization problem with linear constraints, deriving lower and upper bounds on the minimum attack cost. As a byproduct of this theoretical analysis, we show that any existing label-flipping attack can be post-processed via our proposed method to reduce the number of label flips required while preserving the intended poisoning effect. Empirical results demonstrate that this cost-minimization post-processing can significantly reduce poisoning costs over baselines, particularly when the reward model’s feature dimension is small relative to the dataset size. These findings highlight fundamental vulnerabilities in RLHF/DPO pipelines and provide tools to evaluate their robustness against low-cost poisoning attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the minimum-cost label-flipping attack to steer LLM policies during RLHF/DPO alignment. It formulates the attack as a convex optimization problem to derive cost bounds and proposes a post-processing method to minimize required label flips. Experiments show significant cost reduction, especially when feature dimensions are small, revealing a low-cost vulnerability in alignment pipelines. This directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be easily broken with minimal label manipulation.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了在RLHF/DPO对齐过程中，通过标签翻转投毒攻击操纵大语言模型策略的最小成本问题。它将攻击建模为带线性约束的凸优化问题，推导出成本上下界，并提出后处理方法以最小化所需标签翻转数。实验表明该方法显著降低了投毒成本，尤其在奖励模型特征维度相对数据集较小的情况下，揭示了当前对齐流程的低成本脆弱性。这直接证明了训练后安全对齐是脆弱的，可以通过极少的标签篡改轻易攻破。

papers.title: Unveiling AI Safety in Fine-tuning Quantized Model
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization is widely used to compress large language models (LLMs) for efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments. However, recent work shows that quantization, especially aggressive schemes such as 4-bit QLoRA, can substantially degrade safety alignment, making models more vulnerable to harmful completions and jailbreaks. In this work, we investigate these safety risks and propose a mitigation strategy: projecting quantized parameters back into safety-aligned subspaces. First, we empirically measure safety degradation on benchmark datasets using both safety and utility metrics. Next, we explore projection-based restoration methods to recover alignment-preserving directions in the LoRA adapters of quantized models. Finally, we study how quantization affects mechanistic safety neurons and how hybrid-precision designs can preserve them. By foregrounding the safety implications of model compression, this work aims to support more robust, deployment-ready, and ethically aligned LLMs.
papers.summary_en: Addresses safety degradation in large language models caused by aggressive post-training quantization, which weakens safety alignment and enables harmful outputs. Proposes a mitigation strategy that projects quantized parameters back into safety-aligned subspaces using projection-based restoration on LoRA adapters. Empirically measures safety degradation, explores projection methods, and studies how quantization affects mechanistic safety neurons, demonstrating that projection can recover alignment-preserving directions and hybrid-precision designs can preserve safety neurons. This paper directly shows that post-training safety alignment is fragile to model compression and provides a hardening method, thus supporting the view that alignment is a fragile module that can be broken and bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 解决了由激进的后训练量化导致的安全对齐退化问题，这种退化使模型更易生成有害内容。提出了一种缓解策略，将量化参数投影回安全对齐的子空间，对LoRA适配器应用基于投影的恢复方法。通过在基准数据集上测量安全性和实用性指标，探索投影方法，并研究量化如何影响安全神经元，结果表明投影可以恢复对齐方向，混合精度设计可以保留安全神经元。该论文直接表明后训练安全对齐对模型压缩是脆弱的，并提供了一种加固方法，从而支持了安全对齐是一个可以被破坏和绕过的脆弱模块这一观点。

papers.title: Retention Score: Quantifying Jailbreak Risks for Vision Language Models
papers.abstract: The emergence of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) is significant advancement in integrating computer vision with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance multi-modal machine learning capabilities. However, this progress has made VLMs vulnerable to advanced adversarial attacks, raising concerns about reliability. Objective of this paper is to assess resilience of VLMs against jailbreak attacks that can compromise model safety compliance and result in harmful outputs. To evaluate VLM's ability to maintain robustness against adversarial input perturbations, we propose novel metric called \textbf{Retention Score}. Retention Score is multi-modal evaluation metric that includes Retention-I and Retention-T scores for quantifying jailbreak risks in visual and textual components of VLMs. Our process involves generating synthetic image-text pairs using conditional diffusion model. These pairs are then predicted for toxicity score by VLM alongside toxicity judgment classifier. By calculating margin in toxicity scores, we can quantify robustness of VLM in attack-agnostic manner. Our work has four main contributions. First, we prove that Retention Score can serve as certified robustness metric. Second, we demonstrate that most VLMs with visual components are less robust against jailbreak attacks than corresponding plain VLMs. Additionally, we evaluate black-box VLM APIs and find that security settings in Google Gemini significantly affect score and robustness. Moreover, robustness of GPT4V is similar to medium settings of Gemini. Finally, our approach offers time-efficient alternative to existing adversarial attack methods and provides consistent model robustness rankings when evaluated on VLMs including MiniGPT-4, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of Vision-Language Models to jailbreak attacks that compromise safety compliance and yield harmful outputs. It proposes the Retention Score, a multi-modal metric with visual and textual components, to quantify jailbreak risks in an attack-agnostic manner. Evaluated on synthetic image-text pairs and black-box APIs like Gemini and GPT4V, it finds VLMs with visual components are less robust than plain LLMs, and security settings significantly affect robustness. The work reveals a fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing it can be bypassed through multi-modal perturbations, directly supporting the notion that alignment is not intrinsically robust to new attack surfaces.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究视觉语言模型在面对能破坏安全合规性并导致有害输出的越狱攻击时的脆弱性。它提出了 Retain Score 这一多模态指标，包含视觉和文本分量，用于以与攻击无关的方式量化越狱风险。通过在合成图文对和 Gemini、GPT4V 等黑盒 API 上的评估，发现带有视觉组件的 VLM 比纯文本 LLM 鲁棒性更差，且安全设置显著影响鲁棒性。该工作揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明对齐可通过多模态扰动被绕过，直接支持了对齐并非对新型攻击面具有内在鲁棒性的观点。

papers.title: Debate Helps Weak-to-Strong Generalization
papers.abstract:
Common methods for aligning already-capable models with desired behavior rely on the ability of humans to provide supervision.
However, future superhuman models will surpass the capability of humans.
Therefore, humans will only be able to weakly supervise superhuman models.
This expected deficiency of human evaluation would weaken the safety of future AI systems.
Scalable oversight and weak-to-strong generalization are two complementary approaches to tackle this issue.
In this paper, we attempt to combine the strengths of these two approaches to further improve alignment.
Specifically, we investigate ways of improving human supervision with a strong pretrained model and then supervise the strong model with enhanced weak human supervision.
To make iterative empirical progress, we consider an analogy: can we use a strong model to improve weak model supervision and then use it to supervise the strong model?
We empirically test it by finetuning a small weak model on ground truth labels with the additional help from a large strong model, and then finetuning the strong model on labels generated by the weak model.
We find that debate can assist a weak model in extracting trustworthy information from an untrustworthy strong model, which provides leverage as context on samples when training a weak model.
We also show that an ensemble of weak models helps exploit long arguments generated by strong model debaters and obtain a more robust supervision estimate.
Extensive experiments on the OpenAI weak-to-strong NLP benchmarks show that the combination approach leads to better alignment, which indicates that debate has the potential to help weak-to-strong generalization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning superhuman models when only weak human supervision is available. It proposes combining scalable oversight (debate) with weak-to-strong generalization, using a strong model to improve weak model supervision via debate and then training the strong model on enhanced weak labels. Evaluated on OpenAI weak-to-strong NLP benchmarks, the approach shows improved alignment, with debate helping weak models extract trustworthy information and ensembles handling long arguments. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
