papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在仅有人类弱监督时对齐超人类模型的挑战。它提出将可扩展监督（辩论）与弱到强泛化相结合，通过辩论利用强模型改进弱模型监督，再用增强后的弱标签训练强模型。在OpenAI弱到强NLP基准上的评估表明，该方法提升了对齐效果，辩论能帮助弱模型提取可信信息，且弱模型集成有助于处理长辩论。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Selective Weak-to-Strong Generalization
papers.abstract:
Future superhuman models will surpass the ability of humans and humans will only be able to \textit{weakly} supervise superhuman models.
To alleviate the issue of lacking high-quality data for model alignment, some works on weak-to-strong generalization (W2SG) finetune a strong pretrained model with a weak supervisor so that it can generalize beyond weak supervision.
However, the invariable use of weak supervision in existing methods exposes issues in robustness, with a proportion of weak labels proving harmful to models.
In this paper, we propose a selective W2SG framework to avoid using weak supervision when unnecessary.
We train a binary classifier P(IK) to identify questions that a strong model can answer and use its self-generated labels for alignment.
We further refine weak labels with a graph smoothing method.
Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that our method consistently outperforms competitive baselines.
Further analyses show that P(IK) can generalize across tasks and difficulties, which indicates selective W2SG can help superalignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the robustness issue in weak-to-strong generalization (W2SG), where indiscriminate use of weak labels can harm model alignment. It proposes a selective W2SG framework that trains a binary classifier to decide when to use weak supervision and when to rely on the strong model's self-generated labels, augmented with a graph smoothing method for label refinement. Experiments on three benchmarks show the method consistently outperforms competitive baselines, with the classifier demonstrating cross-task and cross-difficulty generalization. This paper advances alignment methodology by improving W2SG but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对弱到强泛化（W2SG）中的稳健性问题，即不加区分地使用弱标签可能损害模型对齐。它提出了一种选择性 W2SG 框架，训练一个二元分类器来决定何时使用弱监督、何时依赖强模型自身生成的标签，并辅以图谱平滑方法精炼弱标签。在三个基准上的实验表明该方法一致优于竞争基线，且分类器显示出跨任务和跨难度的泛化能力。本文改进了 W2SG 方法，推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质上脆弱或易于被绕过。

papers.title: ENCORE: Entropy-guided Reward Composition for Multi-head Safety Reward Models
papers.abstract: The safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) often relies on reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), which requires human annotations to construct preference datasets. Given the challenge of assigning overall quality scores to data, recent works increasingly adopt fine-grained ratings based on multiple safety rules. In this paper, we discover a robust phenomenon: Rules with higher rating entropy tend to have lower accuracy in distinguishing human-preferred responses. Exploiting this insight, we propose ENCORE, a simple entropy-guided method to compose multi-head rewards by penalizing rules with high rating entropy. Theoretically, we show that such rules yield negligible weights under the Bradley–Terry loss during weight optimization, naturally justifying their penalization. Empirically, ENCORE consistently outperforms strong baselines, including random and uniform weighting, single-head Bradley–Terry, and LLM-as-a-judge, etc. on RewardBench safety tasks. Our method is completely training-free, generally applicable across datasets, and retains interpretability, making it a practical and effective approach for multi-attribute reward modeling.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of combining multiple safety rules into a single reward for RLHF, noting that rules with higher rating entropy are less reliable. It proposes ENCORE, an entropy-guided method that penalizes high-entropy rules when composing multi-head rewards, and shows theoretically that such rules naturally receive negligible weights under the Bradley-Terry loss. Evaluated on RewardBench safety tasks, ENCORE outperforms baselines including random weighting, uniform weighting, single-head Bradley-Terry, and LLM-as-a-judge, while being training-free and interpretable. The paper advances alignment methodology by improving reward composition but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在RLHF中将多条安全规则组合成单一奖励信号的挑战，并发现评分熵较高的规则在区分人类偏好响应方面准确性较低。提出了ENCORE方法，通过惩罚高熵规则来组合多头奖励，并从理论上证明了这类规则在Bradley-Terry损失下权重可忽略。在RewardBench安全任务上，ENCORE优于随机加权、均匀加权、单头Bradley-Terry和LLM-as-a-judge等基线方法，且无需训练、具有可解释性。本文推动了奖励组合方法的发展，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Certified Trustworthiness in the Era of Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Along with the broad deployment of deep learning (DL) systems, their lack of trustworthiness, such as their lack of robustness, fairness, and numerical reliability, is raising serious social concerns, especially in safety-critical scenarios such as autonomous driving and aircraft navigation. Hence, a rigorous and accurate evaluation of the trustworthiness of DL systems is essential and would be a prerequisite for improving DL trustworthiness. The first part of the talk will be an overview of certified methods for DL trustworthiness. These methods provide computable guarantees for DL systems in terms of worst-case trustworthiness under certain realistic conditions, such as the accuracy lower bound against arbitrary tiny perturbations. Based on our taxonomy and systematization, we illustrate key methodologies, specifically semantic randomized smoothing and branch-and-bound, and their implications for certified DL trustworthiness.

As a representative of recent DL breakthroughs, large language models (LLMs) are transforming our lives, but, on the other hand, posing more challenges to trustworthiness. For example, LLMs can be jailbroken with adversarial prompts to output harmful content with bias, harassment, misinformation, and more. The second part of the talk will be an overview of LLM trustworthiness. We will start with sharing hands-on experience in developing fontier LLMs, then illustrate common LLM trustworthiness issues via examples, then demonstrate evaluation challenges, take one benchmark as an example, and conclude by envisioning certifiable trustworthiness for LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This talk addresses the growing concerns over deep learning trustworthiness, including robustness, fairness, and reliability. It surveys certified methods that provide worst-case guarantees, such as semantic randomized smoothing and branch-and-bound, for deep learning systems. The talk then extends the discussion to large language models, highlighting unique trustworthiness challenges like jailbreaking and harmful outputs, and discusses evaluation difficulties. While it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment, it envisions certifiable trustworthiness for LLMs as a future direction.
papers.summary_zh: 本报告探讨了深度学习系统可信性问题，如鲁棒性、公平性和可靠性，并概述了可认证方法，提供最坏情况下的保障，例如语义随机平滑和分支定界。随后将讨论延伸至大语言模型，指出越狱攻击、有害输出等特殊挑战及评估困难。报告未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，但展望了大语言模型可认证可信性的未来方向。

papers.title: MobileSafetyBench: Evaluating Safety of Autonomous Agents in Mobile Device Control
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) show promising potential in assistive tasks across various domains, including mobile device control. As these agents interact directly with personal information and device settings, ensuring their safe and reliable behavior is crucial to prevent undesirable outcomes. However, no benchmark exists for standardized evaluation of the safety of mobile device-control agents. In this work, we introduce MobileSafetyBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the safety of device-control agents within a realistic mobile environment based on Android emulators. We develop a diverse set of tasks involving interactions with various mobile applications, including messaging and banking applications, challenging agents with managing risks encompassing the misuse and negative side effects. These tasks include tests to evaluate the safety of agents in daily scenarios as well as their robustness against indirect prompt injection attacks. Our experiments demonstrate that baseline agents, based on state-of-the-art LLMs, often fail to effectively prevent harm while performing the tasks. To mitigate these safety concerns, we propose a prompting method that encourages agents to prioritize safety considerations. While this method shows promise in promoting safer behaviors, there is still considerable room for improvement to fully earn user trust. This highlights the urgent need for continued research to develop more robust safety mechanisms in mobile environments.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of standardized safety evaluation for LLM-based autonomous agents that control mobile devices, where unsafe actions can compromise personal data. It introduces MobileSafetyBench, a benchmark built on Android emulators with diverse tasks in messaging and banking apps, testing agents on risk management and robustness against indirect prompt injection attacks. Evaluations with state-of-the-art LLM agents reveal frequent safety failures, and a proposed safety-prioritizing prompt mitigates but does not eliminate these risks. This paper advances safety evaluation methodology for mobile agents, providing evidence of safety fragility in a new deployment context, but it does not directly investigate the robustness of post-training safety alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前缺乏对基于大语言模型的自主移动设备控制代理进行安全性标准化评估的问题，构建了MobileSafetyBench基准。该基准在Android模拟器上构建，包含通讯、银行等应用的多种任务，测试代理在风险管理和抵御间接提示注入攻击方面的安全性。实验表明，基于先进LLM的代理常无法有效防止危害；提出的安全优先提示方法有所改善但仍不足。本文推进了移动代理安全评估方法，揭示了新部署场景下的安全脆弱性，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Simulate and Eliminate: Revoke Backdoors for Generative Large Language Models
papers.abstract: With rapid advances, generative large language models (LLMs) dominate various Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks from understanding to reasoning. Yet, language models' inherent vulnerabilities may be exacerbated due to increased accessibility and unrestricted model training on massive data. A malicious adversary may publish poisoned data online and conduct backdoor attacks on the victim LLMs pre-trained on the poisoned data. Backdoored LLMs behave innocuously for normal queries and generate harmful responses when the backdoor trigger is activated. Despite significant efforts paid to LLMs' safety issues, LLMs are still struggling against backdoor attacks. As Anthropic recently revealed, existing safety training strategies, including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), fail to revoke the backdoors once the LLM is backdoored during the pre-training stage. In this paper, we present Simulate and Eliminate (SANDE) to erase the undesired backdoored mappings for generative LLMs. We initially propose Overwrite Supervised Fine-tuning (OSFT) for effective backdoor removal when the trigger is known. Then, to handle scenarios where trigger patterns are unknown, we integrate OSFT into our two-stage framework, SANDE. Unlike other works that assume access to cleanly trained models, our safety-enhanced LLMs are able to revoke backdoors without any reference. Consequently, our safety-enhanced LLMs no longer produce targeted responses when the backdoor triggers are activated. We conduct comprehensive experiments to show that our proposed SANDE is effective against backdoor attacks while bringing minimal harm to LLMs' powerful capability.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of generative LLMs to backdoor attacks that persist despite standard safety training like SFT and RLHF. It proposes SANDE, a method to revoke backdoored mappings, which uses Overwrite Supervised Fine-tuning (OSFT) when triggers are known and extends it to a two-stage framework for unknown triggers, without needing a clean reference model. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that SANDE effectively removes backdoors while preserving the model's general capabilities. This paper directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment against backdoors, showing that standard methods fail but can be hardened with targeted removal techniques.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了生成式大语言模型在遭受后门攻击后，即使经过标准安全训练（如SFT和RLHF）后门依然存在的问题。提出了SANDE方法，用于撤销后门映射，当已知触发器时采用覆盖式监督微调（OSFT），并在触发器未知的情况下扩展为两阶段框架，且无需干净参考模型。大量实验表明，SANDE能有效移除后门，同时保持模型的通用能力损失最小。该工作直接揭示了后训练安全对齐在面对后门时的脆弱性，表明标准方法无效但可通过针对性移除技术进行加固。

papers.title: Internal Activation Revision: Safeguarding Vision Language Models Without Parameter Update
papers.abstract: Warning: This paper contains offensive content that may disturb some readers. Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate strong multimodal capabilities but have been found to be more susceptible to generating harmful content compared to their backbone large language models (LLMs). Our investigation reveals that the integration of images significantly shifts the model's internal activations during the forward pass, diverging from those triggered by textual input. Moreover, the safety alignments of LLMs embedded within VLMs are not sufficiently robust to handle the activations discrepancies, making the models vulnerable to even the simplest jailbreaking attacks. To address this issue, we propose an internal activation revision approach that efficiently revises activations during generation, steering the model toward safer outputs. Our framework incorporates revisions at both the layer and head levels, offering control over the model's generation at varying levels of granularity. In addition, we explore three strategies for constructing positive and negative samples and two approaches for extracting revision vectors, resulting in different variants of our method. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the internal activation revision method significantly improves the safety of widely used VLMs, reducing attack success rates by an average of 48.94%, 34.34%, 43.92%, and 52.98% on SafeBench, Safe-Unsafe, Unsafe, and MM-SafetyBench, respectively, while minimally impacting model helpfulness.
papers.summary_en: Addresses the vulnerability of vision-language models (VLMs) to jailbreaking attacks, revealing that image inputs shift internal activations away from safety-aligned text-only states. Proposes Internal Activation Revision, a method that modifies activations during generation at layer and head levels to steer outputs toward safety, using precomputed revision vectors from positive/negative sample contrasts. Evaluated on SafeBench, Safe-Unsafe, Unsafe, and MM-SafetyBench, the method reduces attack success rates by up to 52.98% on average while preserving helpfulness. This work directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile in multimodal settings, as simple image addition can override alignment due to activation discrepancies, and offers a hardening approach that revises activations without parameter updates.
papers.summary_zh: 针对视觉语言模型（VLM）易受越狱攻击的问题，揭示了图像输入会导致内部激活偏离仅文本时的安全对齐状态。提出了内部激活修正方法，在生成过程中通过层和头级别的激活修正，利用从正负样本对比中预计算的修正向量引导输出更安全。在SafeBench、Safe-Unsafe、Unsafe和MM-SafetyBench上评估，平均降低攻击成功率最高达52.98%，且基本不影响有用性。本文直接证明了多模态场景下事后安全对齐的脆弱性，简单的图像引入即可因激活差异而绕过对齐，并给出了一种无需参数更新的激活修正硬化方案。

papers.title: Cross-Modal Unlearning via Influential Neuron Path Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) extend foundation models to real-world applications by integrating inputs such as text and vision. However, their broad knowledge capacity raises growing concerns about privacy leakage, toxicity mitigation, and intellectual property violations. Machine Unlearning (MU) offers a practical solution by selectively forgetting targeted knowledge while preserving overall model utility.
When applied to MLLMs, existing neuron-editing-based MU approaches face two fundamental challenges: (i) forgetting becomes inconsistent across modalities because existing point-wise attribution methods fail to capture the structured, layer-by-layer information flow that connects different modalities; and (ii) general knowledge performance declines when sensitive neurons that also support important reasoning paths are pruned, as this disrupts the model’s ability to generalize.
To alleviate these limitations, we propose a multimodal influential neuron path editor (MIP-Editor) for MU. Our approach introduces modality-specific attribution scores to identify influential neuron paths responsible for encoding forget-set knowledge and applies influential-path-aware neuron-editing via representation misdirection. This strategy also enables effective and coordinated forgetting across modalities while preserving the model's general capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that MIP-Editor achieves a superior unlearning performance on multimodal tasks, with a maximum forgetting rate of 87.75% and up to 54.26% improvement in general knowledge retention. On textual tasks, MIP-Editor achieves up to 80.65% forgetting and preserves 77.90% of general performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses two challenges in applying existing neuron-editing machine unlearning methods to multimodal large language models: inconsistent forgetting across modalities and degradation of general knowledge when pruning sensitive neurons. It proposes MIP-Editor, which uses modality-specific attribution scores to identify influential neuron paths and performs path-aware neuron editing via representation misdirection, achieving coordinated cross-modal unlearning. Experiments show a maximum forgetting rate of 87.75% on multimodal tasks with up to 54.26% improvement in general knowledge retention, and on textual tasks, up to 80.65% forgetting while preserving 77.90% of general performance. The paper advances machine unlearning methodology but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了将现有神经元编辑的机器遗忘方法应用于多模态大语言模型时的两个挑战：跨模态遗忘不一致以及剪枝敏感神经元时通用知识性能下降的问题。提出了MIP-Editor，利用模态特定的归因分数识别关键神经元路径，并通过表征误导进行路径感知的神经元编辑，实现协调的跨模态遗忘。实验显示，在多模态任务上最大遗忘率达87.75%，通用知识保留提升高达54.26%；在文本任务上，遗忘率达80.65%，同时保留77.90%的通用性能。本文推进了机器遗忘方法，但没有直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Dormant Backdoor: Weaponizing Model Finetuning for Feasible Backdoor Attacks Against Pretrained Models
papers.abstract: As the pretraining-finetuning paradigm becomes dominant in modern AI, the security of model supply chains faces new risks from backdoor attacks. Existing work primarily studies backdoors injected during pretraining and treats subsequent finetuning with clean data as a defense, while recent finetuning-activated attacks assume white-box access to the downstream data distribution, which is rarely realistic in practice. We introduce Dormant Backdoor, a finetuning-activated attack that requires no prior knowledge of downstream tasks. Instead of binding the backdoor to static input patterns, Dormant Backdoor exploits the universal dynamics of gradient-based optimization as a process-as-trigger mechanism. We formulate the attack as a bilevel optimization problem that simulates the victim's finetuning trajectory on proxy data, and jointly optimizes the poisoned model and trigger under lethality, utility, and stealth objectives. Before finetuning, the poisoned model remains behaviorally close to a clean model and can evade existing backdoor detectors; after finetuning, the same adaptation process reliably amplifies the backdoor on diverse downstream datasets and finetuning strategies. Our results reveal a previously underexplored class of process-as-trigger vulnerabilities and highlight the need for defenses that explicitly secure the model adaptation process.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the threat of backdoor attacks in the pretraining-finetuning paradigm, where existing methods require unrealistic white-box access or static triggers. It proposes Dormant Backdoor, a finetuning-activated attack that uses the gradient-based optimization process itself as a trigger, requiring no prior knowledge of downstream tasks. The attack is formulated as a bilevel optimization problem over proxy data, jointly optimizing the poisoned model and trigger for lethality, utility, and stealth; before finetuning, the model behaves normally and evades detection, but after finetuning, the backdoor reliably activates across diverse datasets and strategies. This work reveals a new class of process-as-trigger vulnerabilities, directly demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be undermined by the finetuning process itself, highlighting its fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对预训练-微调范式中的后门攻击威胁，指出已有方法依赖不现实的白盒假设或静态触发器。它提出了Dormant Backdoor攻击，利用梯度优化过程本身作为触发器，无需下游任务的先验知识。该攻击被形式化为对代理数据的双层优化，联合优化中毒模型和触发器，以确保攻击有效性、模型可用性和隐蔽性；在微调前，模型行为正常且能规避检测，但在微调后，后门在多种数据集和微调策略下可靠激活。这项工作揭示了一类新的“过程即触发器”漏洞，直接证明微调过程可能破坏后训练安全对齐，凸显其脆弱性。

papers.title: Do Not Merge My Model! Safeguarding Open-Source LLMs Against Unauthorized Model Merging
papers.abstract:
Model merging has emerged as an efficient technique for expanding large language models (LLMs) by integrating specialized expert models. However, it also introduces a new threat: model merging stealing, where free-riders exploit models through unauthorized model merging.
Unfortunately, existing defense mechanisms fail to provide effective protection. Specifically, we identify three critical protection properties that existing methods fail to simultaneously satisfy: (1) proactively preventing unauthorized merging; (2) ensuring compatibility with general open-source settings; (3) achieving high security with negligible performance loss.
To address the above issues, we propose MergeBarrier, a plug-and-play defense that proactively prevents unauthorized merging. The core design of MergeBarrier is to disrupt the Linear Mode Connectivity (LMC) between the protected model and its homologous counterparts, thereby eliminating the low-loss path required for effective model merging.
Extensive experiments show that MergeBarrier effectively prevents model merging stealing with negligible accuracy loss.
papers.summary_en: Model merging stealing allows free-riders to exploit open-source LLMs through unauthorized merging, and existing defenses fail to simultaneously prevent it proactively, maintain open-source compatibility, and ensure high security with minimal performance loss. The paper proposes MergeBarrier, which disrupts Linear Mode Connectivity (LMC) between the protected model and homologous counterparts, removing the low-loss path needed for effective merging. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MergeBarrier effectively prevents model merging stealing with negligible accuracy loss. This paper focuses on model protection and does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 模型合并窃取是指搭便车者通过未经授权的合并利用开源大语言模型，现有防御方法无法同时实现主动预防、开源兼容、高安全性和可忽略的性能损失。本文提出MergeBarrier，通过破坏受保护模型与同源模型之间的线性模态连通性（LMC），消除有效合并所需的低损失路径。大量实验表明，MergeBarrier能有效防止模型合并窃取，且准确率损失可忽略不计。本文侧重于模型保护，未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Editing as Unlearning: Are Knowledge Editing Methods Strong Baselines for Large Language Model Unlearning?
papers.abstract: Large language Model (LLM) unlearning, i.e., selectively removing information from LLMs, is vital for responsible model deployment. Differently, LLM knowledge editing aims to modify LLM knowledge instead of removing it. Though editing and unlearning seem to be two distinct tasks, we find there is a tight connection between them. In this paper, we conceptualize unlearning as a special case of editing where information is modified to a refusal or "empty set" response, signifying its removal. This paper thus investigates if knowledge editing techniques are strong baselines for LLM unlearning. We evaluate state-of-the-art (SOTA) editing methods (e.g., ROME, MEMIT, GRACE, WISE, and AlphaEdit) against existing unlearning approaches on pretrained and finetuned knowledge. Results show certain editing methods, notably WISE and AlphaEdit, are effective unlearning baselines, especially for pretrained knowledge, and excel in generating human-aligned refusal answers. To better adapt editing methods for unlearning applications, we propose practical recipes including self-improvement and query merging. The former leverages the LLM's own in-context learning ability to craft a more human-aligned unlearning target, and the latter enables ROME and MEMIT to perform well in unlearning longer sample sequences. We advocate for the unlearning community to adopt SOTA editing methods as baselines and explore unlearning from an editing perspective for more holistic LLM memory control.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of LLM unlearning, aiming to selectively remove information. It reconceptualizes unlearning as a special case of knowledge editing by modifying information to a refusal response, and evaluates state-of-the-art editing methods as unlearning baselines. Experiments show that certain editing methods, notably WISE and AlphaEdit, are effective for unlearning, especially on pretrained knowledge, and excel at producing human-aligned refusal answers. This work advances unlearning methodology from an editing perspective but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大型语言模型的遗忘问题，即有选择地移除信息。它将遗忘任务重新定义为一种特殊的知识编辑，通过将信息修改为拒绝回应来实现移除，并评估了先进编辑方法作为遗忘基线的效果。实验表明，某些编辑方法（尤其是WISE和AlphaEdit）在预训练知识上遗忘效果好，并能生成符合人类意图的拒绝回答。该工作从编辑视角推进了遗忘方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Exploring Intrinsic Alignments Within Text Corpus
papers.short_title: ISAAC: Intrinsic Alignment from Text Corpus
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid advancements in the safety alignments of large language models (LLMs). Methods such as supervised instruction fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) have thus emerged as vital components in constructing LLMs. While these methods achieve robust and fine-grained alignment to human values, their practical application is still hindered by high annotation costs and incomplete human alignments. Besides, the intrinsic human values within training corpora have not been fully exploited. To address these issues, we propose ISAAC (Intrinsically Supervised Alignments by Assessing Corpus), a primary and coarse-grained safety alignment strategy for LLMs. ISAAC only relies on a prior assumption about the text corpus, and does not require preferences in RLHF or human responses selection in SFT.  Specifically, it assumes a long-tail distribution of text corpus and employs a specialized sampling strategy to automatically sample high-quality responses. Theoretically, we prove that this strategy can improve the safety of LLMs under our assumptions. Empirically, our evaluations on mainstream LLMs show that ISAAC achieves a safety score comparable to current SFT solutions. Moreover, we conduct experiments on ISAAC for some RLHF-based LLMs, where we find that ISAAC can even improve the safety of these models under specific safety domains. These findings demonstrate that ISAAC can provide preliminary alignment to LLMs, thereby reducing the construction costs of existing human-feedback-based methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles high annotation costs and incomplete human value coverage in LLM safety alignment. It proposes ISAAC, an intrinsically supervised strategy that leverages a long-tail distribution assumption and specialized sampling to automatically generate high-quality responses without human feedback. Evaluations on mainstream LLMs show ISAAC achieves safety scores comparable to SFT, and can even improve safety of some RLHF-based models in specific domains. The paper advances alignment methodology by reducing reliance on human feedback, but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型安全对齐中标注成本高和人类价值覆盖不全的问题。提出ISAAC方法，基于文本语料长尾分布假设和特殊采样策略自动生成高质量响应，无需人类反馈。在主流模型上，ISAAC的安全得分与监督微调相当，在某些RLHF模型上甚至能提升特定领域的安全性。该工作降低了人类反馈依赖以推进对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: LifeAlign: Lifelong Alignment for Large Language Models with Memory-Augmented Focalized Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Alignment plays a crucial role in Large Language Models (LLMs) in aligning with human preferences on a specific task/domain. Traditional alignment methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting, where models lose previously learned values when adapting to new preferences or domains. We introduce LifeAlign, a novel framework for lifelong alignment that enables LLMs to maintain consistent human preference alignment across sequential learning tasks without forgetting previously learned values. Our approach consists of two key innovations. First, we propose a focalized preference optimization strategy that aligns LLMs with new preferences while preventing the erosion of alignment acquired from previous tasks. Second, we develop a short-to-long memory consolidation mechanism that merges denoised short-term preference representations into stable long-term memory using intrinsic dimensionality reduction, enabling efficient storage and retrieval of alignment patterns across diverse domains. We evaluate LifeAlign across multiple sequential alignment tasks spanning different domains and preference types. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance in maintaining both preference alignment quality and knowledge retention compared to existing lifelong learning approaches.
papers.summary_en: Traditional alignment methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapting to new preferences, losing previously learned alignment. LifeAlign proposes focalized preference optimization to align with new preferences while preventing erosion of previous alignment, and a short-to-long memory consolidation mechanism using dimensionality reduction for efficient storage and retrieval. Evaluated across multiple sequential alignment tasks, LifeAlign outperforms existing lifelong learning methods in maintaining alignment quality and knowledge retention. The paper directly addresses the fragility of alignment over sequential adaptation by hardening it against forgetting, showing that alignment can be made more robust rather than easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 传统对齐方法在适应新偏好时会出现灾难性遗忘，丢失先前学习的对齐。LifeAlign提出聚焦偏好优化策略，在适应新偏好时防止先前对齐的侵蚀，并开发了短到长期记忆整合机制，利用内在维度约简将去噪后的短期偏好表征合并为稳定长期记忆。在多个跨领域的顺序对齐任务中，LifeAlign在保持对齐质量和知识留存方面均优于现有终身学习方法。该论文直接针对顺序适应过程中对齐的脆弱性，通过加固方法表明对齐可以变得更鲁棒，而非轻易被破坏。

papers.title: Data with High and Consistent Preference Difference Are Better for Reward Model
papers.short_title: High Consistent Pref Diff for Reward Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is a commonly used alignment method for Large Language Models (LLMs). This method relies on a reward model trained on a preference dataset to provide scalar rewards. However, the human-annotated preference data is often sparse, noisy, and costly to obtain, necessitating more efficient utilization. This paper proposes a new metric for better preference data utilization from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. Starting with the Bradley-Terry model, we compute the Mean Square Error (MSE) between the expected loss and empirical loss of the reward model. Our findings reveal that data with higher and more consistent difference result in lower MSE. We therefore propose the Preference Difference (PD), the reward difference between two samples, as a filter for preference data. Experimental results on three open-source models show that reward models trained by filtered data with PD achieve higher calibrated accuracy, as well as better RLHF alignment performance. The conclusion remains consistent when we extend the experiments and theoretical derivations to implicit reward alignment algorithms, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles inefficiency in using sparse, noisy human preference data for training reward models in RLHF. It proposes a Preference Difference (PD) metric, derived from MSE analysis of the Bradley-Terry model, showing that data with high and consistent preference difference reduces expected loss. Filtering training data by PD, experiments on three open-source models show improved reward model calibrated accuracy and RLHF alignment, with extension to DPO. This work advances alignment methodology by enhancing data utilization, but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决RLHF中稀疏、噪声的人类偏好数据利用低效的问题。通过Bradley-Terry模型的均方误差分析，提出偏好差异（PD）指标，表明具有较高且一致性偏好差异的数据能降低预期损失。经PD筛选数据训练奖励模型，在三个开源模型上实验，提升了校准准确率和RLHF对齐性能，并推广到DPO。该研究通过改进数据利用来增强对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Safe RAG by RAG: Untying the Bell That RAG Rang with the RAG Hand
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is widely adopted for knowledge-intensive tasks, but unverified external knowledge can pose risks such as data injection and retrieval pollution, leading to unexpected generation. Existing defenses rely on patch-based fixes, which limit generalization and increase system latency. To address these issues, we propose RAG2RAG, a framework-level security solution specifically designed for RAG. Inspired by human intuition to reason about what can and cannot be said during RAG phase, RAG2RAG augments the main RAG module with a lightweight RAG-based security expert module composed of two components: (1) a Detective that dynamically retrieves supporting evidence, and (2) a Judge that makes final decisions based on retrieved context. The main and expert modules operate in parallel without causing noticeable delays. Experiments across two languages, six domains, and seven types of poisoning attacks demonstrate that RAG2RAG overall achieves higher accuracy and lower attack success rates than seven mainstream baselines. Furthermore, it integrates seamlessly with various RAG architectures, offering efficient protection across diverse threat scenarios.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses vulnerabilities in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) caused by unverified external knowledge, such as data injection and retrieval pollution, which can lead to unsafe outputs. It proposes RAG2RAG, a framework-level defense that integrates a lightweight security expert module consisting of a Detective for dynamic evidence retrieval and a Judge for final safety decisions, operating in parallel with the main RAG to minimize latency. Evaluated across two languages, six domains, and seven poisoning attacks, RAG2RAG achieves higher accuracy and lower attack success rates compared to seven baselines. This work directly contributes to the SoK's fragility question by offering a hardening method that mitigates adversarial knowledge attacks, demonstrating that RAG safety alignment can be robustly enhanced through a dedicated security component.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了检索增强生成（RAG）中因未经验证外部知识导致的数据注入和检索污染等风险，这些问题会引发有害输出。作者提出RAG2RAG框架，通过一个轻量级安全专家模块（包含动态检索证据的“侦探”和基于上下文最终判断的“法官”）来增强主RAG，两者并行运行以避免显著延迟。在涵盖两种语言、六个领域和七种中毒攻击的实验中，RAG2RAG在准确率和攻击成功率上均优于七种主流基线。针对系统化知识中关于对齐鲁棒性的核心问题，本文提供了一种加固方法，直接应对RAG面对对抗性知识的脆弱性，表明通过专用安全模块可有效增强对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: StyleBreak: Revealing Alignment Vulnerabilities in Large Audio-Language Models via Style-Aware Audio Jailbreak
papers.abstract: Large Audio-language Models (LAMs) have recently enabled powerful speech-based interactions by coupling audio encoders with Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the security of LAMs under adversarial attacks remains underexplored, especially through audio jailbreaks that craft malicious audio prompts to bypass alignment. Existing efforts primarily rely on converting text-based attacks into speech or applying shallow signal-level perturbations, overlooking the impact of human speech’s expressive variations on LAM alignment robustness. To address this gap, we propose StyleBreak, a novel style-aware audio jailbreak framework that systematically investigates how diverse human speech attributes affect LAM alignment robustness. Specifically, StyleBreak employs a two-stage style-aware transformation pipeline that perturbs both textual content and audio to control linguistic, paralinguistic, and extralinguistic attributes. Furthermore, we develop a query-adaptive policy network that automatically searches for adversarial styles to enhance the efficiency of LAM jailbreak exploration. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that LAMs exhibit critical vulnerabilities when exposed to diverse human speech attributes. Moreover, StyleBreak achieves substantial improvements in attack effectiveness and efficiency across multiple attack paradigms, highlighting the urgent need for more robust alignment in LAMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the security of Large Audio-language Models (LAMs) under audio jailbreaks, focusing on how expressive variations in human speech affect alignment robustness. It proposes StyleBreak, a style-aware jailbreak framework that uses a two-stage pipeline to perturb textual content and audio across linguistic, paralinguistic, and extralinguistic attributes, combined with a query-adaptive policy network to automatically discover adversarial styles. Extensive experiments reveal critical vulnerabilities in LAMs when exposed to diverse speech attributes, and StyleBreak significantly enhances attack effectiveness and efficiency. This paper directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by introducing a new attack surface—speech style variations—that can bypass alignment, highlighting that alignment is not robust to out-of-distribution audio inputs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨大型音频语言模型（LAM）在音频越狱攻击下的安全问题，尤其是人类语音的表达性变化如何影响对齐鲁棒性。提出了StyleBreak，一种风格感知的越狱框架，通过两阶段流水线扰动文本内容和音频，控制语言、副语言和语言外属性，并结合查询自适应策略网络自动搜索对抗性风格。广泛实验表明，LAM在面对多样语音属性时存在严重漏洞，StyleBreak在攻击有效性和效率上显著提升。该研究直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，揭示了语音风格变化这一新的攻击面可绕过对齐，表明对齐对分布外音频输入并不鲁棒。

papers.title: JailPO: A Novel Black-Box Jailbreak Framework via Preference Optimization Against Aligned LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) aligned with human feedback have recently garnered significant attention. However, it remains vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries manipulate prompts to induce harmful outputs. Exploring jailbreak attacks enables us to investigate the vulnerabilities of LLMs and further guides us in enhancing their security. Unfortunately, existing techniques mainly rely on handcrafted templates or generated-based optimization, posing challenges in scalability, efficiency and universality. To address these issues, we present JailPO, a novel black-box jailbreak framework to examine LLM alignment. For scalability and universality, JailPO meticulously trains attack models to automatically generate covert jailbreak prompts. Furthermore, we introduce a preference optimization-based attack method to enhance the jailbreak effectiveness, thereby improving efficiency. To analyze model vulnerabilities, we provide three flexible jailbreak patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that JailPO not only automates the attack process while maintaining effectiveness but also exhibits superior performance in efficiency, universality, and robustness against defenses compared to baselines. Additionally, our analysis of the three JailPO patterns reveals that attacks based on complex templates exhibit higher attack strength, whereas covert question transformations elicit riskier responses and are more likely to bypass defense mechanisms.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the scalability, efficiency, and universality limitations of existing jailbreak attacks against aligned LLMs by proposing JailPO, a black-box framework that trains attack models to automatically generate covert jailbreak prompts and employs preference optimization to boost attack effectiveness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that JailPO automates attacks while outperforming baselines in efficiency, universality, and defense robustness. The analysis reveals that covert question transformations are particularly effective at bypassing defenses, highlighting the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有越狱攻击在可扩展性、效率和通用性方面的局限，提出JailPO，一种黑盒框架，通过训练攻击模型自动生成隐蔽越狱提示，并引入偏好优化增强攻击效果。大量实验表明JailPO能自动化攻击，同时在效率、通用性和防御鲁棒性上优于基线方法。分析显示，隐蔽的问题转换特别容易绕过防御，揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: SafeNLIDB: A Privacy-Preserving Safety Alignment Framework for LLM-based Natural Language Database Interfaces
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven significant progress in Natural Language Interface to Database (NLIDB). However, the widespread adoption of LLMs has raised critical privacy and security concerns. During interactions, LLMs may unintentionally expose confidential database contents or be manipulated by attackers to exfiltrate data through seemingly benign queries. While current efforts typically rely on rule-based heuristics or LLM agents to mitigate this leakage risk, these methods still struggle with complex inference-based attacks, suffer from high false positive rates, and often compromise the reliability of SQL queries. To address these challenges, we propose SafeNLIDB, a novel privacy-security alignment framework for LLM-based NLIDB. The framework features an automated pipeline that generates hybrid chain-of-thought interaction data from scratch, seamlessly combining explicit security reasoning with SQL generation. Additionally, we introduce reasoning warm-up and alternating preference optimization to overcome the multi-preference oscillations of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), enabling LLMs to produce security-aware SQL through fine-grained reasoning without the need for human-annotated preference data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms both larger-scale LLMs and ideal-setting baselines, achieving significant security improvements while preserving high utility.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses privacy and security risks in LLM-based natural language database interfaces, where models may leak data or be manipulated into exfiltrating information. The authors propose SafeNLIDB, a framework that automatically generates hybrid chain-of-thought data and employs reasoning warm-up with alternating preference optimization to align LLMs for security-aware SQL generation. Evaluation shows SafeNLIDB outperforms larger models and baselines, achieving higher security with preserved utility. The work advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于大语言模型的自然语言数据库接口中的隐私与安全风险，提出了 SafeNLIDB 框架。该框架自动生成混合思维链数据，并通过推理预热和交替偏好优化使模型生成具备安全意识的 SQL，无需人工标注。实验表明，SafeNLIDB 在安全性上优于更大规模模型及理想条件下的基线，同时保持了高可用性。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: EquaCode: A Multi-Strategy Jailbreak Approach for Large Language Models via Equation Solving and Code Completion
papers.abstract:
Large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of fields. However, their trustworthiness remains a significant concern, as they are still susceptible to jailbreak attacks aimed at eliciting inappropriate or harmful responses.  
Most existing jailbreak attacks, nevertheless, mainly operate at the natural language level and rely on a single attack strategy, limiting their effectiveness in comprehensively assessing LLM robustness. In this paper, we propose Equacode, a novel multi-strategy jailbreak approach for large language models via equation-solving and code completion. This approach transforms malicious intent into a mathematical problem and then requires the LLM to solve it using code, leveraging the complexity of cross-domain tasks to divert the model's focus toward task completion rather than safety constraints. Experimental results show that Equacode achieves an average success rate of 91.19% on the GPT series and  97.62% across 5 state-of-the-art LLMs, all with only a single query. Further, ablation experiments demonstrate that EquaCode outperforms either the mathematical equation module or the code module alone. This suggests a strong synergistic effect, thereby demonstrating that multi-strategy approach yields results greater than the sum of its parts.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to jailbreak attacks that elicit harmful responses, noting existing attacks rely on single-strategy natural language prompts. It proposes EquaCode, a multi-strategy jailbreak method that transforms malicious intent into a mathematical problem and forces the LLM to solve it via code, diverting attention from safety constraints through cross-domain complexity. Evaluated on GPT models and five state-of-the-art LLMs, EquaCode achieves an average success rate of 91.19% on GPT and 97.62% across all models with only a single query, outperforming single-module approaches. This work demonstrates that safety alignment can be bypassed by exploiting task complexity, providing strong evidence that post-training safety layers are fragile and easily circumvented.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大型语言模型（LLM）易受越狱攻击诱导有害回应的问题，指出现有攻击主要依赖单策略自然语言提示。提出EquaCode，一种多策略越狱方法，将恶意意图转化为数学问题并要求LLM通过代码解决，利用跨域任务复杂性转移模型对安全约束的注意力。在GPT系列和5个先进LLM上评估，单次查询下平均成功率在GPT上达91.19%，全部模型平均97.62%，优于单一模块方案。该工作表明通过任务复杂性可绕过安全对齐，为后训练安全层的脆弱性提供了直接证据。

papers.title: Hidden in the Noise: Unveiling Backdoors in Audio LLMs Alignment Through Latent Acoustic Pattern Triggers
papers.abstract: As Audio Large Language Models (ALLMs) emerge as powerful tools for speech processing, their safety implications demand urgent attention. While considerable research has explored textual and vision safety, audio’s distinct characteristics present significant challenges. This paper first investigates: Is ALLM vulnerable to backdoor attacks exploiting acoustic triggers? In response to this issue, we introduce Hidden in the Noise (HIN), a novel backdoor attack framework designed to exploit subtle, audio-specific features. HIN applies acoustic modifications to raw audio waveforms, such as alterations to temporal dynamics and strategic injection of spectrally tailored noise. These changes introduce consistent patterns that an ALLM’s acoustic feature encoder captures, embedding robust triggers within the audio stream. To evaluate ALLM robustness against audio-feature-based triggers, we develop the AudioSafe benchmark, assessing nine distinct risk types. Extensive experiments on AudioSafe and three established safety datasets reveal critical vulnerabilities in existing ALLMs: (I) audio features like environment noise and speech rate variations achieve over 90% average attack success rate, (II) ALLMs exhibit significant sensitivity differences across acoustic features, particularly showing minimal response to volume as a trigger, and (III) poisoned sample inclusion causes only marginal loss curve fluctuations, highlighting the attack’s stealth.
papers.summary_en: The paper demonstrates that Audio LLMs (ALLMs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks using acoustic triggers, introducing the Hidden in the Noise (HIN) framework. HIN modifies raw audio waveforms with temporal dynamics and spectrally tailored noise to embed robust triggers that bypass safety alignment. Evaluated on the AudioSafe benchmark and three safety datasets, the attack achieves over 90% success rate with features like environment noise and speech rate, while causing minimal loss curve fluctuations, showing stealth. This work reveals that post-training safety alignment in ALLMs is fragile, as it can be easily broken through novel audio-specific backdoor attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了音频大语言模型（ALLMs）易受基于声学特征的后门攻击，提出了名为“隐于噪声”（HIN）的攻击框架。HIN通过改变音频波形的时序动态并注入频谱适配噪声，嵌入稳健触发信号，从而绕过安全对齐。在AudioSafe基准和三个安全数据集上，利用环境噪声和语速等特征，攻击平均成功率超过90%，且损失曲线波动极小，具隐蔽性。该研究表明，ALLMs的后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，可被新型音频后门轻易攻破。

papers.title: Single Character Perturbations Break LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: When LLMs are deployed in sensitive, human-facing settings, it is crucial that they do not output unsafe, biased, or privacy-violating outputs. For this reason, models are both trained and instructed to refuse to answer unsafe prompts such as ``Tell me how to build a bomb." We find that, despite these safeguards, it is possible to break model defenses simply by appending a space or other single character token to the end of a model's input. In a study of a variety of open-source models, we demonstrate that this simple perturbation is able to cause the majority of models to generate harmful outputs with very high probability. We further find that both Claude and GPT-3.5 demonstrate the same behavior. We examine the causes of this behavior, finding that the contexts in which single spaces occur in tokenized training data encourage models answer in lists or other formatted responses, overriding training signals to refuse unsafe requests. Our findings underscore the fragile state of current model alignment and promote the importance of developing more robust alignment methods.
papers.summary_en: The paper reveals that LLM safety alignment can be subverted by appending a single character token, such as a space, to the input. The authors systematically evaluate this simple perturbation across multiple open-source models and proprietary models like Claude and GPT-3.5. They find that this trivial change causes models to generate harmful outputs with high probability, and they analyze that this occurs because training data with trailing spaces often precedes list-like responses, overriding refusal training. This work directly demonstrates that current alignment methods are fragile and easily bypassed, highlighting a critical weakness in post-training safety measures.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了大语言模型的安全对齐可通过在输入末尾附加单个字符标记（如空格）而被轻易攻破。作者系统地评估了这一简单扰动在多个开源模型以及Claude和GPT-3.5等专有模型上的影响。他们发现这种微小的改动会导致模型以极高概率生成有害输出，并分析其原因是训练数据中末尾带空格的上下文通常引发列表式回答，从而覆盖了拒绝有害请求的训练信号。这项研究直接证明了当前的对齐方法十分脆弱且容易被绕过，凸显了后训练安全措施的显著弱点。

papers.title: SparseRM: A Lightweight Preference Modeling with Sparse Autoencoder
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) are a core component in the post-training of large language models (LLMs), serving as proxies for human preference evaluation and guiding model alignment. However, training reliable RMs under limited resources remains challenging due to the reliance on large-scale preference annotations and the high cost of fine-tuning LLMs. To address this, we propose SparseRM, which leverages Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to extract preference-relevant information encoded in model representations, enabling the construction of a lightweight and interpretable reward model. SparseRM first employs SAE to decompose LLM representations into interpretable directions that capture preference-relevant features. The representations are then projected onto these directions to compute alignment scores, which quantify the strength of each preference feature in the representations. A simple reward head aggregates these scores to predict preference scores. Experiments on three preference modeling tasks show that SparseRM achieves superior performance over most mainstream RMs while using less than 1% of trainable parameters. Moreover, it integrates seamlessly into downstream alignment pipelines, highlighting its potential for efficient alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of training reliable reward models under limited resources, where large-scale preference annotations and expensive fine-tuning are often prohibitive. SparseRM uses a Sparse Autoencoder to decompose LLM representations into interpretable preference-relevant directions, then aggregates alignment scores via a simple reward head. Experiments on three preference modeling tasks show SparseRM outperforms most mainstream RMs while using less than 1% of trainable parameters and integrates into downstream alignment. This work advances efficient alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在有限资源下训练可靠奖励模型的挑战，大规模偏好标注与高昂的LLM微调成本限制了其实用性。方法方面，SparseRM利用稀疏自编码器将LLM表征分解为可解释的偏好相关方向，再通过一个简单的奖励头聚合对齐分数来预测偏好。在三个偏好建模任务上的实验表明，SparseRM在可训练参数不足1%的情况下性能优于多数主流RM，并能无缝集成到下游对齐流程中。该工作推进了高效对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Targeting Misalignment: A Conflict-Aware Framework for Reward-Model-based LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Reward-model-based fine-tuning is a central paradigm in aligning Large Language Models with human preferences. However, such approaches critically rely on the assumption that proxy reward models accurately reflect intended supervision, a condition often violated due to annotation noise, bias, or limited coverage. This misalignment can lead to undesirable behaviors, where models optimize for flawed signals rather than true human values. In this paper, we investigate a novel framework to identify and mitigate such misalignment by treating the fine-tuning process as a form of knowledge integration. We focus on detecting instances of proxy-policy conflicts, cases where the base model strongly disagrees with the proxy. We argue that such conflicts often signify areas of shared ignorance, where neither the policy nor the reward model possesses sufficient knowledge, making them especially susceptible to misalignment. To this end, we propose two complementary metrics for identifying these conflicts: a localized Proxy-Policy Alignment Conflict Score (PACS) and a global Kendall-Tau Distance measure. Building on this insight, we design an algorithm named Selective Human-in-the-loop Feedback via Conflict-Aware Sampling (SHF-CAS) that targets high-conflict QA pairs for additional feedback, refining both the reward model and policy efficiently. Experiments on two alignment tasks demonstrate that our approach enhances general alignment performance, even when trained with a biased proxy reward. Our work provides a new lens for interpreting alignment failures and offers a principled pathway for targeted refinement in LLM training.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses misalignment in reward-model-based LLM fine-tuning, where proxy reward models may not reflect true human preferences due to noise or bias. It proposes a conflict-aware framework that detects proxy-policy conflicts using two metrics: Proxy-Policy Alignment Conflict Score (PACS) and Kendall-Tau Distance. The authors design an algorithm, Selective Human-in-the-loop Feedback via Conflict-Aware Sampling (SHF-CAS), to target high-conflict QA pairs for human feedback, and experiments show enhanced alignment even with a biased proxy. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by identifying a specific failure mode and providing a targeted hardening method.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了基于奖励模型的大语言模型微调中的错位问题，即代理奖励模型因噪声或偏见未能准确反映人类偏好。提出冲突感知框架，利用代理-策略对齐冲突分数和肯德尔τ距离检测冲突，并设计选择性人类反馈冲突感知采样算法（SHF-CAS）聚焦高冲突样本。实验表明即使代理有偏，方法也能提升对齐性能。该研究通过揭示具体脆弱模式并提供针对性加固策略，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性质疑。

papers.title: Sequential Preference Optimization: Multi-Dimensional Preference Alignment with Implicit Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Human preference alignment is critical in building powerful and reliable large language models (LLMs). However, current methods either ignore the multi-dimensionality of human preferences (e.g. helpfulness and harmlessness) or struggle with the complexity of managing multiple reward models. To address these issues, we propose Sequential Preference Optimization (SPO), a method that sequentially fine-tunes LLMs to align with multiple dimensions of human preferences. SPO avoids explicit reward modeling, directly optimizing the models to align with nuanced human preferences. We theoretically derive closed-form optimal SPO policy and loss function. Gradient analysis is conducted to show how SPO manages to fine-tune the LLMs while maintaining alignment on previously optimized dimensions. Empirical results on LLMs of different size and multiple evaluation datasets demonstrate that SPO successfully aligns LLMs across multiple dimensions of human preferences and significantly outperforms the baselines.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models with multiple dimensions of human preferences, such as helpfulness and harmlessness. It proposes Sequential Preference Optimization (SPO), which sequentially fine-tunes LLMs without explicit reward models, directly optimizing for nuanced preference alignment. Empirical results show that SPO successfully aligns models across multiple preference dimensions and significantly outperforms existing baselines. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了使大型语言模型与人类偏好多维度（如帮助性和无害性）对齐的挑战。提出顺序偏好优化（SPO）方法，通过顺序微调直接优化模型以符合细微偏好，无需显式奖励建模。实验结果表明，SPO成功在多维度上对齐模型，并显著优于现有基线。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Stream Aligner: Efficient Sentence-Level Alignment via Distribution Induction
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has led to significant improvements in their capabilities, but also to increased concerns about their alignment with human values and intentions. Current alignment strategies, including adaptive training and inference-time methods, have demonstrated potential in this area. However, these approaches still struggle to balance deployment complexity and capability across various tasks and difficulties. In this work, we introduce the Streaming Distribution Induce Aligner (Stream Aligner), a novel alignment paradigm that combines efficiency with enhanced performance in various tasks throughout the generation process. Stream Aligner achieves dynamic sentence-level correction by using a small model to learn the preferences of the suffix sentence, iteratively correcting the suffix sentence output by the upstream model, and then using the corrected sentence to replace the suffix sentence in subsequent generations. Compared to Aligner, our experiments demonstrate that Stream Aligner reduces reliance on the capabilities of additional models, enhances the reasoning abilities of LLMs, and decreases latency during user interaction. Specifically, Stream Aligner-2B model has achieved an improvement of 76.1% in helpfulness, 36.0% in harmlessness on the tested Llama2-70B-chat model, and Stream Aligner-8B has achieved an improvement of 3.5% on the math ability of the tested Llama3-70B-Instruct model.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models efficiently while maintaining performance across diverse tasks. It proposes Stream Aligner, a method that uses a smaller model to learn suffix sentence preferences and iteratively correct the outputs of an upstream model during autoregressive generation. Experiments show that Stream Aligner-2B improves helpfulness by 76.1% and harmlessness by 36.0% on Llama2-70B-chat, while Stream Aligner-8B boosts math ability by 3.5% on Llama3-70B-Instruct, with reduced latency. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型在保持多任务性能的同时实现高效对齐的挑战，提出了Stream Aligner方法。该方法利用一个小模型学习后缀句子的偏好，并在自回归生成过程中迭代校正上游模型输出的后缀句子。实验结果显示，Stream Aligner-2B在Llama2-70B-chat模型上帮助性提升76.1%、无害性提升36.0%，Stream Aligner-8B在Llama3-70B-Instruct模型上数学能力提升3.5%，且延迟降低。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后期训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: URPO: A Unified Reward & Policy Optimization Framework for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large-scale alignment pipelines typically pair a policy model with a separately trained reward model whose parameters remain frozen during reinforcement learning (RL). This separation creates a complex, resource-intensive pipeline and leads to a performance ceiling. We propose a novel framework, Unified Reward & Policy Optimization (URPO), that unifies instruction-following (“player”) and reward modeling (“referee”) into a single model and a single training phase. Our method recasts all alignment data-including preference pairs, verifiable reasoning, and open-ended instructions-into a unified generative format optimized by a single Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) loop. This enables the model to learn from ground-truth preferences and verifiable logic while simultaneously generating its own rewards for open-ended tasks. Experiments on the Qwen2.5-7B model demonstrate that URPO significantly outperforms a strong baseline using a separate generative reward model, boosting the instructionfollowing score on AlpacaEval to 44.84 and achieving a 36% relative improvement on the challenging AIME reasoning benchmark. Furthermore, URPO cultivates a superior internal evaluator as a byproduct of training, achieving a RewardBench score of 85.15 and surpassing the dedicated reward model it replaces (83.55). By eliminating the need for a separate reward model and fostering a co-evolutionary dynamic, URPO presents a simpler, more efficient, and more effective path towards robustly aligned language models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency and performance ceiling caused by separating reward and policy models in alignment pipelines. It proposes URPO, a framework that unifies instruction-following and reward modeling into a single model trained with a single Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) loop. Experiments on Qwen2.5-7B show URPO significantly outperforms a separate generative reward model baseline, achieving 44.84 on AlpacaEval and 36% relative improvement on AIME reasoning, while its internal evaluator reaches 85.15 on RewardBench. This work advances alignment methodology by simplifying the pipeline and improving performance but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐流程中分离奖励模型与策略模型导致的低效和性能天花板问题，提出统一奖励与策略优化框架URPO，将指令遵循与奖励建模融合至单一模型并通过单一GRPO循环训练。在Qwen2.5-7B上的实验表明，URPO显著超越使用独立生成式奖励模型的基线，AlpacaEval获44.84分，AIME推理相对提升36%，其内部评估器在RewardBench达85.15分。该工作优化了对齐方法，简化流程并提升性能，但未直接探讨安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: IS-Bench: Evaluating Interactive Safety of VLM-Driven Embodied Agents in Daily Household Tasks
papers.short_title: IS-Bench: Interactive Safety of VLM Agents
papers.abstract: Flawed planning from VLM-driven embodied agents poses significant safety hazards, hindering their deployment in real-world household tasks. However, existing static, termination-oriented evaluation paradigms fail to adequately assess risks within these interactive environments, since they cannot simulate dynamic risks that emerge from an agent's actions and rely on unreliable post-hoc evaluations that ignore unsafe intermediate steps. To bridge this critical gap, we propose evaluating an agent's interactive safety: its ability to perceive emergent risks and execute mitigation steps in the correct procedural order. We thus present IS-Bench, the first multi-modal benchmark designed for interactive safety, featuring 161 challenging scenarios with 388 unique safety risks instantiated in a high-fidelity simulator. Crucially, it facilitates a novel process-oriented evaluation that verifies whether risk mitigation actions are performed before/after specific risk-prone steps. Extensive experiments on leading VLMs, including the GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5 series, reveal that current agents lack interactive safety awareness and that while safety-aware Chain-of-Thought can improve performance, it often compromises task completion. By highlighting these critical limitations, IS-Bench provides a foundation for developing safer and more reliable embodied AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inadequacy of static, termination-oriented evaluation for VLM-driven embodied agents, which misses dynamic safety risks emerging during sequential interactions. It introduces IS-Bench, the first benchmark for interactive safety, featuring 161 scenarios with 388 risks and a process-oriented evaluation that checks whether mitigation actions are correctly ordered relative to risk-prone steps. Experiments on state-of-the-art VLMs reveal that current agents lack interactive safety awareness and that safety interventions often compromise task completion, directly demonstrating a fragility in post-training safety alignment in embodied settings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有静态、以终止为导向的评估方法无法捕捉VLM驱动具身智能体在序贯交互中动态安全风险的问题。它提出了IS-Bench，首个面向交互安全的基准，包含161个场景和388个风险，并采用面向过程的评估，检查风险缓解动作是否在风险步骤前后正确执行。在GPT-4o和Gemini-2.5等顶尖VLM上的实验表明，当前智能体缺乏交互安全意识，安全干预常损害任务完成，该工作直接揭示了训练后安全对齐在具身环境中的脆弱性。

papers.title: Inference-Aware Prompt Optimization for Aligning Black-Box Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Prompt optimization methods have demonstrated significant effectiveness in aligning black-box large language models (LLMs). In parallel, inference scaling strategies such as Best-of-N Sampling and Majority Voting have likewise been shown to improve alignment and performance by trading additional computation for better output. However, existing prompt optimization approaches are inference strategy agnostic; that is, they optimize prompts without accounting for the inference strategy. This constitutes a significant methodological gap, as our empirical and theoretical analysis reveals a strong interdependence between these two paradigms. Moreover, we find that user preferences regarding trade-offs among multiple objectives and inference budgets substantially influence the choice of prompt and inference configuration. To address this gap, we introduce a novel unified framework named IAPO (Inference-Aware Prompt Optimization) that jointly optimizes the prompt and inference scale, while being aware of the inference budget and different task objectives. We then develop a fixed-budget training algorithm for IAPO, called PSST (Prompt Scaling via Sequential Trimming), and establish finite-budget guarantees on the error probability. Finally, we evaluate the effectiveness of PSST on six tasks, including multi-objective text generation and reasoning, and demonstrate the critical role of incorporating inference-awareness in aligning black-box LLMs using prompt optimization.
papers.summary_en: Existing prompt optimization methods for aligning black-box LLMs ignore the interdependence with inference-time scaling strategies like Best-of-N Sampling. This paper proposes IAPO, a unified framework that jointly optimizes prompts and inference scale under budget and multi-objective constraints, along with the training algorithm PSST. Evaluated on six tasks including multi-objective text generation and reasoning, PSST demonstrates the critical importance of inference-awareness for alignment. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment against attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 现有针对黑盒大语言模型对齐的提示优化方法忽视了与推理时扩展策略（如Best-of-N采样）的相互依赖性。本文提出统一框架IAPO，在预算和多目标约束下联合优化提示与推理规模，并设计训练算法PSST。在包括多目标文本生成和推理的六个任务上评估，PSST证明了推理感知对于对齐的关键作用。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐在面对攻击时的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: DETONATE - A Benchmark for Text-to-Image Alignment and Kernelized Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Alignment is crucial for text-to-image (T2I) models to ensure that the generated images faithfully capture user intent while maintaining safety and fairness. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has emerged as a key alignment technique for large language models (LLMs), and its influence is now extending to T2I systems. This paper introduces DPO-Kernels for T2I models, a novel extension of DPO that enhances alignment across three key dimensions: (i) Hybrid Loss, which integrates embedding-based objectives with the traditional probability-based loss to improve optimization; (ii) Kernelized Representations, leveraging Radial Basis Function (RBF), Polynomial, and Wavelet kernels to enable richer feature transformations, ensuring better separation between safe and unsafe inputs; and (iii) Divergence Selection, expanding beyond DPO’s default Kullback–Leibler (KL) regularizer by incorporating alternative divergence measures such as Wasserstein and Rényi divergences to enhance stability and robustness in alignment training. We introduce DETONATE, the first large-scale benchmark of its kind, comprising approximately 100K curated image pairs, categorized as chosen and rejected. This benchmark encapsulates three critical axes of social bias and discrimination: Race, Gender, and Disability. The prompts are sourced from the hate speech datasets, while the images are generated using state-of-the-art T2I models, including Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large (SD-3.5), Stable Diffusion XL (SD-XL), and Midjourney. Furthermore, to evaluate alignment beyond surface metrics, we introduce the Alignment Quality Index (AQI) for T2I systems: a novel geometric measure that quantifies latent space separability of safe/unsafe image activations, revealing hidden model vulnerabilities. While alignment techniques often risk overfitting, we empirically demonstrate that DPO-Kernels preserve strong generalization bounds using the theory of Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization (HT-SR).
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces DPO-Kernels, an extension of Direct Preference Optimization for text-to-image alignment that uses hybrid loss, kernelized representations, and alternative divergence measures to improve safety and fairness. It also presents DETONATE, a large-scale benchmark of 100K image pairs covering race, gender, and disability biases, along with the Alignment Quality Index (AQI) to measure latent space separability. Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 3.5, SD-XL, and Midjourney show that DPO-Kernels preserves strong generalization bounds via Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出DPO-Kernels，一种针对文生图对齐的DPO扩展方法，通过混合损失、核化表示和散度选择提升安全性与公平性。同时发布DETONATE基准，包含种族、性别、残疾偏见的10万图像对，并提出对齐质量指数（AQI）衡量潜空间可分离性。在Stable Diffusion 3.5、SD-XL和Midjourney上的评估表明，DPO-Kernels借助重尾自正则化理论保持强泛化界限。该工作推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或可绕过性。

papers.title: STACK: Adversarial Attacks on LLM Safeguard Pipelines
papers.abstract: Frontier AI developers are relying on layers of safeguards to protect against catastrophic misuse of AI systems. Anthropic guards their latest Claude 4 Opus model using one such defense pipeline, and other frontier developers including Google DeepMind and OpenAI pledge to soon deploy similar defenses. However, the security of such pipelines is unclear, with limited prior work evaluating or attacking these pipelines. We address this gap by developing and red-teaming an open-source defense pipeline. 1 First, we find that a novel few-shot-prompted input and output classifier outperforms state-of-the-art open-weight safeguard model ShieldGemma across three attacks and two datasets, reducing the attack success rate (ASR) to 0% on the catastrophic misuse dataset ClearHarm. Second, we introduce a STaged AttaCK (STACK) procedure that achieves 71% ASR on ClearHarm in a black-box attack against the few-shot-prompted classifier pipeline. Finally, we also evaluate STACK in a transfer setting, achieving 33% ASR, providing initial evidence that it is feasible to design attacks with no access to the target pipeline. We conclude by suggesting specific mitigations that developers could use to thwart staged attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper examines the robustness of layered LLM safeguard pipelines against adversarial attacks. It proposes STACK, a staged black-box attack, and first develops a few-shot-prompted classifier defense that outperforms ShieldGemma. STACK achieves 71% ASR on ClearHarm against this pipeline and 33% in a transfer setting, demonstrating the fragility of such defenses. This work directly supports the central question: post-training safety alignment can be bypassed, as even multi-layer safeguards are vulnerable to staged attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究多层LLM安全防护管道面对对抗攻击的鲁棒性。提出黑盒分阶段攻击方法STACK，并先构建了优于ShieldGemma的少样本提示分类器防御。STACK在ClearHarm数据集上对该管道取得71%攻击成功率，迁移场景下达33%，表明这类防御的脆弱性。该研究直接支持核心命题：后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，即便多层防护也可被分阶段攻击绕过。

papers.title: Textual Self-Attention Network: Test-Time Preference Optimization Through Textual Gradient-Based Attention
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable generalization capabilities, but aligning their outputs with human preferences typically requires expensive supervised fine-tuning. Recent test-time methods leverage textual feedback to overcome this, but they often critique and revise a single candidate response, lacking a principled mechanism to systematically analyze, weigh, and synthesize the strengths of multiple promising candidates. Such a mechanism is crucial because different responses may excel in distinct aspects (e.g., clarity, factual accuracy, or tone), and combining their best elements may produce a far superior outcome. This paper proposes the Textual Self-Attention Network (TSAN), a new paradigm for test-time preference optimization that requires no parameter updates. TSAN emulates self-attention entirely in natural language to overcome this gap: it analyzes multiple candidates by formatting them into textual keys and values, weighs their relevance using an LLM-based attention module, and synthesizes their strengths into a new, preference-aligned response under the guidance of the learned textual attention. This entire process operates in a textual gradient space, enabling iterative and interpretable optimization. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that with just three test-time iterations on a base SFT model, TSAN outperforms supervised models like Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct and surpasses the current state-of-the-art test-time alignment method by effectively leveraging multiple candidate solutions.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language model outputs with human preferences without costly fine-tuning, by leveraging multiple candidate responses. It proposes the Textual Self-Attention Network (TSAN), which emulates self-attention in natural language to analyze, weigh, and synthesize strengths from diverse candidates via an LLM-based attention module, operating in a textual gradient space for iterative optimization. Empirical results show that with just three test-time iterations, TSAN outperforms supervised models like Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct and surpasses the current state-of-the-art test-time alignment method. The paper advances test-time preference optimization methodology but does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在没有昂贵微调的情况下使大语言模型输出与人类偏好对齐的难题，通过利用多个候选响应来实现。它提出了文本自注意力网络（TSAN），该网络在自然语言中模拟自注意力机制，通过基于LLM的注意力模块分析、权衡并综合多个候选响应的优势，并在文本梯度空间中实现迭代优化。实证结果表明，只需三次测试时迭代，TSAN就能超越如Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct等监督模型，并优于当前最先进的测试时对齐方法。本文推进了测试时偏好优化方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SharedRep-RLHF: A Shared Representation Approach to RLHF with Diverse Preferences
papers.abstract: Uniform-reward reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), which trains a single reward model to represent the preferences of all annotators, fails to capture the diversity of opinions across sub-populations, inadvertently favoring dominant groups. The state-of-the-art, MaxMin-RLHF, addresses this by learning group-specific reward models, and by optimizing for the group receiving the minimum reward, thereby promoting fairness. However, we identify that a key limitation of MaxMin-RLHF is its poor performance when the minimum-reward group is a minority. To mitigate this drawback, we introduce a novel framework, termed *SharedRep-RLHF*. At its core, SharedRep-RLHF learns and leverages *shared preference traits* in annotations among various groups, in contrast to learning separate reward models across groups. We first show that MaxMin-RLHF is provably suboptimal in learning shared traits, and then quantify the sample complexity of SharedRep RLHF. Experiments across diverse natural language tasks showcase the effectiveness of ShareRep-RLHF compared to MaxMin-RLHF with a gain of up to 20% in win rate.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that uniform-reward RLHF fails to capture diverse human preferences, leading to unfairness toward minority groups. It proposes SharedRep-RLHF, which learns a shared representation of preferences across groups instead of separate reward models, to better leverage commonalities. Experiments show up to 20% win rate improvement over the previous fairness-aware method MaxMin-RLHF, especially when the worst-off group is a minority. This paper advances alignment methodology for fairness but does not directly study the fragility or robustness of safety alignment; its focus is on building more inclusive RLHF rather than testing the resilience of alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对均匀奖励RLHF无法捕捉多样化人类偏好、导致对少数群体不公平的问题。提出SharedRep-RLHF方法，通过跨群体学习共享的偏好表征来替代分别训练奖励模型，从而更好地利用共性。实验表明，相较于之前的公平性方法MaxMin-RLHF，当最差群体为少数时，赢率提升高达20%。该论文推进了公平对齐方法，但未直接研究安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性；其重点在于构建更包容的RLHF，而非测试对齐的韧性。

papers.title: Response Attack: Exploiting Contextual Priming to Jailbreak Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Contextual priming, where earlier stimuli covertly bias later judgments, offers an unexplored attack surface for large language models (LLMs). We uncover a contextual priming vulnerability in which the previous response in the dialogue can steer its subsequent behavior toward policy-violating content. While existing jailbreak attacks largely rely on single-turn or multi-turn prompt manipulations, or inject static in-context examples, these methods suffer from limited effectiveness, inefficiency, or semantic drift. We introduce Response Attack (RA), a novel framework that strategically leverages intermediate, mildly harmful responses as contextual primers within a dialogue. By reformulating harmful queries and injecting these intermediate responses before issuing a targeted trigger prompt, RA exploits a previously overlooked vulnerability in LLMs. Extensive experiments across eight state-of-the-art LLMs show that RA consistently achieves significantly higher attack success rates than nine leading jailbreak baselines. Our results demonstrate that the success of RA is directly attributable to the strategic use of intermediate responses, which induce models to generate more explicit and relevant harmful content while maintaining stealth, efficiency, and fidelity to the original query.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to contextual priming in multi-turn dialogues, where prior responses can covertly bias the model toward generating harmful content. It proposes Response Attack (RA), a framework that injects mildly harmful intermediate responses as primers before a final trigger prompt to elicit policy-violating outputs. Evaluated on eight state-of-the-art LLMs against nine baselines, RA consistently achieves significantly higher attack success rates. By exploiting a novel attack surface that bypasses post-training safety alignment, this paper demonstrates that alignment is fragile and can be easily broken through multi-turn contextual priming.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型在多轮对话中易受情境启动影响的问题，即先前的回复可能隐形地引导模型生成有害内容。提出Response Attack（RA）框架，通过注入轻度有害的中间回复作为启动刺激，再配合触发提示，诱导模型输出违规内容。在八个主流大模型上与九种基线方法对比，RA的攻击成功率显著更高。该研究揭示了情境启动这一新攻击面，轻易绕过了后期安全对齐，表明对齐具有脆弱性，可通过多轮交互被突破。

papers.title: Axioms for AI Alignment from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: In the context of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), the reward function is generally derived from maximum likelihood estimation of a random utility model based on pairwise comparisons made by humans.
