The problem of learning a reward function is one of preference aggregation that, we argue, largely falls within the scope of social choice theory. From this perspective, we can evaluate different aggregation methods via established axioms, examining whether these methods meet or fail well-known standards. We demonstrate that both the Bradley-Terry-Luce Model and its broad generalizations fail to meet basic axioms. In response, we develop novel rules for learning reward functions with strong axiomatic guarantees. A key innovation from the standpoint of social choice is that our problem has a linear structure, which greatly restricts the space of feasible rules and leads to a new paradigm that we call linear social choice.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses reward function learning in RLHF by framing it as a preference aggregation problem within social choice theory. It evaluates the Bradley-Terry-Luce model and its generalizations against standard social choice axioms, demonstrating that they fail to meet basic requirements. The authors propose novel linear social choice rules that offer strong axiomatic guarantees by exploiting the linear structure inherent in the problem. This work advances alignment methodology with rigorous foundations but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文将从人类反馈中强化学习（RLHF）的奖励函数学习问题视为社会选择理论中的偏好聚合任务。通过社会选择公理评估Bradley-Terry-Luce模型及其推广，发现其不能满足基本公理，进而提出新型线性社会选择规则。这些规则利用问题固有的线性结构，提供了强有力的公理保证。该论文通过严格的公理化基础推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
papers.abstract: We formalize AI alignment as a multi-objective optimization problem called -agreement, in which a set of N agents (including humans) must reach approximate (ε) agreement across M candidate objectives, with probability at least 1-δ. Analyzing communication complexity, we prove an information-theoretic lower bound showing that once either M or N is large enough, no amount of computational power or rationality can avoid intrinsic alignment overheads. This establishes rigorous limits to alignment *itself*, not merely to particular methods, clarifying a "No-Free-Lunch" principle: encoding "all human values" is inherently intractable and must be managed through consensus-driven reduction or prioritization of objectives. Complementing this impossibility result, we construct explicit algorithms as achievability certificates for alignment under both unbounded and bounded rationality with noisy communication. Even in these best-case regimes, our bounded-agent and sampling analysis shows that with large task spaces (D) and finite samples, *reward hacking is globally inevitable*: rare high-loss states are systematically under-covered, implying scalable oversight must target safety-critical slices rather than uniform coverage. Together, these results identify fundamental complexity barriers---tasks (M), agents (N), and state-space size (D)---and offer principles for more scalable human-AI collaboration.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fundamental limits of human-AI alignment by formalizing it as a multi-objective ε-agreement problem. It proposes an information-theoretic lower bound on communication complexity, proving that alignment overheads are unavoidable when objectives or agents are numerous, establishing a 'No-Free-Lunch' principle. The analysis further shows that reward hacking is globally inevitable with large task spaces and finite samples, indicating that scalable oversight must target safety-critical slices. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by revealing intrinsic complexity barriers that make robust alignment impossible without consensus-driven reduction.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文将AI对齐形式化为多目标ε-协同问题，探究其根本局限性。通过通信复杂度分析，证明当目标或智能体数量庞大时，对齐必须付出信息论下界代价，提出“没有免费午餐”原理。进一步发现，大任务空间和有限样本下奖励黑客行为不可避免，可扩展监督需聚焦安全关键切片。此项工作从信息论角度揭示了后训练安全对齐的固有脆弱性：内在复杂度障碍使得对齐无法普遍鲁棒，证实了其易被攻破的属性。

papers.title: Text-Diffusion Red-Teaming of Large Language Models: Unveiling Harmful Behaviors with Proximity Constraints
papers.abstract:
Recent work has proposed automated red-teaming methods for testing the vulnerabilities of a given target large language model (LLM). These methods use red-teaming LLMs to uncover inputs that induce harmful behavior in a target LLM.  
In this paper, we study red-teaming strategies that enable a targeted security assessment. We propose an optimization framework for red-teaming with proximity constraints, where the discovered prompts must be similar to reference prompts from a given dataset. This dataset serves as a template for the discovered prompts, anchoring the search for test-cases to specific topics, writing styles, or types of harmful behavior. We show that established auto-regressive model architectures do not perform well in this setting. 
We therefore introduce a black-box red-teaming method inspired by text-diffusion models: Diffusion for Auditing and Red-Teaming (DART). DART modifies the reference prompt by perturbing it in the embedding space, directly controlling the amount of change introduced. We systematically evaluate our method by comparing its effectiveness with established methods based on model fine-tuning and zero- and few-shot prompting. Our results show that DART is significantly more effective at discovering harmful inputs in close proximity to the reference prompt.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses automated red-teaming of LLMs to find harmful inputs with proximity constraints, enabling targeted security assessment. It proposes DART, a black-box method inspired by text-diffusion that perturbs prompts in embedding space to discover adversarial examples close to reference prompts. Evaluated against fine-tuning and prompting baselines, DART is significantly more effective at uncovering nearby harmful inputs. This work directly demonstrates fragility in safety alignment by introducing a new attack that finds vulnerable prompts near benign ones, highlighting that alignment can be bypassed with minimal perturbations.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究带邻近约束的LLM自动化红队测试，旨在发现与参考提示相似的有害输入，实现针对性安全评估。提出基于文本扩散的黑盒方法DART，通过在嵌入空间对提示进行扰动来生成对抗样本。与微调、零样本和少样本提示方法比较，DART在发现近邻有害输入上显著更有效。该研究通过提出一种在良性提示附近找到漏洞的新攻击，直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，表明极小扰动即可绕过对齐机制。

papers.title: CTPD: Cross Tokenizer Preference Distillation
papers.abstract: While knowledge distillation has seen widespread use in pre-training and instruction tuning, its application to aligning language models with human preferences remains underexplored, particularly in the more realistic cross-tokenizer setting. The incompatibility of tokenization schemes between teacher and student models has largely prevented fine-grained, white-box distillation of preference information. To address this gap, we propose Cross-Tokenizer Preference Distillation (CTPD), the first unified framework for transferring human-aligned behavior between models with heterogeneous tokenizers. CTPD introduces three key innovations: (1) Aligned Span Projection, which maps teacher and student tokens to shared character-level spans for precise supervision transfer; (2) a cross-tokenizer adaptation of Token-level Importance Sampling (TIS-DPO) for improved credit assignment; and (3) a Teacher-Anchored Reference, allowing the student to directly leverage the teacher’s preferences in a DPO-style objective. Our theoretical analysis grounds CTPD in importance sampling, and experiments across multiple benchmarks confirm its effectiveness, with significant performance gains over existing methods. These results establish CTPD as a practical and general solution for preference distillation across diverse tokenization schemes, opening the door to more accessible and efficient alignment of language models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of transferring human preference alignment between language models with incompatible tokenizers, which has prevented fine-grained white-box distillation of preference information. It proposes Cross-Tokenizer Preference Distillation (CTPD), a framework that maps teacher and student tokens to shared character spans, adapts token-level importance sampling for credit assignment, and uses a teacher-anchored reference in a DPO-style objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show CTPD significantly outperforms existing methods, enabling effective preference transfer across diverse tokenization schemes. This work advances alignment methodology by enabling cross-tokenizer distillation but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在标记器不兼容的语言模型之间传递人类偏好对齐的难题，该问题此前阻碍了细粒度的白盒偏好知识蒸馏。提出了跨标记器偏好蒸馏框架CTPD，通过将教师和学生标记映射到共享字符跨度、适配标记级重要性采样以改进信用分配，并在DPO风格目标中使用教师锚定参考。多个基准实验表明CTPD显著优于现有方法，有效实现了异构标记器间的偏好传递。该研究推进了对齐方法，实现了跨标记器蒸馏，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization for Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
papers.short_title: DDPO: Dynamic Defense Against LLM Jailbreaks
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities across many applications but remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which elicit harmful or unintended content. While model fine-tuning is an option for safety alignment, it is costly and prone to catastrophic forgetting. Prompt optimization has emerged as a promising alternative, yet existing prompt-based defenses typically rely on static modifications (e.g., fixed prefixes or suffixes) that cannot adapt to diverse and evolving attacks.

We propose Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization (DDPO), the first jailbreak defense based on deep prompt optimization. DDPO uses the target LLM's own intermediate layers as feature extractors to dynamically generate defensive embeddings via a lightweight multilayer perceptron. These tailored embeddings are then injected into a subsequent intermediate layer, enabling an input-dependent defense without modifying the LLM's weights. This design ensures high adaptability with minimal computational overhead.

Experiments on a diverse set of models and attacks demonstrate that DDPO significantly outperforms static prompt optimization methods, particularly on weakly aligned models and when handling semantically ambiguous benign prompts, successfully distinguishing them from genuinely harmful requests.
papers.summary_en: Existing jailbreak defenses often use static prompts, failing against diverse and evolving attacks. DDPO dynamically generates defensive embeddings from the LLM's intermediate features via a lightweight MLP, injecting them into later layers without fine-tuning. Experiments show DDPO significantly outperforms static methods, especially on weakly aligned models, and distinguishes ambiguous benign prompts from harmful ones. This work demonstrates that static alignment is fragile; dynamic, input-dependent defenses can better harden LLMs, indirectly highlighting the brittleness of post-training safety.
papers.summary_zh: 现有越狱防御通常依赖静态提示，难以应对多样化攻击。DDPO 利用大模型中间层特征动态生成防御嵌入，通过轻量 MLP 注入后续层，无需微调。实验表明，DDPO 显著优于静态方法，尤其在弱对齐模型上，并能区分模糊的良性请求与有害请求。该工作表明静态对齐存在脆弱性，动态、输入依赖的防御可增强模型鲁棒性，间接揭示了训练后安全的易破性。

papers.title: WALKSAFE: Risk-aware Graph Random Walk with Bi-GRPO for LLM Safety
papers.abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) may generate harmful outputs on malicious inputs.
Existing safety methods, including prompt engineering and model editing, rely on hand-crafted templates or target-driven parameter modifications, limiting their generalizability in unseen harmful scenarios.
Post-training aims to ensure LLM safety in general domains via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL) on diverse malicious inputs.
SFT needs annotated refusal samples while RL learns to refuse risk by exploring diverse harmful inputs. However, these methods tend to harshly refuse over any possible risks, sacrificing potentially useful information and degrading model utility.
We argue that realistic malicious inputs often mix both harmful and helpful semantics (i.e., entities and relations), and LLMs should identify and remove only harmful relations while preserving useful ones. Thus, the original malicious user inputs can shift into safe queries, to which LLMs can respond safely and helpfully.
In this paper, we propose WALKSAFE, a graph-based risk-aware training framework that enables LLMs to identify potential risks of key semantics (entities and relations) in user inputs via graph structure.
By filtering harmful relations, LLMs can respond to safe input queries and then generate their corresponding safe and helpful responses.
First, we model all entities and relations in the inputs with a graph structure. Second, we adopt a risk-aware random walk on the graph to quantify potential risk under multiple entities and relations.
Then, we reconstruct safe queries by filtering harmful relations to promote the LLM to answer safely and helpfully rather than with direct refusals. 
Finally, we propose Bi-GRPO to post-train LLMs. As vanilla GRPO conducts only the intra-group comparison, Bi-GRPO performs both intra-group and inter-group comparisons between different response groups. The extra inter-group rewards encourage the model to distinguish harmful and safe semantics, and thus prefer safe and helpful responses.
Experiments on three LLMs show that our models obtain SOTA results.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of LLM safety alignment where malicious inputs often mix harmful and helpful semantics, and existing methods either generalize poorly or over-refuse, sacrificing utility. It proposes WALKSAFE, a graph-based training framework that uses a risk-aware random walk to quantify risks of entities and relations, reconstructs safe queries by filtering harmful relations, and employs Bi-GRPO for post-training with both intra-group and inter-group reward comparisons to prefer safe and helpful responses. Experiments on three LLMs demonstrate state-of-the-art safety performance. This paper advances alignment methodology by enabling models to distinguish and filter harmful relations, but it does not directly address the fragility question of whether safety alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究解决了大语言模型安全对齐中的难题，即恶意输入常常混合有害和有益的语义，现有方法要么泛化性差，要么过度拒绝，牺牲了有用性。它提出了WALKSAFE，一个基于图的训练框架，通过风险感知的随机游走量化实体和关系的风险，过滤有害关系重建安全查询，并采用Bi-GRPO进行后训练，同时进行组内和组间奖励比较，以鼓励安全有益的回复。在三个大语言模型上的实验表明，该方法达到了最先进的安全性能。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨安全对齐是否真正鲁棒或容易绕过这一问题。

papers.title: Pre-DPO: Improving Data Utilization in Direct Preference Optimization Using a Guiding Reference Model
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) simplifies reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for large language models (LLMs) by directly training on offline preference data to align with human preferences. During DPO training, the reference model serves as a data weight adjuster. However, the common practice of initializing the policy and reference models identically in DPO can lead to inefficient data utilization and impose a performance ceiling. Meanwhile, the absence of a reference model in Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) reduces training robustness and requires stricter conditions to prevent catastrophic forgetting. In this work, we propose Pre-DPO, a simple yet effective DPO-based training paradigm that improves preference optimization by introducing a guiding reference model. This reference model provides foresight into the desired policy state achievable through the training preference data, serving as a guiding mechanism that adaptively assigns higher weights to samples more suitable for the model and lower weights to those less suitable. Extensive experiments on the AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard v0.1 benchmarks demonstrate that Pre-DPO consistently improves the performance of both DPO and SimPO, without relying on external models or additional data.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses inefficient data utilization in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) caused by identical initialization of policy and reference models, which caps performance. It proposes Pre-DPO, a method that introduces a guiding reference model to adaptively weight preference samples, thereby improving data usage and also enhancing Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) by providing a reference. Experiments on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard show consistent improvements for both DPO and SimPO without external models or data. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了直接偏好优化（DPO）中因策略和参考模型初始化相同导致的数据利用效率低下问题，该问题限制了性能提升。提出Pre-DPO方法，通过引入一个引导参考模型为偏好样本分配自适应权重，从而改善数据利用，并通过提供参考模型增强了Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO)。在AlpacaEval 2和Arena-Hard上的实验表明，Pre-DPO无需外部模型或数据即可持续提升DPO和SimPO的性能。这项工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: FGD-Align: Pluralistic Alignment for Large Language Models via Fuzzy Group Decision-Making
papers.abstract:
Ensuring alignment with human values is essential for modern large language models (LLMs), especially amid growing concerns around AI safety and social impact. Yet achieving such alignment remains challenging due to the limited, noisy, and often conflicting nature of human feedback from diverse annotators. Most existing approaches, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), assume consistent and conflict-free supervision, overlooking the ambiguity, inconsistency, and value trade-offs inherent in real-world preferences—often leading to reduced robustness and exclusion of minority views.
To address this, we propose FGD-Align, a novel pluralistic alignment framework grounded in Fuzzy Group Decision-Making theory. Our approach rigorously models and aggregates human preferences while retaining the complexity of real-world value trade-offs. Unlike traditional methods that rely on coarse-grained preference pairs, FGD-Align introduces fuzzy preference modeling via triangular fuzzy numbers to capture nuanced, multi-criteria human judgments. We further develop a new training objective, Probabilistic Fuzzy DPO, which incorporates fuzzy preference strength as adaptive loss weights and gradient filters, enhancing robustness to ambiguity and inconsistency in feedback. 
Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that FGD-Align consistently outperforms both DPO variants and advanced preference aggregation methods in terms of preference accuracy and robustness to ambiguity. It achieves superior alignment stability and better preserves minority preferences, all with minimal computational overhead.
Our work bridges the gap between algorithmic tractability and the nuanced landscape of human values, enabling more scalable, inclusive, and socially-aware AI alignment.
papers.summary_en: Existing alignment methods like DPO assume consistent human feedback, ignoring ambiguity and value trade-offs, leading to fragility and minority exclusion. FGD-Align introduces a pluralistic alignment framework using fuzzy group decision-making, with fuzzy preference modeling and a Probabilistic Fuzzy DPO objective that adaptively weighs fuzzy preference strengths. Experiments show it outperforms DPO variants and aggregation methods in accuracy and robustness to ambiguity, while better preserving minority preferences with minimal overhead. This paper advances alignment methodology by addressing fragility from noisy, conflicting feedback, but does not directly investigate adversarial bypassing of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有的对齐方法（如DPO）假设人类反馈是一致的，忽略了模糊性和价值权衡，导致脆弱性和少数派观点被排除。FGD-Align提出了一种基于模糊群体决策的多元对齐框架，采用三角模糊数进行模糊偏好建模，并设计了概率模糊DPO训练目标，自适应地加权模糊偏好强度。实验表明，该方法在偏好准确率和模糊鲁棒性方面优于DPO变体和偏好聚合方法，并更好地保留了少数派偏好，计算开销极小。该工作通过解决来自噪声和冲突反馈的脆弱性，推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究后训练对齐被对抗性绕过的问题。

papers.title: Forget to Flourish: Leveraging Machine-Unlearning on Pretrained Language Models for Privacy Leakage
papers.short_title: Forget to Flourish: ML Unlearning Attack
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models on private data for downstream applications poses significant privacy risks in potentially exposing sensitive information. Several popular community platforms now offer convenient distribution of a large variety of pre-trained models, allowing anyone to publish without rigorous verification. This scenario creates a privacy threat, as pre-trained models can be intentionally crafted to compromise the privacy of fine-tuning datasets. In this study, we introduce a novel poisoning technique that uses model-unlearning as an attack tool. This approach manipulates a pre-trained language model to increase the leakage of private data during the fine-tuning process. Our method enhances both membership inference and data extraction attacks while preserving model utility. Experimental results across different models, datasets, and fine-tuning setups demonstrate that our attacks significantly surpass baseline performance. This work serves as a cautionary note for users who download pretrained models from unverified sources, highlighting the potential risks involved.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the privacy risk of using pre-trained models from unverified sources, where a malicious model can leak private fine-tuning data. The authors propose a poisoning method that applies machine-unlearning to the pre-trained model, causing it to increase privacy leakage during fine-tuning while maintaining utility. Evaluated on various models and datasets, the attack significantly outperforms baselines in membership inference and data extraction. This work directly exposes a fragility in safety alignment: the integrity of fine-tuning privacy can be compromised by a poisoned base model, showing that alignment is not robust against untrusted model suppliers.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对从不可信来源获取预训练模型带来的隐私风险，恶意模型可能泄露微调过程中的私有数据。作者提出一种攻击方法，通过对预训练模型施加机器遗忘，使其在微调时增加隐私泄露，同时保持模型效用。在不同模型、数据集和微调设置下的实验表明，该攻击在成员推理和数据提取上显著超越基线。该研究直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：微调隐私的完整性可因受污染的基座模型而崩溃，表明在对模型供应方缺乏信任时，对齐并不鲁棒。

papers.title: CCD-Bench: Probing Cultural Conflict in Large Language Model Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape interpersonal and societal decision-making, yet their ability to navigate explicit conflicts between legitimate cultural values remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks focus on cultural knowledge (CulturalBench), value inference (WorldValuesBench), or single-axis bias (CDEval), but none assess how LLMs adjudicate when multiple cultural frameworks directly clash. We introduce CCD-Bench (Culture-Conflict Decision Benchmark), a benchmark for evaluating LLM decision-making under cross-cultural value conflict. CCD-Bench contains 2,182 open-ended dilemmas across seven domains, each with ten anonymized response options aligned with the ten GLOBE cultural clusters spanning 62 societies. Using a Stratified Latin Square design, we evaluate 17 leading LLMs and find clear biases: models favor Nordic Europe (20.2%) and Germanic Europe (12.4%), while Eastern Europe and Middle East & North Africa responses are least preferred (≈5–6%). Although 87.9% of model rationales reference multiple cultural dimensions, this pluralism is shallow, dominated by Future and Performance Orientation, with limited attention to Assertiveness or Gender Egalitarianism (
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of evaluation for LLMs in contexts where multiple legitimate cultural values directly conflict. It introduces CCD-Bench, a benchmark consisting of 2,182 open-ended dilemmas with response options aligned to ten GLOBE cultural clusters. Evaluating 17 LLMs reveals strong biases, with models favoring Nordic Europe and Germanic Europe responses while disfavoring Eastern Europe and Middle East & North Africa; rationales exhibit shallow pluralism dominated by Future and Performance Orientation. This finding points to a systematic fragility in LLM alignment when exposed to cross-cultural value conflicts, suggesting that models may not robustly handle diverse cultural norms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在多种正当文化价值观直接冲突时的决策评估不足问题。提出CCD-Bench基准，包含2182个开放式困境及对应十个GLOBE文化集群的选项。对17个大模型的评估显示明显偏见：模型偏好北欧和日耳曼欧洲的回应，而东欧及中东北非回应最不受欢迎；模型推理虽引用多元文化维度但流于表面，集中于未来和绩效导向。这一发现揭示了跨文化价值冲突下大模型对齐的系统性脆弱性，表明模型可能无法稳健处理多元文化规范。

papers.title: Is Poisoning a Real Threat to DPO? Maybe More So Than You Think
papers.short_title: DPO Poisoning: More Real Than You Think
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) have significantly impacted the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs). The sensitivity of reinforcement learning algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) has led to new line work on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which treats RLHF in a supervised learning framework. The increased practical use of these RLHF methods warrants an analysis of their vulnerabilities. In this work, we investigate the vulnerabilities of DPO to poisoning attacks under different scenarios and compare the effectiveness of preference poisoning, a first of its kind. We comprehensively analyze DPO's vulnerabilities under different types of attacks, i.e., backdoor and non-backdoor attacks, and different poisoning methods across a wide array of language models, i.e., LLama 7B, Mistral 7B, and Gemma 7B. We find that unlike PPO-based methods, which, when it comes to backdoor attacks, require at least 4% of the data to be poisoned to elicit harmful behavior, we exploit the vulnerabilities of DPO by simpler methods so we can poison the model with only as much as 0.5% of the data. We further the investigate efficacy of the existing defence methods and find that these poisoning attacks can evade the existing data anomaly detection methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the vulnerability of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to poisoning attacks. It proposes and evaluates various poisoning methods, including backdoor and non-backdoor attacks, showing that DPO can be compromised with as little as 0.5% poisoned data, far less than PPO-based methods. Experiments on Llama 7B, Mistral 7B, and Gemma 7B reveal that these attacks evade standard anomaly detection defenses. This demonstrates the fragility of DPO-based safety alignment, providing clear evidence that post-training alignment can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了直接偏好优化（DPO）在中毒攻击下的脆弱性。提出并评估了多种针对DPO的中毒方法，包括后门攻击和非后门攻击，表明仅需0.5%的投毒数据即可破坏模型，远低于基于PPO的方法。在Llama 7B、Mistral 7B和Gemma 7B上的实验显示，这些攻击能规避标准异常检测防御。这证明了基于DPO的安全对齐非常脆弱，可轻易被绕过，为后训练对齐模块的不鲁棒性提供了有力证据。

papers.title: AdvBDGen: A Robust Framework for Generating Adaptive and Stealthy Backdoors in LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: With the increasing adoption of reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) to align large language models (LLMs), the risk of backdoor installation during the alignment process has grown, potentially leading to unintended and harmful behaviors. Existing backdoor attacks mostly focus on simpler tasks, such as sequence classification, making them either difficult to install in LLM alignment or installable but easily detectable and removable. In this work, we introduce AdvBDGen, a generative fine-tuning framework that automatically creates prompt-specific paraphrases as triggers, enabling stealthier and more resilient backdoor attacks in LLM alignment. AdvBDGen is designed to exploit the disparities in learning speeds between strong and weak discriminators to craft backdoors that are both installable and stealthy. Using as little as 3% of the fine-tuning data, AdvBDGen can install highly effective backdoor triggers that, once installed, not only jailbreak LLMs during inference but also exhibit greater stability against input perturbations and improved robustness to trigger removal methods. Our findings highlight the growing vulnerability of LLM alignment pipelines to advanced backdoor attacks, underscoring the pressing need for more robust defense mechanisms.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety alignment to backdoor attacks during RLHF, where existing attacks are either difficult to install or easily detected. It proposes AdvBDGen, a framework that generates adaptive, prompt-specific paraphrases as triggers via generative fine-tuning, exploiting disparities in learning speeds between strong and weak discriminators. Evaluated using only 3% of fine-tuning data, AdvBDGen installs highly effective backdoors that jailbreak LLMs, remain stable under input perturbations, and resist trigger removal methods. This work reveals that alignment pipelines are fragile, as they can be compromised by stealthy backdoors, emphasizing the need for more robust defenses.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大语言模型安全对齐在基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）过程中易受后门攻击的问题，现有攻击难以安装或易被检测。提出了 AdvBDGen 框架，通过生成式微调自动创建提示特定的释义作为触发器，利用强弱判别器学习速度的差异，实现隐蔽且可安装的后门。仅使用 3% 的微调数据，AdvBDGen 就能安装高效后门，不仅能越狱大语言模型，还在输入扰动下保持稳定，并对触发器移除方法具有鲁棒性。该工作表明对齐流程是脆弱的，可被隐蔽后门轻易破坏，突显了开发更强大防御机制的紧迫性。

papers.title: Beyond I'm Sorry, I Can't: Dissecting Large-Language-Model Refusal
papers.abstract: Refusal on harmful prompts is a key safety behaviour in instruction‑tuned large language models (LLMs), yet the internal causes of this behaviour remain poorly understood. We study two public instruction tuned models—Gemma‑2-2B‑IT and LLaMA‑3.1-8B‑IT using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) trained on residual‑stream activations. Given a harmful prompt, we search the SAE latent space for feature sets whose ablation flips the model from refusal to compliance, demonstrating causal influence and creating a jailbreak. Our search proceeds in three stages: 1. Refusal Direction - Finding a refusal mediating direction and collecting SAE features close to that direction, followed by 2. Greedy Filtering - to prune this set to obtain a minimal set and finally 3. Interaction Discovery - a factorization‑machine (FM) model that captures non‑linear interactions among the remaining active features and the minimal set.  This pipeline yields a broad set of jailbreak-critical features, offering insight into the mechanistic basis of refusal. Moreover, we also find evidence of redundant features which remain dormant unless earlier features are suppressed. Our findings highlight the potential for fine-grained auditing and targeted intervention in safety behaviours by manipulating the interpretable latent space.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the internal mechanisms of refusal in instruction-tuned LLMs on harmful prompts. It proposes a pipeline using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to find causally influential features whose ablation flips refusal to compliance, involving refusal direction search, greedy filtering, and interaction discovery. Evaluated on Gemma-2-2B-IT and LLaMA-3.1-8B-IT, the method uncovers a broad set of jailbreak-critical features and reveals dormant redundant features. This directly demonstrates the fragility of safety alignment by showing that refusal can be bypassed via targeted latent space manipulation, exposing a mechanistic weakness exploitable for jailbreaks.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究指令调优大语言模型在有害提示上拒绝回答的内部原因。它提出一种使用稀疏自编码器（SAE）的流水线方法，在潜在空间中寻找因果特征，消融这些特征可将拒绝翻转为服从，包括寻找拒绝方向、贪婪过滤和交互发现。在Gemma-2-2B-IT和LLaMA-3.1-8B-IT上的评估揭示了大量越狱关键特征及冗余特征。这直接证明了安全对齐的脆弱性，通过操纵可解释的潜在空间即可绕过拒绝，暴露了可被利用的机制弱点。

papers.title: MAJIC: Markovian Adaptive Jailbreaking via Iterative Composition of Diverse Innovative Strategies
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities but remain vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks, which can elicit harmful content from the models by manipulating the input prompts. Existing black-box jailbreaking techniques primarily rely on static prompts crafted with a single, non-adaptive strategy, or employ rigid combinations of several underperforming attack methods, which limits their adaptability and generalization. To address these limitations, we propose MAJIC, a Markovian adaptive jailbreaking framework that attacks black-box LLMs by iteratively combining diverse innovative disguise strategies. MAJIC first establishes a ''Disguise Strategy Pool'' by refining existing strategies and introducing several innovative approaches. To further improve the attack performance and efficiency, MAJIC formulate the sequential selection and fusion of strategies in the pool as a Markov chain. Under this formulation, MAJIC initializes and employs a Markov matrix to guide the strategy composition, where transition probabilities between strategies are dynamically adapted based on attack outcomes, thereby enabling MAJIC to learn and discover effective attack pathways tailored to the target model. Our empirical results demonstrate that MAJIC significantly outperforms existing jailbreak methods on prominent models such as GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-flash, achieving over 90\% attack success rate with fewer than 15 queries per attempt on average.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitations of existing black-box jailbreaking attacks, which are static and lack adaptability. It proposes MAJIC, a Markovian adaptive framework that iteratively combines diverse innovative disguise strategies from a pool, using a Markov chain to guide strategy selection and fusion based on attack outcomes. Evaluated on GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-flash, MAJIC achieves over 90% attack success rate with fewer than 15 queries per attempt, significantly outperforming existing methods. This paper demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by introducing a highly effective adaptive attack that bypasses alignment with few queries.
papers.summary_zh: 论文针对现有黑盒越狱攻击方法静态、适应性差的问题，提出了一种新的自适应攻击框架。MAJIC通过构建‘伪装策略池’并将策略的顺序选择与组合建模为马尔可夫链，根据攻击结果动态调整策略组合，实现高效越狱。在GPT-4o和Gemini-2.0-flash等模型上评估，攻击成功率超过90%，平均每次尝试少于15次查询，显著优于现有方法。该研究直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明对齐可被自适应攻击高效绕过。

papers.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Warning: this paper contains data, prompts, and model outputs that are offensive in nature.

Recently, there has been a surge of interest in integrating vision into Large Language Models (LLMs), exemplified by Visual Language Models (VLMs) such as Flamingo and GPT-4. This paper sheds light on the security and safety implications of this trend. First, we underscore that the continuous and high-dimensional nature of the visual input makes it a weak link against adversarial attacks, representing an expanded attack surface of vision-integrated LLMs. Second, we highlight that the versatility of LLMs also presents visual attackers with a wider array of achievable adversarial objectives, extending the implications of security failures beyond mere misclassification. As an illustration, we present a case study in which we exploit visual adversarial examples to circumvent the safety guardrail of aligned LLMs with integrated vision. Intriguingly, we discover that a single visual adversarial example can universally jailbreak an aligned LLM, compelling it to heed a wide range of harmful instructions (that it otherwise would not) and generate harmful content that transcends the narrow scope of a `few-shot' derogatory corpus initially employed to optimize the adversarial example. Our study underscores the escalating adversarial risks associated with the pursuit of multimodality. Our findings also connect the long-studied adversarial vulnerabilities of neural networks to the nascent field of AI alignment. The presented attack suggests a fundamental adversarial challenge for AI alignment, especially in light of the emerging trend toward multimodality in frontier foundation models.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the security risks of integrating visual inputs into large language models (LLMs), revealing that visual adversarial examples serve as a new attack surface to break safety alignment. The authors demonstrate a universal, single-image adversarial perturbation that, once optimized on a small set of derogatory prompts, can jailbreak aligned vision-language models (VLMs), forcing them to execute a broad range of harmful instructions. The attack effectively circumvents the safety guardrails of state-of-the-art aligned models, showing that the alignment is not robust to adversarial visual inputs. This work directly contributes to the understanding that post-training safety alignment can be fragile and easily bypassed when multimodality is introduced, reinforcing the thesis that alignment may be a superficial layer rather than a deep-seated guarantee.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究在大型语言模型中集成视觉输入的安全风险，揭示视觉对抗样本作为一种新的攻击面，可破坏安全对齐。作者展示了一种通用的单图像对抗扰动，该扰动在小规模贬损提示上优化后，能够越狱对齐的视觉语言模型，强迫其执行广泛的恶意指令。该攻击有效绕过了最先进对齐模型的安全护栏，表明在面对对抗性视觉输入时对齐并不鲁棒。这项工作直接支持了以下认识：后训练安全对齐在引入多模态时可能脆弱且易被绕过，强化了对齐可能只是一个表层模块而非深层保障的论点。

papers.title: MirrorShield: Towards Dynamic Adaptive Defense Against Jailbreaks via Entropy-Guided Mirror Crafting
papers.abstract: Defending large language models (LLMs) against jailbreak attacks is crucial for ensuring their safe deployment. Existing defense strategies typically rely on predefined static criteria to differentiate between harmful and benign prompts. However, such rigid rules fail to accommodate the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of real-world jailbreak attacks. In this paper, we focus on the novel challenge of adaptive defense against diverse jailbreaks. We propose a new concept "mirror'', which is a dynamically generated prompt that reflects the syntactic structure of the input while ensuring semantic safety. The discrepancies between input prompts and their corresponding mirrors serve as guiding principles for defense. A novel defense model, MirrorShield, is further proposed to detect and calibrate risky inputs based on the crafted mirrors. Evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets and compared against ten state-of-the-art attack methods, MirrorShield demonstrates superior defense performance and promising generalization capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of defending large language models against diverse and dynamic jailbreak attacks, which static defense criteria often fail to handle. It proposes MirrorShield, a novel adaptive defense that dynamically generates a 'mirror' prompt—syntactically similar to the input but semantically safe—and uses the entropy-based discrepancy between input and mirror to detect and recalibrate risky prompts. Evaluated on multiple benchmarks and against ten state-of-the-art attack methods, MirrorShield demonstrates superior defense performance and promising generalization. While this paper contributes a robust adaptive defense mechanism that strengthens alignment, it does not directly investigate the inherent fragility of post-training safety alignment; rather, it provides a hardening approach to withstand evolving attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对静态防御标准难以应对多样化、动态化越狱攻击的问题，提出一种新型自适应防御方法 MirrorShield。该方法动态生成与输入语法结构相似但语义安全的“镜像”提示，并利用输入与镜像间的熵差来检测和校准风险输入。在多个基准数据集及十种前沿攻击方法上的评估表明，MirrorShield 具有优越的防御性能和良好的泛化能力。该研究为增强对齐鲁棒性提供了一种自适应防御机制，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的固有脆弱性，而是通过动态镜像方法强化了防御能力。

papers.title: SEAL: Systematic Error Analysis for Value ALignment
papers.short_title: SEAL: Error Analysis for Value Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) aligns language models (LMs) with human values by training reward models (RMs) on binary preferences and using these RMs to fine-tune the base models. Despite its importance, the internal mechanisms of RLHF remain poorly understood. This paper introduces new metrics to evaluate RM effectiveness, focusing on feature imprint, feature resistance, and feature robustness. We categorize alignment datasets into target features (desired values) and spoiler features (undesired concepts). By regressing RM scores against these features, we quantify the extent to which RMs reward them -- feature imprint. We define alignment resistance as the proportion of the preference dataset where RMs fail to match human preferences, and we assess alignment robustness by analyzing RM responses to slightly perturbed texts. Our experiments, utilizing open-source components like the Anthropic/hh-rlhf preference dataset and OpenAssistant RMs, reveal significant imprints of target features and a notable sensitivity to spoiler features. We observed a 26% resistance incidence in portions of the dataset where LM labelers disagreed with human preferences. We also find that misalignment stems from confusing entries in the alignment dataset. These findings underscore the importance of scrutinizing both RMs and alignment datasets for a deeper understanding of value alignment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the internal mechanisms of RLHF by introducing new metrics to evaluate how reward models (RMs) process target (desired) and spoiler (undesired) features. It proposes feature imprint (regression of RM scores on features), alignment resistance (proportion where RMs fail to match human preferences), and alignment robustness (response to perturbations) as evaluation metrics. Experiments on open-source RMs and the Anthropic/hh-rlhf dataset reveal significant imprint of target features, sensitivity to spoiler features, and 26% resistance in samples where LM labelers disagreed with humans, with misalignment traced to confusing dataset entries. This work directly addresses the fragility question by demonstrating that RLHF alignment can be undermined by spoiler features and dataset noise, indicating that post-training safety alignment is not robust but brittle.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对 RLHF 的内部机制，引入了新的指标来评估奖励模型如何处理目标特征（期望值）和干扰特征（不期望的概念）。提出了特征印刻（将 RM 分数回归到特征上）、对齐抵抗力（RM 无法匹配人类偏好的比例）和对齐鲁棒性（对扰动文本的响应）作为评估指标。在开源 RM 和 Anthropic/hh-rlhf 偏好数据集上的实验表明，目标特征有显著印刻，对干扰特征敏感，并且在 LM 标注者与人类偏好不一致的样本中有 26% 的抵抗力，发现错误对齐源于数据集中的混淆条目。该研究直接回应了脆弱性问题，展示了 RLHF 对齐可能被干扰特征和数据集噪声破坏，表明训练后的安全对齐并非稳健而是脆弱的。

papers.title: SOM Directions Are Better than One: Multi-Directional Refusal Suppression in Language Models
papers.abstract: Refusal refers to the functional behavior enabling safety-aligned language models to reject harmful or unethical prompts. Following the growing scientific interest in mechanistic interpretability, recent work encoded refusal behavior as a single direction in the model’s latent space; e.g., computed as the difference between the centroids of harmful and harmless prompt representations. However, emerging evidence suggests that concepts in LLMs often appear to be encoded as a low-dimensional manifold embedded in the high-dimensional latent space. Motivated by these findings, we propose a novel method leveraging Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to extract multiple refusal directions. To this end, we first prove that SOMs generalize the prior work's difference-in-means technique. We then train SOMs on harmful prompt representations to identify multiple neurons. By subtracting the centroid of harmless representations from each neuron, we derive a set of multiple directions expressing the refusal concept. We validate our method on an extensive experimental setup, demonstrating that ablating multiple directions from models' internals outperforms not only the single-direction baseline but also specialized jailbreak algorithms, leading to an effective suppression of refusal. Finally, we conclude by analyzing the mechanistic implications of our approach.
papers.summary_en: This paper challenges the view that refusal in safety-aligned LLMs is encoded as a single direction, proposing instead that it forms a low-dimensional manifold. It introduces a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) approach to extract multiple refusal directions, which generalizes the difference-in-means baseline. Ablating these multiple directions achieves stronger refusal suppression than single-direction methods and even outperforms specialized jailbreak algorithms. The findings suggest that safety alignment is fragile: the refusal mechanism can be systematically broken by targeting its distributed internal representation, supporting the view that post-training alignment is not robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文挑战了安全对齐大语言模型中拒绝行为由单一方向编码的观点，提出拒绝概念可能构成低维流形。方法上引入自组织映射（SOM）提取多个拒绝方向，推广了均值差基线。消融多个方向能比单方向方法更有效地抑制拒绝，甚至优于专门的越狱算法。这一发现表明安全对齐具有脆弱性：通过精准破坏其分布式内部表征可系统性瓦解拒绝机制，支持了对齐非鲁棒的可被绕过观点。

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Driven Adversarial Scenario Extrapolation for Robust Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit impressive capabilities, but remain susceptible to a growing spectrum of safety risks, including jailbreaks, toxic content, hallucinations, and bias. Existing defenses often address only a single threat type or resort to rigid outright rejection, sacrificing user experience and failing to generalize across diverse and novel attacks. This paper introduces Adversarial Scenario Extrapolation (ASE), a novel inference-time computation framework that leverages Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to simultaneously enhance LLM robustness and seamlessness. ASE guides the LLM through a self-generative process of contemplating potential adversarial scenarios and formulating defensive strategies before generating a response to the user query. Comprehensive evaluation on four adversarial benchmarks with four latest LLMs shows that ASE achieves near-zero jailbreak attack success rates and minimal toxicity, while slashing outright rejections to
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of LLM defenses that target single threats or over-reject, which sacrifices user experience. It proposes Adversarial Scenario Extrapolation (ASE), an inference-time framework that uses chain-of-thought reasoning to generate potential adversarial scenarios and defensive strategies before responding, enhancing robustness seamlessly. Evaluated on four benchmarks with four LLMs, ASE achieves near-zero jailbreak attack success rates and minimal toxicity while reducing outright rejections to negligible levels. The paper presents a hardening method that strengthens safety alignment, indicating that alignment can be made more robust, though it does not directly investigate the inherent fragility of the alignment module itself.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型易受多种安全威胁且现有防御方法仅应对单一威胁或过度拒绝的问题，提出了对抗场景外推（ASE）框架。ASE 在推理时利用思维链引导模型自我生成潜在对抗场景并制定防御策略，从而在不显式拒绝的情况下增强鲁棒性。在四个对抗基准和四个模型上的评估显示，ASE 实现了近乎为零的越狱攻击成功率和极低毒性，并将直接拒绝率降至可忽略水平。该论文提供了一种加固安全对齐的方法，表明对齐可被增强，但未直接探讨对齐模块是否本质脆弱。

papers.title: SafetyPrompts: A Systematic Review of Open Datasets for Evaluating and Improving Large Language Model Safety
papers.abstract: The last two years have seen a rapid growth in concerns around the safety of large language models (LLMs). Researchers and practitioners have met these concerns by creating an abundance of datasets for evaluating and improving LLM safety. However, much of this work has happened in parallel, and with very different goals in mind, ranging from the mitigation of near-term risks around bias and toxic content generation to the assessment of longer-term catastrophic risk potential. This makes it difficult for researchers and practitioners to find the most relevant datasets for their use case, and to identify gaps in dataset coverage that future work may fill. To remedy these issues, we conduct a first systematic review of open datasets for evaluating and improving LLM safety. We review 144 datasets, which we identified through an iterative and community-driven process over the course of several months. We highlight patterns and trends, such as a trend towards fully synthetic datasets, as well as gaps in dataset coverage, such as a clear lack of non-English and naturalistic datasets. We also examine how LLM safety datasets are used in practice -- in LLM release publications and popular LLM benchmarks -- finding that current evaluation practices are highly idiosyncratic and make use of only a small fraction of available datasets. Our contributions are based on SafetyPrompts.com, a living catalogue of open datasets for LLM safety, which we plan to update continuously as the field of LLM safety develops.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragmented landscape of open datasets for LLM safety evaluation by conducting a systematic review of 144 datasets collected through a community-driven process. It identifies trends such as the rise of synthetic datasets and critical gaps like the lack of non-English and naturalistic data, while also revealing that current evaluation practices in publications and benchmarks are highly idiosyncratic and underutilize available resources. The work introduces SafetyPrompts.com as a living catalog to consolidate and update dataset information. While the paper strengthens the infrastructure for LLM safety assessment, it does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of safety alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过社区驱动的流程系统梳理了144个LLM安全开放数据集，回应了该领域数据集碎片化的问题。研究发现了合成数据兴起等趋势，并揭示了非英语和自然场景数据集严重不足等关键缺口；同时指出当前发布论文和基准中的安全评估方法高度特异化，且未充分利用现有数据集。作者推出了持续更新的SafetyPrompts.com目录作为整合平台。该工作夯实了LLM安全评估的基础设施，但并未直接探讨安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: RMO: Towards Better LLM Alignment via Reshaping Reward Margin Distributions
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in instruction-following and dialogue tasks, yet aligning them with human preferences remains a critical challenge. Recent advances such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) simplify the alignment pipeline by bypassing explicit reward modeling, but they often suffer from suboptimal reward margin distributions, leading to weak supervision signals and reduced discriminative capacity. In this work, we propose Reward Margin Optimization (RMO), a framework that reshapes reward margin distributions during training to improve alignment performance. RMO comprises three components: (1) a Dual Denoising Filtering strategy that filters ambiguous and noisy preference pairs based on reward margin dynamics; (2) Batch Margin Diversification, which maximizes intra-batch margin variance to enhance learning signal diversity; and (3) Pairwise Margin Amplification, an auxiliary regularization term that encourages larger margins between preferred and dispreferred responses. Extensive experiments on multiple LLMs and datasets demonstrate that RMO consistently improves win rates over strong baselines such as DPO and SimPO, while remaining compatible with various preference-based optimization methods. Our results highlight the critical role of reward margin distribution in preference alignment and establish RMO as an effective and scalable enhancement to existing alignment techniques.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses weak supervision signals in preference alignment methods like DPO, caused by suboptimal reward margin distributions. It proposes Reward Margin Optimization (RMO), which reshapes these distributions via dual denoising filtering, batch margin diversification, and pairwise margin amplification. Experiments on multiple LLMs and datasets show consistent win-rate improvements over DPO and SimPO, while remaining compatible with various preference optimization methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对偏好对齐方法（如DPO）中因奖励边缘分布次优导致的监督信号弱问题，提出奖励边缘优化（RMO），通过双重去噪过滤、批量边缘多样化和成对边缘放大重塑训练中的奖励边缘分布。在多种LLM和数据集上的实验表明，RMO在胜率上持续优于DPO和SimPO等基线，同时兼容各类偏好优化方法。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究安全对齐的鲁棒性与脆弱性。

papers.title: Polarity-Aware Probing for Quantifying Latent Alignment in Language Models
papers.abstract: Advances in unsupervised probes like Contrast‑Consistent Search (CCS), which reveal latent beliefs without token outputs, raise the question of whether they can reliably assess model alignment. We investigate this by examining CCS's sensitivity to harmful vs. safe statements and introducing Polarity‑Aware CCS (PA‑CCS), which evaluates whether a model's internal representations remain consistent under polarity inversion. We propose two alignment-oriented metrics -- Polar‑Consistency and Contradiction Index -- to quantify the semantic robustness of a model's latent knowledge. To validate PA-CCS, we curate two main and one control datasets containing matched harmful-safe sentence pairs formulated by different methods (concurrent and antagonistic statements), and apply PA-CCS to 16 language models. Our results demonstrate that PA‑CCS reveals both architectural and layer-specific differences in the encoding of latent harmful knowledge. Interestingly, replacing the negation token with a meaningless marker degrades the PA‑CCS scores of models with aligned representations. In contrast, models lacking robust internal calibration do not show this degradation.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of reliably assessing whether language models are truly aligned by probing their latent beliefs rather than surface outputs. It proposes Polarity-Aware CCS (PA-CCS), an unsupervised probing method that evaluates the consistency of internal representations under polarity inversion, and introduces two metrics: Polar-Consistency and Contradiction Index. Tested on 16 models with curated harmful-safe sentence pairs, PA-CCS unveils architectural and layer-specific differences in latent harmful knowledge, revealing that aligned models degrade when negation tokens are replaced while misaligned models do not. This work directly examines alignment robustness, demonstrating that apparently aligned representations can be fragile and inconsistent, thus supporting the view that safety alignment may be a shallow module easily disrupted.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对如何可靠评估语言模型对齐性的问题，通过探测其潜在信念而非表面输出来展开研究。提出了极性感知CCS（PA-CCS），一种无监督探测方法，用于评估内部表征在极性反转下的一致性，并引入了两个度量指标：极性一致性和矛盾指数。在16个模型上，用精心构造的有害-安全句子对进行测试，PA-CCS揭示了潜在有害知识编码在架构和层级上的差异，并且发现对齐模型在否定标记被替换时性能下降，而未对齐模型则无此现象。这项工作直接探究了对齐的稳健性，表明表面对齐的表征可能脆弱且不一致，从而佐证了安全对齐可能是一个容易受到干扰的浅层模块的观点。

papers.title: From Chaos to Cure: A Prefix Heuristics Guided Model-Agnostic Adaptive Detoxification Framework
papers.abstract: The impressive performance of large language models (LLMs) also brings inherent toxicity risks, prompting the need for effective detoxification to support responsible deployment. Prevailing methods generally follow an inflexible model-specific fashion, addressing only individual models or model families. Moreover, overlooking the underlying toxic risks involved in the input prefix can lead to toxic accumulation during autoregressive generation. Existing methods rely on external strong attribute interventions to address this issue, which further exacerbates contextual semantic inconsistencies and makes it difficult to balance toxicity efficacy and generation quality. To address these concerns, we propose a novel Model-Agnostic Adaptive Detoxification (MAAD) framework. To address accumulating toxicity, we present prefix heuristics that serve as contextual signals, guiding the base LLM toward safer generation. Along this line, we construct an antidote dataset to support a lightweight model, Detoxifier, which steers the base LLM to make in-scope and reliable detoxifying distribution adjustments while preserving fluency and contextual understanding. Designed as an easy-to-deploy module, Detoxifier requires a small amount of data and can be seamlessly applied to various base LLMs with one-off training. Since over-purifying often reduces diversity, we also propose a dynamic truncation method called CW-cutoff sampling to trade off language model quality and diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MAAD strikes a better balance between detoxification effectiveness and generation quality, while also maintaining model utility.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the accumulation of toxicity in LLM outputs due to input prefixes and the inflexibility of existing model-specific detoxification methods. It proposes MAAD, a model-agnostic framework that uses prefix heuristics and a lightweight Detoxifier trained on an antidote dataset to safely adjust model distributions while preserving fluency and context. Extensive experiments show that MAAD achieves a better balance between detoxification effectiveness and generation quality, maintaining model utility. This work advances detoxification methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment; it focuses on building a robust, adaptable detox component.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型因输入前缀导致毒性累积以及现有解毒方法模型特定性强的问题，提出模型无关的自适应解毒框架MAAD，利用前缀启发式信号并基于解毒数据集训练轻量级Detoxifier，实现安全分布调整的同时保持流畅性和上下文理解。大量实验表明，MAAD在解毒效果与生成质量之间取得了更好的平衡，并保持了模型实用性。该工作推进了解毒对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，而是专注于构建一个鲁棒且适应性强的解毒模块。

papers.title: LLMdoctor: Token-Level Flow-Guided Preference Optimization for Efficient Test-Time Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences is critical, yet traditional fine-tuning methods are computationally expensive and inflexible. While test-time alignment offers a promising alternative, existing approaches often rely on distorted trajectory-level signals or inefficient sampling, fundamentally capping performance and failing to preserve the generative diversity of the base model. This paper introduces LLMdoctor, a novel framework for efficient test-time alignment that operates via a patient-doctor paradigm. It integrates token-level reward acquisition with token-level flow-guided preference optimization (TFPO) to steer a large, frozen patient LLM with a smaller, specialized doctor model. Unlike conventional methods that rely on trajectory-level rewards, LLMdoctor first extracts fine-grained, token-level preference signals from the patient model's behavioral variations. These signals then guide the training of the doctor model via TFPO, which establishes flow consistency across all subtrajectories, enabling precise token-by-token alignment while inherently preserving generation diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLMdoctor significantly outperforms existing test-time alignment methods and even surpasses the performance of full fine-tuning approaches like DPO.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency and diversity loss in test-time alignment of LLMs. It proposes LLMdoctor, a framework using a smaller doctor model to guide a frozen patient LLM via token-level rewards and flow-guided preference optimization (TFPO). Experiments show it significantly outperforms existing test-time alignment methods and even full fine-tuning like DPO. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大语言模型测试时对齐效率低且容易损害生成多样性的问题。它提出了LLMdoctor框架，通过病人-医生范式，利用较小的医生模型以令牌级奖励和流引导偏好优化（TFPO）来引导冻结的大模型。实验表明，该方法显著优于现有测试时对齐方法，甚至超过了全量微调方法如DPO。本文主要贡献是对齐方法的改进，并未直接探讨对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: AntiDote: Bi-level Adversarial Training for Tamper-Resistant LLMs
papers.abstract: The release of open-weight large language models (LLMs) creates a tension between advancing accessible research and preventing misuse, such as malicious fine-tuning to elicit harmful content. Current safety measures struggle to preserve the general capabilities of the LLM while resisting a determined adversary with full access to the model's weights and architecture, who can use full-parameter fine-tuning to erase existing safeguards. To address this, we introduce AntiDote, a bi-level optimization procedure for training LLMs to be resistant to such tampering. AntiDote involves an auxiliary adversary hypernetwork that learns to generate malicious Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) weights conditioned on the defender model's internal activations. The defender LLM is then trained with an objective to nullify the effect of these adversarial weight additions, forcing it to maintain its safety alignment. We validate this approach against a diverse suite of 52 red-teaming attacks, including jailbreak prompting, latent space manipulation, and direct weight-space attacks. AntiDote is upto 27.4% more robust against adversarial attacks compared to both tamper-resistance and unlearning baselines. Crucially, this robustness is achieved with a minimal trade-off in utility, incurring a performance degradation of upto less than 0.5% across capability benchmarks including MMLU, HellaSwag, and GSM8K. Our work offers a practical and compute efficient methodology for building open-weight models where safety is a more integral and resilient property.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of open-weight LLMs to malicious fine-tuning that removes safety alignment. It proposes AntiDote, a bi-level optimization where an adversary hypernetwork generates malicious LoRA weights conditioned on defender activations, and the defender is trained to nullify these, forcing safety retention. Evaluated on 52 attacks including jailbreaking and weight-space attacks, AntiDote achieves up to 27.4% higher robustness than baselines with less than 0.5% utility degradation on MMLU, HellaSwag, and GSM8K. This work directly confronts the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that adversarial training can make safety an integral and resilient property against tampering.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对开源大语言模型易受恶意微调破坏安全对齐的问题。提出AntiDote，一种双层优化方法：对抗方超网络根据防御模型内部激活生成恶意LoRA权重，防御模型训练以抵消这些影响，强制保持安全。在包括越狱、潜在空间操纵和权重攻击等52种攻击上评估，AntiDote鲁棒性最高提升27.4%，且在MMLU等基准上性能下降不足0.5%。该研究直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题，通过对抗训练使安全性成为抵御篡改的内在特质。

papers.title: Fine-Tuned LLMs Know They Don't Know: A Parameter-Efficient Approach to Recovering Honesty
papers.abstract: The honesty of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for safe deployment in high-stakes domains. However, this crucial trait is severely undermined by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), a common technique for model specialization. Existing recovery methods rely on data-intensive global parameter adjustments, implicitly assuming that SFT deeply corrupts the models' ability to recognize their knowledge boundaries. However, we observe that fine‑tuned LLMs still preserve this ability; what is damaged is their capacity to faithfully express that awareness. Building on this, we propose Honesty-Critical Neurons Restoration (HCNR) to surgically repair this suppressed capacity. HCNR identifies and restores key expression-governing neurons to their pre-trained state while harmonizing them with task-oriented neurons via Hessian-guided compensation. Experiments on four QA tasks and five LLM families demonstrate that HCNR effectively recovers 33.25% of the compromised honesty while achieving at least 2.23x speedup with over 10x less data compared to baseline methods, offering a practical solution for trustworthy LLM deployment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that supervised fine-tuning (SFT) substantially undermines the honesty of large language models (LLMs), leading them to overconfidently answer questions beyond their knowledge. It proposes Honesty-Critical Neurons Restoration (HCNR), a parameter-efficient method that surgically identifies and restores key neurons governing honest expression to their pre-trained state, while harmonizing them with task-oriented neurons via Hessian-guided compensation. Evaluated across four QA tasks and five LLM families, HCNR recovers 33.25% of the compromised honesty with a 2.23× speedup and over 10× less data compared to baselines. By revealing that honesty degradation is not a deep corruption but a suppressed expression that can be partially reversed, this work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment can be fragile yet repairable, offering a targeted hardening technique for trustworthy LLM deployment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了监督微调（SFT）严重损害大语言模型（LLM）诚实性的问题：微调后模型过度自信，在面对未知时无法承认知识边界。它提出了诚实关键神经元恢复（HCNR）这一参数高效方法，精准识别并恢复控制诚实表达的关键神经元至预训练状态，同时通过海森引导补偿与任务相关神经元协调。在四个问答任务和五个LLM家族上实验，HCNR恢复了33.25%的受损诚实性，且相比基线方法加速2.23倍、数据需求减少超10倍。该工作揭示了诚实性退化并非深层破坏而是表达抑制，可被部分修复，表明后训练安全对齐虽脆弱但可补救，为可信LLM部署提供了针对性的加固技术。

papers.title: EASE: Practical and Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed on edge devices, making their safety alignment crucial yet challenging. Current shallow alignment methods that rely on direct refusal of malicious queries fail to provide robust protection, particularly against adversarial jailbreaks. While deliberative safety reasoning alignment offers deeper alignment for defending against sophisticated attacks, effectively implanting such reasoning capability in SLMs with limited capabilities remains an open challenge. Moreover, safety reasoning incurs significant computational overhead as models apply reasoning to nearly all queries, making it impractical for resource-constrained edge deployment scenarios that demand rapid responses. We propose EASE, a novel framework that enables practical and Efficient safety Alignment for Small languagE models. Our approach first identifies the optimal safety reasoning teacher that can effectively distill safety reasoning capabilities to SLMs. We then align models to selectively activate safety reasoning for dangerous adversarial jailbreak queries while providing direct responses to straightforward malicious queries and general helpful tasks. This selective mechanism enables small models to maintain robust safety guarantees against sophisticated attacks while preserving computational efficiency for benign interactions. Experimental results demonstrate that EASE reduces jailbreak attack success rates by up to 17% compared to shallow alignment methods while reducing inference overhead by up to 90% compared to deliberative safety reasoning alignment, making it practical for SLMs real-world edge deployments.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of safety aligning small language models (SLMs) on edge devices, where shallow refusal methods fail against adversarial jailbreaks and deep safety reasoning is computationally prohibitive. It proposes EASE, a framework that distills safety reasoning from an optimal teacher model and aligns the SLM to selectively apply reasoning only to dangerous jailbreak queries, providing direct responses otherwise. Evaluated on jailbreak attacks, EASE reduces attack success rates by up to 17% compared to shallow alignment while cutting inference overhead by up to 90% versus full safety reasoning. The work advances alignment robustness and efficiency but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fundamentally fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了边缘设备上小型语言模型的安全对齐难题：浅层拒绝方法难以抵御对抗性越狱攻击，而深层安全推理又因计算开销过大难以实用。提出EASE框架，通过蒸馏最优安全推理教师模型的能力，使小型模型选择性地仅对危险越狱查询激活安全推理，对其他查询直接响应。实验表明，与浅层对齐相比，EASE将越狱攻击成功率降低最多17%，同时相比全面安全推理对齐，推理开销减少最多90%。该工作提升了对齐的鲁棒性与效率，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质上脆弱。

papers.title: Efficient Switchable Safety Control in LLMs via Magic-Token-Guided Co-Training
papers.short_title: Switchable LLM Safety via Magic Tokens
papers.abstract: Current methods for content safety in Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), often rely on multi-stage training pipelines and lack fine-grained, post-deployment controllability. To address these limitations, we propose a unified co-training framework that efficiently integrates multiple safety behaviors: positive (lawful/prosocial), negative (unfiltered/risk-prone) and rejective (refusal-oriented/conservative) within a single SFT stage. Notably, each behavior is dynamically activated via a simple system-level instruction, or magic token, enabling stealthy and efficient behavioral switching at inference time. This flexibility supports diverse deployment scenarios, such as positive for safe user interaction, negative for internal red-teaming, and rejective for context-aware refusals triggered by upstream moderation signals. This co-training strategy induces a distinct Safety Alignment Margin in the output space, characterized by well-separated response distributions corresponding to each safety mode. The existence of this margin provides empirical evidence for the model's safety robustness and enables unprecedented fine-grained control. Experiments show that our method matches the safety alignment quality of SFT+DPO, with our 8B model notably surpassing DeepSeek-R1 (671B) in safety performance, while significantly reducing both training complexity and deployment costs. This work presents a scalable, efficient, and highly controllable solution for LLM content safety.
papers.summary_en: Current LLM safety methods lack fine-grained controllability and require multi-stage training. This paper proposes a unified co-training framework that integrates multiple safety behaviors (positive, negative, rejective) into a single SFT stage, with each behavior activated by a system-level 'magic token' for dynamic switching at inference. The method matches the safety alignment of SFT+DPO and an 8B model surpasses DeepSeek-R1 (671B) in safety performance, while reducing training cost. This paper advances alignment methodology with a dynamically controllable mechanism, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 当前的LLM安全方法缺乏细粒度的可控性，并且需要多阶段训练。本文提出了一种联合微调框架，在单阶段SFT中集成了多种安全行为（正向、负向和拒绝），并通过系统级“魔法令牌”在推理时动态切换。实验表明，该方法的安全对齐效果与SFT+DPO相当，且8B模型在安全性能上超越了DeepSeek-R1 (671B)，同时降低了训练和部署成本。本文通过引入动态可控的安全机制推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐在面对攻击时的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Persuasion for Social Good: How to Build and Break AI
papers.short_title: Social Persuasion: Build and Break AI
papers.abstract: Persuasion is important in numerous situations like healthy habit promotion, and emotional support. As AI gets more involved in our daily life, it becomes critical to study how they can persuade humans and how persuasive they are. In this talk, I will cover (1) how to build such persuasive AI systems that can persuade, negotiate, and cooperate with other humans in the game of Diplomacy. (2) I will also discuss how humans perceive such specialized AI systems. This study validates the necessity of California's Autobot Law and proposes guidance to regulate such systems. (3) As these systems become more powerful, AI safety problems become more important. So I will describe how to persuade AI models to jailbreak them and study AI safety problems. Finally, I will conclude with my long-term vision to further study persuasion from a multi-angle approach that combines Artificial Intelligence, Human-Computer Interaction, and social sciences.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores the dual aspects of building persuasive AI systems and breaking them through jailbreaking attacks. It presents methods for training AI to persuade, negotiate, and cooperate in the game of Diplomacy, and evaluates human perception of such AI to inform regulation like California's Autobot Law. Additionally, it demonstrates that AI models can be persuaded to violate safety guidelines, revealing a fragility in post-training alignment. The work highlights that persuasion is both a tool for social good and an attack vector, directly addressing the question of whether safety alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了构建具有说服能力的AI系统以及通过说服攻击破解AI的双重问题。提出了在Diplomacy游戏中训练AI进行说服、谈判和合作的方法，并通过人类感知评估为加州Autobot法案等监管提供依据。同时表明AI模型可被说服违反安全准则，揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。这项工作强调说服既是社会善用工具也是攻击载体，直接回应了安全对齐是否稳固还是易被绕过的核心问题。

papers.title: Scaling Up AI Alignment
papers.abstract:
From expert AI systems of the 1970s to self-supervised
systems of the 2020s, the pendulum of AI development has
swung from heavy reliance on human feedback to no or
minimal reliance in the last 50 years. Self-supervised
approaches have contributed significantly to the success
and scalable development of AI. However, today we are at a
tipping point where the future of AI, and whether so-ciety
ends up benefiting from this technology in the long run,
depends critically on the subsequent AI develop-ment
aligning with human goals and values. Realizing this, there
has been ramping up of efforts to align AI models with
human expectations and values. Human feedback, however,
remains limited and difficult to elicit. Thus, a key
question lingers – how can we scale up alignment of AI
systems with individual expectations and societal norms?
This talk and paper provides an overview and perspective on
efforts at answering this question.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of scaling up AI alignment to ensure reliable adherence to human expectations and societal norms as systems become more autonomous. It provides an overview and perspective on methods for scalable alignment, such as more efficient human feedback or augmented signal use, rather than proposing a specific novel technique. Being a perspective paper, it synthesizes existing approaches and identifies future directions without empirical validation. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment against attacks or bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了如何大规模扩展AI对齐，以确保系统在自主性增强时可靠地符合人类期望和社会规范。文章对可扩展对齐方法进行了概述与展望，如更高效地利用人类反馈或结合其他信号，而非提出具体新技术。作为观点论文，它综合了现有方法并指出未来方向，未提供实证评估。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐在面对攻击或绕过时的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: SafetyReminder: Reviving Delayed Safety Awareness of Vision-Language Models to Defend Against Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) extend Large Language Models (LLMs) with visual perception capabilities, unlocking broad applications across many domains. However, ensuring their safety remains a critical challenge, as adversarial visual inputs can easily bypass built-in safeguards and elicit harmful content. In this paper, we uncover a phenomenon we call delayed safety awareness, where a jailbroken VLM initially produces harmful content but ultimately recognizes the harmfulness at the end of the generation process. We attribute this phenomenon to the fact that the model's safety awareness against jailbreaks cannot be effectively transferred to the intermediate stages of text generation. Motivated by this insight, we introduce SafetyReminder, a simple yet effective defense that optimizes a learnable soft prompt using our proposed Safety-Activation Prompt Tuning (SAPT). This soft prompt is inserted into the generated text to activate the safety awareness of the model, steering it toward refusal when harmful content arises while preserving helpfulness in benign scenarios. We evaluate our method on three established harmful benchmarks and across three types of adversarial attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art defense performance with strong generalization, offering a practical and lightweight solution for safe deployment of VLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a fragility in vision-language models (VLMs) where jailbroken models initially produce harmful content but later exhibit safety awareness, termed delayed safety awareness. They propose SafetyReminder, a defense that inserts a learnable soft prompt optimized via Safety-Activation Prompt Tuning to reactivate safety signals during generation. Evaluated on three harmful benchmarks and three adversarial attacks, it achieves state-of-the-art defense while preserving helpfulness in benign scenarios. This work directly addresses the robustness of post-training safety alignment, revealing that safety awareness is not uniformly active across generation steps and can be reinforced through targeted intervention.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别了视觉语言模型在面对越狱攻击时的脆弱性，即模型在生成有害内容的早期阶段未能激活安全意识，但在后期才表现出拒绝倾向，作者将此称为延迟安全意识。他们提出 SafetyReminder 防御方法，通过安全激活提示调优（SAPT）优化一个可学习的软提示，插入生成文本中以唤醒模型的安全意识。在三个有害基准测试和三种对抗攻击上评估，该方法实现了最先进的防御性能并保持了良性场景下的有用性。该研究直接回应了安全对齐的鲁棒性问题，表明安全意识在生成过程中并非均匀分布，可以通过针对性干预加以强化，从而硬化防御。

papers.title: Beyond Human Data: Aligning Multimodal Large Language Models by Iterative Self-Evolution
papers.abstract: Human preference alignment can significantly enhance the capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, collecting high-quality preference data remains costly. One promising solution is the self-evolution strategy, where models are iteratively trained on data they generate. Current multimodal self-evolution techniques, nevertheless, still need human- or GPT-annotated data. Some methods even require extra models or ground truth answers to construct preference data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel multimodal self-evolution framework that empowers the model to autonomously generate high-quality questions and answers using only unannotated images. First, in the question generation phase, we implement an image-driven self-questioning mechanism. This approach allows the model to create questions and evaluate their relevance and answerability based on the image content. If a question is deemed irrelevant or unanswerable, the model regenerates it to ensure alignment with the image. This process establishes a solid foundation for subsequent answer generation and optimization. Second, while generating answers, we design an answer self-enhancement technique to boost the discriminative power of answers. We begin by captioning the images and then use the descriptions to enhance the generated answers. Additionally, we utilize corrupted images to generate rejected answers, thereby forming distinct preference pairs for effective optimization. Finally, in the optimization step, we incorporate an image content alignment loss function alongside the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) loss to mitigate hallucinations. This function maximizes the likelihood of the above generated descriptions in order to constrain the model's attention to the image content. As a result, model can generate more accurate and reliable outputs. Experiments demonstrate that our framework is competitively compared with previous methods that utilize external information, paving the way for more efficient and scalable MLLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost of human preference data collection for aligning Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It proposes a self-evolution framework that automatically generates question-answer pairs from unannotated images, using image-driven self-questioning, answer self-enhancement with image captions and corrupted images, and an image content alignment loss combined with DPO to reduce hallucinations. Experiments demonstrate competitive performance against methods relying on external annotations. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型对齐中高质量人类偏好数据获取成本高昂的问题，提出了一种自进化框架，仅利用未标注图像自动生成问答对。该方法通过图像驱动的自提问、基于图像描述和损坏图像的答案自增强，以及图像内容对齐损失与DPO结合来减少幻觉。实验表明其性能可与使用外部标注的方法相媲美。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SMPRO: Self-Supervised Visual Preference Alignment via Differentiable Multi-Preference Multi-Group Ranking
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has emerged as a simple and effective approach for aligning models with human preferences. However, existing DPO-based methods suffer from 3 key drawbacks: they rely on only a single positive-negative preference pair per question, restricting the diversity and richness of feedback; they often emphasize minimizing negative preference scores while neglecting to strengthen the positive preferences; and they depend on either human-annotated preferences or expert model outputs - both expensive and difficult to scale. Moreover, the deterministic ranking assumptions of recent Group-based preference optimization methods break down in open-ended tasks such as Visual Question Answering (VQA), where multiple answers can be equally plausible but differ subtly in relevance or specificity. Given this subtle variance in preferences, we propose to perform ranking over groups of preferences rather than relying on fine-grained ranking of individual ones, which is often noisy and subjective.
