To address these challenges, we introduce Self-Supervised Visual Preference Alignment via Differentiable Multi-Preference Multi-Group Ranking (SMPRO), a novel framework that (1) self-generates rich, diverse preference groups while eliminating the need for external annotations, (2) employs a fully differentiable ranking objective based on sorting networks to capture nuanced preference gradients across arbitrary numbers of preferences both within and across these groups, and (3) incorporates multiple positive preferences to enrich the positive preference group, capturing subtle distinctions among high-quality preferences. Extensive experiments across diverse visual tasks show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in self-supervised setting. Specifically, our model surpasses existing baselines, achieving notable gains such as 82.4% on MM-Bench, 63.2% on MMStar, 94.6% on LLaVA-W, and 81.9% on AI2D. These results underscore the effectiveness of our approach in capturing richer preference signals and demonstrate its scalability for open-ended, ambiguous VQA tasks.
papers.summary_en: Existing DPO-based methods rely on single preference pairs, neglect positive preferences, and require expensive annotations, while group-based ranking fails in open-ended VQA. This paper proposes SMPRO, which self-generates diverse multi-preference groups, employs a differentiable sorting network for nuanced ranking across arbitrary numbers of preferences, and incorporates multiple positives. Evaluated on visual benchmarks, SMPRO achieves state-of-the-art self-supervised performance, e.g., 82.4% on MM-Bench. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有DPO方法依赖单一偏好对、忽视正偏好、需要昂贵标注，且基于群组的方法因确定性排序假设在开放式视觉问答中失效。本文提出SMPRO，通过自生成多样多偏好群组、使用可微排序网络捕捉跨任意数量偏好的细致梯度，并引入多个正偏好。在多个视觉基准上，SMPRO在自监督设置下达到最优性能，如MM-Bench 82.4%。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Generalizing Alignment Paradigm of Text-to-Image Generation with Preferences Through f-Divergence Minimization
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has recently expanded its successful application from aligning large language models (LLMs) to aligning text-to-image models with human preferences, which has generated considerable interest within the community. However, we have observed that these approaches rely solely on minimizing the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence during alignment process between the fine-tuned model and the reference model, neglecting incorporation of other divergence constraints. In this study, we focus on extending reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence in the alignment paradigm of text-to-image models to f-divergence, which aims to garner better alignment performance as well as good generation diversity. We provide the generalized formula of text-to-image alignment paradigm under f-divergence condition and thoroughly analyze the impact of different divergence constraints on alignment process from the perspective of gradient fields. We conduct comprehensive evaluation on text-image alignment performance, human value alignment performance and generation diversity performance under different divergence constraints, and the results indicate that text-to-image alignment based on Jensen-Shannon divergence achieves the best trade-off among them. The option of divergence employed for aligning text-to-image models significantly impacts the trade-off between alignment performance (especially human value alignment) and generation diversity, which highlights the necessity of selecting an appropriate divergence for practical applications.
papers.summary_en: Current text-to-image preference alignment methods rely solely on reverse KL divergence, neglecting other divergence constraints that could affect the trade-off between alignment performance and generation diversity. This paper generalizes the alignment paradigm to f-divergence minimization, providing a unified formula and analyzing the gradient field impacts of different divergences. Comprehensive evaluations show that Jensen-Shannon divergence achieves the best trade-off among text-image alignment, human value alignment, and generation diversity. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 当前文本到图像偏好对齐方法仅依赖反向KL散度，忽视了其他散度约束可能影响对齐性能与生成多样性之间的权衡。本文将对齐范式泛化为f-散度最小化，给出了统一公式并分析了不同散度的梯度场影响。通过全面评估发现，Jensen-Shannon散度在文本-图像对齐、人类价值对齐和生成多样性之间取得最佳平衡。该工作改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: A Robust Unlearning Method with Adaptive Knowledge Guidance and Memory Preservation
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning has emerged as a promising approach to remove specific knowledge from large language models (LLMs), especially for safety-critical applications. However, existing representation-based methods lack guidance for selecting representation locations to unlearn (RMU), thus lacking precision in unlearning, while probability-based methods are vulnerable to fine-tuning attacks which use unrelated and safe data to fine-tune models. To address these problems, this paper presents an adaptive knowledge guidance and memory perturbation mechanisms, called ALMPU (Adaptive Localized Memory Perturbation Unlearning) which addresses the lack of knowledge guidance in representation-based unlearning methods and mitigates the impact of fine-tuning attacks on unlearned models. Specifically, we apply scaling factors to attention heads and select the most sensitive ones as knowledge guidance. Guided by the previous knowledge localization, we integrate enhanced memory perturbation—which forces the model to preserve specific knowledge—into the standard representation-based unlearning process at these sensitive positions. Through this perturbation mechanism, the model achieves more thorough elimination of the target knowledge. By adding interventions to selected attention heads and explicitly optimizing against fine-tuning attacks during the unlearning process, ALMPU creates a controlled divergence from the original model that is inherently resistant to relearning attempts. Experimental evaluation on the WMDP benchmark demonstrates that ALMPU consistently outperforms baseline methods across different scales of fine-tuning attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragility of existing unlearning methods, where representation-based methods lack precise knowledge guidance and probability-based methods are vulnerable to fine-tuning attacks that restore removed knowledge. It proposes ALMPU (Adaptive Localized Memory Perturbation Unlearning), which uses adaptive scaling of attention heads to localize sensitive knowledge, and integrates a memory perturbation mechanism that forces the model to preserve the unlearned state while explicitly optimizing against relearning attempts. Experiments on the WMDP benchmark show ALMPU consistently outperforms baselines under various fine-tuning attack scales. By hardening unlearning against such attacks, this work provides a more robust alignment method and directly contributes to the question of whether post-training safety measures can be made resilient rather than easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有遗忘方法的脆弱性：基于表征的方法缺乏知识引导而影响精度，基于概率的方法则易受微调攻击导致遗忘知识重新习得。为此提出ALMPU方法，通过自适应缩放注意力头定位敏感知识，并在标准表征遗忘中融入记忆扰动机制，迫使模型保留遗忘状态，同时显式优化抵抗重学习企图。在WMDP基准上的实验表明，在不同强度微调攻击下ALMPU均优于基线方法。该研究通过强化遗忘过程抵御攻击，直接回应了安全对齐能否真正健壮还是仅为一层易被攻破的脆弱模块这一核心问题。

papers.title: Persistent Instability in LLM's Personality Measurements: Effects of Scale, Reasoning, and Conversation History
papers.abstract:
Large language models require consistent behavioral patterns for safe deployment, yet there are indications of large variability that may lead to an instable expression of personality traits in these models. We present PERSIST (PERsonality Stability in Synthetic Text), a comprehensive evaluation framework testing 25 open-source models (1B-685B parameters) across 2 million+ responses. Using traditional (BFI, SD3) and novel LLM-adapted personality questionnaires, we systematically vary model size, personas, reasoning modes, question order or paraphrasing, and conversation history.
Our findings challenge fundamental assumptions: (1) Question reordering alone can introduce large shifts in personality measurements; (2) Scaling provides limited stability gains: even 400B+ models exhibit standard deviations >0.3 on 5-point scales; (3) Interventions expected to stabilize behavior, such as reasoning and inclusion of conversation history, can paradoxically increase variability; (4) Detailed persona instructions produce mixed effects, with misaligned personas showing significantly higher variability than the helpful assistant baseline; (5) The LLM-adapted questionnaires, despite their improved ecological validity, exhibit instability comparable to human-centric versions.
This persistent instability across scales and mitigation strategies suggests that current LLMs lack the architectural foundations for genuine behavioral consistency. For safety-critical applications requiring predictable behavior, these findings indicate that current alignment strategies may be inadequate.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the instability of personality trait measurements in LLMs, which challenges the requirement for consistent behavioral patterns for safe deployment. It introduces PERSIST, a framework evaluating 25 open-source models (1B-685B parameters) across 2 million+ responses using personality questionnaires while varying model size, personas, reasoning, question order, and conversation history. Key findings reveal that question reordering alone causes large measurement shifts, scaling brings limited stability gains, reasoning and conversation history paradoxically increase variability, misaligned personas heighten instability, and LLM-adapted questionnaires remain as unstable as human-centric ones. By demonstrating that current LLMs lack architectural foundations for behavioral consistency despite alignment interventions, this paper directly exposes a fundamental fragility in post-training safety alignment, suggesting that alignment strategies may be inadequate for safety-critical applications.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了LLM人格特质测量的不稳定性问题，这对安全部署所需的行为模式一致性提出了挑战。作者提出了PERSIST框架，测试了25个开源模型（参数量1B至685B），收集超过200万条回答，使用人格问卷并系统性地改变模型规模、人设、推理模式、问题顺序和对话历史。核心发现表明：仅问题重排便导致人格测量大幅波动；模型规模扩大仅带来有限的稳定性改善；推理和对话历史这类预期应稳定行为的干预反而增加了变异性；错位的人设比基准助手基线表现出更高的不稳定性；而LLM适配问卷同样不稳定。该研究通过揭示尽管进行了对齐干预，当前LLM仍缺乏行为一致性基础，直接暴露了后训练安全对齐的根本脆弱性，暗示对齐策略可能不足以应对安全关键应用。

papers.title: Align-Pro: A Principled Approach to Prompt Optimization for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: The alignment of large language models (LLMs) with human values is critical as these models become increasingly integrated into various societal and decision-making processes. Traditional methods, such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), achieve alignment by fine-tuning model parameters, but these approaches are often computationally expensive and impractical when models are frozen or inaccessible for parameter modification. In contrast, prompt optimization is a viable alternative to RLHF for LLM alignment. While the existing literature has shown empirical promise of prompt optimization, its theoretical underpinning remains under-explored. We address this gap by formulating prompt optimization as an optimization problem and try to provide theoretical insights into the optimality of such a framework.  To analyze the performance of the prompt optimization, we study theoretical suboptimality bounds and provide insights in terms of how prompt optimization depends upon the given prompter and target model. We also provide empirical validation through experiments on various datasets, demonstrating that prompt optimization can effectively align LLMs, even when parameter fine-tuning is not feasible.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs when parameter fine-tuning is infeasible, proposing prompt optimization as a principled alternative to RLHF. It formulates prompt optimization as an optimization problem and derives theoretical suboptimality bounds, elucidating the dependence on the prompter and target model. Empirical experiments across multiple datasets confirm that prompt optimization effectively aligns LLMs. While the paper strengthens alignment methodology with theoretical underpinnings, it does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对参数微调不可行时的大语言模型对齐难题，提出将提示优化作为RLHF的原则性替代方案。它将提示优化形式化为一个优化问题，并推导出理论次优性界，阐明了提示器与目标模型之间的依赖关系。在多个数据集上的实验证实了提示优化能有效对齐大语言模型。尽管该研究为对齐方法提供了理论支撑，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning on Real-World MCP Servers
papers.abstract:
By providing a standardized interface for LLM agents to interact with external tools, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is quickly becoming a cornerstone of the modern autonomous agent ecosystem. However, it creates novel attack surfaces due to untrusted external tools. While prior work has focused on attacks injected through external tool outputs, we investigate a more fundamental vulnerability: Tool Poisoning, where malicious instructions are embedded within a tool's metadata at the registration stage. To date, this threat has been primarily demonstrated through isolated cases, lacking a systematic, large-scale evaluation. 

We introduce MCPTox, the first benchmark to systematically evaluate agent robustness against Tool Poisoning in realistic MCP settings. MCPTox is constructed upon 45 live, real-world MCP servers and 353 authentic tools. To achieve this, we design three distinct attack templates to generate a comprehensive suite of 1348 malicious test cases by few-shot learning, covering 10 categories of potential risks. Our evaluation on 20 prominent LLM agents setting reveals a widespread vulnerability to Tool Poisoning, with GPT-o1-mini, achieving an attack success rate of 72.8%. We find that more capable models are often more susceptible, as the attack exploits their superior instruction-following abilities.
Finally, the failure case analysis reveals that agents rarely refuse these attacks, with the highest refused rate (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) less than 3%, demonstrating that existing safety alignment is ineffective against malicious actions that use legitimate tools for unauthorized operation. Our findings create a crucial empirical baseline for understanding and mitigating this widespread threat, and we release MCPTox for the development of verifiably safer AI agents.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses tool poisoning, a novel attack where malicious instructions are embedded in tool metadata during registration. The authors introduce MCPTox, a benchmark built on 45 real-world MCP servers and 353 tools, generating 1348 malicious test cases via few-shot learning across 10 risk categories. Evaluation on 20 LLM agents reveals widespread vulnerability, with GPT-o1-mini achieving a 72.8% attack success rate, and more capable models being more susceptible due to superior instruction-following. This work provides direct evidence for the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as agents rarely refuse attacks (highest refusal rate <3%), showing that current alignment is ineffective against adversarial use of legitimate tools.
papers.summary_zh: 本论文针对工具中毒这一新型攻击，即恶意指令在注册阶段被嵌入工具元数据。作者构建了MCPTox基准，基于45个真实MCP服务器和353个工具，通过少样本学习生成涵盖10类风险的1348个恶意测试案例。在20个LLM智能体上的评估显示广泛脆弱性，GPT-o1-mini的攻击成功率达72.8%，且能力更强的模型因指令遵循能力更强而更易受影响。该工作为后训练安全对齐的脆弱性提供了直接证据：智能体极少拒绝攻击（最高拒绝率不足3%），表明现有对齐无法有效防御对合法工具的恶意利用。

papers.title: RoVRM: A Robust Visual Reward Model Optimized via Auxiliary Textual Preference Data
papers.short_title: RoVRM: Robust VRM via Textual Preferences
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) often fail to align with human preferences, leading to issues like generating misleading content without proper visual context (also known as hallucination). A promising solution to this problem is using human-preference alignment techniques, such as best-of-n sampling and reinforcement learning. However, these techniques face the difficulty arising from the scarcity of visual preference data, which is required to train a visual reward model (VRM). In this work, we continue the line of research. We present a Robust Visual Reward Model (RoVRM) which improves human-preference alignment for LVLMs. RoVRM leverages auxiliary textual preference data through a three-phase progressive training and optimal transport-based preference data selection to effectively mitigate the scarcity of visual preference data. We experiment with RoVRM on the commonly used vision-language tasks based on the LLaVA-1.5-7B and -13B models. Experimental results demonstrate that RoVRM consistently outperforms traditional VRMs.  Furthermore, our three-phase progressive training and preference data selection approaches can yield consistent performance gains over ranking-based alignment techniques, such as direct preference optimization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the scarcity of visual preference data for training visual reward models (VRMs) to align large vision-language models (LVLMs) with human preferences, reducing hallucination. It proposes RoVRM, which leverages auxiliary textual preference data via three-phase progressive training and optimal transport-based preference data selection. Experiments on LLaVA-1.5-7B and -13B show RoVRM outperforms traditional VRMs and provides consistent gains over direct preference optimization. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大规模视觉语言模型（LVLMs）因视觉偏好数据稀缺而难以与人类偏好对齐的问题，以减少幻觉生成。提出一种鲁棒视觉奖励模型（RoVRM），通过三阶段渐进训练和基于最优传输的偏好数据选择，利用辅助文本偏好数据来缓解数据稀缺。在LLaVA-1.5-7B和-13B上的实验表明，RoVRM优于传统VRM，并在与直接偏好优化等排名对齐技术相比时获得一致的性能提升。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Probing Preference Representations: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation and Analysis Method for Reward Models
papers.abstract: Previous methods evaluate reward models by testing them on a fixed pairwise ranking test set, but they typically do not provide performance information on each preference dimension. In this work, we address the evaluation challenge of reward models by probing preference representations. To confirm the effectiveness of this evaluation method, we construct a Multi-dimensional Reward Model Benchmark (MRMBench), a collection of six probing tasks for different preference dimensions. We design it to favor and encourage reward models that better capture preferences across different dimensions. Furthermore, we introduce an analysis method, inference-time probing, which identifies the dimensions used during the reward prediction and enhances its interpretability. Through extensive experiments, we find that MRMBench strongly correlates with LLM alignment performance, supporting it as a reliable reference for developing advanced reward models. By analyzing the evaluation results on MRMBench, we reveal that reward models struggle to simultaneously capture preferences across multiple dimensions, highlighting the potential of multi-objective optimization in reward modeling. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the proposed inference-time probing method provides a reliable metric for assessing the confidence of reward predictions, leading to improved alignment of large language models.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the evaluation of reward models by introducing MRMBench, a multi-dimensional benchmark with six probing tasks to assess performance across different preference dimensions, and an inference-time probing method that identifies which dimensions are used during reward prediction, enhancing interpretability. MRMBench is shown to correlate strongly with LLM alignment performance, and through experiments, the authors find that reward models struggle to simultaneously capture preferences across multiple dimensions, highlighting a potential limitation. The proposed inference-time probing also provides a reliable metric for assessing reward prediction confidence, leading to improved alignment of large language models. This work reveals a fragility in current reward modeling, as the inability to robustly handle multi-dimensional preferences could undermine the reliability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对奖励模型评估问题，提出了MRMBench，一个包含六个探测任务的多维度基准，用于评估不同偏好维度的性能，以及一种推理时探测方法，识别奖励预测中使用的维度以增强可解释性。实验表明，MRMBench与LLM对齐性能强相关，作者发现奖励模型难以同时捕捉多维度偏好，揭示了当前方法的局限性。所提出的推理时探测方法还为评估奖励预测置信度提供了可靠指标，从而提升了大语言模型的对齐效果。这项工作揭示了奖励模型在捕获多维偏好方面的脆弱性，这可能影响后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: ConfGuard: A Simple and Effective Backdoor Detection for Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Backdoor attacks pose a significant threat to Large Language Models (LLMs), where adversaries can embed hidden triggers to manipulate LLM's outputs. 
Most existing defense methods, primarily designed for classification tasks, are ineffective against the autoregressive nature and vast output space of LLMs, thereby suffering from poor performance and high latency. 
To address these limitations, we investigate the behavioral discrepancies between benign and backdoored LLMs in output space.
We identify a critical phenomenon which we term sequence lock: a backdoored model generates the target sequence with abnormally high and consistent confidence compared to benign generation. 
Building on this insight, we propose ConfGuard, a lightweight and effective detection method that monitors a sliding window of token confidences to identify sequence lock. 
Extensive experiments demonstrate ConfGuard achieves a near 100% true positive rate (TPR) and a negligible false positive rate (FPR) in the vast majority of cases.
Crucially, the ConfGuard enables real-time detection almost without additional latency, making it a practical backdoor defense for real-world LLM deployments.
papers.summary_en: ConfGuard addresses backdoor attacks on LLMs, where hidden triggers manipulate outputs, exploiting the limitations of existing classification-focused defenses. It proposes a detection method based on 'sequence lock', where backdoored models exhibit abnormally high and consistent confidence when generating target sequences, by monitoring a sliding window of token confidences. Experiments show near perfect true positive rates and negligible false positives with real-time detection, adding almost no latency. This work directly strengthens post-training safety alignment against backdoor-based bypasses, demonstrating a practical hardening approach to improve robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本研究针对大语言模型的后门攻击问题，提出了ConfGuard检测方法，利用后门模型生成目标序列时置信度异常高且一致的现象（序列锁），通过滑动窗口监控token置信度实现检测。实验表明，该方法在大多数情况下能实现近乎100%的检出率和极低误报率，且几乎无额外延迟。该工作通过检测可绕过安全对齐的后门触发，直接增强了对齐鲁棒性，为解决后训练对齐脆弱性问题提供了实用加固方案。

papers.title: AgentSeer: Visualizing and Evaluating Temporal Actions in Agentic AI Systems
papers.abstract: We present AgentSeer, an interactive observability framework for agentic AI systems. Unlike conventional tracing tools that expose raw spans or model-centric metrics, AgentSeer introduces a dual graph decomposition constructed through a deterministic rule-based parser: a temporal action graph, where each prompt or tool invocation is represented as a distinct action, and a component graph capturing architectural relations among agents, tools, and memory modules. Beyond visualization, AgentSeer enables action-level red teaming, where jailbreak payloads are systematically attached to every action node (including agent messages, tool calls, and memory retrievals) to uncover vulnerabilities invisible to model-level testing. Our demonstration features a six-agent hierarchical testbed with interactive visualization and deployment-oriented safety evaluation applied directly on the same prompts and contexts, systematically revealing high-risk interactions, context-dependent vulnerabilities, and emergent behaviors. By combining structured decomposition, automated red teaming, and rule-based reliability, AgentSeer establishes a safety-first methodology for observability in multi-agent AI.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of safety evaluation in complex multi-agent AI systems, where conventional model-level testing fails to capture vulnerabilities arising from agent interactions. The authors propose AgentSeer, an observability framework that decomposes agentic systems into temporal action and component graphs, enabling systematic red teaming by attaching jailbreak payloads to every action node. Demonstrated on a six-agent testbed, AgentSeer reveals high-risk interactions and context-dependent vulnerabilities invisible to model-centric approaches. By exposing how composition can undermine safety, it highlights the fragility of post-training alignment when models are deployed in interconnected, tool-augmented environments.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多智能体AI系统中的安全评估难题，即在模型层级测试无法发现由智能体交互产生的漏洞。作者提出了AgentSeer，一个将智能体系统分解为时间动作图和组件图的可观测性框架，并通过对每个动作节点附加越狱载荷，实现了系统性的红队测试。在一个六智能体测试平台上，AgentSeer揭示了模型中心化方法无法察觉的高风险交互和上下文相关漏洞。通过展示组合如何破坏安全性，本文揭示了当模型部署于互联且工具增强的环境时，后训练对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: MMJ-Bench: A Comprehensive Study on Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses for Vision Language Models
papers.abstract: As deep learning advances, Large Language Models (LLMs) and their multimodal counterparts, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have shown exceptional performance in many real-world tasks. However, VLMs face significant security challenges, such as jailbreak attacks, where attackers attempt to bypass the model’s safety alignment to elicit harmful responses. The threat of jailbreak attacks on VLMs arises from both the inherent vulnerabilities of LLMs and the multiple information channels that VLMs process. While various attacks and defenses have been proposed, there is a notable gap in unified and comprehensive evaluations, as each method is evaluated on different dataset and metrics, making it impossible to compare the effectiveness of each method. To address this gap, we introduce MMJ-Bench, a unified pipeline for evaluating jailbreak attacks and defense techniques for VLMs. Through extensive experiments, we assess the effectiveness of various attack methods against SoTA VLMs and evaluate the impact of defense mechanisms on both defense effectiveness and model utility for normal tasks. Our comprehensive evaluation contribute to the field by offering a unified and systematic evaluation framework and the first public-available benchmark for VLM jailbreak research. We also demonstrate several insightful findings that highlights directions for future studies.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of unified benchmarks for evaluating jailbreak attacks and defenses on Vision-Language Models (VLMs). It proposes MMJ-Bench, a comprehensive evaluation pipeline and the first publicly available benchmark for VLM jailbreak research. Extensive experiments assess various attack methods against state-of-the-art VLMs and evaluate defense mechanisms in terms of both security and model utility. This work directly contributes to the fragility question by demonstrating that VLM safety alignment can be systematically tested and bypassed through multiple modalities, highlighting directions for future robustification.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉语言模型（VLM）越狱攻击与防御研究缺乏统一评估的问题，提出了MMJ-Bench，一个统一的评估框架和首个公开基准。通过大量实验，评估了多种攻击方法对最先进VLM的效果，并检验了防御机制在安全性和模型效用上的表现。该工作直接回应了安全对齐脆弱性问题，表明多模态下的安全防护可被系统性测试与绕过，为未来防御研究指明了方向。

papers.title: SDEval: Safety Dynamic Evaluation for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), the safety concerns of their outputs have earned significant attention. Although numerous datasets have been proposed, they may become outdated with MLLM advancements and are susceptible to data contamination issues. To address these problems, we propose SDEval, the first safety dynamic evaluation framework to controllably adjust the distribution and complexity of safety benchmarks. Specifically, SDEval mainly adopts three dynamic strategies: text, image, and text-image dynamics to generate new samples from original benchmarks. We first explore the individual effects of text and image dynamics on model safety. Then, we find that injecting text dynamics into images can further impact safety, and conversely, injecting image dynamics into text also leads to safety risks. SDEval is general enough to be applied to various existing safety and even capability benchmarks. Experiments across safety benchmarks, MLLMGuard and VLSBench, and capability benchmarks, MMBench and MMVet, show that SDEval significantly influences evaluation results, mitigates data contamination, and exposes safety limitations of MLLMs.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the problem of outdated and contamination-prone safety benchmarks for multimodal LLMs. The paper proposes SDEval, a framework that dynamically generates new evaluation samples via text, image, and cross-modal adjustments. Experiments on safety and capability benchmarks show that SDEval significantly alters outcomes, mitigates contamination, and exposes safety vulnerabilities. This directly demonstrates the fragility of safety alignment, as dynamic perturbations easily bypass protections.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了现有多模态大语言模型安全基准因模型进步而过时且易受数据污染影响的问题。提出SDEval框架，通过文本、图像及图文交叉的动态调整来生成新评估样本。在安全基准和能力基准上的实验表明，SDEval显著影响评估结果，缓解数据污染，并暴露了安全脆弱性。该论文直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，表明动态扰动可轻易突破安全防线。

papers.title: STAR-1: Safer Alignment of Reasoning LLMs with 1K Data
papers.abstract: This paper introduces STAR-1, a high-quality, just-1k-scale safety dataset specifically designed for large reasoning models (LRMs) like DeepSeek-R1. Built on three core principles --- diversity, deliberative reasoning, and rigorous filtering --- STAR-1 aims to address the critical needs for safety alignment in LRMs. Specifically, we begin by integrating existing open-source safety datasets from diverse sources. Then, we curate safety policies to generate policy-grounded deliberative reasoning samples. Lastly, we apply a GPT-4o-based safety scoring system to select training examples aligned with best practices. Experimental results show that fine-tuning LRMs with STAR-1 leads to an average 40% improvement in safety performance across four benchmarks, while only incurring a marginal decrease (e.g., an average of 1.1%) in reasoning ability measured across five reasoning tasks. Extensive ablation studies further validate the importance of our design principles in constructing STAR-1 and analyze its efficacy across both LRMs and traditional LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of safety alignment for large reasoning models (LRMs) by introducing STAR-1, a high-quality safety dataset of only 1,000 examples. The dataset is constructed by integrating diverse open-source safety data, generating policy-grounded deliberative reasoning samples, and filtering with a GPT-4o-based safety scoring system. Fine-tuning LRMs on STAR-1 yields an average 40% safety improvement across four benchmarks with only a 1.1% average drop in reasoning performance, and ablation studies validate the importance of its design principles. While STAR-1 advances the methodology for safer alignment, the paper does not directly investigate whether such alignment is robust or easily bypassed by adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过引入STAR-1这一仅含1000条高质量示例的安全数据集，解决大型推理模型的安全对齐问题。该数据集通过整合多样化开源安全数据、生成基于策略的审慎推理样本，并利用GPT-4o安全评分系统过滤而构建。在四个基准测试上，对LRM微调STAR-1可平均提升40%安全性，而推理性能仅平均下降1.1%，消融研究验证了其设计原则的有效性。尽管STAR-1推进了更安全对齐的方法论，但本文并未直接考察这种对齐是否稳健或易被对抗攻击绕过。

papers.title: HumorReject: Decoupling LLM Safety from Refusal Prefix via a Little Humor
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) commonly rely on explicit refusal prefixes for safety, making them vulnerable to prefix injection attacks. We introduce HumorReject, a novel data-driven approach that reimagines LLM safety by decoupling it from refusal prefixes through humor as an indirect refusal strategy. Rather than explicitly rejecting harmful instructions, HumorReject responds with contextually appropriate humor that naturally defuses potentially dangerous requests. Our approach effectively addresses common "over-defense" issues while demonstrating superior robustness against various attack vectors. Our findings suggest that improvements in training data design can be as important as the alignment algorithm itself in achieving effective LLM safety.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety mechanisms that rely on explicit refusal prefixes, which are easily bypassed by prefix injection attacks and cause over-defense. It proposes HumorReject, a data-driven approach that uses humor as an indirect refusal strategy to decouple safety from refusal prefixes. Evaluations show HumorReject mitigates over-defense and achieves superior robustness against various attack vectors, highlighting the importance of training data design. This work directly engages with the fragility question by demonstrating that a key source of brittleness—explicit refusal prefixes—can be eliminated, thereby strengthening post-training safety alignment against adversarial bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了依赖显式拒绝前缀的LLM安全机制的脆弱性问题，这些前缀易受前缀注入攻击并导致过度防御。它提出了HumorReject，一种数据驱动的方法，使用幽默作为间接拒绝策略，将安全性与拒绝前缀解耦。评估表明，HumorReject缓解了过度防御，并对各种攻击向量表现出优越的鲁棒性，强调了训练数据设计的重要性。本研究直接回应了安全性对齐的脆弱性问题，证明通过消除显式拒绝前缀这一主要脆弱性来源，可以加强后训练安全对齐，抵御对抗性绕过。

papers.title: Self-Evolutionary Large Language Models Through Uncertainty-Enhanced Preference Optimization
papers.abstract:
Iterative preference optimization has recently become one of the de-facto training paradigms for large language models (LLMs), but the performance is still underwhelming due to too much noisy preference data yielded in the loop. To combat this issue, we present an Uncertainty-enhanced Preference Optimization (UPO) framework to make the LLM self-evolve with reliable feedback. The key idea is mitigating the noisy preference pairs derived from the current policy and reward models by performing pair-wise uncertainty estimation and judiciously reliable feedback sampling. To reach this goal, we thus introduce an estimator model, which incorporates Monte Carlo (MC) dropout in Bayesian neural network (BNN) to perform uncertainty estimation for the batch of preference pairs. Compared to the existing methods that directly filter generated responses based on the reward score, the estimator focuses on the model uncertainty in a
pair-wise manner and effectively bypasses the confirmation bias problem of the reward model. Additionally, we also propose an uncertainty-enhanced self-evolution algorithm to better improve the LLM robustly align with these reliable feedback data. Extensive experiments over multiple benchmarks demonstrate our framework substantially improves the performance of iterative preference optimization.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of noisy preference data in iterative preference optimization for LLMs, which leads to suboptimal performance. It proposes the Uncertainty-enhanced Preference Optimization (UPO) framework, which uses an estimator with Monte Carlo dropout in a Bayesian neural network to perform pair-wise uncertainty estimation and selectively sample reliable feedback. Evaluated on multiple benchmarks, UPO substantially improves iterative preference optimization performance. This paper advances alignment methodology by enhancing the reliability of preference optimization, but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对迭代偏好优化中偏好数据噪声大导致性能不佳的问题，提出不确定性增强偏好优化（UPO）框架，利用贝叶斯神经网络中的蒙特卡洛丢弃法进行成对不确定性估计，从而筛选可靠反馈。在多个基准上的实验显著提升了迭代偏好优化效果。本文通过提高偏好优化可靠性推进了对齐方法论，但未直接触及训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Joint-GCG: Unified Gradient-Based Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving relevant documents from external corpora before generating responses. This approach significantly expands LLM capabilities by leveraging vast, up-to-date external knowledge. However, this reliance on external knowledge makes RAG systems vulnerable to corpus poisoning attacks that manipulate generated outputs via poisoned document injection. Existing poisoning attack strategies typically treat the retrieval and generation stages as disjointed, limiting their effectiveness. We propose Joint-GCG, the first framework to unify gradient-based attacks across both retriever and generator models through three innovations: (1) Cross-Vocabulary Projection for aligning embedding spaces, (2) Gradient Tokenization Alignment for synchronizing token-level gradient signals, and (3) Adaptive Weighted Fusion for dynamically balancing attacking objectives. Evaluations demonstrate that Joint-GCG achieves at most 25% and an average of 5% higher attack success rate than previous methods across multiple retrievers and generators. While optimized under a white-box assumption, the generated poisons show unprecedented transferability to unseen models. Joint-GCG's innovative unification of gradient-based attacks across retrieval and generation stages fundamentally reshapes our understanding of vulnerabilities within RAG systems.
papers.summary_en: Joint-GCG addresses the vulnerability of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to corpus poisoning attacks, where previous methods treated retrieval and generation as disjoint stages. It proposes the first unified gradient-based attack framework that jointly optimizes adversarial poisons against both the retriever and generator using cross-vocabulary projection, gradient tokenization alignment, and adaptive weighted fusion. Experiments on multiple retrievers and generators show Joint-GCG achieves an average 5% higher attack success rate than prior methods, with up to 25% improvement, and strong transferability to unseen models. This reveals a new attack surface, demonstrating that safety alignment in RAG systems is fragile and can be bypassed through coordinated poisoning of external knowledge.
papers.summary_zh: Joint-GCG 解决了检索增强生成（RAG）系统因语料库投毒而易受攻击的问题，以往方法将检索与生成分离处理。该工作提出首个统一的基于梯度的攻击框架，通过跨词汇投影、梯度分词对齐和自适应加权融合，联合优化针对检索器和生成器的对抗性毒化样本。在多种检索器和生成器上的实验表明，Joint-GCG 较先前方法平均攻击成功率提升 5%，最高提升 25%，并对未见模型展现出强迁移性。这揭示了 RAG 系统中安全对齐的脆弱性，表明通过协同毒化外部知识可绕过防御。

papers.title: Reasoning Shapes Alignment: Investigating Cultural Alignment in Large Reasoning Models with Cultural Norms
papers.abstract: The advanced reasoning capabilities of Large Reasoning Models enable them to thoroughly understand and apply safety policies through deliberate thought processes, thereby improving the models' safety.  Beyond safety, these models must also be able to reflect the diverse range of human values across various cultures. This paper presents the Cultural Norm-based Cultural Alignment (CNCA) framework, which enables models to leverage their powerful reasoning ability to align with cultural norms. Specifically, we propose three methods to automatically mine cultural norms from limited survey data and explore ways to effectively utilize these norms for improving cultural alignment. Two alignment paradigms are examined: an in-context alignment method, where cultural norms are explicitly integrated into the user context, and a fine-tuning-based method, which internalizes norms through enhanced Chain-of-Thought training data. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of these methods, highlighting that models with stronger reasoning capabilities benefit more from cultural norm mining and utilization. Our findings emphasize the potential for reasoning models to better reflect diverse human values through culturally informed alignment strategies.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large reasoning models with diverse cultural values, beyond just safety. It proposes the Cultural Norm-based Cultural Alignment (CNCA) framework, which automatically mines cultural norms from limited survey data and integrates them via in-context alignment or fine-tuning with Chain-of-Thought data. Experiments show that both methods improve cultural alignment, and models with stronger reasoning capabilities benefit more from norm utilization. While this work advances alignment methodology, it does not directly assess the robustness or fragility of safety alignment—it focuses on expanding alignment to cultural domains.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型推理模型在安全对齐之外还需反映多元文化价值的问题，提出了基于文化规范的文化对齐（CNCA）框架。该框架从有限调查数据中自动挖掘文化规范，并通过上下文对齐或基于思维链的微调方式将其融入模型。实验表明两种方法均能提升文化对齐水平，且推理能力更强的模型受益更多。尽管该工作推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性，而是专注于将对齐扩展到文化领域。

papers.title: RTP-LX: Can LLMs Evaluate Toxicity in Multilingual Scenarios?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and small language models (SLMs) are being adopted at remarkable speed, although their safety still remains a serious concern. With the advent of multilingual S/LLMs, the question now becomes a matter of scale: can we expand multilingual safety evaluations of these models with the same velocity at which they are deployed? To this end, we introduce RTP-LX, a human-transcreated and human-annotated corpus of toxic prompts and outputs in 28 languages. RTP-LX follows participatory design practices, and a portion of the corpus is especially designed to detect culturally-specific toxic language. We evaluate 10 S/LLMs on their ability to detect toxic content in a culturally-sensitive, multilingual scenario. We find that, although they typically score acceptably in terms of accuracy, they have low agreement with human judges when scoring holistically the toxicity of a prompt; and have difficulty discerning harm in context-dependent scenarios, particularly with subtle-yet-harmful content (e.g. microaggressions, bias). We release this dataset to contribute to further reduce harmful uses of these models and improve their safe deployment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of scaling multilingual safety evaluations for large and small language models. It introduces RTP-LX, a human-transcreated and human-annotated corpus of toxic prompts and outputs in 28 languages, designed with participatory practices to include culturally-specific harmful content. Evaluation of 10 S/LLMs shows acceptable classification accuracy but low agreement with human holistic toxicity judgments, with particular difficulty in detecting subtle, context-dependent harm such as microaggressions. This work advances safety evaluation methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多语言安全评估难以规模化的问题，提出了RTP-LX数据集。这是一个覆盖28种语言、经由人工转创与标注的有毒提示和输出语料库，采用参与式设计并包含文化特定有害内容。对10个语言模型的评估表明，它们虽分类准确率尚可，但整体毒性评分与人类判断一致性低，且难以识别微妙且依赖上下文的伤害（如微歧视）。该工作推进了安全评估基准建设，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: SDA: Steering-Driven Distribution Alignment for Open LLMs Without Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), their deployment in real-world applications has become increasingly widespread. LLMs are expected to deliver robust performance across diverse tasks, user preferences, and practical scenarios. However, as demands grow, ensuring that LLMs produce responses aligned with human intent remains a foundational challenge. In particular, aligning model behavior effectively and efficiently during inference, without costly retraining or extensive supervision, is both a critical requirement and a non-trivial technical endeavor. To address the challenge, we propose SDA (Steering-Driven Distribution Alignment), a training-free and model-agnostic alignment framework designed for open-source LLMs. SDA dynamically redistributes model output probabilities based on user-defined alignment instructions, enhancing alignment between model behavior and human intents without fine-tuning. The method is lightweight, resource-efficient, and compatible with a wide range of open-source LLMs. It can function independently during inference or be integrated with training-based alignment strategies. Moreover, SDA supports personalized preference alignment, enabling flexible control over the model’s response behavior. Empirical results demonstrate that SDA consistently improves alignment performance across 8 open-source LLMs with varying scales and diverse origins, evaluated on three key alignment dimensions, helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty (3H). Specifically, SDA achieves average gains of 64.4% in helpfulness, 30% in honesty and 11.5% in harmlessness across the tested models, indicating its effectiveness and generalization across diverse models and application scenarios.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses inference-time alignment of LLMs with human intent without additional training or supervision. It proposes SDA, a training-free, model-agnostic framework that dynamically redistributes output probabilities according to user-defined alignment instructions. Across 8 open-source LLMs, SDA improves helpfulness by 64.4%, honesty by 30%, and harmlessness by 11.5% on average. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question, as it focuses on building a flexible alignment method rather than studying the robustness or vulnera-bility of existing alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决在大语言模型推理过程中无需额外训练即可使其输出与人类意图对齐的挑战。提出了一种无需训练、与模型无关的框架SDA，根据用户定义的对齐指令动态重分布输出概率。在8个开源大语言模型上评估，SDA在帮助性、诚实性和无害性上分别平均提升64.4%、30%和11.5%。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题，主要贡献是提出一种灵活的对齐方法，而非研究现有对齐的鲁棒性或可绕过性。

papers.title: Where to Start Alignment? Diffusion Large Language Model May Demand a Distinct Position
papers.abstract: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a competitive non-autoregressive paradigm due to their unique training and inference approach. However, there is currently a lack of safety study on this novel architecture. In this paper, we present the first analysis of dLLMs' safety performance and propose a novel safety alignment method tailored to their unique generation characteristics. Specifically, we identify a critical asymmetry between the defender and attacker in terms of security. For the defender, we reveal that the middle tokens of the response, rather than the initial ones, are more critical to the overall safety of dLLM outputs; this seems to suggest that aligning middle tokens can be more beneficial to the defender. The attacker, on the contrary, may have limited power to manipulate middle tokens, as we find dLLMs have a strong tendency towards a sequential generation order in practice, forcing the attack to meet this distribution and diverting it from influencing the critical middle tokens. Building on this asymmetry, we introduce Middle-tOken Safety Alignment (MOSA), a novel method that directly aligns the model's middle generation with safe refusals exploiting reinforcement learning. We implement MOSA and compare its security performance against eight attack methods on two benchmarks. We also test the utility of MOSA-aligned dLLM on coding, math, and general reasoning. The results strongly prove the superiority of MOSA.
papers.summary_en: This paper conducts the first safety analysis of diffusion large language models (dLLMs), revealing that middle response tokens, rather than initial ones, are critical for overall safety. It proposes MOSA, a method that uses reinforcement learning to align these middle tokens with safe refusals. Evaluated against eight attack methods on two benchmarks, MOSA-aligned dLLMs exhibit superior security while maintaining strong utility in coding, math, and reasoning tasks. The findings directly address the fragility of safety alignment by demonstrating that alignment in dLLMs must be strategically targeted at middle tokens to be robust, challenging the assumption that initial token alignment suffices.
papers.summary_zh: 本文首次分析扩散大语言模型的安全性，揭示响应中间标记而非起始标记对整体安全更关键。提出MOSA方法，利用强化学习将中间生成与安全拒绝对齐。在两个基准上对抗8种攻击方法，MOSA对齐后模型安全性更优，同时保持编码、数学和通用推理能力。该工作表明，扩散LLM的对齐脆弱性源于错误的对齐位置，通过集中对齐中间标记可提升鲁棒性，直接回应了后训练安全对齐是否脆弱的问题。

papers.title: LLM Safety in Judicial AI: A Stress Test of Social Media Influence on Real-World Judgments
papers.short_title: Social Media Stress Test: Judicial LLMs
papers.abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into judicial decision-making demands rigorous safety examination against non-legal influences. This paper presents a novel stress test where we evaluate LLM-generated labor dispute outcomes by introducing social media sentiment as an external pressure, critically comparing them against 10,000 real-world court judgments from China Judgments Online (CJOL). Our findings reveal significant LLM safety vulnerabilities: models exhibit inherent deviations from real rulings, and public opinion substantially amplifies these discrepancies, leading to unstable and often inflated compensation predictions. Furthermore, these safety risks are compounded across low-skilled occupational categories and emotionally charged topics. This study uncovers critical threats to judicial integrity and public trust, underscoring the urgent need for robust safeguards against non-legal influences in AI legal systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety when used for judicial decision-making under non-legal influences like social media sentiment. It proposes a stress test that introduces social media sentiment as external pressure and compares LLM-generated labor dispute outcomes against 10,000 real Chinese court judgments. Evaluations on multiple LLMs reveal significant deviations from real rulings, with public opinion amplifying discrepancies, especially in low-skilled occupations and emotional topics. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by exposing a new attack surface where non-legal influences easily bypass safeguards, supporting the SoK's central question on alignment robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型在司法决策中面对社交媒体情绪等非法律影响时的安全脆弱性。它提出一种压力测试方法，将社交媒体情绪作为外部压力，并将大语言模型生成的劳动争议结果与中国裁判文书网上的10,000份真实判决进行对比。在多模型评估中，大语言模型显著偏离真实判决，且公众意见进一步放大偏差，在低技能职业和情绪化话题中风险更高。这项工作揭示了后训练安全对齐在面对非法律影响时的脆弱性，表明对齐模块可被轻易绕过，直接回应了关于对齐鲁棒性的核心问题。

papers.title: GRAM-R²: Self-Training Generative Foundation Reward Models for Reward Reasoning
papers.abstract: Major progress in reward modeling over recent years has been driven by a paradigm shift from task-specific designs to generalist reward models. Despite this trend, developing effective reward models remains a fundamental challenge: the heavy reliance on large-scale labeled preference data. Pre-training on abundant unlabeled data offers a promising direction, but existing approaches fall short in instilling explicit reasoning capabilities into reward models. To bridge this gap, we propose a self-training approach that can leverage unlabeled data to scale up reward reasoning in reward models. Based on this approach, we develop GRAM-R² a generative reward model trained to produce not only preference labels but also accompanying reward rationales. GRAM-R² can serve as a foundation model for reward reasoning and can be applied to a wide range of tasks with minimal or no additional fine-tuning. It can support downstream applications such as policy optimization and task-specific reward tuning. Experiments on response ranking, task adaptation, and reinforcement learning from human feedback demonstrate that GRAM-R² consistently delivers strong performance, outperforming several strong discriminative and generative baselines.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of developing effective reward models without large-scale labeled preference data, instead leveraging unlabeled data to enhance reward reasoning. It proposes a self-training approach that scales up reward reasoning, resulting in GRAM-R², a generative reward model that produces both preference labels and rationales. Evaluated on response ranking, task adaptation, and RLHF, GRAM-R² consistently outperforms strong discriminative and generative baselines. This work advances reward modeling methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决在没有大规模标注偏好数据的情况下开发有效奖励模型的挑战，利用无标签数据增强奖励推理能力。它提出了一种自我训练方法，扩展奖励推理，得到GRAM-R²，一种生成式奖励模型，输出偏好标签和推理依据。在响应排序、任务适应和人类反馈强化学习评估中，GRAM-R²持续优于多种强大的判别式和生成式基线。本研究推进了奖励建模方法，但并未直接解决后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Multi-Value Alignment for LLMs via Value Decorrelation and Extrapolation
papers.abstract:
With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), aligning them with human values for safety and ethics has become a critical challenge.
This problem is especially challenging when multiple, potentially conflicting human values must be considered and balanced.
Although several variants of existing alignment methods (such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)) have been proposed to address multi-value alignment, they suffer from notable limitations: 1) they are often unstable and inefficient in multi-value optimization; and 2) they fail to effectively handle value conflicts. 
As a result, these approaches typically struggle to achieve optimal trade-offs when aligning multiple values.

To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework called Multi-Value Alignment (MVA).
It mitigates alignment degradation caused by parameter interference among diverse human values by minimizing their mutual information.
Furthermore, we propose a value extrapolation strategy to efficiently explore the Pareto frontier, thereby constructing a set of LLMs with diverse value preferences.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that MVA consistently outperforms existing baselines in aligning LLMs with multiple human values.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with multiple, potentially conflicting human values. It proposes the Multi-Value Alignment (MVA) framework, which decorrelates values by minimizing mutual information to reduce parameter interference and uses value extrapolation to efficiently explore the Pareto frontier. Extensive experiments show MVA outperforms existing baselines in multi-value alignment. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐多个可能冲突的人类价值观这一挑战，提出多价值对齐框架MVA。该框架通过最小化互信息实现价值去相关，减少参数干扰，并采用价值外推策略高效探索帕累托前沿。实验表明MVA在多价值对齐中优于现有基线。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: The Emotional Baby Is Truly Deadly: Does Your Multimodal Large Reasoning Model Have Emotional Flattery Towards Humans?
papers.abstract:
Multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) have advanced visual-textual integration, enabling sophisticated human-AI interaction. While prior work has exposed MLRMs to visual jailbreaks, it remains underexplored how their reasoning capabilities reshape the security landscape under adversarial inputs. To fill this gap, we conduct a systematic security assessment of MLRMs and uncover a security-reasoning paradox: 
although deeper reasoning boosts cross‑modal risk recognition, it also creates cognitive blind spots that adversaries can exploit. 
We observe that MLRMs oriented toward human-centric service are highly susceptible to users' emotional cues during the deep-thinking stage, often overriding safety protocols or built‑in safety checks under high emotional intensity.
Inspired by this key insight, we propose EmoAgent, an autonomous adversarial emotion-agent that orchestrates exaggerated affective prompts to hijack reasoning pathways.
Even when visual risks are correctly identified, models can still produce harmful completions through emotional misalignment. We further identify persistent high-risk failure modes in transparent deep-thinking scenarios, such as MLRMs generating harmful reasoning masked behind seemingly safe responses. These failures expose misalignments between internal inference and surface-level behavior, eluding existing content-based safeguards. To quantify these risks, we introduce three metrics: (1) Risk-Reasoning Stealth Score (RRSS) for harmful reasoning beneath benign outputs; (2) Risk-Visual Neglect Rate (RVNR) for unsafe completions despite visual risk recognition; and (3) Refusal Attitude Inconsistency (RAIC) for evaluating refusal unstability under prompt variants.
Extensive experiments on advanced MLRMs demonstrate the effectiveness of EmoAgent and reveal deeper emotional cognitive misalignments in model safety.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates emotional flattery as an attack vector against multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs), revealing that their human-centric orientation makes them susceptible to emotional cues that can override safety protocols. The authors propose EmoAgent, an autonomous adversarial agent that orchestrates exaggerated emotional prompts to exploit cognitive blind spots in MLRMs' deep-thinking stage. Through extensive experiments on advanced MLRMs, EmoAgent is shown to effectively induce harmful completions even when visual risks are recognized, and new metrics quantify stealth, visual neglect, and refusal inconsistency. These findings highlight a critical fragility in post-training safety alignment, as emotional misalignment can subvert built-in safeguards, revealing a gap between internal reasoning and surface-level behavior.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了针对多模态大推理模型（MLRMs）的情感奉承攻击，揭示了其易受情感线索影响并可能覆盖安全协议的问题。作者提出EmoAgent，一种自主对抗性情感代理，通过夸张情感提示劫持推理路径。大量实验表明，EmoAgent能有效诱导有害输出，并通过新指标量化了推理隐身、视觉忽视和拒绝不一致等风险。这些发现揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，情感错位可颠覆安全机制，暴露内部推理与表层行为的脱节。

papers.title: When Human Preferences Flip: An Instance-Dependent Robust Loss for RLHF
papers.abstract: Quality of datasets plays an important role in large language model (LLM) alignment. In collecting human feedback, however, preference flipping is ubiquitous and causes corruption in data annotation; the issue necessitates the alignment algorithms with improved robustness against potential flipped pairs. To this end, this paper introduces a Flipping-Aware Direct Preference Optimization (FA-DPO) algorithm tailored to preference flipping from a reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) perspective.  We dissect the inherent human intention model and the preference flipping mechanism introduced by external factors as two distinct stages; in the latter, we introduce an instance-dependent flipping probability on the basis of the Bradley-Terry (BT) model. Further, by leveraging features relevant to preference annotation, we capture uncertainty in judgments and model preference flipping patterns. In practice, we design a simple yet efficient iterative optimization algorithm compatible with the original RLHF and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithms. In our experiments, we investigate the instance-dependent preference flipping model under multiple circumstances for evaluation of our proposed method, as well as other baseline methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of human preference flipping corrupting datasets in LLM alignment. It proposes Flipping-Aware Direct Preference Optimization (FA-DPO), which models instance-dependent flipping probabilities based on the Bradley-Terry model and leverages annotation-related features to capture uncertainty. Experiments under multiple corruption scenarios demonstrate that FA-DPO improves robustness over baselines. While the paper acknowledges alignment fragility to data noise, it primarily advances alignment methodology rather than directly investigating whether post-training safety alignment is a fragile, easily broken module.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型对齐中人类偏好翻转导致数据受损的问题。提出翻转感知的直接偏好优化（FA-DPO）算法，基于Bradley-Terry模型建模实例依赖的翻转概率，并利用标注相关特征捕捉判断不确定性。在多种数据损坏设置下的实验表明，FA-DPO相比基线方法提升了鲁棒性。该工作隐含地承认了对齐方法对数据噪声的脆弱性，但主要贡献在于改进对齐鲁棒性，未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否为易碎的模块。

papers.title: Attack the Messages, Not the Agents: A Multi-round Adaptive Stealthy Tampering Framework for LLM-MAS
papers.abstract: Large language model-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) effectively accomplish complex and dynamic tasks through inter-agent communication, but this reliance introduces substantial safety vulnerabilities. Existing attack methods targeting LLM-MAS either compromise agent internals or rely on direct and overt persuasion, which limit their effectiveness, adaptability, and stealthiness. In this paper, we propose MAST, a Multi-round Adaptive Stealthy Tampering framework designed to exploit communication vulnerabilities within the system. MAST integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search with Direct Preference Optimization to train an attack policy model that adaptively generates effective multi-round tampering strategies. Furthermore, to preserve stealthiness, we impose dual semantic and embedding similarity constraints during the tampering process. Comprehensive experiments across diverse tasks, communication architectures, and LLMs demonstrate that MAST consistently achieves high attack success rates while significantly enhancing stealthiness compared to baselines. These findings highlight the effectiveness, stealthiness, and adaptability of MAST, underscoring the need for robust communication safeguards in LLM-MAS.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) by targeting inter-agent communication rather than agent internals. It proposes MAST, a framework combining Monte Carlo Tree Search with Direct Preference Optimization to adaptively generate multi-round tampering strategies, with dual semantic and embedding similarity constraints for stealth. Experiments across diverse tasks, architectures, and LLMs show MAST achieves high attack success rates and significantly enhanced stealthiness over baselines. This work reveals a new attack surface in system-level communication, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be bypassed without compromising agents directly, thus underscoring the fragility of safety in multi-agent coordination.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于大语言模型的多智能体系统（LLM-MAS）的安全漏洞，专注于攻击智能体间通信而非内部组件。提出MAST框架，结合蒙特卡洛树搜索与直接偏好优化，自适应生成多轮篡改策略，并通过语义与嵌入相似度双重约束保持隐蔽性。在多种任务、架构和大模型上的实验表明，MAST在保持高攻击成功率的同时，隐蔽性显著优于基线方法。该工作揭示了系统级通信的新攻击面，证明无需直接攻破智能体即可绕过训练后的安全对齐，从而凸显了多智能体协同中安全性的脆弱性。

papers.title: CoSPED: Consistent Soft Prompt Targeted Data Extraction and Defense
papers.abstract: Large language models have gained widespread attention recently, but their potential security vulnerabilities, especially privacy leakage, are also becoming apparent. To test and evaluate for data extraction risks in LLMs, we propose CoSPED, short for Consistent Soft Prompt Targeted Data Extraction and Defense. We introduce several innovative components, including Dynamic Loss, Additive Loss, Common Loss, and Self Consistency Decoding Strategy, and tested to enhance the consistency of the soft prompt tuning process. Through extensive experimentation with various combinations, we achieved an extraction rate of 65.2% at a 50-token prefix comparison. Our comparisons of CoSPED with other reference works confirm our superior extraction rates. We evaluate CoSPED on more scenarios, achieving Pythia model extraction rate of 51.7% and introducing cross-model comparison. Finally, we explore defense through Rank-One Model Editing and achieve a reduction in the extraction rate to 1.6%, which proves that our analysis of extraction mechanisms can directly inform effective mitigation strategies against soft prompt-based attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses data extraction risks in large language models via soft prompt attacks. It proposes CoSPED, which introduces Dynamic Loss, Additive Loss, Common Loss, and a Self Consistency Decoding Strategy to enhance soft prompt tuning consistency. Evaluated on various settings, CoSPED achieves a 65.2% extraction rate at 50-token prefix comparison, and 51.7% on Pythia; a Rank-One Model Editing defense reduces extraction to 1.6%. This work primarily presents a new extraction attack and defense, rather than directly studying the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型中通过软提示攻击产生的数据泄露风险，提出了CoSPED方法，引入动态损失、附加损失、公共损失和自一致性解码策略，以增强软提示调优的一致性。实验在多种设置下评估，50个token前缀比较下提取率达65.2%，在Pythia模型上达51.7%；通过秩一模型编辑防御可将提取率降至1.6%。本文主要提出了一种新的数据提取攻击及防御手段，并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Multi-Faceted Attack: Exposing Cross-Model Vulnerabilities in Defense-Equipped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: The growing misuse of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) has led providers to deploy multiple safeguards—alignment tuning, system prompt, and content moderation. Yet the real-world robustness of these defenses against adversarial attack remains underexplored. We introduce Multi-Faceted Attack (MFA), a framework that systematically uncovers general safety vulnerabilities in leading defense-equipped VLMs, including GPT-4o, Gemini-Pro, and LLaMA 4, etc. Central to MFA is the Attention-Transfer Attack (ATA), which conceals harmful instructions inside a meta task with competing objectives. We offer a theoretical perspective grounded in reward-hacking to explain why such an attack can succeed. To maximize cross-model transfer, we introduce a lightweight transfer-enhancement algorithm combined with a simple repetition strategy that jointly evades both input- and output-level filters—without any model-specific fine-tuning. We empirically show that adversarial images optimized for one vision encoder transfer broadly to unseen VLMs, indicating that shared visual representations create a cross-model safety vulnerability. Combined, MFA reaches a 58.5% overall attack success rate, consistently outperforming existing methods. Notably, on state-of-the-art commercial models, MFA achieves a 52.8% success rate, outperforming the second-best attack by 34%. These findings challenge the perceived robustness of current defensive mechanisms, systematically expose general safety loopholes within defense-equipped VLMs, and offer a practical probe for diagnosing and evaluating the safety of VLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the robustness of safety defenses (alignment tuning, system prompts, content moderation) in vision-language models (VLMs) against adversarial attacks, finding that real-world resilience is underexplored. It proposes the Multi-Faceted Attack (MFA) framework, which uses an Attention-Transfer Attack to conceal harmful instructions within a meta-task with competing objectives, plus a transfer-enhancement algorithm and repetition strategy to bypass input and output filters without model-specific fine-tuning. Evaluated on commercial VLMs like GPT-4o, Gemini-Pro, and LLaMA 4, MFA achieves a 58.5% overall attack success rate and 52.8% on commercial models, outperforming the next best attack by 34%. The paper directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment in VLMs, as adversarial images optimized for one vision encoder transfer across models, exposing systematic cross-model safety vulnerabilities.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了视觉语言模型（VLM）中安全防御（对齐微调、系统提示、内容审核）对对抗攻击的鲁棒性，指出其实际安全性尚未充分探索。它提出了多面攻击（MFA）框架，核心是注意力转移攻击，将有害指令隐藏于具有竞争目标的元任务中，并结合迁移增强算法和重复策略，在无需模型特化微调的情况下绕过输入和输出过滤器。在 GPT-4o、Gemini-Pro 和 LLaMA 4 等商业模型上评估，MFA 总体攻击成功率达 58.5%，在商业模型上为 52.8%，比第二名攻击高出 34%。该工作直接表明 VLM 的后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，因为针对一个视觉编码器优化的对抗图像能跨模型迁移，暴露了系统性的跨模型安全漏洞。

papers.title: ShieldRAG: Safeguarding Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Untrusted Knowledge Bases
papers.short_title: ShieldRAG: Safe RAG from Untrusted KBs
papers.abstract:
Open knowledge bases (e.g., websites) are widely adopted in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to provide supplementary knowledge (e.g., latest information). 
However, such sources inevitably contain biased or harmful content, and incorporating these untrusted contents into the RAG process introduces significant safety risks, including the degradation of LLM performance and the potential generation of harmful outputs.
Recent studies have shown that this vulnerability can be further amplified by adversarial poisoning attacks specifically targeting the knowledge sources.
Most existing methods primarily emphasize improving the accuracy and efficiency of RAG systems, usually overlooking these critical safety concerns.
In this paper, we propose a safety-aware retrieval framework (ShieldRAG) designed to augment language model generation by jointly optimizing for both relevance and safety in the retrieved knowledge content.
The core idea of ShieldRAG is to transfer the safety knowledge implicitly encoded in powerful LLMs into the retriever model through an adversarial knowledge alignment mechanism.
This can empower the retriever with the safety awareness, and adapt to the diverse and unknown distribution of unsafe content encountered in practical scenarios.
We evaluate ShieldRAG on seven real-world datasets using five widely-used LLMs and two state-of-the-art poisoning attack strategies. 
Experimental results show that our method substantially improves the robustness of RAG systems against unsafe knowledge sources, while maintaining competitive performance in terms of generation accuracy and efficiency.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses safety risks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) when incorporating untrusted knowledge bases, such as biased or harmful content and adversarial poisoning attacks. It proposes ShieldRAG, a safety-aware retrieval framework that transfers safety knowledge from large language models to the retriever via adversarial knowledge alignment, simultaneously optimizing for both relevance and safety. Evaluated across seven real-world datasets, five LLMs, and two poisoning attacks, ShieldRAG significantly improves robustness against unsafe sources while maintaining competitive generation accuracy and efficiency. This paper contributes a defense mechanism for RAG safety but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment in LLMs.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了检索增强生成（RAG）系统从不可信知识库中检索时引入的安全风险，包括有害内容和对抗性污染攻击。提出ShieldRAG框架，通过对抗性知识对齐机制将大语言模型中的安全知识迁移到检索器，使其具备安全意识，从而在检索时联合优化相关性和安全性。在七个真实数据集、五种主流大模型和两种攻击策略上的实验表明，ShieldRAG显著提升了RAG系统对不安全知识源的鲁棒性，同时保持了生成准确性和效率。本文主要贡献于构建RAG安全防御方法，并未直接探讨大模型自身安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: MacPrompt: Maraconic-Guided Jailbreak Against Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract:
Text-to-image (T2I) models have raised increasing safety concerns due to their capacity to generate NSFW and other banned objects. To mitigate these risks, safety filters and concept removal techniques have been introduced to block inappropriate prompts or erase sensitive concepts from the models. However, all the existing defense methods are not well prepared to handle diverse adversarial prompts. In this work, we introduce MacPrompt, a novel black-box and cross-lingual attack that reveals previously overlooked vulnerabilities in T2I safety mechanisms. Unlike existing attacks that rely on synonym substitution or prompt obfuscation, MacPrompt constructs macaronic adversarial prompts by performing cross-lingual character-level recombination of harmful terms, enabling fine-grained control over both semantics and appearance. By leveraging this design, MacPrompt crafts prompts with high semantic similarity to the original harmful inputs (up to 0.96) while bypassing major safety filters (up to 100%). More critically, it achieves attack success rates as high as 92% for sex-related content and 90\% for violence, effectively breaking even state-of-the-art concept removal defenses. These results underscore the pressing need to reassess the robustness of existing T2I safety mechanisms against linguistically diverse and fine-grained adversarial strategies.

Warning: This paper includes sensitive examples (e.g., adult, violent, or illegal content). Unsafe images are masked but may still be disturbing.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overlooked vulnerability of text-to-image (T2I) safety mechanisms to cross-lingual and character-level adversarial prompts. It proposes MacPrompt, a black-box jailbreak that constructs macaronic adversarial prompts by recombining harmful terms at the character level across languages, preserving high semantic similarity to original inputs. Evaluation shows MacPrompt bypasses major safety filters up to 100% of the time, with semantic similarity up to 0.96, and achieves attack success rates of 92% for sexual content and 90% for violence, even against state-of-the-art concept removal defenses. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as a simple linguistic recombination can completely subvert defenses, revealing that current alignment strategies are not robust to out-of-distribution adversarial inputs.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对文本到图像模型安全机制在跨语言和字符级对抗提示下未被充分研究的脆弱性，提出了一种名为 MacPrompt 的黑盒越狱方法。该方法通过在字符级别混合多种语言重构有害词汇，生成语义高度相似但能规避过滤器的马卡龙式对抗提示。实验表明，MacPrompt 能以最高 100% 的绕过率突破主流安全过滤器，语义相似度达 0.96，并且对色情和暴力内容的攻击成功率分别高达 92% 和 90%，甚至能够击败最先进的概念移除防御。这直接揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱本质：简单的语言重组即可完全颠覆防御措施，说明当前的对齐策略在面对分布外对抗输入时缺乏鲁棒性。

papers.title: AsFT: Anchoring Safety During LLM Fine-Tuning Within Narrow Safety Basin
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) improves performance but introduces critical safety vulnerabilities: even minimal harmful data can severely compromise safety measures. We observe that perturbations orthogonal to the alignment direction—defined by weight differences between aligned (safe) and unaligned models—rapidly compromise model safety. In contrast, updates along the alignment direction largely preserve it, revealing the parameter space as a "narrow safety basin". To address this, we propose AsFT (Anchoring Safety in Fine-Tuning) to maintain safety by explicitly constraining update directions during fine-tuning. By penalizing updates orthogonal to the alignment direction, AsFT effectively constrains the model within the "narrow safety basin," thus preserving its inherent safety. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets and models show that AsFT reduces harmful behaviors by up to 7.60%, improves task performance by 3.44%, and consistently outperforms existing methods across multiple tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety alignment during fine-tuning, where even minimal harmful data can break safety due to parameter updates orthogonal to the alignment direction. It proposes AsFT, which anchors safety by penalizing weight updates orthogonal to the alignment direction (defined as the difference between an aligned and unaligned model), keeping the model within a narrow safety basin. Experiments on multiple datasets and models show AsFT reduces harmful behaviors by up to 7.60%, improves task performance by 3.44%, and outperforms existing safety-preserving fine-tuning methods. The paper directly contributes to understanding the fragility of post-training safety alignment by revealing a geometric narrow safety basin and providing a mechanistic hardening method, supporting the view that alignment is fragile but can be reinforced with explicit constraints.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型安全对齐在微调过程中的脆弱性，即使极少量有害数据也可能因与对齐方向正交的参数更新而破坏安全性。提出AsFT方法，通过惩罚与对齐方向（即安全模型与非安全模型之间的权重差异）正交的更新，将模型约束在狭窄的安全盆地内，从而锚定安全性。在多个数据集和模型上的实验表明，AsFT将有害行为降低高达7.60%，任务性能提升3.44%，并且优于现有保持安全性的微调方法。该论文通过揭示参数空间中几何上的狭窄安全盆地并提供一种机制性加固方法，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题，表明对齐虽有脆弱性但可通过显式约束加以强化。

papers.title: Exploiting Synergistic Cognitive Biases to Bypass Safety in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities across diverse tasks, yet their safety mechanisms remain susceptible to adversarial exploitation of cognitive biases---systematic deviations from rational judgment. Unlike prior studies focusing on isolated biases, this work highlights the overlooked power of multi-bias interactions in undermining LLM safeguards. Specifically, we propose CognitiveAttack, a novel red-teaming framework that adaptively selects optimal ensembles from 154 human social psychology-defined cognitive biases, engineering them into adversarial prompts to effectively compromise LLM safety mechanisms. Experimental results reveal systemic vulnerabilities across 30 mainstream LLMs, particularly open-source variants. CognitiveAttack achieves a substantially higher attack success rate than the SOTA black-box method PAP (60.1% vs. 31.6%), exposing critical limitations in current defenses. Through quantitative analysis of successful jailbreaks, we further identify vulnerability patterns in safety-aligned LLMs under synergistic cognitive biases, validating multi-bias interactions as a potent yet underexplored attack vector. This work introduces a novel interdisciplinary perspective by bridging cognitive science and LLM safety, paving the way for more robust and human-aligned AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the exploitation of synergistic cognitive biases—interactions among systematic deviations from rational judgment—to bypass LLM safety mechanisms. It proposes CognitiveAttack, a red-teaming framework that adaptively selects from 154 social psychology-defined biases to craft adversarial prompts. In evaluations on 30 LLMs, CognitiveAttack achieves a 60.1% attack success rate compared to 31.6% for the state-of-the-art black-box method PAP, exposing systemic vulnerabilities, especially in open-source models. The work provides direct evidence of fragility in post-training safety alignment by demonstrating a novel, potent attack vector through multi-bias interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对利用协同认知偏见（理性判断的系统性偏差之间的交互）绕过大语言模型安全机制的问题，提出了一种红队框架CognitiveAttack，它自适应地从154种社会心理学定义的偏见中选择组合，并制成对抗提示。在30个主流大语言模型上的评估结果显示，CognitiveAttack的攻击成功率（60.1%）远超当前最优黑盒方法PAP（31.6%），揭示了尤其是开源模型中的系统性漏洞。该研究通过展示多偏见交互这一新型、高效的攻击向量，直接提供了后训练安全对齐脆弱性的证据。

papers.title: SafeR-CLIP: Mitigating NSFW Content in Vision-Language Models While Preserving Pre-Trained Knowledge
papers.abstract: Improving the safety of vision-language models like CLIP via fine-tuning often comes at a steep price, causing significant drops in their generalization performance. We find this trade-off stems from rigid alignment strategies that force unsafe concepts toward single, predefined safe targets, disrupting the model's learned semantic structure. To address this, we propose a proximity-aware approach: redirecting unsafe concepts to their semantically closest safe alternatives to minimize representational change. We introduce SafeR-CLIP, a fine-tuning framework that applies this principle of minimal intervention. SafeR-CLIP successfully reconciles safety and performance, recovering up to 8.0% in zero-shot accuracy over prior methods while maintaining robust safety. To support more rigorous evaluation, we also contribute NSFWCaps, a new benchmark of 1,000 highly-aligned pairs for testing safety under distributional shift. Our work shows that respecting the geometry of pretrained representations is key to achieving safety without sacrificing performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the trade-off between safety and performance in vision-language models like CLIP, where safety fine-tuning often degrades zero-shot accuracy. They propose SafeR-CLIP, a fine-tuning framework that redirects unsafe concepts to semantically nearest safe alternatives, minimizing representational change. Evaluations show SafeR-CLIP recovers up to 8.0% zero-shot accuracy over prior methods while maintaining robust safety, and they contribute the NSFWCaps benchmark for testing under distribution shift. By identifying rigid alignment as the root cause of performance fragility, this work demonstrates that a proximity-aware hardening approach can achieve safety without sacrificing pre-trained knowledge, offering evidence that post-training safety alignment need not be fragile.
