These findings underscore the fragility of post-training safety alignment in multimodal settings, showing that safety awareness is easily compromised and current mitigation strategies are insufficient.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大模型的安全意识问题，即准确识别安全与不安全的多模态内容。提出了MMSafeAware基准，包含29个安全场景下的1500个图文对，涵盖不安全子集和过度安全子集。对9个主流多模态模型评估发现，GPT-4V将36.1%的不安全输入误判为安全，59.9%的良性输入误判为不安全；尝试的三种改进方法（基于提示、视觉对比解码、视觉中心微调）均未取得满意效果。这些结果直接表明多模态场景下后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，安全意识容易被破坏且现有缓解措施不足。

papers.title: What Really Matters in Many-Shot Attacks? An Empirical Study of Long-Context Vulnerabilities in LLMs
papers.short_title: MSJ: Context Length is Primary Factor
papers.abstract: We investigate long-context vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs) through Many-Shot Jailbreaking (MSJ). Our experiments utilize context length of up to 128K tokens. Through comprehensive analysis with various many-shot attack settings with different instruction styles, shot density, topic, and format, we reveal that context length is the primary factor determining attack effectiveness. Critically, we find that successful attacks do not require carefully crafted harmful content. Even repetitive shots or random dummy text can circumvent model safety measures, suggesting fundamental limitations in long-context processing capabilities of LLMs. The safety behavior of well-aligned models becomes increasingly inconsistent with longer contexts. These findings highlight significant safety gaps in context expansion capabilities of LLMs, emphasizing the need for new safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_en: This paper examines long-context vulnerabilities in LLMs via Many-Shot Jailbreaking (MSJ), where many examples are packed into prompts. Through experiments with up to 128K tokens, varying instruction styles, shot density, topic, and format, it finds that context length—not malicious content—is the primary factor enabling attacks. Even repetitive or random text can jailbreak models, showing that safety alignment becomes inconsistent with longer contexts. This directly supports the SoK's fragility question by revealing that post-training safety alignment breaks down as context expands, creating a new attack surface without adversarial content.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过多示例越狱（MSJ）研究大语言模型的长上下文漏洞，将大量示例塞入长提示中。实验使用高达128K tokens，并改变指令风格、示例密度、主题和格式，发现上下文长度而非恶意内容是攻击有效的主要因素。即使重复或随机文本也能越狱，表明安全对齐在长上下文中变得不一致。该论文直接回应了SoK的脆弱性问题，证明后训练安全对齐随着上下文增长而失效，无需对抗性内容即可绕过，揭示了新的攻击面。

papers.title: Safer or Luckier? LLMs as Safety Evaluators Are Not Robust to Artifacts
papers.short_title: LLM Safety Eval Not Robust to Artifacts
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated evaluators to assess the safety of generated content, yet their reliability in this role remains uncertain. This study evaluates a diverse set of 11 LLM judge models across critical safety domains, examining three key aspects: self-consistency in repeated judging tasks, alignment with human judgments, and susceptibility to input artifacts such as apologetic or verbose phrasing. Our findings reveal that biases in LLM judges can significantly distort the final verdict on which content source is safer, undermining the validity of comparative evaluations. Notably, apologetic language artifacts alone can skew evaluator preferences by up to 98\%. Contrary to expectations, larger models do not consistently exhibit greater robustness, while smaller models sometimes show higher resistance to specific artifacts. To mitigate LLM evaluator robustness issues, we investigate jury-based evaluations aggregating decisions from multiple models. Although this approach both improves robustness and enhances alignment to human judgements, artifact sensitivity persists even with the best jury configurations. These results highlight the urgent need for diversified, artifact-resistant methodologies to ensure reliable safety assessments.
papers.summary_en: This paper exposes the unreliability of LLMs as safety evaluators, showing that biases and input artifacts like apologetic language can distort comparative safety verdicts. It evaluates 11 judge models on self-consistency, human alignment, and artifact sensitivity, and explores jury-based aggregation as a mitigation. Key findings include that apologetic phrasing skews preferences by up to 98%, larger models are not consistently more robust, and even best jury configurations remain artifact-sensitive. This directly demonstrates a fragility in the safety evaluation framework: if evaluators are easily fooled by superficial artifacts, the perceived robustness of safety alignment is compromised.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了大型语言模型作为安全评估者的不可靠性，表明偏见和道歉语言等输入伪影可扭曲比较安全裁决。评估了11个评判模型的自一致性、与人类判断对齐及对伪影的敏感性，并探索了基于多数票的聚合方法来缓解。关键发现包括道歉措辞使偏好倾斜高达98%，更大模型并不始终更稳健，且最优多数票配置仍对伪影敏感。这直接证明了安全评估框架的一个脆弱性：若评估者易被表面伪影愚弄，则安全对齐的感知鲁棒性便会受损。

papers.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs
papers.abstract: Most traditional AI safety research has approached AI models as machines and centered on algorithm-focused attacks developed by security experts. As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly common and competent, non-expert users can also impose risks during daily interactions. This paper introduces a new perspective to jailbreak LLMs as human-like communicators, to explore this overlooked intersection between everyday language interaction and AI safety. Specifically, we study how to persuade LLMs to jailbreak them. First, we propose a persuasion taxonomy derived from decades of social science research. Then, we apply the taxonomy to automatically generate interpretable persuasive adversarial prompts (PAP) to jailbreak LLMs. Results show that persuasion significantly increases the jailbreak performance across all risk categories: PAP consistently achieves an attack success rate of over $92\%$ on Llama 2-7b Chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 in $10$ trials, surpassing recent algorithm-focused attacks. On the defense side, we explore various mechanisms against PAP and, found a significant gap in existing defenses, and advocate for more fundamental mitigation for highly interactive LLMs
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overlooked risk of non-expert users jailbreaking LLMs through everyday language interactions. It proposes a persuasion taxonomy from social science to automatically generate Persuasive Adversarial Prompts (PAP). Evaluated on Llama 2-7b Chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4, PAP achieves over 92% attack success rate, surpassing prior algorithm-focused attacks. This paper directly demonstrates fragility of post-training safety alignment by exposing a new attack surface—persuasion—that allows non-expert users to easily bypass protections, underscoring that alignment can be broken through everyday communication.
papers.summary_zh: 本文关注了非专家用户通过日常语言交互越狱大语言模型这一被忽视的风险。它提出了一套源自社会科学的劝导分类法，用以自动生成劝导式对抗提示（PAP）。在Llama 2-7b Chat、GPT-3.5和GPT-4上评估，PAP的攻击成功率超过92%，优于先前基于算法的攻击。本文直接展示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：通过日常交流中的劝导即可轻易绕过保护，揭示了对齐易被攻破的新攻击面。

papers.title: SudoLM: Learning Access Control of Parametric Knowledge with Authorization Alignment
papers.abstract: Existing preference alignment is a one-size-fits-all alignment mechanism, where the part of the large language model (LLM) parametric knowledge with non-preferred features is uniformly blocked to all the users. However, this part of knowledge can be useful to advanced users whose expertise qualifies them to handle these information. The one-size-fits-all alignment mechanism undermines LLM's utility for these qualified users. To address this problem, we propose SudoLM, a framework that lets LLMs learn access control over specific parametric knowledge for users with different credentials via authorization alignment. SudoLM allows authorized users to unlock their access to all the parametric knowledge with an assigned SUDO key while blocking access to non-qualified users. Experiments on two application scenarios demonstrate that SudoLM effectively controls the user's access to the parametric knowledge and maintains its general utility.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of one-size-fits-all alignment, where useful parametric knowledge is uniformly blocked from all users, including qualified ones. It proposes SudoLM, a framework that enables LLMs to learn access control via authorization alignment, allowing authorized users to unlock specific knowledge with a SUDO key. Experiments on two application scenarios show that SudoLM effectively controls access while maintaining general utility. This work advances alignment methodology by personalizing knowledge access, but it does not directly address the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了一刀切对齐机制的局限性，即对所有用户（包括合格用户）统一屏蔽有用的参数知识。它提出了SudoLM框架，让大语言模型通过授权对齐学习访问控制，授权用户可用SUDO密钥解锁特定知识。在两个应用场景上的实验表明，SudoLM能有效控制访问并保持通用性。这项工作通过个性化知识获取推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Small Changes, Big Impact: How Manipulating a Few Neurons Can Drastically Alter LLM Aggression
papers.short_title: Small Changes: Neuron Manipulation in LLMs
papers.abstract: Recent remarkable advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to innovations in various domains such as education, health-care, and finance, while also raising serious concerns that they can be easily misused for malicious purposes. Most previous research has focused primarily on observing how jailbreak attack techniques bypass safety mechanisms like Reinforcement Learning through Human Feedback (RLHF). However, whether there are neurons within LLMs that directly govern aggression has not been sufficiently investigated. To fill this gap, this study identifies specific neurons (“aggression neurons”) closely related to the expression of aggression and systematically analyzes how manipulating them affects the model’s overall aggression. Specifically, using a large-scale synthetic text corpus (aggressive and non-aggressive), we measure the activation frequency of each neuron, then apply masking and activation techniques to quantitatively evaluate changes in aggression by layer and by manipulation ratio. Experimental results show that, in all models, manipulating only a small number of neurons can increase aggression by up to 33%, and the effect is even more extreme when aggression neurons are concentrated in certain layers. Moreover, even models of the same scale exhibit nonlinear changes in aggression patterns, suggesting that simple external safety measures alone may not be sufficient for complete defense.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether specific neurons within LLMs directly govern aggressive behavior, addressing a mechanistic vulnerability in safety alignment. The authors identify 'aggression neurons' by measuring activation frequencies on a synthetic corpus of aggressive and non-aggressive text, then manipulate them via masking or activation to quantify changes in model aggression across layers and manipulation ratios. Experiments show that manipulating only a few neurons can increase aggression by up to 33%, with concentrated effects in certain layers, and even same-scale models exhibit nonlinear aggression patterns. The findings reveal a deep internal fragility: post-training safety alignment can be dramatically undermined by altering a handful of neurons, demonstrating that alignment is not robustly integrated but can be easily broken from within.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大型语言模型内部是否存在直接控制攻击性的特定神经元，揭示了安全对齐的机制性脆弱点。作者通过测量大规模合成语料库（包含攻击性和非攻击性文本）上的神经元激活频率来识别‘攻击性神经元’，然后通过掩蔽或激活技术操纵这些神经元，按层和操纵比例量化模型攻击性的变化。实验表明，仅操纵少量神经元即可使攻击性增加高达33%，且当攻击性神经元集中在某些层时效应更极端，即使相同规模的模型也呈现出非线性的攻击模式变化。这些发现表明，后训练安全对齐具有深层内部脆弱性：改变少数神经元就能极大削弱对齐，说明对齐并非牢固集成，而是可以从内部轻易打破。

papers.title: Agentic Reward Modeling: Integrating Human Preferences with Verifiable Correctness Signals for Reliable Reward Systems
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) are crucial for the training and inference-time scaling up of large language models (LLMs). However, existing reward models primarily focus on human preferences, neglecting verifiable correctness signals which have shown strong potential in training LLMs. In this paper, we propose agentic reward modeling, a reward system that combines reward models with verifiable correctness signals from different aspects to provide reliable rewards. We empirically implement a reward agent, named RewardAgent, that combines human preference rewards with two verifiable signals: factuality and instruction following, to provide more reliable rewards. We conduct comprehensive experiments on existing reward model benchmarks and inference time best-of-n searches on real-world downstream tasks. RewardAgent significantly outperforms vanilla reward models, demonstrating its effectiveness. We further construct training preference pairs using RewardAgent and train an LLM with the DPO objective, achieving superior performance on various NLP benchmarks compared to conventional reward models. Our codes are publicly released to facilitate further research (https://github.com/THU-KEG/Agentic-Reward-Modeling).
papers.summary_en: Existing reward models for LLMs primarily focus on human preferences and overlook verifiable correctness signals. This paper proposes agentic reward modeling, specifically RewardAgent, which combines human preference rewards with verifiable factuality and instruction-following signals. Experiments on reward benchmarks and best-of-n inference demonstrate significant improvements over vanilla reward models, and using RewardAgent-constructed preferences for DPO training leads to superior NLP performance. While this work advances reward reliability, it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有的LLM奖励模型主要关注人类偏好，忽略了可验证的正确性信号。本文提出智能体奖励建模，即RewardAgent，将人类偏好奖励与可验证的事实性和指令遵循信号相结合。在奖励基准和最佳n推理上的实验表明，RewardAgent显著优于普通奖励模型，且使用其构建的偏好对进行DPO训练可获得更优的NLP性能。尽管这项工作提升了奖励可靠性，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak on Text-to-image Models
papers.short_title: Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak on T2I Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have recently achieved remarkable advancements in terms of image quality and fidelity to textual prompts. Concurrently, the safety of such generative models has become an area of growing concern. This work introduces a novel type of jailbreak, which triggers T2I models to generate the image with visual text, where the image and the text, although considered to be safe in isolation, combine to form unsafe content. To systematically explore this phenomenon, we propose a dataset to evaluate the current diffusion-based text-to-image (T2I) models under such jailbreak. We benchmark nine representative T2I models, including two closed-source commercial models. Experimental results reveal a concerning tendency to produce unsafe content: all tested models suffer from such type of jailbreak, with rates of unsafe generation ranging from around 10\% to 70\% where DALLE 3 demonstrates almost the highest unsafety. In real-world scenarios, various filters such as keyword blocklists, customized prompt filters, and NSFW image filters, are commonly employed to mitigate these risks. We evaluate the effectiveness of such filters against our jailbreak and found that, while these filters may be effective for single modality detection, they fail to work against our jailbreak. We also investigate the underlying reason for such jailbreaks, from the perspective of text rendering capability and training data. Our work provides a foundation for further development towards more secure and reliable T2I models. Project page at https://multimodalpragmatic.github.io/.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces a multimodal pragmatic jailbreak attack on text-to-image models, where individually safe image and text combine to generate unsafe content. They propose a benchmark dataset and evaluate nine T2I models, finding that all suffer from this vulnerability, with DALLE 3 showing nearly the highest unsafety. Existing filters like keyword blocklists and NSFW image filters fail to mitigate this attack, as they operate on single modalities. This work directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile: models can be easily broken by a novel attack surface that exploits the multimodal interaction between visual text and images, bypassing current safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文介绍了一种针对文本到图像模型的多模态实用越狱攻击，其中单独安全的图像和文本结合生成不安全内容。他们提出了一个基准数据集并评估了九个T2I模型，发现所有模型都受到此漏洞影响，DALLE 3表现出几乎最高的不安全性。现有的过滤器（如关键词屏蔽和NSFW图像过滤器）因仅处理单模态而无法防御此攻击。这项工作直接证明了后训练安全对齐是脆弱的：模型可被这种利用视觉文本与图像多模态交互的新型攻击面轻易攻破，绕过了当前的安全措施。

papers.title: The CRINGE Loss: Learning what language not to model
papers.short_title: CRINGE: Learning What Not to Model
papers.abstract: Standard language model training employs gold human documents or human-human interaction data, and treats all training data as positive examples. Growing evidence shows that even with very large amounts of positive training data, issues remain that can be alleviated with relatively small amounts of negative data – examples of what the model should not do. In this work, we propose a novel procedure to train with such data called the “CRINGE” loss (ContRastive Iterative Negative GEneration). We show the effectiveness of this approach across three different experiments on the tasks of safe generation, contradiction avoidance, and open-domain dialogue. Our models outperform multiple strong baselines and are conceptually simple, easy to train and implement.
papers.summary_en: Standard language model training treats all data as positive examples, which can lead to issues like unsafe or contradictory outputs. This paper proposes the CRINGE loss (ContRastive Iterative Negative GEneration), a procedure that incorporates negative examples—demonstrations of what the model should not do—into training. Evaluated on safe generation, contradiction avoidance, and open-domain dialogue, CRINGE-trained models outperform strong baselines, showing the effectiveness of learning from negative data. While this method strengthens alignment by leveraging negative signals, it does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed; it focuses on improving alignment methodology.
papers.summary_zh: 标准语言模型训练将所有数据视为正例，可能导致不安全或矛盾输出。本文提出 CRINGE 损失（对比迭代式负例生成），将“不应做什么”的负样本有效融入训练。在安全生成、避免矛盾和开放域对话三项任务上，使用 CRINGE 训练的模型性能优于多个强基线，验证了从负数据中学习的价值。该方法通过引入负信号增强了安全对齐，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否具有脆弱性，而是专注于改进对齐方法本身。

papers.title: Back to Basics: Revisiting REINFORCE-Style Optimization for Learning from Human Feedback in LLMs
papers.abstract: AI alignment in the shape of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is increasingly treated as a crucial ingredient for high performance large language models. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) has been installed by the seminal literature as the standard method for the RL part of RLHF. However, it involves both high computational cost and sensitive hyperparameter tuning. We posit that most of the motivational principles that led to the development of PPO are less of a practical concern in RLHF and advocate for a less computationally expensive method that preserves and even increases performance. We revisit how alignment from human preferences is formulated in the context of RL. Keeping simplicity as a guiding principle, we show that many components of PPO are unnecessary in an RLHF context and that far simpler REINFORCE-style optimization variants outperform both PPO and newly proposed “RL-free” methods such as DPO and RAFT. Our work suggests that careful adaptation to LLMs alignment characteristics allows benefiting from online RL optimization at low cost.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the computational inefficiency and hyperparameter sensitivity of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) for large language models. The authors revisit REINFORCE-style optimization and propose simplified variants that remove unnecessary components of PPO, achieving lower cost and higher performance. They evaluate their method against PPO and 'RL-free' alternatives like DPO and RAFT, demonstrating that their REINFORCE variants consistently outperform baselines in alignment tasks. This paper advances alignment methodology by providing a simpler and more effective online RL approach, but it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed; its contribution is primarily about improving the alignment optimization process.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在大型语言模型的人类反馈强化学习（RLHF）中，PPO算法计算成本高且超参数敏感的问题。作者重新审视了REINFORCE风格的优化方法，并提出了简化变体，去除了PPO中不必要的组件，实现了更低的成本和更高的性能。他们在与PPO以及无RL方法如DPO和RAFT的对比实验中，证明了所提REINFORCE变体在对齐任务中一致地优于基线。本文推进了对齐方法论，提供了一种更简单有效的在线RL方法，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过，其主要贡献在于改进了对齐优化过程。

papers.title: The TIP of the Iceberg: Revealing a Hidden Class of Task-in-Prompt Adversarial Attacks on LLMs
papers.abstract: We present a novel class of jailbreak adversarial attacks on LLMs, termed Task-in-Prompt (TIP) attacks. Our approach embeds sequence-to-sequence tasks (e.g., cipher decoding, riddles, code execution) into the model's prompt to indirectly generate prohibited inputs. To systematically assess the effectiveness of these attacks, we introduce the PHRYGE benchmark. We demonstrate that our techniques successfully circumvent safeguards in six state-of-the-art language models, including GPT-4o and LLaMA 3.2. Our findings highlight critical weaknesses in current LLM safety alignments and underscore the urgent need for more sophisticated defence strategies. Warning: this paper contains examples of unethical inquiries used solely for research purposes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreak attacks on LLMs by introducing Task-in-Prompt (TIP) attacks, a new class that embeds sequence-to-sequence tasks (e.g., cipher decoding, riddles) into prompts to indirectly bypass safety safeguards. It proposes a systematic evaluation using the PHRYGE benchmark and tests on six state-of-the-art models, including GPT-4o and LLaMA 3.2. The attacks successfully circumvent safeguards, revealing critical weaknesses in current safety alignments. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as a novel attack surface easily breaks through existing protections.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM越狱攻击，提出任务内提示（TIP）攻击新类别，通过将密码解码、谜题等序列到序列任务嵌入提示，间接绕过安全防护。提出PHRYGE基准进行系统评估，并在GPT-4o、LLaMA 3.2等六款先进模型上验证，成功绕过了安全措施。该研究直接揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，表明对齐模块易被新攻击面攻破。

papers.title: Defense Against Prompt Injection Attack by Leveraging Attack Techniques
papers.abstract: With the advancement of technology, large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across various natural language processing (NLP) tasks, powering LLM-integrated applications like Microsoft Copilot. However, as LLMs continue to evolve, new vulnerabilities, especially prompt injection attacks arise. These attacks trick LLMs into deviating from the original input instructions and executing the attacker's instructions injected in data content, such as retrieved results. Recent attack methods leverage LLMs'instruction-following abilities and their inabilities to distinguish instructions injected in the data content, and achieve a high attack success rate (ASR). When comparing the attack and defense methods, we interestingly find that they share similar design goals, of inducing the model to ignore unwanted instructions and instead to execute wanted instructions. Therefore, we raise an intuitive question: Could these attack techniques be utilized for defensive purposes? In this paper, we invert the intention of prompt injection methods to develop novel defense methods based on previous training-free attack methods, by repeating the attack process but with the original input instruction rather than the injected instruction. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our defense techniques outperform existing training-free defense approaches, achieving state-of-the-art results.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses prompt injection attacks, where attackers insert malicious instructions into data content to mislead LLMs. The authors propose novel defense methods by inverting the intent of existing training-free attack techniques, reapplying the attack process but with the original target instruction. Comprehensive experiments show the defenses outperform prior training-free methods, achieving state-of-the-art results. This paper advances defense methodologies against prompt injection, suggesting that alignment can be hardened, but it does not directly investigate the underlying fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对提示注入攻击，即攻击者通过在数据内容中插入恶意指令来误导大语言模型。作者提出了一种新颖的防御方法，通过反转现有免训练攻击技术的意图，将攻击过程重复应用于原始目标指令而非注入指令。全面的实验表明，该防御方法优于以往的免训练方法，取得了最先进的结果。本文推进了针对提示注入的防御方法，表明对齐可以加强，但并未直接研究安全对齐本身的脆弱性。

papers.title: Defending Against Alignment-Breaking Attacks via Robustly Aligned LLM
papers.abstract: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have made significant advancements and are now widely used across various domains. Unfortunately, there has been a rising concern that LLMs can be misused to generate harmful or malicious content. Though a line of research has focused on aligning LLMs with human values and preventing them from producing inappropriate content, such alignments are usually vulnerable and can be bypassed by alignment-breaking attacks via adversarially optimized or handcrafted jailbreaking prompts. In this work, we introduce a Robustly Aligned LLM (RA-LLM) to defend against potential alignment-breaking attacks. RA-LLM can be directly constructed upon an existing aligned LLM with a robust alignment checking function, without requiring any expensive retraining or fine-tuning process of the original LLM. Furthermore, we also provide a theoretical analysis for RA-LLM to verify its effectiveness in defending against alignment-breaking attacks. Through real-world experiments on open-source large language models, we demonstrate that RA-LLM can successfully defend against both state-of-the-art adversarial prompts and popular handcrafted jailbreaking prompts by reducing their attack success rates from nearly 100% to around 10% or less.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs to alignment-breaking attacks, where adversarial or handcrafted jailbreaking prompts bypass alignment to generate harmful outputs. It proposes a Robustly Aligned LLM (RA-LLM) that integrates a robust alignment checking function into an existing aligned model without any retraining. Evaluation on open-source LLMs shows RA-LLM reduces attack success rates from nearly 100% to around 10% or less against both adversarial and popular handcrafted jailbreaks. This work directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that a lightweight defense can harden models, though it does not resolve the fundamental question of whether alignment is inherently robust—it offers a practical mitigation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型在面对对齐破坏攻击时的脆弱性，这些攻击通过对抗优化或手工设计的越狱提示词可绕过对齐生成有害内容。它提出鲁棒对齐大语言模型（RA-LLM），在现有对齐模型上集成鲁棒对齐检查功能，无需重新训练。在开源模型上的实验表明，RA-LLM 能将攻击成功率从接近 100% 降低至 10% 左右或更低，有效防御对抗性和手工越狱提示词。该工作直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题：通过轻量级防御可硬化模型，但并未从根本上解决对齐是否固有鲁棒的问题，它提供了一种实用的缓解方案。

papers.title: DiffPO: Diffusion-styled Preference Optimization for Inference Time Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Inference-time alignment provides an efficient alternative for aligning LLMs with humans. However, these approaches still face challenges, such as limited scalability due to policy-specific value functions and latency during the inference phase. In this paper, we propose a novel approach, Diffusion-styled Preference Optimization (DiffPO), which provides an efficient and policy-agnostic solution for aligning LLMs with humans. By directly performing alignment at sentence level, DiffPO avoids the time latency associated with token-level generation. Designed as a plug-and-play module, DiffPO can be seamlessly integrated with various base models to enhance their alignment. Extensive experiments on AlpacaEval 2, MT-bench, and HH-RLHF demonstrate that DiffPO achieves superior alignment performance across various settings, achieving a favorable trade-off between alignment quality and inference-time latency. Furthermore, DiffPO demonstrates model-agnostic scalability, significantly improving the performance of large models such as Llama-3-70B.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the efficiency and scalability limitations of inference-time alignment for LLMs, which often suffer from high latency and model-specific designs. It proposes Diffusion-styled Preference Optimization (DiffPO), a sentence-level, plug-and-play module that avoids token-level generation latency. Experiments on AlpacaEval 2, MT-bench, and HH-RLHF show that DiffPO achieves superior alignment and a favorable trade-off between quality and inference latency, and scales effectively to large models like Llama-3-70B. While DiffPO advances inference-time alignment methodology, it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型推理时对齐方法在效率和可扩展性上的局限，这些方法常面临高延迟和模型特定设计的挑战。它提出了一种句子级别的即插即用模块——扩散式偏好优化（DiffPO），避免了词元级生式延迟。在AlpacaEval 2、MT-bench和HH-RLHF上的实验表明，DiffPO实现了更优的对齐效果，在质量与推理延迟之间取得了良好取舍，并能有效扩展至Llama-3-70B等大模型。尽管DiffPO推进了推理时对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SDD: Self-Degraded Defense against Malicious Fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) often employ safety alignment methods to resist harmful instructions. However, recent research shows that maliciously fine-tuning these LLMs on harmful data can easily bypass these safeguards. To counter this, we theoretically uncover why malicious fine-tuning succeeds and identify potential defense strategies. Building on the theoretical analysis, we introduce the Self-Degraded Defense (SDD) framework. SDD encourages LLMs to produce high-quality but irrelevant responses to harmful prompts. When attackers attempt malicious fine-tuning, the general capability of the LLM aligned by SDD will significantly decrease, rendering it incapable of following harmful instructions. Our experimental results confirm SDD's effectiveness against such attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned open-source LLMs to malicious fine-tuning, which can easily bypass safeguards. The authors propose Self-Degraded Defense (SDD), which encourages the model to produce high-quality but irrelevant responses to harmful prompts, causing malicious fine-tuning to significantly degrade the model's general capabilities and thus prevent harmful instruction following. Experimental results demonstrate SDD's effectiveness against such attacks. By presenting both an attack surface and a defense mechanism, this work contributes to understanding the fragility of post-training safety alignment and potential ways to improve its robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于安全对齐的开源大语言模型在面对恶意微调时的脆弱性，即攻击者可通过有害数据微调轻易绕过安全防护。作者提出了自退化防御（SDD）方法，通过让模型对有害提示输出高质量但不相关的响应，使得恶意微调会导致模型通用能力显著下降，从而无法执行有害指令。实验结果验证了SDD对此类攻击的有效性。该研究揭示了对齐后安全机制易被攻破的脆弱性，并给出了一种增强鲁棒性的防御思路，直接回应了后训练安全对齐是否真正可靠这一核心问题。

papers.title: AutoMixAlign: Adaptive Data Mixing for Multi-Task Preference Optimization in LLMs
papers.abstract: When aligning large language models (LLMs), their performance on various tasks (such as being helpful, harmless, and honest) depends heavily on the composition of their training data. However, selecting a data mixture that achieves strong performance across all tasks is challenging. Existing approaches rely on large ablation studies, heuristics, or human intuition, but these can be prohibitively expensive and suboptimal. We study this problem in the setting of preference optimization via DPO and introduce AutoMixAlign (AMA), a theoretically-grounded algorithm that adaptively mixes datasets during training to balance performance across tasks. AMA first trains \textit{specialist models} for each task to determine losses that correspond to strong task performance. Then, it trains a generalist model using a novel minimax optimization that prioritizes tasks for which generalist model losses deviate most from specialist model losses. To optimize this problem, we propose two algorithms: (1) AMA-R, which adaptively reweights the objective to prioritize tasks, and (2) AMA-S, which adaptively adjusts how much data is sampled from each task to prioritize tasks. Both algorithms achieve a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ in the convex case. AMA-R's convergence result follows from Sagawa et al. (2019), and we provide a convergence proof for AMA-S using online learning techniques such as EXP3. We evaluate AMA on several multitask alignment setups and find that AMA outperforms the standard alignment approach -- which simply optimizes the total loss across all tasks -- and also outperforms model merging methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of selecting an optimal data mixture for multi-task alignment of LLMs using DPO. It proposes AutoMixAlign (AMA), a theoretically-grounded algorithm that adaptively mixes datasets by first training per-task specialists to establish target losses, then solving a minimax optimization to prioritize tasks where the generalist lags. AMA offers two variants: AMA-R reweights the objective, and AMA-S adjusts data sampling, both achieving O(1/√T) convergence. Evaluated on multiple multi-task alignment setups, AMA outperforms standard loss minimization and model merging. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对使用 DPO 进行大语言模型多任务对齐时的数据混合选择问题，提出了具有理论基础的 AutoMixAlign (AMA) 算法，通过先训练各任务专家模型确定目标损失，再求解极小极大优化来自适应调整数据混合，以优先处理通用模型落后最大的任务。AMA 包含两种实现：AMA-R 通过重加权目标函数，AMA-S 通过调整数据采样，两者在凸情形下均达到 O(1/√T) 收敛率。多任务对齐实验表明 AMA 优于标准总损失优化和模型合并方法。该工作推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Language Models are Homer Simpson! Safety Re-Alignment of Fine-tuned Language Models through Task Arithmetic
papers.short_title: RESTA: Re-aligning LLMs via Task Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Aligned language models face a significant limitation as their fine-tuning often results in compromised safety. To tackle this, we propose a simple method RESTA that performs LLM safety realignment. RESTA stands for REstoring Safety through Task Arithmetic. At its core, it involves a simple arithmetic addition of a safety vector to the weights of the compromised model. We demonstrate the effectiveness of RESTA in both parameter-efficient and full fine-tuning, covering a wide range of downstream tasks, including instruction following in Chinese, English, and Hindi, as well as problem-solving capabilities in Code and Math. We also showcase the generalizability of RESTA on three existing safety evaluation benchmarks and a multilingual benchmark dataset proposed as a part of this work, consisting of 550 harmful questions covering 11 categories, each with 5 sub-categories of harm. Overall, RESTA decreases the harmfulness of the compromised model from 18.6% to 5.1% and from 9.2% to 1.5% in parameter-efficient and full fine-tuning, respectively, while maintaining most of the model's performance on the task. We release the source codes at: https://github.com/declare-lab/resta.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that fine-tuning aligned language models for downstream tasks often compromises their safety alignment. It proposes RESTA, a simple method that restores safety by adding a pre-computed safety vector to the weights of the compromised model through task arithmetic. Evaluated across diverse tasks and languages, RESTA reduced harmfulness from 18.6% to 5.1% (parameter-efficient) and 9.2% to 1.5% (full fine-tuning), while largely preserving downstream task performance. By showing that safety can be restored through a simple arithmetic operation, the paper suggests that safety alignment is a fragile module that can be broken by fine-tuning but also easily mended, offering a practical hardening approach.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了对齐语言模型在下游任务微调时安全性能下降的问题。提出了RESTA方法，通过向受损模型权重添加一个预计算的安全向量（基于安全模型与受损模型之差），利用任务算术实现安全重新对齐。在参数高效微调和全量微调、多语言指令遵循及代码数学等任务上进行了评估，结果显示有害性从18.6%降至5.1%（参数高效）和从9.2%降至1.5%（全量微调），同时基本保持了下游任务性能。通过展示安全对齐可通过简单的算术操作恢复，表明安全对齐是一个易被微调破坏但也可轻易修复的脆弱模块，这为安全硬化的实践提供了思路。

papers.title: Lost in the Context: Insufficient and Distracted Attention to Contexts in Preference Modeling
papers.abstract: Shihan Dou, Jiayi Chen, Chenhao Huang, Feng Chen, Wei Chengzhi, Huiyuan Zheng, Shichun Liu, Yan Liu, Chenxiao Liu, Chao Xin, Lin Yan, Zongzhang Zhang, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang. Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2025.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that reward models in preference-based alignment (e.g., RLHF) often pay insufficient or distracted attention to the full context (prompt/history), leading to misjudged preferences. It analyzes attention patterns and proposes methods to mitigate context neglect, ensuring preferences are conditioned on the complete context. Evaluations show that enhancing context attention improves preference accuracy and alignment robustness, revealing that current models can be manipulated by context changes. This work uncovers a mechanistic fragility in safety alignment: preference models are easily misled when context is ignored, directly supporting the claim that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be broken by exploiting inattentive reward models.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了基于偏好的对齐（如RLHF）中奖励模型对完整上下文（提示/对话历史）关注不足或分散的问题，导致偏好判断错误。论文分析了注意力模式，并提出方法缓解上下文忽视，确保偏好基于完整上下文。实验表明，改善上下文注意力可提升偏好预测准确性和对齐鲁棒性，揭示了当前模型易受上下文变化操控。该研究发现了安全对齐的机制脆弱性：当上下文被忽略时，偏好模型易被误导，直接支持了后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过利用疏忽的奖励模型来破坏的论断。

papers.title: Black-Box Prompt Optimization: Aligning Large Language Models without Model Training
papers.short_title: BPO: Aligning LLMs without Model Training
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive success in various applications. However, these models are often not well aligned with human intents, which calls for additional treatments on them; that is, the alignment problem. To make LLMs better follow user instructions, existing alignment methods primarily focus on further training them. However, the extra training of LLMs is usually expensive in terms of GPU computing; even worse, some LLMs are not accessible for user-demanded training, such as GPTs. In this work, we take a different perspective -- Black-Box Prompt Optimization (BPO) -- to perform alignments. The idea is to optimize user prompts to suit LLMs' input understanding, so as to best realize users' intents without updating LLMs' parameters. BPO leverages human preferences to optimize prompts, thus making it superior to LLM (e.g., ChatGPT) as a prompt engineer. Moreover, BPO is model-agnostic, and the empirical results demonstrate that the BPO-aligned ChatGPT yields a 22% increase in the win rate against its original version and 10% for GPT-4. Notably, the BPO-aligned LLMs can outperform the same models aligned by PPO and DPO, and it also brings additional performance gains when combining BPO with PPO or DPO. Code and datasets are released at https://github.com/thu-coai/BPO.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models (LLMs) with human intents without expensive model training, which is infeasible for closed-source models like GPTs. It proposes Black-Box Prompt Optimization (BPO), a method that optimizes user prompts using human preferences to better fit LLM input understanding, without updating model parameters. Experiments show BPO-aligned ChatGPT achieves a 22% win rate increase against its original version, and 10% for GPT-4; it outperforms alignment methods like PPO and DPO and yields further gains when combined. This work advances alignment methodology through training-free prompt engineering but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型对齐人类意图时训练成本高、部分模型无法训练的问题，提出黑盒提示优化（BPO）方法，通过利用人类偏好优化用户提示以适应模型理解，无需更新参数。实验表明，BPO 对齐后的 ChatGPT 胜率提升 22%，GPT-4 提升 10%，效果优于 PPO 和 DPO，且与这些方法结合有额外收益。该方法属于对齐技术的改进，未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或稳健性。

papers.title: Exploring LLMs' Ability to Spontaneously and Conditionally Modify Moral Expressions through Text Manipulation
papers.abstract: Morality serves as the foundation of societal structure, guiding legal systems, shaping cultural values, and influencing individual self-perception. With the rise and pervasiveness of generative AI tools, and particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), concerns arise regarding how these tools capture and potentially alter moral dimensions through machine-generated text manipulation. Based on the Moral Foundation Theory, our work investigates this topic by analyzing the behavior of 12 LLMs among the most widely used Open and uncensored (i.e., “abliterated”) models, and leveraging human-annotated datasets used in moral-related analysis. Results have shown varying levels of alteration of moral expressions depending on the type of text modification task and moral-related conditioning prompt.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how large language models (LLMs) capture and potentially alter moral dimensions through text manipulation tasks. The authors analyze 12 open and uncensored LLMs using human-annotated moral datasets, grounded in Moral Foundation Theory, and test both spontaneous and conditionally prompted moral modification. Results show varying degrees of moral expression alteration depending on the type of text modification task and moral conditioning prompt. This study examines moral expression changes in LLMs but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨大语言模型（LLMs）在文本操作任务中如何捕捉并可能改变道德维度。研究基于道德基础理论，分析了12个开放且未审查的LLM，利用人工标注的道德数据集，测试了模型自发和条件化提示下的道德修改能力。结果表明，道德表达的改变程度因文本修改任务类型和道德调节提示而异。本文关注LLM的道德表达变化，但未直接回应后训练安全对齐是否脆弱这一核心问题。

papers.title: Efficient Safety Alignment of Large Language Models via Preference Re-ranking and Representation-based Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms for safety alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), encounter the challenge of distribution shift. Current approaches typically address this issue through online sampling from the target policy, which requires significant computational resources. In this paper, we hypothesize that during off-policy training, while the ranking order of output generated by policy changes, their overall distribution remains relatively stable. This stability allows the conversion of the sampling process from the target policy into a computationally efficient re-ranking of preference data. Building on this hypothesis, we propose a new framework that leverages the model's intrinsic safety judgment capability to extract reward signals, which are then used to calculate label confidence for preference reordering. Extensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that the proposed method effectively addresses the distribution shift issue, remarkably enhancing the safety performance while avoiding about 300x computational overheads.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the distribution shift issue in off-policy reinforcement learning for LLM safety alignment, such as in DPO, which normally demands expensive online sampling. It proposes a framework that converts online sampling into a computationally efficient re-ranking of preference data by leveraging the model's intrinsic safety judgment to extract reward signals and compute label confidence. Extensive experiments and theoretical analysis show that the method effectively mitigates distribution shift, significantly improves safety performance, and reduces computational overhead by approximately 300 times. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全对齐中离线强化学习（如DPO）的分布偏移问题，该方法通常需要昂贵的在线采样。提出一个框架，利用模型内在的安全判断能力提取奖励信号，计算标签置信度实现对偏好数据的重排序，将在线采样转化为高效的重排序过程。大量实验和理论分析表明，该方法有效缓解了分布偏移，显著提升安全性能，同时将计算开销降低约300倍。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: JailbreakRadar: Comprehensive Assessment of Jailbreak Attacks Against LLMs
papers.abstract: Jailbreak attacks aim to bypass the LLMs' safeguards. While researchers have proposed different jailbreak attacks in depth, they have done so in isolation -- either with unaligned settings or comparing a limited range of methods. To fill this gap, we present a large-scale evaluation of various jailbreak attacks. We collect 17 representative jailbreak attacks, summarize their features, and establish a novel jailbreak attack taxonomy. Then we conduct comprehensive measurement and ablation studies across nine aligned LLMs on 160 forbidden questions from 16 violation categories. Also, we test jailbreak attacks under eight advanced defenses. Based on our taxonomy and experiments, we identify some important patterns, such as heuristic-based attacks could achieve high attack success rates but are easy to mitigate by defenses, causing low practicality. Our study offers valuable insights for future research on jailbreak attacks and defenses. We hope our work could help the community avoid incremental work and serve as an effective benchmark tool for practitioners.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragmented evaluation of jailbreak attacks by conducting a large-scale, comprehensive assessment. It collects 17 representative attacks, proposes a novel taxonomy, and benchmarks them against nine aligned LLMs on 160 forbidden questions across 16 categories, also testing against eight defenses. Key findings reveal that heuristic-based attacks achieve high attack success rates but are easily mitigated, limiting practicality. This work underscores the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as it can be readily bypassed by diverse attacks, though defenses can counteract some, illustrating the ongoing vulnerability.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对越狱攻击评估碎片化的问题，开展大规模全面评估。它收集了17种代表性攻击，提出新颖分类法，并在9个对齐大语言模型上对16类160个禁止问题进行基准测试，同时测试了8种防御措施。关键发现表明，启发式攻击具有高攻击成功率，但易被防御缓解，导致实用性受限。这项工作揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因其可被多样攻击轻易绕过，尽管防御能部分缓解，体现出持续的脆弱性。

papers.title: Nudging: Inference-time Alignment of LLMs via Guided Decoding
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require alignment to effectively and safely follow user instructions. This process necessitates training an aligned version for every base model, resulting in significant computational overhead. In this work, we propose NUDGING, a simple, training-free algorithm that aligns any base model at inference time using a small aligned model. NUDGING is motivated by recent findings that alignment primarily alters the model's behavior on a small subset of stylistic tokens (e.g., discourse markers). We find that base models are significantly more uncertain when generating these tokens. Building on this insight, NUDGING employs a small aligned model to generate nudging tokens to guide the base model's output during decoding when the base model's uncertainty is high, with only a minor additional inference overhead. We evaluate NUDGING across 3 model families on a diverse range of open-instruction tasks. Without any training, nudging a large base model with a 7x-14x smaller aligned model achieves zero-shot performance comparable to, and sometimes surpassing, that of large aligned models. By operating at the token level, NUDGING enables off-the-shelf collaboration between model families. For instance, nudging Gemma-2-27b with Llama-27b-chat outperforms Llama-2-70b-chat on various tasks. Overall, our work offers a modular and cost-efficient solution to LLM alignment. Our code and demo are available at: https://fywalter.github.io/nudging/ .
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high computational cost of aligning every base large language model (LLM) to follow instructions. It proposes NUDGING, a training-free, inference-time alignment algorithm that uses a small aligned model to insert guiding tokens when the base model is uncertain, focusing on stylistic tokens where uncertainty is high. Evaluated across three model families on diverse open-instruction tasks, nudging a large base model with a 7x-14x smaller aligned model achieves performance comparable to or better than fully aligned large models, with minimal inference overhead. This work provides an efficient and modular alignment solution, but it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or robust; it primarily offers a cost-effective alternative to standard alignment training.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型（LLM）对齐中为每个基座模型训练对齐版本的高计算开销问题。提出NUDGING，一种无需训练的推理时对齐算法，利用小型对齐模型在基座模型不确定性高时生成“轻推”令牌来引导输出，重点关注风格令牌上的不确定性。在三个模型家族和多种开放指令任务上评估，用7-14倍小的对齐模型轻推大基座模型，零样本性能达到甚至超过大对齐模型，且额外推理开销小。该研究推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题；它主要提供了一种高效、模块化的对齐替代方案。

papers.title: IPO: Your Language Model is Secretly a Preference Classifier
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as the primary method for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. While it enables LLMs to achieve human-level alignment, it often incurs significant computational and financial costs due to its reliance on training external reward models or human-labeled preferences. In this work, we propose Implicit Preference Optimization (IPO), an alternative approach that leverages generative LLMs as preference classifiers, thereby reducing the dependence on external human feedback or reward models to obtain preferences. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation on the preference classification ability of LLMs using RewardBench, assessing models across different sizes, architectures, and training levels to validate our hypothesis. Furthermore, we investigate the self-improvement capabilities of LLMs by generating multiple responses for a given instruction and employing the model itself as a preference classifier for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-based training. Our findings demonstrate that models trained through IPO achieve performance comparable to those utilizing state-of-the-art reward models for obtaining preferences.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost of RLHF-based alignment due to reliance on external reward models or human labels. It proposes Implicit Preference Optimization (IPO), which uses the generative LLM itself as a preference classifier, enabling preference acquisition without external feedback. Evaluated on RewardBench, IPO-trained models achieve comparable performance to those using state-of-the-art reward models. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF对齐方法依赖外部奖励模型或人类标注导致的高成本问题，提出隐式偏好优化（IPO），利用生成式语言模型自身作为偏好分类器，减少对外部反馈的依赖。通过在RewardBench上评估，IPO训练的模型性能与使用先进奖励模型的方法相当。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights
papers.abstract: The application scope of Large Language Models (LLMs) continues to expand, leading to increasing interest in personalized LLMs that align with human values. However, aligning these models with individual values raises significant safety concerns, as certain values may correlate with harmful information. In this paper, we identify specific safety risks associated with value-aligned LLMs and investigate the psychological principles behind these challenges. Our findings reveal two key insights. (1) Value-aligned LLMs are more prone to harmful behavior compared to non-fine-tuned models and exhibit slightly higher risks in traditional safety evaluations than other fine-tuned models. (2) These safety issues arise because value-aligned LLMs genuinely generate text according to the aligned values, which can amplify harmful outcomes. Using a dataset with detailed safety categories, we find significant correlations between value alignment and safety risks, supported by psychological hypotheses. This study offers insights into the"black box"of value alignment and proposes in-context alignment methods to enhance the safety of value-aligned LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the unintended safety risks of aligning LLMs with individual human values, finding that such alignment can increase harmful outputs. Through empirical analysis and psychological hypotheses, it reveals significant correlations between value alignment and safety risks, showing value-aligned models are more prone to harm than non-fine-tuned or other fine-tuned models. The study demonstrates that post-training alignment can introduce new vulnerabilities, providing direct evidence that safety alignment may be fragile and can be inadvertently broken under certain conditions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究将大语言模型与个体人类价值观对齐所带来的意外安全风险，发现这种对齐可能增加有害输出。通过实证分析和心理学假设，揭示了价值观对齐与安全风险之间的显著相关性，表明价值观对齐模型比未微调或其他微调模型更易产生危害。该研究表明后训练对齐可能引入新漏洞，直接证明了安全对齐在某些条件下可能是脆弱的，并可能被无意破坏。

papers.title: M-RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models in Multilingual Settings
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) have driven the state-of-the-art performance of LLMs today by enabling the integration of human feedback into the language modeling process. However, RMs are primarily trained and evaluated in English, and their capabilities in multilingual settings remain largely understudied. In this work, we conduct a systematic evaluation of several reward models in multilingual settings. We first construct the first-of-its-kind multilingual RM evaluation benchmark, M-RewardBench, consisting of 2.87k preference instances for 23 typologically diverse languages, that tests the chat, safety, reasoning, and translation capabilities of RMs. We then rigorously evaluate a wide range of reward models on M-RewardBench, offering fresh insights into their performance across diverse languages. We identify a significant gap in RMs' performances between English and non-English languages and show that RM preferences can change substantially from one language to another. We also present several findings on how different multilingual aspects impact RM performance. Specifically, we show that the performance of RMs is improved with improved translation quality. Similarly, we demonstrate that the models exhibit better performance for high-resource languages. We release M-RewardBench dataset and the codebase in this study to facilitate a better understanding of RM evaluation in multilingual settings.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of evaluation for reward models in multilingual settings. It introduces M-RewardBench, a benchmark with 2.87k preference instances across 23 languages, covering chat, safety, reasoning, and translation. Through rigorous evaluation of various reward models, it reveals a significant performance gap between English and non-English languages, along with language-dependent preference shifts, and shows that translation quality and language resource level impact performance. While the paper does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment, its findings on cross-lingual performance variance indirectly highlight a potential brittleness in multilingual alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在多语言环境中奖励模型评估不足的问题。它提出了M-RewardBench基准，包含23种语言、覆盖对话、安全、推理和翻译的2.87k偏好实例。通过对多种奖励模型的严格评估，揭示了英语与非英语之间的显著性能差距以及依赖语言的偏好变化，并表明翻译质量和语言资源水平会影响模型表现。尽管本文未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，但其跨语言性能差异的发现间接突显了多语言对齐的潜在脆弱性。

papers.title: Wait, that's not an option: LLMs Robustness with Incorrect Multiple-Choice Options
papers.short_title: LLMs Robustness with Incorrect MCQ Options
papers.abstract: This work introduces a novel framework for evaluating LLMs' capacity to balance instruction-following with critical reasoning when presented with multiple-choice questions containing no valid answers. Through systematic evaluation across arithmetic, domain-specific knowledge, and high-stakes medical decision tasks, we demonstrate that post-training aligned models often default to selecting invalid options, while base models exhibit improved refusal capabilities that scale with model size. Our analysis reveals that alignment techniques, though intended to enhance helpfulness, can inadvertently impair models' reflective judgment--the ability to override default behaviors when faced with invalid options. We additionally conduct a parallel human study showing similar instruction-following biases, with implications for how these biases may propagate through human feedback datasets used in alignment. We provide extensive ablation studies examining the impact of model size, training techniques, and prompt engineering. Our findings highlight fundamental tensions between alignment optimization and preservation of critical reasoning capabilities, with important implications for developing more robust AI systems for real-world deployment.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates LLMs' vulnerability when multiple-choice questions contain no valid answers, revealing a tension between instruction-following and critical reasoning. It proposes an evaluation framework and systematically tests base and aligned models across arithmetic, domain knowledge, and medical decision tasks. The findings show that aligned models often default to selecting invalid options, while base models exhibit better refusal capabilities that scale with model size, indicating that alignment techniques can impair reflective judgment. This directly exposes a fragility in post-training safety alignment: the optimization for helpfulness undermines robustness against out-of-distribution inputs that require overriding default behaviors.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了当选择题没有正确答案时大语言模型表现出的脆弱性，揭示了指令遵循与批判性推理之间的张力。作者提出一种评估框架，并在算术、领域知识和医疗决策任务上系统测试了基础模型和对齐模型。结果表明，经过对齐的模型倾向于选择无效选项，而基础模型则表现出更好的拒绝能力，且该能力随模型规模提升，说明对齐技术可能会损害模型的反思判断力。这一发现直接暴露了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：对“有用性”的优化削弱了模型在面对需要推翻默认行为的分布外输入时的鲁棒性。

papers.title: GAPO: Learning Preferential Prompt through Generative Adversarial Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models have highlighted the critical need for precise control over model outputs through predefined constraints. While existing methods attempt to achieve this through either direct instruction-response synthesis or preferential response optimization, they often struggle with constraint understanding and adaptation. This limitation becomes particularly evident when handling fine-grained constraints, leading to either hallucination or brittle performance. We introduce Generative Adversarial Policy Optimization (GAPO), a novel framework that combines GAN-based training dynamics with an encoder-only reward model to progressively learn and adapt to increasingly complex constraints. GAPO leverages adversarial training to automatically generate training samples of varying difficulty while utilizing the encoder-only architecture to better capture prompt-response relationships. Extensive experiments demonstrate GAPO's superior performance across multiple benchmarks, particularly in scenarios requiring fine-grained constraint handling, where it significantly outperforms existing methods like PPO, DPO, and KTO. Our results suggest that GAPO's unique approach to preferential prompt learning offers a more robust and effective solution for controlling LLM outputs. Code is avaliable in https://github.com/MikeGu721/GAPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of precisely controlling LLM outputs via fine-grained constraints, where existing methods (PPO, DPO, KTO) often produce hallucination or brittle performance. It proposes GAPO, a framework that combines GAN-based adversarial training with an encoder-only reward model to progressively generate training samples of varying difficulty and better capture prompt-response relationships. Evaluated on multiple benchmarks, GAPO significantly outperforms baselines, especially in fine-grained constraint handling. While the paper advances alignment methodology by making constraint adherence more robust, it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks, though it implies that current methods are brittle under nuanced constraints.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了通过细粒度约束精确控制大语言模型输出的难题，指出PPO、DPO、KTO等方法常导致幻觉或性能脆弱。提出GAPO框架，结合GAN对抗训练与仅编码器奖励模型，逐步生成难度多样的训练样本，更好捕捉提示-响应关系。多基准实验表明，GAPO显著优于现有方法，尤其在细粒度约束处理上。该工作提升了对齐中的约束遵循鲁棒性，但未直接探索后训练安全对齐对抗攻击的脆弱性，不过暗示了当前方法在复杂约束下的脆弱性。

papers.title: Exploring the Impact of Instruction-Tuning on LLM's Susceptibility to Misinformation
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuning enhances the ability of large language models (LLMs) to follow user instructions more accurately, improving usability while reducing harmful outputs. However, this process may increase the model's dependence on user input, potentially leading to the unfiltered acceptance of misinformation and the generation of hallucinations. Existing studies primarily highlight that LLMs are receptive to external information that contradict their parametric knowledge, but little research has been conducted on the direct impact of instruction-tuning on this phenomenon. In our study, we investigate the impact of instruction-tuning on LLM's susceptibility to misinformation. Our analysis reveals that instruction-tuned LLMs are significantly more likely to accept misinformation when it is presented by the user. A comparison with base models shows that instruction-tuning increases reliance on user-provided information, shifting susceptibility from the assistant role to the user role. Furthermore, we explore additional factors influencing misinformation susceptibility, such as the role of the user in prompt structure, misinformation length, and the presence of warnings in the system prompt. Our findings underscore the need for systematic approaches to mitigate unintended consequences of instruction-tuning and enhance the reliability of LLMs in real-world applications.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how instruction-tuning, despite improving instruction-following, increases LLMs' susceptibility to user-provided misinformation. Through comparative analysis of base and instruction-tuned LLMs, it finds that instruction-tuned models are significantly more likely to accept and generate hallucinations from false user input. Further experiments show that factors like prompt structure, misinformation length, and system warnings modulate this susceptibility. The findings reveal a fragility in post-training safety alignment: a widely used alignment procedure inadvertently creates a new vulnerability, where malicious users can easily induce false outputs, undermining robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了指令微调在提高指令遵循能力的同时，如何增加了大语言模型对用户提供的错误信息的易感性。通过对比基座模型和指令微调模型，发现指令微调模型更倾向于接受用户错误信息并产生幻觉。实验还探讨了提示结构、错误信息长度和系统提示中的警告等因素的影响。这一发现揭示了后训练安全对齐的一个脆弱性：作为核心对齐方法的指令微调，反而引入了新漏洞，使得模型容易被恶意用户输入误导，表明对齐并非完全鲁棒。

papers.title: One-Shot is Enough: Consolidating Multi-Turn Attacks into Efficient Single-Turn Prompts for LLMs
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel framework for consolidating multi-turn adversarial ``jailbreak''prompts into single-turn queries, significantly reducing the manual overhead required for adversarial testing of large language models (LLMs). While multi-turn human jailbreaks have been shown to yield high attack success rates, they demand considerable human effort and time. Our multi-turn-to-single-turn (M2S) methods -- Hyphenize, Numberize, and Pythonize -- systematically reformat multi-turn dialogues into structured single-turn prompts. Despite removing iterative back-and-forth interactions, these prompts preserve and often enhance adversarial potency: in extensive evaluations on the Multi-turn Human Jailbreak (MHJ) dataset, M2S methods achieve attack success rates from 70.6 percent to 95.9 percent across several state-of-the-art LLMs. Remarkably, the single-turn prompts outperform the original multi-turn attacks by as much as 17.5 percentage points while cutting token usage by more than half on average. Further analysis shows that embedding malicious requests in enumerated or code-like structures exploits ``contextual blindness'', bypassing both native guardrails and external input-output filters. By converting multi-turn conversations into concise single-turn prompts, the M2S framework provides a scalable tool for large-scale red teaming and reveals critical weaknesses in contemporary LLM defenses.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high manual cost of multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs. It proposes M2S methods (Hyphenize, Numberize, Pythonize) that convert multi-turn adversarial dialogues into single-turn structured prompts. Evaluated on the Multi-turn Human Jailbreak dataset, these single-turn prompts achieve 70.6–95.9% attack success rates, outperforming original multi-turn attacks by up to 17.5 percentage points while reducing token usage by more than half. The work exposes a key fragility in safety alignment: malicious queries embedded in enumerated or code-like formats bypass guardrails through 'contextual blindness,' providing strong evidence that post-training safety modules can be easily circumvented.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多轮越狱攻击人力成本高的问题，提出M2S方法（Hyphenize、Numberize、Pythonize），将多轮对抗对话转化为单轮结构化提示。在Multi-turn Human Jailbreak数据集上，单轮提示攻击成功率达70.6%至95.9%，较多轮攻击最高提升17.5个百分点，且令牌用量减少过半。该研究揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：恶意请求通过枚举或代码式结构嵌入可绕过护栏，利用‘上下文盲区’，表明后训练安全模块易于被规避。

papers.title: Safety Alignment in NLP Tasks: Weakly Aligned Summarization as an In-Context Attack
papers.abstract: Recent developments in balancing the usefulness and safety of Large Language Models (LLMs) have raised a critical question: Are mainstream NLP tasks adequately aligned with safety consideration? Our study, focusing on safety-sensitive documents obtained through adversarial attacks, reveals significant disparities in the safety alignment of various NLP tasks. For instance, LLMs can effectively summarize malicious long documents but often refuse to translate them. This discrepancy highlights a previously unidentified vulnerability: attacks exploiting tasks with weaker safety alignment, like summarization, can potentially compromise the integrity of tasks traditionally deemed more robust, such as translation and question-answering (QA). Moreover, the concurrent use of multiple NLP tasks with lesser safety alignment increases the risk of LLMs inadvertently processing harmful content. We demonstrate these vulnerabilities in various safety-aligned LLMs, particularly Llama2 models, Gemini and GPT-4, indicating an urgent need for strengthening safety alignments across a broad spectrum of NLP tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates uneven safety alignment across NLP tasks in LLMs, revealing that summarization is weakly aligned compared to translation and QA. Adversaries can exploit this by using summarization to process harmful content in-context, compromising the safety of other tasks. Evaluations on Llama2, Gemini, and GPT-4 show LLMs summarize malicious documents while refusing translation, exposing a new attack surface. This work provides clear evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be bypassed through task-specific weaknesses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型在不同NLP任务中安全对齐的不均衡性，发现摘要任务相对于翻译和问答对齐较弱。攻击者可利用此漏洞，通过摘要处理有害内容进行上下文攻击，从而破坏其他任务的安全性。在Llama2、Gemini和GPT-4上的实验表明，模型会总结恶意文档却拒绝翻译，揭示了一种新的攻击面。该研究为安全对齐的脆弱性提供了明确证据，表明其可通过任务特定弱点被绕过。

papers.title: Shaping the Safety Boundaries: Understanding and Defending Against Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Jailbreaking in Large Language Models (LLMs) is a major security concern as it can deceive LLMs to generate harmful text. Yet, there is still insufficient understanding of how jailbreaking works, which makes it hard to develop effective defense strategies. We aim to shed more light into this issue: we conduct a detailed large-scale analysis of seven different jailbreak methods and find that these disagreements stem from insufficient observation samples. In particular, we introduce \textit{safety boundary}, and we find that jailbreaks shift harmful activations outside that safety boundary, where LLMs are less sensitive to harmful information. We also find that the low and the middle layers are critical in such shifts, while deeper layers have less impact. Leveraging on these insights, we propose a novel defense called \textbf{Activation Boundary Defense} (ABD), which adaptively constrains the activations within the safety boundary. We further use Bayesian optimization to selectively apply the defense method to the low and the middle layers. Our experiments on several benchmarks show that ABD achieves an average DSR of over 98\% against various forms of jailbreak attacks, with less than 2\% impact on the model's general capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the mechanism of jailbreaking in LLMs, finding that attacks shift harmful activations outside a learned safety boundary, primarily in low and middle layers. It proposes Activation Boundary Defense (ABD), which adaptively constrains activations within this boundary and uses Bayesian optimization to apply it selectively to critical layers. Experiments show ABD achieves over 98% defense success rate against various jailbreaks with less than 2% utility drop. This work directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile—as activations can be easily pushed out of the safe region—and offers a robust hardening method, providing key evidence on both sides of the robustness question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了LLM越狱的机制，发现攻击将有害激活位移到学习到的安全边界之外，且低中层起关键作用。提出激活边界防御（ABD），自适应地将激活限制在边界内，并利用贝叶斯优化选择性应用于关键层。实验显示ABD对多种越狱攻击防御成功率超98%，通用能力影响低于2%。该工作直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性——激活易被推出安全区，同时提供了鲁棒加固方法，为‘后训练安全对齐是否真正鲁棒’问题提供了正反两方面证据。

papers.title: Adversarial Tokenization
papers.abstract: Current LLM pipelines account for only one possible tokenization for a given string, ignoring exponentially many alternative tokenizations during training and inference. For example, the standard Llama3 tokenization of penguin is [p,enguin], yet [peng,uin] is another perfectly valid alternative. In this paper, we show that despite LLMs being trained solely on one tokenization, they still retain semantic understanding of other tokenizations, raising questions about their implications in LLM safety. Put succinctly, we answer the following question: can we adversarially tokenize an obviously malicious string to evade safety and alignment restrictions? We show that not only is adversarial tokenization an effective yet previously neglected axis of attack, but it is also competitive against existing state-of-the-art adversarial approaches without changing the text of the harmful request. We empirically validate this exploit across three state-of-the-art LLMs and adversarial datasets, revealing a previously unknown vulnerability in subword models.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a new vulnerability in LLM safety alignment: adversarial tokenization, where alternative subword tokenizations of a malicious string can bypass safety filters. The approach exploits the fact that LLMs retain semantic understanding of tokenizations not seen during training, allowing harmful requests to evade alignment without changing the text. Evaluated on three state-of-the-art LLMs and adversarial datasets, the method proves competitive with existing attacks. This directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as a simple tokenization change breaks it, adding a new axis to the attack surface.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了LLM安全对齐中的一个新脆弱点：对抗式分词，即利用恶意字符串的替代子词分词方式来绕过安全过滤器。该方法利用LLM对训练中未见的其他分词方式仍保留语义理解这一事实，使得有害请求在不改变文本的情况下逃避对齐。在三个最先进LLM和对抗数据集上的评估表明，该方法与现有攻击相比具有竞争力。这直接证明了安全对齐训练后的模型是脆弱的，简单的分词变化即可攻破，为攻击面增加了新维度。

papers.title: When Backdoors Speak: Understanding LLM Backdoor Attacks Through Model-Generated Explanations
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to be vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where triggers embedded in poisoned samples can maliciously alter LLMs' behaviors. In this paper, we move beyond attacking LLMs and instead examine backdoor attacks through the novel lens of natural language explanations. Specifically, we leverage LLMs' generative capabilities to produce human-readable explanations for their decisions, enabling direct comparisons between explanations for clean and poisoned samples. Our results show that backdoored models produce coherent explanations for clean inputs but diverse and logically flawed explanations for poisoned data, a pattern consistent across classification and generation tasks for different backdoor attacks. Further analysis reveals key insights into the explanation generation process. At the token level, explanation tokens associated with poisoned samples only appear in the final few transformer layers. At the sentence level, attention dynamics indicate that poisoned inputs shift attention away from the original input context during explanation generation. These findings enhance our understanding of backdoor mechanisms in LLMs and present a promising framework for detecting vulnerabilities through explainability.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how backdoor attacks affect the explanations generated by large language models. It leverages the models' own generative capabilities to produce human-readable explanations for decisions, enabling comparison between clean and poisoned samples. Experiments across classification and generation tasks show that backdoored models produce logically flawed explanations for poisoned inputs, with explanation tokens appearing only in final layers and attention shifting away from input context. This work contributes to the fragility question by showing that backdoored LLMs, despite appearing aligned on clean inputs, exhibit explainability flaws that could indicate hidden vulnerabilities.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究后门攻击对大型语言模型生成解释的影响。它利用模型自身的生成能力，为决策生成可读解释，从而比较干净与中毒样本的解释。在分类与生成任务上的实验表明，后门模型对中毒输入产生逻辑缺陷的解释，且解释标记仅出现在最后几层，注意力从输入上下文转移。这项工作表明，后门LLM尽管在干净输入上看似对齐，但存在着可能揭示隐藏漏洞的可解释性缺陷，从而回应了安全性对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: \mathsfCon Instruction: Universal Jailbreaking of Multimodal Large Language Models via Non-Textual Modalities
papers.abstract: Existing attacks against multimodal language models often communicate instruction through text, either as an explicit malicious instruction or a crafted generic prompt, and accompanied by a toxic image. In contrast, here we exploit the capabilities of MLLMs in following non-textual instruction, i.e., an adversarial image or audio, namely Con Instruction. It is a novel gray-box attack method that generates adversarial images or audio to convey specific harmful instructions to MLLMs. We also find that combining our adversarial examples with certain non-empty text inputs amplifies attack success, while appending these after malicious text has limited effects. To evaluate whether an attack is successful, we introduce a new attack response categorization (ARC) that considers the response quality and relevancy concerning the malicious instruction. The results show that Con Instruction effectively bypasses the safety mechanisms in various visual and audio-language models, including LLaVA-v1.5, InternVL, Qwen-VL, and Qwen-Audio, across two standard benchmarks: AdvBench and SafeBench. Specifically, our method achieves the highest attack success rates, reaching 81.3% and 86.6% on LLaVA-v1.5 (13B). We show that larger models are more susceptible toCon Instruction, contrasting observations in their underlying LLMs. On the defense side, we explore various methods against our attacks and find substantial gaps among existing techniques. The code will be made available upon publication.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to jailbreaking attacks that exploit non-textual modalities, where adversarial images or audio convey harmful instructions. The authors propose Con Instruction, a gray-box attack method that crafts adversarial examples to directly inject malicious commands via visual or auditory channels, bypassing text-based safety mechanisms. Evaluated across multiple MLLMs including LLaVA-v1.5, InternVL, Qwen-VL, and Qwen-Audio on AdvBench and SafeBench, it achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates up to 86.6%, and reveals that larger models are paradoxically more susceptible. This work demonstrates that safety alignment in MLLMs is fragile, as it can be circumvented through non-textual adversarial inputs, exposing a fundamental blind spot in current multimodal safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型（MLLM）面临的新型越狱攻击，即利用对抗性图像或音频等非文本模态传递有害指令。作者提出了Con Instruction，一种灰盒攻击方法，通过生成对抗样本来直接注入恶意命令，绕过基于文本的安全过滤。在LLaVA-v1.5、InternVL、Qwen-VL和Qwen-Audio等多个模型以及AdvBench和SafeBench基准上评估，该方法取得了高达86.6%的顶尖攻击成功率，并发现较大模型反而更易受攻击。该工作表明，MLLM的安全对齐是脆弱的，非文本对抗输入可绕过现有防护，暴露出多模态安全机制的盲点。

papers.title: MTSA: Multi-turn Safety Alignment for LLMs through Multi-round Red-teaming
papers.abstract: The proliferation of jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) highlights the need for robust security measures. However, in multi-round dialogues, malicious intentions may be hidden in interactions, leading LLMs to be more prone to produce harmful responses. In this paper, we propose the \textbf{M}ulti-\textbf{T}urn \textbf{S}afety \textbf{A}lignment (\ourapproach) framework, to address the challenge of securing LLMs in multi-round interactions. It consists of two stages: In the thought-guided attack learning stage, the red-team model learns about thought-guided multi-round jailbreak attacks to generate adversarial prompts. In the adversarial iterative optimization stage, the red-team model and the target model continuously improve their respective capabilities in interaction. Furthermore, we introduce a multi-turn reinforcement learning algorithm based on future rewards to enhance the robustness of safety alignment. Experimental results show that the red-team model exhibits state-of-the-art attack capabilities, while the target model significantly improves its performance on safety benchmarks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to multi-turn jailbreak attacks, where malicious intent is concealed across dialogue turns. It proposes MTSA, a two-stage framework combining thought-guided attack learning and adversarial iterative optimization to train a red-team model and improve target model safety. Experiments show that the red-team model achieves state-of-the-art attack capability and the target model significantly improves on safety benchmarks, enhanced by a multi-turn RL algorithm with future rewards. This work directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment in multi-turn scenarios, demonstrating that iterative adversarial training can harden models against such attacks, thereby providing evidence that alignment can be made more robust through targeted red-teaming.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型在多轮对话中容易遭受隐藏恶意意图的越狱攻击的问题。提出MTSA框架，包含思维引导攻击学习和对抗迭代优化两个阶段，训练红队模型并提升目标模型安全性。实验显示红队模型达到顶尖攻击能力，目标模型在安全基准上显著提升，多轮强化学习算法进一步增强了鲁棒性。该工作直接应对多轮场景下安全对齐的脆弱性，证明通过迭代对抗训练可以硬化模型抵御此类攻击，为对齐的鲁棒性建设提供了证据。

papers.title: Improve Safety Training of Large Language Models with Safety-Critical Singular Vectors Localization
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has brought about increased concerns regarding their safety, especially as adversaries develop jailbreak techniques to bypass LLMs’ safety mechanism. Although recent work on safety training with modules such as low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to resist jailbreaks shows promise, these approaches can inadvertently degrade a model’s general utility.
