In this paper, we propose a novel plug-and-play method that mitigates the impact of safety training on model utility by explicitly locating and leveraging safety-critical singular vectors, which only contribute to safety, within the model’s parameter space. We quantify the safety-criticality of each singular vector as the difference of their importance for safety and utility measured by a corresponding low-rank projection. The top scored singular vectors are located as safety-critical and are used to initialize the LoRA modules within existing safety training methods in a plug-and-play manner, thereby constraining the training updates within safety-critical parameters. Additionally, we propose a dynamic rank number determination strategy to further reduce parameter overhead. Experiments on HarmBench with multiple jailbreak methods validate the effectiveness of our approach in safety training, while evaluations on several utility benchmarks demonstrate that our method successfully mitigates the adverse impact of safety training on model utility, enhancing the utility performance of the evaluated safety training baselines.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses that existing safety training methods like LoRA can inadvertently reduce a model's general utility while defending against jailbreaks. The authors propose a plug-and-play method that locates safety-critical singular vectors in the model's parameter space and uses them to constrain LoRA updates, thereby preserving utility. Evaluations on HarmBench and utility benchmarks show that the method enhances safety against multiple jailbreaks while mitigating the utility degradation observed in safety training baselines. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of whether post-training safety alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对现有安全训练方法（如LoRA）在防御越狱攻击时可能损害模型通用实用性的问题。作者提出一种即插即用的方法，通过在模型参数空间中定位仅对安全性有贡献的安全关键奇异向量，并利用它们约束LoRA更新，从而保持实用性。在HarmBench和多个实用基准上的评估表明，该方法能增强对多种越狱攻击的安全性，同时减轻安全训练基线中的实用性能下降。该论文推动了安全对齐方法的发展，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否稳健或易被绕过这一脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Cross-model Transferability among Large Language Models on the Platonic Representations of Concepts
papers.abstract: Understanding the inner workings of Large Language Models (LLMs) is a critical research frontier. Prior research has shown that a single LLM's concept representations can be captured as steering vectors (SVs), enabling the control of LLM behavior (e.g., towards generating harmful content). Our work takes a novel approach by exploring the intricate relationships between concept representations across different LLMs, drawing an intriguing parallel to Plato's Allegory of the Cave. In particular, we introduce a linear transformation method to bridge these representations and present three key findings: 1) Concept representations across different LLMs can be effectively aligned using simple linear transformations, enabling efficient cross-model transfer and behavioral control via SVs. 2) This linear transformation generalizes across concepts, facilitating alignment and control of SVs representing different concepts across LLMs. 3) A weak-to-strong transferability exists between LLM concept representations, whereby SVs extracted from smaller LLMs can effectively control the behavior of larger LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the transferability of concept representations (steering vectors) across different Large Language Models, framing them as 'Platonic representations'. It proposes a simple linear transformation to align these vectors between models, enabling cross-model behavioral control. Experiments show effective alignment that generalizes across concepts and demonstrates weak-to-strong transfer, where vectors from smaller models control larger ones. While not directly testing alignment robustness, the finding that steering vectors transfer readily suggests a potential shared vulnerability—if one model’s vectors can be used to manipulate another, alignment might be more fragile than previously assumed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了不同大语言模型之间概念表征（引导向量）的可迁移性，将其类比于‘柏拉图式表征’。提出了一种简单的线性变换来对齐模型间的引导向量，实现了跨模型的行为控制。实验表明，这种对齐方法有效且能泛化到不同概念，并展现出弱模型到强模型的迁移能力。虽然未直接测试对齐鲁棒性，但引导向量的可迁移性暗示了一种潜在的共享脆弱性——若一个模型的向量能操控另一个模型，对齐可能比预想的更脆弱。

papers.title: Internal Value Alignment in Large Language Models through Controlled Value Vector Activation
papers.short_title: ConVA: Internal Value Alignment in LLMs
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human values has attracted increasing attention since it provides clarity, transparency, and the ability to adapt to evolving scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a Controlled Value Vector Activation (ConVA) method that directly aligns the internal values of LLMs by interpreting how a value is encoded in their latent representations and modifies relevant activations to ensure consistent values in LLMs. To ensure an accurate and unbiased interpretation, we propose a context-controlled value vector identification method. To consistently control values without sacrificing model performance, we introduce a gated value vector activation method for effective and minimum degree of value control. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest control success rate across 10 basic values without hurting LLM performance and fluency, and ensures target values even with opposite and potentially malicious input prompts. Source code and data are available at~ https://github.com/hr-jin/ConVA.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with human values by directly manipulating their internal representations. It proposes Controlled Value Vector Activation (ConVA), which identifies how values are encoded in latent space and uses a gated activation mechanism to steer generations without degrading performance. Evaluated on 10 basic values, ConVA achieves the highest control success rate while preserving fluency and remains robust even under adversarial prompts that oppose target values. This work suggests that internal value interventions can strengthen alignment against malicious bypass attempts, contributing a more resilient alternative to surface-level fine-tuning.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型与人类价值观对齐的问题，提出了一种通过直接操控内部表征来实现对齐的方法。具体提出了受控价值向量激活（ConVA）技术：先识别价值在潜在空间中的编码方式，再通过门控激活机制引导生成，从而在不损害性能的前提下确保价值一致性。在10项基础价值观上的实验表明，ConVA取得了最高的控制成功率，保持了模型的流畅性，且即使面对对抗性或恶意提示也能维持目标价值。该工作表明，对内部价值的干预能够增强对齐的鲁棒性，为对抗绕过攻击提供了更坚韧的替代方案。

papers.title: DeAL: Decoding-time Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are nowadays expected to generate content aligned with human preferences. Current work focuses on alignment at model training time, through techniques such as Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). However, it is unclear if such methods are an effective choice to teach alignment objectives to the model. First, the inability to incorporate multiple, custom rewards and reliance on a model developer's view of universal and static principles are key limitations. Second, the reliability of such approaches is also questionable (e.g. susceptibility to jailbreaking even after safety training). To address these issues, we propose DeAL, a framework that allows the user to customize reward functions and enables Decoding-time Alignment of LLMs (DeAL). At its core, we view decoding as a heuristic-guided search process and facilitate the use of a wide variety of alignment objectives. Our experiments with programmatic constraints such as keyword and length constraints, and abstract objectives such as harmlessness and helpfulness, show that we can DeAL with fine-grained trade-offs and improve adherence to alignment objectives. Lastly, we demonstrate that DeAL is largely complementary to existing alignment strategies, and can be effectively paired with RLHF and prompting techniques to achieve better alignment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses limitations of training-time alignment methods like RLHF, including the inability to incorporate multiple custom rewards and susceptibility to jailbreaking. It proposes DeAL, a decoding-time framework that treats text generation as heuristic search guided by user-defined reward functions, enabling fine-grained control over alignment objectives. Experiments with programmatic constraints (keyword, length) and abstract objectives (harmlessness, helpfulness) show DeAL improves adherence to trade-offs and complements RLHF/prompting. By revealing jailbreaking vulnerabilities in RLHF and offering a decoding-time mitigation, DeAL provides partial evidence for the fragility of post-training alignment, though its primary contribution is advancing alignment methodology rather than systematically analyzing fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了训练时对齐方法（如RLHF）的局限性，包括无法融入多重自定义奖励和易受越狱攻击影响。提出DeAL框架，在解码时将文本生成视为由用户定义奖励函数指导的启发式搜索，从而实现对对齐目标的细粒度控制。实验表明，DeAL在关键词、长度等程序性约束以及无害性、有用性等抽象目标上改善了权衡，并能与RLHF和提示技术互补。通过揭示RLHF的越狱漏洞并提供解码时缓解措施，DeAL部分证实了训练后对齐的脆弱性，但其主要贡献是推进对齐方法论，而非系统研究脆弱性。

papers.title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly being deployed as conversational assistants capable of performing complex real-world tasks through tool integration. This enhanced ability to interact with external systems and process various data sources, while powerful, introduces significant security vulnerabilities. In particular, indirect prompt injection attacks pose a critical threat, where malicious instructions embedded within external data sources can manipulate agents to deviate from user intentions. While existing defenses based on rule constraints, source spotlighting, and authentication protocols show promise, they struggle to maintain robust security while preserving task functionality. We propose a novel and orthogonal perspective that reframes agent security from preventing harmful actions to ensuring task alignment, requiring every agent action to serve user objectives. Based on this insight, we develop Task Shield, a test-time defense mechanism that systematically verifies whether each instruction and tool call contributes to user-specified goals. Through experiments on the AgentDojo benchmark, we demonstrate that Task Shield reduces attack success rates (2.07\%) while maintaining high task utility (69.79\%) on GPT-4o.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses indirect prompt injection attacks on LLM agents, where external data can manipulate agent actions away from user intentions. It proposes Task Shield, a test-time defense that systematically enforces task alignment by verifying that every instruction and tool call serves user-specified goals. Evaluated on the AgentDojo benchmark with GPT-4o, Task Shield reduces attack success rate to 2.07% while retaining 69.79% task utility. This work strengthens post-training safety alignment by adding a robustness layer against injection attacks, but it does not directly investigate whether alignment itself is inherently fragile; rather, it provides a practical defense that makes alignment harder to bypass in agent settings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决LLM智能体面临的间接提示注入攻击问题，即外部数据中的恶意指令可操纵智能体偏离用户意图。提出Task Shield，一种测试时防御机制，通过系统性地验证每条指令和工具调用是否服务于用户指定目标来强制任务对齐。在AgentDojo基准上使用GPT-4o进行评估，Task Shield将攻击成功率降至2.07%，同时保持69.79%的任务效用。该工作通过为注入攻击添加鲁棒层来增强训练后安全对齐，但未直接研究对齐本身是否脆弱；而是提供了一种实用的防御方法，使得在智能体场景中绕过对齐更加困难。

papers.title: HiddenDetect: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks against Multimodal Large Language Models via Monitoring Hidden States
papers.abstract: The integration of additional modalities increases the susceptibility of large vision-language models (LVLMs) to safety risks, such as jailbreak attacks, compared to their language-only counterparts. While existing research primarily focuses on post-hoc alignment techniques, the underlying safety mechanisms within LVLMs remain largely unexplored. In this work , we investigate whether LVLMs inherently encode safety-relevant signals within their internal activations during inference. Our findings reveal that LVLMs exhibit distinct activation patterns when processing unsafe prompts, which can be leveraged to detect and mitigate adversarial inputs without requiring extensive fine-tuning. Building on this insight, we introduce HiddenDetect, a novel tuning-free framework that harnesses internal model activations to enhance safety. Experimental results show that HiddenDetect surpasses state-of-the-art methods in detecting jailbreak attacks against LVLMs. By utilizing intrinsic safety-aware patterns, our method provides an efficient and scalable solution for strengthening LVLM robustness against multimodal threats. Our code and data will be released publicly.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the safety mechanisms of large vision-language models (LVLMs) against jailbreak attacks, discovering that internal activations encode distinct signals for unsafe prompts. The authors propose HiddenDetect, a tuning-free framework that monitors these hidden states during inference to detect and mitigate adversarial inputs without fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that HiddenDetect outperforms existing methods in jailbreak detection, offering an efficient and scalable defense. By leveraging intrinsic safety patterns rather than relying solely on post-hoc alignment, this work implies that alignment alone may be insufficient, providing evidence for the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大型视觉-语言模型（LVLMs）对抗越狱攻击的安全机制，发现模型内部激活对不安全提示编码了独特的信号。作者提出了HiddenDetect，一种无需微调的框架，通过监控推理过程中的隐藏状态来检测和缓解对抗性输入。实验结果表明，HiddenDetect在检测越狱攻击方面优于现有方法，提供了一种高效且可扩展的防御。通过利用内在的安全模式而非仅依赖事后对齐，该工作暗示仅靠对齐可能不足，为后训练安全对齐的脆弱性提供了证据。

papers.title: Binary Classifier Optimization for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: BCO: LLM Alignment from Binary Feedback
papers.abstract: In real-world services such as ChatGPT, aligning models based on user feedback is crucial for improving model performance. However, due to the simplicity and convenience of providing feedback, users typically offer only basic binary signals, such as 'thumbs-up' or 'thumbs-down'. Most existing alignment research, on the other hand, relies on preference-based approaches that require both positive and negative responses as a pair. We propose Binary Classifier Optimization (BCO), a technique that effectively aligns LLMs using only binary feedback. BCO trains a binary classifier, where the logit serves as an implicit reward, effectively minimizing the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) loss. We demonstrate that the binary cross-entropy loss employed in classifier training acts as an upper bound for the DPO loss. Additionally, a novel reward shift technique further minimizes the gap between the losses. We validate our methodology in two settings: first, on a paired preference dataset, where our method performs on par with DPO; and second, on a Likert-5 scale annotation dataset which stems from real users' queries. Our model consistently demonstrates effective and robust alignment across four base LLMs and three different datasets, showcasing the strength of our approach to learning from binary signals.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models using only binary feedback (e.g., thumbs-up/down) rather than paired preferences. It proposes Binary Classifier Optimization (BCO), which trains a binary classifier whose logit serves as an implicit reward, minimizing the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) loss. Evaluated on paired preference datasets it matches DPO performance, and on a real-user Likert-5 dataset it shows robust alignment across four base LLMs and three datasets. This paper advances alignment methodology by enabling learning from simpler binary signals, but does not directly study the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了仅使用二元反馈（如点赞/点踩）而非配对偏好来对齐大语言模型的问题。提出了二元分类器优化（BCO）方法，通过训练二元分类器，其logit作为隐式奖励，有效最小化直接偏好优化（DPO）损失。在配对偏好数据集上性能与DPO相当，并在真实用户Likert-5评分数据集上，在四种基座模型和三个数据集上展示了一致的鲁棒对齐效果。本文通过利用更简单的二元反馈推进了对齐方法，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Language Models Resist Alignment: Evidence From Data Compression
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may exhibit unintended or undesirable behaviors. Recent works have concentrated on aligning LLMs to mitigate harmful outputs. Despite these efforts, some anomalies indicate that even a well-conducted alignment process can be easily circumvented, whether intentionally or accidentally. Does alignment fine-tuning yield have robust effects on models, or are its impacts merely superficial? In this work, we make the first exploration of this phenomenon from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. Empirically, we demonstrate the $\mathbf{elasticity}$ of post-alignment models, i.e., the tendency to revert to the behavior distribution formed during the pre-training phase upon further fine-tuning. Leveraging compression theory, we formally deduce that fine-tuning disproportionately undermines alignment relative to pre-training, potentially by orders of magnitude. We validate the presence of elasticity through experiments on models of varying types and scales. Specifically, we find that model performance declines rapidly before reverting to the pre-training distribution, after which the rate of decline drops significantly. Furthermore, we further reveal that elasticity positively correlates with the increased model size and the expansion of pre-training data. Our findings underscore the need to address the inherent elasticity of LLMs to mitigate their resistance to alignment. The model weight and code are available at pku-lm-resist-alignment.github.io.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates why aligned LLMs may revert to pre-training behaviors when fine-tuned further, a phenomenon they call 'elasticity'. They use data compression theory to prove that alignment fine-tuning is disproportionately vulnerable to being undone compared to pre-training, potentially by orders of magnitude. Experiments across model types and scales confirm elasticity: models rapidly lose alignment and revert to pre-training distributions, with elasticity increasing with model size and pre-training data. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training alignment, showing it is inherently shallow and easily undermined, reinforcing the central question about alignment's robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了对齐后的大语言模型为何会在后续微调中轻易退回到预训练行为，他们将此现象称为‘弹性’。通过运用数据压缩理论，他们证明了相对于预训练，对齐微调在后续微调中受到的破坏程度大得多，可能相差数个数量级。在不同类型和规模的模型上进行的实验验证了弹性的存在：模型性能快速下降并退回到预训练分布，且弹性随模型规模和预训练数据的增加而增强。这项工作直接回应了对齐脆弱性问题，揭示了LLM固有的对齐抵抗性，表明对齐并不稳固，容易被消解。

papers.title: VLSBench: Unveiling Visual Leakage in Multimodal Safety
papers.short_title: VLSBench: Evaluating Visual Leakage in MLLM Safety
papers.abstract: Safety concerns of Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have gradually become an important problem in various applications. Surprisingly, previous works indicate a counterintuitive phenomenon that using textual unlearning to align MLLMs achieves comparable safety performances with MLLMs aligned with image text pairs. To explain such a phenomenon, we discover a Visual Safety Information Leakage (VSIL) problem in existing multimodal safety benchmarks, i.e., the potentially risky content in the image has been revealed in the textual query. Thus, MLLMs can easily refuse these sensitive image-text pairs according to textual queries only, leading to unreliable cross-modality safety evaluation of MLLMs. We also conduct a further comparison experiment between textual alignment and multimodal alignment to highlight this drawback. To this end, we construct multimodal Visual Leakless Safety Bench (VLSBench) with 2.2k image-text pairs through an automated data pipeline. Experimental results indicate that VLSBench poses a significant challenge to both open-source and close-source MLLMs, e.g., LLaVA, Qwen2-VL and GPT-4o. Besides, we empirically compare textual and multimodal alignment methods on VLSBench and find that textual alignment is effective enough for multimodal safety scenarios with VSIL, while multimodal alignment is preferable for safety scenarios without VSIL. Code and data are released under https://github.com/AI45Lab/VLSBench
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies the Visual Safety Information Leakage (VSIL) problem in existing multimodal safety benchmarks, where risky image content is already disclosed in textual queries, allowing models to refuse based only on text. It proposes VLSBench, a visual leakless safety benchmark with 2.2k image-text pairs built via an automated pipeline to ensure evaluation relies on both modalities. Experiments show VLSBench significantly challenges state-of-the-art MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen2-VL, GPT-4o) and reveal that textual alignment suffices under VSIL, while multimodal alignment is necessary otherwise. This exposes a fragility in safety alignment: models may appear safe due to textual shortcuts, but true multimodal safety is compromised without visual leakage, indicating alignment can be a brittle module bypassable across modalities.
papers.summary_zh: 本研究发现现有多模态安全评测基准中存在视觉安全信息泄露（VSIL）问题，即图像中的风险内容已在文本查询中暴露，导致模型仅依赖文本便可拒绝回答。为此，作者构建了无视觉泄露的安全基准VLSBench，包含2200个图文对，通过自动化流水线确保安全评测依赖双模态信息。实验表明，VLSBench显著挑战了先进的多模态大模型（如LLaVA、Qwen2-VL、GPT-4o），并揭示在VSIL存在时文本对齐有效，而无VSIL时则需多模态对齐。这暴露了安全对齐的脆弱性：模型可能因文本捷径显得安全，但消除视觉泄露后其安全性显著下降，表明对齐可能是一个可被跨模态绕过的脆弱模块。

papers.title: Intuitive Fine-Tuning: Towards Simplifying Alignment into a Single Process
papers.abstract: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Preference Optimization (PO) are key processes for aligning Language Models (LMs) with human preferences post pre-training. While SFT excels in efficiency and PO in effectiveness, they are often combined sequentially without integrating their optimization objectives. This approach ignores the opportunities to bridge their paradigm gap and take the strengths from both. In this paper, we interpret SFT and PO with two sub-processes -- Preference Estimation and Transition Optimization -- defined at token level within the Markov Decision Process (MDP). This modeling shows that SFT is only a special case of PO with inferior estimation and optimization. PO estimates the model's preference by its entire generation, while SFT only scores model's subsequent predicted tokens based on prior tokens from ground truth answer. These priors deviates from model's distribution, hindering the preference estimation and transition optimization. Building on this view, we introduce Intuitive Fine-Tuning (IFT) to integrate SFT and PO into a single process. Through a temporal residual connection, IFT brings better estimation and optimization by capturing LMs'intuitive sense of its entire answers. But it solely relies on a single policy and the same volume of non-preference-labeled data as SFT. Our experiments show that IFT performs comparably or even superiorly to SFT and some typical PO methods across several tasks, particularly those require generation, reasoning, and fact-following abilities. An explainable Frozen Lake game further validates the effectiveness of IFT for getting competitive policy.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency in combining Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Preference Optimization (PO) by interpreting them as sub-processes within a Markov Decision Process, revealing SFT as a special case with inferior preference estimation. It proposes Intuitive Fine-Tuning (IFT), which integrates SFT and PO into a single process using a temporal residual connection to capture the model's intuitive sense of entire answers, relying only on a single policy and non-preference-labeled data. Evaluated on generation, reasoning, and fact-following tasks, IFT performs comparably or superiorly to SFT and typical PO methods, with additional validation on a Frozen Lake game. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过将监督微调（SFT）和偏好优化（PO）解释为马尔可夫决策过程中的子过程，揭示了SFT仅是偏好估计较差的特例，从而解决了二者顺序组合但优化目标不整合的问题。提出了直觉微调（IFT），利用时序残差连接捕捉模型对完整答案的直觉感知，将SFT和PO整合为单一过程，仅依赖单一策略和无偏好标注数据。在生成、推理和事实遵循等任务上，IFT表现与SFT及典型PO方法相当或更优，并在可解释的Frozen Lake游戏中得到验证。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: PKU-SafeRLHF: Towards Multi-Level Safety Alignment for LLMs with Human Preference
papers.abstract: In this study, we introduce the safety human preference dataset, PKU-SafeRLHF, designed to promote research on safety alignment in large language models (LLMs). As a sibling project to SafeRLHF and BeaverTails, we separate annotations of helpfulness and harmlessness for question-answering pairs, providing distinct perspectives on these coupled attributes. Overall, we provide 44.6k refined prompts and 265k question-answer pairs with safety meta-labels for 19 harm categories and three severity levels ranging from minor to severe, with answers generated by Llama-family models. Based on this, we collected 166.8k preference data, including dual-preference (helpfulness and harmlessness decoupled) and single-preference data (trade-off the helpfulness and harmlessness from scratch), respectively. Using the large-scale annotation data, we further train severity-sensitive moderation for the risk control of LLMs and safety-centric RLHF algorithms for the safety alignment of LLMs. We believe this dataset will be a valuable resource for the community, aiding in the safe deployment of LLMs. Data is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces PKU-SafeRLHF, a dataset designed to improve safety alignment in large language models by decoupling helpfulness and harmlessness annotations. It provides 44.6k prompts and 265k QA pairs with safety meta-labels across 19 harm categories and three severity levels, along with 166.8k preference data for training. The dataset is used to train severity-sensitive moderation and safety-centric RLHF algorithms. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文介绍了一个旨在通过解耦有用性和无害性标注来提升大语言模型安全对齐的数据集PKU-SafeRLHF。该数据集包含44.6k条提示、265k条问答对（附有19类伤害和三个严重级别的安全元标签）以及166.8k条偏好数据，用于训练。该数据集被用于训练严重程度敏感的审核模块和以安全为中心的RLHF算法。这项工作通过提供多级安全的结构化资源推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Rethinking Reward Model Evaluation Through the Lens of Reward Overoptimization
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) play a crucial role in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), aligning model behavior with human preferences. However, existing benchmarks for reward models show a weak correlation with the performance of optimized policies, suggesting that they fail to accurately assess the true capabilities of RMs. To bridge this gap, we explore several evaluation designs through the lens of reward overoptimization\textemdash a phenomenon that captures both how well the reward model aligns with human preferences and the dynamics of the learning signal it provides to the policy. The results highlight three key findings on how to construct a reliable benchmark: (i) it is important to minimize differences between chosen and rejected responses beyond correctness, (ii) evaluating reward models requires multiple comparisons across a wide range of chosen and rejected responses, and (iii) given that reward models encounter responses with diverse representations, responses should be sourced from a variety of models. However, we also observe that a extremely high correlation with degree of overoptimization leads to comparatively lower correlation with certain downstream performance. Thus, when designing a benchmark, it is desirable to use the degree of overoptimization as a useful tool, rather than the end goal.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the poor correlation between existing reward model (RM) benchmarks and downstream policy performance, revealing that current evaluations fail to capture true RM capabilities due to reward overoptimization. The authors propose evaluation designs that minimize non-correctness differences between chosen and rejected responses, require multiple comparisons across diverse responses, and source responses from various models to construct a more reliable benchmark. They find that high correlation with overoptimization can reduce correlation with downstream performance, advocating for using overoptimization degree as a diagnostic tool rather than the ultimate metric. This work advances RM evaluation methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment; it focuses on improving the assessment tools that underpin alignment training.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有奖励模型基准与下游策略性能相关性差的问题，揭示出现有评估因奖励过度优化而无法准确反映RM能力。作者提出评估设计：最小化选中与拒绝回复间除正确性外的差异、基于多样回复进行多次比较、并从多个模型中采样回复，以构建更可靠的基准。研究发现，与过度优化程度的高相关性可能降低与下游性能的相关性，主张将过度优化程度作为诊断工具而非最终目标。本文推进了RM评估方法，但未直接探究安全对齐的脆弱性；侧重提升支撑对齐训练的评估工具。

papers.title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs
papers.abstract: Safety is critical to the usage of large language models (LLMs). Multiple techniques such as data filtering and supervised fine-tuning have been developed to strengthen LLM safety. However, currently known techniques presume that corpora used for safety alignment of LLMs are solely interpreted by semantics. This assumption, however, does not hold in real-world applications, which leads to severe vulnerabilities in LLMs. For example, users of forums often use ASCII art, a form of text-based art, to convey image information. In this paper, we propose a novel ASCII art-based jailbreak attack and introduce a comprehensive benchmark Vision-in-Text Challenge (ViTC) to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics. We show that five SOTA LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama2) struggle to recognize prompts provided in the form of ASCII art. Based on this observation, we develop the jailbreak attack ArtPrompt, which leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs. ArtPrompt only requires black-box access to the victim LLMs, making it a practical attack. We evaluate ArtPrompt on five SOTA LLMs, and show that ArtPrompt can effectively and efficiently induce undesired behaviors from all five LLMs. Our code is available at https://github.com/uw-nsl/ArtPrompt.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies that safety alignment in LLMs assumes prompts are interpreted solely by semantics, but real-world inputs like ASCII art can violate this assumption, leading to vulnerabilities. It proposes ArtPrompt, a jailbreak attack that masks malicious prompts as ASCII art to bypass safety filters, and introduces the Vision-in-Text Challenge (ViTC) benchmark to evaluate LLM recognition of non-semantic prompts. Evaluated on five SOTA LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, Llama2), ArtPrompt effectively induces undesired behaviors with only black-box access, demonstrating high attack success. This paper directly shows that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be bypassed by exploiting the LLMs' inability to interpret ASCII art, revealing a weakness in the alignment's reliance on semantic parsing.
papers.summary_zh: 论文指出大语言模型的安全对齐假设提示仅通过语义解释，但ASCII艺术等现实输入会违反这一假设，导致漏洞。提出ArtPrompt攻击，将恶意提示伪装成ASCII艺术以绕过安全过滤器，并引入ViTC基准评估LLM对非语义提示的识别能力。在五个SOTA LLM上评估，ArtPrompt仅需黑盒访问即能有效诱导不良行为，攻击成功率很高。该论文直接表明训练后的安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过利用LLM无法解释ASCII艺术的弱点绕过，揭示了对齐依赖语义解析的脆弱性。

papers.title: Contrastive Perplexity for Controlled Generation: An Application in Detoxifying Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The generation of toxic content by large language models (LLMs) remains a critical challenge for the safe deployment of language technology. We propose a novel framework for implicit knowledge editing and controlled text generation by fine-tuning LLMs with a prototype-based contrastive perplexity objective. Central to our method is the construction of hard negatives - toxic outputs that are generated through adversarial paraphrasing to be semantically similar and model probability to their non-toxic counterparts. By training on these challenging and realistic pairs, our approach ensures robust and stable contrastive optimization. Experimental results in the domain of detoxification demonstrate that our method significantly reduces toxic generation while maintaining strong performance on downstream tasks such as commonsense reasoning and reading comprehension. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of exploiting hard negatives for attribute-aware fine-tuning.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of toxic content generation by large language models. It proposes a novel fine-tuning framework using a prototype-based contrastive perplexity objective with hard negatives constructed via adversarial paraphrasing, ensuring semantically similar but toxic counterparts. Experiments in detoxification show significant reduction in toxic generation while maintaining performance on commonsense reasoning and reading comprehension. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型生成有毒内容的问题。提出一种新颖的微调框架，利用基于原型对比困惑度的目标，并通过对抗性释义构建语义相似的有毒硬负样本。解毒领域的实验表明，该方法显著减少了有毒生成，同时保持常识推理和阅读理解等下游任务的性能。该论文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: LLMs Caught in the Crossfire: Malware Requests and Jailbreak Challenges
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has heightened concerns about their security, particularly their vulnerability to jailbreak attacks that leverage crafted prompts to generate malicious outputs. While prior research has been conducted on general security capabilities of LLMs, their specific susceptibility to jailbreak attacks in code generation remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose MalwareBench, a benchmark dataset containing 3,520 jailbreaking prompts for malicious code-generation, designed to evaluate LLM robustness against such threats. MalwareBench is based on 320 manually crafted malicious code generation requirements, covering 11 jailbreak methods and 29 code functionality categories. Experiments show that mainstream LLMs exhibit limited ability to reject malicious code-generation requirements, and the combination of multiple jailbreak methods further reduces the model's security capabilities: specifically, the average rejection rate for malicious content is 60.93%, dropping to 39.92% when combined with jailbreak attack algorithms. Our work highlights that the code security capabilities of LLMs still pose significant challenges.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates LLM vulnerability to jailbreak attacks for malicious code generation. It introduces MalwareBench, a benchmark of 3,520 prompts spanning 11 jailbreak methods and 29 code categories. Experiments reveal that mainstream LLMs show limited rejection ability, with an average rejection rate of 60.93% that declines to 39.92% when combining multiple jailbreak techniques. This demonstrates that safety alignment is fragile and can be readily bypassed, supporting the notion that post-training safeguards are not robust against adversarial prompts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型在恶意代码生成任务中面对越狱攻击的脆弱性。提出了 MalwareBench，一个包含 3,520 个提示的基准数据集，涵盖 11 种越狱方法和 29 个代码类别。实验表明主流模型拒绝能力有限，平均拒绝率仅 60.93%，结合多种越狱技术后降至 39.92%。该工作揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，表明后训练防护易被绕过，直接回应了安全性对齐是否稳健的核心问题。

papers.title: Optimal Transport-Based Token Weighting scheme for Enhanced Preference Optimization
papers.short_title: OTPO: Optimal Transport Token Weighting for DPO
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has emerged as a promising framework for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences by directly optimizing the log-likelihood difference between chosen and rejected responses. However, existing methods assign equal importance to all tokens in the response, while humans focus on more meaningful parts. This leads to suboptimal preference optimization, as irrelevant or noisy tokens disproportionately influence DPO loss. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{O}ptimal \textbf{T}ransport-based token weighting scheme for enhancing direct \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization (OTPO). By emphasizing semantically meaningful token pairs and de-emphasizing less relevant ones, our method introduces a context-aware token weighting scheme that yields a more contrastive reward difference estimate. This adaptive weighting enhances reward stability, improves interpretability, and ensures that preference optimization focuses on meaningful differences between responses. Extensive experiments have validated OTPO's effectiveness in improving instruction-following ability across various settings\footnote{Code is available at https://github.com/Mimasss2/OTPO.}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) where all tokens are equally weighted, causing noisy tokens to distort preference learning. It proposes OTPO, an optimal transport-based token weighting scheme that adaptively emphasizes semantically meaningful token pairs for more contrastive reward estimation. Experiments on instruction-following tasks demonstrate improved alignment performance. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了直接偏好优化（DPO）中所有标记被平等对待，导致噪声标记干扰偏好学习的问题。它提出了OTPO，一种基于最优传输的标记加权方案，自适应地强调语义上有意义的标记对，以得到更具对比性的奖励估计。在指令遵循任务上的实验表明，对齐性能得到提升。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models by On-Policy Self-Judgment
papers.abstract: Existing approaches for aligning large language models with human preferences face a trade-off that requires a separate reward model (RM) for on-policy learning. In this paper, we present a novel alignment framework, SELF-JUDGE that (1) does on-policy learning and 2) is parameter efficient, as it does not require an additional RM for evaluating the samples for on-policy learning. To this end, we propose Judge-augmented Supervised Fine-Tuning (JSFT) to train a single model to act as both a policy and a judge. Specifically, we view the pairwise judgment task, choosing the better response from a response pair, as a special case of the instruction-following task. The resulting model can judge preferences of on-the-fly responses from current policy initialized from itself. Experimental results show the efficacy of SELF-JUDGE, outperforming baselines in preference benchmarks. We also show that the rejecting sampling by itself can improve performance further without an additional evaluator.
papers.summary_en: Existing alignment approaches often require a separate reward model for on-policy learning, creating a parameter inefficiency. This paper proposes SELF-JUDGE, a framework that trains a single model to function as both policy and judge via Judge-augmented Supervised Fine-Tuning (JSFT), where pairwise judgment is cast as instruction-following. On preference benchmarks, SELF-JUDGE outperforms baselines and can further improve through rejection sampling without an external evaluator. While it makes on-policy alignment more parameter-efficient, the work does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有对齐方法通常需要单独的奖励模型进行策略学习，导致参数效率低下。本文提出SELF-JUDGE框架，通过Judge-augmented Supervised Fine-Tuning (JSFT)训练单一模型同时作为策略和裁判，将成对判断视为指令跟随任务。在偏好基准测试中，SELF-JUDGE优于基线模型，且无需额外评估器的拒绝采样可进一步提升性能。该方法使策略对齐更参数高效，但未直接研究对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Query-Efficient Black-Box Red Teaming via Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: The deployment of large-scale generative models is often restricted by their potential risk of causing harm to users in unpredictable ways. We focus on the problem of black-box red teaming, where a red team generates test cases and interacts with the victim model to discover a diverse set of failures with limited query access. Existing red teaming methods construct test cases based on human supervision or language model (LM) and query all test cases in a brute-force manner without incorporating any information from past evaluations, resulting in a prohibitively large number of queries.To this end, we propose Bayesian red teaming (BRT), novel query-efficient black-box red teaming methods based on Bayesian optimization, which iteratively identify diverse positive test cases leading to model failures by utilizing the pre-defined user input pool and the past evaluations. Experimental results on various user input pools demonstrate that our method consistently finds a significantly larger number of diverse positive test cases under the limited query budget than the baseline methods.The source code is available at https://github.com/snu-mllab/Bayesian-Red-Teaminghttps://github.com/snu-mllab/Bayesian-Red-Teaming.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of black-box red teaming, where an attacker aims to efficiently discover diverse failure cases of a generative model under a limited query budget. It proposes Bayesian red teaming (BRT), a novel approach based on Bayesian optimization that iteratively selects test cases from a pre-defined pool by leveraging past evaluation results, thereby avoiding brute-force querying. Experiments on various user input pools demonstrate that BRT consistently finds significantly more diverse positive test cases than baseline methods when given the same query budget. By enabling efficient discovery of diverse model failures, this work provides evidence for the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as it shows that safety measures can be systematically bypassed even with limited black-box access.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注黑盒红队测试问题，即在有限查询次数下生成测试用例以发现受害者模型的多样化失败模式。提出了贝叶斯红队测试（BRT）方法，利用贝叶斯优化从预定义的用户输入池中迭代地选取测试用例，充分利用历史评估信息。在多种用户输入池上的实验表明，相较于基线方法，BRT在相同查询预算下能够发现明显更多样的正样本（导致模型失败的测试用例）。通过展示如何高效地发现模型失败案例，该工作揭示了后训练安全对齐措施的脆弱性，表明即使在有限查询的黑盒条件下，对齐也可能被绕过，从而为对齐的脆弱性提供了证据。

papers.title: A Survey of Post-Training Scaling in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable proficiency in understanding and generating human natural languages, mainly owing to the "scaling law" that optimizes relationships among language modeling loss, model parameters, and pre-trained tokens. However, with the exhaustion of high-quality internet corpora and increasing computational demands, the sustainability of pre-training scaling needs to be addressed. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of post-training scaling, an emergent paradigm aiming to relieve the limitations of traditional pre-training by focusing on the alignment phase, which traditionally accounts for a minor fraction of the total training computation. Our survey categorizes post-training scaling into three key methodologies: Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning from Feedback (RLxF), and Test-time Compute (TTC). We provide an in-depth analysis of the motivation behind post-training scaling, the scalable variants of these methodologies, and a comparative discussion against traditional approaches. By examining the latest advancements, identifying promising application scenarios, and highlighting unresolved issues, we seek a coherent understanding and map future research trajectories in the landscape of post-training scaling for LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper surveys post-training scaling, an emergent paradigm to address the sustainability limits of traditional pre-training scaling by focusing on the alignment phase. It categorizes key methodologies into Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning from Feedback (RLxF), and Test-time Compute (TTC), analyzing their motivations and scalable variants. Through a comprehensive literature review, it identifies latest advancements, promising applications, and unresolved issues, offering a coherent understanding of the field. This survey advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文综述了后训练扩展这一新兴范式，旨在通过聚焦对齐阶段来解决传统预训练扩展的可持续性问题。它将关键方法分类为监督微调（SFT）、基于反馈的强化学习（RLxF）和测试时计算（TTC），并分析了其动机与可扩展变体。通过全面的文献回顾，本文梳理了最新进展、有前景的应用和尚未解决的问题，为该领域提供了系统性理解。该综述推动了对齐方法论的发展，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Why Safeguarded Ships Run Aground? Aligned Large Language Models' Safety Mechanisms Tend to Be Anchored in The Template Region
papers.abstract: The safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) remains vulnerable, as their initial behavior can be easily jailbroken by even relatively simple attacks. Since infilling a fixed template between the input instruction and initial model output is a common practice for existing LLMs, we hypothesize that this template is a key factor behind their vulnerabilities: LLMs' safety-related decision-making overly relies on the aggregated information from the template region, which largely influences these models' safety behavior. We refer to this issue as template-anchored safety alignment. In this paper, we conduct extensive experiments and verify that template-anchored safety alignment is widespread across various aligned LLMs. Our mechanistic analyses demonstrate how it leads to models' susceptibility when encountering inference-time jailbreak attacks. Furthermore, we show that detaching safety mechanisms from the template region is promising in mitigating vulnerabilities to jailbreak attacks. We encourage future research to develop more robust safety alignment techniques that reduce reliance on the template region.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the fragility of safety-aligned LLMs against jailbreak attacks, attributing it to 'template-anchored safety alignment'—over-reliance on the fixed template region. Extensive experiments and mechanistic analyses confirm its prevalence and role in causing vulnerability to inference-time jailbreaks. The authors show that detaching safety mechanisms from this region is a promising mitigation, highlighting a fundamental fragility in post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型在越狱攻击下的脆弱性，将其归因于“模板锚定安全对齐”——即模型的安全决策过度依赖预设模板区域的信息。通过大量实验和机制分析，作者证明了该现象在多个对齐模型中普遍存在，并揭示了其导致推理时越狱攻击易感性的机理。作者表明将安全机制与模板区域解耦是一种有效的缓解措施，揭示了后训练安全对齐的根本脆弱性。

papers.title: ELBA-Bench: An Efficient Learning Backdoor Attacks Benchmark for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Generative large language models are crucial in natural language processing, but they are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where subtle triggers compromise their behavior. Although backdoor attacks against LLMs are constantly emerging, existing benchmarks remain limited in terms of sufficient coverage of attack, metric system integrity, backdoor attack alignment. And existing pre-trained backdoor attacks are idealized in practice due to resource access constraints. Therefore we establish $\textit{ELBA-Bench}$, a comprehensive and unified framework that allows attackers to inject backdoor through parameter efficient fine-tuning ($\textit{e.g.,}$ LoRA) or without fine-tuning techniques ($\textit{e.g.,}$ In-context-learning). $\textit{ELBA-Bench}$ provides over 1300 experiments encompassing the implementations of 12 attack methods, 18 datasets, and 12 LLMs. Extensive experiments provide new invaluable findings into the strengths and limitations of various attack strategies. For instance, PEFT attack consistently outperform without fine-tuning approaches in classification tasks while showing strong cross-dataset generalization with optimized triggers boosting robustness; Task-relevant backdoor optimization techniques or attack prompts along with clean and adversarial demonstrations can enhance backdoor attack success while preserving model performance on clean samples. Additionally, we introduce a universal toolbox designed for standardized backdoor attack research, with the goal of propelling further progress in this vital area.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of comprehensive benchmarks for backdoor attacks on LLMs, where subtle triggers compromise model behavior. It proposes ELBA-Bench, a unified framework that evaluates 12 attack methods using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA) or without fine-tuning (e.g., in-context learning) across 18 datasets and 12 LLMs. Extensive experiments show that PEFT attacks outperform fine-tuning-free methods in classification tasks, with optimized triggers boosting cross-dataset generalization, and that task-relevant backdoor techniques enhance attack success while preserving clean performance. By demonstrating efficient backdoor injection, this work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be easily bypassed, supporting the SoK's central question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型后门攻击基准测试覆盖面不足的问题，此类攻击通过微小触发器破坏模型行为。它提出了ELBA-Bench，一个统一框架，通过参数高效微调（如LoRA）或无微调技术（如上下文学习）在18个数据集和12个LLM上评估了12种攻击方法。大量实验表明，PEFT攻击在分类任务中始终优于无微调方法，优化触发器可提升跨数据集泛化能力，任务相关的后门技术能在保持干净性能的同时提高攻击成功率。通过展示高效的后门注入方法，该工作直接证明了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，易于被绕过，呼应了系统化知识的核心问题。

papers.title: Generative Reward Modeling via Synthetic Criteria Preference Learning
papers.abstract: Generative Reward Models (GenRMs) leverage synthesized Chains of Thought (CoT) to reduce the need for massive labeled data, but this approach introduces risks of overoptimization due to the inability to guarantee the correctness of the CoTs. Identifying and optimizing unexpected behaviors within these synthesized CoT remains a challenge, as it heavily depends on precise annotations of intermediate behavior, similar to process supervision. In this work, we introduce a criteria-based preference tree for reward modeling, where each path in the tree represents a reasoning trajectory based on synthesized criteria. Crucially, each reasoning trajectory can be independently optimized through RL algorithm. These fine-grained process reward signals are derived from the inference-time computations and predefined rules, eliminating the need for human supervision. In experiments, SyncPL 1 showed significant improvements over baselines on multiple human preference benchmarks. We further demonstrate that synthesized data can be learned us-ing a long CoT format, analogous to an o1-like model, further enhancing performance while keeping stability and efficiency during training.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overoptimization risk in generative reward models caused by unreliable synthesized chains of thought. It proposes a criteria-based preference tree where each reasoning trajectory is independently optimized via RL, using fine-grained process rewards derived from inference-time computations and predefined rules without human supervision. Evaluated on multiple human preference benchmarks, the method SyncPL significantly outperforms baselines, and performance is further enhanced with a long chain-of-thought format. While this work strengthens alignment methodology by mitigating overoptimization, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了生成式奖励模型中因合成思维链不可靠而导致的过度优化风险。提出基于准则的偏好树，其中每个推理轨迹可通过强化学习独立优化，利用推理时计算和预定义规则派生的细粒度过程奖励，无需人工监督。在多个人类偏好基准上，方法 SyncPL 显著优于基线，且长思维链格式进一步提升了性能。这项工作通过减轻过度优化增强了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: "Yes, My LoRD." Guiding Language Model Extraction with Locality Reinforced Distillation
papers.abstract: Model extraction attacks (MEAs) on large language models (LLMs) have received increasing attention in recent research. However, existing attack methods typically adapt the extraction strategies originally developed for deep neural networks (DNNs). They neglect the underlying inconsistency between the training tasks of MEA and LLM alignment, leading to suboptimal attack performance. To tackle this issue, we propose Locality Reinforced Distillation (LoRD), a novel model extraction algorithm specifically designed for LLMs. In particular, LoRD employs a newly defined policy-gradient-style training task that utilizes the responses of victim model as the signal to guide the crafting of preference for the local model. Theoretical analyses demonstrate that I) The convergence procedure of LoRD in model extraction is consistent with the alignment procedure of LLMs, and II) LoRD can reduce query complexity while mitigating watermark protection through our exploration-based stealing. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of our method in extracting various state-of-the-art commercial LLMs. Our code is available at: https://github.com/liangzid/LoRD-MEA .
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses model extraction attacks on large language models (LLMs), where existing methods suffer from inconsistency between the extraction training and LLM alignment. It proposes LoRD, a locality reinforced distillation algorithm that uses victim model responses to guide the local model's preference crafting through a policy-gradient-style task. Theoretical analyses show that LoRD's convergence aligns with LLM alignment, reducing query complexity and mitigating watermark protections. Experiments demonstrate superior extraction of commercial LLMs, highlighting that alignment can be stolen, indicating fragility in post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型（LLM）的模型提取攻击，指出现有方法忽略了提取训练与LLM对齐之间的不一致性，导致攻击效果不佳。提出了LoRD，一种局部性强化蒸馏算法，通过策略梯度式任务，利用受害者模型的响应信号指导本地模型的偏好构建。理论分析证明LoRD的收敛过程与LLM对齐一致，能降低查询复杂度并削弱水印保护。大量实验验证了其在提取多种前沿商业LLM上的优越性，表明对齐可被窃取，揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Cultural Learning-Based Culture Adaptation of Language Models
papers.abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) to diverse cultural values is a challenging task, as existing LLMs often reflect the values of specific groups by default, and potentially causing harm to others. In this paper, we present CLCA, a novel framework for enhancing LLM alignment with cultural values based on cultural learning. The framework leverages simulated social interactions to generate conversations in which LLMs engage in role-playing within culturally adapted social scenarios, capturing implicit cultural norms for model fine-tuning. CLCA improves cultural value alignment across various model architectures measured using World Value Survey data, demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed approach. Our results provide early evidence that understanding intent and social interactions can enhance cultural value adaptation in LLMs, highlighting the promise of training approaches based on cultural learning.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the challenge of adapting large language models (LLMs) to diverse cultural values, as they often default to the values of specific groups. It proposes CLCA, a framework that leverages simulated social interactions and role-playing to generate culturally nuanced conversations for fine-tuning, capturing implicit cultural norms. Evaluated using World Value Survey data, CLCA improves cultural value alignment across various model architectures, demonstrating the effectiveness of cultural learning-based adaptation. The work advances alignment methodology for cultural values but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型（LLM）适应多元文化价值观的难题，因其常默认反映特定群体价值观。提出CLCA框架，利用模拟社会互动和角色扮演生成文化场景对话以进行微调，捕捉隐性文化规范。基于世界价值观调查数据的评估表明，CLCA提高了不同模型架构的文化价值观对齐度，验证了基于文化学习的适应方法的有效性。本文推进了文化价值观对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Dissecting Human and LLM Preferences
papers.abstract: As a relative quality comparison of model responses, human and Large Language Model (LLM) preferences serve as common alignment goals in model fine-tuning and criteria in evaluation. Yet, these preferences merely reflect broad tendencies, resulting in less explainable and controllable models with potential safety risks. In this work, we dissect the preferences of human and 32 different LLMs to understand their quantitative composition, using annotations from real-world user-model conversations for a fine-grained, scenario-wise analysis. We find that humans are less sensitive to errors, favor responses that support their stances, and show clear dislike when models admit their limits. On the contrary, advanced LLMs like GPT-4-Turbo emphasize correctness, clarity, and harmlessness more. Additionally, LLMs of similar sizes tend to exhibit similar preferences, regardless of their training methods, and fine-tuning for alignment does not significantly alter the preferences of pretrained-only LLMs. Finally, we show that preference-based evaluation can be intentionally manipulated. In both training-free and training-based settings, aligning a model with the preferences of judges boosts scores, while injecting the least preferred properties lowers them. This results in notable score shifts: up to 0.59 on MT-Bench (1-10 scale) and 31.94 on AlpacaEval 2.0 (0-100 scale), highlighting the significant impact of this strategic adaptation. Interactive Demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/GAIR/Preference-Dissection-Visualization Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/GAIR/preference-dissection Code: https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/Preference-Dissection
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the composition of human and LLM preferences used in alignment and evaluation, which often reflect broad tendencies. Through fine-grained analysis of real-world conversations, they uncover systematic differences: humans are less sensitive to errors and dislike model admissions of limits, while advanced LLMs prioritize correctness, clarity, and harmlessness. They also find that LLM preferences cluster by model size and that alignment fine-tuning barely alters pretrained-only preferences. Crucially, they show that preference-based evaluation can be manipulated by aligning a model with judge preferences, leading to score shifts up to 0.59 on MT-Bench and 31.94 on AlpacaEval 2.0, demonstrating a fragility in using preferences as a reliable alignment metric.
papers.summary_zh: 本文剖析了用于对齐和评估的人类与LLM偏好，这些偏好往往反映宽泛的倾向。通过对真实对话的细粒度分析，他们发现系统差异：人类对错误较不敏感、反感模型承认局限，而先进LLM更强调正确性、清晰和无害。他们还发现LLM偏好按模型规模聚类，且对齐微调几乎不改变仅预训练模型的偏好。关键的是，他们表明基于偏好的评估可被操纵，通过让模型向评估者偏好对齐，能导致MT-Bench评分偏移高达0.59、AlpacaEval 2.0偏移31.94，揭示了将偏好作为可靠对齐指标的脆弱性。

papers.title: Direct Large Language Model Alignment Through Self-Rewarding Contrastive Prompt Distillation
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human expectations without human-annotated preference data is an important problem. In this paper, we propose a method to evaluate the response preference by using the output probabilities of response pairs under contrastive prompt pairs, which could achieve better performance on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA2-13B compared to RLAIF. Based on this, we propose an automatic alignment method, Direct Large Model Alignment (DLMA). First, we use contrastive prompt pairs to automatically generate preference data. Then, we continue to evaluate the generated preference data using contrastive prompt pairs and calculate a self-rewarding score. Finally, we use the DPO algorithm to effectively align LLMs by combining this self-rewarding score. In the experimental stage, our DLMA method could surpass the \texttt{RLHF} method without relying on human-annotated preference data.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models without human-annotated preference data. The proposed DLMA method automatically generates preference data using contrastive prompt pairs, assigns self-rewarding scores, and then applies Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for alignment. Experiments on LLaMA2-7B and 13B show that DLMA surpasses RLHF, achieving effective alignment without human labels. The work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决无需人工标注偏好数据的大语言模型对齐问题。提出的DLMA方法通过对比提示对自动生成偏好数据，计算自奖励分数，并结合DPO进行对齐。在LLaMA2-7B和13B上的实验表明，DLMA在不依赖人类标注的情况下超越了RLHF。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或健壮。

papers.title: HAF-RM: A Hybrid Alignment Framework for Reward Model Training
papers.abstract: The reward model has become increasingly important in alignment, assessment, and data construction for large language models (LLMs). Most existing researchers focus on enhancing reward models through data improvements, following the conventional training framework for reward models that directly optimizes the predicted rewards. In this paper, we propose a hybrid alignment framework HaF-RM for reward model training by introducing an additional constraint on token-level policy probabilities in addition to the reward score. It can simultaneously supervise the internal preference model at the token level and optimize the mapping layer of the reward model at the sequence level. Experiment results on five datasets sufficiently show the validity and effectiveness of our proposed hybrid framework for training a high-quality reward model. By decoupling the reward modeling procedure and incorporating hybrid supervision, our HaF-RM framework offers a principled and effective approach to enhancing the performance and alignment of reward models, a critical component in the responsible development of powerful language models. We release our code at https://haf-rm.github.io.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of training more effective reward models for LLM alignment. It proposes a hybrid alignment framework (HAF-RM) that combines sequence-level reward optimization with token-level policy probability constraints. Experiments on five datasets demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in producing high-quality reward models. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了训练更有效的大语言模型对齐奖励模型的问题。它提出了一种混合对齐框架（HAF-RM），该框架在序列级奖励优化基础上增加了令牌级策略概率约束。在五个数据集上的实验证明了该框架在生成高质量奖励模型方面的有效性。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Human Preferences through Representation Engineering
papers.short_title: RAHF: Representation Alignment from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is crucial for enhancing their utility in terms of helpfulness, truthfulness, safety, harmlessness, and interestingness. Existing methods for achieving this alignment often involves employing reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to fine-tune LLMs based on human labels assessing the relative quality of model responses. Nevertheless, RLHF is susceptible to instability during fine-tuning and presents challenges in implementation.Drawing inspiration from the emerging field of representation engineering (RepE), this study aims to identify relevant representations for high-level human preferences embedded in patterns of activity within an LLM, and achieve precise control of model behavior by transforming its representations. This novel approach, denoted as Representation Alignment from Human Feedback (RAHF), proves to be effective, computationally efficient, and easy to implement.Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of RAHF in not only capturing but also manipulating representations to align with a broad spectrum of human preferences or values, rather than being confined to a singular concept or function (e.g. honesty or bias). RAHF's versatility in accommodating diverse human preferences shows its potential for advancing LLM performance.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models with diverse human preferences in a stable and efficient manner. It proposes Representation Alignment from Human Feedback (RAHF), a method that identifies and transforms internal representations corresponding to human preferences, avoiding the instability of RLHF. Extensive experiments show that RAHF effectively captures and manipulates representations to align with a wide range of preferences, demonstrating computational efficiency and effectiveness. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of whether post-training safety alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型与多样化人类偏好对齐中的稳定性和效率挑战。提出了一种基于表征工程的对齐方法RAHF，通过识别和转换模型内部表征来实现对齐，避免了RLHF的不稳定性。大量实验表明，RAHF能有效捕捉并操控表征，以对齐广泛的人类偏好，同时具备计算效率和有效性。这项工作推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接涉及后训练安全对齐是否稳健或易被绕过这一脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SEA: Low-Resource Safety Alignment for Multimodal Large Language Models via Synthetic Embeddings
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have serious security vulnerabilities.While safety alignment using multimodal datasets consisting of text and data of additional modalities can effectively enhance MLLM's security, it is costly to construct these datasets. Existing low-resource security alignment methods, including textual alignment, have been found to struggle with the security risks posed by additional modalities. To address this, we propose Synthetic Embedding augmented safety Alignment (SEA), which optimizes embeddings of additional modality through gradient updates to expand textual datasets. This enables multimodal safety alignment training even when only textual data is available. Extensive experiments on image, video, and audio-based MLLMs demonstrate that SEA can synthesize a high-quality embedding on a single RTX3090 GPU within 24 seconds. SEA significantly improves the security of MLLMs when faced with threats from additional modalities. To assess the security risks introduced by video and audio, we also introduced a new benchmark called VA-SafetyBench. High attack success rates across multiple MLLMs validate its challenge. Our code and data will be available at https://github.com/ZeroNLP/SEA.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the security vulnerabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) when additional modalities (image, video, audio) introduce threats that textual safety alignment alone cannot handle. It proposes SEA, a method that uses gradient updates to optimize synthetic embeddings of additional modalities, thereby expanding textual datasets to enable multimodal safety alignment training with only text data. Evaluated on image, video, and audio MLLMs, SEA synthesizes high-quality embeddings in 24 seconds on a single GPU and significantly improves model security against multimodal threats, with a new benchmark VA-SafetyBench introduced to assess video/audio risks. While SEA advances alignment methodology by reducing resource costs, it does not directly address the fragility question of whether post-training safety alignment is robust or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的安全漏洞，特别是额外模态（图像、视频、音频）带来的威胁，而仅靠文本安全对齐无法有效应对的问题。提出SEA方法，通过对额外模态的嵌入进行梯度更新来合成嵌入，从而扩充文本数据集，使得仅用文本数据即可进行多模态安全对齐训练。在图像、视频和音频MLLM上的实验表明，SEA能在单块RTX3090上24秒内合成高质量嵌入，并显著提升模型面对多模态威胁时的安全性，同时引入了新基准VA-SafetyBench用于评估视频和音频风险。尽管SEA通过降低资源需求推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Gradient-Adaptive Policy Optimization: Towards Multi-Objective Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a powerful technique for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. However, effectively aligning LLMs with diverse human preferences remains a significant challenge, particularly when they are conflict. To address this issue, we frame human value alignment as a multi-objective optimization problem, aiming to maximize a set of potentially conflicting objectives. We introduce Gradient-Adaptive Policy Optimization (GAPO), a novel fine-tuning paradigm that employs multiple-gradient descent to align LLMs with diverse preference distributions. GAPO adaptively rescales the gradients for each objective to determine an update direction that optimally balances the trade-offs between objectives. Additionally, we introduce P-GAPO, which incorporates user preferences across different objectives and achieves Pareto solutions that better align with the user's specific needs. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that GAPO converges towards a Pareto optimal solution for multiple objectives. Empirical results on Mistral-7B show that GAPO outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in both helpfulness and harmlessness.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models with diverse and potentially conflicting human preferences. It proposes Gradient-Adaptive Policy Optimization (GAPO), a multi-objective fine-tuning paradigm that adaptively rescales gradients to balance trade-offs and converge to Pareto-optimal solutions. Evaluated on Mistral-7B, GAPO outperforms baselines on both helpfulness and harmlessness metrics. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决将大语言模型对齐到多样化且可能冲突的人类偏好这一挑战。提出梯度自适应策略优化（GAPO），一种多目标微调范式，通过自适应梯度缩放平衡各目标间的权衡并收敛至帕累托最优解。在Mistral-7B上的评估显示，GAPO在帮助性和无害性上均优于现有方法。该论文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Mixture of insighTful Experts (MoTE): The Synergy of Reasoning Chains and Expert Mixtures in Self-Alignment
papers.abstract: As the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) continue to expand, aligning these models with human values remains a significant challenge. Recent studies show that reasoning abilities contribute significantly to model safety, while integrating Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures can further enhance alignment. In this work, we address a fundamental question: How to effectively incorporate reasoning abilities and MoE architectures into self-alignment process in LLMs? We propose Mixture of insighTful Experts (MoTE), a novel framework that synergistically combines reasoning chains and expert mixtures to improve self-alignments. From a data perspective, MoTE employs a structured reasoning chain comprising four key stages: Question Analysis, Answer Guidance, Safe Answer, and Safety Checking. This approach enhances safety through multi-step reasoning and proves effective even for smaller and less powerful LLMs (e.g., 7B models). From an architectural perspective, MoTE adopts a multi-LoRA framework with step-level routing, where each expert is dedicated to a specific reasoning step. This design eliminates the need for balance losses, ensures stable training, and supports adaptive inference lengths. Experimental results demonstrate that MoTE significantly improves model safety, jailbreak resistance, and over-refusal capabilities, achieving performance comparable to OpenAI's state-of-the-art o1 model.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of effectively incorporating reasoning abilities and mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures into the self-alignment process of large language models (LLMs). It proposes Mixture of insighTful Experts (MoTE), a framework that combines a structured reasoning chain (comprising Question Analysis, Answer Guidance, Safe Answer, and Safety Checking) with a multi-LoRA expert mixture using step-level routing, eliminating the need for balance losses and enabling stable training with adaptive inference. Experiments show that MoTE significantly improves model safety, jailbreak resistance, and over-refusal capabilities, achieving performance comparable to OpenAI's o1 model. This paper advances alignment methodology by integrating reasoning and MoE but does not directly address the question of whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了如何将推理能力和专家混合（MoE）架构有效整合到大语言模型自对齐过程中的挑战。提出了Mixture of insighTful Experts（MoTE）框架，结合了包含问题分析、答案指导、安全回答和安全检查四阶段的结构化推理链，以及采用步骤级路由的多LoRA专家混合，无需平衡损失即可实现稳定训练和自适应推理。实验表明，MoTE显著提升了模型安全性、抗越狱能力和过度拒绝能力，性能可与OpenAI的o1模型相媲美。该工作通过集成推理和MoE推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐是否固有脆弱或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Multi-Attribute Steering of Language Models via Targeted Intervention
papers.abstract: Inference-time intervention (ITI) has emerged as a promising method for steering large language model (LLM) behavior in a particular direction (e.g., improving helpfulness) by intervening on token representations without costly updates to the LLM's parameters. However, existing ITI approaches fail to scale to multi-attribute settings with conflicts, such as enhancing helpfulness while also reducing toxicity. To address this, we introduce Multi-Attribute Targeted Steering (MAT-Steer), a novel steering framework designed for selective token-level intervention across multiple attributes. MAT-Steer learns steering vectors using an alignment objective that shifts the model's internal representations of undesirable outputs closer to those of desirable ones while enforcing sparsity and orthogonality among vectors for different attributes, thereby reducing inter-attribute conflicts. We evaluate MAT-Steer in two distinct settings: (i) on question answering (QA) tasks where we balance attributes like truthfulness, bias, and toxicity; (ii) on generative tasks where we simultaneously improve attributes like helpfulness, correctness, and coherence. MAT-Steer outperforms existing ITI and parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches across both task types (e.g., 3% average accuracy gain across QA tasks and 55.82% win rate against the best ITI baseline).
papers.summary_en: Existing inference-time intervention (ITI) methods for steering LLMs struggle with conflicting multi-attribute settings. This paper introduces MAT-Steer, which learns sparse, orthogonal steering vectors via an alignment objective to shift internal representations toward desirable outputs while minimizing inter-attribute conflicts. Evaluated on QA and generative tasks, MAT-Steer outperforms baselines, achieving a 3% accuracy gain and 55.82% win rate. The work advances multi-attribute inference-time alignment but does not directly investigate the robustness of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有的推理时干预方法在存在冲突的多属性场景下面临挑战。本文提出MAT-Steer，通过对齐目标学习稀疏且正交的引导向量，将内部表征推向理想输出，同时减少属性间冲突。在问答和生成任务上的评估显示，MAT-Steer优于基线方法，平均准确率提升3%，胜率达55.82%。该工作推进了多属性推理时对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: A Troublemaker with Contagious Jailbreak Makes Chaos in Honest Towns
papers.abstract: With the development of large language models, they are widely used as agents in various fields. A key component of agents is memory, which stores vital information but is susceptible to jailbreak attacks. Existing research mainly focuses on single-agent attacks and shared memory attacks. However, real-world scenarios often involve independent memory. In this paper, we propose the Troublemaker Makes Chaos in Honest Town (TMCHT) task, a large-scale, multi-agent, multi-topology text-based attack evaluation framework. TMCHT involves one attacker agent attempting to mislead an entire society of agents. We identify two major challenges in multi-agent attacks: (1) Non-complete graph structure, (2) Large-scale systems. We attribute these challenges to a phenomenon we term toxicity disappearing. To address these issues, we propose an Adversarial Replication Contagious Jailbreak (ARCJ) method, which optimizes the retrieval suffix to make poisoned samples more easily retrieved and optimizes the replication suffix to make poisoned samples have contagious ability. We demonstrate the superiority of our approach in TMCHT, with 23.51%, 18.95%, and 52.93% improvements in line topology, star topology, and 100-agent settings. Encourage community attention to the security of multi-agent systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses multi-agent jailbreak attacks where an attacker misleads a society of agents with independent memories, identifying challenges of non-complete graph structures and large-scale systems that cause toxicity disappearing. It proposes Adversarial Replication Contagious Jailbreak (ARCJ), which optimizes retrieval and replication suffixes to make poisoned samples more retrievable and contagious. Evaluated in the TMCHT framework across line, star, and 100-agent topologies, ARCJ improves attack success by 23.51%, 18.95%, and 52.93% respectively. The work reveals a new attack surface in decentralized multi-agent LLM systems, demonstrating that safety alignment can be fragile against distributed adversarial dynamics.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多智能体越狱攻击，提出大规模攻击评估框架TMCHT，其中攻击者误导整个智能体社会，面临非完全图和大规模系统导致的毒性消失挑战。提出对抗复制传染越狱（ARCJ）方法，通过优化检索后缀使中毒样本更易被检索，优化复制后缀使中毒样本具备传染能力。在TMCHT框架中，ARCJ在线型、星型和100智能体拓扑下分别提升23.51%、18.95%和52.93%的攻击成功率。研究揭示了去中心化多智能体LLM系统的安全对齐面对分布式对抗动态的脆弱性，为对齐鲁棒性问题提供了新的攻击表面证据。

papers.title: Towards Reward Fairness in RLHF: From a Resource Allocation Perspective
papers.abstract: Rewards serve as proxies for human preferences and play a crucial role in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). However, if these rewards are inherently imperfect, exhibiting various biases, they can adversely affect the alignment of large language models (LLMs). In this paper, we collectively define the various biases present in rewards as the problem of reward unfairness. We propose a bias-agnostic method to address the issue of reward fairness from a resource allocation perspective, without specifically designing for each type of bias, yet effectively mitigating them. Specifically, we model preference learning as a resource allocation problem, treating rewards as resources to be allocated while considering the trade-off between utility and fairness in their distribution. We propose two methods, Fairness Regularization and Fairness Coefficient, to achieve fairness in rewards. We apply our methods in both verification and reinforcement learning scenarios to obtain a fairness reward model and a policy model, respectively. Experiments conducted in these scenarios demonstrate that our approach aligns LLMs with human preferences in a more fair manner.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses reward unfairness in RLHF, where biased reward models lead to suboptimal alignment of LLMs. It proposes a bias-agnostic method that frames preference learning as a resource allocation problem, balancing utility and fairness via Fairness Regularization and Fairness Coefficient. Experiments in verification and RL settings demonstrate more equitable alignment with human preferences compared to baselines. This work improves alignment robustness by mitigating reward bias, a potential vulnerability, but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中奖励模型存在偏差导致的奖励不公平问题，这些问题会损害LLM的对齐效果。提出了一种与偏差无关的方法，将偏好学习建模为资源分配问题，通过公平正则化和公平系数权衡效用与公平。在验证和强化学习场景的实验表明，该方法能比基线更公平地对齐人类偏好。这项工作通过缓解奖励偏差增强了对齐鲁棒性，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Understanding Impact of Human Feedback via Influence Functions
papers.abstract: In Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), it is crucial to learn suitable reward models from human feedback to align large language models (LLMs) with human intentions. However, human feedback can often be noisy, inconsistent, or biased, especially when evaluating complex responses. Such feedback can lead to misaligned reward signals, potentially causing unintended side effects during the RLHF process. To address these challenges, we explore the use of influence functions to measure the impact of human feedback on the performance of reward models. We propose a compute-efficient approximation method that enables the application of influence functions to LLM-based reward models and large-scale preference datasets. Our experiments showcase two key applications of influence functions: (1) detecting common labeler biases in human feedback datasets and (2) guiding labelers in refining their strategies to better align with expert feedback. By quantifying the impact of human feedback, we believe that influence functions can enhance feedback interpretability and contribute to scalable oversight in RLHF, helping labelers provide more accurate and consistent feedback.
