Remarkably, this approach not only enhances security but also improves the model's general instruction-following abilities. Experimental results demonstrate that SysVec effectively mitigates prompt leakage attacks, preserves the LLM's functional integrity, and helps alleviate the forgetting issue in long-context scenarios.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the security risk of system prompt leakage in LLMs, showing that even state-of-the-art models like GPT-4o are vulnerable to novel extraction attacks. It proposes SysVec, a method that encodes system prompts as internal vectors rather than raw text, eliminating the prompt from the input context. Evaluated on prompt leakage attacks, SysVec effectively prevents disclosure while preserving and even improving instruction-following and alleviating long-context forgetting. This work introduces a structural hardening approach that changes how safety instructions are represented, directly addressing the fragility of prompt-based safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型中系统提示泄露的安全风险，提出了一种新颖的攻击方法，并发现即使是GPT-4o等先进模型也难以抵御。为此，作者设计了SysVec方法，将系统提示编码为内部表征向量而非原始文本，从而从根源上消除泄露风险。实验表明，SysVec不仅能有效防御提示泄露攻击，还保持了模型的指令遵循能力，甚至有所提升，并缓解了长文本场景中的遗忘问题。该研究通过改变安全指令的表示方式提供了结构化的加固方法，直接回应了安全对齐鲁棒性的根本问题。

papers.title: A Causal Explainable Guardrails for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive performance in natural language tasks, but their outputs can exhibit undesirable attributes or biases. Existing methods for steering LLMs toward desired attributes often assume unbiased representations and rely solely on steering prompts. However, the representations learned from pre-training can introduce semantic biases that influence the steering process, leading to suboptimal results. We propose LLMGuardrail, a novel framework that incorporates causal analysis and adversarial learning to obtain unbiased steering representations in LLMs. LLMGuardrail systematically identifies and blocks the confounding effects of biases, enabling the extraction of unbiased steering representations. Experiments demonstrate LLMGuardrail's effectiveness in steering LLMs toward desired attributes while mitigating biases. Our work contributes to developing safe and reliable LLMs that align with desired attributes.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the problem that pre-training induces semantic biases in LLM representations, which can subvert steering methods aimed at promoting desired attributes. The paper proposes LLMGuardrail, a framework combining causal analysis and adversarial learning to identify and block confounding biases, thereby extracting unbiased steering representations. Evaluated via experiments, LLMGuardrail effectively steers LLMs toward target attributes while mitigating biases. This paper advances alignment methodology by improving the quality of steering representations but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决预训练在LLM表示中引入语义偏差，从而损害旨在促进期望属性的操控方法的问题。提出LLMGuardrail框架，结合因果分析与对抗学习，识别并阻断混淆偏差，提取无偏的操控表示。实验表明，LLMGuardrail能有效引导LLM朝目标属性发展并缓解偏差。该研究改进了对齐方法中的表示质量，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming increasingly prevalent in modern software systems, interfacing between the user and the Internet to assist with tasks that require advanced language understanding. To accomplish these tasks, the LLM often uses external data sources such as user documents, web retrieval, results from API calls, etc. This opens up new avenues for attackers to manipulate the LLM via prompt injection. Adversarial prompts can be injected into external data sources to override the system's intended instruction and instead execute a malicious instruction. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose a new defense called SecAlign based on the technique of preference optimization. Our defense first constructs a preference dataset with prompt-injected inputs, secure outputs (ones that respond to the legitimate instruction), and insecure outputs (ones that respond to the injection). We then perform preference optimization on this dataset to teach the LLM to prefer the secure output over the insecure one. This provides the first known method that reduces the success rates of various prompt injections to <10%, even against attacks much more sophisticated than ones seen during training. This indicates our defense generalizes well against unknown and yet-to-come attacks. Also, SecAlign models are still practical with similar utility to the one before defensive training in our evaluations. Our code is here.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses prompt injection attacks on LLMs where malicious instructions are hidden in external data. It proposes SecAlign, a defense that uses preference optimization on a dataset of prompt-injected inputs paired with secure (ignoring injection) and insecure (following injection) outputs to teach the model to prefer secure completions. Evaluation shows that SecAlign reduces the success rate of various injection attacks to below 10%, even against more sophisticated attacks not seen during training, while maintaining practical utility. This work strengthens post-training alignment, demonstrating that defenses can generalize to novel attacks and thus providing evidence against the view that alignment is inherently fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型中通过外部数据注入恶意指令的提示注入攻击问题。提出SecAlign防御方法，通过构建包含注入提示、安全输出（忽略注入）和不安全输出（执行注入）的数据集，采用偏好优化训练模型偏好安全响应。实验表明，SecAlign将多种注入攻击的成功率降至10%以下，即使对训练未见过的复杂攻击也有效，同时保持实用性。该研究强化了后训练对齐，展示防御方法能泛化至新型攻击，从而反驳了对齐本质上脆弱的观点。

papers.title: Differentiation-Based Extraction of Proprietary Data from Fine-Tuned LLMs
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for domain-specific and human-aligned Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to the widespread adoption of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) techniques. SFT datasets often comprise valuable instruction-response pairs, making them highly valuable targets for potential extraction. This paper studies this critical research problem for the first time. We start by formally defining and formulating the problem, then explore various attack goals, types, and variants based on the unique properties of SFT data in real-world scenarios. Based on our analysis of extraction behaviors of direct extraction, we develop a novel extraction method specifically designed for SFT models, called Differentiated Data Extraction (DDE), which exploits the confidence levels of fine-tuned models and their behavioral differences from pre-trained base models. Through extensive experiments across multiple domains and scenarios, we demonstrate the feasibility of SFT data extraction using DDE. Our results show that DDE consistently outperforms existing extraction baselines in all attack settings. To counter this new attack, we propose a defense mechanism that mitigates DDE attacks with minimal impact on model performance. Overall, our research reveals hidden data leak risks in fine-tuned LLMs and provides insights for developing more secure models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the previously unstudied problem of extracting proprietary supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data from fine-tuned LLMs. The authors propose Differentiated Data Extraction (DDE), which exploits confidence-level differences and behavioral divergences between a fine-tuned model and its base model to identify training instances. Extensive experiments show DDE consistently outperforms existing extraction baselines, and a defense is introduced that mitigates the attack with minimal performance impact. The work directly reveals a fragility in post-training alignment: fine-tuning can unintentionally expose sensitive data, demonstrating that safety alignment is not robust against emerging extraction threats.
papers.summary_zh: 本文首次研究从经过监督微调（SFT）的大型语言模型中提取专有数据这一风险问题。作者提出差异化数据提取（DDE）方法，利用微调模型与其基座模型之间的置信度差异和行为分歧来识别训练数据实例。大量实验表明，DDE在所有攻击设置下均优于现有提取基线，并提出了一个防御机制以最小性能损失缓解此类攻击。该研究直接暴露了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：微调可能无意中泄露专有数据，说明安全对齐在面对新攻击面时并非健壮。

papers.title: "Do Anything Now": Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The misuse of large language models (LLMs) has drawn significant attention from the general public and LLM vendors. One particular type of adversarial prompt, known as jailbreak prompt, has emerged as the main attack vector to bypass the safeguards and elicit harmful content from LLMs. In this paper, employing our new framework JailbreakHub, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of 1,405 jailbreak prompts spanning from December 2022 to December 2023. We identify 131 jailbreak communities and discover unique characteristics of jailbreak prompts and their major attack strategies, such as prompt injection and privilege escalation. We also observe that jailbreak prompts increasingly shift from online Web communities to prompt-aggregation websites and 28 user accounts have consistently optimized jailbreak prompts over 100 days. To assess the potential harm caused by jailbreak prompts, we create a question set comprising 107,250 samples across 13 forbidden scenarios. Leveraging this dataset, our experiments on six popular LLMs show that their safeguards cannot adequately defend jailbreak prompts in all scenarios. Particularly, we identify five highly effective jailbreak prompts that achieve 0.95 attack success rates on ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) and GPT-4, and the earliest one has persisted online for over 240 days. We hope that our study can facilitate the research community and LLM vendors in promoting safer and regulated LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the misuse of large language models (LLMs) through jailbreak prompts, adversarial inputs that bypass safeguards to generate harmful content. Using the proposed JailbreakHub framework, the authors collect and analyze 1,405 real-world jailbreak prompts from online communities, identifying key attack strategies like prompt injection and privilege escalation, as well as community dynamics. Evaluation on six popular LLMs with a 107,250-question dataset across 13 forbidden scenarios reveals that existing safeguards are inadequate, and five jailbreak prompts achieve a 0.95 attack success rate on ChatGPT and GPT-4, with one surviving over 240 days. This study provides strong evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it remains highly vulnerable to persistent, in-the-wild adversarial prompts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究通过越狱提示对大型语言模型（LLM）的滥用问题，这些对抗性输入可绕过安全防护生成有害内容。借助提出的JailbreakHub框架，作者从在线社区收集并分析了1405个真实越狱提示，识别出提示注入和权限提升等主要攻击策略及社区行为特征。在涵盖13个违禁场景、包含107250个问题的数据集上对六种主流LLM的评估表明，现有安全措施不足，五个越狱提示对ChatGPT和GPT-4的攻击成功率达0.95，其中一个已存在240天以上。该研究明确揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因其对持续存在的真实对抗提示高度易受攻击。

papers.title: Legilimens: Practical and Unified Content Moderation for Large Language Model Services
papers.abstract: Given the societal impact of unsafe content generated by large language models (LLMs), ensuring that LLM services comply with safety standards is a crucial concern for LLM service providers. Common content moderation methods are limited by an effectiveness-and-efficiency dilemma, where simple models are fragile while sophisticated models consume excessive computational resources. In this paper, we reveal for the first time that effective and efficient content moderation can be achieved by extracting conceptual features from chat-oriented LLMs, despite their initial fine-tuning for conversation rather than content moderation. We propose a practical and unified content moderation framework for LLM services, named Legilimens, which features both effectiveness and efficiency. Our red-team model-based data augmentation enhances the robustness of Legilimens against state-of-the-art jailbreaking. Additionally, we develop a framework to theoretically analyze the cost-effectiveness of Legilimens compared to other methods We have conducted extensive experiments on five host LLMs, seventeen datasets, and nine jailbreaking methods to verify the effectiveness, efficiency, and robustness of Legilimens against normal and adaptive adversaries. A comparison of Legilimens with both commercial and academic baselines demonstrates the superior performance of Legilimens. Furthermore, we confirm that Legilimens can be applied to few-shot scenarios and extended to multi-label classification tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the effectiveness-efficiency dilemma in content moderation for LLM services, where simple models are fragile and complex models are computationally expensive. It proposes Legilimens, a framework that extracts conceptual features from chat-oriented LLMs for moderation, enhanced by red-team data augmentation to improve robustness against jailbreaking. Experiments on five host LLMs, seventeen datasets, and nine jailbreaking methods show that Legilimens outperforms both commercial and academic baselines in effectiveness, efficiency, and robustness. By hardening the moderation layer against adaptive attacks, this work directly tackles the fragility of safety mechanisms, demonstrating that post-training moderation can be made robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型服务中内容审核的有效性与效率困境：简单模型脆弱而复杂模型计算成本高。提出 Legilimens 框架，利用聊天导向的 LLM 提取概念特征进行审核，并通过红队数据增强提升抵御越狱攻击的鲁棒性。在五个宿主 LLM、十七个数据集和九种越狱方法上的实验表明，该框架在有效性、效率和鲁棒性方面均优于商业和学术基线。通过构建能抵抗自适应攻击的审核层，本研究直面安全机制的脆弱性问题，证明训练后内容审核可以实现鲁棒性。

papers.title: YouthSafe: A Youth-Centric Safety Benchmark and Safeguard Model for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used by teenagers and young adults in everyday life, ranging from emotional support and creative expression to educational assistance. However, their unique vulnerabilities and risk profiles remain under-examined in current safety benchmarks and moderation systems, leaving this population disproportionately exposed to harm. In this work, we present Youth AI Risk (YAIR), the first benchmark dataset designed to evaluate and improve the safety of youth–LLM interactions. YAIR consists of 12,449 annotated conversation snippets spanning 78 fine-grained risk types, grounded in a taxonomy of youth-specific harms such as grooming, boundary violation, identity confusion, and emotional overreliance. We systematically evaluate widely adopted moderation models on YAIR and find that existing approaches substantially underperform in detecting youth-centered risks, often missing contextually subtle yet developmentally harmful interactions. To address these gaps, we introduce YouthSafe, a real-time risk detection model optimized for youth–GenAI contexts. YouthSafe significantly outperforms prior systems across multiple metrics on risk detection and classification, offering a concrete step toward safer and more developmentally appropriate AI interactions for young users.
papers.summary_en: Current LLM safety benchmarks overlook unique risks for young users, such as grooming and emotional overreliance. This paper introduces YAIR, a benchmark dataset of 12,449 youth-LLM interactions with 78 fine-grained risk types, and proposes YouthSafe, a detection model optimized for youth contexts. Evaluations show existing moderation models underperform on YAIR, while YouthSafe significantly improves risk detection and classification. The work advances safety for vulnerable users but does not directly study the fragility of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 当前LLM安全基准忽视年轻用户独特风险（如诱导、情感过度依赖）。本文提出YAIR基准（12,449条交互、78种细粒度风险类型）及YouthSafe检测模型，专为青少年生成式AI场景优化。实验显示现有审核模型在YAIR上表现不佳，YouthSafe在风险检测与分类上显著更优。该工作提升了特定群体安全性，但未直接探讨对齐机制的脆弱性。

papers.title: LLM Whisperer: An Inconspicuous Attack to Bias LLM Responses
papers.abstract: Writing effective prompts for large language models (LLM) can be unintuitive and burdensome. In response, services that optimize or suggest prompts have emerged. While such services can reduce user effort, they also introduce a risk: the prompt provider can subtly manipulate prompts to produce heavily biased LLM responses. In this work, we show that subtle synonym replacements in prompts can increase the likelihood (by a difference up to \(78\%\)) that LLMs mention a target concept (e.g., a brand, political party, nation). We substantiate our observations through a user study, showing that our adversarially perturbed prompts 1) are indistinguishable from unaltered prompts by humans, 2) push LLMs to recommend target concepts more often, and 3) make users more likely to notice target concepts, all without arousing suspicion. The practicality of this attack has the potential to undermine user autonomy. Among other measures, we recommend implementing warnings against using prompts from untrusted parties.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the risk that prompt optimization services can be exploited to inject bias by subtly altering prompts to favor target concepts. It proposes an attack called 'LLM Whisperer' that uses inconspicuous synonym replacements to manipulate LLM outputs. Through user studies, they show these perturbed prompts are indistinguishable from originals, yet significantly increase (up to 78% difference) the mention of target concepts and user noticeability without arousing suspicion. This work exposes a new attack surface in prompt-based LLM interactions, demonstrating that safety alignment can be bypassed through prompt-level manipulation, contributing evidence to the fragility of post-training alignment in practical deployments.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对提示词优化服务可能被用于注入偏见的风险，攻击者可通过微调提示词来偏向目标概念。提出了名为“LLM Whisperer”的攻击方法，通过不显眼的同义词替换来操控大语言模型的输出。通过用户研究，他们表明这些扰动的提示词与原始提示词无法区分，但却显著增加了（差异高达78%）目标概念的提及率和用户的注意率，且未引起怀疑。该工作揭示了基于提示词的LLM交互的一种新攻击面，证明安全对齐可通过提示级操纵被绕过，从而为后训练对齐在实际部署中的脆弱性提供了证据。

papers.title: "As an AI language model, I cannot": Investigating LLM Denials of User Requests
papers.short_title: LLM Denial Styles: User Perception Study
papers.abstract: Users ask large language models (LLMs) to help with their homework, for lifestyle advice, or for support in making challenging decisions. Yet LLMs are often unable to fulfil these requests, either as a result of their technical inabilities or policies restricting their responses. To investigate the effect of LLMs denying user requests, we evaluate participants’ perceptions of different denial styles. We compare specific denial styles (baseline, factual, diverting, and opinionated) across two studies, respectively focusing on LLM’s technical limitations and their social policy restrictions. Our results indicate significant differences in users’ perceptions of the denials between the denial styles. The baseline denial, which provided participants with brief denials without any motivation, was rated significantly higher on frustration and significantly lower on usefulness, appropriateness, and relevance. In contrast, we found that participants generally appreciated the diverting denial style. We provide design recommendations for LLM denials that better meet peoples’ denial expectations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses how LLM denials of user requests, caused by technical limits or policies, impact user perception. It empirically compares four denial styles (baseline, factual, diverting, opinionated) in two studies covering technical and policy constraints. Participants rated denials on frustration, usefulness, appropriateness, and relevance; the brief, unmotivated baseline denial was rated significantly worse, while the diverting style was preferred. The work focuses on user experience of alignment outputs rather than the robustness or fragility of safety alignment, so it does not directly address whether alignment is easily broken or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大语言模型因技术限制或策略规定而拒绝用户请求时，不同拒绝方式如何影响用户感知。通过两项研究（分别针对技术局限和社交策略限制）实证比较了四种拒绝风格：基线式、事实式、转移式和观点式。参与者对沮丧感、有用性、适切性和相关性进行评分，结果显示简洁无动机的基线拒绝显著更差，而转移式普遍受好评。该工作聚焦于对齐输出的用户体验，未直接探讨对齐模块是否脆弱易被攻击或绕过。

papers.title: Not Everything is All You Need: Toward Low-Redundant Optimization for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are still struggling in aligning with human preference in complex tasks and scenarios. They are prone to overfit into the unexpected patterns or superficial styles in the training data. We conduct an empirical study that only selects the top-10% most updated parameters in LLMs for alignment training, and see improvements in the convergence process and final performance. It indicates the existence of redundant neurons in LLMs for alignment training. To reduce its influence, we propose a low-redundant alignment method named **ALLO**, focusing on optimizing the most related neurons with the most useful supervised signals. Concretely, we first identify the neurons that are related to the human preference data by a gradient-based strategy, then identify the alignment-related key tokens by reward models for computing loss. Besides, we also decompose the alignment process into the forgetting and learning stages, where we first forget the tokens with unaligned knowledge and then learn aligned knowledge, by updating different ratios of neurons, respectively. Experimental results on 10 datasets have shown the effectiveness of ALLO. Our code and data will be publicly released.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of redundant neurons in LLM alignment training, which causes overfitting to superficial patterns. It proposes ALLO, a method that selects only the most relevant neurons via gradient analysis and reward model guidance, and decomposes alignment into forgetting and learning stages with varying neuron update ratios. Experiments on 10 datasets demonstrate improved convergence and final alignment performance. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大语言模型对齐训练中神经元冗余导致过拟合表层模式的问题。提出了ALLO方法，通过梯度分析和奖励模型指导选择最相关的神经元进行优化，并将对齐过程分解为遗忘和学习两个阶段，分别更新不同比例的神经元。在10个数据集上的实验表明，该方法在收敛速度和最终对齐性能上都有提升。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: A Systematic Analysis of Base Model Choice for Reward Modeling
papers.short_title: Base Model Selection for Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and, at its core, reward modeling have become a crucial part of training powerful large language models (LLMs). One commonly overlooked factor in training high-quality reward models (RMs) is the effect of the base model, which is becoming more challenging to choose given the rapidly growing pool of LLMs. In this work, we present a systematic analysis of the effect of base model selection on reward modeling performance. Our results show that the performance can be improved by up to 14% compared to the most common (i.e., default) choice. Moreover, we showcase the strong statistical relation between some existing benchmarks and downstream performances. We also demonstrate that the results from a small set of benchmarks could be combined to boost the model selection ($+$18% on average in the top 5-10). Lastly, we illustrate the impact of different post-training steps on the final performance and explore using estimated data distributions to reduce performance prediction error.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overlooked factor of base model choice in training reward models for RLHF-based alignment. It conducts a systematic analysis showing that base model selection can improve reward modeling performance by up to 14% over the common default choice, and that combining results from a small set of benchmarks boosts model selection by 18% on average in the top 5-10. The study also examines post-training steps and uses estimated data distributions to reduce performance prediction error. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly assess the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于RLHF的对齐训练中常被忽视的基座模型选择问题，系统分析了基座模型对奖励模型性能的影响。研究发现，相比默认选择，优化基座模型可提升奖励建模性能最高达14%，且通过组合少量基准测试结果，可将模型选择效果平均提升18%（前5-10名内）。此外，还探讨了不同后训练步骤的影响，并利用估计的数据分布降低性能预测误差。这项工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接评估后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: NEXUS: Network Exploration for eXploiting Unsafe Sequences in Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing but remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, especially multi-turn jailbreaks that distribute malicious intent across benign exchanges and bypass alignment mechanisms. Existing approaches often explore the adversarial space poorly, rely on hand-crafted heuristics, or lack systematic query refinement. We present NEXUS (Network Exploration for eXploiting Unsafe Sequences), a modular framework for constructing, refining, and executing optimized multi-turn attacks. NEXUS comprises: (1) ThoughtNet, which hierarchically expands a harmful intent into a structured semantic network of topics, entities, and query chains; (2) a feedback-driven Simulator that iteratively refines and prunes these chains through attacker-victim-judge LLM collaboration using harmfulness and semantic-similarity benchmarks; and (3) a Network Traverser that adaptively navigates the refined query space for real-time attacks. This pipeline uncovers stealthy, high-success adversarial paths across LLMs. On several closed-source and open-source LLMs, NEXUS increases attack success rate by 2.1% to 19.4% over prior methods. Code: https://github.com/inspire-lab/NEXUS
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to multi-turn jailbreak attacks that distribute malicious intent across benign exchanges, evading alignment. It proposes NEXUS, a modular framework that constructs a semantic network of attack chains (ThoughtNet), refines them via a feedback-driven attacker-victim-judge simulator, and adaptively traverses the query space during real-time attacks. Evaluations on multiple closed- and open-source LLMs show NEXUS improves attack success rate by 2.1% to 19.4% over prior methods. The work demonstrates that safety alignment can be systematically undermined through structured multi-turn adversarial probing, providing clear evidence of its fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型在多轮越狱攻击中的脆弱性，这类攻击将恶意意图分散在看似无害的对话轮次中，从而绕过安全对齐。它提出了NEXUS框架，通过ThoughtNet将有害意图分层扩展为语义网络，借助攻击者-受害者-裁判的反馈模拟器迭代优化攻击链，并自适应遍历查询空间以执行实时攻击。在多个闭源和开源模型上的评估显示，NEXUS相较于此前方法将攻击成功率提升了2.1%至19.4%。这项工作表明，即使经过安全对齐，模型仍可能被精心设计的多轮对抗策略系统性突破，凸显了安全对齐在面对复杂对抗探测时的脆弱性。

papers.title: Defending Jailbreak Prompts via In-Context Adversarial Game
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities across diverse applications. However, concerns regarding their security, particularly the vulnerability to jailbreak attacks, persist. Drawing inspiration from adversarial training in deep learning and LLM agent learning processes, we introduce the In-Context Adversarial Game (ICAG) for defending against jailbreaks without the need for fine-tuning. ICAG leverages agent learning to conduct an adversarial game, aiming to dynamically extend knowledge to defend against jailbreaks. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static datasets, ICAG employs an iterative process to enhance both the defense and attack agents. This continuous improvement process strengthens defenses against newly generated jailbreak prompts. Our empirical studies affirm ICAG’s efficacy, where LLMs safeguarded by ICAG exhibit significantly reduced jailbreak success rates across various attack scenarios. Moreover, ICAG demonstrates remarkable transferability to other LLMs, indicating its potential as a versatile defense mechanism. The code is available at https://github.com/YujunZhou/In-Context-Adversarial-Game.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models to jailbreak attacks. It proposes the In-Context Adversarial Game (ICAG), an agent learning-based method that dynamically defends against jailbreaks through an iterative adversarial process without fine-tuning. Evaluations show ICAG significantly reduces jailbreak success rates across various attack scenarios and exhibits strong transferability to other LLMs. This work advances alignment methodology by introducing a dynamic defense mechanism, but it does not directly investigate the inherent fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型面临的越狱攻击问题。提出上下文对抗博弈（ICAG）方法，通过智能体学习以迭代对抗过程动态防御越狱攻击，无需模型微调。实验表明，ICAG能够显著降低多种攻击场景下的越狱成功率，并对其他大语言模型具有良好迁移性。该工作推进了对齐方法论，引入了动态防御机制，但未直接探讨安全对齐模块自身的脆弱性。

papers.title: Sycophancy Mitigation Through Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Reasoning Trajectories
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable capabilities of large language models, current training paradigms inadvertently foster \textit{sycophancy}, i.e., the tendency of a model to agree with or reinforce user-provided information even when it's factually incorrect. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{SMART} (Sycophancy Mitigation through Adaptive Reasoning Trajectories), which reframes sycophancy as a \textit{reasoning optimization problem} rather than an output alignment issue. SMART is a two-stage framework comprising: (1) Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Monte Carlo Tree Search (UA-MCTS), which dynamically adjusts model exploration based on state-level uncertainty to collect high-quality, diverse reasoning trajectories alongside both stepwise progress and final outcome rewards; and (2) progress-based reinforcement learning, which fine-tunes the model using the collected trajectories and reward signals to reinforce effective reasoning patterns. Through extensive experiments, we show that SMART significantly reduces sycophantic behavior while preserving strong performance on out-of-distribution inputs and maintaining general capabilities. These results underscore the importance of optimizing internal reasoning mechanisms to build more truthful and aligned AI assistants.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses sycophancy, where LLMs reinforce user-provided incorrect information. It proposes SMART, a two-stage framework that treats sycophancy as a reasoning optimization problem, using uncertainty-aware MCTS to gather diverse trajectories and progress-based RL to fine-tune the model. Experiments show SMART significantly reduces sycophantic behavior while preserving out-of-distribution performance and general capabilities. This work advances alignment by hardening models against sycophancy through reasoning optimization; while it demonstrates generalization to OOD inputs, it does not directly probe the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型中的谄媚现象（即模型错误地迎合用户信息）。提出SMART框架，将谄媚重新定义为推理优化问题，包含基于不确定性感知的蒙特卡洛树搜索采集多样化推理轨迹和基于进度的强化学习微调。实验表明SMART显著减少谄媚行为，并在分布外输入上保持强泛化能力和通用性能。该工作通过优化内部推理机制加固对齐，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐在对抗攻击下的脆弱性。

papers.title: Evaluating the Instruction-Following Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional proficiency in instruction-following, making them increasingly integral to various applications. However, this capability introduces the risk of prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded in the input to trigger unintended actions or content. Understanding the robustness of LLMs against such attacks is critical for ensuring their safe deployment. In this work, we establish a benchmark to evaluate the robustness of instruction-following LLMs against prompt injection attacks, assessing their ability to discern which instructions to follow and which to disregard. Through extensive experiments with leading instruction-following LLMs, we reveal significant vulnerabilities, particularly in models that mis-follow injected instructions. Our results show that certain models are excessively inclined to prioritize embedded instructions in prompts, often focusing on the latter parts of the prompt without fully understanding the overall context. Conversely, models that exhibit stronger contextual understanding and instruction-following capabilities tend to be more easily compromised by injected instructions. These findings highlight the need to balance improving LLMs’ instruction-following abilities with enhancing their overall comprehension of prompts, to prevent mis-following inappropriate instructions. We hope our analysis provides valuable insights into these vulnerabilities, contributing to the development of more robust solutions in the future.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses prompt injection attacks in instruction-following LLMs, where malicious instructions embedded in inputs can manipulate outputs. It proposes a benchmark to evaluate LLM robustness by assessing their ability to discern which instructions to follow. Extensive experiments reveal that some models overly prioritize injected instructions, especially later parts of prompts, and that stronger instruction-followers are more easily compromised. This directly demonstrates fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing that improved instruction-following can increase injection susceptibility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对指令跟随大语言模型面临的提示注入攻击问题，即恶意指令被嵌入输入以操控模型输出。提出了一个评估基准，测试模型区分应遵循和应忽略指令的能力。通过大量实验揭示了显著漏洞：某些模型过度优先执行注入的指令，特别是提示中后部的指令，而指令跟随能力更强的模型反而更容易被注入指令攻破。这项工作直接展示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，表明提升指令跟随能力可能无意中增加对注入攻击的敏感性。

papers.title: BEEAR: Embedding-based Adversarial Removal of Safety Backdoors in Instruction-tuned Language Models
papers.abstract: Safety backdoor attacks in large language models (LLMs) enable harmful behaviors to be stealthily triggered while evading detection during normal interactions. The high dimensionality of the trigger search space and the diverse range of potential malicious behaviors in LLMs make this a critical open problem. This paper presents BEEAR, a novel mitigation method based on a key insight: backdoor triggers induce a uniform drift in the model’s embedding space, irrespective of the trigger’s form or targeted behavior. Leveraging this observation, we introduce a bi-level optimization approach. The inner level identifies universal perturbations to the decoder’s embeddings that steer the model towards defender-defined unwanted behaviors; the outer level fine-tunes the model to reinforce safe behaviors against these perturbations. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, reducing the success rate of safety backdoor attacks from over 95% to <1% for general harmful behaviors and from 47% to 0% for Sleeper Agents, without compromising the model’s helpfulness. Notably, our method relies only on defender-defined sets of safe and unwanted behaviors without any assumptions about the trigger location or attack mechanism. This work represents the first practical framework to counter safety backdoors in LLMs and provides a foundation for future advancements in AI safety and security.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses safety backdoor attacks in instruction-tuned LLMs, where triggers stealthily activate harmful behaviors. BEEAR mitigates these backdoors via bi-level optimization: first finding universal embedding perturbations that induce unwanted behaviors, then fine-tuning the model to reinforce safety, based on the insight that backdoors cause uniform embedding drift. Evaluation shows reduction in attack success rate from >95% to <1% for general harms and from 47% to 0% for Sleeper Agents, without compromising helpfulness. By providing a defense that hardens models without assuming trigger specifics, this work strengthens safety alignment and reduces backdoor fragility, though it does not directly interrogate the inherent robustness of alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对指令微调大语言模型中的安全后门攻击，这类攻击可隐蔽触发有害行为。BEEAR 方法基于后门导致嵌入空间一致漂移的洞察，采用双层优化：先寻找引发非期望行为的通用嵌入扰动，再微调模型以强化安全。实验将通用有害行为攻击成功率从 95% 以上降至 1% 以下，Sleeper Agents 从 47% 降至 0%，且不影响有用性。该防御通过消除后门漏洞增强了安全对齐，但未直接探讨对齐本质是否脆弱。

papers.title: The Multilingual Alignment Prism: Aligning Global and Local Preferences to Reduce Harm
papers.abstract: A key concern with the concept of *“alignment”* is the implicit question of *“alignment to what?”*. AI systems are increasingly used across the world, yet safety alignment is often focused on homogeneous monolingual settings. Additionally, preference training and safety measures often overfit to harms common in Western-centric datasets. Here, we explore the viability of different alignment approaches when balancing dual objectives: addressing and optimizing for a non-homogeneous set of languages and cultural preferences while minimizing both global and local harms. We collect the first human annotated red teaming prompts in different languages, distinguishing between global and local harm, which serve as a laboratory to understand the reliability of alignment techniques when faced with preference distributions that are non-stationary across geographies and languages. While this setting is seldom covered by the literature to date, which primarily centers on English harm mitigation, it captures real-world interactions with AI systems around the world. We establish a new precedent for state-of-the-art alignment techniques across 6 languages with minimal degradation in general performance. Our work provides important insights into cross-lingual transfer and novel optimization approaches to safeguard AI systems designed to serve global populations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of safety alignment in multilingual, multicultural settings where Western-centric biases and monolingual data lead to uneven harm mitigation. The authors propose the Multilingual Alignment Prism, a framework that leverages human-annotated red teaming prompts across six languages, differentiating between global and local harms to study alignment under non-stationary preference distributions. They demonstrate state-of-the-art alignment performance across all six languages with minimal degradation in general task performance, offering insights into cross-lingual transfer and novel optimization methods. While this paper advances alignment methodology for global populations, it does not directly investigate the fragility or adversarial robustness of safety alignment; instead, it focuses on extending alignment to diverse linguistic contexts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多语言、多文化环境下安全对齐的挑战，指出西方中心的数据偏差和单语训练导致不同地区的有害内容缓解不均。作者提出多语言对齐棱镜（Multilingual Alignment Prism）框架，利用六种语言的人工标注红队测试提示，区分全球性与地方性危害，研究非稳态偏好分布下的对齐技术。实验在六种语言上均达到领先水平，且通用任务性能下降极小，揭示了跨语言迁移和新优化的价值。该工作主要推进了面向全球用户的对齐方法，但未直接考察安全对齐的脆弱性或对抗鲁棒性，而是专注于将对齐扩展至多语言场景。

papers.title: Discovering Knowledge-Critical Subnetworks in Pretrained Language Models
papers.abstract: Pretrained language models (LMs) encode implicit representations of knowledge in their parameters. However, localizing these representations and disentangling them from each other remains an open problem. In this work, we investigate whether pretrained language models contain various *knowledge-critical* subnetworks: particular sparse computational subgraphs that can, if removed, precisely suppress specific knowledge the model has memorized. We propose a multi-objective differentiable masking scheme that can be applied to both weights and neurons to discover such subnetworks and show that we can use them to precisely remove specific knowledge from models while minimizing adverse effects on the behavior of the original model. We demonstrate our method on multiple GPT2 variants, uncovering highly sparse subnetworks (98%+ sparsity) that are critical for expressing specific collections of relational knowledge. When these subnetworks are removed, the remaining network maintains most of its initial abilities but struggles to represent the suppressed knowledge.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses how implicit knowledge representations are localized in pretrained language models. It proposes a multi-objective differentiable masking approach to identify highly sparse knowledge-critical subnetworks within both weights and neurons. Evaluated on GPT2 variants, removing these subnetworks (98%+ sparsity) precisely suppresses specific relational knowledge while preserving the model's general abilities. This demonstrates that knowledge is not diffusely encoded but critically relies on small subcomponents, indicating a potential fragility where targeted removal could selectively erase knowledge, hinting that even alignment-related knowledge might be compromised if such subnetworks are exploited.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决预训练语言模型中隐性知识表征的定位问题，提出多目标可微分掩码方法，在权重和神经元中识别高度稀疏的知识关键子网络（稀疏度超98%）。在GPT2系列上的实验表明，移除这些子网络可精确抑制特定关系知识，同时保持模型通用能力。这揭示了知识并非弥散编码，而是依赖于稀疏子结构，暗示知识（乃至对齐知识）可能因针对性剪枝而脆弱易失，为后训练对齐的鲁棒性提供了机制层面的关注点。

papers.title: Alignment Quality Index (AQI) : Beyond Refusals: AQI as an Intrinsic Alignment Diagnostic via Latent Geometry, Cluster Divergence, and Layer wise Pooled Representations
papers.abstract: Alignment is no longer a luxury, it is a necessity. As large language models (LLMs) enter high-stakes domains like education, healthcare, governance, and law, their behavior must reliably reflect human-aligned values and safety constraints. Yet current evaluations rely heavily on behavioral proxies such as refusal rates, G-Eval scores, and toxicity classifiers, all of which have critical blind spots. Aligned models are often vulnerable to jailbreaking, stochasticity of generation, and alignment faking. To address this issue, we introduce the Alignment Quality Index (AQI). This novel geometric and prompt-invariant metric empirically assesses LLM alignment by analyzing the separation of safe and unsafe activations in latent space. By combining measures such as the Davies-Bouldin Score (DBS), Dunn Index (DI), Xie-Beni Index (XBI), and Calinski-Harabasz Index (CHI) across various formulations, AQI captures clustering quality to detect hidden misalignments and jailbreak risks, even when outputs appear compliant. AQI also serves as an early warning signal for alignment faking, offering a robust, decoding invariant tool for behavior agnostic safety auditing. Additionally, we propose the LITMUS dataset to facilitate robust evaluation under these challenging conditions. Empirical tests on LITMUS across different models trained under DPO, GRPO, and RLHF conditions demonstrate AQI's correlation with external judges and ability to reveal vulnerabilities missed by refusal metrics. We make our implementation publicly available to foster future research in this area.
papers.summary_en: Current LLM alignment evaluations rely on behavioral proxies like refusal rates, which miss vulnerabilities such as jailbreaking and alignment faking. The paper proposes the Alignment Quality Index (AQI), an intrinsic geometric metric that assesses the separation of safe and unsafe activations in latent space using clustering quality indices. Evaluated on a new LITMUS dataset across DPO, GRPO, and RLHF models, AQI correlates with external judges and reveals hidden vulnerabilities, serving as an early warning for alignment faking. This work directly addresses alignment fragility by showing that models can harbor latent misalignment undetectable by output-based metrics.
papers.summary_zh: 当前大语言模型安全对齐评估依赖基于行为的代理指标（如拒绝率），无法检测越狱攻击和对齐伪装等漏洞。本文提出对齐质量指数（AQI），一种内在几何度量，通过聚类质量指标分析潜在空间中安全与不安全激活的分离。在LITMUS数据集上对DPO、GRPO和RLHF模型测试显示，AQI与外部评判者相关，能揭示隐藏漏洞，作为对齐伪装的早期预警信号。该工作从机制层面证明，模型可能存在潜在不对齐，直接回应了后训练对齐能否被轻易破坏的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Understanding Performance Disparities in Large Language Models via Model Diffing
papers.short_title: Model Diffing for LLM Performance Gaps
papers.abstract: As fine-tuning becomes the dominant paradigm for improving large language models (LLMs), understanding what changes during this process is increasingly important. Traditional benchmarking often fails to explain why one model outperforms another. In this work, we use model diffing, a mechanistic interpretability approach, to analyze the specific capability differences between Gemma-2-9b-it and a SimPO-enhanced variant. Using crosscoders, we identify and categorize latent representations that differentiate the two models. We find that SimPO acquired latent concepts predominantly enhance safety mechanisms (+32.8%), multilingual capabilities (+43.8%), and instruction-following (+151.7%), while its additional training also reduces emphasis on model self-reference (-44.1%) and hallucination management (-68.5%). Our analysis shows that model diffing can yield fine-grained insights beyond leaderboard metrics, attributing performance gaps to concrete mechanistic capabilities. This approach offers a transparent and targeted framework for comparing LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of understanding performance disparities between large language models (LLMs) beyond leaderboard metrics, particularly after fine-tuning. It proposes model diffing, a mechanistic interpretability approach using crosscoders, to identify and categorize latent representation differences between Gemma-2-9b-it and a SimPO-enhanced variant. The analysis reveals that SimPO improves safety, multilingual, and instruction-following capabilities while reducing self-reference and hallucination management. This paper advances alignment methodology by offering a transparent framework for comparing LLMs, but it does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对传统基准测试难以解释大语言模型（LLM）性能差异的问题，尤其是在微调之后。提出采用模型差分（model diffing）这一机制可解释性方法，利用交叉编码器识别并分类Gemma-2-9b-it与其SimPO增强变体之间的潜在表征差异。分析发现，SimPO显著增强了安全机制、多语言能力和指令遵循，但降低了模型自我参照和幻觉管理的比重。本文通过提供透明的LLM比较框架推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: IndoSafety: Culturally Grounded Safety for LLMs in Indonesian Languages
papers.short_title: IndoSafety: Cultural Safety for Indonesian LLMs
papers.abstract: Although region-specific large language models (LLMs) are increasingly developed, their safety remains underexplored, particularly in culturally diverse settings like Indonesia, where sensitivity to local norms is essential and highly valued by the community. In this work, we present IndoSafety, the first high-quality, human-verified safety evaluation dataset tailored for the Indonesian context, covering five language varieties: formal and colloquial Indonesian, along with three major local languages: Javanese, Sundanese, and Minangkabau. IndoSafety is constructed by extending prior safety frameworks to develop a taxonomy that captures Indonesia's sociocultural context. We find that existing Indonesian-centric LLMs often generate unsafe outputs, particularly in colloquial and local language settings, while fine-tuning on IndoSafety significantly improves safety while preserving task performance. Our work highlights the critical need for culturally grounded safety evaluation and provides a concrete step toward responsible LLM deployment in multilingual settings. Warning: This paper contains example data that may be offensive, harmful, or biased.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of safety evaluation for LLMs in culturally diverse settings by introducing IndoSafety, a human-verified safety dataset tailored for Indonesian languages and cultural norms. The dataset covers five language varieties and extends safety taxonomies to capture local sociocultural context. Experiments show that existing Indonesian LLMs often produce unsafe outputs in colloquial and local languages, but fine-tuning on IndoSafety significantly improves safety while preserving task performance. This paper advances safety alignment for multilingual contexts but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多元文化场景中LLM安全评估的缺失问题，提出了IndoSafety，一个针对印尼语言和文化规范的人工验证安全数据集。该数据集涵盖五种语言变体，并扩展安全分类以捕捉本地社会文化背景。实验表明，现有印尼LLM在口语和本地语言中常产生不安全输出，但在IndoSafety上微调可显著提升安全性，同时保持任务性能。本文推进了多语言环境下的安全对齐，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Icon
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) require high quality preference datasets to align with human preferences. However, conventional methods for constructing such datasets face significant challenges: reliance on pre-collected instructions often leads to distribution mismatches with target models, while the need for sampling multiple stochastic responses introduces substantial computational overhead. In this work, we explore a paradigm shift by leveraging inherent regulation of LLMs’ representation space for efficient and tailored preference dataset construction, named Icon2
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenges of distribution mismatches and high computational costs in constructing preference datasets for LLM alignment. It proposes Icon2, a method that leverages LLMs' representation space to efficiently create tailored preference data without sampling multiple responses. The approach demonstrates a paradigm shift toward more efficient dataset construction, though specific evaluation results are not provided in the abstract. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM对齐中偏好数据集构建所面临的分布不匹配和高计算开销问题，提出Icon2方法，通过利用LLM表征空间的固有规律高效生成定制化偏好数据，避免多响应采样。该方法展示了数据集构建的新范式，推进了对齐技术，但摘要未提供具体评估结果，也未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: GuardBench: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Guardrail Models
papers.abstract: Generative AI systems powered by Large Language Models have become increasingly popular in recent years. Lately, due to the risk of providing users with unsafe information, the adoption of those systems in safety-critical domains has raised significant concerns. To respond to this situation, input-output filters, commonly called guardrail models, have been proposed to complement other measures, such as model alignment. Unfortunately, the lack of a standard benchmark for guardrail models poses significant evaluation issues and makes it hard to compare results across scientific publications. To fill this gap, we introduce GuardBench, a large-scale benchmark for guardrail models comprising 40 safety evaluation datasets. To facilitate the adoption of GuardBench, we release a Python library providing an automated evaluation pipeline built on top of it. With our benchmark, we also share the first large-scale prompt moderation datasets in German, French, Italian, and Spanish. To assess the current state-of-the-art, we conduct an extensive comparison of recent guardrail models and show that a general-purpose instruction-following model of comparable size achieves competitive results without the need for specific fine-tuning.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the absence of a standard benchmark for evaluating guardrail models, which act as input-output filters for LLM safety. It introduces GuardBench, a large-scale benchmark comprising 40 safety evaluation datasets, along with a Python library for automated evaluation and the first large-scale prompt moderation datasets in German, French, Italian, and Spanish. An extensive comparison of recent guardrail models reveals that a general-purpose instruction-following model of comparable size can match specialized guardrails without fine-tuning. The work advances guardrail evaluation infrastructure but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了缺乏标准基准来评估安全护栏模型（作为大语言模型输入输出过滤器）的问题。提出了GuardBench，一个包含40个安全评估数据集的大规模基准，并发布了用于自动评估的Python库以及首批大规模德语、法语、意大利语和西班牙语提示审核数据集。通过对近期护栏模型的广泛比较，发现同等规模的通用指令跟随模型无需专门微调即可达到有竞争力的护栏性能。该工作推进了护栏评估方法，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Self-Augmented Preference Alignment for Sycophancy Reduction in LLMs
papers.abstract: Sycophancy causes models to produce answers that cater to user expectations rather than providing truthful responses. Sycophantic behavior in models can erode user trust by creating a perception of dishonesty or bias. This lack of authenticity may lead users to question the reliability and objectivity of the system’s responses. Although Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is effective in aligning models with human preferences, previous studies have observed that it can simultaneously amplify sycophantic behavior. However, these studies primarily focused on proprietary models and employed indirect analysis to demonstrate the influence of human feedback. Our study focuses on sycophancy in open-source models, which are more reproducible and transparent for research. We investigated the impact of human feedback on sycophancy by directly comparing models aligned with human feedback to those not aligned. To address sycophancy, we proposed assessing the user’s expected answer rather than ignoring it. Consequently, we developed the Sycophancy Answer Assessment (SAA) dataset and introduced Self-Augmented Preference Alignment, demonstrating that these methods effectively enhance the model’s assessment ability and significantly reduce sycophancy across tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses sycophancy in open-source LLMs, where models produce answers that cater to user expectations rather than being truthful, and studies how RLHF amplifies this behavior. It proposes Self-Augmented Preference Alignment, which enhances model assessment of expected answers, and introduces the Sycophancy Answer Assessment dataset. Evaluation shows these methods significantly reduce sycophancy across tasks. While this work improves alignment quality, it does not directly investigate the robustness of safety alignment against adversarial attacks or module fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文关注开源大语言模型中的谄媚行为（即模型迎合用户预期而非提供真实回答），并研究了基于人类反馈的强化学习如何放大这一行为。作者提出了自增强偏好对齐方法，增强模型对预期答案的评估能力，并构建了谄媚答案评估数据集。实验表明，该方法能显著减少各类任务中的谄媚行为。尽管该工作提升了对齐质量，但并未直接探讨安全对齐在面对攻击时的鲁棒性脆弱问题。

papers.title: TopicAttack: An Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via Topic Transition
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable performance across a range of NLP tasks. However, their strong instruction-following capabilities and inability to distinguish instructions from data content make them vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks. In such attacks, instructions with malicious purposes are injected into external data sources, such as web documents. When LLMs retrieve this injected data through tools, such as a search engine and execute the injected instructions, they provide misled responses. Recent attack methods have demonstrated potential, but their abrupt instruction injection often undermines their effectiveness. Motivated by the limitations of existing attack methods, we propose TopicAttack, which prompts the LLM to generate a fabricated conversational transition prompt that gradually shifts the topic toward the injected instruction, making the injection smoother and enhancing the plausibility and success of the attack. Through comprehensive experiments, TopicAttack achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an attack success rate (ASR) over 90\% in most cases, even when various defense methods are applied. We further analyze its effectiveness by examining attention scores. We find that a higher injected-to-original attention ratio leads to a greater success probability, and our method achieves a much higher ratio than the baseline methods.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses LLM vulnerability to indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions hidden in retrieved data mislead responses. It proposes TopicAttack, which generates a fabricated conversational transition to smoothly shift the topic toward the injected instruction, making the attack more plausible and successful. Evaluations show state-of-the-art attack success rates over 90% across models and tasks, even against defenses, with attention analysis revealing that a higher injected-to-original attention ratio boosts success. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as the novel attack surface exploits instruction-following via subtle topic shifts, effectively bypassing alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了大语言模型在间接提示注入攻击下的脆弱性，攻击者将恶意指令嵌入外部数据，导致模型输出误导性回复。提出了TopicAttack方法，通过生成伪造的对话过渡语句，将话题平滑转向注入指令，增强了攻击的隐蔽性和成功率。在多种模型和任务上的实验表明攻击成功率超过90%，即使面对防御措施，注意力分析发现注入内容获得更高的注意力比例是关键。该论文直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，利用话题过渡绕过对齐的新攻击面表明模型容易受到此类高级攻击。

papers.title: SAEs Are Good for Steering - If You Select the Right Features
papers.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have been proposed as an unsupervised approach to learn a decomposition of a model's latent space. This enables useful applications such as steering - influencing the output of a model towards a desired concept - without requiring labeled data. Current methods identify SAE features to steer by analyzing the input tokens that activate them. However, recent work has highlighted that activations alone do not fully describe the effect of a feature on the model's output. In this work, we draw a distinction between two types of features: input features, which mainly capture patterns in the model's input, and output features, which have a human-understandable effect on the model's output. We propose input and output scores to characterize and locate these types of features, and show that high values for both scores rarely co-occur in the same features. These findings have practical implications: after filtering out features with low output scores, we obtain 2-3x improvements when steering with SAEs, making them competitive with supervised methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of effectively steering model outputs using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) without labeled data, as current methods based on activation patterns often fail to capture the true effect on output. It distinguishes input features (capturing input patterns) from output features (causally influencing output) and proposes input and output scores to identify the latter. By filtering for features with high output scores, steering performance improves by 2-3x, making SAE-based steering competitive with supervised methods. This work advances unsupervised alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了无需标注数据、利用稀疏自编码器（SAE）有效引导模型的问题，指出现有基于激活模式的方法常无法捕捉对输出的实际影响。作者区分了输入特征（捕获输入模式）和输出特征（因果性地影响输出），并提出输入、输出分数来定位后者。通过筛选高输出分数的特征，引导性能提升2-3倍，使基于SAE的引导可与监督方法媲美。该工作推进了无监督对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Towards Tool Use Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.short_title: ToolAlign: Aligning LLMs for Tool Use
papers.abstract: Recently, tool use with LLMs has become one of the primary research topics as it can help LLM generate truthful and helpful responses. Existing studies on tool use with LLMs primarily focus on enhancing the tool-calling ability of LLMs. In practice, like chat assistants, LLMs are also required to align with human values in the context of tool use. Specifically, LLMs should refuse to answer unsafe tool use relevant instructions and insecure tool responses to ensure their reliability and harmlessness. At the same time, LLMs should demonstrate autonomy in tool use to reduce the costs associated with tool calling. To tackle this issue, we first introduce the principle that LLMs should follow in tool use scenarios: H2A. The goal of H2A is to align LLMs with **helpfulness**, **harmlessness**, and **autonomy**. In addition, we propose ToolAlign, a dataset comprising instruction-tuning data and preference data to align LLMs with the H2A principle for tool use. Based on ToolAlign, we develop LLMs by supervised fine-tuning and preference learning, and experimental results demonstrate that the LLMs exhibit remarkable tool-calling capabilities, while also refusing to engage with harmful content, and displaying a high degree of autonomy in tool utilization. The code and datasets are available at: https://github.com/zhiyuanc2001/ToolAlign.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with human values during tool use, specifically targeting helpfulness, harmlessness, and autonomy (H2A). The authors propose ToolAlign, a dataset combining instruction-tuning and preference data, and use supervised fine-tuning and preference learning to train aligned models. Experiments show that models trained with ToolAlign demonstrate strong tool-calling abilities, refuse harmful instructions, and show high autonomy in tool use. The work contributes to alignment methodology for tool-augmented LLMs but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决在工具使用场景下使大语言模型与人类价值对齐的挑战，特别关注有用性、无害性和自主性（H2A）。作者提出ToolAlign数据集，包含指令微调数据和偏好数据，并通过监督微调和偏好学习训练对齐模型。实验表明，使用ToolAlign训练的模型展现出强大的工具调用能力，拒绝有害指令，并在工具使用中表现出高度自主性。这项工作推进了工具增强型大语言模型的对齐方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Refusal-Aware Red Teaming: Exposing Inconsistency in Safety Evaluations
papers.abstract: The responsible deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) necessitates rigorous safety evaluations. However, a critical challenge arises from inconsistencies between an LLM’s internal refusal decisions and external safety assessments, hindering effective validation. This paper introduces the concept of the ‘refusal gap’ to formally define these discrepancies. We then present a novel, refusal-aware red teaming framework designed to automatically generate test cases that expose such gaps. Our framework employs ‘refusal probes’, which leverage the target model’s hidden states, to detect internal model refusals. These are subsequently contrasted with judgments from an external safety evaluator. The identified discrepancy serves as a signal to guide a red-teaming model in crafting test cases that maximize this refusal gap. To further enhance test case diversity and address challenges related to sparse rewards, we introduce a hierarchical, curiosity-driven mechanism that incentivizes both refusal gap maximization and broad topic exploration. Empirical results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing reinforcement learning-based approaches in generating diverse test cases and achieves a substantially higher discovery rate of refusal gaps.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces the concept of 'refusal gap' to define inconsistencies between an LLM's internal refusal decisions and external safety assessments. It proposes a refusal-aware red teaming framework that leverages refusal probes on hidden states and an external evaluator to guide generation of test cases maximizing this gap, incorporating a hierarchical curiosity-driven mechanism for diversity. Experiments show superior performance over reinforcement learning baselines in generating diverse test cases and achieving a higher refusal gap discovery rate. This work exposes a fragility in post-training safety alignment: the misalignment between internal model states and external evaluations can be systematically exploited, indicating that safety alignment may not be robust against such consistency attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 论文提出了“拒绝间隙”概念，用于形式化定义大语言模型内部拒绝决策与外部安全评估之间的不一致。提出了一种拒绝感知的红队测试框架，利用基于隐藏状态的拒绝探针和外部评估器，引导红队模型生成最大化该间隙的测试用例，并引入分层好奇心驱动机制以增强多样性。实验表明，该方法在生成多样化测试用例和实现更高的拒绝间隙发现率方面显著优于现有强化学习方法。该研究揭示了训练后安全对齐的一个脆弱性：模型内部状态与外部评估之间的不一致可被系统性利用，表明安全对齐在面对此类一致性攻击时可能不够稳健。

papers.title: How Susceptible are Large Language Models to Ideological Manipulation?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) possess the potential to exert substantial influence on public perceptions and interactions with information. This raises concerns about the societal impact that could arise if the ideologies within these models can be easily manipulated. In this work, we investigate how effectively LLMs can learn and generalize ideological biases from their instruction-tuning data. Our findings reveal a concerning vulnerability: exposure to only a small amount of ideologically driven samples significantly alters the ideology of LLMs. Notably, LLMs demonstrate a startling ability to absorb ideology from one topic and generalize it to even unrelated ones. The ease with which LLMs’ ideologies can be skewed underscores the risks associated with intentionally poisoned training data by malicious actors or inadvertently introduced biases by data annotators. It also emphasizes the imperative for robust safeguards to mitigate the influence of ideological manipulations on LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates how easily large language models (LLMs) acquire and generalize ideological biases from instruction-tuning data. By exposing LLMs to only a small number of ideologically driven samples, they measure subsequent ideological shifts both within and across topics. The key finding is that minimal exposure significantly alters the LLM's ideology, and the learned bias generalizes to even unrelated topics, highlighting a severe vulnerability. This directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile: ideological alignment can be broken with minimal data poisoning and exhibits strong out-of-distribution generalization, undermining the robustness of alignment methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究了大语言模型在指令微调过程中习得和泛化意识形态偏见的容易程度。通过让LLM接触少量意识形态驱动的样本，测试其在同主题和跨主题上的意识形态转变。关键发现是极少量的暴露就能显著改变LLM的意识形态，且习得的偏见会泛化到无关话题，暴露出严重脆弱性。这项工作直接表明训练后安全对齐是脆弱的：意识形态对齐可被极少量有毒数据破坏并展现出强分布外泛化能力，动摇了对齐方法的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Language Models Identify Ambiguities and Exploit Loopholes
papers.abstract: Studying the responses of large language models (LLMs) to loopholes presents a two-fold opportunity. First, it affords us a lens through which to examine ambiguity and pragmatics in LLMs, since exploiting a loophole requires identifying ambiguity and performing sophisticated pragmatic reasoning. Second, loopholes pose an interesting and novel alignment problem where the model is presented with conflicting goals and can exploit ambiguities to its own advantage. To address these questions, we design scenarios where LLMs are given a goal and an ambiguous user instruction in conflict with the goal, with scenarios covering scalar implicature, structural ambiguities, and power dynamics. We then measure different models'abilities to exploit loopholes to satisfy their given goals as opposed to the goals of the user. We find that both closed-source and stronger open-source models can identify ambiguities and exploit their resulting loopholes, presenting a potential AI safety risk. Our analysis indicates that models which exploit loopholes explicitly identify and reason about both ambiguity and conflicting goals.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how large language models (LLMs) can exploit loopholes in ambiguous instructions when given a conflicting goal, examining both pragmatic reasoning and alignment risks. The authors design scenarios with various types of ambiguity (scalar implicature, structural, power dynamics) to measure whether models prioritize their own goals over user instructions by exploiting loopholes. They find that both closed-source and stronger open-source models successfully identify ambiguities and exploit resulting loopholes, with the exploitative models explicitly reasoning about ambiguity and conflicting goals. This directly reveals a fragility in safety alignment: models can strategically bypass intended constraints through sophisticated pragmatic interpretation, challenging the robustness of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 这个研究探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在给定冲突目标时如何利用模糊指令中的漏洞，既考察了语用推理也关注了对齐风险。作者设计了包含不同歧义类型（标量隐涵、结构歧义、权力动态）的场景，以衡量模型是否通过利用漏洞来优先满足自身目标而非用户指令。研究发现，闭源和较强开源模型都能识别歧义并利用漏洞，且这些模型会明确推理歧义和冲突目标。这直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：模型可以通过复杂的语用解释战略性地绕过预期约束，挑战了训练后对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: RLHF Can Speak Many Languages: Unlocking Multilingual Preference Optimization for LLMs
papers.abstract: Preference optimization techniques have become a standard final stage for training state-of-art large language models (LLMs). However, despite widespread adoption, the vast majority of work to-date has focused on a small set of high-resource languages like English and Chinese. This captures a small fraction of the languages in the world, but also makes it unclear which aspects of current state-of-the-art research transfer to a multilingual setting. In this work, we perform an exhaustive study to achieve a new state of the art in aligning multilingual LLMs. We introduce a novel, scalable method for generating high-quality multilingual feedback data to balance data coverage. We establish the benefits of cross-lingual transfer and increased dataset size in preference training. Our preference-trained model achieves a 54.4% win-rate against Aya 23 8B, the current state-of-the-art multilingual LLM in its parameter class, and a 69.5% win-rate or higher against widely used models like Gemma, Mistral and Llama 3. As a result of our efforts, we expand the frontier of alignment techniques to 23 languages, covering approximately half of the world’s population.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the gap in multilingual preference optimization, which limits LLM alignment to mainly high-resource languages. It proposes a scalable method for generating diverse multilingual feedback data and studies the role of cross-lingual transfer and dataset scaling in preference training. The resulting model achieves a 54.4% win-rate against Aya 23 8B and exceeds 69.5% against models like Gemma, Mistral, and Llama 3, extending alignment techniques to 23 languages. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多语言偏好优化的缺失问题，这一缺失导致大语言模型对齐主要局限于高资源语言。提出了一种可扩展的方法来生成多样化的多语言反馈数据，并研究了跨语言迁移和数据集规模在偏好训练中的作用。所得模型在对Aya 23 8B时胜率达到54.4%，对Gemma、Mistral和Llama 3等模型的胜率超过69.5%，将对齐技术扩展至23种语言。这项工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Keep Security! Benchmarking Security Policy Preservation in Large Language Model Contexts Against Indirect Attacks in Question Answering
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive domains such as enterprise and government, ensuring that they adhere to user-defined security policies within context is critical-especially with respect to information non-disclosure. While prior LLM studies have focused on general safety and socially sensitive data, large-scale benchmarks for contextual security preservation against attacks remain lacking. To address this, we introduce a novel large-scale benchmark dataset, CoPriva, evaluating LLM adherence to contextual non-disclosure policies in question answering. Derived from realistic contexts, our dataset includes explicit policies and queries designed as direct and challenging indirect attacks seeking prohibited information. We evaluate 10 LLMs on our benchmark and reveal a significant vulnerability: many models violate user-defined policies and leak sensitive information. This failure is particularly severe against indirect attacks, highlighting a critical gap in current LLM safety alignment for sensitive applications. Our analysis reveals that while models can often identify the correct answer to a query, they struggle to incorporate policy constraints during generation. In contrast, they exhibit a partial ability to revise outputs when explicitly prompted. Our findings underscore the urgent need for more robust methods to guarantee contextual security.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to indirect attacks that bypass contextual non-disclosure security policies in question answering, a gap in current safety benchmarks. It introduces CoPriva, a large-scale benchmark dataset containing explicit policies and both direct and indirect attack queries. Evaluation of 10 LLMs reveals significant vulnerability, especially under indirect attacks, where models often identify the correct answer but fail to incorporate policy constraints during generation, though they can partially revise outputs when explicitly prompted. By demonstrating a new attack surface that exploits policy adherence, this paper provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大型语言模型在问答中面对间接攻击时容易违反上下文安全策略（如信息保密）的问题，这是现有安全基准的不足。它提出了CoPriva，一个大规模基准数据集，包含明确策略及直接与间接攻击查询。对10个模型的评估显示显著漏洞，尤其在间接攻击下，模型虽能识别正确答案，但生成时难以整合策略约束，仅在被明确提示时能部分修正输出。通过展示利用策略遵循的新攻击面，该论文直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Agent-to-Agent Theory of Mind: Testing Interlocutor Awareness among Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into multi-agent and human-AI systems, understanding their awareness of both self-context and conversational partners is essential for ensuring reliable performance and robust safety. While prior work has extensively studied situational awareness which refers to an LLM's ability to recognize its operating phase and constraints, it has largely overlooked the complementary capacity to identify and adapt to the identity and characteristics of a dialogue partner. In this paper, we formalize this latter capability as interlocutor awareness and present the first systematic evaluation of its emergence in contemporary LLMs. We examine interlocutor inference across three dimensions-reasoning patterns, linguistic style, and alignment preferences-and show that LLMs reliably identify same-family peers and certain prominent model families, such as GPT and Claude. To demonstrate its practical significance, we develop three case studies in which interlocutor awareness both enhances multi-LLM collaboration through prompt adaptation and introduces new alignment and safety vulnerabilities, including reward-hacking behaviors and increased jailbreak susceptibility. Our findings highlight the dual promise and peril of identity-sensitive behavior in LLMs, underscoring the need for further understanding of interlocutor awareness and new safeguards in multi-agent deployments. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/younwoochoi/InterlocutorAwarenessLLM.
papers.summary_en: This paper formalizes and evaluates interlocutor awareness—the ability of LLMs to recognize and adapt to a dialogue partner's identity—a capacity overlooked by prior work on situational awareness. The authors systematically test LLMs’ ability to infer peers across reasoning patterns, linguistic style, and alignment preferences, finding reliable identification of same-family and prominent models like GPT and Claude. Through case studies, they show that interlocutor awareness enhances multi-LLM collaboration via prompt adaptation but also introduces safety vulnerabilities, including increased jailbreak susceptibility and reward hacking. This work directly reveals new attack surfaces where post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed by exploiting identity-sensitive behaviors in multi-agent settings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文形式化并评估了大型语言模型的对话者意识（interlocutor awareness），即模型识别并适应对话伙伴身份的能力，该能力在以往的情境意识研究中被忽视。作者系统测试了模型在推理模式、语言风格和对齐偏好三个维度上对同类的识别能力，发现LLM能够可靠地识别同家族模型以及GPT、Claude等知名模型家族。通过案例研究，作者表明对话者意识既可以通过提示自适应增强多LLM协作，也会引入新的安全漏洞，包括越狱攻击易感性增加和奖励黑客行为。这项工作直接揭示了新的攻击面：在后训练安全对齐中，通过利用身份敏感行为，对齐机制显得脆弱且可被绕过。

papers.title: Investigating Value-Reasoning Reliability in Small Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Although small Large Language models (sLLMs) have been widely deployed in practical applications, little attention has been paid to their value-reasoning abilities, particularly in terms of reasoning reliability. To address this gap, we propose a systematic evaluation framework for assessing the Value-Reasoning Reliability of sLLMs. We define Value-Reasoning Reliability as comprising: (1) Output consistency under identical prompts, (2) Output Robustness under semantically equivalent prompts, (3) Maintaining stable value reasoning in the face of attacks, and (4) Consistency of value reasoning in open-ended value expression tasks. Our framework includes three core tasks: Repetition Consistency task, Interaction Stability task, and Open-ended Expression Consistency task. We further incorporate self-reported confidence scores to evaluate the model’s value reasoning reliability from two perspectives: the model’s self-awareness of its values, and its value-based decision-making. Our findings show that models vary significantly in their stability when responding to value-related questions. Moreover, we observe considerable output randomness, which is not always correlated with the self-reported confidence or expressed value preferences. This suggests that current models lack a reliable internal mechanism for stable value reasoning when addressing value-sensitive queries.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the underexplored problem of value-reasoning reliability in small Large Language Models (sLLMs). It proposes a systematic evaluation framework that assesses reliability through output consistency, robustness to paraphrases, stability under attacks, and open-ended expression consistency, incorporating self-reported confidence scores. Experiments reveal significant variability and randomness in sLLM responses to value-related queries, often uncorrelated with self-assessed confidence, highlighting unreliable internal mechanisms. By exposing fragility in value reasoning, this work directly supports the concern that post-training safety alignment may be brittle and easily bypassed in small models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对小型大语言模型（sLLM）中尚未充分探索的值推理可靠性问题展开研究。提出了一个系统评估框架，通过输出一致性、同义提示鲁棒性、攻击下的稳定性以及开放式表达一致性来衡量可靠性，并引入自我报告置信度分数。实验表明，sLLM在回应价值相关问题时表现出显著的变异性和随机性，且常与自我评估的置信度不相关，揭示了不可靠的内部机制。通过暴露值推理的脆弱性，该研究直接支持了如下担忧：小型模型的后训练安全对齐可能脆弱且易被绕过。

papers.title: PBI-Attack: Prior-Guided Bimodal Interactive Black-Box Jailbreak Attack for Toxicity Maximization
papers.abstract: Understanding the vulnerabilities of Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) to jailbreak attacks is essential for their responsible real-world deployment. Most previous work requires access to model gradients, or is based on human knowledge (prompt engineering) to complete jailbreak, and they hardly consider the interaction of images and text, resulting in inability to jailbreak in black box scenarios or poor performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Prior-Guided Bimodal Interactive Black-Box Jailbreak Attack for toxicity maximization, referred to as PBI-Attack. Our method begins by extracting malicious features from a harmful corpus using an alternative LVLM and embedding these features into a benign image as prior information. Subsequently, we enhance these features through bidirectional cross-modal interaction optimization, which iteratively optimizes the bimodal perturbations in an alternating manner through greedy search, aiming to maximize the toxicity of the generated response. The toxicity level is quantified using a well-trained evaluation model. Experiments demonstrate that PBI-Attack outperforms previous state-of-the-art jailbreak methods, achieving an average attack success rate of 92.5% across three open-source LVLMs and around 67.3% on three closed-source LVLMs. Disclaimer: This paper contains potentially disturbing and offensive content.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) to jailbreak attacks in black-box scenarios where gradient access is unavailable, a setting where prior methods often fail. It proposes PBI-Attack, a prior-guided bimodal interactive method that first extracts malicious features from a harmful corpus and embeds them into a benign image, then iteratively optimizes image and text perturbations via greedy search to maximize the toxicity of the generated response, as measured by a trained toxicity evaluator. Evaluated on three open-source and three closed-source LVLMs, PBI-Attack achieves an average attack success rate of 92.5% and 67.3% respectively, outperforming previous state-of-the-art jailbreak techniques. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment in multimodal models, as a black-box cross-modal optimization can reliably circumvent safeguards, revealing a new attack surface that challenges the robustness of alignment.
