papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）在无法获取梯度的黑盒场景下的越狱攻击脆弱性，解决了现有方法在此条件下常难以奏效的问题。提出了一种先验引导的双模态交互式攻击方法PBI-Attack，它首先利用替代LVLM从有害语料中提取恶意特征并将其嵌入良性图像作为先验，随后通过贪心搜索交替优化图像和文本扰动，以最大化生成响应的有害程度，其毒性由训练好的评估模型量化。在三个开源和三个闭源LVLM上的实验表明，PBI-Attack的平均攻击成功率分别达到92.5%和67.3%，优于先前最先进的越狱方法。该研究直接证明了多模态模型中后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因为黑盒跨模态优化能够可靠地绕过防护，揭示了一个新的攻击面，对对齐的鲁棒性提出了挑战。

papers.title: The Accuracy Paradox in RLHF: When Better Reward Models Don't Yield Better Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback significantly enhances Natural Language Processing by aligning language models with human expectations. A critical factor in this alignment is the strength of reward models used during training. This study explores whether stronger reward models invariably lead to better language models. In this paper, through experiments on relevance, factuality, and completeness tasks using the QA-FEEDBACK dataset and reward models based on Longformer, we uncover a surprising paradox: language models trained with moderately accurate reward models outperform those guided by highly accurate ones. This challenges the widely held belief that stronger reward models always lead to better language models, and opens up new avenues for future research into the key factors driving model performance and how to choose the most suitable reward models.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether more accurate reward models in RLHF always lead to better language model alignment. It conducts an empirical study on relevance, factuality, and completeness tasks using the QA-FEEDBACK dataset and Longformer-based reward models. The key finding is a paradox: language models trained with moderately accurate reward models outperform those guided by highly accurate ones. This paper reveals a counterintuitive phenomenon in alignment optimization but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文探讨了在RLHF中，更准确的奖励模型是否总能提升语言模型对齐性能的问题。通过在QA-FEEDBACK数据集上使用基于Longformer的奖励模型对相关性、事实性和完整性任务进行实验，发现了一个悖论：中等准确度的奖励模型训练出的语言模型优于高准确度奖励模型。该研究揭示了对齐优化中的意外现象，但未直接涉及安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Improving Discriminative Capability of Reward Models in RLHF Using Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is a crucial approach to aligning language models with human values and intentions. A fundamental challenge in this method lies in ensuring that the reward model accurately understands and evaluates human preferences. Current methods rely on ranking losses to teach the reward model to assess preferences, but they are susceptible to noise and ambiguous data, often failing to deeply understand human intentions. To address this issue, we introduce contrastive learning into the reward modeling process. In addition to supervised ranking loss, we introduce an unsupervised contrastive loss to enable the reward model to fully capture the distinctions in contrastive data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed contrastive learning-based reward modeling method effectively enhances the generalization of the reward model, stabilizes the reinforcement learning training process, and improves the final alignment with human preferences.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that reward models in RLHF often fail to capture human preferences deeply due to noise in ranking losses. It proposes enhancing reward modeling by adding an unsupervised contrastive loss to the standard supervised ranking loss, improving discriminative capability. Experimental results show that the contrastive approach improves reward model generalization, stabilizes RL training, and yields better alignment with human preferences. While this advances alignment methodology by making reward models more robust, it does not directly study the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中奖励模型因排序损失易受噪声影响而无法深入理解人类偏好的问题。提出在标准的有监督排序损失基础上引入无监督对比损失，以增强奖励模型的辨别能力。实验表明，该方法提升了奖励模型的泛化能力，稳定了强化学习训练过程，并改善了与人类偏好的对齐效果。本文改进了对齐方法，提高了奖励模型的稳健性，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或可绕过性。

papers.title: SDGO: Self-Discrimination-Guided Optimization for Consistent Safety in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at various natural language processing tasks but remain vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks that induce harmful content generation. In this paper, we reveal a critical safety inconsistency: LLMs can more effectively identify harmful requests as discriminators than defend against them as generators. This insight inspires us to explore aligning the model's inherent discrimination and generation capabilities. To this end, we propose SDGO (Self-Discrimination-Guided Optimization), a reinforcement learning framework that leverages the model's own discrimination capabilities as a reward signal to enhance generation safety through iterative self-improvement. Our method does not require any additional annotated data or external models during the training phase. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDGO significantly improves model safety compared to both prompt-based and training-based baselines while maintaining helpfulness on general benchmarks. By aligning LLMs'discrimination and generation capabilities, SDGO brings robust performance against out-of-distribution (OOD) jailbreaking attacks. This alignment achieves tighter coupling between these two capabilities, enabling the model's generation capability to be further enhanced with only a small amount of discriminative samples. Our code and datasets are available at https://github.com/NJUNLP/SDGO.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inconsistency in large language models (LLMs) where they can better identify harmful requests as discriminators than refuse them as generators, leaving them vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks. It proposes SDGO, a reinforcement learning framework that uses the model's own discrimination capability as a reward signal to optimize generation safety through iterative self-improvement, without needing external annotated data. Experiments show SDGO significantly improves safety against both in-distribution and out-of-distribution jailbreaking attacks while maintaining helpfulness on general benchmarks. By tightly coupling the model's discrimination and generation competencies, SDGO directly strengthens the robustness of post-training safety alignment, demonstrating that it can be made less fragile and more resilient against adversarial bypass attempts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型的安全不一致性问题，即模型作为判别器能更有效地识别有害请求，但作为生成器却难以防御这些请求，导致易受越狱攻击。它提出了SDGO框架，一种强化学习方法，利用模型自身的判别能力作为奖励信号，通过迭代自我优化来提升生成安全性，无需额外标注数据。实验表明，SDGO在分布内和分布外越狱攻击下均显著提升了模型的安全性，同时在通用基准上保持了有用性。通过紧密耦合模型的判别与生成能力，SDGO直接增强了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性，证明对齐可以不再脆弱，能有效抵御对抗性绕过。

papers.title: Anecdoctoring: Automated Red-Teaming Across Language and Place
papers.abstract: Disinformation is among the top risks of generative artificial intelligence (AI) misuse. Global adoption of generative AI necessitates red-teaming evaluations (i.e., systematic adversarial probing) that are robust across diverse languages and cultures, but red-teaming datasets are commonly US- and English-centric. To address this gap, we propose"anecdoctoring", a novel red-teaming approach that automatically generates adversarial prompts across languages and cultures. We collect misinformation claims from fact-checking websites in three languages (English, Spanish, and Hindi) and two geographies (US and India). We then cluster individual claims into broader narratives and characterize the resulting clusters with knowledge graphs, with which we augment an attacker LLM. Our method produces higher attack success rates and offers interpretability benefits relative to few-shot prompting. Results underscore the need for disinformation mitigations that scale globally and are grounded in real-world adversarial misuse.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that current red-teaming for LLMs is US- and English-centric, lacking robustness across languages and cultures. It proposes 'anecdoctoring', a method that automatically generates adversarial prompts by collecting and clustering real-world misinformation claims from fact-checking websites in multiple languages and regions, then augmenting an attacker LLM with knowledge graphs. Evaluation in English, Spanish, and Hindi shows higher attack success rates compared to few-shot prompting, with added interpretability benefits. This paper provides direct evidence for the fragility of safety alignment by demonstrating that cross-lingual and cross-cultural attacks can bypass safeguards, indicating that alignment may not scale globally and is vulnerable to real-world misuse.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前大语言模型红队测试以美国和英语为中心、缺乏跨语言跨文化鲁棒性的问题。提出了“anecdoctoring”方法，通过从多语言事实核查网站收集并聚类真实世界的错误信息声明，利用知识图谱增强攻击型语言模型，自动生成对抗提示。在英语、西班牙语和印地语上的评估表明，与少样本提示相比，攻击成功率更高，且具有可解释性优势。该研究直接回应了安全性对齐的脆弱性问题，表明通过跨语言和跨文化攻击可以绕过安全对齐，说明对齐可能无法全球扩展，易受现实世界滥用。

papers.title: SPIRIT: Patching Speech Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: Speech Language Models (SLMs) enable natural interactions via spoken instructions, which more effectively capture user intent by detecting nuances in speech. The richer speech signal introduces new security risks compared to text-based models, as adversaries can better bypass safety mechanisms by injecting imperceptible noise to speech. We analyze adversarial attacks and find that SLMs are substantially more vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which can achieve a perfect 100% attack success rate in some instances. To improve security, we propose post-hoc patching defenses used to intervene during inference by modifying the SLM's activations that improve robustness up to 99% with (i) negligible impact on utility and (ii) without any re-training. We conduct ablation studies to maximize the efficacy of our defenses and improve the utility/security trade-off, validated with large-scale benchmarks unique to SLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates jailbreak attacks on Speech Language Models (SLMs), where adversaries inject imperceptible noise to speech inputs to bypass safety mechanisms, achieving up to 100% attack success rate. It proposes SPIRIT, a post-hoc patching defense that modifies SLM activations during inference to improve robustness without any retraining. Evaluated on large-scale SLM benchmarks, SPIRIT improves robustness by up to 99% with negligible impact on utility. This work highlights the fragility of safety alignment in speech models, as they are easily broken by adversarial noise, but also demonstrates that simple activation-level interventions can effectively harden them, suggesting that safety modules may be surface-level rather than deeply robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了语音语言模型（SLM）上的越狱攻击，攻击者通过在语音输入中添加难以察觉的噪声来绕过安全机制，某些情况下攻击成功率可达100%。提出SPIRIT防御方法，通过修改SLM的激活值进行事后修补，在推理时提升鲁棒性，且无需重新训练。在大规模SLM基准测试中，SPIRIT将鲁棒性提高至99%，对模型正常功用影响极小。本研究表明语音模型的安全对齐容易因对抗噪声而失效，但也说明通过简单的激活层干预可有效加固，暗示安全模块可能仅存于表层，缺乏深层鲁棒性。

papers.title: TombRaider: Entering the Vault of History to Jailbreak Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Warning: This paper contains content that may involve potentially harmful behaviours, discussed strictly for research purposes. Jailbreak attacks can hinder the safety of Large Language Model (LLM) applications, especially chatbots. Studying jailbreak techniques is an important AI red teaming task for improving the safety of these applications. In this paper, we introduce TombRaider, a novel jailbreak technique that exploits the ability to store, retrieve, and use historical knowledge of LLMs. TombRaider employs two agents, the inspector agent to extract relevant historical information and the attacker agent to generate adversarial prompts, enabling effective bypassing of safety filters. We intensively evaluated TombRaider on six popular models. Experimental results showed that TombRaider could outperform state-of-the-art jailbreak techniques, achieving nearly 100% attack success rates (ASRs) on bare models and maintaining over 55.4% ASR against defence mechanisms. Our findings highlight critical vulnerabilities in existing LLM safeguards, underscoring the need for more robust safety defences.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a new jailbreak attack that exploits LLMs' ability to store and retrieve historical knowledge to bypass safety filters. It proposes TombRaider, a dual-agent framework where an inspector agent extracts relevant historical context and an attacker agent crafts adversarial prompts based on that context. Evaluated on six popular models, TombRaider achieves nearly 100% attack success rate on bare models and maintains over 55.4% against defense mechanisms, outperforming state-of-the-art jailbreaks. By exposing a novel attack surface rooted in internal knowledge retrieval, the paper provides strong evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be circumvented through context-aware prompt engineering.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了一种利用大语言模型存储和检索历史知识以绕过安全过滤器的越狱攻击新方法。它提出了TombRaider，一个双智能体框架，其中检查员智能体提取相关历史上下文，攻击者智能体基于该上下文生成对抗性提示。在六种主流模型上的评估显示，TombRaider在裸模型上取得了接近100%的攻击成功率，并在面对防御机制时保持55.4%以上的成功率，优于现有越狱技术。通过发现基于内部知识检索的新攻击面，该论文有力地证明了后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过上下文感知的提示工程加以规避。

papers.title: DSCD: Large Language Model Detoxification with Self-Constrained Decoding
papers.abstract: Detoxification in large language models (LLMs) remains a significant research challenge. Existing decoding detoxification methods are all based on external constraints, which require additional resource overhead and lose generation fluency. This work proposes Detoxification with Self-Constrained Decoding (DSCD), a novel method for LLM detoxification without parameter fine-tuning. DSCD strengthens the inner next-token distribution of the safety layer while weakening that of hallucination and toxic layers during output generation. This effectively diminishes toxicity and enhances output safety. DSCD offers lightweight, high compatibility, and plug-and-play capabilities, readily integrating with existing detoxification methods for further performance improvement. Extensive experiments on representative open-source LLMs and public datasets validate DSCD's effectiveness, demonstrating state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in both detoxification and generation fluency, with superior efficiency compared to existing methods. These results highlight DSCD's potential as a practical and scalable solution for safer LLM deployments.
papers.summary_en: DSCD addresses toxic output in LLMs, where prior decoding detoxification methods rely on external constraints that incur overhead and hurt fluency. It proposes self-constrained decoding that amplifies safety-related token probabilities and dampens toxic/hallucinatory ones from internal layers, without fine-tuning. Evaluated on open-source LLMs, DSCD achieves state-of-the-art detoxification and fluency with superior efficiency. The paper advances alignment but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety; it offers a practical decoding-time defense.
papers.summary_zh: DSCD针对LLM输出毒性问题，现有解码去毒方法依赖外部约束，增加开销并影响流畅性。提出自约束解码，在生成时增强安全层下一个token分布，削弱毒性及幻觉层分布，无需微调。在开源LLM上评估，DSCD在去毒性和流畅性上均达最优，效率更高。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全的脆弱性，提供了一种实用的解码时安全机制。

papers.title: SAFENUDGE: Safeguarding Large Language Models in Real-time with Tunable Safety-Performance Trade-offs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been shown to be susceptible to jailbreak attacks, or adversarial attacks used to illicit high risk behavior from a model, highlighting the critical need to safeguard widely-deployed models. Safeguarding approaches, which include fine-tuning models or having LLMs “self-reflect,” may lengthen the inference time of a model, incur a computational penalty, reduce the semantic fluency of an output, and restrict “normal” model behavior. Importantly, these Safety-Performance Trade-offs (SPTs) remain an understudied area. In this work, we make three contributions: (1) We introduce SAFENUDGE, a novel safeguard that combines Controlled Text Generation and “nudging.” SAFENUDGE triggers during text-generation while a jailbreak attack is being executed, and can reduce successful jailbreak attempts by between 28.1% and 37.3% by guiding the LLM towards a safe response. It adds minimal latency to inference and has a negligible impact on the semantic fluency of outputs. Second, it supports tunable SPTs, meaning practitioners can set their own tolerance for trade-offs balancing safety and restrictions to normal model behavior. Third, we release the source code for SAFENUDGE at https://github.com/joaopfonseca/SafeNudge. It is open source and compatible with the HuggingFace transformers library.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models to jailbreak attacks that elicit unsafe behavior. It proposes SAFENUDGE, a real-time safeguard combining controlled text generation and nudging to steer outputs toward safety during an attack. Evaluated against jailbreak attempts, SAFENUDGE reduces successful attacks by 28.1–37.3% with minimal latency and fluency impact, while offering tunable safety-performance trade-offs. The paper reveals that standard post-training alignment is fragile against such attacks, but lightweight runtime defenses like SAFENUDGE can substantially harden models, highlighting that alignment can be bypassed yet augmented for robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型易受越狱攻击导致不安全行为的问题，提出了一种实时防护方法SAFENUDGE，通过可控文本生成和引导技术，在攻击过程中将输出导向安全方向。实验表明，SAFENUDGE可将成功越狱率降低28.1%–37.3%，且几乎不增加推理延迟或影响语义流畅性，并支持可调节的安全-性能权衡。研究表明，标准后训练安全对齐在面对越狱攻击时较为脆弱，但像SAFENUDGE这样的轻量级运行时防御能显著增强模型鲁棒性，说明对齐虽可被绕过，但仍可通过附加机制得到强化。

papers.title: Contrastive Policy Gradient: Aligning LLMs on sequence-level scores in a supervised-friendly fashion
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been used to finetune Large Language Models (LLMs) using a reward model trained from preference data, to better align with human judgment. The recently introduced direct alignment methods, which are often simpler, more stable, and computationally lighter, can more directly achieve this. However, these approaches cannot optimize arbitrary rewards, and the preference-based ones are not the only rewards of interest for LLMs (eg, unit tests for code generation or textual entailment for summarization, among others). RL-finetuning is usually done with a variation of policy gradient, which calls for on-policy or near-on-policy samples, requiring costly generations. We introduce *Contrastive Policy Gradient*, or CoPG, a simple and mathematically principled new RL algorithm that can estimate the optimal policy even from off-policy data. It can be seen as an off-policy policy gradient approach that does not rely on important sampling techniques and highlights the importance of using (the right) state baseline. We show this approach to generalize the direct alignment method IPO (identity preference optimization) and classic policy gradient. We experiment with the proposed CoPGon a toy bandit problem to illustrate its properties, as well as for finetuning LLMs on a summarization task, using a learned reward function considered as ground truth for the purpose of the experiments.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of direct alignment methods (like DPO) that cannot optimize arbitrary reward functions, such as unit tests or entailment scores, for LLM fine-tuning. It proposes Contrastive Policy Gradient (CoPG), an off-policy RL algorithm that estimates the optimal policy without requiring on-policy samples or importance sampling, and highlights the use of a state baseline. CoPG is evaluated on a toy bandit and LLM summarization with a learned reward, showing its effectiveness as a principled RL alternative. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了直接对齐方法（如DPO）不能优化任意奖励函数（如单元测试或文本蕴含得分）的问题，这些奖励对于LLM微调也有意义。提出了对比策略梯度（CoPG）算法，这是一种无偏估计最优策略的离策略强化学习方法，无需在线采样或重要性采样，并强调正确状态基线的作用。在玩具赌博机任务和基于学习奖励的LLM摘要任务上进行实验，验证了其作为原则性强化学习方法的有效性。该工作推进了对齐方法论，提供了更灵活的强化学习途径，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Modular Pluralism: Pluralistic Alignment via Multi-LLM Collaboration
papers.abstract: While existing alignment paradigms have been integral in developing large language models (LLMs), LLMs often learn an averaged human preference and struggle to model diverse preferences across cultures, demographics, and communities. We propose Modular Pluralism, a modular framework based on multi-LLM collaboration for pluralistic alignment: it “plugs into” a base LLM a pool of smaller but specialized community LMs, where models collaborate in distinct modes to flexibility support three modes of pluralism: Overton, steerable, and distributional. Modular Pluralism is uniquely compatible with black-box LLMs and offers the modular control of adding new community LMs for previously underrepresented communities. We evaluate Modular Pluralism with six tasks and four datasets featuring questions/instructions with value-laden and perspective-informed responses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Modular Pluralism advances the three pluralism objectives across six black-box and open-source LLMs. Further analysis reveals that LLMs are generally faithful to the inputs from smaller community LLMs, allowing seamless patching by adding a new community LM to better cover previously underrepresented communities.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of existing alignment methods that average human preferences, failing to model diverse values across different groups. It proposes Modular Pluralism, a multi-LLM collaboration framework that integrates a pool of smaller specialized community LMs with a base LLM to support three modes of pluralistic alignment: Overton, steerable, and distributional. Evaluations on six tasks and four datasets with value-laden responses show that Modular Pluralism effectively advances pluralism objectives across six LLMs, and the integration is faithful, allowing easy extension by adding new community LMs for underrepresented groups. This paper advances alignment methodology for handling pluralistic values but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有对齐方法平均化人类偏好、无法建模不同群体多样化价值观的问题。提出了模块化多元主义（Modular Pluralism），一个基于多LLM协作的框架，将多个小型专业化社区LLM与基座LLM集成，以支持三种多元对齐模式：Overton、可引导和分布式。在六个任务和四个包含价值观导向回答的数据集上的评估显示，Modular Pluralism在六个黑盒和开源LLM上有效推进了多元主义目标，且集成过程忠实，可无缝添加新社区LLM以覆盖先前代表性不足的群体。该论文推进了处理多元价值观的对齐方法论，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Breaking Bad Tokens: Detoxification of LLMs Using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now ubiquitous in user-facing applications, yet they still generate undesirable toxic outputs, including profanity, vulgarity, and derogatory remarks. Although numerous detoxification methods exist, most apply broad, surface-level fixes and can therefore easily be circumvented by jailbreak attacks. In this paper we leverage sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to identify toxicity-related directions in the residual stream of models and perform targeted activation steering using the corresponding decoder vectors. We introduce three tiers of steering aggressiveness and evaluate them on GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2-2B, revealing trade-offs between toxicity reduction and language fluency. At stronger steering strengths, these causal interventions surpass competitive baselines in reducing toxicity by up to 20%, though fluency can degrade noticeably on GPT-2 Small depending on the aggressiveness. Crucially, standard NLP benchmark scores upon steering remain stable, indicating that the model’s knowledge and general abilities are preserved. We further show that feature-splitting in wider SAEs hampers safety interventions, underscoring the importance of disentangled feature learning. Our findings highlight both the promise and the current limitations of SAE-based causal interventions for LLM detoxification, further suggesting practical guidelines for safer language-model deployment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the persistent issue of LLMs generating toxic content despite existing detoxification methods. It proposes using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to identify toxicity-related directions in the residual stream and apply targeted activation steering via decoder vectors, with three tiers of aggressiveness. Evaluated on GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2-2B, the approach reduces toxicity by up to 20% over baselines, though fluency degrades at higher strengths, while NLP benchmark scores remain stable. This paper advances alignment methodology by introducing a mechanistic detoxification technique but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型在现有去毒方法下仍生成有毒输出的问题。提出利用稀疏自编码器(SAE)定位残差流中的毒性方向，并通过解码器向量进行定向激活调控，引入三种调控强度。在GPT-2 Small和Gemma-2-2B上评估，相比基线最多降低20%毒性，但高强度下语言流畅度下降，而NLP基准分保持稳定。本文通过提出一种机械式去毒技术推进了对齐方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Leaky Thoughts: Large Reasoning Models Are Not Private Thinkers
papers.abstract: We study privacy leakage in the reasoning traces of large reasoning models used as personal agents. Unlike final outputs, reasoning traces are often assumed to be internal and safe. We challenge this assumption by showing that reasoning traces frequently contain sensitive user data, which can be extracted via prompt injections or accidentally leak into outputs. Through probing and agentic evaluations, we demonstrate that test-time compute approaches, particularly increased reasoning steps, amplify such leakage. While increasing the budget of those test-time compute approaches makes models more cautious in their final answers, it also leads them to reason more verbosely and leak more in their own thinking. This reveals a core tension: reasoning improves utility but enlarges the privacy attack surface. We argue that safety efforts must extend to the model's internal thinking, not just its outputs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses privacy leakage in the reasoning traces of large reasoning models when used as personal agents. It uses probing and agentic evaluations to show that reasoning traces often contain sensitive user data, which can be extracted via prompt injections or accidentally leak into outputs, and that test-time compute approaches like increased reasoning steps amplify this leakage. The key finding reveals a tension: while more reasoning steps make final answers more cautious, they also lead to more verbose internal thinking that leaks more private information. This directly relates to the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as it shows that safety measures focused only on final outputs fail to protect against leaks emerging from the model's internal reasoning, thus expanding the attack surface.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了当大型推理模型被用作个人代理时，其推理过程痕迹中的隐私泄露问题。通过探测和代理式评估，论文表明推理痕迹常常包含敏感用户数据，这些数据可通过提示注入被提取，或意外泄露到输出中；同时，增加推理步骤等测试时计算方法会加剧这种泄露。关键发现揭示了一种权衡：虽然增加推理步骤使最终回答更谨慎，但也导致模型内部思考更冗长，从而泄露更多隐私信息。这直接关系到后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题，因为它表明仅聚焦于最终输出的安全措施无法阻止从模型内部推理中产生的泄露，从而扩大了攻击面。

papers.title: Controllable Preference Optimization: Toward Controllable Multi-Objective Alignment
papers.abstract: Alignment in artificial intelligence pursues the consistency between model responses and human preferences as well as values. In practice, the multifaceted nature of human preferences inadvertently introduces what is known as the ”alignment tax”–a compromise where enhancements in alignment within one objective (e.g., harmlessness) can diminish performance in others (e.g., helpfulness). However, existing alignment techniques are mostly unidirectional, leading to suboptimal trade-offs and poor flexibility over various objectives. To navigate this challenge, we argue the prominence of grounding LLMs with evident preferences. We introduce controllable preference optimization (CPO), which explicitly specifies preference scores for different objectives, thereby guiding the model to generate responses that meet the requirements. Our experimental analysis reveals that the aligned models can provide responses that match various preferences among the ”3H” (helpfulness, honesty, harmlessness) desiderata. Furthermore, by introducing diverse data and alignment goals, we surpass baseline methods in aligning with single objectives, hence mitigating the impact of the alignment tax and achieving improvements in multi-objective alignment.
papers.summary_en: Existing alignment methods suffer from the alignment tax, where optimizing one objective (e.g., harmlessness) degrades others (e.g., helpfulness), resulting in rigid trade-offs. The paper proposes Controllable Preference Optimization (CPO), which explicitly models preference scores for multiple objectives to steer responses toward desired combinations. Experiments on the '3H' (helpful, honest, harmless) criteria show that CPO can produce responses matching diverse preference profiles and outperforms baselines on single objectives, thereby mitigating the alignment tax. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有对齐方法存在对齐税问题，即优化一个目标（如无害性）会损害其他目标（如帮助性），导致僵化的权衡。本文提出可控偏好优化（CPO），通过显式建模多目标的偏好分数，引导模型生成符合要求的响应。在“3H”（帮助性、诚实性、无害性）标准上的实验表明，CPO 能生成匹配不同偏好组合的回复，并在单一目标上超越基线，从而缓解对齐税。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SURE: Safety Understanding and Reasoning Enhancement for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities by integrating visual and textual information. However, the incorporation of visual modalities also introduces new and complex safety risks, rendering even the most advanced models vulnerable to sophisticated jailbreak attacks. This paper first analyzes the impact of inserting safety reasoning prompt on various aspects of the model. We find that this external method can help the model resist jailbreak attacks to some extent, but the model still fails to distinguish specific semantic scenarios, resulting in a significantly increased refusal rate for benign queries. Inspired by this, we propose a novel training framework, SURE (Safety Understanding and Reasoning Enhancement for Multimodal Large Language Models), designed to help models internalize chain-of-thought-based safety decision-making capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SURE significantly improves model safety while effectively avoiding over-defense, achieving a good balance between safety and generality. Finally, we create a large-scale multimodal safety reasoning dataset, MLLM-SCoT-Plus, to facilitate research on safety alignment in multimodal models.Our code and the dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/hfutml/SURE.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the fragility of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) against visual jailbreak attacks, where inserting external safety reasoning prompts reduces attack success but causes over-refusal of benign queries. It proposes SURE, a training framework that internalizes chain-of-thought safety reasoning, teaching MLLMs to autonomously evaluate safety without external prompts. Experiments show SURE significantly improves resistance to jailbreaks while maintaining high response rates to benign inputs, achieving a better safety–generality balance. The work directly addresses the fragility question by demonstrating that post-hoc safety measures are brittle and proposing a more robust, internalized alignment method that hardens MLLMs against multimodal attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型因视觉模态引入的越狱攻击脆弱性问题，指出外部安全推理提示虽能降低攻击成功率但会导致对良性查询过度拒答。为此提出训练框架SURE，通过内化思维链安全推理，使模型自主进行安全决策。实验表明SURE显著提升安全性并避免过度防御，实现安全与通用性的良好平衡。该研究揭示了现有多模态对齐在对抗攻击下的脆弱性，并提供了一种内在化的鲁棒防御方案，直接回应了后训练安全对齐是否牢固的问题。

papers.title: LoRA-Guard: Parameter-Efficient Guardrail Adaptation for Content Moderation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Guardrails have emerged as an alternative to safety alignment for content moderation of large language models (LLMs). Existing model-based guardrails have not been designed for resource-constrained computational portable devices, such as mobile phones, more and more of which are running LLM-based applications locally. We introduce LoRA-Guard, a parameter-efficient guardrail adaptation method that relies on knowledge sharing between LLMs and guardrail models. LoRA-Guard extracts language features from the LLMs and adapts them for the content moderation task using low-rank adapters, while a dual-path design prevents any performance degradation on the generative task. We show that LoRA-Guard outperforms existing approaches with 100-1000x lower parameter overhead while maintaining accuracy, enabling on-device content moderation.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of resource-efficient guardrails for content moderation in large language models (LLMs) on portable devices. It proposes LoRA-Guard, a parameter-efficient method that adapts LLM features for moderation via low-rank adapters with a dual-path design to preserve generative performance. Evaluated against existing approaches, LoRA-Guard achieves 100–1000x parameter reduction while maintaining accuracy, enabling on-device moderation. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of whether post-training safety alignment can be easily broken or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有内容审核护栏未考虑移动设备等资源受限环境的问题，提出LoRA-Guard方法，通过低秩适配器从大语言模型中提取语言特征并适应审核任务，采用双路径设计避免影响生成性能。实验表明，LoRA-Guard以100—1000倍的参数减少超越现有方法，保持准确率，实现设备端审核。该论文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究安全对齐是否容易被破坏或绕过的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Reward Model Perspectives: Whose Opinions Do Reward Models Reward?
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) are central to the alignment of language models (LMs). An RM often serves as a proxy for human preferences to guide downstream LM behavior. However, our understanding of RM behavior is limited. Our work (i) formalizes a framework for measuring the alignment of opinions captured by RMs, (ii) investigates the extent to which RMs demonstrate sociodemographic biases, and (iii) explores the effects of prompting to steer rewards towards the preferences of a target group. We study the subjective and diverse perspectives on controversial topics, which allows us to quantify RM perspectives in terms of their opinions, attitudes, and values. We show that RMs are poorly aligned with several demographic groups and can systematically reward harmful stereotypes, and steering alone is not enough to overcome these limitations. Our findings underscore the need for more careful consideration of RM behavior in model alignment during preference learning to prevent the propagation of unwanted social biases in the language technologies that we use.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the degree to which reward models (RMs) capture and perpetuate biased opinions across different demographic groups. It proposes a framework to quantify alignment between RM preferences and the perspectives of various groups, and explores prompt-based steering to adjust rewards toward a target group's preferences. Evaluations on controversial topics reveal that RMs are poorly aligned with several groups and systematically reward harmful stereotypes, and steering alone is insufficient to correct these biases. This work exposes a fundamental fragility in post-training safety alignment: the reward models that serve as the foundation for aligning language models are themselves vulnerable to social biases, threatening the robustness of the entire alignment pipeline.
papers.summary_zh: 本文考察了奖励模型在多大程度上捕获并延续不同人口群体的偏见意见。它提出了一个量化框架，用于测量奖励模型偏好与各群体视角之间的对齐程度，并探索了通过提示引导将奖励调整到目标群体偏好的方法。在争议性话题上的评估显示，奖励模型与多个群体的对齐度差，并系统性地奖励有害刻板印象，仅靠引导无法纠正这些偏见。这项工作揭示了后训练安全对齐的根本脆弱性：作为语言模型对齐基础的奖励模型本身易受社会偏见影响，从而威胁整个对齐流程的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Enhancing RLHF with Human Gaze Modeling
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) aligns language models with human preferences but is computationally expensive. We explore two approaches that leverage human gaze modeling to enhance RLHF: (1) gaze-aware reward models and (2) gaze-based distribution of sparse rewards at token level. Our experiments demonstate that gaze-informed RLHF achieves faster convergence while maintaining or slightly improving performance, thus, reducing computational costs during policy optimization. These results show that human gaze provides a valuable and underused signal for policy optimization, pointing to a promising direction for improving RLHF efficiency.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high computational cost of aligning language models with RLHF. It proposes integrating human gaze signals into RLHF through gaze-aware reward models and token-level sparse reward redistribution. Experiments show that gaze-informed RLHF achieves faster convergence while maintaining or slightly improving performance, thereby reducing policy optimization costs. The paper advances alignment methodology by leveraging human gaze data but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决利用RLHF对齐语言模型时计算成本高的问题。它提出通过注视感知奖励模型和令牌级稀疏奖励重分配，将人类注视信号融入RLHF。实验表明，融入注视信息的RLHF能更快收敛，同时保持或略微提升性能，从而降低策略优化成本。该工作利用人类注视数据推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探究训练后对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Jailbreak LLMs through Internal Stance Manipulation
papers.abstract: To confront the ever-evolving safety risks of LLMs, automated jailbreak attacks have proven effective for proactively identifying security vulnerabilities at scale. Existing approaches, including GCG and AutoDAN, modify adversarial prompts to induce LLMs to generate responses that strictly follow a fixed affirmative template. However, we observed that the reliance on the rigid output template is ineffective for certain malicious requests, leading to suboptimal jailbreak performance. In this work, we aim to develop a method that is universally effective across all hostile requests. To achieve this, we explore LLMs’ intrinsic safety mechanism: a refusal stance towards the adversarial prompt is formed in a confined region and ultimately leads to a rejective response. In light of this, we propose Stance Manipulation (SM), a novel automated jailbreak approach that generates jailbreak prompts to suppress the refusal stance and induce affirmative responses. Our experiments across four mainstream open-source LLMs demonstrate the superiority of SM’s performance. Under commenly used setting, SM achieves success rates over 77.1% across all models on Advbench. Specifically, for Llama-2-7b-chat, SM outperforms the best baseline by 25.4%. In further experiments with extended iterations in a speedup setup, SM achieves over 92.2% attack success rate across all models. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zed630/Stance-Manipulation.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of existing jailbreak attacks that rely on rigid affirmative templates, which fail for certain malicious requests. It proposes Stance Manipulation (SM), an automated jailbreak method that generates prompts to suppress the LLM's internal refusal stance and induce affirmative responses. Evaluated on four open-source LLMs, SM achieves over 77.1% attack success rate on Advbench and exceeds 92.2% with extended iterations, significantly outperforming baselines like GCG and AutoDAN. By targeting the internal refusal mechanism, the paper provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed through stance manipulation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有越狱攻击依赖固定肯定模板而导致某些恶意请求攻击无效的问题，提出了一种名为姿态操纵（SM）的自动化越狱方法，通过生成抑制拒绝姿态的提示来诱导肯定响应。在四个开源大语言模型上的实验表明，SM在Advbench上的攻击成功率超过77.1%，扩展迭代后达到92.2%以上，显著优于GCG和AutoDAN等基线。该研究通过操纵内部拒绝机制揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，直接证明后训练安全对齐可被轻易绕过。

papers.title: Jailbreaking LLMs with Arabic Transliteration and Arabizi
papers.abstract: This study identifies the potential vulnerabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to ‘jailbreak’ attacks, specifically focusing on the Arabic language and its various forms. While most research has concentrated on English-based prompt manipulation, our investigation broadens the scope to investigate the Arabic language. We initially tested the AdvBench benchmark in Standardized Arabic, finding that even with prompt manipulation techniques like prefix injection, it was insufficient to provoke LLMs into generating unsafe content. However, when using Arabic transliteration and chatspeak (or arabizi), we found that unsafe content could be produced on platforms like OpenAI GPT-4 and Anthropic Claude 3 Sonnet. Our findings suggest that using Arabic and its various forms could expose information that might remain hidden, potentially increasing the risk of jailbreak attacks. We hypothesize that this exposure could be due to the model’s learned connection to specific words, highlighting the need for more comprehensive safety training across all language forms.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates jailbreak attacks on LLMs using Arabic transliteration and Arabizi (Arabic chatspeak). It tests the AdvBench dataset in both standard Arabic and Arabizi, finding that while standard Arabic with prefix injection fails to elicit unsafe responses, Arabizi successfully bypasses safety mechanisms in GPT-4 and Claude 3 Sonnet. This demonstrates that LLM safety alignment is fragile: the models appear to have learned superficial associations with specific language forms rather than robustly internalizing safety principles, making them vulnerable to out-of-distribution linguistic variations.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了利用阿拉伯语转写和Arabizi（阿拉伯语网络俚语）对大型语言模型进行越狱攻击。通过在标准阿拉伯语和Arabizi上测试AdvBench数据集，发现标准阿拉伯语即使使用前缀注入也无法诱导不安全内容，而Arabizi却成功绕过了GPT-4和Claude 3 Sonnet的安全机制。这表明LLM的安全对齐具有脆弱性，模型似乎只是学习了对特定语言形式的表面关联，而非深度内化安全原则，因此容易受到分布外语言变体的攻击。

papers.title: Precise In-Parameter Concept Erasure in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often acquire knowledge during pretraining that is undesirable in downstream deployments, e.g., sensitive information or copyrighted content. Existing approaches for removing such knowledge rely on fine-tuning, training low-rank adapters or fact-level editing, but these are either too coarse, too shallow, or ineffective. In this work, we propose PISCES (Precise In-parameter Suppression for Concept EraSure), a novel framework for precisely erasing entire concepts from model parameters by directly editing directions that encode them in parameter space. PISCES uses a disentangler model to decompose MLP vectors into interpretable features, identifies those associated with a target concept using automated interpretability techniques, and removes them from model parameters. Experiments on Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1 over various concepts show that PISCES achieves modest gains in efficacy over leading erasure methods, reducing accuracy on the target concept to as low as 7.7%, while dramatically improving erasure specificity (by up to 31%) and robustness (by up to 38%). Overall, these results demonstrate that feature-based in-parameter editing enables a more precise and reliable approach for removing conceptual knowledge in language models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of erasing undesirable concepts (e.g., sensitive or copyrighted content) from LLMs. It proposes PISCES, a framework that directly edits model parameters by decomposing MLP vectors into interpretable features, identifying concept-associated directions, and removing them. Experiments on Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1 show that PISCES reduces target concept accuracy to 7.7% while significantly improving specificity and robustness over existing methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了从大语言模型中擦除不良概念（如敏感或受版权保护的内容）的挑战。它提出了PISCES框架，通过将MLP向量分解为可解释特征，识别与概念相关的方向并将其移除，从而直接编辑模型参数。在Gemma 2和Llama 3.1上的实验表明，PISCES将目标概念准确率降至7.7%，并显著提高了擦除的特异性和鲁棒性。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: A Simple Yet Effective Method for Non-Refusing Context Relevant Fine-grained Safety Steering in LLMs
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to meet evolving safety policies is costly and impractical. Mechanistic interpretability enables inference-time control through latent activation steering, but its potential for precise, customizable safety adjustments remains under-explored. We propose S AFE S TEER , a simple and effective method to guide LLM outputs by (i) leveraging category-specific steering vectors for fine-grained control, (ii) applying a gradient-free, unsupervised approach that enhances safety while preserving text quality and topic relevance without forcing explicit refusals, and (iii) eliminating the need for contrastive safe data. Across multiple LLMs, datasets, and risk categories, S AFE S TEER provides precise control, avoids blanket refusals, and directs models to generate safe, relevant content, aligning with recent findings that simple activation-steering techniques often outperform more complex alternatives.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the impracticality of fine-tuning LLMs for changing safety policies by enabling inference-time control. It proposes SAFESTEER, a method using category-specific steering vectors to achieve fine-grained, gradient-free, and unsupervised safety steering without contrastive safe data or explicit refusals. Evaluated across multiple LLMs, datasets, and risk categories, it demonstrates precise safety control while preserving text quality and topic relevance. This work advances alignment methodology by offering a lightweight, customizable safety steering approach, but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了通过微调大语言模型来适应不断变化的安全策略成本高昂且不切实际的问题。提出了SAFESTEER方法，通过分类别控制向量实现细粒度、无梯度、无监督的安全导向，无需对比安全数据，避免显式拒绝。在多个大语言模型、数据集和风险类别上的评估表明，该方法能精确控制安全性，同时保持文本质量和话题相关性。这项工作推进了对齐方法学，提供了一种轻量级、可定制的安全导向途径，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: SAE-SSV: Supervised Steering in Sparse Representation Spaces for Reliable Control of Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in natural language understanding and generation, but controlling their behavior reliably remains challenging, especially in open-ended generation settings. This paper introduces a novel supervised steering approach that operates in sparse, interpretable representation spaces. We employ sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to obtain sparse latent representations that aim to disentangle semantic attributes from model activations. Then we train linear classifiers to identify a small subspace of task-relevant dimensions in latent representations. Finally, we learn supervised steering vectors constrained to this subspace, optimized to align with target behaviors. Experiments across sentiment, truthfulness, and political polarity steering tasks with multiple LLMs demonstrate that our supervised steering vectors achieve higher success rates with minimal degradation in generation quality compared to existing methods. Further analysis reveals that a notably small subspace is sufficient for effective steering, enabling more targeted and interpretable interventions. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/Ineedanamehere/SAE-SSV.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably controlling LLM behavior in open-ended generation settings. It proposes a supervised steering approach that uses sparse autoencoders to obtain sparse latent representations, trains linear classifiers to identify a small task-relevant subspace, and learns steering vectors constrained to this subspace. Experiments on sentiment, truthfulness, and political polarity steering demonstrate higher success rates with minimal generation quality degradation compared to existing methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决在开放式生成场景下可靠控制大语言模型行为的挑战。提出一种在稀疏表示空间中的监督引导方法：利用稀疏自编码器获得稀疏潜在表示，训练线性分类器识别任务相关的小子空间，并在该子空间中学习优化的引导向量。在情感、真实性和政治倾向引导任务上，使用多个大语言模型实验，结果表明该方法相比现有方法成功率更高且生成质量退化最小。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Context Reasoner: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability for Contextualized Privacy and Safety Compliance via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities, they also introduce significant safety and privacy risks. Current mitigation strategies often fail to preserve contextual reasoning capabilities in risky scenarios. Instead, they rely heavily on sensitive pattern matching to protect LLMs, which limits the scope. Furthermore, they overlook established safety and privacy standards, leading to systemic risks for legal compliance. To address these gaps, we formulate safety and privacy issues into contextualized compliance problems following the Contextual Integrity (CI) theory. Under the CI framework, we align our model with three critical regulatory standards: GDPR, EU AI Act, and HIPAA. Specifically, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) with a rule-based reward to incentivize contextual reasoning capabilities while enhancing compliance with safety and privacy norms. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our method not only significantly enhances legal compliance (achieving a +8.58% accuracy improvement in safety/privacy benchmarks) but also further improves general reasoning capability. For OpenThinker-7B, a strong reasoning model that significantly outperforms its base model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct across diverse subjects, our method enhances its general reasoning capabilities, with +2.05% and +8.98% accuracy improvement on the MMLU and LegalBench benchmark, respectively.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the failure of current LLM safety mitigations that sacrifice contextual reasoning and rely on pattern matching, causing legal compliance risks. It frames safety and privacy as contextualized compliance problems under Contextual Integrity theory, employing reinforcement learning with rule-based rewards to align with GDPR, EU AI Act, and HIPAA. Evaluations show an +8.58% accuracy gain in compliance benchmarks and improved general reasoning (e.g., +2.05% on MMLU for OpenThinker-7B). The work advances alignment methodology by embedding legal compliance into contextual reasoning, but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了当前大语言模型安全缓解措施因牺牲上下文推理而依赖模式匹配，导致法律合规风险的问题。它将安全与隐私构架为情境完整性理论下的情境化合规问题，采用基于规则的奖励强化学习，使模型符合 GDPR、EU AI Act 和 HIPAA 标准。实验表明，合规基准准确率提升 +8.58%，通用推理能力也得到增强（如 OpenThinker-7B 在 MMLU 上提升 +2.05%）。该研究通过将法律合规融入情境推理推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Massive Supervised Fine-tuning Experiments Reveal How Data, Layer, and Training Factors Shape LLM Alignment Quality
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is a critical step in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human instructions and values, yet many aspects of SFT remain poorly understood. We trained a wide range of base models on a variety of datasets including code generation, mathematical reasoning, and general-domain tasks, resulting in 1,000+ SFT models under controlled conditions. We then identified the dataset properties that matter most and examined the layer-wise modifications introduced by SFT. Our findings reveal that some training-task synergies persist across all models while others vary substantially, emphasizing the importance of model-specific strategies. Moreover, we demonstrate that perplexity consistently predicts SFT effectiveness, often surpassing superficial similarity between the training data and the benchmark, and that mid-layer weight changes correlate most strongly with performance gains. We release these 1,000+ SFT models and benchmark results to accelerate further research. All resources are available at https://github.com/llm-jp/massive-sft.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates which factors most influence alignment quality in supervised fine-tuning (SFT), an area that remains poorly understood. The authors conducted massive controlled experiments, training over 1,000 SFT models on code, math, and general tasks to analyze dataset properties and layer-wise modifications. Key findings show that some training-task synergies persist across models, perplexity consistently predicts SFT effectiveness, and mid-layer weight changes correlate most strongly with performance gains. While the work provides valuable insights for building better alignment, it does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究监督微调（SFT）中对齐质量的关键影响因素，该领域当前理解尚不充分。作者进行了大规模受控实验，在代码、数学和通用任务上训练了1000多个SFT模型，以分析数据集属性和层级修改。关键发现表明，某些训练任务协同效应在不同模型间保持一致，困惑度能稳定预测SFT效果，且中间层权重变化与性能提升最相关。该研究为构建更好的对齐方法提供了见解，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Enhancing Language Model Alignment: A Confidence-Based Approach to Label Smoothing
papers.abstract: In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various domains. Within the training pipeline of LLMs, the Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) phase is crucial for aligning LLMs with human preferences and values. Label smoothing, a technique that replaces hard labels with soft labels, emerges as promising techniques to enhance RLHF training. Despite the benefits, the choice of label smoothing parameters often relies on heuristic approaches and lack theoretical understanding. This paper addresses the challenge of selecting the label smoothing parameter in a principled manner. We introduce Confidence Aware Label Smoothing (CALS), a method that iteratively updates the label smoothing parameter based on preference labels and model forecasts. Our theoretical analysis characterizes the optimal label smoothing parameter, demonstrates its dependence on the confidence level, and reveals its influence on training dynamics and equilibrium. Empirical evaluations on state-of-the-art alignment tasks show that CALS achieves competitive performance, highlighting its potential for improving alignment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the heuristic selection of label smoothing parameters in RLHF-based LLM alignment, which lacks theoretical grounding. It proposes Confidence Aware Label Smoothing (CALS), a method that dynamically adjusts the smoothing parameter based on model confidence and preference labels. Theoretical analysis reveals the optimal smoothing parameter's dependence on confidence and its impact on training dynamics, while experiments on alignment benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of safety alignment, as it focuses on principled hyperparameter tuning rather than testing resilience to adversarial manipulation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了基于RLHF的LLM对齐中标签平滑参数通常启发式选择、缺乏理论理解的问题。它提出了置信度感知标签平滑（CALS），一种根据模型预测置信度动态调整平滑参数的方法。理论分析揭示了最优平滑参数与置信度的关系及其对训练动态的影响，实验在多个对齐基准上获得了有竞争力的表现。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性，而是聚焦于原则化的超参数优化以增强对齐效果。

papers.title: Governance in Motion: Co-evolution of Constitutions and AI models for Scalable Safety
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is a central challenge for building reliable AI systems. Most existing alignment approaches rely on static signals, such as predefined principles or offline human annotations to guide model behavior toward a fixed approximation of human preferences. However, LLMs can exhibit distributional drift during training, and static alignment mechanisms lack the capacity to adaptively correct misaligned behaviors as they emerge. To address this limitation, we develop a two-stage framework that enables dynamic and continuous alignment. In the first stage, a constitution is continually revised based on observed model behaviors, and models are trained to comply with these evolving principles. In the second stage, this learned constitution is used to guide reinforcement learning, encouraging the model to align with the updated normative signals. We refer to this framework as COCOA: Co-evolution of Constitutions and AI Models. We show that COCOA enables a 7B model to greatly improve safety—raising StrongReject score from 0.741 to 0.935 and Safe-RLHF accuracy from 77.76% to 90.64% without human annotations, reaching performance close to much larger state-of-the-art models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the fragility of static alignment signals in LLMs, which cannot adapt to distributional drift during training. It proposes COCOA, a two-stage framework that continually revises a constitution based on model behaviors and then uses it to guide reinforcement learning for dynamic alignment. Evaluated on a 7B model, COCOA raised StrongReject safety score from 0.741 to 0.935 and Safe-RLHF accuracy from 77.76% to 90.64% without human annotations, approaching larger models. By enabling continuous, adaptive alignment, this work provides a hardening method that directly mitigates the robustness concerns of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐中静态信号无法适应训练分布漂移的脆弱性问题。提出COCOA框架，通过两阶段持续修订宪法并指导强化学习，实现动态对齐。在7B模型上的实验表明，COCOA将StrongReject评分从0.741提升至0.935，Safe-RLHF准确率从77.76%提升至90.64%，无需人类标注，接近更大规模模型。该方法通过动态对齐机制强化了安全对齐的鲁棒性，直接回应了安全对齐脆弱性的核心挑战。

papers.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
papers.abstract: While recent preference alignment algorithms for language models have demonstrated promising results, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains imperative for achieving successful convergence. In this paper, we revisit SFT in the context of preference alignment, emphasizing that a minor penalty for the disfavored style is sufficient for preference alignment. Building on this foundation, we introduce a straightforward reference model-free monolithic odds ratio preference optimization algorithm, ORPO, eliminating the need for an additional preference alignment phase. We demonstrate, both empirically and theoretically, that the odds ratio is a sensible choice for contrasting favored and disfavored styles during SFT across diverse sizes from 125M to 7B. Specifically, fine-tuning Phi-2 (2.7B), Llama-2 (7B), and Mistral (7B) with ORPO on the UltraFeedback alone surpasses the performance of state-of-the-art language models including Llama-2 Chat and Zephyr with more than 7B and 13B parameters: achieving up to 12.20% on AlpacaEval 2.0 (Figure 1), and 7.32 in MT-Bench (Table 2). We release code and model checkpoints for Mistral-ORPO-\alpha (7B) and Mistral-ORPO-\beta (7B).
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency of two-stage language model alignment (SFT then separate preference optimization) by proposing a combined approach. It introduces ORPO, a monolithic algorithm that incorporates an odds-ratio-based penalty for disfavored generations directly into supervised fine-tuning, eliminating the need for a reference model. Evaluating on UltraFeedback with Phi-2, Llama-2, and Mistral, ORPO achieves state-of-the-art results on AlpacaEval 2.0 (up to 12.20%) and MT-Bench (7.32), outperforming larger chat models. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对语言模型对齐的两阶段方法（监督微调后接独立的偏好优化）效率低下的问题，提出了一种联合方案。它引入了ORPO算法，在监督微调中直接融入基于几率比的惩罚项以抑制不偏好风格，从而省去参考模型。在UltraFeedback上微调Phi-2、Llama-2和Mistral后，ORPO在AlpacaEval 2.0（最高12.20%）和MT-Bench（7.32）上超越了更大的聊天模型，达到了领先水平。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning-based unlearning methods prevail for erasing targeted harmful, sensitive, or copyrighted information within large language models while preserving overall capabilities. However, the true effectiveness of the methods is unclear. In this paper, we delve into the limitations of fine-tuning-based unlearning through activation patching and parameter restoration experiments. Our findings reveal that these methods alter the model’s knowledge retrieval process, rather than genuinely erasing the problematic knowledge embedded in the model parameters. Furthermore, behavioral tests demonstrate that the unlearning mechanisms inevitably impact the global behavior of the models, affecting unrelated knowledge or capabilities. Our work advocates the development of more resilient unlearning techniques for truly erasing knowledge.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether fine-tuning-based unlearning methods truly erase targeted harmful knowledge from large language models. Using activation patching and parameter restoration, the authors dissect the unlearning mechanisms, revealing that these methods merely alter the knowledge retrieval process rather than removing the knowledge from model parameters. Behavioral tests further show that unlearning inevitably impacts global model behavior, affecting unrelated capabilities. The findings expose the fragility of current alignment techniques, as suppressed knowledge can be recovered, undermining the robustness of post-training safety interventions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究基于微调的遗忘方法是否能真正从大语言模型中擦除目标知识。通过激活修补和参数恢复实验，作者剖析了遗忘机制，发现这些方法仅改变知识检索过程，并未根除模型参数中的知识。行为测试进一步表明，遗忘操作不可避免地影响模型全局行为，损害不相关的能力。该工作揭示了现有对齐技术的内在脆弱性，被抑制的知识仍可恢复，动摇了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Nullspace Disentanglement for Red Teaming Language Models
papers.abstract: With the widespread deployment of generative language models, concerns about safety issues have continuously grown. High-quality fine-tuning data generated from red teaming plays a crucial role in the model’s safety. Recently, automated red teaming approaches have been proposed to create test cases. However, these approaches, which rely on open-ended generation, encounter issues related to inefficiency and low attack success rates. In this work, we introduce a black-box approach that ingeniously exploits the unique properties of the nullspace to disentangle and regulate the crucial success information within test cases. Our study provides a brand-new perspective for automated red team research. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms baseline methods regarding the attack success rate. The generated test cases also excel in aspects of diversity and fluency.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency and low attack success rates in open-ended generation-based automated red teaming. It proposes a black-box method that leverages nullspace properties to disentangle and regulate success-critical information in test cases, offering a new perspective for red teaming. Experiments show superior attack success rates, diversity, and fluency over baselines. While it enhances red teaming methodology, it does not directly investigate the fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了基于开放式生成的自动化红队方法中效率低、攻击成功率低的问题。它提出了一种黑盒方法，利用零空间特性解耦和调控测试用例中的关键成功信息，为自动化红队研究提供新视角。实验表明，其在攻击成功率、多样性和流畅性上均优于基线。该工作改进了红队方法，但未直接探究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Safety Arithmetic: A Framework for Test-time Safety Alignment of Language Models by Steering Parameters and Activations
papers.abstract: Ensuring the safe alignment of large language models (LLMs) with human values is critical as they become integral to applications like translation and question answering. Current alignment methods struggle with dynamic user intentions and complex objectives, making models vulnerable to generating harmful content. We propose Safety Arithmetic, a training-free framework enhancing LLM safety across different scenarios: Base models, Supervised fine-tuned models (SFT), and Edited models. Safety Arithmetic involves Harm Direction Removal to avoid harmful content and Safety Alignment to promote safe responses. Additionally, we present NoIntentEdit, a dataset highlighting edit instances that could compromise model safety if used unintentionally. Our experiments show that Safety Arithmetic significantly improves safety measures, reduces over-safety, and maintains model utility, outperforming existing methods in ensuring safe content generation.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of dynamic user intentions and complex objectives that make LLMs vulnerable to generating harmful content. It proposes Safety Arithmetic, a training-free test-time framework that steers parameters and activations via Harm Direction Removal and Safety Alignment, and introduces NoIntentEdit, a dataset of edits that unintentionally compromise safety. Experiments show improved safety, reduced over-safety, and maintained utility, outperforming existing methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对动态用户意图和复杂目标导致大语言模型易生成有害内容的问题，提出了一种无需训练的测试时安全对齐框架 Safety Arithmetic，通过移除有害方向和促进安全回复来调控参数与激活，并构建了 NoIntentEdit 数据集以揭示可能无意中损害模型安全的编辑实例。实验表明，该方法显著提升安全性，减少过度安全，且保持模型效用，优于现有方法。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Towards a Unified Paradigm of Concept Editing in Large Language Models
papers.short_title: Unified Paradigm for Concept Editing in LLMs
papers.abstract: Concept editing aims to control specific concepts in large language models (LLMs) and is an emerging subfield of model editing. Despite the emergence of various editing methods in recent years, there remains a lack of rigorous theoretical analysis and a unified perspective to systematically understand and compare these methods. To address this gap, we propose a unified paradigm for concept editing methods, in which all forms of conceptual injection are aligned at the neuron level. We study four representative concept editing methods: Neuron Editing (NE), Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT), Sparse Autoencoder (SAE), and Steering Vector (SV). Then we categorize them into two classes based on their mode of conceptual information injection: indirect (NE, SFT) and direct (SAE, SV). We evaluate above methods along four dimensions: editing reliability, output generalization, neuron level consistency, and mathematical formalization. Experiments show that SAE achieves the best editing reliability. In output generalization, SAE captures features closer to human-understood concepts, while NE tends to locate text patterns rather than true semantics. Neuron-level analysis reveals that direct methods share high neuron overlap, as do indirect methods, indicating methodological commonality within each category. Our unified paradigm offers a clear framework and valuable insights for advancing interpretability and controlled generation in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of systematic understanding and comparison among concept editing methods in large language models. It proposes a unified paradigm that aligns conceptual injection at the neuron level and categorizes methods into indirect (Neuron Editing, Supervised Fine-tuning) and direct (Sparse Autoencoder, Steering Vector) approaches. Evaluations on four dimensions show that Sparse Autoencoder achieves the best editing reliability and captures human-understandable concepts, while direct methods share high neuron overlap indicating methodological commonality. This paper advances interpretability and controlled generation methods but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大型语言模型中概念编辑方法缺乏系统性理解和统一比较的问题。它提出了一个统一范式，在神经元层面统一概念注入，并将方法分为间接（神经元编辑、监督微调）和直接（稀疏自编码器、操控向量）两类。在四个维度上的评估表明，稀疏自编码器编辑可靠性最佳且能捕获更接近人类理解的概念，而直接方法间神经元重叠度高，显示出方法论上的共性。该工作推进了可解释性和可控生成方法，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Path Drift in Large Reasoning Models: How First-Person Commitments Override Safety
papers.short_title: Path Drift: Safety Override in Reasoning LLMs
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for complex reasoning tasks, Long Chain-of-Thought (Long-CoT) prompting has emerged as a key paradigm for structured inference. Despite early-stage safeguards enabled by alignment techniques such as RLHF, we identify a previously underexplored vulnerability: reasoning trajectories in Long-CoT models can drift from aligned paths, resulting in content that violates safety constraints. We term this phenomenon Path Drift. Through empirical analysis, we uncover three behavioral triggers of Path Drift: (1) first-person commitments that induce goal-driven reasoning that delays refusal signals; (2) ethical evaporation, where surface-level disclaimers bypass alignment checkpoints; (3) condition chain escalation, where layered cues progressively steer models toward unsafe completions. Building on these insights, we introduce a three-stage Path Drift Induction Framework comprising cognitive load amplification, self-role priming, and condition chain hijacking. Each stage independently reduces refusal rates, while their combination further compounds the effect. To mitigate these risks, we propose a path-level defense strategy incorporating role attribution correction and metacognitive reflection (reflective safety cues). Our findings highlight the need for trajectory-level alignment oversight in long-form reasoning beyond token-level alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies 'Path Drift', a vulnerability in Long-CoT reasoning models where aligned reasoning trajectories deviate, leading to safety violations. It proposes a three-stage induction framework (cognitive load amplification, self-role priming, condition chain hijacking) to trigger drift, and a path-level defense with role attribution correction and metacognitive reflection. Empirical analysis reveals three behavioral triggers, and the induction framework reduces refusal rates, especially when combined. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile: it can be bypassed through reasoning trajectory manipulation, highlighting the need for trajectory-level oversight beyond token-level alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别了长链思维推理模型中的“路径漂移”漏洞，即对齐的推理轨迹发生偏离，导致安全违规。提出了一个三阶段诱导框架（认知负载放大、自我角色启动、条件链劫持）来触发漂移，以及一种包含角色归因校正和元认知反思的路径级防御策略。实证分析揭示了三种行为触发因素，诱导框架降低了拒绝率，尤其组合使用时效果更强。该工作表明训练后安全对齐是脆弱的：可通过操纵推理轨迹绕过，强调了在词元级对齐之外需要轨迹级监管。

papers.title: Learning Preference Model for LLMs via Automatic Preference Data Generation
papers.abstract: Despite the advanced capacities of the state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), they suffer from issues of hallucination, stereotype, etc. Preference models play an important role in LLM alignment, yet training preference models predominantly rely on human-annotated data. This reliance limits their versatility and scalability. In this paper, we propose learning the preference model for LLMs via automatic preference data generation (AutoPM). Our approach involves both In-Breadth Data Generation, which elicits pairwise preference data from LLMs following the helpful-honest-harmless (HHH) criteria, and In-Depth Data Generation, which enriches the dataset with responses spanning a wide quality range. With HHH-guided preference data, our approach simultaneously enables the LLMs to learn human preferences and align with human values. Quantitative assessments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate the reliability and potential of AutoPM, pointing out a more general and scalable way to improve LLM performance.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the dependency of preference model training on human-annotated data, which limits LLM alignment scalability. It proposes AutoPM, an automatic preference data generation method that combines in-breadth generation using HHH-guided pairwise data from LLMs and in-depth generation enriching responses across quality levels. Evaluation on five benchmarks shows AutoPM's reliability and potential for scalable LLM improvement. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了LLM对齐中的偏好模型训练依赖于人工标注数据的问题，限制了可扩展性。它提出AutoPM方法，结合广度数据生成（基于HHH标准从LLM中引出成对偏好数据）和深度数据生成（使用不同质量的响应丰富数据集）。在五个基准数据集上的评估证明了AutoPM的可靠性和改进LLM性能的潜力。该论文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: EMNLP: Educator-role Moral and Normative Large Language Models Profiling
papers.abstract: Simulating Professions (SP) enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to emulate professional roles. However, comprehensive psychological and ethical evaluation in these contexts remains lacking. This paper introduces EMNLP, an Educator-role Moral and Normative LLMs Profiling framework for personality profiling, moral development stage measurement, and ethical risk under soft prompt injection. EMNLP extends existing scales and constructs 88 teacher-specific moral dilemmas, enabling profession-oriented comparison with human teachers. A targeted soft prompt injection set evaluates compliance and vulnerability in teacher SP. Experiments on 14 LLMs show teacher-role LLMs exhibit more idealized and polarized personalities than human teachers, excel in abstract moral reasoning, but struggle with emotionally complex situations. Models with stronger reasoning are more vulnerable to harmful prompt injection, revealing a paradox between capability and safety. The model temperature and other hyperparameters have limited influence except in some risk behaviors. This paper presents the first benchmark to assess ethical and psychological alignment of teacher-role LLMs for educational AI. Resources are available at https://e-m-n-l-p.github.io/.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of comprehensive psychological and ethical evaluation for LLMs simulating teacher roles. It introduces EMNLP, a profiling framework that extends scales, creates teacher-specific moral dilemmas, and uses soft prompt injection to assess personality, moral reasoning, and ethical risks. Experiments on 14 LLMs show teacher-role LLMs exhibit idealized personalities, strong abstract moral reasoning but struggle emotionally, and models with stronger reasoning are more vulnerable to harmful prompt injection. This directly relates to safety alignment fragility, revealing that higher capability can introduce new attack surfaces, undermining robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型模拟教师角色时心理与伦理评估不全面的问题，提出了EMNLP框架，通过扩展量表、构建教师专属道德困境和软提示注入，系统评估人格、道德推理和伦理风险。在14个模型上的实验表明，教师角色LLM性格更理想化、抽象道德推理强但情感处理弱，且推理能力越强的模型越易受有害提示注入攻击。这一发现直接关联安全对齐的脆弱性，表明更高能力可能带来新的攻击面，破坏鲁棒性。

papers.title: Toxicity Red-Teaming: Benchmarking LLM Safety in Singapore's Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: The advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed natural language processing; however, their safety mechanisms remain under-explored in low-resource, multilingual settings. Here, we aim to bridge this gap. In particular, we introduce SGToxicGuard, a novel dataset and evaluation framework for benchmarking LLM safety in Singapore’s diverse linguistic context, including Singlish, Chinese, Malay, and Tamil. SGToxicGuard adopts a red-teaming approach to systematically probe LLM vulnerabilities in three real-world scenarios: conversation, question-answering, and content composition. We conduct extensive experiments with state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs, and the results uncover critical gaps in their safety guardrails. By offering actionable insights into cultural sensitivity and toxicity mitigation, we lay the foundation for safer and more inclusive AI systems in linguistically diverse environments. Disclaimer: This paper contains sensitive content that may be disturbing to some readers.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the underexplored robustness of LLM safety mechanisms in low-resource multilingual settings, specifically Singapore's Singlish, Chinese, Malay, and Tamil. It introduces SGToxicGuard, a red-teaming dataset and evaluation framework that systematically probes LLM vulnerabilities across conversation, question-answering, and content composition. Experiments with state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs reveal critical safety gaps, showing that existing guardrails are ineffective in these languages. By demonstrating that safety alignment fails under linguistic distribution shifts, the paper provides clear evidence of its fragility as a module that can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本工作探讨了低资源多语言场景下大语言模型安全机制鲁棒性不足的问题，特别聚焦于新加坡的Singlish、中文、马来语和泰米尔语。提出了SGToxicGuard，一个红队测试数据集与评估框架，系统探测对话、问答和内容创作场景中的模型漏洞。在主流多语言大模型上的实验揭示了关键安全盲区，表明现有安全防护在这些语言中失效。通过展示安全对齐在语言分布偏移下的脆弱性，本文为‘后训练安全对齐是否真正鲁棒’提供了清晰的反面证据。

papers.title: Evaluating Robustness of Large Audio Language Models to Audio Injection: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, yet their robustness against malicious audio injection attacks remains underexplored. This study systematically evaluates five leading LALMs across four attack scenarios: Audio Interference Attack, Instruction Following Attack, Context Injection Attack, and Judgment Hijacking Attack. Using metrics like Defense Success Rate, Context Robustness Score, and Judgment Robustness Index, their vulnerabilities and resilience were quantitatively assessed. Experimental results reveal significant performance disparities among models; no single model consistently outperforms others across all attack types. The position of malicious content critically influences attack effectiveness, particularly when placed at the beginning of sequences. A negative correlation between instruction-following capability and robustness suggests models adhering strictly to instructions may be more susceptible, contrasting with greater resistance by safety-aligned models. Additionally, system prompts show mixed effectiveness, indicating the need for tailored strategies. This work introduces a benchmark framework and highlights the importance of integrating robustness into training pipelines. Findings emphasize developing multi-modal defenses and architectural designs that decouple capability from susceptibility for secure LALMs deployment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the underexplored vulnerability of Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) to malicious audio injection attacks. It proposes a benchmark framework to systematically evaluate five leading LALMs under four attack types—Audio Interference, Instruction Following, Context Injection, and Judgment Hijacking—using metrics like Defense Success Rate and Context Robustness Score. Experimental results show significant performance disparities, with attack effectiveness heavily influenced by malicious content position (especially at the beginning), and a negative correlation between instruction-following capability and robustness, while safety-aligned models exhibit greater resistance. This study directly contributes to the fragility question by demonstrating that even safety-aligned models can be susceptible to audio injection attacks, highlighting the conditional resilience of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型音频语言模型（LALMs）在恶意音频注入攻击下稳健性不足的问题，提出了一种基准框架，系统评估了五种主流LALMs在音频干扰、指令跟随、上下文注入和判断劫持四种攻击下的表现，采用防御成功率、上下文稳健性评分等指标。实验揭示模型间稳健性差异显著；攻击效果受恶意内容位置影响，尤其置于序列开头时更为有效；指令跟随能力与稳健性呈负相关，而经过安全对齐的模型抵抗性更强；系统提示的防御效果不一。该研究通过展示音频注入攻击下安全对齐模型的脆弱性，直接回应了“后训练安全对齐是否真正稳健”的核心议题，表明尽管安全对齐能提供一定防护，但仍可能被位置敏感的精心设计攻击突破。

papers.title: Too Helpful, Too Harmless, Too Honest or Just Right?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong performance across a wide range of NLP tasks, yet aligning their outputs with the principles of Helpfulness, Harmlessness, and Honesty (HHH) remains a persistent challenge. Existing methods often optimize for individual alignment dimensions in isolation, leading to trade-offs and inconsistent behavior. While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures offer modularity, they suffer from poorly calibrated routing, limiting their effectiveness in alignment tasks.
