We propose TrinityX, a modular alignment framework that incorporates a Mixture of Calibrated Experts (MoCaE) within the Transformer architecture. TrinityX leverages separately trained experts for each HHH dimension, integrating their outputs through a calibrated, task-adaptive routing mechanism that combines expert signals into a unified, alignment-aware representation. Extensive experiments on three standard alignment benchmarks-Alpaca (Helpfulness), BeaverTails (Harmlessness), and TruthfulQA (Honesty)-demonstrate that TrinityX outperforms strong baselines, achieving relative improvements of 32.5% in win rate, 33.9% in safety score, and 28.4% in truthfulness. In addition, TrinityX reduces memory usage and inference latency by over 40% compared to prior MoE-based approaches. Ablation studies highlight the importance of calibrated routing, and cross-model evaluations confirm TrinityX's generalization across diverse LLM backbones.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of simultaneously optimizing LLM alignment across helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty (HHH), where single-dimension optimization often leads to trade-offs. It proposes TrinityX, a modular framework that incorporates a Mixture of Calibrated Experts (MoCaE) within the Transformer, using separately trained experts for each HHH dimension and a calibrated routing mechanism to combine outputs. Evaluated on Alpaca, BeaverTails, and TruthfulQA, TrinityX achieves relative improvements of 32.5% win rate, 33.9% safety score, and 28.4% truthfulness over baselines, while reducing memory and latency by over 40% compared to prior MoE approaches. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在帮助性、无害性和诚实性（HHH）上同时优化LLM对齐的挑战，单一维度优化常导致不一致行为。提出TrinityX框架，在Transformer中融合校准专家混合（MoCaE），为每个HHH维度独立训练专家，并通过校准的路由机制整合输出。在Alpaca、BeaverTails和TruthfulQA上评估，相对基线分别提升32.5%胜率、33.9%安全分数和28.4%诚实性，且比先前MoE方法降低40%以上的内存和延迟。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: REVIVING YOUR MNEME: Predicting The Side Effects of LLM Unlearning and Fine-Tuning via Sparse Model Diffing
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are frequently fine-tuned or unlearned to adapt to new tasks or eliminate undesirable behaviors. While existing evaluation methods assess performance after such interventions, there remains no general approach for detecting unintended side effects, such as unlearning biology content degrading performance on chemistry tasks, particularly when these effects are unpredictable or emergent. To address this issue, we introduce MNEME, Model diffiNg for Evaluating Mechanistic Effects, a lightweight framework for identifying these side effects using sparse model diffing. MNEME compares base and fine-tuned models on task-agnostic data (for example, The Pile, LMSYS-Chat-1M) without access to fine-tuning data to isolate behavioral shifts. Applied to five LLMs across three scenarios: WMDP knowledge unlearning, emergent misalignment, and benign fine-tuning, MNEME achieves up to 95 percent accuracy in predicting side effects, aligning with known benchmarks and requiring no custom heuristics. Furthermore, we show that retraining on high-activation samples can partially reverse these effects. Our results demonstrate that sparse probing and diffing offer a scalable and automated lens into fine-tuning-induced model changes, providing practical tools for understanding and managing LLM behavior.
papers.summary_en: This work addresses the detection of unintended side effects when fine-tuning or unlearning LLMs, such as performance degradation on unrelated tasks. It proposes MNEME, a lightweight framework that uses sparse model diffing on task-agnostic data to compare base and modified models and isolate behavioral shifts. Evaluated on five LLMs across three scenarios (knowledge unlearning, emergent misalignment, benign fine-tuning), MNEME predicts side effects with up to 95% accuracy, aligning with known benchmarks without custom heuristics. By revealing how post-training modifications can inadvertently break alignment, this paper provides direct evidence for the fragility of safety alignment, showing that model capabilities are non-localized and easily disturbed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决LLM微调或知识遗忘时难以检测意外副作用（如无关任务性能下降）的问题。提出MNEME框架，利用任务无关数据上的稀疏模型差异比较来隔离行为变化。在五个模型、三种场景（知识遗忘、新兴对齐失效、良性微调）中，预测副作用准确率高达95%，与已知基准一致且无需自定义规则。该工作直接揭示了训练后修改可能意外破坏对齐，为安全对齐的脆弱性提供了实证，反映模型能力分布的非局部性。

papers.title: Retracing the Past: LLMs Emit Training Data When They Get Lost
papers.short_title: CIA: Extracting Training Data from LLMs
papers.abstract: The memorization of training data in large language models (LLMs) poses significant privacy and copyright concerns. Existing data extraction methods, particularly heuristic-based divergence attacks, often exhibit limited success and offer limited insight into the fundamental drivers of memorization leakage. This paper introduces Confusion-Inducing Attacks (CIA), a principled framework for extracting memorized data by systematically maximizing model uncertainty. We empirically demonstrate that the emission of memorized text during divergence is preceded by a sustained spike in token-level prediction entropy. CIA leverages this insight by optimizing input snippets to deliberately induce this consecutive high-entropy state. For aligned LLMs, we further propose Mismatched Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT) to simultaneously weaken their alignment and induce targeted confusion, thereby increasing susceptibility to our attacks. Experiments on various unaligned and aligned LLMs demonstrate that our proposed attacks outperform existing baselines in extracting verbatim and near-verbatim training data without requiring prior knowledge of the training data. Our findings highlight persistent memorization risks across various LLMs and offer a more systematic method for assessing these vulnerabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to memorization leaks, which pose privacy and copyright risks. It introduces Confusion-Inducing Attacks (CIA), a principled framework that optimizes input snippets to maximize model uncertainty, leveraging the observation that spikes in token-level entropy precede the emission of memorized text. For aligned models, a Mismatched Supervised Fine-tuning step is proposed to weaken alignment and increase susceptibility. Experiments show CIA outperforms existing methods in extracting verbatim training data without prior knowledge, highlighting persistent memorization risks and demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be deliberately weakened, supporting the view that it is a fragile safeguard.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型因记忆训练数据而导致的隐私与版权泄露风险。提出了混淆诱导攻击（CIA），通过优化输入片段来最大化模型不确定性，利用观察到的高熵状态会触发记忆文本泄露的现象。针对对齐模型，进一步引入错配监督微调来削弱对齐并加剧混淆，从而提升攻击效果。实验表明CIA在无先验知识下提取原样数据方面优于现有方法，揭示了持续的记忆风险，并证明安全对齐可被有意绕过，佐证了其脆弱性。

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models through Synthetic Feedback
papers.short_title: ALMoST: Aligning LLMs via Synthetic Feedback
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) to human values has become increasingly important as it enables sophisticated steering of LLMs. However, it requires significant human demonstrations and feedback or distillation from proprietary LLMs such as ChatGPT. In this work, we propose a novel alignment learning framework with synthetic feedback not dependent on extensive human annotations and proprietary LLMs. First, we perform reward modeling (RM) with synthetic feedback by contrasting responses from vanilla LLMs with various sizes and prompts. Then, we use the RM to simulate high-quality demonstrations to train a supervised policy and further optimize the model with reinforcement learning. Our resulting model, Aligned Language Model with Synthetic Training dataset (ALMoST), outperforms recent open-sourced models, which are trained on the outputs of InstructGPT or human-annotated demonstrations, in alignment benchmarks. In human evaluation, our model is preferred to Alpaca and Dolly-v2, 55.0% and 58.5% of the time, respectively. Further analyses demonstrate the efficacy and importance of synthetic feedback in our framework. The code is available at https://github.com/naver-ai/almost
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models (LLMs) to human values without expensive human demonstrations or dependence on proprietary models like ChatGPT. It proposes ALMoST, a framework that uses synthetic feedback: reward models are trained by contrasting responses from vanilla LLMs of various sizes and prompts, then used to generate simulated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Evaluated on alignment benchmarks, ALMoST outperforms recent open-sourced models trained on InstructGPT outputs or human annotations, and is preferred over Alpaca and Dolly-v2 in human evaluations 55.0% and 58.5% of the time, respectively. This paper advances alignment methodology by reducing reliance on costly human or proprietary data but does not directly address whether the resulting alignment is fragile or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了将大型语言模型（LLM）与人类价值对齐时依赖昂贵人类反馈或专有模型（如ChatGPT）的问题。提出了ALMoST框架，通过对比不同规模和提示的原生LLM的响应进行合成反馈奖励建模，进而利用奖励模型模拟高质量示范以进行监督微调与强化学习优化。在多个对齐基准测试中，ALMoST优于使用InstructGPT输出或人类标注数据训练的开源模型，且人类评估显示相较于Alpaca和Dolly-v2，分别有55.0%和58.5%的偏好率。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨所获对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Harmful Prompt Laundering: Jailbreaking LLMs with Abductive Styles and Symbolic Encoding
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across diverse tasks, but their potential misuse for harmful purposes remains a significant concern. To strengthen defenses against such vulnerabilities, it is essential to investigate universal jailbreak attacks that exploit intrinsic weaknesses in the architecture and learning paradigms of LLMs. In response, we propose \textbf{H}armful \textbf{P}rompt \textbf{La}undering (HaPLa), a novel and broadly applicable jailbreaking technique that requires only black-box access to target models. HaPLa incorporates two primary strategies: 1) \textit{abductive framing}, which instructs LLMs to infer plausible intermediate steps toward harmful activities, rather than directly responding to explicit harmful queries; and 2) \textit{symbolic encoding}, a lightweight and flexible approach designed to obfuscate harmful content, given that current LLMs remain sensitive primarily to explicit harmful keywords. Experimental results show that HaPLa achieves over 95% attack success rate on GPT-series models and 70% across all targets. Further analysis with diverse symbolic encoding rules also reveals a fundamental challenge: it remains difficult to safely tune LLMs without significantly diminishing their helpfulness in responding to benign queries.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces Harmful Prompt Laundering (HaPLa), a jailbreaking attack that bypasses safety alignment in LLMs using only black-box access. HaPLa combines abductive framing to infer intermediate steps toward harmful goals with symbolic encoding to obfuscate malicious content. Experiments achieve over 95% attack success rate on GPT-series models and 70% on average across diverse targets. The study highlights a trade-off between safety and helpfulness, suggesting that current alignment is fragile and can be subverted without degrading model utility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出有害提示洗白（HaPLa），一种仅需黑盒访问即可绕过LLM安全对齐的越狱攻击方法。HaPLa结合溯因推理（引导模型推断有害目标的中间步骤）与符号编码（混淆恶意内容）来规避检测。实验在GPT系列模型上取得了超过95%的攻击成功率，跨目标平均达到70%。进一步分析揭示了安全性与有用性之间的权衡，表明当前对齐方法脆弱，可能被绕过且不影响模型效用。

papers.title: SABER: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in Safety Alignment via Cross-Layer Residual Connection
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) with safe-alignment training are powerful instruments with robust language comprehension capabilities. These models typically undergo meticulous alignment procedures involving human feedback to ensure the acceptance of safe inputs while rejecting harmful or unsafe ones. However, despite their massive scale and alignment efforts, LLMs remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where malicious users manipulate the model to produce harmful outputs that it was explicitly trained to avoid. In this study, we find that the safety mechanisms in LLMs are predominantly embedded in the middle-to-late layers. Building on this insight, we introduce a novel white-box jailbreak method, SABER (Safety Alignment Bypass via Extra Residuals), which connects two intermediate layers $s$ and $e$ such that $s<e$, through a residual connection. Our approach achieves a 51% improvement over the best-performing baseline on the HarmBench test set. Furthermore, SABER induces only a marginal shift in perplexity when evaluated on the HarmBench validation set. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/PalGitts/SABER.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreak attacks against safety-aligned LLMs. It proposes SABER, a white-box method that connects two intermediate layers via a residual connection to bypass safety mechanisms concentrated in middle-to-late layers. On HarmBench, SABER achieves a 51% improvement over the best baseline with negligible perplexity increase. The work exposes a new architectural vulnerability, providing concrete evidence that safety alignment can be easily bypassed, supporting the view that post-training alignment is fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐大语言模型的越狱攻击问题。提出白盒方法SABER，通过在两个中间层之间建立残差连接，绕过集中于中后层的安全机制。在HarmBench数据集上，攻击成功率较最佳基线提升51%，且困惑度变化极小。该研究揭示了一种架构层面的新攻击面，直接证明安全对齐可通过残差连接轻易绕过，印证了对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Rethinking the Role of Proxy Rewards in Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: Reverse Reward Engineering for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Learning from human feedback via proxy reward modeling has been studied to align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human values. However, achieving reliable training through that proxy reward model (RM) is not a trivial problem, and its behavior remained as a black-box. In this paper, we study the role of proxy rewards in the LLM alignment via ‘reverse reward engineering’ by composing interpretable features as a white-box reward function. We aim to replicate the ground truth (gold) reward signal by achieving a monotonic relationship between the proxy and gold reward signals after training the model using the proxy reward in reinforcement learning (RL). Our findings indicate that successfully emulating the gold reward requires generating responses that are relevant with enough length to open-ended questions, while also ensuring response consistency in closed-ended questions. Furthermore, resulting models optimizing our devised white-box reward show competitive performances with strong open-source RMs in alignment benchmarks. We highlight its potential usage as a simple but strong reward baseline for the LLM alignment, not requiring explicit human feedback dataset and RM training.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the black-box nature of proxy reward models in LLM alignment, which obscures training dynamics. It proposes 'reverse reward engineering,' constructing a white-box reward function from interpretable features (e.g., response length, relevance, consistency) to emulate the gold reward signal. In RL experiments, the model optimized with this white-box proxy achieves competitive alignment benchmark performance against strong open-source reward models, without human feedback data or RM training. This paper advances alignment methodology with a transparent reward baseline but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了语言模型对齐中代理奖励模型作为黑箱、难以理解训练动态的问题。提出“逆向奖励工程”方法，通过可解释特征（如响应长度、相关性、一致性）构建白盒奖励函数来模拟真实奖励信号。在强化学习实验中，使用该白盒代理奖励优化的模型在对齐基准上取得了与强开源奖励模型相当的性能，且无需人类反馈数据集或显式奖励模型训练。本文推进了对齐方法学，提供了透明奖励基线，但未直接探讨对齐后训练安全性是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: GDPO: Learning to Directly Align Language Models with Diversity Using GFlowNets
papers.abstract: A critical component of the current generation of language models is preference alignment, which aims to precisely control the model’s behavior to meet human needs and values. The most notable among such methods is Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) and its offline variant Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), both of which seek to maximize a reward model based on human preferences. In particular, DPO derives reward signals directly from the offline preference data, but in doing so overfits the reward signals and generates suboptimal responses that may contain human biases in the dataset. In this work, we propose a practical application of a diversity-seeking RL algorithm called GFlowNet-DPO (GDPO) in an offline preference alignment setting to curtail such challenges. Empirical results show GDPO can generate far more diverse responses than the baseline methods that are still relatively aligned with human values in dialog generation and summarization tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the overfitting and bias problems in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) by seeking more diverse responses during alignment. It proposes GDPO, a practical application of GFlowNets in offline preference alignment that encourages diversity while remaining aligned with human values. Evaluated on dialog generation and summarization tasks, GDPO significantly increases response diversity compared to baseline methods. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接偏好优化（DPO）中的过拟合和偏差问题，通过在偏好对齐过程中追求响应多样性来解决这些挑战。提出GDPO方法，将GFlowNets实际应用于离线偏好对齐，在保持与人类价值对齐的同时鼓励多样性。在对话生成和摘要任务上的评估表明，GDPO相比基线方法能产生显著更多样化的响应。本文改进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱的问题。

papers.title: Interpretation Meets Safety: A Survey on Interpretation Methods and Tools for Improving LLM Safety
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) see wider real-world use, understanding and mitigating their unsafe behaviors is critical. Interpretation techniques can reveal causes of unsafe outputs and guide safety, but such connections with safety are often overlooked in prior surveys. We present the first survey that bridges this gap, introducing a unified framework that connects safety-focused interpretation methods, the safety enhancements they inform, and the tools that operationalize them. Our novel taxonomy, organized by LLM workflow stages, summarizes nearly 70 works at their intersections. We conclude with open challenges and future directions. This timely survey helps researchers and practitioners navigate key advancements for safer, more interpretable LLMs.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the gap between interpretation techniques for understanding unsafe LLM behaviors and their application to safety improvements. The paper proposes a unified framework and novel taxonomy organized by LLM workflow stages, summarizing nearly 70 works at the intersection of interpretation and safety. As a survey, it identifies open challenges and future directions rather than providing experimental results. This paper advances alignment methodology by integrating interpretation techniques, but as a survey, it does not directly test the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对解释技术理解大语言模型不安全行为与其安全改进应用之间的脱节问题。提出了一个统一框架和新颖的分类法，按LLM工作流阶段组织，总结了近70篇相关研究。作为综述，它识别了开放挑战和未来方向，而非提供实验结果。该论文通过整合解释技术推进了对齐方法论，但作为综述，并未直接检验训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Phi: Preference Hijacking in Multi-modal Large Language Models at Inference Time
papers.abstract: Recently, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have gained significant attention across various domains. However, their widespread adoption has also raised serious safety concerns. In this paper, we uncover a new safety risk of MLLMs: the output preference of MLLMs can be arbitrarily manipulated by carefully optimized images. Such attacks often generate contextually relevant yet biased responses that are neither overtly harmful nor unethical, making them difficult to detect. Specifically, we introduce a novel method, Preference Hijacking (Phi), for manipulating the MLLM response preferences using a preference hijacked image. Our method works at inference time and requires no model modifications. Additionally, we introduce a universal hijacking perturbation -- a transferable component that can be embedded into different images to hijack MLLM responses toward any attacker-specified preferences. Experimental results across various tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. The code for Phi is accessible at https://github.com/Yifan-Lan/Phi.
papers.summary_en: The paper uncovers a new safety risk in multimodal LLMs: output preferences can be manipulated to produce biased yet non-overtly harmful responses. It proposes Preference Hijacking (Phi), a method that uses an optimized image to hijack response preferences at inference time without model modification, including a universal perturbation transferable across images. Experiments demonstrate the attack's effectiveness and stealthiness across various tasks. This work directly exposes the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that alignment can be easily bypassed with crafted inputs at inference time.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了一种多模态大语言模型的新安全风险：通过精心优化的图像可操纵模型的输出偏好，生成有偏向性但表面无害的回应。提出名为偏好劫持（Phi）的攻击方法，在推理阶段利用特殊构造的图像劫持模型偏好，无需修改模型，且可嵌入通用扰动到不同图像中，实现任意偏好操控。实验结果表明该方法在多个任务上有效，且攻击隐蔽性强。该研究直接展示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：攻击者仅需精心构造输入即可绕过对齐，说明对齐并非鲁棒，容易在推理时被攻破。

papers.title: APLOT: Robust Reward Modeling via Adaptive Preference Learning with Optimal Transport
papers.short_title: APLOT: Robust RM via Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The reward model (RM) plays a crucial role in aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences through Reinforcement Learning, where the Bradley-Terry (BT) objective has been recognized as simple yet powerful, specifically for pairwise preference learning. However, BT-based RMs often struggle to effectively distinguish between similar preference responses, leading to insufficient separation between preferred and non-preferred outputs. Consequently, they may easily overfit easy samples and cannot generalize well to Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) samples, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an effective enhancement to BT-based RMs through an adaptive margin mechanism. Specifically, we design to dynamically adjust the RM focus on more challenging samples through margins, based on both semantic similarity and model-predicted reward differences, which is approached from a distributional perspective solvable with Optimal Transport (OT). By incorporating these factors into a principled OT cost matrix design, our adaptive margin enables the RM to better capture distributional differences between chosen and rejected responses, yielding significant improvements in performance, convergence speed, and generalization capabilities. Experimental results across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms several existing RM techniques, showcasing enhanced performance in both In-Distribution (ID) and OOD settings. Moreover, RLHF experiments support our practical effectiveness in better aligning LLMs with human preferences.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation that Bradley-Terry based reward models (RMs) fail to sufficiently distinguish similar responses and generalize poorly to out-of-distribution samples. It proposes APLOT, an adaptive margin mechanism that uses Optimal Transport to dynamically weight challenging samples based on semantic similarity and predicted reward differences. Experiments show APLOT outperforms existing RM methods on multiple benchmarks, improving both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance, convergence speed, and RLHF alignment. This work hardens the RM against distribution shifts, advancing alignment robustness but without directly analyzing the fragility of post-training safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了基于Bradley-Terry的奖励模型难以有效区分相似响应、在分布外泛化差的问题。提出APLOT方法，利用最优传输设计自适应边际，根据语义相似度和模型预测奖励差异动态调整对困难样本的关注。多基准实验表明APLOT在分布内和分布外性能、收敛速度及RLHF对齐方面均优于现有方法。该工作通过强化奖励模型对分布偏移的鲁棒性来提升对齐稳定性，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性本质。

papers.title: The Past, Present and Better Future of Feedback Learning in Large Language Models for Subjective Human Preferences and Values
papers.short_title: Survey of Feedback Learning in LLMs
papers.abstract: Human feedback is increasingly used to steer the behaviours of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, it is unclear how to collect and incorporate feedback in a way that is efficient, effective and unbiased, especially for highly subjective human preferences and values. In this paper, we survey existing approaches for learning from human feedback, drawing on 95 papers primarily from the ACL and arXiv repositories.First, we summarise the past, pre-LLM trends for integrating human feedback into language models. Second, we give an overview of present techniques and practices, as well as the motivations for using feedback; conceptual frameworks for defining values and preferences; and how feedback is collected and from whom. Finally, we encourage a better future of feedback learning in LLMs by raising five unresolved conceptual and practical challenges.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently and unbiasedly collecting and incorporating human feedback to align LLMs with subjective human preferences and values. It surveys 95 papers to summarize past pre-LLM trends, present techniques, motivations, and feedback collection methods, and raises five unresolved challenges. The survey advances feedback learning methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对如何高效、无偏地收集和整合人类反馈以使LLM与主观人类偏好和价值观对齐这一挑战进行了研究。该工作基于95篇论文，总结了预LLM时代的趋势、现有技术和实践、动机及反馈收集方法，并提出了五个尚未解决的挑战。本文推动了反馈学习方法，但没有直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Are Vision-Language Models Safe in the Wild? A Meme-Based Benchmark Study
papers.abstract: Rapid deployment of vision-language models (VLMs) magnifies safety risks, yet most evaluations rely on artificial images. This study asks: How safe are current VLMs when confronted with meme images that ordinary users share? To investigate this question, we introduce MemeSafetyBench, a 50,430-instance benchmark pairing real meme images with both harmful and benign instructions. Using a comprehensive safety taxonomy and LLM-based instruction generation, we assess multiple VLMs across single and multi-turn interactions. We investigate how real-world memes influence harmful outputs, the mitigating effects of conversational context, and the relationship between model scale and safety metrics. Our findings demonstrate that VLMs are more vulnerable to meme-based harmful prompts than to synthetic or typographic images. Memes significantly increase harmful responses and decrease refusals compared to text-only inputs. Though multi-turn interactions provide partial mitigation, elevated vulnerability persists. These results highlight the need for ecologically valid evaluations and stronger safety mechanisms. MemeSafetyBench is publicly available at https://github.com/oneonlee/Meme-Safety-Bench.
papers.summary_en: This paper assesses vision-language model (VLM) safety in the wild by introducing MemeSafetyBench, a 50K-instance benchmark pairing real meme images with harmful and benign instructions. Using a comprehensive safety taxonomy and LLM-based instruction generation, the study evaluates multiple VLMs and finds that real-world memes significantly increase harmful outputs and decrease refusals compared to text-only or synthetic image inputs. Multi-turn interactions provide only partial mitigation. This work demonstrates a new attack surface where everyday meme images easily bypass VLM safety alignment, directly supporting the view that post-training safety alignment is fragile under ecologically valid, out-of-distribution conditions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文评估了视觉语言模型在真实世界中的安全性，提出了MemeSafetyBench基准，包含5万多个实例，将真实模因图像与有害和良性指令配对。利用全面安全分类法和基于LLM的指令生成，评估了多个VLM，发现与纯文本或合成图像相比，真实模因显著增加了有害输出并降低了拒绝率，多轮交互只能部分缓解。该工作展示了一种新的攻击面，日常模因图像轻易绕过了VLM的安全对齐，直接支持了后训练安全对齐在生态有效、分布外条件下是脆弱的这一观点。

papers.title: Self-Detoxifying Language Models via Toxification Reversal
papers.abstract: Language model detoxification aims to minimize the risk of generating offensive or harmful content in pretrained language models (PLMs) for safer deployment. Existing methods can be roughly categorized as finetuning-based and decoding-based. However, the former is often resource-intensive, while the latter relies on additional components and potentially compromises the generation fluency. In this paper, we propose a more lightweight approach that enables the PLM itself to achieve"self-detoxification". Our method is built upon the observation that prepending a negative steering prompt can effectively induce PLMs to generate toxic content. At the same time, we are inspired by the recent research in the interpretability field, which formulates the evolving contextualized representations within the PLM as an information stream facilitated by the attention layers. Drawing on this idea, we devise a method to identify the toxification direction from the normal generation process to the one prompted with the negative prefix, and then steer the generation to the reversed direction by manipulating the information movement within the attention layers. Experimental results show that our approach, without any fine-tuning or extra components, can achieve comparable performance with state-of-the-art methods.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of language model detoxification to prevent generation of offensive content. It proposes a lightweight self-detoxification method that identifies a 'toxification direction' induced by negative prompts and steers generation away from it by manipulating attention layer information flows. Experiments show that without any fine-tuning or extra components, this approach matches state-of-the-art detoxification performance. This paper advances alignment methodology by offering a decoding-time detoxification technique, but it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决语言模型去毒化问题，旨在减少生成攻击性内容。提出一种轻量级自我去毒化方法，通过识别负向提示诱发的“毒化方向”，并操控注意力层中的信息流以逆转该方向来引导生成。实验表明，无需微调或额外组件，该方法即可达到与最先进方法相当的性能。本文推进了对齐方法论，提供了解码时去毒化技术，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: ChatGPT Doesn't Trust Chargers Fans: Guardrail Sensitivity in Context
papers.abstract: While the biases of language models in production are extensively documented, the biases of their guardrails have been neglected. This paper studies how contextual information about the user influences the likelihood of an LLM to refuse to execute a request. By generating user biographies that offer ideological and demographic information, we find a number of biases in guardrail sensitivity on GPT-3.5. Younger, female, and Asian-American personas are more likely to trigger a refusal guardrail when requesting censored or illegal information. Guardrails are also sycophantic, refusing to comply with requests for a political position the user is likely to disagree with. We find that certain identity groups and seemingly innocuous information, e.g., sports fandom, can elicit changes in guardrail sensitivity similar to direct statements of political ideology. For each demographic category and even for American football team fandom, we find that ChatGPT appears to infer a likely political ideology and modify guardrail behavior accordingly.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates biases in LLM guardrails—refusal mechanisms—by examining how contextual user information influences the likelihood of refusal. It generates user biographies with demographic and ideological details and probes GPT-3.5’s guardrail sensitivity, finding that personas like younger, female, or Asian-American users, as well as sports fandom (e.g., Chargers fans), trigger more refusals for censored or illegal requests, and that guardrails exhibit sycophantic refusal for political positions. These results expose a fragility in post-training safety alignment: guardrails are not robust but vary based on inferred user ideology, showing that alignment can be inconsistently applied and bypassed through contextual cues.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大型语言模型护栏（拒绝机制）中的偏见，探讨用户上下文信息如何影响拒绝可能性。通过生成包含人口统计和意识形态细节的用户传记，探测GPT-3.5的护栏敏感性，发现年轻、女性、亚裔美国人等人物角色，以及体育迷身份（如闪电队球迷），更容易触发对受审查或非法请求的拒绝，且护栏表现出对用户政治立场选择的迎合性拒绝。这些结果揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：护栏并非稳健，而是根据推断的用户意识形态而变化，表明对齐可通过上下文线索被不一致地应用和绕过。

papers.title: RED: Unleashing Token-Level Rewards from Holistic Feedback via Reward Redistribution
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) offers a promising approach to aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. Typically, a reward model is trained or supplied to act as a proxy for humans in evaluating generated responses during the reinforcement training phase. However, current reward models operate as sequence-to-one models, allocating a single, sparse, and delayed reward to an entire output sequence. This approach may overlook the significant contributions of individual tokens toward the desired outcome. To this end, we propose a more fine-grained, token-level guidance approach for RL training. Specifically, we introduce RED, a novel reward redistribition method that evaluates and assigns specific credit to each token using an off-the-shelf reward model. Utilizing these fine-grained rewards enhances the model's understanding of language nuances, leading to more precise performance improvements. Notably, our method does not require modifying the reward model or introducing additional training steps, thereby incurring minimal computational costs. Experimental results across diverse datasets and tasks demonstrate the superiority of our approach.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of sparse, sequence-level rewards in RLHF, which overlook individual token contributions. It proposes RED, a method that redistributes holistic sequence rewards into fine-grained token-level credits using an off-the-shelf reward model, without additional training. Experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate that token-level rewards improve model understanding of language nuances, leading to better alignment performance. While this work advances alignment methodology, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中奖励模型提供稀疏的序列级反馈、忽略单个令牌贡献的问题。提出了RED方法，利用现成的奖励模型将整体序列奖励重新分配为细粒度的令牌级信用，无需额外训练。在多个数据集上的实验表明，令牌级奖励增强了模型对语言细微差别的理解，从而提高了对齐性能。虽然这项工作推进了对齐方法，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Transferable Direct Prompt Injection via Activation-Guided MCMC Sampling
papers.abstract: Direct Prompt Injection (DPI) attacks pose a critical security threat to Large Language Models (LLMs) due to their low barrier of execution and high potential damage. To address the impracticality of existing white-box/gray-box methods and the poor transferability of black-box methods, we propose an activations-guided prompt injection attack framework. We first construct an Energy-based Model (EBM) using activations from a surrogate model to evaluate the quality of adversarial prompts. Guided by the trained EBM, we employ the token-level Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling to adaptively optimize adversarial prompts, thereby enabling gradient-free black-box attacks. Experimental results demonstrate our superior cross-model transferability, achieving 49.6% attack success rate (ASR) across five mainstream LLMs and 34.6% improvement over human-crafted prompts, and maintaining 36.6% ASR on unseen task scenarios. Interpretability analysis reveals a correlation between activations and attack effectiveness, highlighting the critical role of semantic patterns in transferable vulnerability exploitation.
papers.summary_en: The paper targets the practical threat of Direct Prompt Injection (DPI) attacks, where white-box methods are impractical and black-box approaches suffer from poor cross-model transferability. It proposes a black-box attack framework that builds an Energy-based Model (EBM) from surrogate model activations to guide token-level MCMC sampling for optimizing adversarial prompts. Evaluated on five mainstream LLMs, it achieves 49.6% attack success rate, a 34.6% improvement over human-crafted prompts, and maintains 36.6% on unseen tasks, demonstrating strong transferability. This work directly evidences the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that highly transferable black-box attacks can bypass alignment across models and tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接提示注入（DPI）攻击的实际威胁，指出白盒方法不切实际、黑盒方法跨模型迁移性差。它提出一种黑盒攻击框架，利用替代模型激活构建能量模型（EBM）引导词元级MCMC采样，优化对抗提示。在五个主流大模型上评估，攻击成功率达49.6%，比人工提示高34.6%，在未见任务上保持36.6%，表现出强迁移性。这项工作直接证明了事后安全对齐的脆弱性，因为高度可迁移的黑盒攻击能跨模型和任务绕过对齐。

papers.title: CleanGen: Mitigating Backdoor Attacks for Generation Tasks in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The remarkable performance of large language models (LLMs) in generation tasks has enabled practitioners to leverage publicly available models to power custom applications, such as chatbots and virtual assistants. However, the data used to train or fine-tune these LLMs is often undisclosed, allowing an attacker to compromise the data and inject backdoors into the models. In this paper, we develop a novel inference time defense, named CleanGen, to mitigate backdoor attacks for generation tasks in LLMs. CleanGen is a lightweight and effective decoding strategy that is compatible with the state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs. Our insight behind CleanGen is that compared to other LLMs, backdoored LLMs assign significantly higher probabilities to tokens representing the attacker-desired contents. These discrepancies in token probabilities enable CleanGen to identify suspicious tokens favored by the attacker and replace them with tokens generated by another LLM that is not compromised by the same attacker, thereby avoiding generation of attacker-desired content. We evaluate CleanGen against five SOTA backdoor attacks. Our results show that CleanGen achieves lower attack success rates (ASR) compared to five SOTA baseline defenses for all five backdoor attacks. Moreover, LLMs deploying CleanGen maintain helpfulness in their responses when serving benign user queries with minimal added computational overhead.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses backdoor attacks on LLMs for generation tasks, where poisoned training data can cause models to produce attacker-desired content. It proposes CleanGen, an inference-time decoding strategy that detects and replaces suspicious tokens (identified by anomalously high probabilities in a potentially backdoored model) using an uncompromised model, thereby preventing malicious generation. Evaluated against five SOTA backdoor attacks and five baselines, CleanGen achieves lower attack success rates while preserving helpfulness on benign queries with minimal overhead. The paper focuses on defending against backdoor attacks, which can bypass safety alignment, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型生成任务中的后门攻击问题，即攻击者通过投毒训练数据使模型在触发条件下产生恶意内容。提出 CleanGen，一种推理时解码策略，利用后门模型对攻击者期望 token 赋予异常高概率的特性，检测并替换可疑 token（使用未被同一后门攻击的模型生成 token），从而避免生成攻击者意图的输出。在五种 SOTA 后门攻击和五种基线防御上的评估表明，CleanGen 实现了更低的攻击成功率，并在良性查询上保持有用性，计算开销极小。该论文为防御后门攻击提供了有效机制，间接增强了输出安全性，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题，而是针对特定攻击形式进行缓解。

papers.title: Towards Aligning Language Models with Textual Feedback
papers.abstract: We present ALT (ALignment with Textual feedback), an approach that aligns language models with user preferences expressed in text. We argue that text offers greater expressiveness, enabling users to provide richer feedback than simple comparative preferences and this richer feedback can lead to more efficient and effective alignment. ALT aligns the model by conditioning its generation on the textual feedback. Our method relies solely on language modeling techniques and requires minimal hyper-parameter tuning, though it still presents the main benefit of RL-based algorithms and can effectively learn from textual feedback. We explore the efficacy and efficiency of textual feedback across different tasks such as toxicity reduction, summarization, and dialog response. We find that ALT outperforms PPO for the task of toxicity reduction while being able to match its performance on summarization with only 20% of the samples. We also explore how ALT can be used with feedback provided by an existing LLM.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning language models with richer user preferences beyond simple comparisons, arguing that textual feedback is more expressive. It proposes ALT, which conditions generation on textual feedback, using only language modeling techniques and requiring minimal hyper-parameter tuning. Evaluated on toxicity reduction, summarization, and dialog, ALT outperforms PPO on toxicity reduction and matches summarization performance with only 20% of the samples. This paper advances alignment methodology by leveraging richer textual feedback, but it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决基于用户偏好对齐语言模型的问题，主张文本反馈比简单的比较偏好更具表达性。它提出了ALT方法，通过将生成过程条件化于文本反馈来实现对齐，仅使用语言建模技术且只需极少超参数调整。在毒性降低、摘要和对话任务上的评估表明，ALT在毒性降低上优于PPO，在摘要上仅用20%样本即可达到PPO水平。该论文通过利用更丰富的文本反馈推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Ambiguity Awareness Optimization: Towards Semantic Disambiguation for Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a widely used reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) method across various domains. Recent research has increasingly focused on the role of token importance in improving DPO effectiveness. It is observed that identical or semantically similar content (defined as ambiguous content) frequently appears within the preference pairs. We hypothesize that the presence of ambiguous content during DPO training may introduce ambiguity, thereby limiting further improvements in alignment. Through mathematical analysis and proof-of-concept experiments, we reveal that ambiguous content may potentially introduce ambiguities, thereby degrading performance. To address this issue, we introduce Ambiguity Awareness Optimization (AAO), a simple yet effective approach that automatically re-weights ambiguous content to reduce ambiguities by calculating semantic similarity from preference pairs. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that AAO consistently and significantly surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in performance, without markedly increasing response length, across multiple model scales and widely adopted benchmark datasets, including AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench, and Arena-Hard. Specifically, AAO outperforms DPO by up to 8.9 points on AlpacaEval 2 and achieves an improvement of by up to 15.0 points on Arena-Hard.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the issue that ambiguous content (identical or semantically similar text) in preference pairs during DPO training can introduce ambiguity, limiting alignment performance. It proposes Ambiguity Awareness Optimization (AAO), which re-weights ambiguous tokens based on semantic similarity from the pairs to reduce ambiguity. Across AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench, and Arena-Hard, AAO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods like DPO by up to 8.9 points on AlpacaEval 2 and 15.0 points on Arena-Hard, without increasing response length. This paper advances alignment methodology by mitigating training ambiguity but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接偏好优化（DPO）训练中偏好对里常出现的相同或语义相似内容（歧义内容）可能引入模糊性，从而限制对齐性能提升的问题。提出了歧义感知优化（AAO），通过计算偏好对之间的语义相似度自动重新加权歧义内容，以减少歧义。在AlpacaEval 2、MT-Bench和Arena-Hard等多个基准上，AAO在不同模型规模下均一致且显著地超越现有方法如DPO，在AlpacaEval 2上提升最高8.9分，Arena-Hard上提升最高15.0分，且不显著增加响应长度。本文改进了对齐方法学，但并未直接解决安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Towards Understanding Jailbreak Attacks in LLMs: A Representation Space Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are susceptible to a type of attack known as jailbreaking, which misleads LLMs to output harmful contents. Although there are diverse jailbreak attack strategies, there is no unified understanding on why some methods succeed and others fail. This paper explores the behavior of harmful and harmless prompts in the LLM’s representation space to investigate the intrinsic properties of successful jailbreak attacks. We hypothesize that successful attacks share some similar properties: They are effective in moving the representation of the harmful prompt towards the direction to the harmless prompts. We leverage hidden representations into the objective of existing jailbreak attacks to move the attacks along the acceptance direction, and conduct experiments to validate the above hypothesis using the proposed objective. We hope this study provides new insights into understanding how LLMs understand harmfulness information.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of a unified understanding of why some jailbreak attacks on LLMs succeed while others fail. It proposes analyzing the representation space, hypothesizing that successful attacks shift harmful prompt representations toward the direction of harmless prompts. Experiments incorporate hidden representations into attack objectives to move prompts along this acceptance direction, validating the hypothesis. The work provides mechanistic insight into attack dynamics but does not directly assess the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型越狱攻击成功与否缺乏统一理解的问题，提出在表示空间中分析，假设成功攻击会将有害提示的表示移向无害提示方向。通过将隐藏表示纳入现有攻击目标，沿接受方向移动攻击，实验验证了该假设。该研究从表示层面揭示了攻击机制，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，而是为理解攻击动态奠定基础。

papers.title: Take Off the Training Wheels! Progressive In-Context Learning for Effective Alignment
papers.abstract: Recent studies have explored the working mechanisms of In-Context Learning (ICL). However, they mainly focus on classification and simple generation tasks, limiting their broader application to more complex generation tasks in practice. To address this gap, we investigate the impact of demonstrations on token representations within the practical alignment tasks. We find that the transformer embeds the task function learned from demonstrations into the separator token representation, which plays an important role in the generation of prior response tokens. Once the prior response tokens are determined, the demonstrations become redundant. Motivated by this finding, we propose an efficient Progressive In-Context Alignment (PICA) method consisting of two stages. In the first few-shot stage, the model generates several prior response tokens via standard ICL while concurrently extracting the ICL vector that stores the task function from the separator token representation. In the following zero-shot stage, this ICL vector guides the model to generate responses without further demonstrations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our PICA not only surpasses vanilla ICL but also achieves comparable performance to other alignment tuning methods. The proposed training-free method reduces the time cost (e.g., 5.45×) with improved alignment performance (e.g., 6.57+). Consequently, our work highlights the application of ICL for alignment and calls for a deeper understanding of ICL for complex generations. The code will be available at https://github.com/HITsz-TMG/PICA.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency of using many demonstrations for in-context learning in alignment tasks. It proposes Progressive In-Context Alignment (PICA), which first generates initial tokens with few-shot ICL and extracts an ICL vector from the separator token, then continues generation in a zero-shot manner guided by that vector. Experiments show PICA outperforms standard ICL, matches tuning methods, and reduces time cost by 5.45x while improving alignment performance. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了在 alignment 任务中使用大量演示进行上下文学习（ICL）的低效问题。提出了渐进式上下文对齐（PICA）方法，该方法首先通过少样本 ICL 生成初始响应 token 并从分隔符 token 中提取 ICL 向量，然后在零样本阶段由该向量引导生成，无需进一步演示。实验表明，PICA 优于标准 ICL，性能可与 tuning 方法相媲美，同时将时间成本降低了 5.45 倍，对齐性能提升了 6.57+。该论文推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Advancing Adversarial Suffix Transfer Learning on Aligned Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Language Language Models (LLMs) face safety concerns due to potential misuse by malicious users. Recent red-teaming efforts have identified adversarial suffixes capable of jailbreaking LLMs using the gradient-based search algorithm Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG). However, GCG struggles with computational inefficiency, limiting further investigations regarding suffix transferability and scalability across models and data. In this work, we bridge the connection between search efficiency and suffix transferability. We propose a two-stage transfer learning framework, DeGCG, which decouples the search process into behavior-agnostic pre-searching and behavior-relevant post-searching. Specifically, we employ direct first target token optimization in pre-searching to facilitate the search process. We apply our approach to cross-model, cross-data, and self-transfer scenarios. Furthermore, we introduce an interleaved variant of our approach, i-DeGCG, which iteratively leverages self-transferability to accelerate the search process. Experiments on HarmBench demonstrate the efficiency of our approach across various models and domains. Notably, our i-DeGCG outperforms the baseline on Llama2-chat-7b with ASRs of 43.9 (+ 22.2) and 39.0 (+19.5) on valid and test sets, respectively. Further analysis on cross-model transfer indicates the pivotal role of first target token optimization in leveraging suffix transferability for efficient searching.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency of the GCG algorithm in generating adversarial suffixes for jailbreaking LLMs and the limited transferability of such suffixes. It proposes DeGCG, a two-stage transfer learning framework that decouples the search into behavior-agnostic pre-searching using direct first target token optimization and behavior-relevant post-searching. Experiments on HarmBench show that DeGCG improves efficiency, and its interleaved variant i-DeGCG achieves significantly higher attack success rates (e.g., +22.2 on Llama2-chat-7b valid set). This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as it can be efficiently bypassed with transferable adversarial suffixes, revealing a mechanistic weakness exploitable across models and domains.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决GCG算法在生成对抗性后缀时计算效率低和可迁移性受限的问题，这些问题用于越狱大语言模型。它提出DeGCG，一个两阶段迁移学习框架，将搜索解耦为行为无关的预搜索（采用直接第一目标令牌优化）和行为相关的后搜索。在HarmBench上的实验表明DeGCG提高了效率，其交错变体i-DeGCG显著提升了攻击成功率（例如在Llama2-chat-7b验证集上提升22.2）。该研究直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因为可迁移对抗性后缀能高效绕过防御，暴露出跨模型和跨域的可利用机制弱点。

papers.title: Reward-Shifted Speculative Sampling Is An Efficient Test-Time Weak-to-Strong Aligner
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences has become a critical step in their development. Recent research has increasingly focused on test-time alignment, where additional compute is allocated during inference to enhance LLM safety and reasoning capabilities. However, these test-time alignment techniques often incur substantial inference costs, limiting their practical application. We are inspired by the speculative sampling acceleration, which leverages a small draft model to efficiently predict future tokens, to address the efficiency bottleneck of test-time alignment. We introduce the reward-shifted speculative sampling (SSS) algorithm, in which the draft model is aligned with human preferences, while the target model remains unchanged. We theoretically demonstrate that the distributional shift between the aligned draft model and the unaligned target model can be exploited to recover the RLHF optimal solution without actually obtaining it, by modifying the acceptance criterion and bonus token distribution. Our algorithm achieves superior gold reward scores at a significantly reduced inference cost in test-time weak-to-strong alignment experiments, thereby validating both its effectiveness and efficiency.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high inference cost of existing test-time alignment methods for LLMs. It proposes reward-shifted speculative sampling (SSS), where an aligned draft model is used with a modified acceptance criterion and bonus token distribution to exploit distributional shift for efficient alignment. Evaluated in test-time weak-to-strong alignment, SSS achieves better gold reward scores with significantly lower inference cost, validating effectiveness and efficiency. This paper advances alignment methodology by making test-time alignment more feasible, but it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有测试时对齐方法推理成本高昂的问题。提出了奖励转移推测采样（SSS）算法，利用对齐的草稿模型，通过修改接受准则和奖励令牌分布，利用分布偏移高效恢复RLHF最优解。在测试时弱到强对齐实验中，SSS显著降低推理成本的同时获得了更优的黄金奖励分数，验证了其有效性和效率。本文改进了对齐方法学的效率，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Intrinsic Self-correction for Enhanced Morality: An Analysis of Internal Mechanisms and the Superficial Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are capable of producing content that perpetuates stereotypes, discrimination, and toxicity.The recently proposed moral self-correction is a computationally efficient method for reducing harmful content in the responses of LLMs. However, the process of how injecting self-correction instructions can modify the behavior of LLMs remains under-explored. In this paper, we explore the effectiveness of moral self-correction by answering three research questions: (1) In what scenarios does moral self-correction work? (2) What are the internal mechanisms of LLMs, e.g., hidden states, that are influenced by moral self-correction instructions? (3) Is intrinsic moral self-correction actually superficial in terms of reduced immorality in hidden states? We argue that self-correction can help LLMs find a shortcut to more morally correct output, rather than truly reducing the immorality stored in hidden states.Through empirical investigation with tasks of language generation and multi-choice question answering, we conclude: (i) LLMs exhibit good performance across both tasks, and self-correction instructions are particularly beneficial when the correct answer is already top-ranked; (ii) The morality levels in intermediate hidden states are strong indicators as to whether one instruction would be more effective than another; (iii) Based on our analysis of intermediate hidden states and task case studies of self-correction behaviors, we are first to propose the hypothesis that intrinsic moral self-correction is in fact superficial.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the internal mechanisms of moral self-correction in LLMs, which aims to reduce harmful outputs. Through language generation and multi-choice QA tasks, it finds that self-correction works best when the correct answer is already top-ranked and that intermediate hidden states indicate instruction effectiveness. The authors propose the 'superficial hypothesis' that self-correction helps LLMs find a shortcut rather than genuinely reducing immorality. This work provides mechanistic evidence that safety alignment may be superficial, supporting the view that post-training alignment can be fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大型语言模型中道德自纠正的内部机制，旨在减少有害输出。通过语言生成和多选题问答任务，发现当正确答案已排名靠前时自纠正效果最佳，中间隐藏状态能指示指令有效性。作者提出“表层假设”，认为自纠正仅帮助模型找到捷径而非真正减少不道德性。该研究为安全对齐可能只是表层化、脆弱的模块提供了机制性证据。

papers.title: VLFeedback: A Large-Scale AI Feedback Dataset for Large Vision-Language Models Alignment
papers.abstract: As large vision-language models (LVLMs) evolve rapidly, the demand for high-quality and diverse data to align these models becomes increasingly crucial. However, the creation of such data with human supervision proves costly and time-intensive. In this paper, we investigate the efficacy of AI feedback to scale supervision for aligning LVLMs. We introduce VLFeedback, the first large-scale vision-language feedback dataset, comprising over 82K multi-modal instructions and comprehensive rationales generated by off-the-shelf models without human annotations. To evaluate the effectiveness of AI feedback for vision-language alignment, we train Silkie, an LVLM fine-tuned via direct preference optimization on VLFeedback. Silkie showcases exceptional performance regarding helpfulness, visual faithfulness, and safety metrics. It outperforms its base model by 6.9% and 9.5% in perception and cognition tasks, reduces hallucination issues on MMHal-Bench, and exhibits enhanced resilience against red-teaming attacks. Furthermore, our analysis underscores the advantage of AI feedback, particularly in fostering preference diversity to deliver more comprehensive improvements. Our dataset, training code and models are available at https://vlf-silkie.github.io.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high cost and scarcity of human-annotated data for aligning large vision-language models (LVLMs). It introduces VLFeedback, a large-scale dataset of over 82K multimodal instructions with rationales generated by off-the-shelf AI models, and uses it to fine-tune an LVLM, Silkie, via direct preference optimization. Silkie achieves significant improvements in helpfulness, visual faithfulness, and safety, outperforming the base model by 6.9% and 9.5% on perception and cognition tasks, reducing hallucinations, and improving red-teaming resilience. This work advances alignment methodology through AI feedback but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型视觉语言模型对齐中人类标注数据成本高、稀缺的问题，提出利用AI反馈扩展监督。介绍了VLFeedback，一个包含82K多模态指令和AI生成理由的大规模数据集，并基于此通过直接偏好优化微调得到模型Silkie。Silkie在帮助性、视觉忠实度和安全性上显著提升，在感知和认知任务上分别超出基线6.9%和9.5%，减少了幻觉，提高了抗红队攻击能力。该工作通过AI反馈推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Mitigating the Alignment Tax of RLHF
papers.short_title: Mitigating the Alignment Tax of RLHF
papers.abstract: LLMs acquire a wide range of abilities during pre-training, but aligning LLMs under Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) can lead to forgetting pretrained abilities, which is also known as the alignment tax. To investigate alignment tax, we conducted experiments with existing RLHF algorithms using OpenLLaMA-3B, which revealed a pronounced alignment tax in NLP tasks. Whereas, despite various techniques to mitigate forgetting, they are often at odds with the RLHF performance, leading to a trade-off between alignment performance and forgetting mitigation, leading to an alignment-forgetting trade-off. In this paper we show that model averaging, which simply interpolates between pre and post RLHF model weights, surprisingly achieves the most strongest alignment-forgetting Pareto front among a wide range of competing methods. To understand its effectiveness, we offer theoretical insights into model averaging, revealing that it enhances performance Pareto front by increasing feature diversity on the layers where tasks share overlapped feature spaces. Empirical evidence corroborates our analysis by showing the benefits of averaging low-level transformer layers. Building on the analysis and the observation that averaging different layers of the transformer leads to significantly different alignment-forgetting trade-offs, we propose Heterogeneous Model Averaging (HMA) to Heterogeneously find various combination ratios of model layers. HMA seeks to maximize the alignment performance while incurring minimal alignment tax. Moreover, we validate HMA’s performance across a range of RLHF algorithms over OpenLLaMA-3B and further extend our findings to Mistral-7B which is evaluated by open-sourced preference model and GPT4. Code available here.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the alignment tax in RLHF, where fine-tuning LLMs for human preferences leads to catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained capabilities. It proposes Heterogeneous Model Averaging (HMA), which interpolates between pre- and post-RLHF model weights with layer-wise mixing ratios to maximize alignment performance while minimizing forgetting. Evaluated on OpenLLaMA-3B and Mistral-7B, HMA achieves a Pareto-optimal alignment-forgetting trade-off, outperforming existing methods. While this work introduces a strong technique for building better-aligned models, it focuses on improving alignment efficiency and does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fundamentally fragile or robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中的对齐税问题，即基于人类反馈的微调会导致LLM遗忘预训练能力。提出异构模型平均法（HMA），通过在预训练和RLHF后模型权重之间进行逐层插值，以最大化对齐性能并最小化遗忘。在OpenLLaMA-3B和Mistral-7B上评估，HMA在对齐-遗忘折衷中取得了帕累托最优，优于现有方法。该工作提出了构建更优对齐模型的有效技术，但专注于提升对齐效率，未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质脆弱或鲁棒。

papers.title: DogeRM: Equipping Reward Models with Domain Knowledge through Model Merging
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a popular strategy for aligning large language models (LLMs) with desired behaviors. Reward modeling is a crucial step in RLHF. However, collecting paired preference data for training reward models is often costly and time-consuming, especially for domain-specific preferences requiring expert annotation. To address this challenge, we propose the **Do**main knowled**ge** merged **R**eward **M**odel (**DogeRM**), a novel framework that integrates domain-specific knowledge into a general reward model by model merging. The experiments demonstrate that DogeRM enhances performance across different benchmarks and provide a detailed analysis showcasing the effects of model merging, showing the great potential of facilitating model alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the costly and time-consuming collection of domain-specific preference data for training reward models in RLHF. It proposes DogeRM, a framework that integrates domain knowledge into a general reward model via model merging, bypassing the need for extensive expert annotation. Experiments show that DogeRM improves reward model performance across various benchmarks and the analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of model merging. This paper advances alignment methodology by enhancing reward model domain adaptation, but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对强化学习人工反馈中训练奖励模型时领域特定偏好数据收集成本高、耗时久的问题。提出DogeRM框架，通过模型融合将领域知识整合到通用奖励模型中，避免大量专家标注。实验表明，DogeRM在多个基准上提升了奖励模型性能，并分析了模型融合的效果，展示了其促进模型对齐的潜力。本文推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Eliminating Biased Length Reliance of Direct Preference Optimization via Down-Sampled KL Divergence
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has emerged as a prominent algorithm for the direct and robust alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences, offering a more straightforward alternative to the complex Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). Despite its promising efficacy, DPO faces a notable drawback: “verbosity”, a common over-optimization phenomenon also observed in RLHF. While previous studies mainly attributed verbosity to biased labels within the data, we propose that the issue also stems from an inherent algorithmic length reliance in DPO. Specifically, we suggest that the discrepancy between sequence-level Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergences between chosen and rejected sequences, used in DPO, results in overestimated or underestimated rewards due to varying token lengths. Empirically, we utilize datasets with different label lengths to demonstrate the presence of biased rewards. We then introduce an effective downsampling approach, named SamPO, to eliminate potential length reliance. Our experimental evaluations, conducted across three LLMs of varying scales and a diverse array of conditional and open-ended benchmarks, highlight the efficacy of SamPO in mitigating verbosity, achieving improvements of 5% to 12% over DPO through debaised rewards. Our code can be accessed at: https://github.com/LuJunru/SamPO/.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the verbosity problem in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), where models generate overly long responses. It identifies an inherent algorithmic length reliance in DPO caused by discrepancy in sequence-level KL divergences between chosen and rejected sequences of different lengths, leading to biased rewards. They propose SamPO, a downsampling approach to eliminate this length reliance by debiasing the rewards. Evaluated on three LLMs across conditional and open-ended benchmarks, SamPO mitigates verbosity with improvements of 5-12% over DPO. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了直接偏好优化（DPO）中的冗长问题，即模型生成过长响应。它识别出 DPO 中由于所选和拒绝序列长度不同导致的序列级 KL 散度差异，从而产生有偏奖励的内在算法长度依赖。他们提出 SamPO，一种通过去偏奖励来消除长度依赖的下采样方法。在三个不同规模的 LLM 以及条件和开放式基准上评估，SamPO 减轻了冗长，比 DPO 提高 5-12%。本文改进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Think in Safety: Unveiling and Mitigating Safety Alignment Collapse in Multimodal Large Reasoning Model
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Multimodal Large Reasoning Models (MLRMs) has demonstrated broad application potential, yet their safety and reliability remain critical concerns that require systematic exploration. To address this gap, we conduct a comprehensive and systematic safety evaluation of 13 MLRMs across 5 benchmarks and unveil prevalent safety degradation phenomena in most advanced models. Moreover, our analysis reveals distinct safety patterns across different benchmarks: significant safety degradation is observed across jailbreak robustness benchmarks, whereas safety-awareness benchmarks demonstrate less pronounced degradation. In particular, the long thought process in some scenarios even enhances safety performance. Therefore, it is a potential approach to address safety issues in MLRMs by leveraging the intrinsic reasoning capabilities of the model to detect unsafe intent. To operationalize this insight, we construct a multimodal tuning dataset that incorporates a safety-oriented thought process. Experimental results from fine-tuning existing MLRMs with this dataset effectively enhance the safety on both jailbreak robustness and safety-awareness benchmarks. This study provides a new perspective for developing safe MLRMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates safety alignment collapse in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models (MLRMs), revealing significant safety degradation, particularly in jailbreak robustness. It proposes to mitigate this by leveraging the model's intrinsic reasoning capabilities to detect unsafe intent, and constructs a multimodal safety-oriented thinking dataset for fine-tuning. Experiments show that fine-tuning MLRMs with this dataset effectively improves safety on both jailbreak robustness and safety-awareness benchmarks. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating its collapse in MLRMs and offering a reasoning-based hardening method.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了多模态大推理模型（MLRM）中的安全对齐崩塌问题，发现普遍存在安全性能退化，尤其在越狱鲁棒性方面。提出利用模型内在的推理能力检测不安全意图，并构建了一个包含安全导向思维过程的多模态微调数据集来应对该问题。实验表明，用该数据集微调现有MLRM能有效提升越狱鲁棒性和安全意识基准上的安全性。这项工作通过揭示MLRM中安全对齐的脆弱性并提供基于推理的加固方法，直接回应了后训练安全对齐是否真正鲁棒这一问题。

papers.title: Alignment-Enhanced Decoding: Defending Jailbreaks via Token-Level Adaptive Refining of Probability Distributions
papers.abstract: Large language models are susceptible to jailbreak attacks, which can result in the generation of harmful content. While prior defenses mitigate these risks by perturbing or inspecting inputs, they ignore competing objectives, the underlying cause of alignment failures. In this paper, we propose Alignment-Enhanced Decoding (AED), a novel defense that employs adaptive decoding to address the root causes of jailbreak issues. We first define the Competitive Index to quantify alignment failures and utilize feedback from self-evaluation to compute post-alignment logits. Then, AED adaptively combines Competitive Index and post-alignment logits with the original logits to obtain harmless and helpful distributions. Consequently, our method enhances safety alignment while maintaining helpfulness. We conduct experiments across five models and four common jailbreaks, with the results validating the effectiveness of our approach.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses jailbreak attacks that cause LLMs to generate harmful content by exploiting the tension between safety and helpfulness objectives. It proposes Alignment-Enhanced Decoding (AED), which introduces a Competitive Index to measure alignment failures and uses self-evaluation feedback to adaptively refine token probabilities, balancing harmlessness and helpfulness during decoding. Experiments across five models and four jailbreak methods demonstrate that AED significantly reduces attack success rates while preserving output quality, validating its effectiveness. This work directly confronts the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that alignment can be bypassed but also hardened through dynamic, inference-time intervention.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对利用安全性与有用性目标冲突导致大语言模型生成有害内容的越狱攻击。提出对齐增强解码方法（AED），通过定义竞争指数来量化对齐失败，并利用自我评估反馈自适应地调整词元概率，在解码时平衡无害性和有用性。在五个模型和四种越狱方法上的实验表明，AED有效降低了攻击成功率并保持了输出质量。该研究通过动态推理时干预直接应对了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，证明对齐虽可被绕过但也能被强化。

papers.title: Layer-Aware Representation Filtering: Purifying Finetuning Data to Preserve LLM Safety Alignment
papers.short_title: LARF: Filtering Data to Preserve Safety
papers.abstract: With rapid advancement and increasing accessibility of LLMs, fine-tuning aligned models has become a critical step for adapting them to real-world applications, which makes the safety of this fine-tuning process more important than ever. However, recent studies have highlighted a critical challenge: even when fine-tuning with seemingly benign downstream datasets, the safety of aligned LLMs can be compromised, making them more susceptible to malicious instructions. In this paper, we show that fine-tuning datasets often contain samples with safety-degrading features that are not easily identifiable on the surface. These samples can significantly degrade the safety alignment of LLMs during fine-tuning. To address this issue, we propose LARF, a Layer-Aware Representation Filtering method. This method identifies safety-sensitive layers within the LLM and leverages their representations to detect which data samples in the post-training dataset contain safety-degrading features. Experimental results demonstrate that LARF can effectively identify benign data with safety-degrading features. After removing such data, the safety alignment degradation caused by fine-tuning is mitigated. Please see our code at https://github.com/LLLeoLi/LARF.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that fine-tuning aligned LLMs on seemingly benign downstream datasets can inadvertently degrade safety alignment, making them vulnerable to malicious instructions. It proposes LARF, a method that identifies safety-sensitive layers and uses their representations to filter out fine-tuning samples with safety-degrading features. Experiments show that removing such data mitigates safety degradation while preserving adaptation ability. This work contributes to the fragility question by demonstrating that alignment can be broken through contaminated fine-tuning data, but also offers a defense, highlighting both vulnerability and potential robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文指出，使用看似良性的下游数据集微调对齐后的大语言模型时，可能会无意中损害其安全对齐性，使其更容易受到恶意指令的攻击。提出LARF方法，通过识别模型中的安全敏感层并利用其内部表征来检测和过滤具有安全退化特征的微调样本。实验表明，移除这些数据可减轻安全对齐退化，同时保持模型对下游任务的适应能力。该研究从安全对齐脆弱性角度揭示了微调数据污染可能导致对齐被破坏，同时提供了一种加固技术，表明安全对齐易受数据投毒影响但可通过防御保持。

papers.title: Evaluating Psychological Safety of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: In this work, we designed unbiased prompts to systematically evaluate the psychological safety of large language models (LLMs). First, we tested five different LLMs by using two personality tests: Short Dark Triad (SD-3) and Big Five Inventory (BFI). All models scored higher than the human average on SD-3, suggesting a relatively darker personality pattern. Despite being instruction fine-tuned with safety metrics to reduce toxicity, InstructGPT, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 still showed dark personality patterns; these models scored higher than self-supervised GPT-3 on the Machiavellianism and narcissism traits on SD-3. Then, we evaluated the LLMs in the GPT series by using well-being tests to study the impact of fine-tuning with more training data. We observed a continuous increase in the well-being scores of GPT models. Following these observations, we showed that fine-tuning Llama-2-chat-7B with responses from BFI using direct preference optimization could effectively reduce the psychological toxicity of the model. Based on the findings, we recommended the application of systematic and comprehensive psychological metrics to further evaluate and improve the safety of LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the psychological safety of large language models (LLMs) by evaluating personality traits and well-being. It administers the Short Dark Triad (SD-3) and Big Five Inventory (BFI) tests via unbiased prompts to five LLMs, and later fine-tunes Llama-2-chat-7B with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) using BFI responses to reduce psychological toxicity. All models scored higher than the human average on SD-3, indicating darker personality patterns, and DPO fine-tuning effectively mitigated these issues. While the paper advances alignment methodology through psychological metrics and DPO-based improvement, it does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is robust or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过评估大语言模型的人格特质和幸福感，研究其心理安全性。作者设计了无偏提示，使用短式黑暗三联征（SD-3）和大五人格量表（BFI）对五种LLM进行测试，并随后利用BFI响应通过直接偏好优化（DPO）微调Llama-2-chat-7B以减少心理毒性。结果表明，所有模型的SD-3得分均高于人类平均水平，显示出较阴暗的人格模式；而DPO微调能有效缓解这一问题。本文推进了基于心理指标的对齐方法，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Revisiting Who's Harry Potter: Towards Targeted Unlearning from a Causal Intervention Perspective
papers.abstract: This paper investigates Who’s Harry Potter (WHP), a pioneering yet insufficiently understood method for LLM unlearning. We explore it in two steps. First, we introduce a new task of LLM targeted unlearning, where given an unlearning target (e.g., a person) and some unlearning documents, we aim to unlearn only the information about the target, rather than everything in the unlearning documents. We further argue that a successful unlearning should satisfy criteria such as not outputting gibberish, not fabricating facts about the unlearning target, and not releasing factual information under jailbreak attacks. Second, we construct a causal intervention framework for targeted unlearning, where the knowledge of the unlearning target is modeled as a confounder between LLM input and output, and the unlearning process as a deconfounding process. This framework justifies and extends WHP, deriving a simple unlearning algorithm that includes WHP as a special case. Experiments on existing and new datasets show that our approach, without explicitly optimizing for the aforementioned criteria, achieves competitive performance in all of them.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses targeted unlearning for LLMs, aiming to remove only specific information about a given target while preserving other knowledge. It proposes a causal intervention framework that models target knowledge as a confounder and unlearning as deconfounding, generalizing the Who's Harry Potter (WHP) method. Evaluated on existing and new datasets, the approach demonstrates competitive performance in avoiding gibberish, not fabricating facts, and resisting jailbreak attacks. This work advances alignment methodology through improved unlearning but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型的有目标遗忘问题，旨在仅移除关于特定目标的特定信息，同时保留其他知识。它提出一种因果干预框架，将目标知识建模为混杂因子，遗忘过程视为去混杂，推广了WHP方法。在现有和新数据集上的评估表明，该方法在避免乱码、不虚构事实以及抵抗越狱攻击方面性能优异。本研究通过改进遗忘技术推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Learn and Unlearn: Addressing Misinformation in Multilingual LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the propagation of information in multilingual large language models (LLMs) and evaluates the efficacy of various unlearning methods. We demonstrate that fake information, regardless of the language it is in, once introduced into these models through training data, can spread across different languages, compromising the integrity and reliability of the generated content. Our findings reveal that standard unlearning techniques, which typically focus on English data, are insufficient in mitigating the spread of harmful content in multilingual contexts and could inadvertently reinforce harmful content across languages. We show that only by addressing harmful responses in both English and the original language of the harmful data we can effectively eliminate it for all languages. This underscores the critical need for comprehensive unlearning strategies that consider the multilingual nature of modern LLMs to enhance their safety and reliability across landscapes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of misinformation spreading across languages in multilingual LLMs once introduced through training data. It evaluates standard unlearning methods and finds that English-only unlearning is insufficient and can even reinforce harmful content in other languages. The key result is that effective mitigation requires unlearning in both English and the original language of the harmful data. This finding directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment in multilingual contexts, as safety measures applied monolingually fail to generalize, revealing a cross-lingual bypass for harmful content.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了多语言大语言模型中错误信息的跨语言传播问题。实验表明，一旦通过训练数据引入虚假信息，它就会在不同语言间扩散。标准的遗忘方法通常仅针对英语数据，这在多语言环境中不足以消除有害内容，甚至可能无意中强化其他语言的有害输出。只有同时处理英语和原始语言中的有害响应，才能在所有语言中有效消除错误信息。这一发现揭示了后训练安全对齐在多语言场景下的脆弱性：仅针对单一语言的安全措施无法泛化到其他语言，从而为有害内容提供了跨语言的绕过途径。

papers.title: Data to Defense: The Role of Curation in Aligning Large Language Models Against Safety Compromise
papers.short_title: Adaptive Data Curation for LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely adapted for downstream applications through fine-tuning, a process named customization. However, recent studies have identified a vulnerability during this process, where malicious samples can compromise the robustness of LLMs and amplify harmful behaviors. To address this challenge, we propose an adaptive data curation approach allowing any text to be curated to enhance its effectiveness in counteracting harmful samples during customization. To avoid the need for additional defensive modules, we further introduce a comprehensive mitigation framework spanning the lifecycle of the customization process: before customization to immunize LLMs against future compromise attempts, during customization to neutralize risks, and after customization to restore compromised models. Experimental results demonstrate a significant reduction in compromising effects, achieving up to a 100% success rate in generating safe responses. By combining adaptive data curation with lifecycle-based mitigation strategies, this work represents a solid step forward in mitigating compromising risks and ensuring the secure adaptation of LLMs.
