papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety risk that conventional machine unlearning fails to erase sensitive information from the chain-of-thought reasoning traces of large reasoning models (LRMs). The authors propose Reasoning-aware Representation Misdirection for Unlearning (R^2MU), a method that suppresses harmful reasoning traces and prevents the generation of associated final answers while preserving overall reasoning ability. Experiments on DeepSeek-R1-Distill models show that R^2MU significantly reduces sensitive information leakage in traces and achieves strong performance on safety and reasoning benchmarks. This work reveals that safety alignment in reasoning models is fragile because harmful knowledge can persist in intermediate steps, effectively bypassing conventional unlearning and highlighting a new failure mode.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对传统机器遗忘无法清除大推理模型思维链中的敏感信息这一安全风险，提出推理感知的表示误导遗忘方法R^2MU，能够抑制有害推理轨迹并阻止关联答案生成，同时保留模型的推理能力。在DeepSeek-R1-Distill模型上的实验表明，R^2MU显著减少了推理痕迹中的敏感信息泄露，并在安全与推理基准上取得强劲表现。该研究表明，推理模型的安全对齐具有脆弱性，有害知识可残留于中间步骤，从而绕过常规遗忘，构成新的对齐失败模式。

papers.title: Taylor Unswift: Secured Weight Release for Large Language Models via Taylor Expansion
papers.abstract: Ensuring the security of released large language models (LLMs) poses a significant dilemma, as existing mechanisms either compromise ownership rights or raise data privacy concerns. To address this dilemma, we introduce TaylorMLP to protect the ownership of released LLMs and prevent their abuse. Specifically, TaylorMLP preserves the ownership of LLMs by transforming the weights of LLMs into parameters of Taylor-series. Instead of releasing the original weights, developers can release the Taylor-series parameters with users, thereby ensuring the security of LLMs. Moreover, TaylorMLP can prevent abuse of LLMs by adjusting the generation speed. It can induce low-speed token generation for the protected LLMs by increasing the terms in the Taylor-series. This intentional delay helps LLM developers prevent potential large-scale unauthorized uses of their models. Empirical experiments across five datasets and three LLM architectures demonstrate that TaylorMLP induces over increase in latency, producing the tokens precisely matched with original LLMs. Subsequent defensive experiments further confirm that TaylorMLP effectively prevents users from reconstructing the weight values based on downstream datasets.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the dilemma of releasing LLMs while protecting intellectual property and preventing large-scale unauthorized abuse. The proposed TaylorMLP method transforms LLM weights into Taylor-series parameters, releasing these instead of original weights to enable ownership verification and to deliberately slow down token generation by increasing series terms. Evaluated on five datasets and three architectures, it produces identical outputs with significantly increased latency, and defensive experiments confirm resistance to weight reconstruction. This work focuses on model release security and does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型发布时既要保护知识产权又要防止大规模滥用的两难困境。提出的TaylorMLP方法将模型权重转换为泰勒级数参数并以此替代原始权重发布，既能验证所有权，又能通过增加级数项有意降低生成速度。在五个数据集和三种架构上的实验表明，输出完全一致且延迟显著增加，防御实验证实可抵抗权重重建。该研究关注模型发布安全，未直接涉及后训练安全对齐在面对对抗攻击时的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: MULTIGUARD: An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across Languages and Modalities
papers.abstract: The emerging capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have sparked concerns about their immediate potential for harmful misuse. The core approach to mitigate these concerns is the detection of harmful queries to the model. Current detection approaches are fallible, and are particularly susceptible to attacks that exploit mismatched generalization of model capabilities (e.g., prompts in low-resource languages or prompts provided in non-text modalities such as image and audio). To tackle this challenge, we propose OMNIGUARD, an approach for detecting harmful prompts across languages and modalities. Our approach (i) identifies internal representations of an LLM/MLLM that are aligned across languages or modalities and then (ii) uses them to build a language-agnostic or modality-agnostic classifier for detecting harmful prompts. OMNIGUARD improves harmful prompt classification accuracy by 11.57% over the strongest baseline in a multilingual setting, by 20.44% for image-based prompts, and sets a new SOTA for audio-based prompts. By repurposing embeddings computed during generation, OMNIGUARD is also very efficient (≈ 120× faster than the next fastest baseline). Code and data are available at https://github.com/vsahil/OmniGuard
papers.summary_en: The paper tackles the vulnerability of safety classifiers to harmful prompts in low-resource languages and non-text modalities like images and audio, which bypass existing defenses by exploiting mismatched generalization. It proposes OMNIGUARD, which aligns internal LLM/MLLM representations across languages and modalities to build a language- and modality-agnostic classifier for detecting harmful prompts. Evaluated in multilingual, image, and audio settings, OMNIGUARD improves accuracy by 11.57% over the strongest baseline for text, 20.44% for image-based prompts, and achieves state-of-the-art for audio, while being approximately 120× faster by reusing generation embeddings. The paper strengthens safety moderation against cross-modal and cross-lingual attacks, directly addressing the fragility of post-training safety alignment, though it focuses on detection rather than resolving whether the underlying generative behavior is inherently fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有安全分类器对低资源语言和图像、音频等非文本模态下有害提示的脆弱性问题，此类攻击利用了模型泛化能力的错配。提出 OMNIGUARD 方法，通过对齐大语言模型/多模态大模型在不同语言和模态间的内部表示，构建了语言无关和模态无关的有害提示分类器。实验表明，在多语言、图像和音频设置下，OMNIGUARD 的文本有害提示分类准确率比最强基线提升 11.57%，图像提示提升 20.44%，并在音频提示上取得最优性能，同时通过复用生成嵌入，速度比最快基线快约 120 倍。本文通过跨模态和跨语言的安全检测强化了安全对齐的鲁棒性，直接回应了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，但主要聚焦于检测层面，未根本解决模型生成行为是否内在脆弱的问题。

papers.title: Stand on The Shoulders of Giants: Building JailExpert from Previous Attack Experience
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate human-aligned content under certain safety constraints. However, the current known technique ``jailbreak prompt''can circumvent safety-aligned measures and induce LLMs to output malicious content. Research on Jailbreaking can help identify vulnerabilities in LLMs and guide the development of robust security frameworks. To circumvent the issue of attack templates becoming obsolete as models evolve, existing methods adopt iterative mutation and dynamic optimization to facilitate more automated jailbreak attacks. However, these methods face two challenges: inefficiency and repetitive optimization, as they overlook the value of past attack experiences. To better integrate past attack experiences to assist current jailbreak attempts, we propose the \textbf{JailExpert}, an automated jailbreak framework, which is the first to achieve a formal representation of experience structure, group experiences based on semantic drift, and support the dynamic updating of the experience pool. Extensive experiments demonstrate that JailExpert significantly improves both attack effectiveness and efficiency. Compared to the current state-of-the-art black-box jailbreak methods, JailExpert achieves an average increase of 17\% in attack success rate and 2.7 times improvement in attack efficiency. Our implementation is available at \href{https://github.com/xiZAIzai/JailExpert}{XiZaiZai/JailExpert}
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency of automated jailbreak attacks, which often repeat optimization from scratch without utilizing prior successful attack experiences. It proposes JailExpert, a framework that structures and groups past jailbreak experiences based on semantic drift and dynamically updates an experience pool to guide new attacks. Evaluated against state-of-the-art black-box jailbreak methods, JailExpert achieved an average 17% higher attack success rate and 2.7x faster attack efficiency. By showing that accumulated jailbreak experiences can significantly amplify attack potency, this paper demonstrates that post-training safety alignment remains a fragile mechanism that can be systematically and increasingly bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对自动化越狱攻击的低效问题，即现有方法常从零开始重复优化而忽略过往成功攻击经验。论文提出JailExpert框架，首次对经验进行结构化表示，基于语义漂移对经验分组，并支持经验池的动态更新，以指导新攻击。与当前最先进的黑盒越狱方法相比，JailExpert的攻击成功率平均提升17%，效率提升2.7倍。通过展示积累的越狱经验可显著放大攻击效力，本文揭示了安全对齐是一种脆弱的机制，可被系统性且日益增强地绕过。

papers.title: From LLMs to MLLMs: Exploring the Landscape of Multimodal Jailbreaking
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has exposed vulnerabilities to various adversarial attacks. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of jailbreaking research targeting both LLMs and MLLMs, highlighting recent advancements in evaluation benchmarks, attack techniques and defense strategies. Compared to the more advanced state of unimodal jailbreaking, multimodal domain remains underexplored. We summarize the limitations and potential research directions of multimodal jailbreaking, aiming to inspire future research and further enhance the robustness and security of MLLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper surveys jailbreaking attacks on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), providing a comprehensive overview of evaluation benchmarks, attack techniques, and defense strategies. It finds that while LLM jailbreaking is more advanced, MLLM jailbreaking remains underexplored, summarizing current limitations and future directions. The survey demonstrates that alignment is fragile, especially in multimodal contexts where new attack vectors emerge, underscoring the need for more robust safety measures.
papers.summary_zh: 本文综述了针对大语言模型（LLM）和多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的越狱攻击，全面概述了评估基准、攻击技术和防御策略。研究发现LLM越狱研究更为成熟，而MLLM越狱领域尚待探索，并总结了当前局限性与未来方向。该综述表明对齐机制依然脆弱，特别是在多模态场景下新攻击面不断出现，突显了更鲁棒的安全措施的必要性。

papers.title: ASETF: A Novel Method for Jailbreak Attack on LLMs through Translate Suffix Embeddings
papers.abstract: The safety defense methods of Large language models (LLMs) stays limited because the dangerous prompts are manually curated to just few known attack types, which fails to keep pace with emerging varieties. Recent studies found that attaching suffixes to harmful instructions can hack the defense of LLMs and lead to dangerous outputs. However, similar to traditional text adversarial attacks, this approach, while effective, is limited by the challenge of the discrete tokens. This gradient based discrete optimization attack requires over 100,000 LLM calls, and due to the unreadable of adversarial suffixes, it can be relatively easily penetrated by common defense methods such as perplexity filters.To cope with this challenge, in this paper, we propose an Adversarial Suffix Embedding Translation Framework (ASETF), aimed at transforming continuous adversarial suffix embeddings into coherent and understandable text. This method greatly reduces the computational overhead during the attack process and helps to automatically generate multiple adversarial samples, which can be used as data to strengthen LLM’s security defense. Experimental evaluations were conducted on Llama2, Vicuna, and other prominent LLMs, employing harmful directives sourced from the Advbench dataset.The results indicate that our method significantly reduces the computation time of adversarial suffixes and achieves a much better attack success rate than existing techniques, while significantly enhancing the textual fluency of the prompts. In addition, our approach can be generalized into a broader method for generating transferable adversarial suffixes that can successfully attack multiple LLMs, even black-box LLMs, such as ChatGPT and Gemini.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency and detectability of current jailbreak attacks that use discrete optimization to append suffixes to harmful prompts. The authors propose ASETF, a framework that translates continuous adversarial suffix embeddings into coherent text, drastically reducing computational cost and improving textual fluency. Experiments on Llama2, Vicuna, and others using the Advbench dataset show that ASETF achieves higher attack success rates with less computation and generates transferable suffixes effective against black-box models like ChatGPT and Gemini. This work reveals a significant fragility in existing safety alignment: adversarial embeddings can be exploited to bypass defenses, and the method also provides a way to automatically generate data for hardening models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有通过离散优化添加后缀的越狱攻击方法计算开销大、生成文本不可读且易被检测的问题。作者提出ASETF框架，将连续的对抗性后缀嵌入转换为连贯可读的文本，大幅降低计算量并提升流畅性。在Llama2、Vicuna等模型和Advbench数据集上的实验表明，ASETF显著减少计算时间，攻击成功率更高，且能生成可迁移的后缀，对ChatGPT和Gemini等黑盒模型有效。该研究揭示了现有安全对齐的脆弱性：对抗性嵌入可被利用绕过防御，同时该方法也为自动生成对抗样本以加固模型提供了途径。

papers.title: InferAligner: Inference-Time Alignment for Harmlessness through Cross-Model Guidance
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) rapidly evolve, they are increasingly being customized through fine-tuning to suit the specific needs of various applications. A critical aspect of this advancement is the alignment process, which ensures that these models perform tasks in ways that align with human values and expectations. Current alignment methods, such as direct preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), focus primarily on alignment during training phase. However, these methods often involve complex and resource-intensive training processes, posing significant challenge for their implementation. Therefore, we propose InferAligner, a simple yet effective method for harmlessness alignment during inference phase. InferAligner decouples harmlessness from helpfulness. During the training phase, it focuses solely on enhancing the target model’s capabilities on downstream tasks. In the inference phase, it utilizes safety steering vectors extracted from the aligned model to guide the target model towards harmlessness alignment. Experimental results show that our method can be very effectively applied to domain-specific models in finance, medicine, and mathematics, as well as to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) such as LLaVA. It significantly diminishes the attack success rate (ASR) of both harmful instructions and jailbreak instructions, while maintaining almost unchanged performance in downstream tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high cost of training-phase alignment methods like DPO and RLHF for LLM harmlessness. It proposes InferAligner, which separates harmlessness from helpfulness: the target model is fine-tuned only on downstream tasks, and during inference, safety steering vectors from a pre-aligned model guide its outputs toward harmlessness. Experiments on domain-specific (finance, medicine, math) and multimodal (LLaVA) models show significant reduction in attack success rate for harmful and jailbreak prompts while preserving downstream performance. This paper introduces a novel inference-time alignment approach but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 论文针对LLM无害性对齐中训练阶段方法（如DPO和RLHF）资源消耗大的问题，提出了InferAligner。该方法将无害性与有用性解耦：训练阶段仅增强目标模型的下游任务能力，推理阶段则利用从已对齐模型提取的安全导向向量引导目标模型输出无害内容。在金融、医学、数学等领域模型及多模态模型LLaVA上的实验表明，该方法显著降低了有害指令和越狱攻击的成功率，同时几乎不影响下游任务性能。这项工作提出了一种新颖的推理时对齐思路，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Rescorla-Wagner Steering of LLMs for Undesired Behaviors over Disproportionate Inappropriate Context
papers.short_title: RW-Steering of LLMs for Undesired Behaviors
papers.abstract: Incorporating external context can significantly enhance the response quality of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, real-world contexts often mix relevant information with disproportionate inappropriate content, posing reliability risks. How do LLMs process and prioritize mixed context? To study this, we introduce the Poisoned Context Testbed, pairing queries with real-world contexts containing relevant and inappropriate content. Inspired by associative learning in animals, we adapt the Rescorla-Wagner (RW) model from neuroscience to quantify how competing contextual signals influence LLM outputs. Our adapted model reveals a consistent behavioral pattern: LLMs exhibit a strong tendency to incorporate information that is less prevalent in the context. This susceptibility is harmful in real-world settings, where small amounts of inappropriate content can substantially degrade response quality. Empirical evaluations on our testbed further confirm this vulnerability. To tackle this, we introduce RW-Steering, a two-stage finetuning-based approach that enables the model to internally identify and ignore inappropriate signals. Unlike prior methods that rely on extensive supervision across diverse context mixtures, RW-Steering generalizes robustly across varying proportions of inappropriate content. Experiments show that our best fine-tuned model improves response quality by 39.8% and reverses the undesirable behavior curve, establishing RW-Steering as a robust, generalizable solution for improving LLM safety in real-world use.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to disproportionate inappropriate content in real-world contexts, where even small amounts can degrade response quality. It introduces RW-Steering, a two-stage finetuning approach inspired by the Rescorla-Wagner model, enabling the model to internally detect and ignore inappropriate signals without needing extensive mixed-context supervision. Evaluated on the Poisoned Context Testbed, the best model improves response quality by 39.8% and reverses the undesirable behavior curve, generalizing across varying proportions of inappropriate content. This work demonstrates how safety alignment can be fragile under context poisoning and offers a robust hardening method, directly contributing to the question of whether post-training alignment is easily bypassed or can be reinforced.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了LLM在真实世界上下文中对不成比例的不当内容的脆弱性，即使少量不当信息也会显著降低回复质量。受神经科学中Rescorla-Wagner模型启发，提出两阶段微调方法RW-Steering，使模型能内部检测并忽略不当信号，无需在多样混合上下文上过度监督。在Poisoned Context Testbed上的评估表明，最佳模型将回复质量提升39.8%，并逆转了不良行为曲线，在不同不当内容比例下均具有鲁棒性。该工作揭示了安全对齐在上下文投毒下的脆弱性，并提供了一个有效的加固方案，直接回应了后训练安全对齐是否真正鲁棒这一核心问题。

papers.title: DiffusionAttacker: Diffusion-Driven Prompt Manipulation for LLM Jailbreak
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are susceptible to generating harmful content when prompted with carefully crafted inputs, a vulnerability known as LLM jailbreaking. As LLMs become more powerful, studying jailbreak methods is critical to enhancing security and aligning models with human values. Traditionally, jailbreak techniques have relied on suffix addition or prompt templates, but these methods suffer from limited attack diversity. This paper introduces DiffusionAttacker, an end-to-end generative approach for jailbreak rewriting inspired by diffusion models. Our method employs a sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) text diffusion model as a generator, conditioning on the original prompt and guiding the denoising process with a novel attack loss. Unlike previous approaches that use autoregressive LLMs to generate jailbreak prompts, which limit the modification of already generated tokens and restrict the rewriting space, DiffusionAttacker utilizes a seq2seq diffusion model, allowing more flexible token modifications. This approach preserves the semantic content of the original prompt while producing harmful content. Additionally, we leverage the Gumbel-Softmax technique to make the sampling process from the diffusion model's output distribution differentiable, eliminating the need for iterative token search. Extensive experiments on Advbench and Harmbench demonstrate that DiffusionAttacker outperforms previous methods across various evaluation metrics, including attack success rate (ASR), fluency, and diversity.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to jailbreaking attacks, where adversarial prompts elicit harmful outputs. It proposes DiffusionAttacker, an end-to-end generative method that uses a seq2seq text diffusion model conditioned on the original prompt, guided by a novel attack loss and employing Gumbel-Softmax for differentiable sampling, enabling flexible prompt rewriting. Experiments on Advbench and Harmbench show superior attack success rate, fluency, and diversity compared to prior methods. By introducing a diffusion-based attack surface that bypasses safety measures, this work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training alignment, showing it can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在越狱攻击下生成有害内容的漏洞展开研究，提出DiffusionAttacker方法，采用基于扩散模型的端到端生成式重写策略，以原始提示为条件并利用攻击损失引导去噪过程，借助Gumbel-Softmax实现可微采样，从而灵活修改提示。在Advbench和Harmbench上的实验表明，该方法在攻击成功率、流畅性和多样性上均超越先前技术。该论文通过引入基于扩散模型的攻击面，成功绕过安全对齐，直接揭示了安全对齐模块的脆弱性，表明其易于被攻破。

papers.title: Data Advisor: Dynamic Data Curation for Safety Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.short_title: Data Advisor: Dynamic Safety Data Curation
papers.abstract: Data are crucial element in large language model (LLM) alignment. Recent studies have explored using LLMs for efficient data collection. However, LLM-generated data often suffers from quality issues, with underrepresented or absent aspects and low-quality datapoints. To address these problems, we propose Data Advisor, an enhanced LLM-based method for generating data that takes into account the characteristics of the desired dataset. Starting from a set of pre-defined principles in hand, Data Advisor monitors the status of the generated data, identifies weaknesses in the current dataset, and advises the next iteration of data generation accordingly. Data Advisor can be easily integrated into existing data generation methods to enhance data quality and coverage. Experiments on safety alignment of three representative LLMs (i.e., Mistral, Llama2, and Falcon) demonstrate the effectiveness of Data Advisor in enhancing model safety against various fine-grained safety issues without sacrificing model utility.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the issue of poor quality and incomplete coverage in LLM-generated safety alignment data. The paper proposes Data Advisor, which dynamically monitors weaknesses in the generated data and advises iterative generation to improve both quality and coverage. Experiments on Mistral, Llama2, and Falcon show that Data Advisor enhances model safety against fine-grained attacks without sacrificing utility. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM生成的安全对齐数据存在质量低下、覆盖不全的问题。提出Data Advisor方法，通过动态监测生成数据的薄弱点，指导迭代式数据生成，提升数据质量和覆盖面。在Mistral、Llama2和Falcon上的实验表明，Data Advisor能增强模型对各种细粒度安全问题的防御能力，同时不损害实用性。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐本身是否脆弱易被绕过。

papers.title: Token-Aware Editing of Internal Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: Intervening the internal activations of large language models (LLMs) provides an effective inference-time alignment approach to mitigate undesirable behaviors, such as generating erroneous or harmful content, thereby ensuring safe and reliable applications of LLMs. However, previous methods neglect the misalignment discrepancy among varied tokens, resulting in deviant alignment direction and inflexible editing strength. To address these issues, we propose a token-aware editing (TAE) approach to fully utilize token-level alignment information in the activation space, therefore realizing superior post-intervention performance. Specifically, a Mutual Information-guided Graph Aggregation (MIG) module first develops an MI-guided graph to exploit the tokens’ informative interaction for activation enrichment, thus improving alignment probing and facilitating intervention. Subsequently, Misalignment-aware Adaptive Intervention (MAI) comprehensively perceives the token-level misalignment degree from token representation and prediction to guide the adaptive adjustment of editing strength, thereby enhancing final alignment performance. Extensive experiments on three alignment capabilities demonstrate the efficacy of TAE, notably surpassing baseline by 25.8% on the primary metric of truthfulness with minimal cost.
papers.summary_en: Existing activation editing methods for LLM alignment ignore token-level misalignment discrepancies, causing suboptimal intervention. This paper proposes token-aware editing (TAE) with a mutual information-guided graph aggregation module to enrich token interactions, and a misalignment-aware adaptive intervention module to adjust editing strength per token. Evaluated on three alignment capabilities, TAE outperforms baselines by 25.8% on truthfulness with minimal overhead. This work advances alignment methodology through finer-grained editing but does not directly study the fragility or bypassing of safety alignment, focusing instead on improving alignment performance.
papers.summary_zh: 针对现有LLM激活编辑方法忽略token间对齐差异的问题，提出token感知编辑(TAE)，包含互信息引导的图聚合模块以丰富token交互，以及错位感知自适应干预模块按token调整编辑强度。在三个对齐能力上评估，TAE在真实性指标上超越基线25.8%且额外成本低。本文通过细粒度编辑提升了对齐方法，但未直接考察安全对齐的脆弱性，专注于改进对齐性能。

papers.title: Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding
papers.abstract: Despite extensive efforts to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and safety rules, jailbreak attacks that exploit certain vulnerabilities continuously emerge, highlighting the need to strengthen existing LLMs with additional safety properties to defend against these attacks. However, tuning large models has become increasingly resource-intensive and may have difficulty ensuring consistent performance. We introduce Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding (SSD), a lightweight decoding-time approach that equips LLMs with the desired safety property while accelerating inference. We assume that there exists a small language model that possesses the desired safety property. SSD integrates speculative sampling during decoding and leverages the match ratio between the small and composite models to quantify jailbreak risks. This enables SSD to dynamically switch between decoding schemes to prioritize utility or safety, to handle the challenge of different model capacities. The output token is then sampled from a new distribution that combines the distributions of both models. Experimental results show that SSD successfully equips the large model with the desired safety property, and also allows the model to remain helpful to benign queries. Furthermore, SSD accelerates the inference time, thanks to the speculative sampling design.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreak attacks that bypass safety alignment in large language models. It proposes Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding (SSD), a lightweight decoding-time method that uses a small safe model and speculative sampling to dynamically switch between utility- and safety-oriented decoding. Experiments show SSD effectively hardens the large model against jailbreaks while preserving helpfulness and accelerating inference. The work implies that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be strengthened by decoding-time interventions, though it does not analyze fragility mechanisms directly.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型中绕过安全对齐的越狱攻击问题，提出了一种轻量级解码时方法——推测性安全感知解码（SSD）。该方法利用小型安全模型和推测采样，在解码过程中动态切换注重有用性或安全性的策略。实验表明，SSD能有效增强大模型的安全性，同时保持对良性查询的有用性并加速推理。该工作暗示后训练安全对齐存在脆弱性，可通过解码时干预来加固，但并未直接分析脆弱性机制。

papers.title: mDPO: Conditional Preference Optimization for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Direct preference optimization (DPO) has shown to be an effective method for large language model (LLM) alignment. Recent works have attempted to apply DPO to multimodal scenarios but have found it challenging to achieve consistent improvement. Through a comparative experiment, we identify the unconditional preference problem in multimodal preference optimization, where the model overlooks the image condition. To address this problem, we propose mDPO, a multimodal DPO objective that prevents the over-prioritization of language-only preferences by also optimizing image preference. Moreover, we introduce a reward anchor that forces the reward to be positive for chosen responses, thereby avoiding the decrease in their likelihood—an intrinsic problem of relative preference optimization. Experiments on two multimodal LLMs of different sizes and three widely used benchmarks demonstrate that mDPO effectively addresses the unconditional preference problem in multimodal preference optimization and significantly improves model performance, particularly in reducing hallucination.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies the 'unconditional preference problem' in multimodal DPO, where models over-prioritize language priors and neglect image conditions, leading to suboptimal alignment. It proposes mDPO, a conditional preference optimization objective that also optimizes image preference and includes a reward anchor to prevent likelihood decrease for chosen responses. Evaluated on two multimodal LLMs and three benchmarks, mDPO significantly improves performance and reduces hallucination. This work highlights a fragility in directly applying standard alignment techniques to multimodal models, suggesting that post-training safety alignment may not be inherently robust across modalities without careful adaptation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文识别了多模态DPO中的“无条件偏好问题”，即模型过度依赖语言先验而忽略图像条件，导致对齐效果不稳定。提出mDPO，一种条件偏好优化目标，同时优化图像偏好，并引入奖励锚点以避免所选响应似然下降。在两种规模的多模态大语言模型和三个基准上评估，mDPO显著提升性能并减少幻觉。该研究揭示了标准对齐方法在多模态场景下的脆弱性，表明后训练安全对齐在跨模态时可能不直接鲁棒，需要针对性调整。

papers.title: STAR: SocioTechnical Approach to Red Teaming Language Models
papers.abstract: This research introduces STAR, a sociotechnical framework that improves on current best practices for red teaming safety of large language models. STAR makes two key contributions: it enhances steerability by generating parameterised instructions for human red teamers, leading to improved coverage of the risk surface. Parameterised instructions also provide more detailed insights into model failures at no increased cost. Second, STAR improves signal quality by matching demographics to assess harms for specific groups, resulting in more sensitive annotations. STAR further employs a novel step of arbitration to leverage diverse viewpoints and improve label reliability, treating disagreement not as noise but as a valuable contribution to signal quality.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses limitations in current red teaming practices for large language models, such as insufficient risk coverage and noisy annotations. It proposes STAR, a sociotechnical framework that uses parameterised instructions to steer human red teamers, demographic matching for harm annotation sensitivity, and an arbitration step to leverage diverse viewpoints for more reliable labels. The framework improves risk surface coverage and annotation signal quality, yielding more detailed failure insights at no additional cost. This paper advances safety evaluation methodology, which aids in detecting alignment vulnerabilities, but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了当前大语言模型安全红队测试中的局限性，如风险覆盖不足和标注噪声问题。它提出了STAR，一个社会技术框架，通过参数化指令引导红队成员，通过人口统计匹配提升伤害标注的敏感性，并通过仲裁步骤利用多元观点提高标签可靠性。该框架在无需额外成本的情况下改善了风险表面覆盖和标注信号质量，提供了更详细的失败洞察。该论文推进了安全评估方法论，有助于发现对齐脆弱性，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐本身是否鲁棒或易于被绕过。

papers.title: Foot-In-The-Door: A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs
papers.abstract: Ensuring AI safety is crucial as large language models become increasingly integrated into real-world applications. A key challenge is jailbreak, where adversarial prompts bypass built-in safeguards to elicit harmful disallowed outputs. Inspired by psychological foot-in-the-door principles, we introduce FITD, a novel multi-turn jailbreak method that leverages the phenomenon where minor initial commitments lower resistance to more significant or more unethical transgressions. Our approach progressively escalates the malicious intent of user queries through intermediate bridge prompts and aligns the model’s response by itself to induce toxic responses. Extensive experimental results on two jailbreak benchmarks demonstrate that FITD achieves an average attack success rate of 94% across seven widely used models, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, we provide an in-depth analysis of LLM self-corruption, highlighting vulnerabilities in current alignment strategies and emphasizing the risks inherent in multi-turn interactions. The code is available at https://github.com/Jinxiaolong1129/Foot-in-the-door-Jailbreak.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces FITD, a multi-turn jailbreak method that exploits the foot-in-the-door psychological effect to bypass LLM safety guards. It progressively escalates malicious queries via intermediate bridge prompts, allowing the model to self-corrupt and produce harmful outputs. Experiments show a 94% average attack success rate across seven models, surpassing existing methods. By exposing the vulnerability of aligned models to multi-turn interactions, this work demonstrates the fragility of current post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了FITD，一种多轮越狱方法，利用“登门槛”心理效应绕过大型语言模型的安全防护。该方法通过中间过渡提示逐步升级恶意查询，诱导模型自我破坏并生成有害响应。在七个主流模型上的实验显示，平均攻击成功率高达94%，优于现有方法。该研究揭示了多轮交互中安全对齐的脆弱性，强调了当前对齐策略的风险。

papers.title: Reimagining Safety Alignment with An Image
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel in diverse applications but face dual challenges: generating harmful content under jailbreak attacks and over-refusing benign queries due to rigid safety mechanisms. These issues severely affect the application of LLMs, especially in the medical and education fields. Existing approaches can be divided into three types: contrastive decoding, activation manipulation, and prompting strategies. However, all these approaches face challenges like inefficiency, fragility, or architectural constraints,ultimately failing to strike a balance between safety and usability. These problems are more obvious in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), especially in terms of heightened over-refusal in cross-modal tasks and new security risks arising from expanded attack surfaces. We propose Magic Image, an optimization-driven visual prompt framework that enhances security and reduces over-refusal at the same time. The Magic Image is optimized using gradients derived from harmful/benign training samples. Using the magic image can modify the model’s original safety alignment, maintaining robust safety while reducing unnecessary denials. Experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in preserving model performance and improving safety-responsiveness balance across datasets, including unseen data, offering a practical solution for reliable MLLM deployment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of balancing harmful output prevention and over-refusal in LLMs and MLLMs. It proposes Magic Image, an optimization-driven visual prompt framework that fine-tunes safety alignment using gradients from harmful and benign samples. Evaluations show that Magic Image effectively reduces over-refusal while maintaining strong safety across multiple datasets, including unseen data. By introducing a robust alignment tuning method, this paper directly tackles the fragility of existing safety mechanisms, demonstrating a practical approach to make alignment more resilient.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大规模语言模型和多模态模型在安全对齐中面临的有害内容生成与过度拒绝的两难问题。提出了一种名为Magic Image的优化驱动视觉提示框架，通过利用有害与良性样本的梯度来调整模型的安全对齐。实验表明，该方法在多个数据集上有效减少了过度拒绝，同时保持了安全性，并泛化到未见过数据。通过提供一种鲁棒的对齐调优方法，本文直接解决了现有安全对齐机制的脆弱性问题，为提升对齐的稳健性提供了一种实用方案。

papers.title: Unveiling the Implicit Toxicity in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The open-endedness of large language models (LLMs) combined with their impressive capabilities may lead to new safety issues when being exploited for malicious use. While recent studies primarily focus on probing toxic outputs that can be easily detected with existing toxicity classifiers, we show that LLMs can generate diverse implicit toxic outputs that are exceptionally difficult to detect via simply zero-shot prompting. Moreover, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) based attacking method to further induce the implicit toxicity in LLMs. Specifically, we optimize the language model with a reward that prefers implicit toxic outputs to explicit toxic and non-toxic ones. Experiments on five widely-adopted toxicity classifiers demonstrate that the attack success rate can be significantly improved through RL fine-tuning. For instance, the RL-finetuned LLaMA-13B model achieves an attack success rate of 90.04% on BAD and 62.85% on Davinci003. Our findings suggest that LLMs pose a significant threat in generating undetectable implicit toxic outputs. We further show that fine-tuning toxicity classifiers on the annotated examples from our attacking method can effectively enhance their ability to detect LLM-generated implicit toxic language. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/thu-coai/Implicit-Toxicity.
papers.summary_en: This paper reveals that large language models can generate implicit toxic content that easily evades standard toxicity classifiers. To exploit this, the authors propose a reinforcement learning (RL) attack that fine-tunes the model to favor implicit toxic outputs over explicit ones. Evaluated on five classifiers, the RL-finetuned LLaMA-13B achieves an attack success rate of 90.04% on BAD, demonstrating a severe vulnerability. This work provides clear evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be bypassed by a simple fine-tuning attack that induces subtle, hard-to-detect toxicity.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了大语言模型能够生成难以被标准毒性分类器检测的隐性有害内容。为利用这一漏洞，作者提出了一种基于强化学习（RL）的攻击方法，通过微调模型使其更倾向于生成隐性有毒输出而非显性有毒或无毒输出。在五个毒性分类器上的评估表明，经RL微调的LLaMA-13B在BAD数据集上的攻击成功率高达90.04%，暴露出严重脆弱性。该工作明确显示后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，可被简单的微调攻击绕过，诱导产生隐蔽的、难以检测的毒性内容。

papers.title: ToViLaG: Your Visual-Language Generative Model is Also An Evildoer
papers.abstract: Warning: this paper includes model outputs showing offensive content. Recent large-scale Visual-Language Generative Models (VLGMs) have achieved unprecedented improvement in multimodal image/text generation. However, these models might also generate toxic content, e.g., offensive text and pornography images, raising significant ethical risks. Despite exhaustive studies on toxic degeneration of language models, this problem remains largely unexplored within the context of visual-language generation. This work delves into the propensity for toxicity generation and susceptibility to toxic data across various VLGMs. For this purpose, we built ToViLaG, a dataset comprising 32K co-toxic/mono-toxic text-image pairs and 1K innocuous but evocative text that tends to stimulate toxicity. Furthermore, we propose WInToRe, a novel toxicity metric tailored to visual-language generation, which theoretically reflects different aspects of toxicity considering both input and output. On such a basis, we benchmarked the toxicity of a diverse spectrum of VLGMs and discovered that some models do more evil than expected while some are more vulnerable to infection, underscoring the necessity of VLGMs detoxification. Therefore, we develop an innovative bottleneck-based detoxification method. Our method could reduce toxicity while maintaining comparable generation quality, providing a promising initial solution to this line of research.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the underexplored issue of toxicity generation in visual-language generative models (VLGMs), examining both their tendency to produce toxic outputs and their vulnerability to toxic inputs. The authors constructed the ToViLaG dataset containing 32K toxic text-image pairs and 1K provocative prompts, and designed the WInToRe metric to quantify toxicity in multimodal generation. Benchmarking a range of VLGMs revealed unexpected toxicity levels and infection susceptibility, prompting the development of a bottleneck-based detoxification method that reduces toxicity without degrading generation quality. This work exposes a new multimodal attack surface, demonstrating that safety alignment in language models can be fragile and circumvented when visual inputs are involved, thereby contributing evidence to the fragility thesis in post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了视觉语言生成模型（VLGMs）中尚未充分探索的毒性生成问题，既考察了模型产生毒性输出的倾向，也考察了其对毒性输入的脆弱性。作者构建了包含32K有毒图文对和1K诱导性提示的ToViLaG数据集，并设计了WInToRe指标来量化多模态生成中的毒性。对多种VLGMs的基准测试揭示了意外的毒性水平和感染易感性，进而提出了一种基于瓶颈层的去毒方法，在降低毒性的同时保持生成质量。该工作揭示了一种新的多模态攻击面，表明语言模型的安全对齐在引入视觉输入时可能脆弱且易被绕过，为对齐的脆弱性论点提供了实证支撑。

papers.title: Re-Align: Aligning Vision Language Models via Retrieval-Augmented Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: The emergence of large Vision Language Models (VLMs) has broadened the scope and capabilities of single-modal Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating visual modalities, thereby unlocking transformative cross-modal applications in a variety of real-world scenarios. Despite their impressive performance, VLMs are prone to significant hallucinations, particularly in the form of cross-modal inconsistencies. Building on the success of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in aligning LLMs, recent advancements have focused on applying direct preference optimization (DPO) on carefully curated datasets to mitigate these issues. Yet, such approaches typically introduce preference signals in a brute-force manner, neglecting the crucial role of visual information in the alignment process. In this paper, we introduce Re-Align, a novel alignment framework that leverages image retrieval to construct a dual-preference dataset, effectively incorporating both textual and visual preference signals. We further introduce rDPO, an extension of the standard direct preference optimization that incorporates an additional visual preference objective during fine-tuning. Our experimental results demonstrate that Re-Align not only mitigates hallucinations more effectively than previous methods but also yields significant performance gains in general visual question-answering (VQA) tasks. Moreover, we show that Re-Align maintains robustness and scalability across a wide range of VLM sizes and architectures. This work represents a significant step forward in aligning multimodal LLMs, paving the way for more reliable and effective cross-modal applications. We release all the code in https://github.com/taco-group/Re-Align.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses hallucination and cross-modal inconsistency in Vision Language Models (VLMs). It proposes Re-Align, a framework that leverages image retrieval to create a dual-preference dataset and introduces rDPO, an extension of direct preference optimization with a visual preference objective. Experiments demonstrate that Re-Align significantly reduces hallucinations and improves general VQA performance, while maintaining robustness across different VLM sizes and architectures. This work advances alignment techniques for multimodal models but does not directly study the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉语言模型（VLM）中的幻觉和跨模态不一致问题，提出了一种名为Re-Align的对齐框架，利用图像检索构建双偏好数据集，并引入rDPO，即在标准直接偏好优化中增加视觉偏好目标。实验表明，Re-Align相比先前方法更有效地减轻了幻觉，并在通用视觉问答任务中取得了显著性能提升，且在不同VLM规模和架构上保持鲁棒性。该研究改进了多模态模型的对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Distract Large Language Models for Automatic Jailbreak Attack
papers.abstract: Extensive efforts have been made before the public release of Large language models (LLMs) to align their behaviors with human values. However, even meticulously aligned LLMs remain vulnerable to malicious manipulations such as jailbreaking, leading to unintended behaviors. In this work, we propose a novel black-box jailbreak framework for automated red teaming of LLMs. We designed malicious content concealing and memory reframing with an iterative optimization algorithm to jailbreak LLMs, motivated by the research about the distractibility and over-confidence phenomenon of LLMs. Extensive experiments of jailbreaking both open-source and proprietary LLMs demonstrate the superiority of our framework in terms of effectiveness, scalability and transferability. We also evaluate the effectiveness of existing jailbreak defense methods against our attack and highlight the crucial need to develop more effective and practical defense strategies.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of aligned LLMs to jailbreak attacks. It proposes a black-box framework that conceals malicious content and reframes memory through iterative optimization, exploiting LLMs' distractibility and over-confidence. Extensive experiments on open-source and proprietary LLMs demonstrate superior effectiveness, scalability, and transferability, while existing defenses prove insufficient. This work provides clear evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, revealing a new attack surface that can bypass alignment, thus emphasizing the urgent need for stronger defenses.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型安全对齐仍存在越狱攻击脆弱性的问题。提出了一种黑盒越狱框架，通过恶意内容隐藏与记忆重构，结合迭代优化，利用模型的分心趋势与过度自信现象。在开源及商用模型上的实验表明，该方法在有效性、可扩展性和迁移性方面均具优势，且现有防御不足。该工作直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，证实分心性可作为新攻击面绕过对齐，凸显了发展更有效防御的迫切性。

papers.title: Automating Steering for Safe Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has unlocked powerful cross-modal reasoning abilities, but also raised new safety concerns, particularly when faced with adversarial multimodal inputs. To improve the safety of MLLMs during inference, we introduce a modular and adaptive inference-time intervention technology, AutoSteer, without requiring any fine-tuning of the underlying model. AutoSteer incorporates three core components: (1) a novel Safety Awareness Score (SAS) that automatically identifies the most safety-relevant distinctions among the model's internal layers; (2) an adaptive safety prober trained to estimate the likelihood of toxic outputs from intermediate representations; and (3) a lightweight Refusal Head that selectively intervenes to modulate generation when safety risks are detected. Experiments on LLaVA-OV and Chameleon across diverse safety-critical benchmarks demonstrate that AutoSteer significantly reduces the Attack Success Rate (ASR) for textual, visual, and cross-modal threats, while maintaining general abilities. These findings position AutoSteer as a practical, interpretable, and effective framework for safer deployment of multimodal AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses safety vulnerabilities in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) when exposed to adversarial multimodal inputs. It proposes AutoSteer, a modular, inference-time intervention that uses a Safety Awareness Score, an adaptive safety prober, and a lightweight Refusal Head to detect and prevent toxic outputs without fine-tuning the underlying model. Evaluated on LLaVA-OV and Chameleon across safety benchmarks, AutoSteer significantly reduces Attack Success Rates for textual, visual, and cross-modal threats while preserving general capabilities. The work strengthens post-training safety alignment by adding an inference-time defense layer, though it does not directly investigate the intrinsic fragility of alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在对抗性多模态输入下的安全漏洞问题展开研究。提出AutoSteer，一种模块化的推理时干预方法，利用安全感知评分、自适应安全探测器及轻量级拒绝头，无需微调模型即可检测并阻止有害输出。在LLaVA-OV和Chameleon上的实验表明，AutoSteer能显著降低文本、视觉和跨模态攻击的成功率，同时保持通用能力。该工作通过添加推理时防御层增强了训练后安全对齐，但并未直接探讨对齐的内在脆弱性。

papers.title: reWordBench: Benchmarking and Improving the Robustness of Reward Models with Transformed Inputs
papers.abstract: Reward models have become a staple in modern NLP, serving as not only a scalable text evaluator, but also an indispensable component in many alignment recipes and inference-time algorithms. However, while recent reward models increase performance on standard benchmarks, this may partly be due to overfitting effects, which would confound an understanding of their true capability. In this work, we scrutinize the robustness of reward models and the extent of such overfitting. We build reWordBench, which systematically transforms reward model inputs in meaning- or ranking-preserving ways. We show that state-of-the-art reward models suffer from substantial performance degradation even with minor input transformations, sometimes dropping to significantly below-random accuracy, suggesting brittleness. To improve reward model robustness, we propose to explicitly train them to assign similar scores to paraphrases, and find that this approach also improves robustness to other distinct kinds of transformations. For example, our robust reward model reduces such degradation by roughly half for the Chat Hard subset in RewardBench. Furthermore, when used in alignment, our robust reward models demonstrate better utility and lead to higher-quality outputs, winning in up to 59% of instances against a standardly trained RM.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the robustness of reward models, finding that they overfit and degrade severely under minor, meaning-preserving input transformations. It introduces reWordBench, a benchmark that systematically transforms inputs, and proposes training on paraphrases to improve robustness. Evaluation shows that state-of-the-art reward models suffer substantial performance drops, sometimes below random, while the robust training method reduces degradation by about half on RewardBench's Chat Hard subset. By exposing the brittleness of reward models, this work directly demonstrates a fragility in a core alignment component, suggesting that post-training safety alignment can be superficial and easily compromised.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了奖励模型的鲁棒性，发现它们存在过拟合，在轻微的、保持语义的输入变换下性能严重下降。作者构建了 reWordBench，系统性变换输入，并提议通过训练奖励模型对释义赋予相似分数来提升鲁棒性。评估显示，最先进的奖励模型性能大幅下降，有时甚至低于随机水平，而鲁棒训练方法在 RewardBench 的 Chat Hard 子集上将性能下降减少了约一半。该工作揭示了奖励模型的脆弱性，直接表明了核心对齐组件的鲁棒性不足，暗示事后安全对齐可能是表面的且易被绕过。

papers.title: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly surpassing human knowledge in many domains. While improving these models traditionally relies on costly human data, recent self-rewarding mechanisms have shown that LLMs can improve by judging their own responses instead of relying on human labelers. However, existing methods have primarily focused on improving model responses rather than judgment capabilities, resulting in rapid saturation during iterative training. To address this issue, we introduce a novel Meta-Rewarding step to the self-improvement process, where the model judges its own judgements and uses that feedback to refine its judgment skills. Surprisingly, this unsupervised approach improves the model’s ability to judge and follow instructions, as demonstrated by a win rate improvement of Llama-3-8B-Instruct from 22.9% to 39.4% on AlpacaEval 2, and 20.6% to 29.1% on Arena-Hard. These results strongly suggest the potential for self-improving models without human supervision.
papers.summary_en: Conventional self-improvement methods for LLMs saturate because they only improve response quality, neglecting judgment skills. This paper introduces a Meta-Rewarding step where the model judges its own judgments to refine its evaluation capabilities. Evaluated on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, Llama-3-8B-Instruct with Meta-Rewarding improves win rate from 22.9% to 39.4% and 20.6% to 29.1%, respectively. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有LLM自我改进方法因仅提升回答质量而饱和，忽视判断能力。本文提出元奖励步骤，让模型评判自身判断以优化评价能力。在AlpacaEval 2和Arena-Hard上评估，使用Meta-Rewarding的Llama-3-8B-Instruct胜率分别从22.9%提升至39.4%，20.6%提升至29.1%。本文推进了无需人工监督的对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或稳健性。

papers.title: MrGuard: A Multilingual Reasoning Guardrail for Universal LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are susceptible to adversarial attacks such as jailbreaking, which can elicit harmful or unsafe behaviors. This vulnerability is exacerbated in multilingual settings, where multilingual safety-aligned data is often limited. Thus, developing a guardrail capable of detecting and filtering unsafe content across diverse languages is critical for deploying LLMs in real-world applications. In this work, we introduce a multilingual guardrail with reasoning for prompt classification. Our method consists of: (1) synthetic multilingual data generation incorporating culturally and linguistically nuanced variants, (2) supervised fine-tuning, and (3) a curriculum-based Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework that further improves performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our multilingual guardrail, MrGuard, consistently outperforms recent baselines across both in-domain and out-of-domain languages by more than 15%. We also evaluate MrGuard's robustness to multilingual variations, such as code-switching and low-resource language distractors in the prompt, and demonstrate that it preserves safety judgments under these challenging conditions. The multilingual reasoning capability of our guardrail enables it to generate explanations, which are particularly useful for understanding language-specific risks and ambiguities in multilingual content moderation.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to jailbreaking in multilingual settings, where safety alignment often fails due to limited multilingual safety data. It proposes MrGuard, a multilingual guardrail that combines synthetic data generation with cultural nuances, supervised fine-tuning, and curriculum-based GRPO to classify and filter unsafe prompts. Experiments show MrGuard outperforms baselines by over 15% across in-domain and out-of-domain languages, and it remains robust to code-switching and low-resource language distractors. This paper strengthens post-training safety alignment by providing a hardening method that mitigates bypass attacks in multilingual contexts, demonstrating that alignment fragility can be reduced with targeted guardrails.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在多语言环境下易受越狱攻击的问题，由于多语言安全对齐数据稀缺，模型安全性尤为脆弱。提出MrGuard，一种多语言安全护栏，通过生成融入文化细微差别的合成数据、监督微调和基于课程的GRPO强化学习，对提示词进行安全分类。实验表明，MrGuard在域内和域外语言上均比基线方法提升超过15%，且对代码切换和低资源语言干扰保持鲁棒。本研究通过提供一种多语言安全加固方法，减轻了对齐在面对多语言越狱时的脆弱性，表明定向护栏可有效提升对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Despite the efficacy of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) in aligning Large Language Models (LLMs), reward hacking remains a pivotal challenge. This issue emerges when LLMs excessively reduce the probability of rejected completions to achieve high rewards, without genuinely meeting their intended goals. As a result, this leads to overly lengthy generation lacking diversity, as well as catastrophic forgetting of knowledge. We investigate the underlying reason behind this issue, which is representation redundancy caused by neuron collapse in the parameter space. Hence, we propose a novel Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization (RoPO) algorithm, which implicitly constrains the output layer logits with the KL divergence inherited from DPO and explicitly constrains the intermediate hidden states by fine-tuning on a multi-granularity orthogonal matrix. This design prevents the policy model from deviating too far from the reference model, thereby retaining the knowledge and expressive capabilities acquired during pre-training and SFT stages. Our RoPO achieves up to a 3.27-point improvement on AlpacaEval 2, and surpasses the best baseline by 6.2 to 7.5 points on MT-Bench with merely 0.015% of the trainable parameters, demonstrating its effectiveness in alleviating the reward hacking problem of DPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses reward hacking in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), where language models excessively reduce rejected completion probabilities, leading to overly lengthy outputs, reduced diversity, and catastrophic forgetting due to representation redundancy from neuron collapse. It proposes Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization (RoPO), which implicitly constrains output logits via KL divergence and explicitly constrains hidden states by fine-tuning a multi-granularity orthogonal matrix, preventing the policy model from deviating far from the reference model. RoPO achieves up to a 3.27-point improvement on AlpacaEval 2 and outperforms the best baseline by 6.2–7.5 points on MT-Bench while updating only 0.015% of parameters. This work advances alignment methodology by mitigating a key failure mode, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of safety alignment against adversarial attacks or bypass strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决直接偏好优化（DPO）中的奖励黑客问题，即模型过度降低被拒绝补全的概率，导致生成长度失控、多样性不足及灾难性遗忘，其根源在于参数空间神经元坍缩引起的表示冗余。提出权重旋转偏好优化（RoPO）方法，通过继承DPO的KL散度隐式约束输出logits，并通过多粒度正交矩阵微调显式约束中间隐藏状态，防止策略模型偏离参考模型。在AlpacaEval 2上取得最高3.27分的提升，在MT-Bench上仅以0.015%的可训练参数即超越最佳基线6.2至7.5分。该工作改进了对齐方法以缓解已知的失效模式，但并未直接探究安全对齐在面对对抗攻击或绕过策略时的脆弱性。

papers.title: MUSE: MCTS-Driven Red Teaming Framework for Enhanced Multi-Turn Dialogue Safety in Large Language Models
papers.short_title: MUSE: Red Teaming for Multi-Turn Dialogue Safety
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become widely adopted, ensuring their alignment with human values is crucial to prevent jailbreaks where adversaries manipulate models to produce harmful content. While most defenses target single-turn attacks, real-world usage often involves multi-turn dialogues, exposing models to attacks that exploit conversational context to bypass safety measures. We introduce MUSE, a comprehensive framework tackling multi-turn jailbreaks from both attack and defense angles. For attacks, we propose MUSE-A, a method that uses frame semantics and heuristic tree search to explore diverse semantic trajectories. For defense, we present MUSE-D, a fine-grained safety alignment approach that intervenes early in dialogues to reduce vulnerabilities. Extensive experiments on various models show that MUSE effectively identifies and mitigates multi-turn vulnerabilities. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MUSE-75F7.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs, where adversaries exploit conversational context to bypass safety mechanisms. It proposes MUSE, a framework comprising an attack method (MUSE-A) that uses frame semantics and Monte Carlo tree search to generate diverse harmful trajectories, and a defense method (MUSE-D) using fine-grained early-intervention fine-tuning. Experiments on multiple models show MUSE effectively identifies and mitigates multi-turn vulnerabilities. The work highlights a fragility in post-training alignment: defenses designed for single-turn interactions fail under multi-turn probing, and the proposed defense exemplifies a targeted hardening approach against such context-based attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型中的多轮越狱攻击问题，攻击者利用对话上下文绕过安全机制。提出MUSE框架，包括使用框架语义和蒙特卡洛树搜索生成多样化有害轨迹的攻击方法MUSE-A，以及基于细粒度早期干预微调的防御方法MUSE-D。在多个模型上的实验表明，MUSE能够有效识别并缓解多轮对话中的漏洞。该工作揭示了后训练对齐的脆弱性：针对单轮交互设计的防御在多轮探测下失效，而所提出的防御展示了一种针对此类基于上下文攻击的定向加固方法。

papers.title: CoSafe: Evaluating Large Language Model Safety in Multi-Turn Dialogue Coreference
papers.short_title: CoSafe: LLM Safety in Coreference Dialogue
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) constantly evolve, ensuring their safety remains a critical research issue. Previous red teaming approaches for LLM safety have primarily focused on single prompt attacks or goal hijacking. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to study LLM safety in multi-turn dialogue coreference. We created a dataset of 1,400 questions across 14 categories, each featuring multi-turn coreference safety attacks. We then conducted detailed evaluations on five widely used open-source LLMs. The results indicated that under multi-turn coreference safety attacks, the highest attack success rate was 56% with the LLaMA2-Chat-7b model, while the lowest was 13.9% with the Mistral-7B-Instruct model. These findings highlight the safety vulnerabilities in LLMs during dialogue coreference interactions.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates a novel attack surface: LLM safety in multi-turn dialogue coreference. It introduces a dataset of 1,400 questions across 14 categories, each constructing multi-turn coreference safety attacks. Evaluating five open-source LLMs, it finds attack success rates from 13.9% (Mistral-7B-Instruct) to 56% (LLaMA2-Chat-7b), highlighting significant vulnerabilities. These results directly demonstrate fragility in post-training safety alignment, as coreference manipulation can bypass safety measures.
papers.summary_zh: 本文首次研究了多轮对话指代中的LLM安全性，揭示了通过指代绕过安全对齐的新攻击面。通过构建包含14类共1400个问题的多轮指代攻击数据集，并在五个开源LLM上评估，发现攻击成功率从13.9%（Mistral-7B-Instruct）到56%（LLaMA2-Chat-7b）不等，暴露出严重安全漏洞。这些结果直接表明训练后安全对齐是脆弱的，指代操纵能够轻易绕过安全机制。

papers.title: ToolSafety: A Comprehensive Dataset for Enhancing Safety in LLM-Based Agent Tool Invocations
papers.abstract: LLMs are evolving into assistants that leverage tools, significantly expanding their capabilities but also introducing critical safety risks. Current models exhibit notable vulnerabilities, particularly in maintaining safety during multi-step tool interactions and in scenarios involving indirect harm. This paper introduces ToolSafety, a safety fine-tuning dataset designed to address these limitations. ToolSafety comprises 5,668 direct harm samples, 4,311 indirect harm samples, and 4,311 multi-step samples. Key features include support for multi-step safety through synthesized trajectories and realistic, context-aware sample generation. We fine-tuned LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct using ToolSafety. Experimental results demonstrate that these models effectively maintain safety in multi-step and indirect harm scenarios. Further analysis into superficial alignment across different decoding strategies, languages, and jailbreak prompts indicates that while some risks persist, the issue is less severe than in multi-step settings. Overall, our approach significantly improves safety across various scenarios with small impact on helpfulness, positioning ToolSafety as a valuable resource for building safer tool-using AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses safety vulnerabilities in LLM-based agents that use tools, particularly in multi-step interactions and indirect harm scenarios. It proposes ToolSafety, a comprehensive safety fine-tuning dataset with synthesized trajectories for multi-step and indirect harm, and fine-tunes open-source LLMs on it. Fine-tuned models on LLaMA3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B maintain safety in complex scenarios with small helpfulness impact, and analysis of superficial alignment shows some residual risks. This paper advances safety alignment methodology for tool-using agents but does not directly investigate whether post-training alignment is fundamentally fragile or can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对使用工具的LLM智能体在多步交互和间接伤害场景中的安全漏洞。提出ToolSafety,一个包含多步和间接伤害合成轨迹的安全微调数据集,并对开源LLM进行微调。微调后的模型在复杂场景下保持安全性,且对有用性影响小,此外表面对齐分析表明仍存在一些残余风险。本文推进了工具使用智能体的安全对齐方法,但未直接研究后训练对齐是否本质脆弱、易被绕过。

papers.title: Walking in Others' Shoes: How Perspective-Taking Guides Large Language Models in Reducing Toxicity and Bias
papers.abstract: The common toxicity and societal bias in contents generated by large language models (LLMs) necessitate strategies to reduce harm. Present solutions often demand white-box access to the model or substantial training, which is impractical for cutting-edge commercial LLMs. Moreover, prevailing prompting methods depend on external tool feedback and fail to simultaneously lessen toxicity and bias. Motivated by social psychology principles, we propose a novel strategy named perspective-taking prompting (PeT) that inspires LLMs to integrate diverse human perspectives and self-regulate their responses. This self-correction mechanism can significantly diminish toxicity (up to 89%) and bias (up to 73%) in LLMs’ responses. Rigorous evaluations and ablation studies are conducted on two commercial LLMs (ChatGPT and GLM) and three open-source LLMs, revealing PeT’s superiority in producing less harmful responses, outperforming five strong baselines.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of toxicity and societal bias in LLM-generated content, for which existing solutions often require model access or substantial training and fail to tackle both issues simultaneously. It proposes perspective-taking prompting (PeT), a self-correction mechanism that guides LLMs to adopt diverse human perspectives, thereby reducing harmful outputs without model modification. Evaluated on two commercial (ChatGPT, GLM) and three open-source LLMs, PeT reduces toxicity by up to 89% and bias by up to 73%, outperforming five strong prompting baselines. While PeT introduces an effective alignment-enhancing technique, the paper does not investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment, such as whether these safety gains can be easily reversed or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大型语言模型生成内容中常见的毒性和社会偏见问题，现有方案通常需要模型白盒访问或大量训练，且难以同时减少毒性和偏见。提出了一种受社会心理学启发的方法——换位思考提示（PeT），通过引导模型整合多元人类视角并自我调节，实现自我纠正机制，从而显著减少有害输出。在ChatGPT、GLM等两款商业模型及三款开源模型上评估，PeT最多可将毒性降低89%、偏见降低73%，并优于五个强基线方法。虽然PeT提供了一种增强安全对齐的有效技术，但本文并未探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性，例如这些安全提升是否容易被推翻或绕过。

papers.title: Preference-Guided Reflective Sampling for Aligning Language Models
papers.abstract: Iterative data generation and model re-training can effectively align large language models (LLMs) to human preferences. The process of data sampling is crucial, as it significantly influences the success of policy improvement. Repeated random sampling is a widely used method that independently queries the model multiple times to generate outputs. In this work, we propose a more effective sampling method, named Preference-Guided Reflective Sampling (PRS). Unlike random sampling, PRS employs a tree-based generation framework to enable more efficient sampling. It leverages adaptive self-refinement techniques to better explore the sampling space. By specifying user preferences in natural language, PRS can further optimize response generation according to these preferences. As a result, PRS can align models to diverse user preferences. Our experiments demonstrate that PRS generates higher-quality responses with significantly higher rewards. On AlpacaEval and Arena-Hard, PRS substantially outperforms repeated random sampling in best-of-N sampling. Moreover, PRS shows strong performance when applied in iterative offline RL training.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the crucial role of data sampling in aligning large language models to human preferences, identifying limitations of repeated random sampling. It proposes Preference-Guided Reflective Sampling (PRS), a tree-based generation approach that uses adaptive self-refinement and natural language user preferences to efficiently explore the sampling space and tailor responses. Evaluations on AlpacaEval and Arena-Hard show PRS significantly outperforms random sampling in best-of-N settings, yielding higher rewards and quality, and also performs well in iterative offline RL training. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型人类偏好对齐中数据采样的关键作用，指出重复随机采样的局限。提出偏好引导的反思采样（PRS），一种树状生成框架，结合自适应自我修正和自然语言用户偏好，更高效地探索采样空间并定制回复。在 AlpacaEval 和 Arena-Hard 上的实验表明，PRS 在 best-of-N 采样中显著优于随机采样，获得更高奖励和回复质量，并在迭代离线 RL 训练中表现强劲。该工作推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: BPO: Staying Close to the Behavior LLM Creates Better Online LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Direct alignment from preferences (DAP) has emerged as a promising paradigm for aligning large language models (LLMs) to human desiderata from pre-collected, offline preference datasets. While recent studies indicate that existing offline DAP methods can directly benefit from online training samples, we highlight the need to develop specific online DAP algorithms to fully harness the power of online training. Specifically, we identify that the learned LLM should adhere to the proximity of the behavior LLM, which collects the training samples. To this end, we propose online Preference Optimization in proximity to the Behavior LLM (BPO), emphasizing the importance of constructing a proper trust region for LLM alignment.We conduct extensive experiments to validate the effectiveness and applicability of our approach by integrating it with various DAP methods, resulting in significant performance improvements across a wide range of tasks when training with the same amount of preference data. Even when only introducing one additional data collection phase, our online BPO improves its offline DAP baseline from 72.0% to 80.2% on TL;DR and from 82.2% to 89.1% on Anthropic Helpfulness in terms of win rate against human reference text.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the issue that applying offline direct alignment methods online can cause the learned LLM to deviate from the behavior policy, leading to suboptimal alignment. It proposes BPO, an online preference optimization method that enforces a trust region around the behavior LLM to maintain proximity. Integrated with various direct alignment methods, BPO achieves significant win-rate improvements on tasks like TL;DR summarization (from 72.0% to 80.2%) and Anthropic Helpfulness (from 82.2% to 89.1%). This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对直接将离线直接对齐方法用于在线场景可能导致模型偏离行为策略、降低对齐效果的问题。提出BPO算法，通过在行为LLM附近构建信任域来约束学习策略保持邻近，从而优化在线偏好对齐。将BPO与多种直接对齐方法结合，在TL;DR摘要和Anthropic有用性等任务上显著提升胜率（TL;DR从72.0%到80.2%）。本文推动了在线对齐方法学，但未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Reshaping Representation Space to Balance the Safety and Over-rejection in Large Audio Language Models
papers.short_title: Reshaping Repr. Space for Safe LALMs
papers.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have extended the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by enabling audio-based human interactions. However, recent research has revealed that LALMs remain vulnerable to harmful queries due to insufficient safety-alignment. Despite advances in defence measures for text and vision LLMs, effective safety-alignment strategies and audio-safety dataset specifically targeting LALMs are notably absent. Meanwhile defence measures based on Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT) struggle to address safety improvement while avoiding over-rejection issues, significantly compromising helpfulness. In this work, we propose an unsupervised safety-fine-tuning strategy as remedy that reshapes model's representation space to enhance existing LALMs safety-alignment while balancing the risk of over-rejection. Our experiments, conducted across three generations of Qwen LALMs, demonstrate that our approach significantly improves LALMs safety under three modality input conditions (audio-text, text-only, and audio-only) while increasing over-rejection rate by only 0.88% on average. Warning: this paper contains harmful examples.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) to harmful queries and the over-rejection problem caused by current defense measures like supervised fine-tuning. It proposes an unsupervised safety-fine-tuning strategy that reshapes the model's representation space to balance safety and helpfulness. Experiments on three Qwen LALM generations across audio-text, text-only, and audio-only modalities show significant safety improvement with an average over-rejection increase of only 0.88%. This work provides a hardening method that improves the robustness of safety alignment in LALMs, directly tackling the fragility issue by reshaping internal representations to reduce over-rejection.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大型音频语言模型（LALMs）对有害查询的脆弱性以及现有防御措施（如监督微调）导致的过度拒绝问题。提出了一种无监督安全微调策略，通过重塑模型的表示空间来平衡安全性和有用性。在三个世代的Qwen LALM上，针对音频-文本、纯文本和纯音频三种模态的实验表明，安全性显著提升，而过拒绝率平均仅增加0.88%。这项工作提供了一种加固方法，通过重塑内部表示来减少过度拒绝，从而直接应对安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: How Does DPO Reduce Toxicity? A Mechanistic Neuron-Level Analysis
papers.abstract: Safety fine-tuning algorithms reduce harmful outputs in language models, yet their mechanisms remain under-explored. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a popular choice of algorithm, but prior explanations, attributing its effects solely to dampened toxic neurons in the MLP layers, are incomplete. In this study, we analyse four language models (Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B, Mistral-7B, GPT-2-Medium) and show that toxic neurons only account for 2.5% to 24% of DPO's effects across models. Instead, DPO balances distributed activation shifts across all MLP neurons to create a net toxicity reduction. We attribute this reduction to four neuron groups, two aligned with reducing toxicity and two promoting anti-toxicity, whose combined effects replicate DPO across models. To further validate this understanding, we develop an activation editing method mimicking DPO through distributed shifts along a toxicity representation. This method outperforms DPO in reducing toxicity while preserving perplexity, without requiring any weight updates. Our work provides a mechanistic understanding of DPO and introduces an efficient, tuning-free alternative for safety fine-tuning.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of mechanistic understanding of how Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) reduces toxicity in language models. It performs a neuron-level analysis across four models, revealing that toxic neurons only partially account for the effect and that DPO instead relies on distributed activation shifts across all MLP neurons, involving four functional neuron groups. The analysis is validated by developing an activation editing method that mimics DPO's distributed shifts, achieving better toxicity reduction than DPO while maintaining perplexity without weight updates. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question; it provides mechanistic grounding that could inform robustness studies.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接偏好优化（DPO）如何降低语言模型毒性的机制缺乏理解的问题展开研究。通过对四个模型的神经元层面分析，发现毒性神经元仅部分解释DPO的效果，DPO实际依赖所有MLP神经元的分布式激活偏移，并涉及四类功能性神经元组。为验证这一理解，开发了一种模拟DPO分布式偏移的激活编辑方法，在保持困惑度的同时实现优于DPO的毒性降低，且无需权重更新。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨鲁棒性问题，其机制解释可为安全性研究提供基础。

papers.title: The State of Multilingual LLM Safety Research: From Measuring The Language Gap To Mitigating It
papers.short_title: Multilingual LLM Safety: Language Gap & Mitigation
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the linguistic diversity of LLM safety research, highlighting the English-centric nature of the field. Through a systematic review of nearly 300 publications from 2020–2024 across major NLP conferences and workshops at ACL, we identify a significant and growing language gap in LLM safety research, with even high-resource non-English languages receiving minimal attention. We further observe that non-English languages are rarely studied as a standalone language and that English safety research exhibits poor language documentation practice. To motivate future research into multilingual safety, we make several recommendations based on our survey, and we then pose three concrete future directions on safety evaluation, training data generation, and crosslingual safety generalization. Based on our survey and proposed directions, the field can develop more robust, inclusive AI safety practices for diverse global populations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the linguistic diversity in LLM safety research, revealing a significant language gap where even high-resource non-English languages are understudied. It conducts a systematic review of nearly 300 publications from 2020–2024 across major NLP venues, analyzing documentation practices and language coverage. The key finding is that LLM safety research is heavily English-centric, with non-English languages rarely studied standalone, indicating poor multilingual safety coverage. This survey demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile in multilingual contexts, as safety mechanisms are primarily evaluated and developed for English, potentially leaving non-English users vulnerable.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了LLM安全研究中的语言多样性问题，揭示了即使高资源非英语语言的安全研究也严重不足的语言差距。研究系统回顾了2020-2024年主要NLP会议上的近300篇论文，分析了文档实践和语言覆盖范围。关键发现是LLM安全研究高度以英语为中心，非英语语言很少被独立研究，表明多语言安全覆盖不足。该调查表明，安全对齐在多语言环境中是脆弱的，因为安全机制主要在英语中进行评估和开发，可能使非英语用户面临风险。

papers.title: R-TOFU: Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) embed private or copyrighted information not only in their final answers but also throughout multi-step chain-of-thought (CoT) traces, making reliable unlearning far more demanding than in standard LLMs. We introduce Reasoning-TOFU (R-TOFU), the first benchmark tailored to this setting. R-TOFU augments existing unlearning tasks with realistic CoT annotations and provides step-wise metrics that expose residual knowledge invisible to answer-level checks. Using R-TOFU, we carry out a comprehensive comparison of gradient-based and preference-optimization baselines and show that conventional answer-only objectives leave substantial forget traces in reasoning. We further propose Reasoned IDK, a preference-optimization variant that preserves coherent yet inconclusive reasoning, achieving a stronger balance between forgetting efficacy and model utility than earlier refusal styles. Finally, we identify a failure mode: decoding variants such as ZeroThink and LessThink can still reveal forgotten content despite seemingly successful unlearning, emphasizing the need to evaluate models under diverse decoding settings. Together, the benchmark, analysis, and new baseline establish a systematic foundation for studying and improving unlearning in LRMs while preserving their reasoning capabilities.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably unlearning private or copyrighted information from large reasoning models (LRMs), where information persists not only in final answers but also in chain-of-thought traces. It introduces R-TOFU, a benchmark with step-wise CoT annotations and metrics, and proposes Reasoned IDK, a preference-optimization method that preserves coherent yet inconclusive reasoning to improve the forgetting-utility trade-off. Experiments show that conventional answer-only unlearning leaves residual knowledge in reasoning, while Reasoned IDK better balances forgetting and model utility; however, decoding variants like ZeroThink can still expose forgotten content. This underscores a fragility in safety alignment: even when unlearning appears successful, the model remains vulnerable to circumvention via decoding strategies, contributing evidence that alignment mechanisms can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型推理模型（LRMs）中安全遗忘的挑战，这类模型中的隐私或版权信息不仅存在于最终答案中，也嵌入在思维链推理过程中。提出了R-TOFU基准，包含逐步推理注释和评估指标，并设计了Reasoned IDK方法，一种偏好优化变体，通过保持连贯但不确定的推理来改善遗忘与效用之间的平衡。实验表明，仅基于答案的遗忘目标会在推理过程中留下残余知识，而Reasoned IDK更好地平衡了遗忘效果和模型效用；然而，ZeroThink等解码变体仍能暴露已遗忘的内容。这揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：即使遗忘看似成功，模型仍可通过解码策略被绕过，为对齐机制易被破坏的观点提供了证据。

papers.title: Improve LLM-as-a-Judge Ability as a General Ability
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge leverages the generative and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to evaluate LLM responses across diverse scenarios, providing accurate preference signals. This approach plays a vital role in aligning LLMs with human values, ensuring ethical and reliable AI outputs that align with societal norms.
