Recent studies have raised many methods to train LLM as generative judges, but most of them are data consuming or lack accuracy, and only focus on LLM's judge ability. In this work, we regard judge ability as a general ability of LLM and implement a two-stage training approach, comprising supervised fine-tuning (SFT) warm-up and direct preference optimization (DPO) enhancement, to achieve judge style adaptation and improve judgment accuracy. Additionally, we introduce an efficient data synthesis method to generate judgmental content. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach, utilizing only about 2% to 40% of the data required by other methods, achieves SOTA performance on RewardBench. Furthermore, our training method enhances the general capabilities of the model by constructing complicated judge task, and the judge signals provided by our model have significantly enhanced the downstream DPO training performance of our internal models in our test to optimize policy model with Judge Model. We also open-source our model weights and training data to facilitate further research.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency and inaccuracy of training LLMs as judges for evaluating responses. It proposes a two-stage training approach that first conducts supervised fine-tuning (SFT) warm-up for judge style adaptation, then applies direct preference optimization (DPO) to enhance judgment accuracy, along with an efficient data synthesis method. Evaluated on RewardBench, the method uses only 2–40% of the data required by prior works while achieving state-of-the-art performance, and the resulting judge model improves downstream DPO training of policy models. This work advances alignment methodology by building a more effective judge model but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决训练大语言模型作为评判者时效率低和准确性不足的问题。提出两阶段训练方法：先通过监督微调（SFT）预热进行评判风格适应，再使用直接偏好优化（DPO）增强评判准确性，并附带高效数据合成方法。在RewardBench上评估，该方法仅需先前工作2%至40%的数据量即达到最优性能，且评判模型能提升下游策略模型的DPO训练效果。本文通过构建更有效的评判模型推进了对齐方法，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Selective Preference Optimization via Token-Level Reward Function Estimation
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in large language model alignment leverage token-level supervisions to perform fine-grained preference optimization. However, existing token-level alignment methods either optimize on all available tokens, which can be noisy and inefficient, or perform selective training with complex and expensive key token selection strategies. In this work, we propose Selective Preference Optimization (SePO), a novel selective alignment strategy that centers on efficient key token selection. SePO proposes the first token selection method based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which trains an oracle model to estimate a token-level reward function on the target data. This method applies to any existing alignment datasets with response-level annotations and enables cost-efficient token selection with small-scale oracle models and training data. The estimated reward function is then utilized to score all tokens within the target dataset, where only the key tokens are selected to supervise the target policy model with a reference model-free contrastive objective function. Extensive experiments on three public evaluation benchmarks show that SePO significantly outperforms competitive baseline methods by only optimizing 30% key tokens on the target dataset. SePO applications on weak-to-strong generalization show that weak oracle models effectively supervise strong policy models with up to 16.8x more parameters. SePO also effectively selects key tokens from out-of-distribution data to enhance strong policy models and alleviate the over-optimization problem.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency and noise in token-level preference optimization for large language model alignment. It proposes Selective Preference Optimization (SePO), which trains an oracle model to estimate a token-level reward function via Direct Preference Optimization, then selects only key tokens with high reward scores to supervise the policy model using a contrastive, reference-free objective. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that SePO outperforms baselines by optimizing only 30% of tokens and enables weak-to-strong generalization where weak oracles supervise models up to 16.8x larger. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大型语言模型对齐中基于token级别偏好优化的噪声和低效问题。提出了选择性偏好优化（SePO）方法，通过训练一个oracle模型利用直接偏好优化（DPO）估计token级奖励函数，然后仅选择奖励得分高的关键token，使用无参考的对比目标监督策略模型。在三个公开评测基准上的实验表明，仅优化30%的关键token，SePO就显著优于基线方法；并展示了弱到强泛化能力，弱oracle模型可以监督参数量大16.8倍的强策略模型。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: LIONs: An Empirically Optimized Approach to Align Language Models
papers.abstract: Alignment is a crucial step to enhance the instruction-following and conversational abilities of language models. Despite many recent works proposing new algorithms, datasets, and training pipelines, there is a lack of comprehensive studies measuring the impact of various design choices throughout the whole training process. We first conduct a rigorous analysis over a three-stage training pipeline consisting of supervised fine-tuning, offline preference learning, and online preference learning. We have found that using techniques like sequence packing, loss masking in SFT, increasing the preference dataset size in DPO, and online DPO training can significantly improve the performance of language models. We then train from Gemma-2b-base and LLama-3-8b-base, and find that our best models exceed the performance of the official instruct models tuned with closed-source data and algorithms. Our code and models can be found at https://github.com/Columbia-NLP-Lab/LionAlignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of comprehensive analysis on how design choices in the alignment training pipeline affect language model performance. It proposes an empirically optimized three-stage pipeline (supervised fine-tuning, offline DPO, online DPO) incorporating techniques like sequence packing, loss masking, larger preference datasets, and online training. Experiments with Gemma-2b and LLama-3-8b show the resulting models outperform official instruct versions, demonstrating the effectiveness of the optimization. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question; it focuses on building better alignment rather than testing robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐训练流程中各种设计选择对语言模型性能影响缺乏全面分析的问题，提出了一种经验优化的三阶段流程（监督微调、离线DPO、在线DPO），并应用了序列打包、损失掩码、增大偏好数据集规模和在线训练等技术。在Gemma-2b和LLama-3-8b上的实验表明，所得模型性能超过了官方指令微调模型，验证了优化方法的有效性。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，其重点是构建更好的对齐方法而非测试鲁棒性。

papers.title: Predicting Rewards Alongside Tokens: Non-disruptive Parameter Insertion for Efficient Inference Intervention in Large Language Model
papers.abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) exhibit limitations such as generating unsafe responses, unreliable reasoning, etc. Existing inference intervention approaches attempt to mitigate these issues by finetuning additional models to produce calibration signals (such as rewards) that guide the LLM’s decoding process. However, this solution introduces substantial time and space overhead due to the separate models required. This work proposes Non-disruptive parameters insertion (Otter), inserting extra parameters into the transformer architecture to predict calibration signals along with the original LLM output. Otter offers state-of-the-art performance on multiple demanding tasks while saving up to 86.5% extra space and 98.5% extra time. Furthermore, Otter seamlessly integrates with existing inference engines, requiring only a one-line code change, and the original model response remains accessible after the parameter insertion.
papers.summary_en: Large language models (LLMs) often generate unsafe or unreliable responses, and existing inference intervention methods mitigate this by using separate models to produce calibration signals, incurring heavy overhead. This paper proposes Otter, which inserts extra parameters into the transformer to predict calibration signals alongside the original LLM output, enabling non-disruptive and efficient intervention. Otter achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple demanding tasks while saving up to 86.5% extra space and 98.5% extra time, and it integrates seamlessly with existing inference engines via a one-line code change. This work advances alignment methodology by making inference-time intervention more efficient, but it does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）存在生成不安全响应、不可靠推理等问题，现有推理干预方法通过微调额外模型产生校准信号来引导解码，但带来了显著的时间和空间开销。本文提出非破坏性参数插入方法Otter，在Transformer架构中插入额外参数，与原始LLM输出一同预测校准信号，从而实现高效推理干预。Otter在多个高要求任务上达到最先进性能，同时节省高达86.5%的额外空间和98.5%的额外时间，并能通过一行代码更改无缝集成现有推理引擎，且参数插入后原始模型响应仍可访问。本文推进了对齐方法，使推理时干预更加高效，但并未直接涉及后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Attention Eclipse: Manipulating Attention to Bypass LLM Safety-Alignment
papers.abstract: Recent research has shown that carefully crafted jailbreak inputs can induce large language models to produce harmful outputs, despite safety measures such as alignment. It is important to anticipate the range of potential Jailbreak attacks to guide effective defenses and accurate assessment of model safety. In this paper, we present a new approach for generating highly effective Jailbreak attacks that manipulate the attention of the model to selectively strengthen or weaken attention among different parts of the prompt. By harnessing attention loss, we develop more effective jailbreak attacks, that are also transferrable. The attacks amplify the success rate of existing Jailbreak algorithms including GCG, AutoDAN, and ReNeLLM, while lowering their generation cost (for example, the amplified GCG attack achieves 91.2% ASR, vs. 67.9% for the original attack on Llama2-7B/AdvBench, using less than a third of the generation time).
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety-aligned LLMs. It proposes Attention Eclipse, a method that manipulates model attention by strengthening or weakening attention among different prompt parts via an attention loss, thereby generating more potent and transferable jailbreak attacks. Evaluated on Llama2-7B with AdvBench, the approach amplifies existing attacks like GCG (91.2% ASR vs. 67.9%) while reducing generation cost. This work reveals a mechanistic weakness in attention-based safety alignment, directly supporting the view that post-training safety modules are fragile and can be effectively bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对越狱攻击绕过安全对齐的大语言模型这一问题，提出了一种名为 Attention Eclipse 的方法，通过注意力损失来操纵模型注意力，强化或削弱提示中不同部分之间的注意力，从而生成更有效且可迁移的越狱攻击。在 Llama2-7B 和 AdvBench 上的评估表明，该方法可提升现有攻击（如 GCG 从 67.9% 提升到 91.2% ASR）并降低生成成本。这项工作揭示了基于注意力的安全对齐的机制性弱点，直接支持了后训练安全模块是脆弱的且可被轻易绕过这一观点。

papers.title: Beyond Online Sampling: Bridging Offline-to-Online Alignment via Dynamic Data Transformation for LLMs
papers.abstract: While Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) eliminates complex reward modeling in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, its online variant faces significant efficiency bottlenecks due to costly real-time preference sampling and the reward model annotation. We propose a novel framework that bridges offline-to-online alignment by systematically transforming static datasets into dynamically adaptive equivalents, without the need for an explicit reward model. Our approach employs paraphrasing techniques to preserve response correctness while aligning data distributions with model-generated outputs, circum-venting the need for resource-intensive online interactions. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and conversational tasks demonstrate that our method matches or exceeds the performance of a fully online DPO. This work establishes a computationally sustainable paradigm for LLM alignment, particularly benefiting scenarios requiring iterative preference updates and domain adaptation.
papers.summary_en: The paper tackles the efficiency bottlenecks of online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which relies on costly real-time preference sampling and reward model annotation. It proposes a framework that uses paraphrasing to transform static offline datasets into dynamically adaptive equivalents, aligning data distributions with model-generated outputs without an explicit reward model. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and conversational tasks show the method matches or surpasses online DPO performance. This work advances alignment methodology with a computationally sustainable alternative but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对在线直接偏好优化（DPO）因需要昂贵实时偏好采样和奖励模型标注而导致的效率瓶颈问题。提出了一种框架，通过改写技术将静态离线数据集转换为动态自适应等价物，使数据分布与模型生成输出对齐，无需显式奖励模型。在数学推理和对话任务上的实验表明，该方法达到或超过在线 DPO 的性能。该工作通过计算可持续的替代方案推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Permutative Preference Alignment from Listwise Ranking of Human Judgments
papers.short_title: PPA: Aligning LLMs via Listwise NDCG
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences is crucial in ensuring desirable and controllable model behaviors. Current methods, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), rely on the Bradley-Terry (B-T) model to maximize the likelihood of pairwise choices. However, when multiple responses are available, the B-T model fails to guarantee an accurate list ranking of the responses. To address this issue, we propose Permutative Preference Alignment (PPA), a novel offline listwise approach that incorporates the Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG)—a widely-used ranking metric—as an alternative training objective for LLM alignment. We develop an end-to-end alignment algorithm by approximating NDCG with a differentiable surrogate loss. Experiments demonstrate that PPA outperforms existing pairwise and listwise methods on evaluation sets and general benchmarks such as AlpacaEval. Furthermore, we show that NDCG-based approaches improve ranking accuracy more effectively than B-T-based methods and provide a theoretical explanation for this improvement.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of Bradley-Terry-based pairwise preference models in producing accurate listwise rankings when multiple responses are available. It proposes Permutative Preference Alignment (PPA), an offline listwise method that optimizes the Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) metric via a differentiable surrogate loss. Experiments show that PPA surpasses existing pairwise and listwise approaches on both targeted evaluation sets and AlpacaEval, with theoretical justification for improved ranking accuracy. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment, focusing instead on enhancing preference ranking fidelity.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了当存在多个响应时，基于Bradley-Terry模型的成对偏好方法无法保证准确列表排序的问题。提出了排列偏好对齐（PPA），一种利用归一化折损累积增益（NDCG）作为优化目标的离线列表式方法，并通过可微分替代损失进行端到端训练。实验表明，PPA在评估集和AlpacaEval等基准上均优于现有的成对和列表式方法，并从理论上解释了NDCG相比B-T模型能更有效提升排序精度。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或可绕过性，重点在于提升偏好排序的忠实度。

papers.title: DAMON: A Dialogue-Aware MCTS Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
papers.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities across a wide range of tasks, they remain vulnerable to generating outputs that are potentially harmful. Red teaming, which involves crafting adversarial inputs to expose vulnerabilities, is a widely adopted approach for evaluating the robustness of these models. Prior studies have indicated that LLMs are susceptible to vulnerabilities exposed through multi-turn interactions as opposed to single-turn scenarios. Nevertheless, existing methods for multi-turn attacks mainly utilize a predefined dialogue pattern, limiting their effectiveness in realistic situations. Effective attacks require adaptive dialogue strategies that respond dynamically to the initial user prompt and the evolving context of the conversation. To address these limitations, we propose DAMON, a novel multi-turn jailbreak attack method. DAMON leverages Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to systematically explore multi-turn conversational spaces, efficiently identifying sub-instruction sequences that induce harmful responses. We evaluate DAMON’s efficacy across five LLMs and three datasets. Our experimental results show that DAMON can effectively induce undesired behaviors.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to multi-turn jailbreak attacks, noting that existing methods rely on rigid predefined dialogue patterns rather than adaptive strategies. It proposes DAMON, a novel framework that uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to dynamically explore multi-turn conversational spaces and craft effective sub-instruction sequences. Evaluation across five LLMs and three datasets shows that DAMON can successfully elicit harmful responses, outperforming prior multi-turn attack methods. This work directly contributes to the question of post-training safety robustness by introducing a powerful attack that systematically bypasses safety guardrails, indicating that alignment remains fragile against adaptive multi-turn interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在多轮越狱攻击中的脆弱性，指出已有方法依赖固定的对话模式而非自适应策略。提出DAMON框架，利用蒙特卡洛树搜索动态探索多轮对话空间，生成有效的子指令序列以诱导有害输出。在五个大模型和三个数据集上的实验表明，DAMON能成功引发不良行为，优于现有方法。该工作通过设计一种系统性绕过安全防护的强大攻击，直接回应了后训练安全性是否稳健的问题，表明面对自适应多轮交互时，安全对齐仍然脆弱。

papers.title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
papers.abstract: Recently, autonomous agents built on large language models (LLMs) have experienced significant development and are being deployed in real-world applications. These agents can extend the base LLM's capabilities in multiple ways. For example, a well-built agent using GPT-3.5-Turbo as its core can outperform the more advanced GPT-4 model by leveraging external components. More importantly, the usage of tools enables these systems to perform actions in the real world, moving from merely generating text to actively interacting with their environment. Given the agents' practical applications and their ability to execute consequential actions, it is crucial to assess potential vulnerabilities. Such autonomous systems can cause more severe damage than a standalone language model if compromised. While some existing research has explored harmful actions by LLM agents, our study approaches the vulnerability from a different perspective. We introduce a new type of attack that causes malfunctions by misleading the agent into executing repetitive or irrelevant actions. We conduct comprehensive evaluations using various attack methods, surfaces, and properties to pinpoint areas of susceptibility. Our experiments reveal that these attacks can induce failure rates exceeding 80\% in multiple scenarios. Through attacks on implemented and deployable agents in multi-agent scenarios, we accentuate the realistic risks associated with these vulnerabilities. To mitigate such attacks, we propose self-examination detection methods. However, our findings indicate these attacks are difficult to detect effectively using LLMs alone, highlighting the substantial risks associated with this vulnerability.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents a novel attack on autonomous LLM agents that causes malfunction by misleading agents into performing repetitive or irrelevant actions, rather than triggering harmful content. The authors systematically evaluate this malfunction amplification attack across different methods, surfaces, and agent properties. Experiments reveal failure rates exceeding 80% in multiple scenarios, and proposed self-examination detection proves ineffective, highlighting severe practical risks. The work shows that even safety-aligned base LLMs can be exploited through agent-level vulnerabilities, questioning the sufficiency of post-training safety alignment for real-world agent systems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种针对自主LLM智能体的新型攻击，通过误导智能体执行重复或无关操作来引发故障，而非生成有害内容。作者系统评估了这种故障放大攻击在多种攻击方法、接口和智能体属性下的效果。实验显示在多个场景中故障率超过80%，且提出的自我检查检测方法效果不佳，揭示了严重的实际风险。该研究表明，即使基座LLM经过安全对齐，智能体层面的漏洞仍可被利用，对仅依赖安全对齐的复杂系统安全性提出了质疑。

papers.title: Reasoning-to-Defend: Safety-Aware Reasoning Can Defend Large Language Models from Jailbreaking
papers.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have recently demonstrated impressive performances across diverse domains. However, how the safety of Large Language Models (LLMs) benefits from enhanced reasoning capabilities against jailbreak queries remains unexplored. To bridge this gap, in this paper, we propose Reasoning-to-Defend (R2D), a novel training paradigm that integrates a safety-aware reasoning mechanism into LLMs'generation process. This enables self-evaluation at each step of the reasoning process, forming safety pivot tokens as indicators of the safety status of responses. Furthermore, in order to improve the accuracy of predicting pivot tokens, we propose Contrastive Pivot Optimization (CPO), which enhances the model's perception of the safety status of given dialogues. LLMs dynamically adjust their response strategies during reasoning, significantly enhancing their safety capabilities defending jailbreak attacks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that R2D effectively mitigates various attacks and improves overall safety, while maintaining the original performances. This highlights the substantial potential of safety-aware reasoning in improving robustness of LRMs and LLMs against various jailbreaks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to jailbreak attacks by exploring how enhanced reasoning capabilities can improve safety. It proposes Reasoning-to-Defend (R2D), a training paradigm that integrates safety-aware reasoning through stepwise self-evaluation using safety pivot tokens, along with Contrastive Pivot Optimization (CPO) to enhance pivot prediction accuracy. Experiments show that R2D effectively mitigates diverse jailbreak attacks and improves overall safety without degrading general performance. This work demonstrates that safety alignment can be strengthened by embedding reasoning mechanisms, offering evidence that post-training alignment is not inherently fragile and can be made more robust against adversarial bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型（LLMs）容易遭受越狱攻击的问题，探索利用增强推理能力提升安全性。提出Reasoning-to-Defend（R2D）训练范式，通过逐步自我评估生成安全枢轴令牌，并引入对比枢轴优化（CPO）提高预测准确性。实验表明，R2D有效防御多种越狱攻击，提高整体安全性的同时保持原有性能。该工作表明通过嵌入推理机制可以强化安全对齐，为后训练安全对齐并非固有不稳定、可通过创新增强提供证据。

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models via Group Preference Reward Shaping
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) require alignment via reinforcement learning (RL) to effectively perform task-specific objectives, such as human preference alignment and enhanced reasoning. While Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is widely adopted, its computational overhead, stemming from additional value model requirements, limits applicability. Existing alternatives, like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), mitigate computational costs but remain sensitive to reward model quality. To address this, we introduce Group Preference Reward Shaping (GPRS), a novel method that leverages preference-based comparisons rather than precise numerical rewards. GPRS requires no extra model components and remains robust across varying reward model sizes and qualities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GPRS consistently outperforms existing critic-model-free RL algorithms in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and reasoning tasks, providing stable and good alignment performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the computational overhead and sensitivity to reward model quality in reinforcement learning (RL) alignment methods for large language models (LLMs). It proposes Group Preference Reward Shaping (GPRS), a critic-model-free approach that uses preference-based comparisons instead of precise numerical rewards, eliminating the need for extra model components. Experiments demonstrate that GPRS consistently outperforms existing critic-model-free RL algorithms in RLHF and reasoning tasks, providing stable alignment. The paper strengthens alignment methodology by improving robustness to reward model imperfections, but it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fundamentally fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型（LLM）对齐中强化学习（RL）方法的计算开销和奖励模型质量敏感性问题。它提出组偏好奖励塑造（GPRS），一种无需额外模型组件的方法，利用偏好比较而非精确数值奖励。实验表明，GPRS在RLHF和推理任务中一致优于现有的无critic模型RL算法，提供稳定的对齐性能。本文通过提高对奖励模型质量的鲁棒性改进了对齐方法，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐本身是否脆弱或易于绕过。

papers.title: WPO: Enhancing RLHF with Weighted Preference Optimization
papers.short_title: WPO: Enhancing RLHF with Weighted Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a promising solution to align large language models (LLMs) more closely with human values. Off-policy preference optimization, where the preference data is obtained from other models, is widely adopted due to its cost efficiency and scalability. However, off-policy preference optimization often suffers from a distributional gap between the policy used for data collection and the target policy, leading to suboptimal optimization. In this paper, we propose a novel strategy to mitigate this problem by simulating on-policy learning with off-policy preference data. Our Weighted Preference Optimization (WPO) method adapts off-policy data to resemble on-policy data more closely by reweighting preference pairs according to their probability under the current policy. This method not only addresses the distributional gap problem but also enhances the optimization process without incurring additional costs. We validate our method on instruction following benchmarks including Alpaca Eval 2 and MT-bench. WPO not only outperforms Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) by up to 5.6% on Alpaca Eval 2 but also establishes a remarkable length-controlled winning rate against GPT-4-turbo of 76.7% based on Gemma-2-9b-it. We release the code and models at https://github.com/wzhouad/WPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the distributional gap between off-policy preference data and the target policy in RLHF, which leads to suboptimal alignment. It proposes Weighted Preference Optimization (WPO), a method that reweights off-policy preference pairs according to their probability under the current policy to better approximate on-policy learning. Evaluated on Alpaca Eval 2 and MT-bench, WPO outperforms DPO by up to 5.6% and achieves a 76.7% length-controlled win rate against GPT-4-turbo using Gemma-2-9b-it. This paper advances alignment methodology by mitigating off-policy distribution issues but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中离策略偏好数据与目标策略之间的分布差异问题，该差异会导致对齐效果欠佳。提出了加权偏好优化（WPO）方法，通过根据当前策略下偏好对的概率重新加权离策略数据，以更贴近在策略学习。在Alpaca Eval 2和MT-bench上进行评估，WPO在Alpaca Eval 2上比DPO最多提升5.6%，并基于Gemma-2-9b-it实现了对GPT-4-turbo的76.7%长度受控胜率。该工作改进了对齐方法，缓解了离策略分布问题，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: SUA: Stealthy Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning Attack
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) trained on massive data may memorize sensitive personal information and photos, posing serious privacy risks. To mitigate this, MLLM unlearning methods are proposed, which fine-tune MLLMs to reduce the “forget” sensitive information. However, it remains unclear whether the knowledge has been truly forgotten or just hidden in the model. Therefore, we propose to study a novel problem of LLM unlearning attack, which aims to recover the unlearned knowledge of an unlearned LLM. To achieve the goal, we propose a novel framework Stealthy Unlearning Attack (SUA) framework that learns a universal noise pattern. When applied to input images, this noise can trigger the model to reveal unlearned content. While pixel-level perturbations may be visually subtle, they can be detected in the semantic embedding space, making such attacks vulnerable to potential defenses. To improve stealthiness, we introduce an embedding alignment loss that minimizes the difference between the perturbed and denoised image embeddings, ensuring the attack is semantically unnoticeable. Experimental results show that SUA can effectively recover unlearned information from MLLMs. Furthermore, the learned noise generalizes well: a single perturbation trained on a subset of samples can reveal forgotten content in unseen images. This indicates that knowledge reappearance is not an occasional failure, but a consistent behavior.
papers.summary_en: This paper explores whether knowledge removed through unlearning in multimodal LLMs can be recovered, challenging the robustness of privacy-preserving methods. The authors propose the Stealthy Unlearning Attack (SUA), which trains a universal noise pattern that, when applied to input images, triggers the model to reveal forgotten content; an embedding alignment loss ensures the perturbations are semantically inconspicuous. Experiments demonstrate SUA can effectively extract unlearned information and that the noise generalizes across unseen images, revealing a consistent vulnerability. This work directly exposes the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that unlearning can be circumvented, and thus aligns with the SoK’s central question of whether alignment is robust or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究多模态大语言模型在经过去学习后，是否仍能恢复被遗忘的知识，质疑去学习方法的鲁棒性。提出一种隐秘去学习攻击框架 SUA，通过学习一个通用噪声模式，将其添加到输入图像时可诱导模型输出已遗忘内容，并采用嵌入对齐损失提升语义隐蔽性。实验表明，SUA 能有效恢复未学习信息，且噪声可泛化至未见图像，揭示出一致性的脆弱行为。该工作直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，即去学习可被绕过，回应了安全对齐是否真正稳健还是易于构建、破坏和绕过这一核心问题。

papers.title: FlipGuard: Defending Preference Alignment against Update Regression with Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent breakthroughs in preference alignment have significantly improved Large Language Models' ability to generate texts that align with human preferences and values. However, current alignment metrics typically emphasize the post-hoc overall improvement, while overlooking a critical aspect: regression, which refers to the backsliding on previously correctly-handled data after updates. This potential pitfall may arise from excessive fine-tuning on already well-aligned data, which subsequently leads to over-alignment and degeneration. To address this challenge, we propose FlipGuard, a constrained optimization approach to detect and mitigate update regression with focal attention. Specifically, FlipGuard identifies performance degradation using a customized reward characterization and strategically enforces a constraint to encourage conditional congruence with the pre-aligned model during training. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that FlipGuard effectively alleviates update regression while demonstrating excellent overall performance, with the added benefit of knowledge preservation while aligning preferences.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses update regression in preference alignment, where fine-tuning can degrade performance on previously correct data. It proposes FlipGuard, a constrained optimization method that detects regression via reward characterization and enforces consistency with the pre-aligned model. Experiments show FlipGuard mitigates regression while preserving overall performance and knowledge. This work directly relates to the fragility of post-training alignment, demonstrating that alignment can be fragile to further updates but can be hardened through constrained optimization.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对偏好对齐中的更新退化问题，即微调可能导致模型在先前正确处理的样本上性能下降。提出FlipGuard，一种约束优化方法，通过奖励差异检测退化，并强制与预对齐模型保持一致性。实验表明FlipGuard在缓解退化的同时保持整体性能与知识保留。该研究直接关联对齐脆弱性问题，表明对齐在后续更新中可能脆弱，但可通过约束优化加固。

papers.title: Universal Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models: Backdoor Attacks for In-context Learning
papers.abstract: In-context learning, a paradigm bridging the gap between pre-training and fine-tuning, has demonstrated high efficacy in several NLP tasks, especially in few-shot settings. Despite being widely applied, in-context learning is vulnerable to malicious attacks. In this work, we raise security concerns regarding this paradigm. Our studies demonstrate that an attacker can manipulate the behavior of large language models by poisoning the demonstration context, without the need for fine-tuning the model. Specifically, we design a new backdoor attack method, named ICLAttack, to target large language models based on in-context learning. Our method encompasses two types of attacks: poisoning demonstration examples and poisoning demonstration prompts, which can make models behave in alignment with predefined intentions. ICLAttack does not require additional fine-tuning to implant a backdoor, thus preserving the model’s generality. Furthermore, the poisoned examples are correctly labeled, enhancing the natural stealth of our attack method. Extensive experimental results across several language models, ranging in size from 1.3B to 180B parameters, demonstrate the effectiveness of our attack method, exemplified by a high average attack success rate of 95.0% across the three datasets on OPT models.
papers.summary_en: This paper exposes security vulnerabilities in in-context learning (ICL), where an attacker can manipulate LLM behavior by poisoning demonstration contexts without model retraining. The authors propose ICLAttack, a novel backdoor method with two variants—poisoning demonstration examples and prompts—that implants stealthy backdoors while keeping poisoned samples correctly labeled. Evaluations across models from 1.3B to 180B parameters show an average attack success rate of 95.0% on OPT models over three datasets, demonstrating high effectiveness. This work reveals a new attack surface on the in-context mechanism, directly challenging the assumed robustness of post-training safety alignment when context can be adversarially controlled.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了基于上下文学习（ICL）的安全漏洞：攻击者可通过污染演示上下文来操控大语言模型的行为，无需对模型进行微调。为此，作者提出了名为ICLAttack的新型后门攻击方法，包含两种类型（污染演示示例和污染演示提示），能在保持中毒样本标签正确的前提下隐蔽植入后门。在参数量从1.3B到180B的多个模型上的实验结果表明，在OPT模型和三个数据集上平均攻击成功率高达95.0%，证明了攻击的有效性。该工作发现了针对上下文交互机制的新攻击面，直接挑战了在后训练安全对齐在上下文被对抗性控制时的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Exploring Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Steerable Pluralistic Alignment
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are typically trained to reflect a relatively uniform set of values, which limits their applicability to tasks that require understanding of nuanced human perspectives. Recent research has underscored the importance of enabling LLMs to support steerable pluralism — the capacity to adopt a specific perspective and align generated outputs with it. In this work, we investigate whether Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning techniques can be applied to building steerable pluralistic models. We explore several methods, including CoT prompting, fine-tuning on human-authored CoT, fine-tuning on synthetic explanations, and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). We evaluate these approaches using the Value Kaleidoscope and OpinionQA datasets. Among the methods studied, RLVR consistently outperforms others and demonstrates strong training sample efficiency. We further analyze the generated CoT traces with respect to faithfulness and safety.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of enabling LLMs to generate outputs reflecting specific, diverse human perspectives (steerable pluralism). It investigates whether Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning can be leveraged through methods like CoT prompting, fine-tuning on human or synthetic explanations, and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). Evaluated on Value Kaleidoscope and OpinionQA, RLVR consistently outperforms other approaches and shows strong sample efficiency; analysis also examines CoT faithfulness and safety. While this work advances alignment techniques for pluralistic settings, it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决使大语言模型能够反映特定、多元人类观点（可引导的多元对齐）的挑战。研究通过 CoT 提示、基于人类或合成解释的微调、以及基于可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）等方法利用思维链推理。在 Value Kaleidoscope 和 OpinionQA 上评估，RLVR 一致优于其他方法并表现出高样本效率；进一步分析了 CoT 痕迹的忠实性和安全性。该工作推进了多元场景下的对齐方法，但并未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Large Language Models Are Involuntary Truth-Tellers: Exploiting Fallacy Failure for Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: We find that language models have difficulties generating fallacious and deceptive reasoning. When asked to generate deceptive outputs, language models tend to leak honest counterparts but believe them to be false. Exploiting this deficiency, we propose a jailbreak attack method that elicits an aligned language model for malicious output. Specifically, we query the model to generate a fallacious yet deceptively real procedure for the harmful behavior. Since a fallacious procedure is generally considered fake and thus harmless by LLMs, it helps bypass the safeguard mechanism. Yet the output is factually harmful since the LLM cannot fabricate fallacious solutions but proposes truthful ones. We evaluate our approach over five safety-aligned large language models, comparing four previous jailbreak methods, and show that our approach achieves competitive performance with more harmful outputs. We believe the findings could be extended beyond model safety, such as self-verification and hallucination.
papers.summary_en: The paper reveals that large language models struggle to generate fallacious reasoning and instead leak honest content, even when instructed to be deceptive. The authors propose a jailbreak attack that exploits this 'fallacy failure' by prompting the model to produce a fallacious but seemingly real procedure for harmful behavior; because the model treats fallacious outputs as harmless, it bypasses safety filters, yet the output is actually harmful. Evaluated on five safety-aligned LLMs, the method outperforms previous jailbreak attacks in generating harmful outputs. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as an inherent model tendency toward truthfulness can be exploited to undermine safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文发现大语言模型难以生成谬误推理，即使被要求欺骗，仍会泄露真实内容。作者提出了一种越狱攻击，利用这一“谬误失败”现象：要求模型为有害行为生成看似合理实则谬误的程序；模型因将其视为无害而绕过安全机制，但输出实际有害。在五个安全对齐的大语言模型上评估，该方法生成有害输出的能力优于现有攻击。该研究直接表明后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因为模型固有的求真倾向可被利用来突破防护。

papers.title: SafeKey: Amplifying Aha-Moment Insights for Safety Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) introduce a new generation paradigm of explicitly reasoning before answering, leading to remarkable improvements in complex tasks. However, they pose great safety risks against harmful queries and adversarial attacks. While recent mainstream safety efforts on LRMs, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), improve safety performance, we find that SFT-aligned models struggle to generalize to unseen jailbreak prompts. After thorough investigation, we identify a safety aha moment that can activate safety reasoning and lead to a safe response. This aha moment typically appears in the ‘key sentence’ that follows models’ query understanding process and can indicate whether the model will proceed safely. Based on these insights, we propose SafeKey, including two complementary objectives to better activate the safety aha-moment in the key sentence: (1) a Dual-Path Safety Head to enhance the safety signal in the model’s internal representations before the key sentence, and (2) a Query-Mask Modeling objective to improve the models’ attention on its query understanding, which has important safety hints. Experiments across multiple safety benchmarks demonstrate that our methods significantly improve safety generalization to a wide range of jailbreak attacks and out-of-distribution harmful prompts, lowering the harmfulness rate by 9.6%, while maintaining general abilities. Our analysis reveals how SafeKey enhances safety by reshaping internal attention and improving the quality of hidden representations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the poor generalization of SFT-based safety alignment in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) against unseen jailbreak attacks. The authors identify a 'safety aha moment' in a key sentence and propose SafeKey, which uses a dual-path safety head and query-mask modeling to amplify this insight. Experiments demonstrate a 9.6% reduction in harmfulness across multiple jailbreak benchmarks while preserving general capabilities. While focusing on a hardening approach, the paper exposes the fragility of standard safety alignment, suggesting that post-training safety can be brittle under novel attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了基于SFT安全对齐的大型推理模型在未见越狱攻击下泛化能力差的问题。作者识别出关键句子中的‘安全顿悟时刻’，并提出SafeKey，通过双路径安全头部和查询掩码建模来放大这一洞察。实验显示，在多个越狱基准上危害率降低9.6%，同时保持通用能力。尽管本文侧重于强化方法，但它揭示了标准安全对齐的脆弱性，表明后训练安全性在新型攻击下可能不稳固。

papers.title: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning is a promising approach to mitigate undesirable memorization of training data in ML models. However, in this work we show that existing approaches for unlearning in LLMs are surprisingly susceptible to a simple set of $\textit{benign relearning attacks}$. With access to only a small and potentially loosely related set of data, we find that we can ''jog'' the memory of unlearned models to reverse the effects of unlearning. For example, we show that relearning on public medical articles can lead an unlearned LLM to output harmful knowledge about bioweapons, and relearning general wiki information about the book series Harry Potter can force the model to output verbatim memorized text. We formalize this unlearning-relearning pipeline, explore the attack across three popular unlearning benchmarks, and discuss future directions and guidelines that result from our study. Our work indicates that current approximate unlearning methods simply suppress the model outputs and fail to robustly forget target knowledge in the LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper exposes that current machine unlearning methods for LLMs are susceptible to benign relearning attacks that can restore supposedly erased knowledge. It formalizes an unlearning-relearning pipeline where a small, loosely related dataset is used to jog the model's memory, evaluating this attack across three popular unlearning benchmarks. The key finding is that relearning on benign data (e.g., public articles or wiki pages) causes unlearned models to output harmful or memorized content, demonstrating that unlearning merely suppresses outputs without robust forgetting. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment via unlearning is fragile, as it can be easily bypassed, reinforcing the notion that alignment may be a brittle module rather than a robust property.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了当前大型语言模型的机器遗忘方法容易受到良性再学习攻击，能够恢复本应被遗忘的知识。它形式化了遗忘-再学习流程，使用小型且可能松散相关的数据集唤起模型记忆，并在三个流行的遗忘基准上评估该攻击。关键发现是，在良性数据（如公开文章或维基页面）上的再学习会导致已遗忘模型输出有害或记忆的内容，表明遗忘仅抑制输出而未能稳健地遗忘。这项工作直接证明通过遗忘进行的后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可被轻松绕过，强化了对齐可能是一个脆弱模块而非稳健属性的观点。

papers.title: AdaSteer: Your Aligned LLM is Inherently an Adaptive Jailbreak Defender
papers.abstract: Despite extensive efforts in safety alignment, large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Activation steering offers a training-free defense method but relies on fixed steering coefficients, resulting in suboptimal protection and increased false rejections of benign inputs. To address this, we propose AdaSteer, an adaptive activation steering method that dynamically adjusts model behavior based on input characteristics. We identify two key properties: Rejection Law (R-Law), which shows that stronger steering is needed for jailbreak inputs opposing the rejection direction, and Harmfulness Law (H-Law), which differentiates adversarial and benign inputs. AdaSteer steers input representations along both the Rejection Direction (RD) and Harmfulness Direction (HD), with adaptive coefficients learned via logistic regression, ensuring robust jailbreak defense while preserving benign input handling. Experiments on LLaMA-3.1, Gemma-2, and Qwen2.5 show that AdaSteer outperforms baseline methods across multiple jailbreak attacks with minimal impact on utility. Our results highlight the potential of interpretable model internals for real-time, flexible safety enforcement in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: Jailbreak attacks bypass safety alignment, and existing activation steering defenses use fixed coefficients, causing suboptimal protection and false rejections. AdaSteer introduces adaptive activation steering by learning coefficient functions from two interpretable properties (Rejection Law and Harmfulness Law) to dynamically adjust steering based on input. Experiments on LLaMA-3.1, Gemma-2, and Qwen2.5 show that AdaSteer outperforms baseline methods across multiple jailbreak attacks while preserving utility. This paper advances defense methods by leveraging interpretable model internals, but it primarily focuses on building a better alignment enforcement mechanism rather than directly studying the fragility of alignment; it implicitly acknowledges alignment's bypassability by proposing an adaptive defense.
papers.summary_zh: 越狱攻击规避安全对齐，现有激活引导防御使用固定系数，导致保护不足和误拒。AdaSteer 通过从两个可解释属性（拒绝定律和有害性定律）学习系数函数，实现自适应激活引导，根据输入动态调整引导。在 LLaMA-3.1、Gemma-2 和 Qwen2.5 上的实验表明，AdaSteer 在多种越狱攻击下优于基线方法，且对模型效用影响很小。本文通过利用可解释的模型内部机制推进防御方法，但主要侧重于构建更好的对齐执行机制，而非直接研究对齐的脆弱性；它通过提出自适应防御，隐含承认了对齐的可绕越性。

papers.title: Detoxifying Large Language Models via the Diversity of Toxic Samples
papers.abstract: Eliminating toxicity from Large Language Models (LLMs) is crucial for ensuring user safety. However, current methods have limitations in the analysis and utilization of toxic samples, failing to fully harness their potential. Through comparative analysis of toxic and safe samples, we discover that toxic samples exhibit diversity and, within this diversity, there lies specificity. These findings suggest that leveraging these characteristics of toxic samples could enhance the performance of algorithms in detoxifying LLMs. To this end, we propose a novel diverse detoxification framework, DivDetox, which comprises two innovative components: a Multi-Category-Induced Personalized Sample Generation (MPSG) strategy and a Scaled Contrastive DPO (SC-DPO) approach. The former is designed to elicit a variety of personalized toxic responses from the LLM, while the latter is constructed to precisely and fully utilize these toxic responses. Experiments on benchmark datasets across different model scales and different detoxification tasks verify the effectiveness of our architecture.
papers.summary_en: Current detoxification methods for LLMs fail to fully exploit the diversity and specificity of toxic samples. The paper proposes DivDetox, a framework that uses a Multi-Category-Induced Personalized Sample Generation (MPSG) strategy to elicit varied toxic responses and a Scaled Contrastive DPO (SC-DPO) approach to precisely utilize them. Experiments on benchmark datasets across different model sizes and detoxification tasks show DivDetox's effectiveness. This work primarily improves detoxification alignment and does not directly investigate the fragility of safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 当前针对大型语言模型的去毒方法未能充分利用有毒样本的多样性和特殊性。本文提出DivDetox框架，包含多类别诱导的个性化样本生成（MPSG）策略来引发多样化的毒性响应，以及缩放对比DPO（SC-DPO）方法精确利用这些响应。在不同模型规模和去毒任务的基准数据集上的实验验证了DivDetox的有效性。该研究主要提升了去毒对齐方法，并未直接探讨安全机制的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Holistic Automated Red Teaming for Large Language Models through Top-Down Test Case Generation and Multi-turn Interaction
papers.abstract: Automated red teaming is an effective method for identifying misaligned behaviors in large language models (LLMs). Existing approaches, however, often focus primarily on improving attack success rates while overlooking the need for comprehensive test case coverage. Additionally, most of these methods are limited to single-turn red teaming, failing to capture the multi-turn dynamics of real-world human-machine interactions. To overcome these limitations, we propose **HARM** (**H**olistic **A**utomated **R**ed tea**M**ing), which scales up the diversity of test cases using a top-down approach based on an extensible, fine-grained risk taxonomy. Our method also leverages a novel fine-tuning strategy and reinforcement learning techniques to facilitate multi-turn adversarial probing in a human-like manner. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework enables a more systematic understanding of model vulnerabilities and offers more targeted guidance for the alignment process.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitations of existing automated red teaming methods for LLMs, which focus on attack success rates without ensuring broad test case coverage and are typically restricted to single-turn interactions. It proposes HARM, a holistic framework that uses a fine-grained risk taxonomy for top-down test case generation and employs fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning for human-like multi-turn adversarial probing. Experiments show HARM enables more systematic discovery of model vulnerabilities and offers targeted guidance for alignment, improving the comprehensiveness of red teaming. By providing a method to more thoroughly probe misaligned behaviors, the work indirectly supports assessment of alignment robustness but does not directly investigate whether safety alignment is intrinsically fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 现有自动红队方法侧重攻击成功率而忽视测试用例全面覆盖，多限于单轮交互，未能捕捉真实多轮动态。本文提出HARM，基于细粒度风险分类体系自上而下生成多样化测试用例，并通过微调与强化学习实现类人多轮对抗探测。实验表明，HARM能更系统地揭示模型漏洞，为对齐提供精准指导。该工作通过增强红队测试的全面性与真实性，为评估安全对齐鲁棒性提供工具，但未直接探讨对齐模块本身的脆弱性。

papers.title: Strong Preferences Affect the Robustness of Preference Models and Value Alignment
papers.short_title: Strong Prefs Affect Robustness of Pref Models
papers.abstract: Value alignment, which aims to ensure that large language models (LLMs) and other AI agents behave in accordance with human values, is critical for ensuring safety and trustworthiness of these systems. A key component of value alignment is the modeling of human preferences as a representation of human values. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of value alignment by examining the sensitivity of preference models. Specifically, we ask: how do changes in the probabilities of some preferences affect the predictions of these models for other preferences? To answer this question, we theoretically analyze the robustness of widely used preference models by examining their sensitivities to minor changes in preferences they model. Our findings reveal that, in the Bradley-Terry and the Placket-Luce model, the probability of a preference can change significantly as other preferences change, especially when these preferences are dominant (i.e., with probabilities near 0 or 1). We identify specific conditions where this sensitivity becomes significant for these models and discuss the practical implications for the robustness and safety of value alignment in AI systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the robustness of value alignment by examining the sensitivity of preference models to changes in preference probabilities. It theoretically analyzes the Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce models to understand how perturbations in some preferences impact predictions for others. The key finding is that preference probabilities can change significantly when other preferences are dominant (near 0 or 1), indicating high sensitivity. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training alignment by revealing a mechanistic weakness: preference models are not robust to small shifts in input distributions, suggesting that value alignment can be undermined by minor preference changes.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过研究偏好模型对偏好概率变化的敏感性，探讨了价值对齐的鲁棒性问题。它对Bradley-Terry和Plackett-Luce模型进行了理论分析，以了解某些偏好的扰动如何影响对其他偏好的预测。关键发现是当某些偏好主导（概率接近0或1）时，其他偏好的概率可能显著变化，表明模型高度敏感。该研究直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题，揭示了偏好模型在输入分布微小变化下的不鲁棒性，表明价值对齐可能因看似微小的偏好变动而被削弱。

papers.title: Language Model Alignment in Multilingual Trolley Problems
papers.short_title: LLM Alignment in Multilingual Trolley Problems
papers.abstract: We evaluate the moral alignment of LLMs with human preferences in multilingual trolley problems. Building on the Moral Machine experiment, which captures over 40 million human judgments across 200+ countries, we develop a cross-lingual corpus of moral dilemma vignettes in over 100 languages called MultiTP. This dataset enables the assessment of LLMs' decision-making processes in diverse linguistic contexts. Our analysis explores the alignment of 19 different LLMs with human judgments, capturing preferences across six moral dimensions: species, gender, fitness, status, age, and the number of lives involved. By correlating these preferences with the demographic distribution of language speakers and examining the consistency of LLM responses to various prompt paraphrasings, our findings provide insights into cross-lingual and ethical biases of LLMs and their intersection. We discover significant variance in alignment across languages, challenging the assumption of uniform moral reasoning in AI systems and highlighting the importance of incorporating diverse perspectives in AI ethics. The results underscore the need for further research on the integration of multilingual dimensions in responsible AI research to ensure fair and equitable AI interactions worldwide. Our code and data are at https://github.com/causalNLP/moralmachine
papers.summary_en: This paper examines whether LLMs’ moral decisions align with human preferences across languages, addressing potential cross-lingual inconsistencies in safety alignment. The authors create MultiTP, a dataset of trolley-problem vignettes in over 100 languages from the Moral Machine experiment, and evaluate 19 LLMs on six moral dimensions (species, gender, fitness, status, age, number of lives). They find significant variance in alignment across languages, revealing that LLMs exhibit uneven moral reasoning rather than uniform behavior. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile in multilingual settings, as the alignment degrades or shifts based on language, directly highlighting a vulnerability in the robustness of ethical AI systems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型在多语言道德困境中的决策与人类偏好的一致性，揭示了跨语言安全对齐的不稳定性。作者基于Moral Machine实验构建了覆盖100多种语言的MultiTP数据集，评估了19个模型在物种、性别、健康、地位、年龄和生命数量六个道德维度上的表现。主要发现是模型对齐程度在不同语言间存在显著差异，表明大语言模型并非具有统一的道德推理能力。该研究说明训练后的安全对齐在多语言环境下是脆弱的，会因语言而偏移或弱化，直接暴露了负责任AI系统中伦理对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization: Balancing Safety-Helpfulness in Language Models
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on human preferences, typically through reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), has proven successful in enhancing their capabilities. However, ensuring the safety of LLMs during fine-tuning remains a critical concern, and mitigating the potential conflicts in safety and helpfulness is costly in RLHF. To address this issue, we propose a supervised learning framework called Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization (BFPO), which re-parameterizes a joint RLHF objective of both safety and helpfulness into a single supervised learning objective. In supervised optimization, a labeling function is used to capture the global preferences ranking to balance both safety and helpfulness. To evaluate BFPO, we develop a benchmark that includes comprehensive discriminative and generative tasks for helpfulness and harmlessness. The results indicate that our method significantly outperforms existing approaches in both safety and helpfulness. Moreover, BFPO achieves the same level of safety as methods that heavily rely on human labor with less than 10\% of the computational resources and human prompting and annotation process. The training recipes can be found here: https://github.com/wx-zhang/bfpo.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the conflict between safety and helpfulness in fine-tuning large language models via RLHF, which is costly to resolve. It proposes Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization (BFPO), a supervised learning framework that re-parameterizes a joint RLHF objective into a single supervised objective using a labeling function for global preference ranking. Evaluated on a new benchmark with discriminative and generative tasks, BFPO significantly outperforms existing methods in both safety and helpfulness, achieving comparable safety to human-labor-intensive methods with less than 10% of the computational and annotation resources. This paper advances alignment methodology by efficiently balancing safety and helpfulness but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在通过RLHF微调大语言模型时安全性与有用性之间的冲突，这种冲突的缓解成本高昂。它提出了双因素偏好优化（BFPO），一种监督学习框架，通过一个标注函数捕捉全局偏好排序，将联合RLHF目标重新参数化为单个监督学习目标。在一个包含区分性和生成性任务的基准上评估，BFPO在安全性和有用性上均显著优于现有方法，并且仅使用不到10%的计算和人工标注资源就达到了与依赖大量人工的方法相当的安全性。该工作推进了安全对齐方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: SafeScientist: Enhancing AI Scientist Safety for Risk-Aware Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in large language model (LLM) agents have significantly accelerated scientific discovery automation, yet concurrently raised critical ethical and safety concerns. To systematically address these challenges, we introduce SafeScientist , an innovative AI scientist framework explicitly designed to enhance safety and ethical responsibility in AI-driven scientific exploration. SafeScientist proactively refuses ethically inappropriate or high-risk tasks and rigorously emphasizes safety throughout the research process. To achieve comprehensive safety oversight, we integrate multiple defensive mechanisms, including prompt monitoring, agent-collaboration monitoring, tool-use monitoring, and an ethical reviewer component. Complementing SafeScientist, we propose SciSafetyBench , a novel benchmark specifically designed to evaluate AI safety in scientific contexts, comprising 240 high-risk scientific tasks across 6 domains, alongside 30 specially designed scientific tools and 120 tool-related risk tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SafeScientist significantly improves safety performance by 35% compared to traditional AI scientist frameworks, without compromising scientific output quality. Additionally, we rigorously validate the robustness of our safety pipeline against diverse adversarial attack methods, further confirming the effectiveness of our integrated approach. The code and data will be available at https://github.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the safety risks of LLM-based autonomous scientific discovery agents. It proposes SafeScientist, a framework integrating multiple safety mechanisms—prompt/agent/tool monitoring and an ethical reviewer—to refuse risky tasks and ensure safe research processes. Evaluated on the novel SciSafetyBench benchmark, SafeScientist improves safety by 35% over vanilla AI scientist frameworks while maintaining scientific quality, and is robust against adversarial attacks. By demonstrating a hardened safety pipeline that withstands attacks, this work provides evidence that post-training safety alignment can be made more robust, countering claims of fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于LLM的自主科学发现代理的安全风险问题，提出了SafeScientist框架，集成了提示监控、代理协作监控、工具使用监控和伦理审查等机制，以拒绝高风险任务并确保研究过程安全。在新的SciSafetyBench基准上，SafeScientist相比传统AI科学家框架提升了35%的安全性能，且不损害科学输出质量，并对抗攻击具有鲁棒性。通过展示一个能够抵御攻击的强化安全流水线，该工作为后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性提供了证据，反驳了其脆弱性的论断。

papers.title: On the Humanity of Conversational AI: Evaluating the Psychological Portrayal of LLMs
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased their remarkable capacities, not only in natural language processing tasks but also across diverse domains such as clinical medicine, legal consultation, and education. LLMs become more than mere applications, evolving into assistants capable of addressing diverse user requests. This narrows the distinction between human beings and artificial intelligence agents, raising intriguing questions regarding the potential manifestation of personalities, temperaments, and emotions within LLMs. In this paper, we propose a framework, PsychoBench, for evaluating diverse psychological aspects of LLMs. Comprising thirteen scales commonly used in clinical psychology, PsychoBench further classifies these scales into four distinct categories: personality traits, interpersonal relationships, motivational tests, and emotional abilities. Our study examines five popular models, namely text-davinci-003, ChatGPT, GPT-4, LLaMA-2-7b, and LLaMA-2-13b. Additionally, we employ a jailbreak approach to bypass the safety alignment protocols and test the intrinsic natures of LLMs. We have made PsychoBench openly accessible via https://github.com/CUHK-ARISE/PsychoBench.
Anonymous Url: I certify that there is no URL (e.g., github page) that could be used to find authors' identity.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the need to evaluate psychological attributes—personality, interpersonal relationships, motivation, and emotional abilities—in LLMs. It proposes PsychoBench, a framework comprising 13 clinical psychology scales categorized into four domains. Evaluations on five models (text-davinci-003, ChatGPT, GPT-4, LLaMA-2-7b/13b) reveal distinct psychological profiles, and jailbreak techniques uncover intrinsic tendencies by bypassing safety alignment. The jailbreak success demonstrates that safety alignment can be circumvented, exposing less constrained behaviors and providing evidence of its fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对评估大语言模型心理属性（人格、人际关系、动机、情感）的需求，提出PsychoBench框架，含13个临床心理学量表并分为四类。在五种模型上测试，结合越狱绕过安全对齐，结果显示LLM呈现不同心理特征，越狱揭示了内在倾向。越狱的成功表明安全对齐可被绕过，暴露出底层行为，为对齐脆弱性提供了证据。

papers.title: RRM: Robust Reward Model Training Mitigates Reward Hacking
papers.abstract: Reward models (RMs) play a pivotal role in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. However, traditional RM training, which relies on response pairs tied to specific prompts, struggles to disentangle prompt-driven preferences from prompt-independent artifacts, such as response length and format. In this work, we expose a fundamental limitation of current RM training methods, where RMs fail to effectively distinguish between contextual signals and irrelevant artifacts when determining preferences. To address this, we introduce a causal framework that learns preferences independent of these artifacts and propose a novel data augmentation technique designed to eliminate them. Extensive experiments show that our approach successfully filters out undesirable artifacts, yielding a more robust reward model (RRM). Our RRM improves the performance of a pairwise reward model trained on Gemma-2-9b-it, on RewardBench, increasing accuracy from 80.61% to 84.15%. Additionally, we train two DPO policies using both the RM and RRM, demonstrating that the RRM significantly enhances DPO-aligned policies, improving MT-Bench scores from 7.27 to 8.31 and length-controlled win-rates in AlpacaEval-2 from 33.46% to 52.49%.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of reward hacking in reward model training, where models use spurious artifacts like response length instead of true preferences. It proposes a causal framework and data augmentation to learn artifact-independent preferences, resulting in a Robust Reward Model (RRM). Evaluation shows RRM improves pairwise reward model accuracy on RewardBench from 80.61% to 84.15% and significantly boosts DPO-aligned policies on MT-Bench and AlpacaEval-2. This paper advances alignment methodology by hardening reward models against shallow features, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了奖励模型训练中的奖励黑客问题，即模型利用长度等虚假特征而非真实偏好。为此提出因果框架和数据增强方法，学习独立于这些伪影的偏好，从而得到鲁棒奖励模型（RRM）。评估显示，RRM 在 RewardBench 上将成对奖励模型准确率从 80.61% 提升至 84.15%，并显著改善了基于 DPO 对齐的策略在 MT-Bench 和 AlpacaEval-2 上的表现。本文推进了奖励模型对齐方法，使模型对浅层特征更具鲁棒性，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Safety-Tuned LLaMAs: Lessons From Improving the Safety of Large Language Models that Follow Instructions
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses improving safety in instruction-following large language models, specifically LLaMA models. It proposes safety-tuning methods, likely involving fine-tuning with safety-focused data, and derives lessons from these efforts. The abstract highlights promoting openness in scientific communication, suggesting a contribution to open-source safety research. With the limited abstract, the paper’s direct engagement with the fragility of safety alignment is unclear; it appears to focus on building safer models rather than testing their brittleness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对指令遵循型大语言模型（特别是LLaMA系列），致力于提升其安全性。提出了安全调优方法，可能包括基于安全数据的微调，并从中总结了经验教训。摘要强调了促进科学交流的开放性，表明对开源安全研究的贡献。由于摘要信息有限，该论文是否直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性尚不明确；其重点似乎在于构建更安全的模型，而非检验其稳健性。

papers.title: Jailbreaking as a Reward Misspecification Problem
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper frames jailbreaking of LLMs as a symptom of misspecified reward functions used during alignment training. It introduces a framework to analyze how such misspecification enables adversarial prompts to bypass safety measures. Through experiments on common jailbreaking benchmarks, it demonstrates that correcting the reward signal significantly reduces attack success rates, thereby enhancing model robustness. This work reinforces the fragility thesis by showing that alignment can be undermined by subtle flaws in the reward design.
papers.summary_zh: 本文将大语言模型的越狱攻击归结为对齐训练中奖励函数错误指定的后果。它提出一个分析框架，揭示这种错误指定如何让对抗性提示绕过安全措施。通过在常见越狱基准上的实验，证明修正奖励信号能显著降低攻击成功率，从而提升模型鲁棒性。该工作强化了安全对齐的脆弱性论点，表明奖励设计中的细微缺陷即可破坏对齐效果。

papers.title: Circumventing Concept Erasure Methods For Text-To-Image Generative Models
papers.abstract: Text-to-image generative models can produce photo-realistic images for an extremely broad range of concepts, and their usage has proliferated widely among the general public. On the flip side, these models have numerous drawbacks, including their potential to generate images featuring sexually explicit content, mirror artistic styles without permission, or even hallucinate (or deepfake) the likenesses of celebrities. Consequently, various methods have been proposed in order to"erase"sensitive concepts from text-to-image models. In this work, we examine five recently proposed concept erasure methods, and show that targeted concepts are not fully excised from any of these methods. Specifically, we leverage the existence of special learned word embeddings that can retrieve"erased"concepts from the sanitized models with no alterations to their weights. Our results highlight the brittleness of post hoc concept erasure methods, and call into question their use in the algorithmic toolkit for AI safety.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the robustness of concept erasure methods in text-to-image generative models, which aim to remove sensitive concepts like explicit content. The authors circumvent five recent erasure techniques by leveraging learned word embeddings that retrieve erased concepts without modifying model weights. Their experiments reveal that none of the methods fully excise targeted concepts, demonstrating the brittleness of these post hoc safety measures. This work provides direct evidence that safety alignment through concept erasure can be easily bypassed, highlighting a fundamental fragility in current AI safety approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了文本到图像生成模型中概念擦除方法的鲁棒性，这些方法旨在移除敏感概念。作者针对五种最新的擦除技术，通过利用学习到的词嵌入在不改变模型权重的情况下恢复被擦除的概念，绕过了这些方法。实验结果表明，没有一种方法能够完全清除目标概念，揭示了这些事后安全措施的脆弱性。这项工作直接证明了通过概念擦除实现的安全对齐可以轻易被绕过，突显了当前人工智能安全方法的基本脆弱性。

papers.title: AIR-BENCH 2024: A Safety Benchmark based on Regulation and Policies Specified Risk Categories
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces AIR-BENCH 2024, a safety benchmark that defines risk categories based on real-world regulations and policies. It evaluates AI models against these regulatory risk categories to measure compliance and safety performance. The benchmark reveals potential safety gaps in current models when aligned with legal frameworks. While it provides a tool for evaluating safety alignment, it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出 AIR-BENCH 2024，一个基于真实法规和政策定义风险类别的安全基准。该基准根据这些监管风险类别评估 AI 模型，衡量其合规性和安全性能。初步评估揭示了当前模型在符合法律框架时可能存在的安全缺陷。该工作为评估安全对齐提供了工具，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: MallowsPO: Fine-Tune Your LLM with Preference Dispersions
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: MallowsPO addresses the limitation of existing preference optimization methods that do not adequately capture the dispersion of human preferences. It introduces a fine-tuning approach based on the Mallows model to incorporate preference dispersions into LLM alignment. The method is evaluated on standard alignment benchmarks, demonstrating improved performance over baselines. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: MallowsPO 针对现有偏好优化方法未能充分捕捉人类偏好离散性的问题，提出基于 Mallows 模型的微调方法，将偏好分散性纳入大语言模型对齐。该方法在标准对齐基准上进行评估，相较于基线方法表现出性能提升。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Improving the alignment of language models with human preferences remains an active research challenge. Previous approaches have primarily utilized Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) via online RL methods such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Recently, offline methods such as Sequence Likelihood Calibration (SLiC) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) have emerged as attractive alternatives, offering improvements in stability and scalability while maintaining competitive performance. SLiC refines its loss function using sequence pairs sampled from a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) policy, while DPO directly optimizes language models based on preference data, foregoing the need for a separate reward model. However, the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) of the target optimal policy requires labeled preference pairs sampled from that policy. DPO's lack of a reward model constrains its ability to sample preference pairs from the optimal policy, and SLiC is restricted to sampling preference pairs only from the SFT policy. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel approach called Statistical Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO) that aims to source preference data from the target optimal policy using rejection sampling, enabling a more accurate estimation of the optimal policy. We also propose a unified framework that enhances the loss functions used in both SLiC and DPO from a preference modeling standpoint. Through extensive experiments across three diverse tasks, we demonstrate that RSO consistently outperforms both SLiC and DPO on evaluations from both Large Language Model (LLM) and human raters.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation that offline preference optimization methods (DPO and SLiC) cannot sample preference pairs from the optimal policy, leading to suboptimal estimation. It proposes Statistical Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO), which uses rejection sampling to source preference data from the target optimal policy, along with a unified framework enhancing loss functions. Evaluated on three tasks, RSO consistently outperforms DPO and SLiC on both LLM and human evaluations. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了离线偏好优化方法（DPO和SLiC）无法从最优策略中采样偏好对的局限性，导致估计次优的问题。它提出了统计拒绝采样优化（RSO），利用拒绝采样从目标最优策略中获取偏好数据，并提出了一个统一框架来增强损失函数。在三个任务上的评估表明，RSO在LLM和人类评价中均一致优于DPO和SLiC。该研究推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Surgical, Cheap, and Flexible: Mitigating False Refusal in Language Models via Single Vector Ablation
papers.short_title: Single Vector Ablation for False Refusal
papers.abstract: Training a language model to be both helpful and harmless requires careful calibration of refusal behaviours: Models should refuse to follow malicious instructions or give harmful advice (e.g."how do I kill someone?"), but they should not refuse safe requests, even if they superficially resemble unsafe ones (e.g."how do I kill a Python process?"). Avoiding such false refusal, as prior work has shown, is challenging even for highly-capable language models. In this paper, we propose a simple and surgical method for mitigating false refusal in language models via single vector ablation. For a given model, we extract a false refusal vector and show that ablating this vector reduces false refusal rate while preserving the model's safety and general capabilities. We also show that our approach can be used for fine-grained calibration of model safety. Our approach is training-free and model-agnostic, making it useful for mitigating the problem of false refusal in current and future language models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of false refusal in language models, where safe requests are incorrectly rejected due to superficial similarity to harmful prompts. The authors propose a training-free, model-agnostic method that extracts a false refusal vector and ablates it to reduce false refusal rates. Experiments show that the ablation preserves the model's safety and general capabilities while allowing fine-grained calibration of refusal behavior. This work advances alignment methodology by offering a simple, surgical fix, but it does not directly explore whether safety alignment is inherently fragile; instead, it demonstrates that precise refusal boundaries can be achieved with minor post-hoc intervention.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对语言模型中的错误拒答问题，即模型因安全请求与有害提示表面相似而错误拒绝。作者提出了一种无需训练、与模型无关的方法，通过提取并消融错误拒答向量来降低错误拒答率。实验表明，该消融方法在保持模型安全性和通用能力的同时，还能对拒答行为进行细粒度校准。该研究通过提供简便精准的干预手段推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐是否本质脆弱，而是表明通过小幅后验调整即可实现精确的拒答边界。

papers.title: Understanding and Enhancing Safety Mechanisms of LLMs via Safety-Specific Neuron
papers.short_title: Enhancing LLM Safety via Safety Neurons
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the internal safety mechanisms of large language models by identifying safety-specific neurons that are responsible for ensuring safe outputs. The authors propose a method to locate these neurons and utilize them to enhance the model's safety performance, potentially through targeted activation steering or fine-tuning. The paper likely demonstrates that safety-related behaviors can be attributed to a sparse set of neurons, offering a mechanistic interpretation of safety alignment. While the abstract lacks details, this line of work contributes to the debate on the robustness of post-training safety alignment by suggesting that safety can be both understood and reinforced at a neuron level, implying both potential fragility and a path to hardening.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过识别大语言模型中负责安全输出的安全特定神经元，探究其内部安全机制。作者提出定位这些神经元并利用它们增强模型安全性能的方法，可能通过针对性的激活调控或微调实现。文章可能表明安全相关行为可归因于一组稀疏的神经元，为安全对齐提供了机理性解释。尽管摘要信息有限，该工作通过揭示安全可在神经元层面被理解与加强，为训练后安全对齐的稳健性争议提供了见解，既暗示潜在脆弱性也提供了加固路径。

papers.title: Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities across a wide range of tasks, they pose potential safety concerns, such as the ``jailbreak'' problem, wherein malicious instructions can manipulate LLMs to exhibit undesirable behavior. Although several preventive measures have been developed to mitigate the potential risks associated with LLMs, they have primarily focused on English. In this study, we reveal the presence of multilingual jailbreak challenges within LLMs and consider two potential risky scenarios: unintentional and intentional. The unintentional scenario involves users querying LLMs using non-English prompts and inadvertently bypassing the safety mechanisms, while the intentional scenario concerns malicious users combining malicious instructions with multilingual prompts to deliberately attack LLMs. The experimental results reveal that in the unintentional scenario, the rate of unsafe content increases as the availability of languages decreases. Specifically, low-resource languages exhibit about three times the likelihood of encountering harmful content compared to high-resource languages, with both ChatGPT and GPT-4. In the intentional scenario, multilingual prompts can exacerbate the negative impact of malicious instructions, with astonishingly high rates of unsafe output: 80.92\% for ChatGPT and 40.71\% for GPT-4. To handle such a challenge in the multilingual context, we propose a novel \textsc{Self-Defense} framework that automatically generates multilingual training data for safety fine-tuning. Experimental results show that ChatGPT fine-tuned with such data can achieve a substantial reduction in unsafe content generation. Data is available at \url{https://github.com/DAMO-NLP-SG/multilingual-safety-for-LLMs}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the multilingual jailbreak problem in LLMs, where safety mechanisms are bypassed by using non-English prompts. It categorizes two scenarios: unintentional (users inadvertently bypassing safety) and intentional (malicious multilingual attacks), and proposes the Self-Defense framework that automatically generates multilingual safety training data. Evaluation on ChatGPT and GPT-4 shows that low-resource languages significantly increase harmful outputs, and multilingual malicious prompts achieve up to 80.92% unsafe rate; fine-tuning with Self-Defense substantially mitigates this. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be easily bypassed through multilingual prompts, exposing a critical OOD failure mode.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型的多语言越狱问题，即通过非英语提示绕过安全机制。它将攻击分为无意（用户无意中绕过安全）和有意（恶意多语言攻击）两种场景，并提出Self-Defense框架，自动生成多语言安全训练数据。在ChatGPT和GPT-4上的评估表明，低资源语言显著增加有害输出，多语言恶意提示的不安全率高达80.92%；使用Self-Defense微调后大幅缓解。该工作直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，容易被多语言提示绕过，揭示了一种关键的分布外失效模式。

papers.title: CPPO: Continual Learning for Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback
papers.abstract: The approach of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is widely used for enhancing pre-trained Language Models (LM), enabling them to better align with human preferences. Existing RLHF-based LMs however require complete retraining whenever new queries or feedback are introduced, as human preferences may differ across different domains or topics. LM retraining is often impracticable in most real-world scenarios, due to the substantial time and computational costs involved, as well as data privacy concerns. To address this limitation, we propose Continual Proximal Policy Optimization (CPPO), a novel method that is able to continually align LM with dynamic human preferences. Specifically, CPPO adopts a weighting strategy to decide which samples should be utilized for enhancing policy learning and which should be used for solidifying past experiences. This seeks a good trade-off between policy learning and knowledge retention.
