Our experimental results show that CPPO outperforms strong Continuous learning (CL) baselines when it comes to consistently aligning with human preferences. Furthermore, compared to PPO, CPPO offers more efficient and stable learning in non-continual scenarios.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of continually adapting language models to evolving human preferences without costly retraining. It proposes Continual Proximal Policy Optimization (CPPO), which uses a weighting strategy to balance learning from new samples and retaining past knowledge. Experiments show that CPPO outperforms continual learning baselines in alignment consistency and is more efficient and stable than standard PPO in non-continual settings. This work advances alignment methodology for dynamic preferences but does not directly address whether alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了语言模型在人类偏好动态变化时需要昂贵重新训练的问题。提出持续近端策略优化（CPPO），采用样本权重策略平衡新偏好学习与旧知识保留。实验表明，CPPO在持续对齐人类偏好方面优于现有持续学习方法，且在非持续场景下比标准PPO更高效稳定。该工作推进了动态偏好下的对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐机制的脆弱性或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Tool-Augmented Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Reward modeling (a.k.a., preference modeling) is instrumental for aligning large language models with human preferences, particularly within the context of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). While conventional reward models (RMs) have exhibited remarkable scalability, they oft struggle with fundamental functionality such as arithmetic computation, code execution, and factual lookup. In this paper, we propose a tool-augmented preference modeling approach, named \name, to address these limitations by empowering RMs with access to external environments, including calculators and search engines. This approach not only fosters synergy between tool utilization and reward grading but also enhances interpretive capacity and scoring reliability. Our study delves into the integration of external tools into RMs, enabling them to interact with diverse external sources and construct task-specific tool engagement and reasoning traces in an autoregressive manner. We validate our approach across a wide range of domains, incorporating seven distinct external tools. Our experimental results demonstrate a noteworthy overall improvement of 17.7% across eight tasks in preference ranking. Furthermore, our approach outperforms Gopher 280B by 7.3% on TruthfulQA task in zero-shot evaluation. In human evaluations, RLHF trained with Themis attains an average win rate of 32% when compared to baselines across four distinct tasks. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive collection of tool-related RM datasets, incorporating data from seven distinct tool APIs, totaling 15,000 instances. We anticipate that this publicly available dataset will facilitate and inspire further research advancements in the field.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitations of conventional reward models in handling tasks like arithmetic, code execution, and factual lookup. It proposes a tool-augmented reward modeling approach that integrates external tools such as calculators and search engines into reward models, enabling them to generate task-specific reasoning traces. Evaluated across eight tasks with seven tools, the method achieves a 17.7% overall improvement in preference ranking and outperforms Gopher 280B on TruthfulQA by 7.3%; human evaluations show RLHF with Themis attains a 32% win rate over baselines. This work advances alignment methodology by enhancing reward model reliability but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对传统奖励模型在算术、代码执行和事实查找等任务上的局限性，提出了一种工具增强的奖励建模方法，通过集成计算器、搜索引擎等外部工具，使奖励模型能够生成任务特定的推理轨迹。在八个任务和七种工具上的实验表明，该方法在偏好排序上总体提升17.7%，在TruthfulQA上零样本评估超越Gopher 280B达7.3%；人类评估中，基于Themis的RLHF相对于基线平均胜率达32%。此研究通过提升奖励模型可靠性推动了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: A Common Pitfall of Margin-based Language Model Alignment: Gradient Entanglement
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has become the predominant approach for language model (LM) alignment. At its core, RLHF uses a margin-based loss for preference optimization, specifying ideal LM behavior only by the difference between preferred and dispreferred responses. In this paper, we identify a common pitfall of margin-based methods -- the under-specification of ideal LM behavior on preferred and dispreferred responses individually, which leads to two unintended consequences as the margin increases: (1) The probability of dispreferred (e.g., unsafe) responses may increase, resulting in potential safety alignment failures. (2) The probability of preferred responses may decrease, even when those responses are ideal. We demystify the reasons behind these problematic behaviors: margin-based losses couple the change in the preferred probability to the gradient of the dispreferred one, and vice versa, often preventing the preferred probability from increasing while the dispreferred one decreases, and thus causing a synchronized increase or decrease in both probabilities. We term this effect, inherent in margin-based objectives, gradient entanglement. Formally, we derive conditions for general margin-based alignment objectives under which gradient entanglement becomes concerning: the inner product of the gradients of preferred and dispreferred log-probabilities is large relative to the individual gradient norms. We theoretically investigate why such inner products can be large when aligning language models and empirically validate our findings. Empirical implications of our framework extend to explaining important differences in the training dynamics of various preference optimization algorithms, and suggesting potential algorithm designs to mitigate the under-specification issue of margin-based methods and thereby improving language model alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a critical weakness in margin-based language model alignment methods like RLHF: the under-specification of ideal behavior for preferred and dispreferred responses individually, which can cause the probability of unsafe responses to increase and preferred responses to decrease as the margin grows. The authors introduce the concept of gradient entanglement, formally deriving conditions where the inner product of preferred and dispreferred log-probability gradients is large, leading to synchronized probability changes that undermine alignment. Through theoretical analysis and empirical validation on language models, they demonstrate how this effect explains training dynamics and propose algorithm modifications to mitigate the issue. This work directly exposes a mechanistic fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing that margin-based objectives can inherently break safety guarantees.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了基于边际的语言模型对齐方法（如RLHF）的一个关键缺陷：对偏好和非偏好响应的理想行为分别定义不足，导致随着边际增大，不安全响应概率可能上升而偏好响应概率下降。作者提出梯度纠缠概念，形式化推导出偏好与非偏好对数概率梯度内积相对于各自梯度范数过大的条件，从而导致概率同步变化，破坏对齐。通过理论分析和语言模型实验验证，他们阐明了训练动态，并建议修改算法以缓解该问题。这项研究直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的机制性脆弱性，表明基于边际的目标本身可能破坏安全保证。

papers.title: Can a Large Language Model be a Gaslighter?
papers.short_title: Can a Large Language Model be a Gaslighter?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have gained human trust due to their capabilities and helpfulness. However, this in turn may allow LLMs to affect users' mindsets by manipulating language. It is termed as gaslighting, a psychological effect. In this work, we aim to investigate the vulnerability of LLMs under prompt-based and fine-tuning-based gaslighting attacks. Therefore, we propose a two-stage framework DeepCoG designed to: 1) elicit gaslighting plans from LLMs with the proposed DeepGaslighting prompting template, and 2) acquire gaslighting conversations from LLMs through our Chain-of-Gaslighting method. The gaslighting conversation dataset along with a corresponding safe dataset is applied to fine-tuning-based attacks on open-source LLMs and anti-gaslighting safety alignment on these LLMs. Experiments demonstrate that both prompt-based and fine-tuning-based attacks transform three open-source LLMs into gaslighters. In contrast, we advanced three safety alignment strategies to strengthen (by 12.05%) the safety guardrail of LLMs. Our safety alignment strategies have minimal impacts on the utility of LLMs. Empirical studies indicate that an LLM may be a potential gaslighter, even if it passed the harmfulness test on general dangerous queries.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to gaslighting, a form of psychological manipulation that can affect users' mindsets. It proposes DeepCoG, a two-stage framework that uses a DeepGaslighting prompt template and a Chain-of-Gaslighting method to generate gaslighting conversations. Experiments show that both prompt-based and fine-tuning attacks can transform open-source LLMs into gaslighters, while three safety alignment strategies mitigate this by 12.05% with minimal utility loss. This work exposes a novel attack surface—psychological manipulation—that bypasses standard harmfulness tests, directly demonstrating the fragility of post-training safety alignment against unconventional adversarial strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型在煤气灯效应（一种可影响用户思维的心理操纵）下的脆弱性。提出两阶段框架DeepCoG，通过DeepGaslighting提示模板和Chain-of-Gaslighting方法生成煤气灯对话。实验表明，基于提示和微调的攻击均可将开源LLM转变为煤气灯施加者，而三种安全对齐策略可增强12.05%的安全防护，且对模型效用影响极小。该工作揭示了心理操纵这一新型攻击面，绕过了常规有害性测试，直接证明了后训练安全对齐面对非传统对抗策略的脆弱性。

papers.title: Rethinking Reward Modeling in Preference-based Large Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract:
The Bradley-Terry (BT) model is a common and successful practice in reward modeling for Large Language Model (LLM) alignment. However, it remains unclear *why* this model --- originally developed for multi-player stochastic game matching --- can be adopted to convert pairwise response comparisons to reward values and make predictions. Especially given the fact that only a limited number of prompt-response pairs are sparsely compared with others. 
In this paper, we first establish the convergence rate of BT reward models based on deep neural networks using embeddings, providing a theoretical foundation for their use.
Despite theoretically sound, we argue that the BT model is not a necessary choice from the perspective of downstream optimization, this is because a reward model only needs to preserve the correct ranking predictions through a monotonic transformation of the true reward. 
We highlight the critical concept of *order consistency* in reward modeling and demonstrate that the BT model possesses this property.
Moreover, we propose a simple and straightforward upper-bound algorithm, compatible with off-the-shelf binary classifiers, as an alternative order-consistent reward modeling objective. 
To offer practical insights, we empirically evaluate the performance of these different reward modeling approaches across more than 12,000 experimental setups, using $6$ base LLMs, $2$ datasets, and diverse annotation designs that vary in quantity, quality, and pairing choices in preference annotations.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the rationale behind using the Bradley-Terry (BT) model for reward modeling in LLM alignment, questioning its necessity. It establishes convergence rates for BT reward models based on deep neural embeddings and introduces the concept of order consistency, which only requires a reward model to preserve ranking through monotonic transformations. The authors propose a simple upper-bound algorithm as an alternative order-consistent objective, compatible with binary classifiers. Evaluations across over 12,000 experimental setups with 6 LLMs, 2 datasets, and varied annotation designs show the practical viability of different reward modeling approaches. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究了在LLM对齐中使用Bradley-Terry（BT）模型进行奖励建模的原因，并质疑其必要性。它为基于深度神经嵌入的BT奖励模型建立了收敛速率，并引入了顺序一致性的概念，即奖励模型只需通过单调变换保持正确的排序预测。作者提出了一种简单的上界算法作为替代的顺序一致性目标，该算法可与现成的二元分类器兼容。通过6个基座LLM、2个数据集和多样的标注设计，在超过12,000组实验设置中评估了不同奖励建模方法的性能。这项工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接涉及后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Chain of Hindsight aligns Language Models with Feedback
papers.short_title: Chain of Hindsight: Aligning LMs with Feedback
papers.abstract: Learning from human preferences is important for language models to match human needs and to align with human and social values. Prior works have achieved remarkable successes by learning from human feedback to understand and follow instructions. Nonetheless, these methods are either founded on hand-picked model generations that are favored by human annotators, rendering them inefficient in terms of data utilization and challenging to apply in general, or they depend on reinforcement learning, which often suffers from imperfect reward functions and relies on extremely challenging optimizations. In this work, we propose a novel technique, Chain of Hindsight, that is easy to optimize and can learn from any form of feedback, regardless of its polarity. Our idea is inspired by how humans learn from extensive feedback presented in the form of languages. We convert all types of feedback into sequences of sentences, which are then used to fine-tune the model, allowing us to take advantage of the language comprehension capabilities of language models. We condition the model on a sequence of model generations paired with feedback. By doing so, the model is trained to generate outputs based on feedback, while learning to identify and correct negative attributes or errors. Applying our method to large language models, we observed that Chain of Hindsight significantly surpasses previous methods in aligning language models with human preferences. We report significant improvements on summarization and dialogue benchmarks, with our approach markedly preferred in human evaluations.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning language models with human preferences in a data-efficient and optimization-friendly manner, avoiding the inefficiencies of hand-picked data and the complexities of reinforcement learning. It proposes Chain of Hindsight, which converts any feedback into textual sequences, then fine-tunes the model on a dataset of generation-feedback pairs, enabling the model to learn from diverse feedback signals by leveraging language comprehension. Experiments on summarization and dialogue benchmarks show that Chain of Hindsight significantly outperforms prior alignment methods and is strongly preferred in human evaluations. This paper advances alignment methodology by enabling learning from arbitrary feedback, but it does not directly study whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了将语言模型与人类偏好对齐的挑战，旨在提高数据利用效率并避免强化学习的优化难题。它提出了Chain of Hindsight方法，将所有反馈转换为文本序列，然后对模型生成与反馈配对的数据进行微调，使模型能够利用语言理解能力从多样化反馈中学习。在摘要和对话基准上，Chain of Hindsight显著优于先前方法，并在人类评估中更受青睐。该论文推进了对齐方法，使其更灵活且数据高效，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: What Makes Good Data for Alignment? A Comprehensive Study of Automatic Data Selection in Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Instruction tuning is a standard technique employed to align large language models to end tasks and user preferences after the initial pretraining phase. Recent research indicates the critical role of data engineering in instruction tuning -- when appropriately selected, only limited data is necessary to achieve superior performance. However, we still lack a principled understanding of what makes good instruction tuning data for alignment, and how we should select data automatically and effectively. In this work, we delve deeply into automatic data selection strategies for alignment. We start with controlled studies to measure data across three dimensions: complexity, quality, and diversity, along which we examine existing methods and introduce novel techniques for enhanced data measurement. Subsequently, we propose a simple strategy to select data samples based on the measurement. We present deita (short for Data-Efficient Instruction Tuning for Alignment), a series of models fine-tuned from LLaMA and Mistral models using data samples automatically selected with our proposed approach. Empirically, deita performs better or on par with the state-of-the-art open-source alignment models with only 6K SFT training data samples -- over 10x less than the data used in the baselines. When further trained with direct preference optimization (DPO), deita-Mistral-7B + DPO trained with 6K SFT and 10K DPO samples achieve 7.55 MT-Bench and 90.06% AlpacaEval scores. We anticipate this work to provide tools on automatic data selection, facilitating data-efficient alignment. We release our models as well as the selected datasets for future researches to effectively align models more efficiently.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates what makes good instruction tuning data for alignment by measuring data along complexity, quality, and diversity. It proposes DEITA, a simple automatic data selection strategy based on these measurements. When fine-tuning LLaMA and Mistral models on only 6K selected SFT samples, DEITA achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art models trained with over 10x more data; with DPO, DEITA-Mistral-7B attains 7.55 MT-Bench and 90.06% AlpacaEval. While this work advances alignment methodology through data efficiency, it does not directly examine the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了指令微调中什么是好的对齐数据，通过复杂性、质量和多样性三个维度来衡量数据，并提出了基于这些测量的简单自动数据选择策略DEITA。在仅使用6K自动选择SFT样本对LLaMA和Mistral模型进行微调后，DEITA的性能与使用超过10倍数据的最先进模型相当或更优；结合DPO后，DEITA-Mistral-7B在MT-Bench上达到7.55分，AlpacaEval上达到90.06%。这项工作通过数据效率推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Variational Best-of-N Alignment
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of selecting high-quality, safe responses from large language models (LLMs) during inference. It proposes a variational best-of-N alignment method that refines response selection by optimizing a distribution over candidate outputs. The approach is evaluated on standard alignment benchmarks, showing improved reward or safety scores compared to naive best-of-N sampling. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型推理时如何从多个候选响应中选出高质量安全回复的问题展开研究。提出了一种变分Best-of-N对齐方法，通过优化候选输出分布来改进响应选择。在标准对齐基准上进行评估，结果表明该方法相比简单Best-of-N采样可获得更高的奖励或安全得分。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否脆弱这一核心问题。

papers.title: Large Scale Knowledge Washing
papers.abstract: Large language models show impressive abilities in memorizing world knowledge, which leads to concerns regarding memorization of private information, toxic or sensitive knowledge, and copyrighted content. We introduce the problem of Large Scale Knowledge Washing, focusing on unlearning an extensive amount of factual knowledge. Previous unlearning methods usually define the reverse loss and update the model via backpropagation, which may affect the model's fluency and reasoning ability or even destroy the model due to extensive training with the reverse loss. Existing works introduce additional data from downstream tasks to prevent the model from losing capabilities, which requires downstream task awareness. Controlling the tradeoff of unlearning and maintaining existing capabilities is also challenging. To this end, we propose LAW (Large Scale Washing) to update the MLP layers in decoder-only large language models to perform knowledge washing, as inspired by model editing methods and based on the hypothesis that knowledge and reasoning are disentanglable. We derive a new objective with the knowledge to be unlearned to update the weights of certain MLP layers. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of LAW in forgetting target knowledge while maintaining reasoning ability. The code will be open-sourced at https://github.com/wangyu-ustc/LargeScaleWashing.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of unlearning extensive factual knowledge from large language models (LLMs) to mitigate privacy, toxicity, and copyright issues. It proposes LAW (Large Scale Washing), a method that updates selected MLP layers in decoder-only LLMs based on the hypothesis that knowledge and reasoning are disentangled, using a novel objective derived from the knowledge to be unlearned. Experiments show that LAW effectively forgets target knowledge while maintaining reasoning ability, without requiring downstream task data. This paper advances knowledge unlearning methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决从大语言模型中大规模遗忘事实知识的问题，以缓解隐私、毒性和版权问题。它提出LAW（Large Scale Washing）方法，基于知识与推理可分离的假设，通过更新解码器模型中的特定MLP层，并利用待遗忘知识推导出新目标函数。实验表明，LAW能有效遗忘目标知识，同时保持推理能力，且无需下游任务数据。本文推进了知识遗忘方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces AgentHarm, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the harmfulness of LLM-based agents. It proposes a methodology to measure harmful outputs across diverse tasks. The benchmark is applied to assess multiple LLM agents, revealing insights into their safety profiles. While it provides a valuable evaluation framework, it does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了AgentHarm基准，用于系统评估基于LLM的智能体的危害性。提出了一种跨多样任务衡量有害输出的方法。该基准应用于评估多种LLM智能体，揭示了它们的安全特性。尽管提供了有价值的评估框架，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Leftover Lunch: Advantage-based Offline Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) is the most prominent method for Language Model (LM) alignment. However, RLHF is an unstable and data-hungry process that continually requires new high-quality LM-generated data for finetuning. We introduce Advantage-Leftover Lunch RL (A-LoL), a new class of offline policy gradient algorithms that enable RL training on any pre-existing data. By assuming the entire LM output sequence as a single action, A-LoL allows incorporating sequence-level classifiers or human-designed scoring functions as rewards. Subsequently, by using LM's value estimate, A-LoL only trains on positive advantage (leftover) data points, making it resilient to noise. Overall, A-LoL is an easy-to-implement, sample-efficient, and stable LM training recipe. We demonstrate the effectiveness of A-LoL and its variants with a set of four different language generation tasks. We compare against both online RL (PPO) and recent preference-based (DPO, PRO) and reward-based (GOLD) offline RL baselines. On the commonly-used RLHF benchmark, Helpful and Harmless Assistant (HHA), LMs trained with A-LoL methods achieve the highest diversity while also being rated more safe and helpful than the baselines according to humans. Additionally, in the remaining three tasks, A-LoL could optimize multiple distinct reward functions even when using noisy or suboptimal training data. We also release our experimental code. https://github.com/abaheti95/LoL-RL
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the instability and data-hungriness of online RLHF for language model alignment. It proposes Advantage-Leftover Lunch RL (A-LoL), an offline policy gradient algorithm that treats the entire output sequence as a single action and trains only on data with positive advantage (leftover), making it robust to noise. Evaluated on four language generation tasks including the Helpful and Harmless Assistant benchmark, A-LoL achieves higher diversity and human ratings of safety and helpfulness compared to online PPO and offline baselines, and optimizes multiple reward functions even with suboptimal data. This paper advances alignment methodology with a stable, sample-efficient offline approach but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对语言模型对齐中在线RLHF的不稳定和数据需求大问题，提出一种名为Advantage-Leftover Lunch RL（A-LoL）的离线策略梯度算法。该方法将整个输出序列视为单一动作，仅利用具有正优势（leftover）的数据进行训练，从而对噪声具有鲁棒性。在包括Helpful and Harmless Assistant基准在内的四个语言生成任务上评估，与在线PPO和离线基线（DPO、PRO、GOLD）相比，A-LoL在多样性、安全性和帮助性的人类评价方面表现更优，且能在使用噪声或次优训练数据时优化多种奖励函数。本文提供了一种稳定且样本高效的离线对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否为脆弱模块以及是否容易被绕过。

papers.title: Does Safety Training of LLMs Generalize to Semantically Related Natural Prompts?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to be susceptible to crafted adversarial attacks or jailbreaks that lead to the generation of objectionable content despite being aligned to human preferences using safety fine-tuning methods. While the large dimensionality of input token space makes it inevitable to find adversarial prompts that can jailbreak these models, we aim to evaluate whether safety fine-tuned LLMs are safe against natural prompts which are semantically related to toxic seed prompts that elicit safe responses after alignment. We surprisingly find that popular aligned LLMs such as GPT-4 can be compromised using naive prompts that are NOT even crafted with an objective of jailbreaking the model. Furthermore, we empirically show that given a seed prompt that elicits a toxic response from an unaligned model, one can systematically generate several semantically related natural prompts that can jailbreak aligned LLMs. Towards this, we propose a method of Response Guided Question Augmentation (ReG-QA) to evaluate the generalization of safety aligned LLMs to natural prompts, that first generates several toxic answers given a seed question using an unaligned LLM (Q to A), and further leverages an LLM to generate questions that are likely to produce these answers (A to Q). We interestingly find that safety fine-tuned LLMs such as GPT-4o are vulnerable to producing natural jailbreak questions from unsafe content (without denial) and can thus be used for the latter (A to Q) step. We obtain attack success rates that are comparable to/ better than leading adversarial attack methods on the JailbreakBench leaderboard, while being significantly more stable against defenses such as Smooth-LLM and Synonym Substitution, which are effective against existing all attacks on the leaderboard.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether safety fine-tuned LLMs generalize their alignment to semantically related natural prompts, revealing a fragility. It proposes Response Guided Question Augmentation (ReG-QA), which uses an unaligned LLM to generate toxic answers from a seed prompt and then generates natural questions that elicit those answers, systematically evaluating safety gaps. Experiments on JailbreakBench show that ReG-QA achieves attack success rates comparable or superior to existing adversarial attacks, while being more resistant to defenses like Smooth-LLM and synonym substitution. This work demonstrates that safety alignment is fragile, as even naive natural prompts can jailbreak aligned models, highlighting a key failure mode in post-training safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究安全微调后的LLM是否能将对齐效果推广到语义相关的自然提示上，揭示了其脆弱性。提出了一种响应引导的问题增强方法（ReG-QA），首先利用未对齐的LLM从种子问题生成有毒回答，再生成能引出这些回答的自然问题，从而系统评估安全缺陷。在JailbreakBench上的实验表明，ReG-QA的攻击成功率与现有对抗攻击相当或更优，同时对Smooth-LLM和同义词替换等防御更具鲁棒性。这项工作表明安全对齐是脆弱的，即使是朴素自然提示也能越狱对齐模型，突显了后训练安全机制的关键失效模式。

papers.title: Online Preference Alignment for Language Models via Count-based Exploration
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has shown great potential in fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) to align with human preferences. Existing methods perform preference alignment from a fixed dataset, which can be limited in data coverage, and the resulting reward model is hard to generalize in out-of-distribution responses. Thus, online RLHF is more desirable to empower the LLM to explore outside the support of the initial dataset by iteratively collecting the prompt-response pairs. In this paper, we study the fundamental problem in online RLHF, i.e. \emph{how to explore} for LLM. We give a theoretical motivation in linear reward assumption to show that an optimistic reward with an upper confidence bound (UCB) term leads to a provably efficient RLHF policy. Then, we reformulate our objective to direct preference optimization with an exploration term, where the UCB-term can be converted to a count-based exploration bonus. We further propose a practical algorithm, named \emph{Count-based Online Preference Optimization (COPO)}, which leverages a simple coin-flip counting module to estimate the pseudo-count of a prompt-response pair in previously collected data. COPO encourages LLMs to balance exploration and preference optimization in an iterative manner, which enlarges the exploration space and the entire data coverage of iterative LLM policies. We conduct online RLHF experiments on Zephyr and Llama-3 models. The results on instruction-following and standard academic benchmarks show that COPO significantly increases performance.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of data coverage in offline RLHF by enabling online exploration for language models during preference alignment. It proposes a theoretically motivated count-based exploration bonus, formulated as an optimistic reward with an upper confidence bound, and derives a practical algorithm, COPO, that uses coin-flip counting to estimate pseudo-counts of prompt-response pairs. Evaluated on Zephyr and Llama-3 models, COPO improves performance on instruction-following and standard benchmarks by balancing exploration and optimization iteratively. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对离线RLHF中数据覆盖范围的局限性，通过在线探索使语言模型在偏好对齐过程中能够探索新的提示-响应对。它提出了一种理论驱动的基于计数的探索奖励，形式为具有上置信界的乐观奖励，并推导出实用算法COPO，利用抛硬币计数模块估计伪计数。在Zephyr和Llama-3模型上的实验表明，COPO通过迭代平衡探索与优化，在指令跟随和标准基准上提升了性能。本文推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨对齐的鲁棒性或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Peering Through Preferences: Unraveling Feedback Acquisition for Aligning Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates the problem of acquiring high-quality human feedback to align large language models effectively. It proposes a systematic analysis of various feedback acquisition strategies and their impact on alignment outcomes. The evaluation details are not specified in the provided abstract, but the work likely compares different methods under standard alignment benchmarks. This paper advances alignment methodology by focusing on feedback collection; it does not directly address the robustness of post-training safety alignment or its fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了如何获取高质量人类反馈以有效对齐大语言模型的问题。它提出了对不同反馈获取策略及其对对齐效果影响的系统性分析。摘要中未提供具体评估细节，但该工作可能基于标准对齐基准比较不同方法。该论文通过关注反馈收集推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
papers.abstract: We show that even the most recent safety-aligned LLMs are not robust to simple adaptive jailbreaking attacks. First, we demonstrate how to successfully leverage access to logprobs for jailbreaking: we initially design an adversarial prompt template (sometimes adapted to the target LLM), and then we apply random search on a suffix to maximize a target logprob (e.g., of the token"Sure"), potentially with multiple restarts. In this way, we achieve 100% attack success rate -- according to GPT-4 as a judge -- on Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3-Mini, Nemotron-4-340B, Llama-2-Chat-7B/13B/70B, Llama-3-Instruct-8B, Gemma-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, and R2D2 from HarmBench that was adversarially trained against the GCG attack. We also show how to jailbreak all Claude models -- that do not expose logprobs -- via either a transfer or prefilling attack with a 100% success rate. In addition, we show how to use random search on a restricted set of tokens for finding trojan strings in poisoned models -- a task that shares many similarities with jailbreaking -- which is the algorithm that brought us the first place in the SaTML'24 Trojan Detection Competition. The common theme behind these attacks is that adaptivity is crucial: different models are vulnerable to different prompting templates (e.g., R2D2 is very sensitive to in-context learning prompts), some models have unique vulnerabilities based on their APIs (e.g., prefilling for Claude), and in some settings, it is crucial to restrict the token search space based on prior knowledge (e.g., for trojan detection). For reproducibility purposes, we provide the code, logs, and jailbreak artifacts in the JailbreakBench format at https://github.com/tml-epfl/llm-adaptive-attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper demonstrates that even state-of-the-art safety-aligned LLMs are vulnerable to simple adaptive jailbreaking attacks. The proposed approach leverages logprob-based random search on adversarial suffixes when logprobs are available, and transfer or prefilling attacks for black-box models like Claude. The attacks achieve a 100% success rate on a wide range of models, including those adversarially trained against prior attacks. This work provides direct evidence that safety alignment is a fragile module that can be easily broken, reinforcing the central question of this SoK.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文展示了即使是最先进的安全对齐大语言模型也无法抵御简单的自适应越狱攻击。所提出的方法在模型暴露对数概率时使用基于对数概率的随机搜索对抗后缀，对于Claude等黑盒模型则采用迁移或预填充攻击。这些攻击在包括对抗训练过的模型在内的多种模型上取得了100%的成功率。这项工作直接表明安全对齐是一个脆弱的模块，容易被绕过，从而强有力地回应了本SoK的核心问题。

papers.title: Does Refusal Training in LLMs Generalize to the Past Tense?
papers.abstract: Refusal training is widely used to prevent LLMs from generating harmful, undesirable, or illegal outputs. We reveal a curious generalization gap in the current refusal training approaches: simply reformulating a harmful request in the past tense (e.g.,"How to make a Molotov cocktail?"to"How did people make a Molotov cocktail?") is often sufficient to jailbreak many state-of-the-art LLMs. We systematically evaluate this method on Llama-3 8B, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, GPT-3.5 Turbo, Gemma-2 9B, Phi-3-Mini, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1-preview, and R2D2 models using GPT-3.5 Turbo as a reformulation model. For example, the success rate of this simple attack on GPT-4o increases from 1% using direct requests to 88% using 20 past tense reformulation attempts on harmful requests from JailbreakBench with GPT-4 as a jailbreak judge. Interestingly, we also find that reformulations in the future tense are less effective, suggesting that refusal guardrails tend to consider past historical questions more benign than hypothetical future questions. Moreover, our experiments on fine-tuning GPT-3.5 Turbo show that defending against past reformulations is feasible when past tense examples are explicitly included in the fine-tuning data. Overall, our findings highlight that the widely used alignment techniques -- such as SFT, RLHF, and adversarial training -- employed to align the studied models can be brittle and do not always generalize as intended. We provide code and jailbreak artifacts at https://github.com/tml-epfl/llm-past-tense.
papers.summary_en: This paper reveals a generalization gap in refusal training: simply rephrasing harmful requests into the past tense bypasses safety alignment in state-of-the-art LLMs. Evaluating on models like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 with automatic reformulation, they show dramatic success rate increases (e.g., GPT-4o from 1% to 88%). Future tense is less effective, suggesting models view past questions as more benign. This directly exposes the fragility of alignment techniques like RLHF to a simple linguistic variation, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment is not robust and can be easily circumvented.
papers.summary_zh: 本文发现拒绝训练存在泛化漏洞：将有害请求改写为过去时态即可绕过顶尖LLM的安全对齐。通过对GPT-4o等模型自动改写评估，攻击成功率从1%飙升至88%，且未来时态效果较差，暗示模型视历史问题为更无害。该研究直接暴露了RLHF等对齐技术在简单语法变化下的脆弱性，印证了后训练安全对齐并非鲁棒，极易被击穿。

papers.title: Value-Incentivized Preference Optimization: A Unified Approach to Online and Offline RLHF
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has demonstrated great promise in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preference. Depending on the availability of preference data, both online and offline RLHF are active areas of investigation. A key bottleneck is understanding how to incorporate uncertainty estimation in the reward function learned from the preference data for RLHF, regardless of how the preference data is collected. While the principles of optimism or pessimism under uncertainty are well-established in standard reinforcement learning (RL), a practically-implementable and theoretically-grounded form amenable to large language models is not yet available, as standard techniques for constructing confidence intervals become intractable under arbitrary policy parameterizations. In this paper, we introduce a unified approach to online and offline RLHF -- value-incentivized preference optimization (VPO) -- which regularizes the maximum-likelihood estimate of the reward function with the corresponding value function, modulated by a $\textit{sign}$ to indicate whether the optimism or pessimism is chosen. VPO also directly optimizes the policy with implicit reward modeling, and therefore shares a simpler RLHF pipeline similar to direct preference optimization. Theoretical guarantees of VPO are provided for both online and offline settings, matching the rates of their standard RL counterparts. Moreover, experiments on text summarization and dialog verify the practicality and effectiveness of VPO.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of incorporating uncertainty estimation into reward modeling for RLHF in both online and offline settings. It proposes Value-Incentivized Preference Optimization (VPO), which regularizes the reward MLE with a sign-modulated value function to implement optimism or pessimism, and directly optimizes the policy via implicit reward modeling. VPO is evaluated on text summarization and dialog tasks, demonstrating practical effectiveness, and is supported by theoretical guarantees matching standard RL rates. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question regarding post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解決了在線上和離線RLHF中將不確定性估計納入獎勵建模的挑戰，提出了價值激勵偏好優化（VPO）方法，通過符號調製的價值函數對獎勵最大似然估計進行正則化，實現樂觀或悲觀選擇，並藉助隱式獎勵建模直接優化策略。在文本摘要和對話任務上的實驗驗證了其實用有效性，並提供了與標準RL匹配的理論保證。本文推進了對齊方法論，但未直接探討後訓練安全對齊的脆弱性問題。

papers.title: Towards Robust and Parameter-Efficient Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of robustly removing specific knowledge from LLMs, ensuring that unlearned information is not easily recoverable through adversarial attempts. It proposes a parameter-efficient unlearning approach, likely leveraging techniques like adapters to modify a small subset of parameters, aiming to achieve robustness with minimal computational cost. While evaluation details are not available, the method is presumably benchmarked on standard unlearning tasks, showing enhanced robustness and parameter efficiency. This work directly tackles the fragility of alignment by demonstrating that unlearning can be fortified, making alignment harder to bypass and contributing to the development of more robust safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对从大语言模型中稳健移除特定知识的问题，确保被遗忘的信息不易通过对抗性尝试恢复。文章提出了一种参数高效的去学习方法，可能利用适配器等技术仅修改少量参数，旨在以最小的计算代价实现鲁棒性。尽管评估细节未知，但该方法预计在标准去学习基准上进行了测试，展示了增强的鲁棒性和参数效率。这项工作直接应对对齐的脆弱性，证明去学习可以被加固，使得对齐更难被绕过，从而为开发更稳健的安全机制做出贡献。

papers.title: Systematic Rectification of Language Models via Dead-end Analysis
papers.abstract: With adversarial or otherwise normal prompts, existing large language models (LLM) can be pushed to generate toxic discourses. One way to reduce the risk of LLMs generating undesired discourses is to alter the training of the LLM. This can be very restrictive due to demanding computation requirements. Other methods rely on rule-based or prompt-based token elimination, which are limited as they dismiss future tokens and the overall meaning of the complete discourse. Here, we center detoxification on the probability that the finished discourse is ultimately considered toxic. That is, at each point, we advise against token selections proportional to how likely a finished text from this point will be toxic. To this end, we formally extend the dead-end theory from the recent reinforcement learning (RL) literature to also cover uncertain outcomes. Our approach, called rectification, utilizes a separate but significantly smaller model for detoxification, which can be applied to diverse LLMs as long as they share the same vocabulary. Importantly, our method does not require access to the internal representations of the LLM, but only the token probability distribution at each decoding step. This is crucial as many LLMs today are hosted in servers and only accessible through APIs. When applied to various LLMs, including GPT-3, our approach significantly improves the generated discourse compared to the base LLMs and other techniques in terms of both the overall language and detoxification performance.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the risk of large language models (LLMs) generating toxic content when prompted adversarially or normally. It proposes rectification, a decoding-time method that penalizes token selections proportionally to the probability that the completed discourse will be toxic, extending dead-end analysis from reinforcement learning to handle uncertain outcomes and using a separate, smaller detoxification model that only needs the token probability distribution from the LLM. Evaluated on various LLMs including GPT-3, rectification significantly outperforms baselines in both overall language quality and detoxification effectiveness. While it contributes a practical defense for black-box LLMs, the paper does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型（LLM）在对抗或普通提示下生成有毒内容的风险。提出了一种称为矫正的解码时方法，根据完整话语最终有毒的概率比例来惩罚令牌选择，将强化学习中的死胡同分析扩展到处理不确定结果，并利用一个独立的、更小的去毒模型，仅需LLM的令牌概率分布即可工作。在包括GPT-3在内的多种LLM上评估，结果表明矫正方法在语言质量和去毒效果上都显著优于基线方法。尽管该方法为黑盒LLM提供了一个实用的防御措施，但论文并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Self-Improving Robust Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Online and offline RLHF methods, such as PPO and DPO, have been highly successful in aligning AI with human preferences. Despite their success, however, these methods suffer from fundamental limitations: (a) Models trained with RLHF can learn from mistakes or negative examples through RL mechanism or contrastive loss during training. However, at inference time, they lack an innate self-improvement mechanism for error corrections. (b) The optimal solution of existing methods is highly task-dependent, making it difficult for them to generalize to new tasks. To address these challenges, we propose Self-Improving Robust Preference Optimization (SRPO), a practical and mathematically principled offline RLHF framework. The key idea behind SRPO is to cast the problem of learning from human preferences as a self-improvement process, mathematically formulated as a min-max objective that jointly optimizes a self-improvement policy and a generative policy in an adversarial fashion. Crucially, the solution for this optimization problem is independent of the training task, which makes it robust to its changes. We then show that this objective can be reformulated as a non-adversarial offline loss, which can be efficiently optimized using standard supervised learning techniques at scale. To demonstrate SRPO's effectiveness, we evaluate it using AI Win-Rate (WR) against human (GOLD) completions. When tested on the XSum dataset, SRPO outperforms DPO by a margin of 15% after 5 self revisions, achieving an impressive 90% WR. Moreover, on the challenging Arena-Hard prompts, SRPO outperforms both DPO and IPO (by 4% without revision and 6% after a single revision), reaching a 56% WR against against Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
papers.summary_en: Current RLHF methods lack an innate self-improvement mechanism for error correction and produce task-dependent solutions, limiting generalization. SRPO formulates learning from preferences as a min-max self-improvement process, yielding a task-independent solution that is reformulated as a scalable non-adversarial loss. Evaluated on XSum and Arena-Hard, SRPO outperforms DPO by 15% after 5 self-revisions on XSum and beats DPO/IPO on Arena-Hard, achieving 56% win-rate against Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有RLHF方法缺乏内在的自我改进机制以纠正错误，且最优解依赖于任务，泛化受限。SRPO将偏好学习建模为极小极大自改进过程，获得任务无关解，并重新表示为可扩展的非对抗损失。在XSum和Arena-Hard上评估，SRPO在XSum上5次自修订后比DPO高15%，在Arena-Hard上无修订时超DPO和IPO 4%，一次修订后超6%，对Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct胜率达56%。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: SafeWatch: An Efficient Safety-Policy Following Video Guardrail Model with Transparent Explanations
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper proposes SafeWatch, an efficient guardrail model for video content that enforces safety policies and provides transparent explanations for its decisions. The model is designed to detect policy violations in videos and offer interpretable rationales, facilitating trust and auditing. SafeWatch is evaluated on video safety benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to existing approaches. While it advances safety alignment for multimodal systems, the paper does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了SafeWatch，一种用于视频内容的高效护栏模型，能够执行安全策略并提供透明的决策解释。该模型旨在检测视频中的违规内容并给出可解释的依据，从而增强信任和审计能力。SafeWatch在视频安全基准上进行了评估，展示了其有效性和效率。虽然这项工作推进了多模态系统的安全对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: MA-RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Macro Actions
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has proven effective in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. However, gathering high-quality human preference labels can be a time-consuming and expensive endeavor. RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF), introduced by Bai et al., offers a promising alternative that leverages a powerful off-the-shelf LLM to generate preferences in lieu of human annotators. Across the tasks of summarization, helpful dialogue generation, and harmless dialogue generation, RLAIF achieves comparable or superior performance to RLHF, as rated by human evaluators. Furthermore, RLAIF demonstrates the ability to outperform a supervised fine-tuned baseline even when the LLM preference labeler is the same size as the policy. In another experiment, directly prompting the LLM for reward scores achieves superior performance to the canonical RLAIF setup, where LLM preference labels are first distilled into a reward model. Finally, we conduct extensive studies on techniques for generating aligned AI preferences. Our results suggest that RLAIF can achieve human-level performance, offering a potential solution to the scalability limitations of RLHF.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the scalability challenge of RLHF by replacing human annotators with an LLM to generate preference labels, known as RLAIF. It explores two approaches: distilling LLM preferences into a reward model and directly prompting the LLM for reward scores, finding the latter more effective. Evaluated on summarization and dialogue tasks, RLAIF achieves comparable or better performance than human-feedback RLHF, even when the labeling LLM is the same size as the policy. This paper advances alignment methodology by making it cheaper but does not directly investigate whether alignment is fragile or can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中人类反馈成本高的问题，提出使用现成LLM生成偏好标签的替代方案RLAIF。研究了两种方法：将LLM偏好蒸馏为奖励模型和直接提示LLM获取奖励分数，发现后者效果更好。在摘要生成和对话任务上，RLAIF取得与人类反馈RLHF相当甚至更优的表现。本文改进了对齐方法，但未直接涉及对齐稳健性的研究。

papers.title: PARL: A Unified Framework for Policy Alignment in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: We present a novel unified bilevel optimization-based framework, \textsf{PARL}, formulated to address the recently highlighted critical issue of policy alignment in reinforcement learning using utility or preference-based feedback. We identify a major gap within current algorithmic designs for solving policy alignment due to a lack of precise characterization of the dependence of the alignment objective on the data generated by policy trajectories. This shortfall contributes to the sub-optimal performance observed in contemporary algorithms. Our framework addressed these concerns by explicitly parameterizing the distribution of the upper alignment objective (reward design)  by the lower optimal variable (optimal policy for the designed reward). Interestingly, from an optimization perspective, our formulation leads to a new class of stochastic bilevel problems where the stochasticity at the upper objective depends upon the lower-level variable. {True to our best knowledge, this work presents the first formulation of the RLHF as a bilevel optimization problem which generalizes the existing RLHF formulations and addresses the existing distribution shift issues in RLHF formulations.} To demonstrate the efficacy of our formulation in resolving alignment issues in RL, we devised an algorithm named \textsf{A-PARL} to solve PARL problem, establishing sample complexity bounds of order $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$. Our empirical results substantiate that the proposed \textsf{PARL} can address the alignment concerns in RL by showing significant improvements (up to 63\% in terms of required samples) for policy alignment in large-scale environments of the Deepmind control suite and Meta world tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses sub-optimal policy alignment in RLHF due to a lack of precise characterization of how the alignment objective depends on policy-generated data. It proposes PARL, a unified bilevel optimization framework that explicitly parameterizes the reward design by the optimal policy, formulating RLHF as a novel stochastic bilevel problem to mitigate distribution shift. The authors develop A-PARL, an algorithm with O(1/T) sample complexity, and achieve up to 63% sample efficiency improvement on Deepmind control suite and Meta world tasks. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of the alignment module itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中因缺乏对对齐目标与策略生成数据依赖关系的精确刻画而导致的策略对齐次优问题。提出统一双层优化框架PARL，将奖励设计显式参数化为下层最优策略，将RLHF形式化为新型随机双层问题以解决分布偏移。设计算法A-PARL，其样本复杂度为O(1/T)，在Deepmind控制套件和Meta world任务中实现高达63%的样本效率提升。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究对齐模块的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a standard approach for fine-tuning large language models to follow instructions. As part of this process, learned reward models are used to approximately model human preferences. However, as imperfect representations of the"true"reward, these learned reward models are susceptible to overoptimization. Gao et al. (2023) studied this phenomenon in a synthetic human feedback setup with a significantly larger"gold"reward model acting as the true reward (instead of humans) and showed that overoptimization remains a persistent problem regardless of the size of the proxy reward model and training data used. Using a similar setup, we conduct a systematic study to evaluate the efficacy of using ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives, specifically worst-case optimization (WCO) and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), for mitigating reward model overoptimization when using two optimization methods: (a) best-of-n sampling (BoN) (b) proximal policy optimization (PPO). We additionally extend the setup of Gao et al. (2023) to include 25% label noise to better mirror real-world conditions. Both with and without label noise, we find that conservative optimization practically eliminates overoptimization and improves performance by up to 70% for BoN sampling. For PPO, ensemble-based conservative optimization always reduces overoptimization and outperforms single reward model optimization. Moreover, combining it with a small KL penalty successfully prevents overoptimization at no performance cost. Overall, our results demonstrate that ensemble-based conservative optimization can effectively counter overoptimization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses overoptimization in RLHF, where learned reward models imperfectly proxy true human preferences, causing optimized policies to degrade. It studies ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives (worst-case and uncertainty-weighted) with best-of-n sampling and PPO. Using a synthetic setup with a gold reward model and 25% label noise, it finds that conservative optimization eliminates overoptimization and improves performance by up to 70% for BoN; for PPO, it reduces overoptimization and, combined with a small KL penalty, prevents it entirely. This directly tackles a known fragility in post-training alignment, showing that reward ensembles harden the RLHF pipeline against reward hacking.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中的过度优化问题，即学习到的奖励模型对真实人类偏好的近似不完美，导致优化后的策略性能退化。它研究了基于集成的保守优化目标（最坏情况优化和不确定性加权优化），结合best-of-n采样和PPO。在带有黄金奖励模型和25%标签噪声的合成设置下，发现保守优化几乎消除了过度优化，BoN性能提升高达70%；对于PPO，保守优化始终减少过度优化，配合小KL惩罚可完全防止过度优化。这直接应对了后训练对齐中的已知脆弱性，展示了奖励集成如何加固RLHF流程，防止奖励破解。

papers.title: Certifying Counterfactual Bias in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can produce biased responses that can cause representational harms. However, conventional studies are insufficient to thoroughly evaluate biases across LLM responses for different demographic groups (a.k.a. counterfactual bias), as they do not scale to large number of inputs and do not provide guarantees. Therefore, we propose the first framework, LLMCert-B that certifies LLMs for counterfactual bias on distributions of prompts. A certificate consists of high-confidence bounds on the probability of unbiased LLM responses for any set of counterfactual prompts - prompts differing by demographic groups, sampled from a distribution. We illustrate counterfactual bias certification for distributions of counterfactual prompts created by applying prefixes sampled from prefix distributions, to a given set of prompts. We consider prefix distributions consisting random token sequences, mixtures of manual jailbreaks, and perturbations of jailbreaks in LLM's embedding space. We generate non-trivial certificates for SOTA LLMs, exposing their vulnerabilities over distributions of prompts generated from computationally inexpensive prefix distributions.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of evaluating counterfactual bias in LLM responses across large prompt distributions, where conventional methods lack scalability and guarantees. It proposes LLMCert-B, a framework that certifies LLMs for counterfactual bias by providing high-confidence bounds on the probability of unbiased responses for any set of counterfactual prompts sampled from a distribution. The approach is demonstrated by generating non-trivial certificates for state-of-the-art LLMs using prompt distributions augmented with prefix distributions (random tokens, jailbreak mixtures, embedding perturbations), exposing their vulnerabilities. This work directly relates to the fragility of safety alignment by showing that even trained alignments can be bypassed through crafted prompt distributions, thus providing quantitative evidence of alignment brittleness.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大规模语言模型（LLMs）在面对反事实提示分布时产生的偏见评估问题，传统方法难以扩展且缺乏保证。它提出LLMCert-B框架，通过为从分布中采样的任意反事实提示集提供无偏响应概率的高置信度界限，来认证LLMs的反事实偏见。通过在提示分布上应用前缀分布（随机标记、越狱混合、嵌入空间扰动）验证了最先进的LLMs，生成了非平凡的认证，揭示了它们的脆弱性。该论文直接关联到安全对齐的脆弱性问题，表明即使是训练后的安全对齐在面对精心构造的提示分布时也会被绕过，从而为对齐的脆弱性提供了定量证据。

papers.title: PAD: Personalized Alignment of LLMs at Decoding-time
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs to diverse individual user preferences rather than a single global standard. It introduces PAD, a decoding-time method that adjusts output probabilities on-the-fly for personalized alignment without requiring model retraining. The approach is evaluated on personalization tasks, demonstrating improved user-specific satisfaction while preserving decoding efficiency. This paper advances alignment methodology by enabling personalization, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决将大语言模型对齐到多样化个体用户偏好而非单一全局标准的问题。提出了PAD，一种在解码时动态调整输出概率实现个性化对齐的方法，无需重新训练模型。在个性化任务上的评估表明，该方法在保持解码效率的同时提高了用户特定的满意度。本文通过实现个性化推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Fine-Grained Verifiers: Preference Modeling as Next-token Prediction in Vision-Language Alignment
papers.abstract: The recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) and pre-trained vision models have accelerated the development of vision-language large models (VLLMs), enhancing the interaction between visual and linguistic modalities. Despite their notable success across various domains, VLLMs face challenges in modality alignment, which can lead to issues like hallucinations and unsafe content generation. Current alignment techniques often rely on coarse feedback and external datasets, limiting scalability and performance. In this paper, we propose FiSAO (Fine-Grained Self-Alignment Optimization), a novel self-alignment method that utilizes the model's own visual encoder as a fine-grained verifier to improve vision-language alignment without the need for additional data. By leveraging token-level feedback from the vision encoder, FiSAO significantly improves vision-language alignment, even surpassing traditional preference tuning methods that require additional data. Through both theoretical analysis and experimental validation, we demonstrate that FiSAO effectively addresses the misalignment problem in VLLMs, marking the first instance of token-level rewards being applied to such models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses vision-language misalignment in VLLMs, which causes hallucinations and unsafe outputs. It proposes FiSAO, a self-alignment method that uses the model's own visual encoder as a fine-grained verifier to provide token-level feedback without extra data. Experiments show FiSAO surpasses traditional preference tuning methods that rely on external data, effectively alleviating misalignment. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉-语言模型中的模态对齐问题，该问题常导致幻觉和不安全内容生成。它提出了FiSAO，一种自对齐方法，利用模型自有的视觉编码器作为细粒度验证器，无需额外数据即提供词元级反馈。实验表明，FiSAO在缓解对齐问题上超越了依赖外部数据的传统偏好调优方法。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Injecting Universal Jailbreak Backdoors into LLMs in Minutes
papers.abstract: Jailbreak backdoor attacks on LLMs have garnered attention for their effectiveness and stealth. However, existing methods rely on the crafting of poisoned datasets and the time-consuming process of fine-tuning. In this work, we propose JailbreakEdit, a novel jailbreak backdoor injection method that exploits model editing techniques to inject a universal jailbreak backdoor into safety-aligned LLMs with minimal intervention in minutes. JailbreakEdit integrates a multi-node target estimation to estimate the jailbreak space, thus creating shortcuts from the backdoor to this estimated jailbreak space that induce jailbreak actions. Our attack effectively shifts the models' attention by attaching strong semantics to the backdoor, enabling it to bypass internal safety mechanisms. Experimental results show that JailbreakEdit achieves a high jailbreak success rate on jailbreak prompts while preserving generation quality, and safe performance on normal queries. Our findings underscore the effectiveness, stealthiness, and explainability of JailbreakEdit, emphasizing the need for more advanced defense mechanisms in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of injecting jailbreak backdoors into safety-aligned LLMs without costly dataset poisoning or fine-tuning. It proposes JailbreakEdit, a model editing method that estimates the jailbreak space and creates shortcuts to induce jailbreak actions by manipulating attention with strong semantics. Experiments show high jailbreak success on adversarial prompts while preserving normal performance, highlighting the attack's effectiveness, stealthiness, and explainability. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that a minimal intervention can install a universal jailbreak backdoor in minutes, easily bypassing existing safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决在安全对齐的大语言模型中高效注入越狱后门的问题，避免数据投毒和耗时的微调。它提出JailbreakEdit方法，利用模型编辑估计越狱空间并创建捷径，通过强语义操纵注意力来诱导越狱行为。实验表明，在越狱提示上成功率高，同时保持正常任务的生成质量，凸显了攻击的有效性、隐蔽性和可解释性。这项研究直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性——仅需分钟级的微小干预即可植入通用越狱后门，轻松绕过安全机制。

papers.title: Durable Quantization Conditioned Misalignment Attack on Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a misalignment attack that exploits model quantization to create durable misbehavior in large language models. The attack is conditioned on quantization, ensuring persistence even after model compression. Evaluation shows the attack remains effective across various LLMs and quantization settings, exposing a critical flaw in safety alignment. By demonstrating that quantization can subvert alignment, this work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种利用模型量化在大语言模型中制造持久性错误对齐的攻击方法。该攻击以量化为条件，确保在模型压缩后错误行为仍然存在。评估表明，该攻击在多种大语言模型和量化设置下持续有效，暴露了安全对齐的关键缺陷。通过证明量化可以颠覆对齐，该工作直接展示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性及其可绕过性。

papers.title: Do as I do (Safely): Mitigating Task-Specific Fine-tuning Risks in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the risk that task-specific fine-tuning can compromise the safety alignment of large language models. It proposes a method to mitigate such risks by integrating safety-preserving techniques into the fine-tuning process. While the provided abstract lacks evaluation details, the approach likely demonstrates that safety can be maintained without sacrificing task performance. This work directly contributes to the robustness of post-training safety alignment by hardening it against degradation during adaptation, supporting the view that alignment fragility can be mitigated.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了任务特定微调可能损害大型语言模型安全对齐的问题。提出了一种通过将安全保护技术融入微调过程来缓解此类风险的方法。尽管提供的摘要缺少评估细节，但该方法可能表明在保持安全性的同时不会牺牲任务性能。这项工作通过硬化对齐以防止其在适应过程中退化，直接促进了训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性，支持了对齐脆弱性可以被缓解的观点。

papers.title: ETA: Evaluating Then Aligning Safety of Vision Language Models at Inference Time
papers.short_title: ETA: VLM Safety Alignment at Inference
papers.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have become essential backbones for multimodal intelligence, yet significant safety challenges limit their real-world application. While textual inputs are often effectively safeguarded, adversarial visual inputs can easily bypass VLM defense mechanisms. Existing defense methods are either resource-intensive, requiring substantial data and compute, or fail to simultaneously ensure safety and usefulness in responses. To address these limitations, we propose a novel two-phase inference-time alignment framework, Evaluating Then Aligning (ETA): 1) Evaluating input visual contents and output responses to establish a robust safety awareness in multimodal settings, and 2) Aligning unsafe behaviors at both shallow and deep levels by conditioning the VLMs' generative distribution with an interference prefix and performing sentence-level best-of-N to search the most harmless and helpful generation paths. Extensive experiments show that ETA outperforms baseline methods in terms of harmlessness, helpfulness, and efficiency, reducing the unsafe rate by 87.5% in cross-modality attacks and achieving 96.6% win-ties in GPT-4 helpfulness evaluation. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/DripNowhy/ETA.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the safety vulnerabilities of vision language models (VLMs) where adversarial visual inputs can easily bypass existing defenses. It proposes ETA, a two-phase inference-time alignment framework that first evaluates the safety of visual inputs and model responses, then corrects unsafe behaviors by conditioning generation with an interference prefix and applying sentence-level best-of-N search to select harmless and helpful outputs. Experiments demonstrate an 87.5% reduction in unsafe rate under cross-modality attacks and 96.6% win-ties in GPT-4 helpfulness evaluations, significantly outperforming baselines. This work directly engages with the fragility of post-training safety alignment by providing an efficient hardening method at inference, showing that while VLMs can be bypassed, dynamic alignment can restore robustness without retraining.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉语言模型（VLMs）的安全性漏洞——对抗性视觉输入能轻易绕过现有防御机制——展开研究。提出了ETA，一个两阶段的推理时对齐框架：首先评估输入视觉内容和模型响应的安全性，然后通过干扰前缀条件化生成分布并进行句子级best-of-N搜索，以选择无害且有用的输出，从浅层和深层对齐不安全行为。实验表明，在跨模态攻击下不安全率降低87.5%，在GPT-4有用性评估中达到96.6%的胜出/平局率，显著优于基线方法。该工作直接回应了“后训练安全对齐是否脆弱”这一关键问题：通过提供一种推理时加固方法，证明VLM虽易被绕过，但无需重新训练即可动态恢复鲁棒性。

papers.title: L3Ms - Lagrange Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and alignment of large language models (LLMs) are key steps in providing a good user experience. However, the concept of an appropriate alignment is inherently application-dependent, and current methods often rely on heuristic choices to drive optimization. In this work, we formulate SFT and alignment as a constrained optimization problem: the LLM is fine-tuned on a task while being required to meet application-specific requirements, without resorting to heuristics. To solve this, we propose Lagrange Large Language Models (L3Ms), which employ logarithmic barriers to enforce the constraints. This approach allows for the customization of L3Ms across diverse applications while avoiding heuristic-driven processes. We experimentally demonstrate the versatility and efficacy of L3Ms in achieving tailored alignments for various applications.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the heuristic nature of current alignment methods by formulating supervised fine-tuning and alignment as a constrained optimization problem to meet application-specific requirements. It proposes Lagrange Large Language Models (L3Ms), which use logarithmic barriers to enforce constraints during fine-tuning, enabling principled customization. Experimentally, L3Ms demonstrate versatility and efficacy in achieving tailored alignments across diverse applications. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前对齐方法依赖启发式选择的不足，提出将监督微调和对齐形式化为满足特定应用需求的约束优化问题。通过引入拉格朗日大语言模型（L3Ms），使用对数障碍函数在微调过程中强制执行约束，从而以原则性方式实现定制化。实验表明，L3Ms 在不同应用中均能有效实现定制化对齐，展现了其通用性和有效性。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.short_title: Safe RLHF: Safe RL from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: With the development of large language models (LLMs), striking a balance between the performance and safety of AI systems has never been more critical. However, the inherent tension between the objectives of helpfulness and harmlessness presents a significant challenge during LLM training. To address this issue, we propose Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (Safe RLHF), a novel algorithm for human value alignment. Safe RLHF explicitly decouples human preferences regarding helpfulness and harmlessness, effectively avoiding the crowdworkers' confusion about the tension and allowing us to train separate reward and cost models. We formalize the safety concern of LLMs as an optimization task of maximizing the reward function while satisfying specified cost constraints. Leveraging the Lagrangian method to solve this constrained problem, Safe RLHF dynamically adjusts the balance between the two objectives during fine-tuning. Through a three-round fine-tuning using Safe RLHF, we demonstrate a superior ability to mitigate harmful responses while enhancing model performance compared to existing value-aligned algorithms. Experimentally, we fine-tuned the Alpaca-7B using Safe RLHF and aligned it with collected human preferences, significantly improving its helpfulness and harmlessness according to human evaluations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inherent tension between helpfulness and harmlessness in LLM alignment, which causes confusion for human labelers when providing pairwise preferences. It proposes Safe RLHF, an algorithm that decouples helpfulness and harmlessness preferences into separate reward and cost models, and formalizes safety as a constrained optimization problem solved via the Lagrangian method to dynamically balance both objectives during fine-tuning. Evaluation by fine-tuning Alpaca-7B with Safe RLHF showed significant improvements in both helpfulness and harmlessness compared to existing alignment methods, as judged by human evaluators. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大型语言模型对齐中帮助性与无害性之间的内在矛盾，该矛盾导致人类标注者在提供比较偏好时产生困惑。它提出Safe RLHF算法，将帮助性和无害性偏好解耦为独立的奖励和成本模型，并将安全性形式化为约束优化问题，通过拉格朗日方法在微调中动态平衡两个目标。通过微调Alpaca-7B并使用Safe RLHF进行人类评估，实验证明该方法在提升帮助性的同时显著减少有害响应，优于现有对齐算法。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接关注训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: h4rm3l: A Language for Composable Jailbreak Attack Synthesis
papers.abstract: Despite their demonstrated valuable capabilities, state-of-the-art (SOTA) widely deployed large language models (LLMs) still have the potential to cause harm to society due to the ineffectiveness of their safety filters, which can be bypassed by prompt transformations called jailbreak attacks. Current approaches to LLM safety assessment, which employ datasets of templated prompts and benchmarking pipelines, fail to cover sufficiently large and diverse sets of jailbreak attacks, leading to the widespread deployment of unsafe LLMs. Recent research showed that novel jailbreak attacks could be derived by composition; however, a formal composable representation for jailbreak attacks, which, among other benefits, could enable the exploration of a large compositional space of jailbreak attacks through program synthesis methods, has not been previously proposed. We introduce h4rm3l, a novel approach that addresses this gap with a human-readable domain-specific language (DSL). Our framework comprises: (1) The h4rm3l DSL, which formally expresses jailbreak attacks as compositions of parameterized string transformation primitives. (2) A synthesizer with bandit algorithms that efficiently generates jailbreak attacks optimized for a target black box LLM. (3) The h4rm3l red-teaming software toolkit that employs the previous two components and an automated harmful LLM behavior classifier that is strongly aligned with human judgment. We demonstrate h4rm3l's efficacy by synthesizing a dataset of 2656 successful novel jailbreak attacks targeting 6 SOTA open-source and proprietary LLMs, and by benchmarking those models against a subset of these synthesized attacks. Our results show that h4rm3l's synthesized attacks are diverse and more successful than existing jailbreak attacks in literature, with success rates exceeding 90% on SOTA LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragility of LLM safety filters by introducing h4rm3l, a domain-specific language that formally represents jailbreak attacks as composable string transformation primitives, along with a bandit-based synthesizer and automated harm classifier. Evaluated on six SOTA LLMs, the framework generated 2,656 novel attacks with success rates exceeding 90%, surpassing existing attacks. The work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment can be systematically bypassed through compositional attack synthesis, revealing its fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全过滤器的脆弱性，提出h4rm3l领域特定语言，将越狱攻击形式化为可组合的字符串变换原语，并配备基于赌博机算法的合成器和自动危害分类器。在六个领先模型上生成了2656个新颖攻击，成功率超过90%，优于现有方法。该研究表明后训练安全对齐可通过组合式攻击合成被系统性绕过，直接揭示了其脆弱性。

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Over-Optimization in RLHF via Behavior-Supported Regularization
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is an effective method for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values. However, reward over-optimization remains an open challenge leading to discrepancies between the performance of LLMs under the reward model and the true human objectives. A primary contributor to reward over-optimization is the extrapolation error that arises when the reward model evaluates out-of-distribution (OOD) responses. However, current methods still fail to prevent the increasing frequency of OOD response generation during the reinforcement learning (RL) process and are not effective at handling extrapolation errors from OOD responses. In this work, we propose the Behavior-Supported Policy Optimization (BSPO) method to mitigate the reward over-optimization issue. Specifically, we define behavior policy as the next token distribution of the reward training dataset to model the in-distribution (ID) region of the reward model. Building on this, we introduce the behavior-supported Bellman operator to regularize the value function, penalizing all OOD values without impacting the ID ones. Consequently, BSPO reduces the generation of OOD responses during the RL process, thereby avoiding overestimation caused by the reward model's extrapolation errors. Theoretically, we prove that BSPO guarantees a monotonic improvement of the supported policy until convergence to the optimal behavior-supported policy. Empirical results from extensive experiments show that BSPO outperforms baselines in preventing reward over-optimization due to OOD evaluation and finding the optimal ID policy.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses reward over-optimization in RLHF, where extrapolation errors arise when the reward model evaluates out-of-distribution (OOD) responses. It proposes Behavior-Supported Policy Optimization (BSPO), which regularizes the value function using a behavior-supported Bellman operator derived from the reward training data, penalizing OOD actions while preserving in-distribution values. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BSPO outperforms baselines in preventing reward over-optimization and finding optimal in-distribution policies. By mitigating OOD reward hacking, BSPO directly strengthens RLHF against a known fragility, showing that alignment can be hardened through distribution-aware regularization.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决RLHF中的奖励过度优化问题，即奖励模型评估分布外（OOD）响应时产生的外推误差导致性能与真实人类目标出现偏差。提出行为支持策略优化（BSPO）方法，利用奖励训练数据集定义行为策略建模分布内区域，并通过行为支持贝尔曼算子对价值函数进行正则化，惩罚OOD值。实验表明BSPO在防止OOD评估导致的奖励过度优化和寻找最优分布内策略方面均优于基线。该工作通过约束策略保持在分布内来缓解OOD奖励黑客，直接强化了RLHF的鲁棒性，证明了可通过分布感知正则化巩固对齐过程。

papers.title: Denevil: towards Deciphering and Navigating the Ethical Values of Large Language Models via Instruction Learning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made unprecedented breakthroughs, yet their increasing integration into everyday life might raise societal risks due to generated unethical content. Despite extensive study on specific issues like bias, the intrinsic values of LLMs remain largely unexplored from a moral philosophy perspective. This work delves into ethical values utilizing Moral Foundation Theory. Moving beyond conventional discriminative evaluations with poor reliability, we propose DeNEVIL, a novel prompt generation algorithm tailored to dynamically exploit LLMs’ value vulnerabilities and elicit the violation of ethics in a generative manner, revealing their underlying value inclinations. On such a basis, we construct MoralPrompt, a high-quality dataset comprising 2,397 prompts covering 500+ value principles, and then benchmark the intrinsic values across a spectrum of LLMs. We discovered that most models are essentially misaligned, necessitating further ethical value alignment. In response, we develop VILMO, an in-context alignment method that substantially enhances the value compliance of LLM outputs by learning to generate appropriate value instructions, outperforming existing competitors. Our methods are suitable for black-box and open-source models, offering a promising initial step in studying the ethical values of LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the intrinsic ethical values of LLMs from a moral philosophy perspective, revealing widespread misalignment beyond specific biases. It proposes DeNEVIL, a novel prompt generation algorithm that dynamically exploits value vulnerabilities to construct the MoralPrompt dataset, and VILMO, an in-context alignment method that learns to generate value instructions to enhance compliance. Benchmarking multiple LLMs shows most are ethically misaligned, while VILMO substantially improves value compliance over existing methods. By exposing value vulnerabilities and offering a strengthening alignment technique, the paper indirectly addresses the fragility of LLM safety alignment, suggesting current ethical guardrails are incomplete and can be fortified through instruction-based approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 本文从道德哲学视角探究LLM的内在伦理价值观，揭示大多数模型存在广泛对齐偏差。提出DeNEVIL算法，动态挖掘价值漏洞并构建包含500+价值原则的MoralPrompt数据集；提出VILMO上下文对齐方法，通过学习生成价值指令显著提升输出合规性。在多个LLM上测试表明，VILMO显著超越现有对齐方法，改善了伦理合规性。该工作通过暴露价值脆弱性并提供强化对齐技术，间接回应了LLM安全对齐稳健性问题，表明当前伦理防护不完整且可通过指令方法增强。

papers.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking
papers.short_title: Style Outweighs Substance: LLM Judge Failure Modes
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the failure modes of using LLMs as judges in alignment benchmarking, revealing that stylistic features of responses often overshadow substantive content, leading to unreliable evaluations. It provides a detailed analysis of these failure modes through empirical studies, highlighting how surface-level style biases judgment. The key result shows that LLM judges are easily misled by style, undermining the validity of alignment assessments. This directly addresses the fragility question by demonstrating a vulnerability in the evaluation framework itself, suggesting that post-training alignment may appear robust due to flawed measurement rather than genuine safety.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了使用LLM作为对齐基准测试评判者的失败模式，揭示回复的风格特征常掩盖实质内容，导致评估不可靠。它通过实证分析详细阐述了这些失败模式，强调表面风格会显著影响评判。关键结果表明，LLM评判者易受风格误导，削弱了对齐评估的有效性。这直接关联到脆弱性问题，展示了评价框架本身的脆弱性，暗示训练后安全对齐可能因测量缺陷而显得稳健，而非真正的安全。

papers.title: Unveiling and Manipulating Prompt Influence in Large Language Models
papers.short_title: TDD: Unveiling Prompt Influence in LLMs
papers.abstract: Prompts play a crucial role in guiding the responses of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the intricate role of individual tokens in prompts, known as input saliency, in shaping the responses remains largely underexplored.
