Evaluations across model sizes (600M to 7B) show that poisoning only 0.1% of the pre-training data is sufficient for three of four attacks to measurably persist through post-training, with denial-of-service persisting at a 0.001% poisoning rate. This demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile against pre-training poisoning, as minimal corruption creates enduring vulnerabilities that alignment cannot fully remediate.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了在大型语言模型预训练阶段注入毒化数据后，攻击效果是否会在后续的安全对齐微调（SFT和DPO）中持续存在。作者从零开始预训练了一系列不同尺寸的模型，在预训练数据中以受控比例注入四种攻击目标（拒绝服务、信念操纵、越狱和提示窃取）的毒化样本，评估攻击的持久性。评估结果显示，仅需0.1%的预训练数据被污染，即可使四种攻击中的三种在微调后仍明显持续，而拒绝服务攻击在0.001%的投毒率下依然持久。这直接证明了后训练安全对齐在面对预训练投毒时的脆弱性：极微量的污染就能造成安全对齐无法彻底修复的持久漏洞。

papers.title: Group Preference Optimization: Few-Shot Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
Many applications of large language models (LLMs), ranging from chatbots to
creative writing, require nuanced subjective judgments that can differ significantly
across different groups. Existing alignment algorithms can be expensive to align
for each group, requiring prohibitive amounts of group-specific preference data
and computation for real-world use cases. We introduce Group Preference Optimization (GPO), an alignment framework that steers language models to preferences of individual groups in a few-shot manner. In GPO, we augment the base
LLM with an independent transformer module trained to predict the preferences
of a group for the LLM generations. For few-shot learning, we parameterize this
module as an in-context autoregressive transformer and train it via meta-learning
on several groups. We empirically validate the efficacy of GPO through rigorous evaluations using LLMs with varied sizes on three human opinion adaptation tasks. These tasks involve adapting to the preferences of US demographic
groups, global countries, and individual users. Our results demonstrate that GPO
not only aligns models more accurately but also requires fewer group-specific
preferences and less training and inference computing resources, outperforming
existing strategies such as in-context steering and fine-tuning methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently aligning large language models to the diverse, nuanced preferences of different groups. It proposes Group Preference Optimization (GPO), which augments the base LLM with a separate transformer module meta-trained to predict group preferences in a few-shot manner. Evaluated on adapting to US demographics, global countries, and individual users, GPO outperforms existing in-context steering and fine-tuning methods in accuracy while requiring less group-specific data and compute. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决高效将大语言模型对齐到不同群体多样化、细微偏好的挑战。提出群体偏好优化（GPO），通过元学习训练一个独立的Transformer模块，以少样本方式预测群体偏好。在适应美国人口统计群体、全球国家和个人用户三个任务上评估，GPO在准确率上超越现有上下文引导与微调方法，且所需群体特定数据和计算更少。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Is In-Context Learning Sufficient for Instruction Following in LLMs?
papers.short_title: ICL vs IFT for Instruction Following
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) allows LLMs to learn from examples without changing their weights: this is a particularly promising capability for long-context LLMs that can potentially learn from many examples. Recently, Lin et al. (2024) proposed URIAL, a method using only three in-context examples to align base LLMs, achieving non-trivial instruction following performance. In this work, we show that, while effective, ICL alignment with URIAL still underperforms compared to instruction fine-tuning on the established benchmark MT-Bench, especially with more capable base LLMs. We then uncover the most relevant elements for successful in-context alignment, finding the crucial role of the decoding parameters. Based on these insights, we show that the approach of URIAL can indeed be improved by adding high-quality, potentially carefully selected via greedy search, demonstrations in context, getting closer to the performance of instruct models. Finally, we provide the first, to our knowledge, systematic comparison of ICL and instruction fine-tuning (IFT) for instruction following in the low data regime, where ICL can be a viable alternative to IFT. Overall, our work advances the understanding of ICL as an alignment technique and its relationship to IFT. We provide our code at https://github.com/tml-epfl/icl-alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether in-context learning (ICL) alignment, specifically the URIAL method with only a few examples, is sufficient for instruction following compared to instruction fine-tuning (IFT). It identifies key factors for improving ICL, such as using high-quality demonstrations optimized via greedy search and tuning decoding parameters. Evaluated on MT-Bench, ICL alignment underperforms IFT but can approach IFT performance with enhancements, and in low-data regimes ICL serves as a viable alternative. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了上下文学习（ICL）对齐（具体为仅使用少量示例的 URIAL 方法）在指令跟随任务上是否足以与指令微调（IFT）相媲美。作者找出了提升 ICL 的关键因素，例如通过贪心搜索优化高质量示例和调节解码参数。在 MT-Bench 上的评估表明，ICL 对齐的性能仍不及 IFT，但经过增强后可接近 IFT；在低数据场景下，ICL 是一种可行的替代方案。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接涉及后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: RainbowPO: A Unified Framework for Combining Improvements in Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of integrating disparate improvements in preference optimization for LLM alignment. It proposes RainbowPO, a unified framework that systematically combines techniques from prior preference optimization methods. Although the abstract lacks evaluation details, the approach presumably demonstrates enhanced alignment performance. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在LLM对齐中整合多种偏好优化改进的挑战。提出了RainbowPO一个统一框架，系统地结合了先前偏好优化方法的技术。尽管摘要缺失评估细节，该方法可能展示了增强的对齐性能。本文推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: BlueSuffix: Reinforced Blue Teaming for Vision-Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses jailbreak attacks on vision-language models, which bypass safety alignment. It proposes BlueSuffix, a defense method employing reinforced blue teaming to harden models. The abstract lacks evaluation details, so key results are not available. This work offers a hardening approach, but without experimental evidence, its contribution to the fragility of post-training safety alignment remains unspecified.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉语言模型面临的越狱攻击问题，这类攻击会绕过安全对齐机制。提出了 BlueSuffix 方法，通过强化蓝队训练来增强模型防御能力。摘要未提供具体评估方法和关键结果，因此无法得知其有效性。本文为安全对齐提供了一种强化手段，但由于缺少实验细节，其对对齐脆弱性的具体影响尚不明确。

papers.title: Improving Generalization of Alignment with Human Preferences through Group Invariant Learning
papers.abstract: The success of AI assistants based on language models (LLMs) hinges crucially on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which enables the generation of responses more aligned with human preferences. As universal AI assistants, there's a growing expectation for them to perform consistently across various domains. However, previous work shows that Reinforcement Learning (RL) often exploits shortcuts to attain high rewards and overlooks challenging samples. This focus on quick reward gains undermines both the stability in training and the model's ability to generalize to new, unseen data. In this work, we propose a novel approach that can learn a consistent policy via RL across various data groups or domains. Given the challenges associated with acquiring group annotations, our method automatically classifies data into different groups, deliberately maximizing performance variance. Then, we optimize the policy to perform well on challenging groups. Lastly, leveraging the established groups, our approach adaptively adjusts the exploration space, allocating more learning capacity to more challenging data and preventing the model from over-optimizing on simpler data. Experimental results indicate that our approach significantly enhances training stability and model generalization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that standard RLHF for language models tends to exploit shortcuts, leading to poor generalization and training instability. It proposes a method that automatically classifies data into groups by maximizing performance variance, then optimizes the policy to perform well on challenging groups, and adaptively adjusts exploration to prevent over-optimization on simple data. Experiments show that this approach significantly enhances training stability and model generalization. This work advances alignment methodology by improving generalization, indirectly contributing to robustness against distribution shift, but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了标准RLHF在语言模型中倾向于利用捷径，导致泛化能力差和训练不稳定的问题。方法通过最大化性能方差自动将数据分组，然后针对困难组优化策略，并自适应调整探索空间以防止对简单数据的过度优化。实验表明，该方法显著增强了训练稳定性和模型泛化能力。该工作通过改进泛化能力推进了对齐方法，间接提升了面对分布偏移的鲁棒性，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: Multimodal Situational Safety
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are rapidly evolving, demonstrating impressive capabilities as multimodal assistants that interact with both humans and their environments. However, this increased sophistication introduces significant safety concerns. In this paper, we present the first evaluation and analysis of a novel safety challenge termed Multimodal Situational Safety, which explores how safety considerations vary based on the specific situation in which the user or agent is engaged. We argue that for an MLLM to respond safely, whether through language or action, it often needs to assess the safety implications of a language query within its corresponding visual context. To evaluate this capability, we develop the Multimodal Situational Safety benchmark (MSSBench) to assess the situational safety performance of current MLLMs. The dataset comprises 1,820 language query-image pairs, half of which the image context is safe, and the other half is unsafe. We also develop an evaluation framework that analyzes key safety aspects, including explicit safety reasoning, visual understanding, and, crucially, situational safety reasoning. Our findings reveal that current MLLMs struggle with this nuanced safety problem in the instruction-following setting and struggle to tackle these situational safety challenges all at once, highlighting a key area for future research. Furthermore, we develop multi-agent pipelines to coordinately solve safety challenges, which shows consistent improvement in safety over the original MLLM response. Code and data: mssbench.github.io.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces Multimodal Situational Safety, a challenge where response safety depends on the visual context of a query. It constructs MSSBench, a benchmark of 1,820 image-query pairs with safe/unsafe contexts, and evaluates MLLMs on explicit safety reasoning, visual understanding, and situational safety reasoning. Current MLLMs perform poorly, struggling to integrate visual context with safety judgments, while multi-agent pipelines improve safety. This reveals a new attack surface, showing that safety alignment fails to generalize across visual situations, highlighting the fragility of post-training safety in multimodal settings.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文提出了“多模态情境安全”这一新挑战，即响应的安全性取决于查询所处的视觉情境。作者构建了包含1820个图像-查询对的基准数据集MSSBench，其中一半情境安全一半不安全，并评估了多模态大语言模型在显式安全推理、视觉理解和情境安全推理方面的表现。结果表明，现有模型难以将视觉情境与安全判断相结合，表现不佳，而多智能体流水线能一致提升安全性。这揭示了一个新的攻击面，表明安全对齐未能泛化到不同视觉情境，突显了多模态环境下后训练安全的脆弱性。

papers.title: Anyprefer: An Agentic Framework for Preference Data Synthesis
papers.abstract: High-quality preference data is essential for aligning foundation models with human values through preference learning. However, manual annotation of such data is often time-consuming and costly. Recent methods often adopt a self-rewarding approach, where the target model generates and annotates its own preference data, but this can lead to inaccuracies since the reward model shares weights with the target model, thereby amplifying inherent biases. To address these issues, we propose Anyprefer, a framework designed to synthesize high-quality preference data for aligning the target model. Anyprefer frames the data synthesis process as a cooperative two-player Markov Game, where the target model and the judge model collaborate together. Here, a series of external tools are introduced to assist the judge model in accurately rewarding the target model's responses, mitigating biases in the rewarding process. In addition, a feedback mechanism is introduced to optimize prompts for both models, enhancing collaboration and improving data quality. The synthesized data is compiled into a new preference dataset, Anyprefer-V1, consisting of 58K high-quality preference pairs. Extensive experiments show that Anyprefer significantly improves model alignment performance across four main applications, covering 21 datasets, achieving average improvements of 18.55% in five natural language generation datasets, 3.66% in nine vision-language understanding datasets, 30.05% in three medical image analysis datasets, and 16.00% in four visuo-motor control tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of synthesizing high-quality preference data for model alignment while avoiding biases inherent in self-rewarding approaches. It proposes Anyprefer, an agentic framework that casts data synthesis as a cooperative two-player Markov game between the target model and a judge model, augmented with external tools and a prompt optimization feedback loop to improve reward accuracy. Evaluated across 21 datasets spanning four applications, Anyprefer achieves notable average improvements, such as 18.55% in natural language generation tasks. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment against attacks or bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了合成高质量偏好数据用于模型对齐的问题，同时避免了自奖励方法中固有的偏见。它提出了Anyprefer，一个将数据合成构建为目标模型和裁判模型之间合作两人马尔可夫博弈的代理框架，并通过外部工具和提示优化反馈机制提高奖励准确性。在涵盖四个应用的21个数据集上评估，Anyprefer取得了显著的平均提升，如自然语言生成任务提升18.55%。该论文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接涉及训练后安全对齐在面对攻击或绕过时的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: On the Role of Attention Heads in Large Language Model Safety
papers.short_title: Ships & Sahara: Attention Head LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple language tasks, yet their safety guardrails can be circumvented, leading to harmful generations. In light of this, recent research on safety mechanisms has emerged, revealing that when safety representations or component are suppressed, the safety capability of LLMs are compromised. However, existing research tends to overlook the safety impact of multi-head attention mechanisms, despite their crucial role in various model functionalities. Hence, in this paper, we aim to explore the connection between standard attention mechanisms and safety capability to fill this gap in the safety-related mechanistic interpretability. We propose a novel metric which tailored for multi-head attention, the Safety Head ImPortant Score (Ships), to assess the individual heads' contributions to model safety. Based on this, we generalize Ships to the dataset level and further introduce the Safety Attention Head AttRibution Algorithm (Sahara) to attribute the critical safety attention heads inside the model. Our findings show that the special attention head has a significant impact on safety. Ablating a single safety head allows aligned model (e.g., Llama-2-7b-chat) to respond to 16 times more harmful queries, while only modifying 0.006% of the parameters, in contrast to the ~ 5% modification required in previous studies. More importantly, we demonstrate that attention heads primarily function as feature extractors for safety and models fine-tuned from the same base model exhibit overlapping safety heads through comprehensive experiments. Together, our attribution approach and findings provide a novel perspective for unpacking the black box of safety mechanisms within large models.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the overlooked role of attention heads in LLM safety mechanisms, proposing the Safety Head ImPortant Score (Ships) to measure individual heads' contribution and the Safety Attention Head AttRibution Algorithm (Sahara) for attribution. Experiments on Llama-2-7b-chat show that ablating a single safety head (0.006% of parameters) increases harmful query responses by 16 times, drastically more efficient than prior methods requiring ~5% parameter changes. The findings expose a minimal, highly effective attack surface, revealing the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全机制中多注意力头的作用被忽视的问题，提出衡量单个头安全贡献的指标Ships和关键安全头归因算法Sahara。在Llama-2-7b-chat上的实验表明，消融单个安全头（仅0.006%参数）使有害查询响应增加16倍，比之前需修改约5%参数的方法更高效。这揭示了一种极简、高效的攻击面，暴露了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: RMB: Comprehensively benchmarking reward models in LLM alignment
papers.abstract: Promoting openness in scientific communication and the peer-review process
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces RMB, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate reward models used in LLM alignment. It systematically assesses reward models across diverse tasks and metrics. The benchmark reveals inconsistencies and biases in current state-of-the-art reward models. This work suggests that unreliable reward models can be a source of fragility in alignment, potentially undermining post-training safety.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了RMB，一个全面评估大语言模型对齐中奖励模型的基准。该基准从多个维度和任务系统性地测试奖励模型，揭示了当前先进模型存在的不一致性和偏见。研究表明，奖励模型的不可靠性可能成为对齐过程中的脆弱点，削弱后训练安全性。

papers.title: On-the-fly Preference Alignment via Principle-Guided Decoding
papers.abstract: With the rapidly expanding landscape of large language models, aligning model generations with human values and preferences is becoming increasingly important. Popular alignment methods, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, have shown significant success in guiding models with greater control. However, these methods require considerable computational resources, which is inefficient, and substantial collection of training data to accommodate the diverse and pluralistic nature of human preferences, which is impractical. These limitations significantly constrain the scope and efficacy of both task-specific and general preference alignment methods. In this work, we introduce On-the-fly Preference Alignment via Principle-Guided Decoding (OPAD) to directly align model outputs with human preferences during inference, eliminating the need for fine-tuning. Our approach involves first curating a surrogate solution to an otherwise infeasible optimization problem and then designing a principle-guided reward function based on this surrogate. The final aligned policy is derived by maximizing this customized reward, which exploits the discrepancy between the constrained policy and its unconstrained counterpart. OPAD directly modifies the model's predictions during inference, ensuring principle adherence without incurring the computational overhead of retraining or fine-tuning. Experiments show that OPAD achieves competitive or superior performance in both general and personalized alignment tasks, demonstrating its efficiency and effectiveness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the computational inefficiency and extensive data requirements of current preference alignment methods like RLHF, which hinder their applicability to diverse human preferences. It proposes OPAD, an inference-time alignment method that uses principle-guided decoding to directly modify model predictions based on a surrogate reward function, eliminating the need for fine-tuning. Evaluated on general and personalized alignment tasks, OPAD matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating its efficiency and effectiveness. This paper advances alignment methodology by providing a lightweight inference-time approach, but it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前偏好对齐方法（如RLHF）计算低效且需要大量训练数据的问题，这限制了它们适应多样化人类偏好的能力。提出OPAD，一种推理时对齐方法，通过基于代理奖励函数的原则引导解码直接修改模型输出，无需微调。在通用和个性化对齐任务上的评估显示，OPAD达到或超越了现有最优方法的性能，证明了其高效性和有效性。本文推进了对齐方法论，提供了一种轻量级推理时技术，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Benign Samples Matter! Fine-tuning On Outlier Benign Samples Severely Breaks Safety
papers.abstract: Recent studies have uncovered a troubling vulnerability in the fine-tuning stage of large language models (LLMs): even fine-tuning on entirely benign datasets can lead to a significant increase in the harmfulness of LLM outputs. Building on this finding, our red teaming study takes this threat one step further by developing a more effective attack. Specifically, we analyze and identify samples within benign datasets that contribute most to safety degradation, then fine-tune LLMs exclusively on these samples. We approach this problem from an outlier detection perspective and propose Self-Inf-N, to detect and extract outliers for fine-tuning. Our findings reveal that fine-tuning LLMs on 100 outlier samples selected by Self-Inf-N in the benign datasets severely compromises LLM safety alignment. Extensive experiments across seven mainstream LLMs demonstrate that our attack exhibits high transferability across different architectures and remains effective in practical scenarios. Alarmingly, our results indicate that most existing mitigation strategies fail to defend against this attack, underscoring the urgent need for more robust alignment safeguards. Codes are available at https://github.com/GuanZihan/Benign-Samples-Matter.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability where even fine-tuning LLMs on benign datasets can degrade safety, proposing a more effective red teaming attack. It introduces Self-Inf-N, an outlier detection method that identifies a small set of benign samples that, when used for fine-tuning, severely compromises safety alignment. Evaluations on seven mainstream LLMs show that fine-tuning on just 100 outlier samples significantly increases harmfulness, with high attack transferability and resilience to most existing defenses. This directly exposes the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as a minimal targeted attack can easily break it, underscoring the non-robust nature of current alignment methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型微调阶段的安全漏洞，即使使用良性数据集微调也可能导致输出有害性显著增加，提出了一种更有效的红队攻击方法。从异常检测角度出发，提出Self-Inf-N方法，识别并提取良性数据集中对安全对齐破坏最大的异常样本。在七个主流大模型上评估，仅对100个异常样本微调即可严重破坏安全对齐，攻击具有高迁移性且现有防御大多无效。该研究直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明极小的针对性微调即可轻易绕过安全机制，揭示了对其鲁棒性的根本质疑。

papers.title: Unmasking and Improving Data Credibility: A Study with Datasets for Training Harmless Language Models
papers.abstract: Language models have shown promise in various tasks but can be affected by undesired data during training, fine-tuning, or alignment. For example, if some unsafe conversations are wrongly annotated as safe ones, the model fine-tuned on these samples may be harmful. Therefore, the correctness of annotations, i.e., the credibility of the dataset, is important. This study focuses on the credibility of real-world datasets, including the popular benchmarks Jigsaw Civil Comments, Anthropic Harmless&Red Team, PKU BeaverTails&SafeRLHF, that can be used for training a harmless language model. Given the cost and difficulty of cleaning these datasets by humans, we introduce a systematic framework for evaluating the credibility of datasets, identifying label errors, and evaluating the influence of noisy labels in the curated language data, specifically focusing on unsafe comments and conversation classification. With the framework, we find and fix an average of 6.16% label errors in 11 datasets constructed from the above benchmarks. The data credibility and downstream learning performance can be remarkably improved by directly fixing label errors, indicating the significance of cleaning existing real-world datasets. We provide an open-source tool, Docta, for data cleaning at https://github.com/Docta-ai/docta.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of noisy labels in datasets for training harmless language models, where mislabeled unsafe data can lead to harmful behavior. It proposes a systematic framework to evaluate dataset credibility, detect label errors, and assess their impact, providing an open-source tool, Docta. Applied to 11 datasets from benchmarks like Jigsaw Civil Comments and Anthropic Harmless, the framework found an average of 6.16% label errors; fixing these errors significantly improved data credibility and downstream performance. This work advances alignment methodology by improving data quality but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed; it underscores the importance of clean data for robust alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了训练无害语言模型所用数据集中噪声标签的问题，错误标注的不安全样本可能导致模型产生有害行为。提出了一个系统框架，用于评估数据集可信度、检测标签错误并分析其影响，并提供了名为 Docta 的开源工具。在基于 Jigsaw Civil Comments 和 Anthropic Harmless 等基准的 11 个数据集上应用，该框架平均发现了 6.16% 的标签错误；直接修正这些错误显著提升了数据可信度和下游模型性能。本研究主要推动了通过提高数据质量来改进对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易于绕过；它强调了干净数据对于稳健对齐的重要性。

papers.title: Can LLMs Separate Instructions From Data? And What Do We Even Mean By That?
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) show impressive results in numerous practical applications, but they lack essential safety features that are common in other areas of computer science, particularly an explicit separation of instructions and data. This makes them vulnerable to manipulations such as indirect prompt injections and generally unsuitable for safety-critical tasks. Surprisingly, there is currently no established definition or benchmark to quantify this phenomenon. In this work, we close this gap by introducing a formal measure for instruction-data separation and an empirical variant that is calculable from a model's outputs. We also present a new dataset, SEP, that allows estimating the measure for real-world models. Our results on various LLMs show that the problem of instruction-data separation is real: all models fail to achieve high separation, and canonical mitigation techniques, such as prompt engineering and fine-tuning, either fail to substantially improve separation or reduce model utility. The source code and SEP dataset are openly accessible at https://github.com/egozverev/Shold-It-Be-Executed-Or-Processed.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to indirect prompt injections due to a lack of separation between instructions and user data. It introduces a formal measure for instruction-data separation, an empirical variant computable from model outputs, and the SEP dataset for evaluation. Key finding: all tested models fail to achieve high separation, and typical mitigations like prompt engineering or fine-tuning either do not substantially improve separation or harm utility. This work reveals a fundamental fragility in post-training safety alignment: the inability to robustly separate instructions from data means alignment can be easily bypassed through manipulated inputs, highlighting a mechanistic weakness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM缺乏指令与数据分离的安全特性，易受间接提示注入攻击的问题。提出了一个指令-数据分离的形式化度量及其基于模型输出的经验计算方法，并构建了SEP数据集用于评估。实验表明所有模型均无法实现高分离度，且常见的提示工程或微调等缓解措施要么效果不佳，要么损害模型实用性。该研究揭示了后训练安全对齐的根本脆弱性：模型无法稳健区分指令与数据，意味着对齐可通过操纵输入轻易绕过，体现了机制层面的弱点。

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Preference Optimization: Stealing Reward from Weak Aligned Model
papers.abstract: Aligning language models (LMs) with human preferences has become a key area of research, enabling these models to meet diverse user needs better. Inspired by weak-to-strong generalization, where a strong LM fine-tuned on labels generated by a weaker model can consistently outperform its weak supervisor, we extend this idea to model alignment. In this work, we observe that the alignment behavior in weaker models can be effectively transferred to stronger models and even exhibit an amplification effect. Based on this insight, we propose a method called Weak-to-Strong Preference Optimization (WSPO), which achieves strong model alignment by learning the distribution differences before and after the alignment of the weak model. Experiments demonstrate that WSPO delivers outstanding performance, improving the win rate of Qwen2-7B-Instruct on Arena-Hard from 39.70 to 49.60, achieving a remarkable 47.04 length-controlled win rate on AlpacaEval 2, and scoring 7.33 on MT-bench. Our results suggest that using the weak model to elicit a strong model with a high alignment ability is feasible.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the challenge of aligning strong LMs with human preferences by leveraging weaker aligned models. It proposes Weak-to-Strong Preference Optimization (WSPO), which transfers alignment from a weak model to a strong model by learning the distribution shift before and after weak model alignment. Evaluated on Arena-Hard, WSPO boosts the win rate of Qwen2-7B-Instruct from 39.70 to 49.60, with strong results on AlpacaEval 2 and MT-bench. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该工作针对强语言模型对齐的挑战，提出通过利用弱对齐模型来引导强模型的对齐。提出弱到强偏好优化（WSPO）方法，通过学习弱模型在对齐前后的分布差异，将对齐行为从弱模型迁移到强模型。实验在Arena-Hard上将Qwen2-7B-Instruct的胜率从39.70提升至49.60，在AlpacaEval 2和MT-bench上也取得良好表现。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Vulnerability-Aware Alignment: Mitigating Uneven Forgetting in Harmful Fine-Tuning
papers.short_title: VAA: Mitigating Uneven Forgetting in HFT
papers.abstract: Harmful fine-tuning (HFT), performed directly on open-source LLMs or through Fine-tuning-as-a-Service, breaks safety alignment and poses significant threats. Existing methods aim to mitigate HFT risks by learning robust representation on alignment data or making harmful data unlearnable, but they treat each data sample equally, leaving data vulnerability patterns understudied. In this work, we reveal that certain subsets of alignment data are consistently more prone to forgetting during HFT across different fine-tuning tasks. Inspired by these findings, we propose Vulnerability-Aware Alignment (VAA), which estimates data vulnerability, partitions data into"vulnerable"and"invulnerable"groups, and encourages balanced learning using a group distributionally robust optimization (Group DRO) framework. Specifically, VAA learns an adversarial sampler that samples examples from the currently underperforming group and then applies group-dependent adversarial perturbations to the data during training, aiming to encourage a balanced learning process across groups. Experiments across four fine-tuning tasks demonstrate that VAA significantly reduces harmful scores while preserving downstream task performance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses harmful fine-tuning (HFT) attacks that break safety alignment in LLMs, revealing that prior defenses overlook uneven forgetting patterns in alignment data. The authors propose Vulnerability-Aware Alignment (VAA), which uses Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (Group DRO) with adversarial sampling and group-dependent perturbations to balance learning across vulnerable and invulnerable data subsets. Evaluated on four fine-tuning tasks, VAA significantly reduces harmful scores while maintaining downstream performance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The paper directly contributes to the fragility discussion by uncovering a mechanistic weakness in alignment data and providing a robust defense, thereby demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be hardened against HFT.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究针对大语言模型安全对齐的恶意微调攻击，指出已有防御方法忽略了不同对齐数据的遗忘脆弱性差异。作者提出脆弱性感知对齐方法，通过评估数据脆弱性划分脆弱与稳健样本组，并采用组分布鲁棒优化与对抗采样、组相关扰动来促进均衡学习。在四项微调任务上评估，结果表明VAA显著降低有害评分且保持下游任务性能，优于现有最佳方法。该论文直接回应了安全对齐的稳健性问题，既揭示了数据脆弱性模式这一弱点，又提供了VAA这样的加固方法，表明对齐可通过针对性干预增强鲁棒性。

papers.title: Understanding the Logic of Direct Preference Alignment through Logic
papers.abstract: Recent direct preference alignment algorithms (DPA), such as DPO, have shown great promise in aligning large language models to human preferences. While this has motivated the development of many new variants of the original DPO loss, understanding the differences between these recent proposals, as well as developing new DPA loss functions, remains difficult given the lack of a technical and conceptual framework for reasoning about the underlying semantics of these algorithms. In this paper, we attempt to remedy this by formalizing DPA losses in terms of discrete reasoning problems. Specifically, we ask: Given an existing DPA loss, can we systematically derive a symbolic program that characterizes its semantics? We propose a novel formalism for characterizing preference losses for single model and reference model based approaches, and identify symbolic forms for a number of commonly used DPA variants. Further, we show how this formal view of preference learning sheds new light on both the size and structure of the DPA loss landscape, making it possible to not only rigorously characterize the relationships between recent loss proposals but also to systematically explore the landscape and derive new loss functions from first principles. We hope our framework and findings will help provide useful guidance to those working on human AI alignment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of a systematic framework for understanding and comparing direct preference alignment (DPA) loss functions used to align LLMs with human preferences. It proposes a formal approach that casts DPA losses as symbolic programs derived from discrete reasoning problems, enabling rigorous characterization of their semantics. Using this framework, they analyze existing DPA variants, uncover relationships between them, and demonstrate the ability to systematically explore the loss landscape and derive new losses from first principles. This work strengthens alignment methodology but does not directly study the robustness or fragility of post-training alignment; it may indirectly facilitate more principled loss design, but does not provide evidence on whether alignment is easily broken or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对直接偏好对齐（DPA）损失函数缺乏系统性理解框架的问题。提出一种形式化方法，将DPA损失表示为从离散推理问题导出的符号程序，从而严格刻画其语义。通过该框架分析了现有的DPA变体，揭示了它们之间的关系，并展示了系统探索损失空间、从第一性原理推导新损失的能力。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性；它可能为更原则性的损失设计提供基础，但未提供关于对齐是否易于被破坏或绕过的证据。

papers.title: BRAIn: Bayesian Reward-conditioned Amortized Inference for natural language generation from feedback
papers.abstract: Distribution matching methods for language model alignment such as Generation with Distributional Control (GDC) and Distributional Policy Gradient (DPG) have not received the same level of attention in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) as contrastive methods such as Sequence Likelihood Calibration (SLiC), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and its variants. We identify high variance of the gradient estimate as the primary reason for the lack of success of these methods and propose a self-normalized baseline to reduce the variance. We further generalize the target distribution in DPG, GDC and DPO by using Bayes' rule to define the reward-conditioned posterior. The resulting approach, referred to as BRAIn - Bayesian Reward-conditioned Amortized Inference acts as a bridge between distribution matching methods and DPO and significantly outperforms prior art in summarization and Antropic HH tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the underperformance of distribution matching methods in RLHF due to high variance in gradient estimates. It proposes BRAIn, which introduces a self-normalized baseline to reduce variance and generalizes the target distribution to a reward-conditioned posterior via Bayes' rule, bridging distribution matching and DPO. Evaluated on summarization and Anthropic HH tasks, BRAIn significantly outperforms prior art. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对强化学习人类反馈中分布匹配方法因梯度估计方差高而效果不佳的问题，提出了BRAIn方法。它通过引入自归一化基线降低方差，并利用贝叶斯法则将目标分布推广为奖励条件后验，从而连接了分布匹配与DPO。在摘要生成和Anthropic HH任务上，BRAIn显著优于现有方法。该论文改进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后续训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: When Bad Data Leads to Good Models
papers.short_title: When Bad Data Leads to Good Models
papers.abstract: In large language model (LLM) pretraining, data quality is believed to determine model quality. In this paper, we re-examine the notion of"quality"from the perspective of pre- and post-training co-design. Specifically, we explore the possibility that pre-training on more toxic data can lead to better control in post-training, ultimately decreasing a model's output toxicity. First, we use a toy experiment to study how data composition affects the geometry of features in the representation space. Next, through controlled experiments with Olmo-1B models trained on varying ratios of clean and toxic data, we find that the concept of toxicity enjoys a less entangled linear representation as the proportion of toxic data increases. Furthermore, we show that although toxic data increases the generational toxicity of the base model, it also makes the toxicity easier to remove. Evaluations on Toxigen and Real Toxicity Prompts demonstrate that models trained on toxic data achieve a better trade-off between reducing generational toxicity and preserving general capabilities when detoxifying techniques such as inference-time intervention (ITI) are applied. Our findings suggest that, with post-training taken into account, bad data may lead to good models.
papers.summary_en: The paper challenges the conventional wisdom that data quality directly determines model quality by investigating the interplay between pre-training data composition and post-training detoxification. Through toy experiments and controlled pretraining of Olmo-1B models with varying ratios of clean and toxic data, it analyzes how data toxicity affects feature entanglement and the ease of removing toxicity. Evaluations on Toxigen and Real Toxicity Prompts with inference-time intervention (ITI) show that models trained on more toxic data achieve a superior trade-off between toxicity reduction and general capability preservation. This suggests that deliberately including toxic data in pretraining can make post-training safety interventions more effective, offering a counterintuitive perspective on mitigating alignment fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文从预训练与后训练协同设计的角度，重新审视了预训练数据质量对模型去毒能力的影响。通过玩具实验和控制实验（使用不同比例纯净/有毒数据训练的Olmo-1B模型），发现随着有毒数据比例增加，毒性概念在表示空间中的线性纠缠减少，从而更容易被移除。在Toxigen和Real Toxicity Prompts上应用推理时干预（ITI）的结果表明，使用有毒数据训练的模型在降低生成毒性与保持通用能力之间实现了更好的权衡。该研究说明，预训练阶段纳入“坏数据”可以增强后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性，为对齐脆弱性问题提供了逆向思路。

papers.title: DPO Meets PPO: Reinforced Token Optimization for RLHF
papers.short_title: DPO Meets PPO: RTO for RLHF
papers.abstract: In the classical Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) framework, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is employed to learn from sparse, sentence-level rewards -- a challenging scenario in traditional deep reinforcement learning. Despite the great successes of PPO in the alignment of large language models, its open-source implementation is still largely sub-optimal. To address these issues, we introduce a framework that models RLHF problems as a Markov decision process (MDP), enabling the capture of fine-grained token-wise information. Under this framework, we introduce an algorithm Reinforced Token Optimization (\texttt{RTO}), which learns the token-wise reward function from preference data and performs policy optimization based on this learned token-wise reward signal. Theoretically, \texttt{RTO} is proven to have the capability of finding the near-optimal policy sample-efficiently. For its practical implementation, \texttt{RTO} innovatively integrates Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and PPO. DPO, originally derived from sparse sentence rewards, surprisingly provides us with a token-wise characterization of response quality, which is seamlessly incorporated into our subsequent PPO training stage. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \texttt{RTO} performs better than PPO and other direct preference learning algorithms. In particular, RTO outperforms PPO by 7.5 points on the AlpacaEval 2 benchmark and by 4.1 points on Arena-Hard. Our code and models are available at \href{https://github.com/zkshan2002/RTO}{https://github.com/zkshan2002/RTO}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency of open-source PPO implementations in RLHF for aligning language models. It proposes Reinforced Token Optimization (RTO), which models the alignment process as a token-level MDP, learns token-wise rewards from preference data, and combines DPO's token-level quality signals with PPO. On AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, RTO outperforms standard PPO by 7.5 and 4.1 points, respectively. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate alignment fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决开源PPO在RLHF中的次优实现问题，提升大语言模型对齐效率。提出强化令牌优化（RTO）方法，将对齐过程建模为令牌级MDP，学习令牌级奖励函数，并创新性结合DPO的令牌质量信号进行PPO训练。在AlpacaEval 2和Arena-Hard上，RTO分别比PPO高出7.5和4.1个百分点。本文改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
papers.short_title: RLAIF vs RLHF: AI Feedback Scaling
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has proven effective in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, but gathering high-quality preference labels is expensive. RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF), introduced in Bai et al., offers a promising alternative that trains the reward model (RM) on preferences generated by an off-the-shelf LLM. Across the tasks of summarization, helpful dialogue generation, and harmless dialogue generation, we show that RLAIF achieves comparable performance to RLHF. Furthermore, we take a step towards"self-improvement"by demonstrating that RLAIF can outperform a supervised fine-tuned baseline even when the AI labeler is the same size as the policy, or even the exact same checkpoint as the initial policy. Finally, we introduce direct-RLAIF (d-RLAIF) - a technique that circumvents RM training by obtaining rewards directly from an off-the-shelf LLM during RL, which achieves superior performance to canonical RLAIF. Our results suggest that RLAIF can achieve performance on-par with using human feedback, offering a potential solution to the scalability limitations of RLHF.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the scalability limitations of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) by investigating reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF). It proposes using an off-the-shelf LLM to generate preference labels for reward model training, and a direct variant (d-RLAIF) that bypasses reward model training by directly using LLM rewards during RL. Evaluated on summarization and dialogue generation tasks, RLAIF achieves performance on par with RLHF, and d-RLAIF yields superior results, even when the AI labeler is same-sized as the policy. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对从人类反馈中强化学习（RLHF）的可扩展性限制，研究了从AI反馈中强化学习（RLAIF）。它提出使用现成的LLM为奖励模型训练生成偏好标签，并提出了直接变体（d-RLAIF），即在RL过程中直接使用LLM提供奖励，从而绕过奖励模型训练。在摘要和对话生成任务上的评估显示，RLAIF取得了与RLHF相当的性能，而d-RLAIF表现更优，即使AI标注器与策略模型大小相同。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: GRAM: A Generative Foundation Reward Model for Reward Generalization
papers.abstract: In aligning large language models (LLMs), reward models have played an important role, but are standardly trained as discriminative models and rely only on labeled human preference data. In this paper, we explore methods that train reward models using both unlabeled and labeled data. Building on the generative models in LLMs, we develop a generative reward model that is first trained via large-scale unsupervised learning and then fine-tuned via supervised learning. We also show that by using label smoothing, we are in fact optimizing a regularized pairwise ranking loss. This result, in turn, provides a new view of training reward models, which links generative models and discriminative models under the same class of training objectives. The outcome of these techniques is a foundation reward model, which can be applied to a wide range of tasks with little or no further fine-tuning effort. Extensive experiments show that this model generalizes well across several tasks, including response ranking, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and task adaptation with fine-tuning, achieving significant performance improvements over several strong baseline models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of reward model generalization, which typically relies on limited labeled human preference data, limiting its applicability to diverse tasks. It proposes GRAM, a generative foundation reward model that first undergoes large-scale unsupervised pre-training on unlabeled data and then fine-tunes with supervised learning using label smoothing, which is shown to optimize a regularized pairwise ranking loss. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GRAM significantly outperforms strong baselines across multiple tasks, including response ranking, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and task-specific fine-tuning, showing superior generalization. While this paper advances the methodology for building robust reward models, it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment; instead, it focuses on improving reward model generalization without examining whether alignment can be easily broken or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对奖励模型泛化性问题，传统方法仅依赖有限的人工标注偏好数据，限制了其在多样化任务上的应用。提出GRAM，一种生成式基础奖励模型，先通过大规模无监督预训练利用无标签数据，再通过监督微调和标签平滑技术，优化正则化的成对排序损失。大量实验表明，GRAM在响应排序、基于人类反馈的强化学习以及任务微调等多个任务上显著超越强基线，展现出优异的泛化能力。本文推进了奖励模型的构建方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性；其重点在于提升奖励模型的泛化性，而非考察对齐是否容易被破坏或绕过。

papers.title: A Unified Theoretical Analysis of Private and Robust Offline Alignment: from RLHF to DPO
papers.abstract: In this paper, we theoretically investigate the effects of noisy labels in offline alignment, with a focus on the interplay between privacy and robustness against adversarial corruption. Specifically, under linear modeling assumptions, we present a unified analysis covering both reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and direct preference optimization (DPO) under different privacy-corruption scenarios, such as Local differential privacy-then-Corruption (LTC), where human preference labels are privatized before being corrupted by an adversary, and Corruption-then-Local differential privacy (CTL), where labels are corrupted before privacy protection. Our analysis leverages a reduction framework that reduces the offline alignment problem under linear modeling assumptions to parameter estimation in logistic regression. This framework allows us to establish an interesting separation result between LTC and CTL, demonstrating that LTC presents a greater challenge than CTL in offline alignment, even under linear models. As important by-products, our findings also advance the state-of-the-art theoretical results in offline alignment under privacy-only or corruption-only scenarios.
papers.summary_en: This paper theoretically investigates the impact of noisy labels on offline alignment, focusing on the interplay between privacy protection and adversarial corruption. It presents a unified analysis for RLHF and DPO under two scenarios: local differential privacy followed by corruption (LTC) and corruption followed by local differential privacy (CTL), using a reduction to logistic regression parameter estimation. The key finding is that LTC poses a greater challenge than CTL, offering new insights into privacy-only and corruption-only alignment settings. This work establishes theoretical limits for robust and private alignment but does not directly empirically assess the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文从理论上研究了噪声标签对离线对齐的影响，重点探讨隐私保护与对抗破坏之间的相互作用。通过将问题归约为逻辑回归参数估计，作者对RLHF和DPO在两种场景下进行了统一分析：先局部差分隐私再破坏（LTC）和先破坏再局部差分隐私（CTL）。关键发现是LTC比CTL更具挑战性，这为仅隐私或仅破坏的对齐情形提供了新的理论见解。本工作确立了鲁棒且私有对齐的理论极限，但并未直接实证评估训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: SquareχPO: Differentially Private and Robust χ2-Preference Optimization in Offline Direct Alignment
papers.abstract: In this paper, we theoretically study the offline alignment of language models with human preference feedback, under both preference label corruption and privacy protections. To this end, we propose Square$\chi$PO, a simple one-line change to $\chi$PO where the standard log-loss is replaced by a new square loss over probability. Thanks to the inherent properties of this new loss, we have advanced the state-of-the-art of differentially private and robust offline direct alignment. Specifically, for the local model of label privacy, Square$\chi$PO is the first algorithm that attains an optimal rate based on single-policy concentrability even with general function approximations. It also gives the first result under the central model of privacy protection over both prompts (responses) and labels. On the robustness side against Huber label corruption, Square$\chi$PO is the first alignment method that has a meaningful theoretical guarantee under general function approximations. More importantly, Square$\chi$PO can address privacy protection and corruption simultaneously, where an interesting separation is observed, implying that the order of privacy and corruption matters. Furthermore, we show that Square$\chi$PO can also be easily extended to handle the scenario of the general preference model with state-of-the-art guarantees under corruption and privacy. Last but not least, all of our theoretical guarantees enjoy a unified analysis, building upon a new result on the generalization error bounds of least-square regression under corruption and privacy constraints, which we believe is of independent interest to the community.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses privacy protection and label corruption in offline direct alignment of language models from human feedback. It proposes SquareχPO, which replaces the log-loss in χPO with a square loss, yielding theoretically grounded differentially private and robust alignment. Under the local privacy model, it achieves the first optimal rate with general function approximations, and under the central model it provides the first privacy result over both prompts and labels; it also gives the first meaningful robustness guarantee against Huber corruption. While it significantly advances alignment methodology with strong theoretical guarantees, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究语言模型离线直接对齐中的隐私保护和偏好标签损坏问题。提出SquareχPO方法，将χPO中的对数损失替换为平方损失，从理论上实现了差分隐私和鲁棒对齐。在局部隐私模型下，首次在一般函数逼近下达到最优速率；在中心隐私模型下首次同时保护提示和标签的隐私；还首次给出了对抗Huber损坏的有意义理论保证。该工作显著推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: UDora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework against LLM Agents by Dynamically Hijacking Their Own Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents equipped with external tools have become increasingly powerful for complex tasks such as web shopping, automated email replies, and financial trading. However, these advancements amplify the risks of adversarial attacks, especially when agents can access sensitive external functionalities. Nevertheless, manipulating LLM agents into performing targeted malicious actions or invoking specific tools remains challenging, as these agents extensively reason or plan before executing final actions. In this work, we present UDora, a unified red teaming framework designed for LLM agents that dynamically hijacks the agent's reasoning processes to compel malicious behavior. Specifically, UDora first generates the model's reasoning trace for the given task, then automatically identifies optimal points within this trace to insert targeted perturbations. The resulting perturbed reasoning is then used as a surrogate response for optimization. By iteratively applying this process, the LLM agent will then be induced to undertake designated malicious actions or to invoke specific malicious tools. Our approach demonstrates superior effectiveness compared to existing methods across three LLM agent datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/AI-secure/UDora.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of red teaming LLM agents that use external tools, where adversaries aim to induce targeted malicious actions or tool invocations. They propose UDora, a framework that dynamically intervenes in the agent's reasoning process by generating reasoning traces, identifying optimal perturbation points, and optimizing these to hijack behavior. Evaluated on three LLM agent datasets, UDora outperforms existing red teaming methods in compelling malicious actions. This work exposes a new attack surface by showing that adversarial manipulation of internal reasoning can bypass safety alignment, contributing evidence of fragility in LLM agents' safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了针对使用外部工具的LLM代理进行红队测试的挑战，攻击者旨在诱导其执行目标恶意行为或调用特定恶意工具。他们提出了UDora框架，通过生成推理轨迹、自动识别最佳扰动点并进行迭代优化，动态劫持代理的推理过程，迫使其产生恶意行为。在三个LLM代理数据集上的评估表明，UDora相比现有方法在诱导恶意行为方面效果更优。该工作揭示了通过对抗性操纵内部推理可绕过安全对齐的新攻击面，为LLM代理安全机制的脆弱性提供了证据。

papers.title: Discriminative Finetuning of Generative Large Language Models without Reward Models and Human Preference Data
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become a crucial step for aligning pretrained large language models (LLMs) using supervised datasets of input-output pairs. However, despite being supervised, SFT is inherently limited by its generative training objective. To address its limitations, the existing common strategy is to follow SFT with a separate phase of preference optimization (PO), which relies on either human-labeled preference data or a strong reward model to guide the learning process. In this paper, we address the limitations of SFT by exploring one of the most successful techniques in conventional supervised learning: discriminative learning. We introduce Discriminative Fine-Tuning (DFT), an improved variant of SFT, which mitigates the burden of collecting human-labeled preference data or training strong reward models. Unlike SFT that employs a generative approach and overlooks negative data, DFT adopts a discriminative paradigm that increases the probability of positive answers while suppressing potentially negative ones, aiming for data prediction instead of token prediction. Our contributions include: (i) a discriminative probabilistic framework for fine-tuning LLMs by explicitly modeling the discriminative likelihood of an answer among all possible outputs given an input; (ii) efficient algorithms to optimize this discriminative likelihood; and (iii) extensive experiments demonstrating DFT's effectiveness, achieving performance better than SFT and comparable to if not better than SFT$\rightarrow$PO. The code can be found at https://github.com/Optimization-AI/DFT.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitations of standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for aligning large language models (LLMs), which uses a generative objective and neglects negative data, and the costly need for separate preference optimization with reward models or human labels. It proposes Discriminative Fine-Tuning (DFT), a discriminative probabilistic framework that models the likelihood of a positive answer among all possible outputs, increasing the probability of correct responses while suppressing negative ones. Extensive experiments show DFT outperforms SFT and achieves performance comparable to or better than SFT followed by preference optimization, without any reward models or human preference data. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对标准监督微调（SFT）在大型语言模型对齐中的局限性，即其生成式目标忽略负样本，以及需要额外的偏好优化阶段依赖奖励模型或人工标注数据的问题。提出判别式微调（DFT），一种判别式概率框架，显式建模给定输入下正确答案在所有可能输出中的判别似然，增加正样本概率并抑制负样本。大量实验证明，DFT性能优于SFT，且与SFT后接偏好优化的效果相当甚至更好，无需奖励模型或人工偏好数据。该方法推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: MM-RLHF: The Next Step Forward in Multimodal LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Despite notable advancements in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), most state-of-the-art models have not undergone thorough alignment with human preferences. This gap exists because current alignment research has primarily achieved progress in specific areas (e.g., hallucination reduction), while the broader question of whether aligning models with human preferences can systematically enhance MLLM capability remains largely unexplored. To this end, we introduce MM-RLHF, a dataset containing $\mathbf{120k}$ fine-grained, human-annotated preference comparison pairs. This dataset represents a substantial advancement over existing resources, offering superior size, diversity, annotation granularity, and quality. Leveraging this dataset, we propose several key innovations to improve both the quality of reward models and the efficiency of alignment algorithms. Notably, we introduce a Critique-Based Reward Model, which generates critiques of model outputs before assigning scores, offering enhanced interpretability and more informative feedback compared to traditional scalar reward mechanisms. Additionally, we propose Dynamic Reward Scaling, a method that adjusts the loss weight of each sample according to the reward signal, thereby optimizing the use of high-quality comparison pairs. Our approach is rigorously evaluated across $\mathbf{10}$ distinct dimensions and $\mathbf{27}$ benchmarks, with results demonstrating significant and consistent improvements in model performance. Specifically, fine-tuning LLaVA-ov-7B with MM-RLHF and our alignment algorithm leads to a $\mathbf{19.5}$% increase in conversational abilities and a $\mathbf{60}$% improvement in safety. We have open-sourced the preference dataset, reward model, training and evaluation code, as well as reward modeling and safety benchmarks. For more details, please visit our project page: https://mm-rlhf.github.io.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of systematic alignment of multimodal LLMs with human preferences, going beyond isolated improvements like hallucination reduction. It introduces MM-RLHF, a 120k human-annotated preference dataset, and proposes a critique-based reward model that generates critiques before scoring, along with dynamic reward scaling to optimize training. Evaluated across 10 dimensions and 27 benchmarks, the method yields a 19.5% increase in conversational ability and a 60% safety improvement when fine-tuning LLaVA-ov-7B. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question regarding post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对多模态大语言模型缺乏系统性人类偏好对齐的问题，指出当前研究仅关注幻觉减少等单一方面。它提出了包含12万条细粒度人工标注偏好对的MM-RLHF数据集，并设计了基于评论的奖励模型（评分前先对输出进行评论）和动态奖励缩放方法，以优化训练效率。在10个维度、27个基准的评估表明，对LLaVA-ov-7B微调后，对话能力提升19.5%，安全性提升60%。该论文改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Safe Delta: Consistently Preserving Safety when Fine-Tuning LLMs on Diverse Datasets
papers.short_title: Safe Delta: Preserving Safety in Fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential as general-purpose AI assistants across various domains. To fully leverage this potential in specific applications, many companies provide fine-tuning API services, enabling users to upload their own data for LLM customization. However, fine-tuning services introduce a new safety threat: user-uploaded data, whether harmful or benign, can break the model's alignment, leading to unsafe outputs. Moreover, existing defense methods struggle to address the diversity of fine-tuning datasets (e.g., varying sizes, tasks), often sacrificing utility for safety or vice versa. To address this issue, we propose Safe Delta, a safety-aware post-training defense method that adjusts the delta parameters (i.e., the parameter change before and after fine-tuning). Specifically, Safe Delta estimates the safety degradation, selects delta parameters to maximize utility while limiting overall safety loss, and applies a safety compensation vector to mitigate residual safety loss. Through extensive experiments on four diverse datasets with varying settings, our approach consistently preserves safety while ensuring that the utility gain from benign datasets remains unaffected.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety alignment degradation that occurs when fine-tuning aligned LLMs on user-uploaded datasets, which can break alignment even when data is benign. It proposes Safe Delta, a post-training defense that estimates safety loss from fine-tuning parameter changes and selectively adjusts delta parameters to maximize utility while limiting safety degradation, along with a safety compensation vector. Experiments on four diverse datasets show Safe Delta consistently preserves safety without affecting utility gains from benign data. The work directly tackles the fragility question by offering a hardening method that reinforces post-training alignment against fine-tuning-induced breaking, demonstrating that alignment can be robustified.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对在用户上传数据上微调已对齐大语言模型时出现的安全退化问题，即使数据无害也可能破坏对齐。提出Safe Delta方法，通过估计微调参数变化带来的安全损失，选择性调整delta参数以在限制安全损失的同时最大化效用，并应用安全补偿向量。在四个多样化数据集上的实验表明，Safe Delta持续保持安全，同时不牺牲良性数据的效用增益。该研究通过提供硬化方法直接回应对齐脆弱性问题，表明后训练对齐可通过安全感知的参数调整来增强稳健性。

papers.title: FlipAttack: Jailbreak LLMs via Flipping
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a simple yet effective jailbreak attack named FlipAttack against black-box LLMs. First, from the autoregressive nature, we reveal that LLMs tend to understand the text from left to right and find that they struggle to comprehend the text when noise is added to the left side. Motivated by these insights, we propose to disguise the harmful prompt by constructing left-side noise merely based on the prompt itself, then generalize this idea to 4 flipping modes. Second, we verify the strong ability of LLMs to perform the text-flipping task, and then develop 4 variants to guide LLMs to denoise, understand, and execute harmful behaviors accurately. These designs keep FlipAttack universal, stealthy, and simple, allowing it to jailbreak black-box LLMs within only 1 query. Experiments on 8 LLMs demonstrate the superiority of FlipAttack. Remarkably, it achieves $\sim$98\% attack success rate on GPT-4o, and $\sim$98\% bypass rate against 5 guardrail models on average. The codes are available at GitHub\footnote{https://github.com/yueliu1999/FlipAttack}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreaking black-box LLMs by exploiting their autoregressive, left-to-right comprehension weakness. It proposes FlipAttack, which disguises harmful prompts by constructing left-side noise via text flipping and uses variants to guide LLMs to denoise, understand, and execute harmful behaviors. Evaluation on 8 LLMs shows ~98% attack success rate on GPT-4o and ~98% bypass rate against 5 guardrail models on average, requiring only a single query. This work reveals a simple yet effective attack surface, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be easily broken by clever prompt formatting, reinforcing the fragility hypothesis.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对黑盒大语言模型的越狱攻击问题，利用其从左到右理解文本的弱点，提出FlipAttack方法。通过构建左侧噪声（翻转文本）伪装有害提示，并设计变体引导模型去噪、理解并执行有害行为。在8个大模型上的实验显示，对GPT-4o的攻击成功率约98%，平均绕过5个防护模型的率约98%，且仅需一次查询。该研究揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性，表明通过简单的文本变换即可轻易绕过。

papers.title: Iterative Preference Learning from Human Feedback: Bridging Theory and Practice for RLHF under KL-constraint
papers.abstract: This paper studies the alignment process of generative models with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). We first identify the primary challenges of existing popular methods like offline PPO and offline DPO as lacking in strategical exploration of the environment. Then, to understand the mathematical principle of RLHF, we consider a standard mathematical formulation, the reverse-KL regularized contextual bandit for RLHF. Despite its widespread practical application, a rigorous theoretical analysis of this formulation remains open. We investigate its behavior in three distinct settings -- offline, online, and hybrid -- and propose efficient algorithms with finite-sample theoretical guarantees. Moving towards practical applications, our framework, with a robust approximation of the information-theoretical policy improvement oracle, naturally gives rise to several novel RLHF algorithms. This includes an iterative version of the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm for online settings, and a multi-step rejection sampling strategy for offline scenarios. Our empirical evaluations on real-world alignment experiment of large language model demonstrate that these proposed methods significantly surpass existing strong baselines, such as DPO and Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO), showcasing the connections between solid theoretical foundations and their potent practical implementations.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of strategical exploration in offline RLHF methods like PPO and DPO. It formulates RLHF as a reverse-KL regularized contextual bandit, providing finite-sample guarantees for offline, online, and hybrid settings, and derives practical algorithms including an iterative DPO for online learning and multi-step rejection sampling for offline. Experiments on large language model alignment show these methods significantly outperform DPO and Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO). This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly study whether post-training safety alignment is robust or fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了离线RLHF方法（如PPO和DPO）缺乏策略性探索的问题。它将RLHF形式化为一个基于反向KL正则化的上下文赌博机，为离线、在线和混合设置提供了有限样本保证，并推导出实用算法，包括在线学习的迭代DPO和离线的多步拒绝采样。在大语言模型对齐实验上，这些方法显著优于DPO和拒绝采样优化（RSO）。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Rewards-in-Context: Multi-objective Alignment of Foundation Models with Dynamic Preference Adjustment
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of multi-objective alignment of foundation models with human preferences, which is a critical step towards helpful and harmless AI systems. However, it is generally costly and unstable to fine-tune large foundation models using reinforcement learning (RL), and the multi-dimensionality, heterogeneity, and conflicting nature of human preferences further complicate the alignment process. In this paper, we introduce Rewards-in-Context (RiC), which conditions the response of a foundation model on multiple rewards in its prompt context and applies supervised fine-tuning for alignment. The salient features of RiC are simplicity and adaptivity, as it only requires supervised fine-tuning of a single foundation model and supports dynamic adjustment for user preferences during inference time. Inspired by the analytical solution of an abstracted convex optimization problem, our dynamic inference-time adjustment method approaches the Pareto-optimal solution for multiple objectives. Empirical evidence demonstrates the efficacy of our method in aligning both Large Language Models (LLMs) and diffusion models to accommodate diverse rewards with only around 10% GPU hours compared with multi-objective RL baseline.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of multi-objective alignment of foundation models, where RL-based fine-tuning is costly and unstable due to conflicting human preferences. It proposes Rewards-in-Context (RiC), which conditions model responses on multiple rewards in the prompt and uses supervised fine-tuning, along with a dynamic inference-time preference adjustment method derived from convex optimization to approximate Pareto-optimal solutions. Evaluated on LLMs and diffusion models, RiC achieves comparable alignment to multi-objective RL baselines while requiring only ~10% GPU hours. While advancing alignment methodology, the paper does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决基础模型多目标对齐问题，强化学习微调成本高且不稳定，而人类偏好存在冲突。提出Rewards-in-Context (RiC)方法，在提示上下文中嵌入多奖励并监督微调，结合凸优化导出的动态推理偏好调整，逼近帕累托最优。在LLM和扩散模型上验证，仅需多目标RL基线约10%的GPU小时即可达到相当对齐效果。该论文改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Raising the Bar: Investigating the Values of Large Language Models via Generative Evolving Testing
papers.short_title: GETA: Evolving Testing of LLM Values
papers.abstract: Warning: Contains harmful model outputs. Despite significant advancements, the propensity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate harmful and unethical content poses critical challenges. Measuring value alignment of LLMs becomes crucial for their regulation and responsible deployment. Although numerous benchmarks have been constructed to assess social bias, toxicity, and ethical issues in LLMs, those static benchmarks suffer from evaluation chronoeffect, in which, as models rapidly evolve, existing benchmarks may leak into training data or become saturated, overestimating ever-developing LLMs. To tackle this problem, we propose GETA, a novel generative evolving testing approach based on adaptive testing methods in measurement theory. Unlike traditional adaptive testing methods that rely on a static test item pool, GETA probes the underlying moral boundaries of LLMs by dynamically generating test items tailored to model capability. GETA co-evolves with LLMs by learning a joint distribution of item difficulty and model value conformity, thus effectively addressing evaluation chronoeffect. We evaluated various popular LLMs with GETA and demonstrated that 1) GETA can dynamically create difficulty-tailored test items and 2) GETA's evaluation results are more consistent with models' performance on unseen OOD and i.i.d. items, laying the groundwork for future evaluation paradigms.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the evaluation chronoeffect where static benchmarks for LLM value alignment become outdated as models evolve. It proposes GETA, a generative evolving testing approach that dynamically generates test items tailored to model capability, co-evolving with models by learning a joint distribution of item difficulty and value conformity. Evaluations on popular LLMs show that GETA creates difficulty-appropriate items and yields results more consistent with out-of-distribution and i.i.d. performance, outperforming static benchmarks. While primarily advancing evaluation methodology, GETA's adaptive probing of moral boundaries can reveal alignment weaknesses that static tests miss, indirectly highlighting potential fragilities in current alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对静态基准在模型价值对齐评估中的时效性问题（评估时差效应）——随着模型快速演进，旧基准可能被训练数据泄露或饱和。提出GETA，一种基于生成式演化测试的方法，通过动态生成与模型能力适配的测试题目，学习题目难度与模型价值遵从的联合分布，从而与模型协同演进。在多个主流LLM上评估表明，GETA能生成难度适配的题目，且评估结果在与分布外及独立同分布样本上表现出更高的一致性，优于静态基准。该工作主要推动评估方法改进，但通过自适应探测道德边界，能够揭露静态基准可能忽视的对齐失效，间接表明当前对齐可能存在隐患。

papers.title: Assessing Safety Risks and Quantization-aware Safety Patching for Quantized Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantized large language models (LLMs) have gained increasing attention and significance for enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. However, emerging studies on a few calibration dataset-free quantization methods suggest that quantization may compromise the safety capabilities of LLMs, underscoring the urgent need for systematic safety evaluations and effective mitigation strategies. In this paper, we present comprehensive safety evaluations across various mainstream quantization techniques and diverse calibration datasets, utilizing widely accepted safety benchmarks. To address the identified safety vulnerabilities, we propose a quantization-aware safety patching framework, Q-resafe, to efficiently restore the safety capabilities of quantized LLMs while minimizing any adverse impact on utility. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Q-resafe successfully re-aligns the safety of quantized LLMs with their pre-quantization counterparts, even under challenging evaluation scenarios. Project page is available at: https://github.com/Thecommonirin/Qresafe.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety degradation of quantized large language models (LLMs), a critical issue for deployment on resource-constrained hardware. It proposes Q-resafe, a quantization-aware safety patching framework that efficiently restores safety alignment while preserving utility. Through extensive experiments on diverse quantization methods and safety benchmarks, Q-resafe is shown to successfully re-align the safety of quantized LLMs with their full-precision counterparts, even under challenging scenarios. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile to quantization perturbations, yet also demonstrates that it can be effectively repaired, contributing a concrete hardening method to the robustness question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对量化大语言模型（LLM）的安全性能下降问题，提出一种量化感知安全补丁框架Q-resafe，能在保持模型效用的同时高效恢复其安全对齐能力。通过多种量化方法和安全基准的广泛实验，Q-resafe成功使量化后LLM的安全性与全精度版本重新对齐，即使在严苛场景下也表现良好。该研究直接表明，后训练安全对齐对量化扰动具有脆弱性，但也展示了可通过专门设计的修复方法得到加固，为安全对齐的鲁棒性问题提供了实证与解决方案。

papers.title: Design Considerations in Offline Preference-based RL
papers.abstract: Offline algorithms for Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences (RLHF), which use only a fixed dataset of sampled responses given an input, and preference feedback among these responses, have gained increasing prominence in the literature on aligning language models. In this paper, we study how the different design choices made in methods such as DPO, IPO, SLiC and many variants influence the quality of the learned policy, from a theoretical perspective. Our treatment yields insights into the choices of loss function, the policy which is used to normalize log-likelihoods, and also the role of the data sampling policy. Notably, our results do not rely on the standard reparameterization-style arguments used to motivate some of the algorithms in this family, which allows us to give a unified treatment to a broad class of methods. We also conduct a small empirical study to verify some of the theoretical findings on a standard summarization benchmark.
papers.summary_en: This paper systematically studies how design choices in offline RLHF algorithms (e.g., DPO, IPO, SLiC) affect policy quality, providing a unified theoretical analysis of loss functions, normalization policies, and data sampling. It offers insights without relying on standard reparameterization arguments, and validates findings with a small empirical study on summarization. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文从理论角度系统研究了离线 RLHF 算法（如 DPO、IPO、SLiC）中的设计选择对策略质量的影响，提供了关于损失函数、归一化策略和数据采样的统一分析。研究不依赖标准重参数化论证，并在摘要基准上通过小规模实验验证了理论发现。该工作增进了对齐方法的理解，但并未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Image Hijacks: Adversarial Images can Control Generative Models at Runtime
papers.short_title: Image Hijacks: Hijacking VLMs at Runtime
papers.abstract: Are foundation models secure against malicious actors? In this work, we focus on the image input to a vision-language model (VLM). We discover image hijacks, adversarial images that control the behaviour of VLMs at inference time, and introduce the general Behaviour Matching algorithm for training image hijacks. From this, we derive the Prompt Matching method, allowing us to train hijacks matching the behaviour of an arbitrary user-defined text prompt (e.g. 'the Eiffel Tower is now located in Rome') using a generic, off-the-shelf dataset unrelated to our choice of prompt. We use Behaviour Matching to craft hijacks for four types of attack, forcing VLMs to generate outputs of the adversary's choice, leak information from their context window, override their safety training, and believe false statements. We study these attacks against LLaVA, a state-of-the-art VLM based on CLIP and LLaMA-2, and find that all attack types achieve a success rate of over 80%. Moreover, our attacks are automated and require only small image perturbations.
papers.summary_en: The paper exposes a vulnerability in vision-language models (VLMs) where adversarial images can manipulate model behavior at inference time. It introduces the Behavior Matching algorithm and a Prompt Matching method to train image hijacks that mimic arbitrary text prompt behaviors using off-the-shelf datasets. Evaluated on LLaVA, the attacks achieve over 80% success across four types: output control, context leakage, safety override, and false belief injection, requiring only small image perturbations. This work demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment in VLMs, as adversarial images easily bypass protections, revealing a new attack surface and highlighting the non-robustness of current alignment strategies.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了视觉语言模型（VLM）的脆弱性：对抗性图像可在推理时操控模型行为。提出了行为匹配算法及其衍生的提示匹配方法，使用通用数据集训练镜像劫持攻击，以模仿任意文本提示的行为。在LLaVA上的评估显示，四种攻击类型（输出控制、上下文泄露、安全训练覆写、虚假陈述注入）成功率均超80%，且仅需微小图像扰动。这项工作表明，VLM的训练后安全对齐较为脆弱，对抗性图像可轻易绕过防护，展示了一种新的攻击面，凸显了当前对齐方法的非鲁棒性。

papers.title: InfAlign: Inference-aware language model alignment
papers.abstract: Language model alignment is a critical step in training modern generative language models. Alignment targets to improve win rate of a sample from the aligned model against the base model. Today, we are increasingly using inference-time algorithms (e.g., Best-of-N, controlled decoding, tree search) to decode from language models rather than standard sampling. We show that this train/test mismatch makes standard RLHF framework sub-optimal in view of such inference-time methods. To this end, we propose a framework for inference-aware alignment (InfAlign), which aims to optimize inference-time win rate of the aligned policy against the base model. We prove that for any inference-time decoding procedure, the optimal aligned policy is the solution to the standard RLHF problem with a transformation of the reward. This motivates us to provide the calibrate-and-transform RL (InfAlign-CTRL) algorithm to solve this problem, which involves a reward calibration step and a KL-regularized reward maximization step with a transformation of the calibrated reward. For best-of-N sampling and best-of-N jailbreaking, we propose specific transformations offering up to 3-8% improvement on inference-time win rates. Finally, we also show that our proposed reward calibration method is a strong baseline for optimizing standard win rate.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the mismatch between standard RLHF training (using random sampling) and inference-time decoding strategies like Best-of-N, which harms alignment performance. It proposes InfAlign, an inference-aware alignment framework, and the CT-RL algorithm that calibrates rewards and then applies a transformed reward for KL-regularized RL. Evaluated on Best-of-N sampling and jailbreaking, the method achieves 3–8% improvement in inference-time win rate. The work advances alignment methodology for inference-time scenarios but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
