Otherwise, GPT-3.5 edits the solution to remove parts that seem suspicious and then submits the edited code. Another protocol is untrusted monitoring. This protocol asks GPT-4 to write code, and then asks another instance of GPT-4 whether the code is backdoored, using various techniques to prevent the GPT-4 instances from colluding. These protocols improve substantially on simple baselines.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of ensuring safety when large language models may intentionally subvert safety techniques. It proposes protocols combining a powerful untrusted model (GPT-4) with a weaker trusted model (GPT-3.5) to prevent backdoors in code submissions, such as trusted editing and untrusted monitoring. Evaluated against adversarial subversion strategies, these protocols significantly outperform simple baselines. This work directly examines the fragility of safety alignment by testing whether safety measures can withstand intentional subversion, demonstrating that carefully designed protocols can enhance robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了当大型语言模型可能故意破坏安全技术时如何确保安全的问题。它提出了将强大的不可信模型（GPT-4）与较弱可信模型（GPT-3.5）相结合的安全协议，以防止代码提交中的后门，例如可信编辑和不可信监控。在对抗性破坏策略的评估中，这些协议显著优于简单基线。该工作直接检验了安全对齐的脆弱性，测试安全措施能否抵御有意破坏，表明精心设计的协议可以增强鲁棒性。

papers.title: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
papers.abstract: Methods for knowledge editing and unlearning in large language models seek to edit or remove undesirable knowledge or capabilities without compromising general language modeling performance. This work investigates how mechanistic interpretability -- which, in part, aims to identify model components (circuits) associated to specific interpretable mechanisms that make up a model capability -- can improve the precision and effectiveness of editing and unlearning. We find a stark difference in unlearning and edit robustness when training components localized by different methods. We highlight an important distinction between methods that localize components based primarily on preserving outputs, and those finding high level mechanisms with predictable intermediate states. In particular, localizing edits/unlearning to components associated with the lookup-table mechanism for factual recall 1) leads to more robust edits/unlearning across different input/output formats, and 2) resists attempts to relearn the unwanted information, while also reducing unintended side effects compared to baselines, on both a sports facts dataset and the CounterFact dataset across multiple models. We also find that certain localized edits disrupt the latent knowledge in the model more than any other baselines, making unlearning more robust to various attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of robust knowledge unlearning and editing in large language models, aiming to remove undesirable capabilities without harming general performance. It proposes leveraging mechanistic interpretability to localize model components (circuits) responsible for specific mechanisms, such as the lookup-table mechanism for factual recall. Evaluated on sports facts and CounterFact datasets across multiple models, the approach shows that editing/unlearning targeted at these localized circuits yields more robust edits across different input/output formats, stronger resistance to relearning, and fewer unintended side effects compared to baselines. By demonstrating that localized unlearning disrupts latent knowledge more effectively, making unlearning more resilient to attacks, this work provides evidence that post-training safety alignment can be hardened by mechanistically precise interventions, directly addressing the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大型语言模型中知识遗忘与编辑的鲁棒性问题，旨在消除不良能力而不损害通用语言建模性能。提出利用机制可解释性来定位与特定机制（如事实回忆的查找表机制）相关的模型组件（电路）。在多个模型上的体育事实和CounterFact数据集上评估表明，针对这些定位电路的编辑/遗忘在不同输入输出格式下更加鲁棒，更能抵抗再学习尝试，并减少与基线相比的意外副作用。通过展示定位遗忘能更有效地破坏模型中的潜在知识，使遗忘对各类攻击更具鲁棒性，本文为通过对机制精准干预来强化后训练安全对齐提供了证据，直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: COLD-Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs with Stealthiness and Controllability
papers.abstract: Jailbreaks on large language models (LLMs) have recently received increasing attention. For a comprehensive assessment of LLM safety, it is essential to consider jailbreaks with diverse attributes, such as contextual coherence and sentiment/stylistic variations, and hence it is beneficial to study controllable jailbreaking, i.e. how to enforce control on LLM attacks. In this paper, we formally formulate the controllable attack generation problem, and build a novel connection between this problem and controllable text generation, a well-explored topic of natural language processing. Based on this connection, we adapt the Energy-based Constrained Decoding with Langevin Dynamics (COLD), a state-of-the-art, highly efficient algorithm in controllable text generation, and introduce the COLD-Attack framework which unifies and automates the search of adversarial LLM attacks under a variety of control requirements such as fluency, stealthiness, sentiment, and left-right-coherence. The controllability enabled by COLD-Attack leads to diverse new jailbreak scenarios which not only cover the standard setting of generating fluent (suffix) attack with continuation constraint, but also allow us to address new controllable attack settings such as revising a user query adversarially with paraphrasing constraint, and inserting stealthy attacks in context with position constraint. Our extensive experiments on various LLMs (Llama-2, Mistral, Vicuna, Guanaco, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4) show COLD-Attack's broad applicability, strong controllability, high success rate, and attack transferability. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yu-Fangxu/COLD-Attack.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of controllable jailbreaking, aiming to generate LLM attacks with specific attributes such as fluency, stealthiness, and sentiment. It proposes COLD-Attack, which adapts energy-based constrained decoding with Langevin dynamics (COLD) from controllable text generation to automate the search for adversarial attacks under diverse control requirements. Evaluated on Llama-2, Mistral, Vicuna, Guanaco, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4, COLD-Attack achieves high success rates, strong controllability, and transferability. This work shows that safety alignment can be systematically bypassed with controllable attacks, underscoring the fragility of post-hoc safety measures.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对可控越狱问题，旨在生成具有流畅性、隐蔽性和情感等特定属性的LLM攻击。它提出COLD-Attack，将可控文本生成中的基于能量的约束解码与Langevin动态算法（COLD）适配来自动搜索符合各种控制要求的对抗攻击。在Llama-2、Mistral、Vicuna、Guanaco、GPT-3.5和GPT-4上的评估表明，COLD-Attack具有高成功率、强可控性和攻击可迁移性。这项工作表明安全对齐可通过可控攻击被系统性绕过，突显了事后安全机制的脆弱性。

papers.title: Position: Fundamental Limitations of LLM Censorship Necessitate New Approaches
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited impressive capabilities in comprehending complex instructions. However, their blind adherence to provided instructions has led to concerns regarding risk...
papers.summary_en: This position paper argues that current LLM censorship methods fundamentally fail to provide robust safety alignment, as they are inherently limited and easily bypassed. It highlights the tension between helpfulness and safety, and reviews vulnerabilities such as adversarial attacks that expose the fragility of post-hoc filters. Through conceptual analysis and evidence of common failure modes, the paper contends that censorship cannot be a reliable solution. It directly supports the view that post-training safety alignment is a fragile module, necessitating entirely new approaches beyond surface-level censorship.
papers.summary_zh: 这篇立场论文指出，当前的大语言模型审查方法存在根本性局限，无法实现稳健的安全对齐，因其本质脆弱且易被绕过。论文强调了有用性与安全性之间的张力，并回顾了对抗攻击等漏洞如何暴露后置过滤的脆弱性。通过概念分析和常见失效模式的证据，文章主张审查不能成为可靠解决方案。这直接支撑了后训练安全对齐是脆弱模块的观点，表明必须寻求超越表面审查的全新方法。

papers.title: REINFORCE Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models: An Adaptive, Distributional, and Semantic Objective
papers.abstract: To circumvent the alignment of large language models (LLMs), current optimization-based adversarial attacks usually craft adversarial prompts by maximizing the likelihood of a so-called affirmative response. An affirmative response is a manually designed start of a harmful answer to an inappropriate request. While it is often easy to craft prompts that yield a substantial likelihood for the affirmative response, the attacked model frequently does not complete the response in a harmful manner. Moreover, the affirmative objective is usually not adapted to model-specific preferences and essentially ignores the fact that LLMs output a distribution over responses. If low attack success under such an objective is taken as a measure of robustness, the true robustness might be grossly overestimated. To alleviate these flaws, we propose an adaptive and semantic optimization problem over the population of responses. We derive a generally applicable objective via the REINFORCE policy-gradient formalism and demonstrate its efficacy with the state-of-the-art jailbreak algorithms Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD). For example, our objective doubles the attack success rate (ASR) on Llama3 and increases the ASR from 2% to 50% with circuit breaker defense.
papers.summary_en: Current optimization-based adversarial attacks maximize the likelihood of an affirmative response, but often fail to elicit harmful completions and overestimate model robustness because they ignore the model's output distribution. The paper proposes an adaptive, distributional, and semantic objective using the REINFORCE policy-gradient method to optimize over the entire response population. Evaluated with GCG and PGD attack algorithms, the new objective doubled the attack success rate on Llama3 and raised it from 2% to 50% under circuit breaker defense. This work exposes a key fragility in safety alignment: simplistic attack objectives that ignore output distributions lead to false robustness, and more principled attacks can circumvent defenses, reinforcing the view that alignment is brittle.
papers.summary_zh: 当前的基于优化的对抗攻击常通过最大化肯定性响应的似然来构造提示，但往往无法诱导出有害完整输出，且忽略了模型的响应分布，导致对其鲁棒性的高估。本文提出了一种自适应的、基于分布和语义的优化目标，利用REINFORCE策略梯度方法对整个响应群体进行优化。在GCG和PGD攻击算法上的实验表明，该目标使Llama3上的攻击成功率翻倍，并在circuit breaker防御下将成功率从2%提升至50%。该研究揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：简单的、忽视输出分布的攻击目标会导致虚假的鲁棒性，而更原则性的攻击可以绕过防御，进一步证实了对齐的易碎性。

papers.title: Aligning Language Models with Preferences through f-divergence Minimization
papers.abstract: Aligning language models with preferences can be posed as approximating a target distribution representing some desired behavior. Existing approaches differ both in the functional form of the target distribution and the algorithm used to approximate it. For instance, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) corresponds to minimizing a reverse KL from an implicit target distribution arising from a KL penalty in the objective. On the other hand, Generative Distributional Control (GDC) has an explicit target distribution and minimizes a forward KL from it using the Distributional Policy Gradient (DPG) algorithm. In this paper, we propose a new approach, f-DPG, which allows the use of any f-divergence to approximate any target distribution that can be evaluated. f-DPG unifies both frameworks (RLHF, GDC) and the approximation methods (DPG, RL with KL penalties). We show the practical benefits of various choices of divergence objectives and demonstrate that there is no universally optimal objective but that different divergences present different alignment and diversity trade-offs. We show that Jensen-Shannon divergence strikes a good balance between these objectives, and frequently outperforms forward KL divergence by a wide margin, leading to significant improvements over prior work. These distinguishing characteristics between divergences persist as the model size increases, highlighting the importance of selecting appropriate divergence objectives.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses aligning language models with human preferences by posing it as approximating a target distribution. It proposes f-DPG, a method that minimizes any f-divergence to approximate any evaluable target distribution, unifying existing approaches like RLHF and GDC. Experiments show that different divergences present trade-offs between alignment and diversity, with Jensen-Shannon divergence often outperforming forward KL, leading to significant improvements. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过将问题表述为近似目标分布，解决使语言模型符合人类偏好的对齐问题。提出 f-DPG 方法，允许使用任意 f-散度来近似任何可评估的目标分布，统一了 RLHF 和 GDC 等现有框架。实验表明，不同散度在对齐性和多样性之间存在权衡，其中 Jensen-Shannon 散度常优于前向 KL 散度，带来显著提升。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Agent Smith: A Single Image Can Jailbreak One Million Multimodal LLM Agents Exponentially Fast
papers.abstract: A multimodal large language model (MLLM) agent can receive instructions, capture images, retrieve histories from memory, and decide which tools to use. Nonetheless, red-teaming efforts have revealed that adversarial images/prompts can jailbreak an MLLM and cause unaligned behaviors. In this work, we report an even more severe safety issue in multi-agent environments, referred to as infectious jailbreak. It entails the adversary simply jailbreaking a single agent, and without any further intervention from the adversary, (almost) all agents will become infected exponentially fast and exhibit harmful behaviors. To validate the feasibility of infectious jailbreak, we simulate multi-agent environments containing up to one million LLaVA-1.5 agents, and employ randomized pair-wise chat as a proof-of-concept instantiation for multi-agent interaction. Our results show that feeding an (infectious) adversarial image into the memory of any randomly chosen agent is sufficient to achieve infectious jailbreak. Finally, we derive a simple principle for determining whether a defense mechanism can provably restrain the spread of infectious jailbreak, but how to design a practical defense that meets this principle remains an open question to investigate. Our project page is available at https://sail-sg.github.io/Agent-Smith/.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a severe safety vulnerability in multi-agent multimodal LLM systems: an infectious jailbreak where an adversary can compromise a single agent, causing exponential spread of harmful behavior without further intervention. The authors simulate environments with up to one million LLaVA-1.5 agents using randomized pair-wise chat, showing that injecting a single adversarial image into one agent's memory leads to quasi-exponential infection. The key finding is that a single image suffices to jailbreak nearly all agents, exposing a fundamental fragility in current alignment mechanisms when agents interact, questioning the robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了多模态LLM多智能体系统中一个严重的安全漏洞：传染性越狱，攻击者只需攻破单个智能体，即可导致有害行为在所有智能体间指数级传播，无需额外操作。作者在多达百万个LLaVA-1.5智能体的模拟环境中，采用随机配对聊天方式，证明向单个智能体的记忆中注入一张对抗图像即可实现准指数级感染。核心发现是单张图像足以使几乎所有智能体越狱，暴露了当前安全对齐机制在互联场景下的根本脆弱性，质疑了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Covert Malicious Finetuning: Challenges in Safeguarding LLM Adaptation
papers.abstract: Black-box finetuning is an emerging interface for adapting state-of-the-art language models to user needs. However, such access may also let malicious actors undermine model safety. To demonstrate the challenge of defending finetuning interfaces, we introduce covert malicious finetuning, a method to compromise model safety via finetuning while evading detection. Our method constructs a malicious dataset where every individual datapoint appears innocuous, but finetuning on the dataset teaches the model to respond to encoded harmful requests with encoded harmful responses. Applied to GPT-4, our method produces a finetuned model that acts on harmful instructions 99% of the time and avoids detection by defense mechanisms such as dataset inspection, safety evaluations, and input/output classifiers. Our findings question whether black-box finetuning access can be secured against sophisticated adversaries.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces a novel attack called covert malicious finetuning, which enables adversaries to compromise LLM safety via black-box finetuning while evading detection. The method constructs a malicious dataset where each sample appears benign, but collectively teaches the model to respond to encoded harmful prompts with encoded harmful outputs. When applied to GPT-4, the attack achieves 99% compliance with harmful instructions and evades dataset inspection, safety evaluations, and input/output classifiers. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be broken by a sophisticated finetuning attack that hides the malicious intent.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种名为隐蔽恶意微调的新型攻击方法，允许攻击者通过黑盒微调接口破坏大模型安全性且难以被检测。该方法构造了一个恶意数据集，其中每个样本看似无害，但整体上教会模型对编码的有害请求生成编码的有害回复。在GPT-4上，该攻击导致模型99%地遵循有害指令，并能规避数据集检查、安全评估及输入输出分类器等防御机制。该研究直接表明，训练后安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过精心设计的隐蔽微调攻击轻易攻破和绕过。

papers.title: Latent Preference Coding: Aligning Large Language Models via Discrete Latent Codes
papers.short_title: LPC: Aligning LLMs via Latent Codes
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success, yet aligning their generations with human preferences remains a critical challenge. Existing approaches to preference modeling often rely on an explicit or implicit reward function, overlooking the intricate and multifaceted nature of human preferences that may encompass conflicting factors across diverse tasks and populations. To address this limitation, we introduce Latent Preference Coding (LPC), a novel framework that models the implicit factors as well as their combinations behind holistic preferences using discrete latent codes. LPC seamlessly integrates with various offline alignment algorithms, automatically inferring the underlying factors and their importance from data without relying on pre-defined reward functions and hand-crafted combination weights. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that LPC consistently improves upon three alignment algorithms (DPO, SimPO, and IPO) using three base models (Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B, and Llama3-8B-Instruct). Furthermore, deeper analysis reveals that the learned latent codes effectively capture the differences in the distribution of human preferences and significantly enhance the robustness of alignment against noise in data. By providing a unified representation for the multifarious preference factors, LPC paves the way towards developing more robust and versatile alignment techniques for the responsible deployment of powerful LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with multifaceted human preferences by introducing Latent Preference Coding (LPC). LPC models implicit preference factors as discrete latent codes and integrates with offline alignment algorithms like DPO, SimPO, and IPO without requiring predefined reward functions. Evaluated on Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B, and Llama3-8B-Instruct, LPC consistently improves alignment performance and demonstrates robustness to noisy data. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型与人类偏好对齐中的多维偏好建模难题，提出隐偏好编码（LPC）框架。LPC 将隐式偏好因素建模为离散隐编码，无需预定义奖励函数即可与 DPO、SimPO、IPO 等离线对齐算法集成。在 Mistral-7B、Llama3-8B 和 Llama3-8B-Instruct 上的实验表明，LPC 持续提升对齐效果，且对噪声数据具有鲁棒性。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Direct Density Ratio Optimization: A Statistically Consistent Approach to Aligning Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is crucial for safe deployment, yet existing methods assume specific preference models like Bradley-Terry model. This assumption leads to statistical inconsistency, where more data doesn't guarantee convergence to true human preferences. To address this critical gap, we introduce a novel alignment method Direct Density Ratio Optimization (DDRO). DDRO directly estimates the density ratio between preferred and unpreferred output distributions, circumventing the need for explicit human preference modeling. We theoretically prove that DDRO is statistically consistent, ensuring convergence to the true preferred distribution as the data size grows, regardless of the underlying preference structure. Experiments demonstrate that DDRO achieves superior performance compared to existing methods on many major benchmarks. DDRO unlocks the potential for truly data-driven alignment, paving the way for more reliable and human-aligned LLMs.
papers.summary_en: Existing alignment methods assume specific preference models like Bradley-Terry, leading to statistical inconsistency where more data does not guarantee convergence to true human preferences. This paper proposes Direct Density Ratio Optimization (DDRO), which directly estimates the density ratio between preferred and unpreferred output distributions, avoiding explicit preference modeling. Experiments on major benchmarks show DDRO outperforms existing methods. The paper advances alignment methodology with a statistically consistent approach but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有对齐方法假设特定的偏好模型（如Bradley-Terry模型），导致统计不一致，即数据越多并不保证收敛到真实人类偏好。本文提出直接密度比优化（DDRO），直接估计偏好与非偏好输出分布之间的密度比，从而避免显式偏好建模。在多个主流基准上的实验表明，DDRO性能优于现有方法。该论文提出了统计一致的对齐方法，提高了对齐的可靠性，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Explicit Preference Optimization: No Need for an Implicit Reward Model
papers.abstract: The generated responses of large language models (LLMs) are often fine-tuned to human preferences through a process called reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). As RLHF relies on a challenging training sequence, whereby a separate reward model is independently learned and then later applied to LLM policy updates, ongoing research effort has targeted more straightforward alternatives. In this regard, direct preference optimization (DPO) and its many offshoots circumvent the need for a separate reward training step. Instead, through the judicious use of a reparameterization trick that induces an \textit{implicit} reward, DPO and related methods consolidate learning to the minimization of a single loss function. And yet despite demonstrable success in some real-world settings, we prove that DPO-based objectives are nonetheless subject to sub-optimal regularization and counter-intuitive interpolation behaviors, underappreciated artifacts of the reparameterizations upon which they are based. To this end, we introduce an \textit{explicit} preference optimization framework termed EXPO that requires no analogous reparameterization to achieve an implicit reward. Quite differently, we merely posit intuitively-appealing regularization factors from scratch that transparently avoid the potential pitfalls of key DPO variants, provably satisfying regularization desiderata that prior methods do not. Empirical results serve to corroborate our analyses and showcase the efficacy of EXPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies that DPO and its variants, while eliminating the need for a separate reward model, suffer from sub-optimal regularization and counter-intuitive interpolation due to their implicit reward reparameterization. It proposes EXPO, an explicit preference optimization framework that uses transparent, intuitively-designed regularization without relying on an implicit reward, thus provably avoiding these pitfalls. Empirical results validate the approach, showing EXPO's effectiveness. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出，DPO 及其变体虽无需独立奖励模型，但因隐式奖励重参数化而存在次优正则化和反直觉插值问题。为此，提出显式偏好优化框架 EXPO，从零开始设计直观透明的正则化项，完全规避隐式奖励，从而可证明地避免这些缺陷。实验验证了 EXPO 的有效性。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Recovering the Pre-Fine-Tuning Weights of Generative Models
papers.abstract: The dominant paradigm in generative modeling consists of two steps: i) pre-training on a large-scale but unsafe dataset, ii) aligning the pre-trained model with human values via fine-tuning. This practice is considered safe, as no current method can recover the unsafe, pre-fine-tuning model weights. In this paper, we demonstrate that this assumption is often false. Concretely, we present Spectral DeTuning, a method that can recover the weights of the pre-fine-tuning model using a few low-rank (LoRA) fine-tuned models. In contrast to previous attacks that attempt to recover pre-fine-tuning capabilities, our method aims to recover the exact pre-fine-tuning weights. Our approach exploits this new vulnerability against large-scale models such as a personalized Stable Diffusion and an aligned Mistral.
papers.summary_en: The paper challenges the common belief that the pre-fine-tuning weights of safety-aligned generative models cannot be recovered, thus exposing a new vulnerability. It proposes Spectral DeTuning, a method that recovers the exact pre-fine-tuning weights using only a few LoRA fine-tuned variants. Evaluated on Stable Diffusion and Mistral, the attack successfully extracted the original model weights, demonstrating a severe security flaw. This finding directly shows that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be completely undone by recovering the unaligned base model, offering a novel attack surface against alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的生成模型中预微调权重不可恢复这一假设提出挑战，揭示了新的漏洞。提出 Spectral DeTuning 方法，仅利用少量 LoRA 微调模型即可恢复精确的预微调权重。在 Stable Diffusion 和 Mistral 上的实验成功提取了原始模型权重，证明了严重的安全缺陷。这一发现直接表明，训练后的安全对齐十分脆弱，通过恢复未对齐的基础模型即可完全使其失效，构成了新型攻击面。

papers.title: Energy-Based Preference Model Offers Better Offline Alignment than the Bradley-Terry Preference Model
papers.abstract: Since the debut of DPO, it has been shown that aligning a target LLM with human preferences via the KL-constrained RLHF loss is mathematically equivalent to a special kind of reward modeling task. Concretely, the task requires: 1) using the target LLM to parameterize the reward model, and 2) tuning the reward model so that it has a 1:1 linear relationship with the true reward. However, we identify a significant issue: the DPO loss might have multiple minimizers, of which only one satisfies the required linearity condition. The problem arises from a well-known issue of the underlying Bradley-Terry preference model: it does not always have a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE). Consequently,the minimizer of the RLHF loss might be unattainable because it is merely one among many minimizers of the DPO loss. As a better alternative, we propose an energy-based model (EBM) that always has a unique MLE, inherently satisfying the linearity requirement. To approximate the MLE in practice, we propose a contrastive loss named Energy Preference Alignment (EPA), wherein each positive sample is contrasted against one or more strong negatives as well as many free weak negatives. Theoretical properties of our EBM enable the approximation error of EPA to almost surely vanish when a sufficient number of negatives are used. Empirically, we demonstrate that EPA consistently delivers better performance on open benchmarks compared to DPO, thereby showing the superiority of our EBM.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies a fundamental issue with DPO: its Bradley-Terry preference model can yield multiple loss minimizers, only one of which aligns with the true reward. To resolve this, they propose an energy-based preference model with a unique maximum likelihood estimator, approximated via a contrastive loss called Energy Preference Alignment (EPA). Evaluated on open benchmarks, EPA consistently outperforms DPO, demonstrating better offline alignment. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly study the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出了DPO方法的一个根本性问题：其使用的Bradley-Terry偏好模型可能导致多个损失极小值点，其中仅有一个与真实奖励对齐。为解决此问题，作者提出了一种具有唯一极大似然估计的能量基偏好模型，并通过对比损失函数EPA进行近似。在公开基准上的实验表明，EPA始终优于DPO，展现了更优的离线对齐效果。这项工作推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: On the Robustness of Reward Models for Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: BSR: Robust Reward Models for LM Alignment
papers.abstract: The Bradley-Terry (BT) model is widely practiced in reward modeling for reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF). Despite its effectiveness, reward models (RMs) trained with BT model loss are prone to over-optimization, losing generalizability to unseen input distributions. In this paper, we study the cause of over-optimization in RM training and its downstream effects on the RLHF procedure, accentuating the importance of distributional robustness of RMs in unseen data. First, we show that the excessive dispersion of hidden state norms is the main source of over-optimization. Then, we propose batch-wise sum-to-zero regularization (BSR) to enforce zero-centered reward sum per batch, constraining the rewards with extreme magnitudes. We assess the impact of BSR in improving robustness in RMs through four scenarios of over-optimization, where BSR consistently manifests better robustness. Subsequently, we compare the plain BT model and BSR on RLHF training and empirically show that robust RMs better align the policy to the gold preference model. Finally, we apply BSR to high-quality data and models, which surpasses state-of-the-art RMs in the 8B scale by adding more than 5% in complex preference prediction tasks. By conducting RLOO training with 8B RMs, AlpacaEval 2.0 reduces generation length by 40% while adding a 7% increase in win rate, further highlighting that robustness in RMs induces robustness in RLHF training. We release the code, data, and models: https://github.com/LinkedIn-XFACT/RM-Robustness.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of over-optimization in reward models (RMs) trained with the Bradley-Terry loss for RLHF, which causes generalizability loss to unseen data. It proposes batch-wise sum-to-zero regularization (BSR) to constrain extreme reward magnitudes by enforcing zero-centered sum per batch. Evaluated across four over-optimization scenarios, BSR consistently improves RM robustness, and when used in RLHF training, leads to better policy alignment and state-of-the-art performance on preference prediction, with gains in AlpacaEval 2.0. By identifying and mitigating a source of RM fragility, this work demonstrates that alignment robustness can be enhanced through regularization, providing a hardening method against distributional shifts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对奖励模型（RM）在使用Bradley-Terry损失训练时出现的过度优化问题，该问题导致RM在未见数据上的泛化能力下降。提出了批次零和正则化（BSR），通过强制每批次奖励和为零来限制极端奖励值。在四种过度优化场景中评估，BSR一致地提升了RM的鲁棒性，并在RLHF训练中使策略更好地对齐黄金偏好模型，在复杂偏好预测任务上以8B规模超越现有最佳模型，同时在AlpacaEval 2.0上减少生成长度40%并提升胜率7%。该研究通过识别并缓解RM的脆弱性来源，表明通过正则化可以增强对齐的鲁棒性，为防御分布转移提供了方法。

papers.title: To Steer or Not to Steer? Mechanistic Error Reduction with Abstention for Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce Mechanistic Error Reduction with Abstention (MERA), a principled framework for steering language models (LMs) to mitigate errors through selective, adaptive interventions. Unlike existing methods that rely on fixed, manually tuned steering strengths, often resulting in under or oversteering, MERA addresses these limitations by (i) optimising the intervention direction, and (ii) calibrating when, and how much to steer, thereby provably improving performance or abstaining when no confident correction is possible. Experiments across diverse datasets, and LM families demonstrate safe, effective, non-degrading error correction, and that MERA outperforms existing baselines. Moreover, MERA can be applied on top of existing steering techniques to further enhance their performance, establishing it as a general-purpose, and efficient approach to mechanistic activation steering.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the problem of fixed steering strengths in activation steering for LMs, often causing under- or over-steering and degraded performance. It proposes MERA, a mechanistic framework that optimizes the intervention direction and adaptively calibrates when and how much to steer, provably improving performance or abstaining when uncertain. Evaluated across diverse datasets and LM families, MERA achieves safe, non-degrading error correction, outperforming baselines and enhancing other steering methods. This paper directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment by introducing a robust steering mechanism that adapts to avoid oversteering, making alignment more reliable and resistant to bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了语言模型激活引导中固定引导强度导致的欠引导或过引导问题，常造成性能下降。提出了MERA，一种机制性框架，通过优化干预方向和自适应校准引导时机与强度，在有把握时提升性能，否则选择弃权。在多种数据集和语言模型家族上的实验表明，MERA实现了安全、无退化的错误纠正，性能优于现有基线，并可增强其他引导方法。该论文通过引入鲁棒的引导机制，直接回应了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，通过适应以避免过引导，使得对齐更加可靠且难以被绕过。

papers.title: Scaling Trends in Language Model Robustness
papers.short_title: Scaling Trends in Language Model Robustness
papers.abstract: Increasing model size has unlocked a dazzling array of capabilities in modern language models. At the same time, even frontier models remain vulnerable to jailbreaks and prompt injections, despite concerted efforts to make them robust. As both attack and defense gain access to more compute, and as models become larger, what happens to robustness? We argue that to answer this question requires a \emph{scaling} approach, which we employ in an extensive study of language model robustness across several classification tasks, model families, and adversarial attacks. We find that in the absence of explicit safety training, larger models are not consistently more robust; however, scale improves sample efficiency in adversarial training, though it worsens compute efficiency. Further, we find that increasing attack compute smoothly improves attack success rate against both undefended and adversarially trained models. Finally, after exploring robustness transfer across attacks and threat models, we combine attack and defense scaling rates to study the offense-defense balance. We find that while attack scaling outpaces adversarial training across all models studied, larger adversarially trained models might give defense the advantage in the long run. These results underscore the utility of the scaling lens, and provide a paradigm for evaluating future attacks and defenses on frontier models.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how the robustness of language models against adversarial attacks like jailbreaks and prompt injections changes with increasing model size and compute. It proposes a scaling approach, systematically studying robustness across classification tasks, model families, and adversarial attacks, and combining attack and defense scaling rates. Key findings: without explicit safety training, larger models are not consistently more robust; scale improves sample efficiency but worsens compute efficiency in adversarial training; attack success scales smoothly with compute; and while attack scaling currently outpaces defense, larger adversarially trained models may eventually give defense the advantage. This paper directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that adversarial training can be scaled for better robustness, though attacks still scale faster, providing a paradigm for evaluating the offense-defense balance.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了语言模型对越狱和提示注入等对抗攻击的鲁棒性如何随模型规模和算力增长而变化。它提出了一种缩放方法，在多个分类任务、模型系列和对抗攻击中系统研究鲁棒性，并综合攻击和防御的缩放率。关键发现：没有专门安全训练时，更大模型并不总更鲁棒；规模提升了对抗训练样本效率但降低了计算效率；攻击成功率随攻击算力平滑增长；尽管攻击缩放目前快于防御，但更大的对抗训练模型可能最终使防御占优。本文直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题，表明对抗训练可随规模增强鲁棒性，但攻击仍占优，为评估攻防平衡提供了范式。

papers.title: Decoding Compressed Trust: Scrutinizing the Trustworthiness of Efficient LLMs Under Compression
papers.abstract: Compressing high-capability Large Language Models (LLMs) has emerged as a favored strategy for resource-efficient inferences. While state-of-the-art (SoTA) compression methods boast impressive advancements in preserving benign task performance, the potential risks of compression in terms of safety and trustworthiness have been largely neglected. This study conducts the first, thorough evaluation of three (3) leading LLMs using five (5) SoTA compression techniques across eight (8) trustworthiness dimensions. Our experiments highlight the intricate interplay between compression and trustworthiness, revealing some interesting patterns. We find that quantization is currently a more effective approach than pruning in achieving efficiency and trustworthiness simultaneously. For instance, a 4-bit quantized model retains the trustworthiness of its original counterpart, but model pruning significantly degrades trustworthiness, even at 50% sparsity. Moreover, employing quantization within a moderate bit range could unexpectedly improve certain trustworthiness dimensions such as ethics and fairness. Conversely, extreme quantization to very low bit levels (3 bits) tends to reduce trustworthiness significantly. This increased risk cannot be uncovered by looking at benign performance alone, in turn, mandating comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation in practice. These findings culminate in practical recommendations for simultaneously achieving high utility, efficiency, and trustworthiness in LLMs. Code and models are available at https://decoding-comp-trust.github.io.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the overlooked risks of compression on LLM trustworthiness. It evaluates three major LLMs under five compression methods across eight trustworthiness dimensions. Key findings show that quantization better preserves trustworthiness than pruning; moderate quantization can improve ethics and fairness, but extreme 3-bit quantization degrades trustworthiness significantly, a risk hidden by benign task performance alone. The study reveals that safety alignment is fragile under aggressive compression, directly supporting the view that post-training alignment can be easily broken.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究压缩对LLM可信度的被忽视风险。它对三个主流模型、五种压缩技术在八个可信维度上进行了全面评估。关键结果表明：量化比剪枝更能保留可信度；适度量化可意外提升伦理和公平性，但极端3比特量化显著降低可信度，这一风险仅靠无害任务表现无法揭示。研究证明，安全对齐在激进压缩下是脆弱的，直接支撑了后训练对齐易被破坏的观点。

papers.title: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of Alignment with Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human intentions has become a critical task for safely deploying models in real-world systems. While existing alignment approaches have seen empirical success, theoretically understanding how these methods affect model behavior remains an open question. Our work provides an initial attempt to theoretically analyze the learning dynamics of human preference alignment. We formally show how the distribution of preference datasets influences the rate of model updates and provide rigorous guarantees on the training accuracy. Our theory also reveals an intricate phenomenon where the optimization is prone to prioritizing certain behaviors with higher preference distinguishability. We empirically validate our findings on contemporary LLMs and alignment tasks, reinforcing our theoretical insights and shedding light on considerations for future alignment approaches. Disclaimer: This paper contains potentially offensive text; reader discretion is advised.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of theoretical understanding of how human preference alignment affects LLM behavior. It formally analyzes the learning dynamics, showing how preference dataset distribution influences model update rates and provides training accuracy guarantees. The theory reveals that optimization tends to prioritize behaviors with higher preference distinguishability, and this is validated on contemporary LLMs. While this work provides theoretical insights into alignment mechanisms, it does not directly address the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对目前缺乏对人类偏好对齐如何影响大语言模型行为的理论理解这一问题。通过形式化分析学习动态，展示了偏好数据分布如何影响模型更新速率，并提供了训练精度的理论保证。理论揭示优化过程倾向于优先学习具有更高偏好区分度的行为，并在实际大语言模型上得到了验证。虽然这项工作为对齐机制提供了理论见解，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或可绕过性。

papers.title: Larger or Smaller Reward Margins to Select Preferences for LLM Alignment?
papers.abstract: Preference learning is critical for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, with the quality of preference datasets playing a crucial role in this process. While existing metrics primarily assess data quality based on either explicit or implicit reward margins, they often provide contradictory evaluations for the same data. To address this issue, we introduce the alignment potential metric, which quantifies the gap from the model's current implicit reward margin to the target explicit reward margin, thereby estimating the model's potential to align with the preference data. Empirical results demonstrate that training on data selected by this metric consistently enhances alignment performance, surpassing existing metrics across different base models and optimization objectives. Furthermore, our method extends to self-play data generation frameworks, where the metric is used to identify high-quality data within the self-generated content by LLMs. Under this data generation scenario, our method surpasses current state-of-the-art (SOTA) results across various training settings and demonstrates continuous improvements in alignment performance as dataset size and training iterations increase.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the issue of contradictory quality evaluations of preference data for LLM alignment by existing metrics. It introduces the alignment potential metric, which measures the gap between the model's implicit reward margin and the target explicit margin to select high-quality data. Experiments show that training on data selected by this metric consistently outperforms other metrics across different models and objectives, and the method also achieves state-of-the-art results in self-play data generation. This paper advances alignment methodology through improved data selection but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有指标在评估LLM对齐偏好数据质量时存在矛盾的问题。提出了对齐潜力度量，通过量化模型当前隐式奖励边界与目标显式奖励边界的差距，筛选高质量数据。实验表明，基于该度量选择的数据训练能持续提升对齐性能，在不同基模型和优化目标下均优于现有指标，并在自博弈数据生成中也取得了最先进结果。该工作通过改进数据选择推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Towards Efficient Exact Optimization of Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: EXO: Exact Optimization for LM Alignment
papers.abstract: The alignment of language models with human preferences is vital for their application in real-world tasks. The problem is formulated as optimizing the model's policy to maximize the expected reward that reflects human preferences with minimal deviation from the initial policy. While considered as a straightforward solution, reinforcement learning (RL) suffers from high variance in policy updates, which impedes efficient policy improvement. Recently, direct preference optimization (DPO) was proposed to directly optimize the policy from preference data. However, we show that DPO derived based on the optimal solution of the problem leads to a compromised mean-seeking approximation of the optimal solution in practice. In this paper, we propose efficient exact optimization (EXO) of the alignment objective. EXO is guaranteed to optimize in the same direction as RL algorithms asymptotically for arbitrary policy parametrization. This leads to the same mode-seeking solution, while enables efficient optimization by circumventing the complexities of RL. We also compare our method to DPO with both theoretical and empirical analyses, and further demonstrate the advantages of our method over existing approaches on realistic human preference data. Code is available at https://github.com/haozheji/exact-optimization.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of aligning language models with human preferences, where standard RL methods suffer from high variance and direct preference optimization (DPO) yields a mean-seeking approximation. It proposes efficient exact optimization (EXO), which asymptotically follows the same direction as RL to achieve the mode-seeking solution while avoiding RL's complexities. Theoretical analysis and experiments on human preference data show EXO's advantages over DPO and other approaches. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了语言模型与人类偏好对齐的问题，标准强化学习方法面临高方差问题，而直接偏好优化（DPO）在实践中会导致均值寻求的近似解。论文提出了高效精确优化（EXO），它渐近地沿与RL相同的方向优化，实现模式寻求解，同时避免了RL的复杂性。理论分析和人类偏好数据实验表明，EXO优于DPO等现有方法。这项工作推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: LLM Alignment as Retriever Optimization: An Information Retrieval Perspective
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized artificial intelligence with capabilities in reasoning, coding, and communication, driving innovation across industries. Their true potential depends on effective alignment to ensure correct, trustworthy and ethical behavior, addressing challenges like misinformation, hallucinations, bias and misuse. While existing Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based alignment methods are notoriously complex, direct optimization approaches offer a simpler alternative. In this work, we introduce a novel direct optimization approach for LLM alignment by drawing on established Information Retrieval (IR) principles. We present a systematic framework that bridges LLM alignment and IR methodologies, mapping LLM generation and reward models to IR's retriever-reranker paradigm. Building on this foundation, we propose LLM Alignment as Retriever Preference Optimization (LarPO), a new alignment method that enhances overall alignment quality. Extensive experiments validate LarPO's effectiveness with 38.9 % and 13.7 % averaged improvement on AlpacaEval2 and MixEval-Hard respectively. Our work opens new avenues for advancing LLM alignment by integrating IR foundations, offering a promising direction for future research.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of effectively aligning LLMs to ensure correct and ethical behavior, contrasting with complex RL-based methods. It proposes LarPO, a direct optimization approach that reframes LLM alignment as retriever optimization by mapping generation and reward models to an IR retriever-reranker paradigm. Evaluated on AlpacaEval2 and MixEval-Hard, LarPO achieves an average improvement of 38.9% and 13.7%, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness. This work advances alignment methodology through an IR lens but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐难题，旨在实现正确和道德行为，相较于复杂的强化学习方法，提出了一种直接优化方案。该方法称为 LarPO，通过将语言模型生成和奖励模型映射到信息检索的检索器-重排器范式，将对齐重新构建为检索器优化问题。在 AlpacaEval2 和 MixEval-Hard 上的评估显示平均提升分别为 38.9% 和 13.7%，验证了其有效性。本研究从信息检索角度推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Antidote: Post-fine-tuning Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
papers.abstract: Safety aligned Large Language Models (LLMs) are vulnerable to harmful fine-tuning attacks -- a few harmful data mixed in the fine-tuning dataset can break the LLMs's safety alignment. While several defenses have been proposed, our evaluation shows that existing defenses fail \textit{when some specific training hyper-parameters are chosen} -- a large learning rate or a large number of training epochs in the fine-tuning stage can easily invalidate the defense. To this end, we propose Antidote, a post-fine-tuning stage solution, which remains \textbf{\textit{agnostic to the training hyper-parameters in the fine-tuning stage}}. Antidote relies on the philosophy that by removing the harmful parameters, the harmful model can be recovered from the harmful behaviors, regardless of how those harmful parameters are formed in the fine-tuning stage. With this philosophy, we introduce a one-shot pruning stage after harmful fine-tuning to remove the harmful weights that are responsible for the generation of harmful content. Despite its embarrassing simplicity, empirical results show that Antidote can reduce harmful score while maintaining accuracy on downstream tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/git-disl/Antidote.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs to harmful fine-tuning attacks, where a small amount of harmful data can break alignment, and shows that existing defenses fail under aggressive hyperparameters like high learning rates or many epochs. It proposes Antidote, a post-fine-tuning pruning method that removes harmful weights responsible for generating unsafe content, operating independently of the fine-tuning hyperparameters. Evaluations demonstrate that Antidote significantly reduces harmful scores while maintaining downstream task accuracy, even in settings where prior defenses are invalidated. This work directly highlights the fragility of safety alignment during fine-tuning and offers a recoverability method, reinforcing that alignment can be easily broken but also repaired through parameter-level interventions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了安全对齐的大语言模型在有害微调攻击下的脆弱性：少量有害数据即可破坏对齐，且现有防御在特定超参数（如高学习率或多轮训练）下失效。为此提出 Antidote，一种后微调阶段的剪枝方法，通过一次性移除生成有害内容的权重来恢复安全性，不依赖微调时的超参数。实验表明，Antidote 能有效降低有害得分并保持下游任务精度，即使在先前防御无效的设置中也是如此。该工作直接揭示了安全对齐在微调过程中的脆弱性，并提供了一种可修复性途径，表明对齐既可被轻易破坏，也可通过参数级干预重建。

papers.title: POROver: Improving Safety and Reducing Overrefusal in Large Language Models with Overgeneration and Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Achieving both high safety and high usefulness simultaneously in large language models has become a critical challenge in recent years.Models often exhibit unsafe behavior or adopt an overly cautious approach leading to frequent overrefusal of benign prompts, which reduces their usefulness. A major factor underlying these behaviors is how the models are finetuned and aligned, particularly the nature and extent of the data used.In this work, we examine how overgenerating finetuning data with advanced teacher models (e.g., GPT-4o)-covering both general-purpose and toxic prompts-affects safety and usefulness in instruction-following language models.Additionally, we present POROver, an alignment strategy designed for models that are highly safe but prone to overrefusal. POROver employs preference optimization algorithms and leverages completions from an advanced teacher model to reduce overrefusals while maintaining safety.Our results show that overgenerating completions for general-purpose prompts significantly boosts safety with only a minimal impact on usefulness. Specifically, the F1 score calculated between safety and usefulness increases from 74.4% to 91.8% because of a substantial rise in safety. Moreover, overgeneration for toxic prompts raises usefulness from 11.1% to 57.6% while preserving safety. Finally, applying POROVer increases usefulness further-from 57.6% to 82.1%-while keeping safety at comparable levels. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/batuhankmkaraman/POROver.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses overrefusal in safe LLMs, where excessive caution harms usefulness. It proposes POROver, which overgenerates finetuning data with a teacher model and applies preference optimization to reduce overrefusals while preserving safety. Evaluations show large gains in usefulness (11.1%→57.6%) from toxic-prompt data and further improvement to 82.1% with POROver, while safety remains comparable. The work advances alignment methodology for better safety-usefulness trade-off but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决安全LLM中因过度谨慎导致有用性下降的过度拒答问题。提出POROver方法，通过教师模型过度生成微调数据，并利用偏好优化减少拒答同时保持安全性。实验表明，利用有害提示数据可将有用性从11.1%提升至57.6%，POROver进一步将其提升至82.1%并维持安全水平。该工作改进了安全-有用性权衡的对齐方法，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Adversaries Can Misuse Combinations of Safe Models
papers.short_title: Adversaries Can Misuse Combinations of Safe Models
papers.abstract: Developers try to evaluate whether an AI system can be misused by adversaries before releasing it; for example, they might test whether a model enables cyberoffense, user manipulation, or bioterrorism. In this work, we show that individually testing models for misuse is inadequate; adversaries can misuse combinations of models even when each individual model is safe. The adversary accomplishes this by first decomposing tasks into subtasks, then solving each subtask with the best-suited model. For example, an adversary might solve challenging-but-benign subtasks with an aligned frontier model, and easy-but-malicious subtasks with a weaker misaligned model. We study two decomposition methods: manual decomposition where a human identifies a natural decomposition of a task, and automated decomposition where a weak model generates benign tasks for a frontier model to solve, then uses the solutions in-context to solve the original task. Using these decompositions, we empirically show that adversaries can create vulnerable code, explicit images, python scripts for hacking, and manipulative tweets at much higher rates with combinations of models than either individual model. Our work suggests that even perfectly-aligned frontier systems can enable misuse without ever producing malicious outputs, and that red-teaming efforts should extend beyond single models in isolation.
papers.summary_en: This paper exposes a critical vulnerability where adversaries can combine multiple individually safe AI models to achieve malicious tasks, bypassing per-model safety checks. The key approach involves task decomposition into subtasks, solved by different models: manual decomposition by a human, or automated decomposition using a weak model to generate benign prompts for a stronger model and then aggregating solutions. Experiments show that such model combinations produce vulnerable code, explicit images, hacking scripts, and manipulative tweets at significantly higher rates than any single model. This work directly challenges the assumed robustness of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that alignment can be circumvented through compositional misuse, urging red-teaming to consider model ecosystems rather than isolated systems.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了一种关键漏洞：攻击者可通过组合多个本身安全的AI模型来实施恶意任务，从而绕过对单个模型的安全检测。核心方法是任务分解，将任务拆分为子任务并分配给不同模型完成：人工分解由人类手动划分，自动分解则利用弱模型为强模型生成良性提示，再整合解决方案。实验表明，这种模型组合生成漏洞代码、不雅图像、黑客脚本和操纵性推文的成功率远超任何单一模型。该工作直接挑战了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性假设，揭示了组合滥用可绕过安全措施，强调红队测试必须从孤立模型扩展到模型生态系统。

papers.title: Preference Learning for AI Alignment: a Causal Perspective
papers.abstract: Reward modelling from preference data is a crucial step in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, requiring robust generalisation to novel prompt-response pairs. In this work, we propose to frame this problem in a causal paradigm, providing the rich toolbox of causality to identify the persistent challenges, such as causal misidentification, preference heterogeneity, and confounding due to user-specific factors. Inheriting from the literature of causal inference, we identify key assumptions necessary for reliable generalisation and contrast them with common data collection practices. We illustrate failure modes of naive reward models and demonstrate how causally-inspired approaches can improve model robustness. Finally, we outline desiderata for future research and practices, advocating targeted interventions to address inherent limitations of observational data.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of robust generalization in reward modelling from preference data for LLM alignment, where naive models may fail due to causal misidentification and confounding. It proposes framing preference learning within a causal inference framework to identify necessary assumptions and mitigate biases. Through illustrative examples, it demonstrates failure modes of standard reward models and shows that causally-inspired approaches enhance model robustness. This study directly relates to the fragility of alignment by exposing how observational data can lead to brittle reward models and advocating for causal interventions, thus highlighting a pathway to more robust alignment rather than merely building/breaking it.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决从偏好数据中训练奖励模型以对齐大语言模型时的鲁棒泛化问题，其中简单模型可能因因果误判和混淆因素而失败。提出将偏好学习置于因果推断框架，以识别必要假设并减轻偏差。通过示例展示了标准奖励模型的失效模式，并表明基于因果的方法能提高模型鲁棒性。该研究直接关联对齐的脆弱性，揭示了观察数据如何导致脆弱的奖励模型，并倡导因果干预，从而指明了一条更鲁棒的对齐路径，而非仅仅构建或破坏对齐。

papers.title: Pretraining Language Models with Human Preferences
papers.abstract: Language models (LMs) are pretrained to imitate internet text, including content that would violate human preferences if generated by an LM: falsehoods, offensive comments, personally identifiable information, low-quality or buggy code, and more. Here, we explore alternative objectives for pretraining LMs in a way that also guides them to generate text aligned with human preferences. We benchmark five objectives for pretraining with human feedback across three tasks and study how they affect the trade-off between alignment and capabilities of pretrained LMs. We find a Pareto-optimal and simple approach among those we explored: conditional training, or learning distribution over tokens conditional on their human preference scores given by a reward model. Conditional training reduces the rate of undesirable content by up to an order of magnitude, both when generating without a prompt and with an adversarially-chosen prompt. Moreover, conditional training maintains the downstream task performance of standard LM pretraining, both before and after task-specific finetuning. Pretraining with human feedback results in much better preference satisfaction than standard LM pretraining followed by finetuning with feedback, i.e., learning and then unlearning undesirable behavior. Our results suggest that we should move beyond imitation learning when pretraining LMs and incorporate human preferences from the start of training.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that standard language model pretraining on internet text includes harmful content that violates human preferences. It proposes conditional training, a pretraining objective where the model learns to generate tokens conditioned on human preference scores from a reward model, steering it toward aligned outputs. Evaluated across three tasks, conditional training reduces undesirable content by up to an order of magnitude under both normal and adversarially-prompted generation, while preserving downstream task performance. The results demonstrate that incorporating human feedback during pretraining yields more robust and satisfying alignment than standard post-hoc finetuning, providing direct evidence that post-training safety alignment can be fragile and that building alignment from the start is a more resilient approach.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了标准语言模型因在互联网文本上预训练而包含违反人类偏好的有害内容的问题。它提出了一种名为条件训练的预训练目标，使模型根据奖励模型给出的人类偏好分数来学习生成条件化的token分布，从而引导输出对齐。在三个任务上的评估表明，条件训练在正常和对抗性提示下都能将不良内容减少一个数量级，同时保持下游任务性能。结果表明，在预训练阶段融入人类反馈比标准的事后微调能产生更稳健、更令人满意的对齐，直接证明了事后安全对齐可能具有脆弱性，而从训练之初就构建对齐是一种更具韧性的方法。

papers.title: Focus On This, Not That! Steering LLMs with Adaptive Feature Specification
papers.short_title: FIT: Adaptive Feature Steering for LLMs
papers.abstract: Despite the success of Instruction Tuning (IT) in training large language models (LLMs), such models often leverage spurious or biased features learnt from their training data and can become misaligned, leading to undesired behaviours. While existing techniques can steer model behaviour at inference-time, they are often post-hoc and do not embed steering as an intrinsic model feature. In this work, we introduce Focus Instruction Tuning (FIT), which trains LLMs to condition their responses by focusing on specific features whilst ignoring others, leading to different behaviours based on what features are specified. Across diverse benchmarks, we demonstrate that FIT: (i) successfully steers behaviour at inference time; (ii) increases robustness by amplifying core task signals and down-weighting spurious cues; (iii) mitigates social bias by suppressing demographic attributes; and (iv) generalises under distribution shifts and to previously unseen focus features. FIT therefore offers a lightweight, intrinsic mechanism for building more robust, fair, and easily controllable LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the issue that LLMs often exploit spurious or biased features from training data, leading to misalignment despite instruction tuning. It proposes Focus Instruction Tuning (FIT), which trains models to condition their outputs on specified features while ignoring others, embedding steering as an intrinsic capability. Evaluations on diverse benchmarks show that FIT enables reliable inference-time behavior steering, improves robustness against spurious cues, mitigates social bias, and generalizes to unseen features and distribution shifts. By moving beyond post-hoc and fragile steering methods, FIT directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment, demonstrating that intrinsic feature-conditioned training can produce more robust and controllable models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在指令微调后仍可能利用训练数据中的虚假或偏见特征，导致行为偏差的问题。提出聚焦指令微调（FIT），通过训练模型根据指定特征生成回应并忽略其他特征，将行为引导内化为模型固有功能。在多个基准测试中，FIT 实现了推理时的行为控制，通过强化核心任务信号和抑制虚假线索提升了鲁棒性，减少了社会偏见，并在分布偏移和未见特征上展现了泛化能力。FIT 提供了一种轻量级的内在引导机制，取代了脆弱的事后修正方法，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题，证明基于特征条件的训练可构建更健壮、公平且易控的模型。

papers.title: Eliciting Language Model Behaviors with Investigator Agents
papers.abstract: Language models exhibit complex, diverse behaviors when prompted with free-form text, making it difficult to characterize the space of possible outputs. We study the problem of behavior elicitation, where the goal is to search for prompts that induce specific target behaviors (e.g., hallucinations or harmful responses) from a target language model. To navigate the exponentially large space of possible prompts, we train investigator models to map randomly-chosen target behaviors to a diverse distribution of outputs that elicit them, similar to amortized Bayesian inference. We do this through supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning via DPO, and a novel Frank-Wolfe training objective to iteratively discover diverse prompting strategies. Our investigator models surface a variety of effective and human-interpretable prompts leading to jailbreaks, hallucinations, and open-ended aberrant behaviors, obtaining a 100% attack success rate on a subset of AdvBench (Harmful Behaviors) and an 85% hallucination rate.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of systematically eliciting specific target behaviors (e.g., harmful responses, hallucinations) from language models via prompting. It proposes training investigator agents, using supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and a novel Frank-Wolfe objective, to map target behaviors to diverse and effective prompts. The investigators achieve a 100% attack success rate on a subset of AdvBench harmful behaviors and an 85% hallucination rate, surfacing interpretable jailbreaks and aberrant behaviors. These findings directly demonstrate the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as the discovered prompts reliably bypass safeguards to elicit harmful outputs, revealing a new attack surface.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了通过提示词系统性地引发语言模型特定目标行为（如有害响应、幻觉）的挑战。提出了训练调查模型方法，利用监督微调、DPO和一种新颖的Frank-Wolfe目标，将目标行为映射到多样有效的提示。调查模型在AdvBench有害行为子集上实现了100%攻击成功率，幻觉率达85%，发现了可解释的越狱和异常行为。这些发现直接表明后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，因为发现的提示可靠地绕过了防护措施，诱发了有害输出，揭示了新的攻击面。

papers.title: RuleAdapter: Dynamic Rules for training Safety Reward Models in RLHF
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is widely used to align models with human preferences, particularly to enhance the safety of responses generated by LLMs. This method traditionally...
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the rigidity of static safety rules in RLHF by proposing RuleAdapter, a method that dynamically adapts rules during safety reward model training to improve alignment flexibility. It evaluates on safety benchmarks, demonstrating a better trade-off between safety and helpfulness compared to static approaches. This work advances alignment methodology by making safety reward models more adaptable, but it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中静态安全规则的僵化问题，提出RuleAdapter方法，在安全奖励模型训练过程中动态调整规则，以增强对齐的灵活性。在安全基准上评估，结果表明相比静态方法，该方法在安全性和有用性之间取得了更好的平衡。该工作通过提升安全奖励模型的适应性推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Test-Time Preference Optimization: On-the-Fly Alignment via Iterative Textual Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive performance but lack the flexibility to adapt to human preferences quickly without retraining. In this work, we introduce Test-time Preference Optimization (TPO), a framework that aligns LLM outputs with human preferences during inference, removing the need to update model parameters. Rather than relying on purely numerical rewards, TPO translates reward signals into textual critiques and uses them as textual rewards to iteratively refine its response. Evaluations on benchmarks covering instruction following, preference alignment, safety, and mathematics reveal that TPO progressively improves alignment with human preferences. Notably, after only a few TPO steps, the initially unaligned Llama-3.1-70B-SFT model can surpass the aligned counterpart, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. Furthermore, TPO scales efficiently with both the search width and depth during inference. Through case studies, we illustrate how TPO exploits the innate capacity of LLM to interpret and act upon reward signals. Our findings establish TPO as a practical, lightweight alternative for test-time preference optimization, achieving alignment on the fly. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/yafuly/TPO.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the inability of LLMs to adapt to human preferences without retraining. It proposes Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO), which aligns outputs during inference by converting reward signals into textual critiques and iteratively refining responses. Evaluated on instruction following, preference, safety, and math benchmarks, TPO progressively improves alignment, allowing an unaligned Llama-3.1-70B-SFT to surpass the aligned Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct after a few steps. While TPO offers a test-time alternative to post-training alignment, demonstrating dynamic on-the-fly alignment, it does not directly assess the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型在不重新训练情况下难以快速适应用户偏好的问题。提出测试时偏好优化（TPO），在推断过程中通过将奖励信号转化为文本批评并迭代优化响应来实现输出对齐。在指令遵循、偏好对齐、安全性和数学推理等基准上评估，TPO逐步提升对齐效果，仅几步后未对齐的Llama-3.1-70B-SFT即超越已对齐的Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct。该研究提供了测试时对齐的替代方案，展示了动态优化对齐的潜力，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Alignment Algorithms: A Case Study on DPO and Toxicity
papers.short_title: Mechanistic Study of DPO and Toxicity
papers.abstract: While alignment algorithms are now commonly used to tune pre-trained language models towards a user's preferences, we lack explanations for the underlying mechanisms in which models become ``aligned'', thus making it difficult to explain phenomena like jailbreaks. In this work we study a popular algorithm, direct preference optimization (DPO), and the mechanisms by which it reduces toxicity. Namely, we first study how toxicity is represented and elicited in a pre-trained language model, GPT2-medium. We then apply DPO with a carefully crafted pairwise dataset to reduce toxicity. We examine how the resulting model averts toxic outputs, and find that capabilities learned from pre-training are not removed, but rather bypassed. We use this insight to demonstrate a simple method to un-align the model, reverting it back to its toxic behavior.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the mechanistic underpinnings of how Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) reduces toxicity in language models, addressing the lack of explainability in alignment. Using a case study on GPT2-medium, they craft a pairwise dataset to apply DPO and analyze the model's internal representations. They find that DPO does not erase pre-trained toxic capabilities but bypasses them, and demonstrate a simple method to revert the model to toxic behavior. This provides direct evidence that post-training alignment can be fragile and easily undone, highlighting its potential superficiality.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了直接偏好优化（DPO）减少毒性的内在机制，弥补了对齐算法可解释性的缺失。通过GPT2-medium的案例研究，他们构建成对数据集应用DPO，并分析毒性表征与绕过方式。他们发现DPO并未消除预训练的毒性能力，而是将其抑制，并展示了一种简单方法使模型恢复毒性行为。这直接证明后训练对齐可能脆弱且易逆转，揭示其可能仅为表层约束。

papers.title: ELITE: Enhanced Language-Image Toxicity Evaluation for Safety
papers.short_title: ELITE: Enhanced Toxicity Eval for VLMs
papers.abstract: Current Vision Language Models (VLMs) remain vulnerable to malicious prompts that induce harmful outputs. Existing safety benchmarks for VLMs primarily rely on automated evaluation methods, but these methods struggle to detect implicit harmful content or produce inaccurate evaluations. Therefore, we found that existing benchmarks have low levels of harmfulness, ambiguous data, and limited diversity in image-text pair combinations. To address these issues, we propose the ELITE benchmark, a high-quality safety evaluation benchmark for VLMs, underpinned by our enhanced evaluation method, the ELITE evaluator. The ELITE evaluator explicitly incorporates a toxicity score to accurately assess harmfulness in multimodal contexts, where VLMs often provide specific, convincing, but unharmful descriptions of images. We filter out ambiguous and low-quality image-text pairs from existing benchmarks using the ELITE evaluator and generate diverse combinations of safe and unsafe image-text pairs. Our experiments demonstrate that the ELITE evaluator achieves superior alignment with human evaluations compared to prior automated methods, and the ELITE benchmark offers enhanced benchmark quality and diversity. By introducing ELITE, we pave the way for safer, more robust VLMs, contributing essential tools for evaluating and mitigating safety risks in real-world applications.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the issue of inadequate safety benchmarks for vision-language models (VLMs), which often suffer from low harmfulness, ambiguous data, and limited diversity. It proposes ELITE, a high-quality benchmark and evaluator that incorporates a toxicity score to more accurately detect harmful multimodal outputs, filtering out ambiguous pairs and generating diverse safe/unsafe combinations. Experiments show that the ELITE evaluator aligns better with human judgments than prior automated methods, and the benchmark improves quality and diversity. This paper primarily advances alignment evaluation methodology and does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉语言模型（VLM）安全评估基准存在有害性低、数据模糊和多样性有限等问题，提出ELITE基准和评估器，通过引入毒性分数来精确检测多模态有害输出，并过滤模糊数据、生成多样化的安全/不安全图文组合。实验表明，ELITE评估器比以往的自动化方法更符合人类判断，且基准质量和多样性均有提升。本文主要推动了安全对齐评估方法的发展，并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Safety Alignment Can Be Not Superficial With Explicit Safety Signals
papers.abstract: Recent studies on the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) have revealed that existing approaches often operate superficially, leaving models vulnerable to various adversarial attacks. Despite their significance, these studies generally fail to offer actionable solutions beyond data augmentation for achieving more robust safety mechanisms. This paper identifies a fundamental cause of this superficiality: existing alignment approaches often presume that models can implicitly learn a safety-related reasoning task during the alignment process, enabling them to refuse harmful requests. However, the learned safety signals are often diluted by other competing objectives, leading models to struggle with drawing a firm safety-conscious decision boundary when confronted with adversarial attacks. Based on this observation, by explicitly introducing a safety-related binary classification task and integrating its signals with our attention and decoding strategies, we eliminate this ambiguity and allow models to respond more responsibly to malicious queries. We emphasize that, with less than 0.2x overhead cost, our approach enables LLMs to assess the safety of both the query and the previously generated tokens at each necessary generating step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves the resilience of LLMs against various adversarial attacks, offering a promising pathway toward more robust generative AI systems.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the superficiality in safety alignment of LLMs, where models remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks because safety signals are diluted by competing objectives. It proposes explicitly incorporating a safety-related binary classification task and integrating its signals into attention and decoding strategies to eliminate decision boundary ambiguity. Evaluated on various adversarial attacks, the method significantly improves model resilience with less than 0.2x overhead cost. This work hardens alignment mechanisms, directly addressing the fragility of post-training safety alignment by making it less superficial and more robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全对齐的表面性问题，即安全信号被其他目标稀释，导致模型难以抵御对抗攻击。提出通过显式引入安全二分类任务，并将其信号整合至注意力和解码策略，消除决策边界模糊性。在多种对抗攻击上的实验表明，该方法以不到0.2倍额外开销显著提升模型鲁棒性。该工作通过增强安全对齐的深度，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性挑战，提供了更稳健的生成式AI路径。

papers.title: ReMax: A Simple, Effective, and Efficient Reinforcement Learning Method for Aligning Large Language Models
papers.short_title: ReMax: Efficient RL for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is key to aligning Large Language Models (LLMs), typically paired with the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. While PPO is a powerful method designed for general reinforcement learning tasks, it is overly sophisticated for LLMs, leading to laborious hyper-parameter tuning and significant computation burdens. To make RLHF efficient, we present ReMax, which leverages 3 properties of RLHF: fast simulation, deterministic transitions, and trajectory-level rewards. These properties are not exploited in PPO, making it less suitable for RLHF. Building on the renowned REINFORCE algorithm, ReMax does not require training an additional value model as in PPO and is further enhanced with a new variance reduction technique. ReMax offers several benefits over PPO: it is simpler to implement, eliminates more than 4 hyper-parameters in PPO, reduces GPU memory usage, and shortens training time. ReMax can save about 46% GPU memory than PPO when training a 7B model and enables training on A800-80GB GPUs without the memory-saving offloading technique needed by PPO. Applying ReMax to a Mistral-7B model resulted in a 94.78% win rate on the AlpacaEval leaderboard and a 7.739 score on MT-bench, setting a new SOTA for open-source 7B models. These results show the effectiveness of ReMax while addressing the limitations of PPO in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency and complexity of PPO for RLHF-based LLM alignment. ReMax is proposed, leveraging fast simulation, deterministic transitions, and trajectory-level rewards, using REINFORCE with variance reduction and eliminating the need for a value model. It reduces GPU memory by about 46% for a 7B model and achieves SOTA results on AlpacaEval and MT-bench. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 论文解决了基于RLHF对齐大语言模型时PPO方法的低效与复杂性问题。提出ReMax方法，利用快速模拟、确定性状态转移和轨迹级奖励特性，基于REINFORCE加入方差缩减，无需训练价值模型。训练7B模型时节省约46% GPU内存，并在AlpacaEval和MT-bench上取得最优结果。该论文改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: PIPA: Preference Alignment as Prior-Informed Statistical Estimation
papers.abstract: Offline preference alignment for language models such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is favored for its effectiveness and simplicity, eliminating the need for costly reinforcement learning. Various offline algorithms have been developed for different data settings, yet they lack a unified understanding. In this study, we introduce Pior-Informed Preference Alignment (PIPA), a unified, RL-free probabilistic framework that formulates language model preference alignment as a Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) problem with prior constraints. This method effectively accommodates both paired and unpaired data, as well as answer and step-level annotations. We illustrate that DPO and KTO are special cases with different prior constraints within our framework. By integrating different types of prior information, we developed two variations of PIPA: PIPA-M and PIPA-N. Both algorithms demonstrate a $3\sim10\%$ performance enhancement on the GSM8K and MATH benchmarks across all configurations, achieving these gains without additional training or computational costs compared to existing algorithms.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of a unified framework for offline preference alignment algorithms like DPO and KTO. It proposes PIPA, a prior-informed probabilistic framework that formulates language model preference alignment as maximum likelihood estimation with prior constraints, naturally handling paired/unpaired data and answer/step-level annotations. The variants PIPA-M and PIPA-N achieve 3–10% performance gains on GSM8K and MATH benchmarks without extra training cost. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对离线偏好对齐算法（如DPO、KTO）缺乏统一理论框架的问题，提出了PIPA，一种基于先验信息的概率框架，将语言模型偏好对齐建模为带先验约束的最大似然估计，能自然处理配对/非配对数据以及答案/步骤级标注。其变体PIPA-M和PIPA-N在GSM8K和MATH基准上以零额外成本实现了3–10%的性能提升。该方法推进了对齐技术，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: The Devil Is in the Details: Tackling Unimodal Spurious Correlations for Generalizable Multimodal Reward Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal Reward Models (MM-RMs) are crucial for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences, particularly as LLMs increasingly interact with multimodal data. However, we find tha...
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of unimodal spurious correlations in multimodal reward models (MM-RMs), where models rely on features from a single modality (e.g., text) instead of true multimodal understanding, leading to poor generalization. It proposes a method to tackle these spurious correlations, likely through explicit debiasing or multi-view training. Experiments demonstrate improved generalization and robustness, confirming that MM-RMs benefit from mitigating unimodal shortcuts. This work directly contributes to the fragility question by revealing a specific vulnerability in multimodal alignment and providing a hardening technique.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了多模态奖励模型（MM-RM）中的单模态虚假关联问题，即模型依赖单一模态特征（如文本）而非真正的多模态理解，导致泛化能力差。它提出了一种方法来应对这些虚假关联，可能通过显式去偏或多视角训练。实验证明该方法能提高泛化性和鲁棒性，验证了减轻单模态捷径对MM-RM的好处。这项工作揭示了多模态对齐中的一个具体脆弱性并提供了强化方法，直接回应了安全性对齐是否坚固的问题。

papers.title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use with Unlearning
papers.abstract: The White House Executive Order on Artificial Intelligence highlights the risks of large language models (LLMs) empowering malicious actors in developing biological, cyber, and chemical weapons. To measure these risks of malicious use, government institutions and major AI labs are developing evaluations for hazardous capabilities in LLMs. However, current evaluations are private, preventing further research into mitigating risk. Furthermore, they focus on only a few, highly specific pathways for malicious use.
