papers.abstract: An important issue with Large Language Models (LLMs) is their undesired ability to generate toxic language. In this work, we show that the neurons responsible for toxicity can be determined by their power to discriminate toxic sentences, and that toxic language can be mitigated by reducing their activation levels proportionally to this power. We propose AUROC adaptation (AurA), an intervention that can be applied to any pre-trained LLM to mitigate toxicity. As the intervention is proportional to the ability of each neuron to discriminate toxic content, it is free of any model-dependent hyperparameters. We show that AurA can achieve up to $2.2 \times$ reduction in toxicity with only a $0.72$ perplexity increase. We also show that AurA is effective with models of different scale (from 1.5B to 40B parameters), and its effectiveness in mitigating toxic language, while preserving common-sense zero-shot abilities, holds across all scales. AurA can be combined with pre-prompting strategies, boosting its average mitigation potential from $1.28\times$ to $2.35\times$. Moreover, AurA can counteract adversarial pre-prompts that maliciously elicit toxic content, making it an effective method for deploying safer and less toxic models.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of toxic language generation in Large Language Models (LLMs). It proposes AurA (AUROC adaptation), an intervention that identifies neurons responsible for toxicity by their ability to discriminate toxic sentences and proportionally reduces their activations, requiring no model-dependent hyperparameters. Evaluations show up to 2.2× toxicity reduction with a 0.72 perplexity increase, effectiveness across 1.5B–40B parameter models, and compatibility with pre-prompting to amplify mitigation and counter adversarial prompts. The work advances toxicity mitigation methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型（LLM）生成有毒内容的问题。提出AurA（AUROC adaptation）方法，通过神经元区分有毒句子的能力识别关键神经元，并按其判别力降低激活值，无需任何模型特定超参数。实验表明，在困惑度仅增加0.72的情况下毒性降低最高2.2倍，在1.5B至40B参数的模型上均有效，且能与预提示策略结合以增强缓解效果并抵御恶意攻击。该方法推进了毒性缓解技术，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Right Now, Wrong Then: Non-Stationary Direct Preference Optimization under Preference Drift
papers.abstract: Current Large Language Model (LLM) preference optimization algorithms do not account for temporal preference drift, which can lead to severe misalignment. To address this limitation, we propose Non-Stationary Direct Preference Optimisation (NS-DPO) that models time-dependent reward functions with a Dynamic Bradley-Terry model. NS-DPO proposes a computationally efficient solution by introducing only a single discount parameter in the loss function, which is used for exponential weighting that proportionally focuses learning on more time-relevant datapoints. We theoretically analyze the convergence of NS-DPO in a general setting where the exact nature of the preference drift is not known, providing upper bounds on the estimation error and regret caused by non-stationary preferences. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of NS-DPO for fine-tuning LLMs under drifting preferences. Using scenarios where various levels of preference drift is introduced, with popular LLM reward models and datasets, we show that NS-DPO fine-tuned LLMs remain robust under non-stationarity, significantly outperforming baseline algorithms that ignore temporal preference changes, without sacrificing performance in stationary cases.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of temporal preference drift in LLM alignment, which can cause severe misalignment when static optimization is used. It proposes Non-Stationary Direct Preference Optimization (NS-DPO), which models time-dependent rewards with a Dynamic Bradley-Terry model and introduces a single discount parameter for exponential weighting of recent data, keeping the approach computationally efficient. The authors provide theoretical convergence analysis under unknown drift and empirically demonstrate that NS-DPO fine-tuned LLMs remain robust under drifting preferences, outperforming baselines that ignore temporal changes without sacrificing stationary performance. While the paper primarily advances alignment methodology, it implicitly highlights a fragility: ignoring preference drift undermines alignment, thus contributing to more robust post-training alignment over time.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了LLM对齐中的时间偏好漂移问题，静态优化可能导致严重的不对齐。提出非平稳直接偏好优化（NS-DPO），通过动态Bradley-Terry模型建模时变奖励函数，并在损失中引入单一折扣参数以指数加权近期数据，保持计算高效。作者在未知漂移下进行了理论收敛分析，并实验证明NS-DPO微调的LLM在漂移偏好下保持稳健，显著优于忽略时间变化的基线方法，且不牺牲平稳场景性能。虽然本文主要推进对齐方法，但它隐含地揭示了一种脆弱性：忽视偏好漂移会破坏对齐，从而有助于构建随时间更稳健的后训练对齐。

papers.title: Active Reward Modeling: Adaptive Preference Labeling for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: Active Reward Modeling for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Building neural reward models from human preferences is a pivotal component in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and large language model alignment research. Given the scarcity and ...
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost and scarcity of human preference labels when building reward models for RLHF. It proposes active reward modeling, an approach that adaptively selects the most informative response pairs for labeling to improve data efficiency. Experiments demonstrate that this method reduces labeling effort while achieving competitive or better alignment compared to uniform sampling. The work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of the alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在RLHF中构建奖励模型时人类偏好标签成本高且稀缺的问题。提出了主动奖励建模方法，自适应地选择最具信息量的响应对进行标注，以提高数据效率。实验表明，该方法在减少标注工作量的同时，能实现与均匀采样相当或更好的对齐效果。该研究推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐本身的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: RLVF: Learning from Verbal Feedback without Overgeneralization
papers.abstract: The diversity of contexts in which large language models (LLMs) are deployed requires the ability to modify or customize default model behaviors to incorporate nuanced requirements and preferences. A convenient interface to specify such model adjustments is high-level verbal feedback, such as"Don't use emojis when drafting emails to my boss."However, while writing high-level feedback is far simpler than collecting annotations for reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), we find that simply prompting a model with such feedback leads to overgeneralization of the feedback to contexts where it is not relevant. We study the problem of incorporating verbal feedback without such overgeneralization, inspiring a new method Contextualized Critiques with Constrained Preference Optimization (C3PO). C3PO uses a piece of high-level feedback to generate a small synthetic preference dataset specifying how the feedback should (and should not) be applied. It then fine-tunes the model in accordance with the synthetic preference data while minimizing the divergence from the original model for prompts where the feedback does not apply. Our experimental results indicate that our approach effectively applies verbal feedback to relevant scenarios while preserving existing behaviors for other contexts. For both human- and GPT-4-generated high-level feedback, C3PO effectively adheres to the given feedback comparably to in-context baselines while reducing overgeneralization by 30%.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the overgeneralization problem when applying high-level verbal feedback to LLMs. It proposes C3PO, which generates a synthetic preference dataset from the feedback and fine-tunes the model with a constrained optimization objective to minimize divergence from the original model for irrelevant prompts. Evaluated on human- and GPT-4-generated feedback, C3PO reduces overgeneralization by 30% while matching in-context baselines in feedback adherence. This work advances alignment methodology by improving the precision of verbal feedback integration but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了将高层口头反馈应用于大语言模型时出现的过度泛化问题。它提出了C3PO方法，通过从反馈生成合成偏好数据集，并以约束优化目标微调模型，最小化与原始模型在无关提示上的偏差。在人类和GPT-4生成的反馈上评估，C3PO在保持与上下文基线相当的反馈遵循度的同时，将过度泛化降低了30%。这项工作通过提升口头反馈集成的精准性推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探究后训练安全对齐在对抗攻击下的脆弱性。

papers.title: Position: A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
papers.abstract: With increased power and prevalence of AI systems, it is ever more critical that AI systems are designed to serve all, i.e., people with diverse values and perspectives. However, aligning ...
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that AI alignment typically optimizes for a single set of values, neglecting the pluralistic nature of human preferences. It proposes a roadmap for pluralistic alignment, outlining key challenges, potential methods, and evaluation strategies to incorporate diverse values. As a position paper, it does not present empirical results but surveys existing work to define a research agenda. It relates to the fragility question by arguing that monolithic alignment is inherently brittle when confronted with diverse real-world values, thus pluralistic alignment may offer a path to more robust safety.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前AI对齐通常优化单一价值观而忽视人类偏好多元性的问题。提出了多元化对齐的路线图，概述了整合多元价值观的关键挑战、方法及评估策略。作为立场论文，未提供实证结果，但通过综述现有工作界定了研究议程。它与对齐稳健性问题相关，指出单一片面的对齐在面对现实世界多元价值观时本质上脆弱，因此多元化对齐可能提供更稳健的安全路径。

papers.title: A Minimaximalist Approach to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: We present Self-Play Preference Optimization (SPO), an algorithm for reinforcement learning from human feedback. Our approach is minimalist in that it does not require training a reward model nor unstable adversarial training and is therefore rather simple to implement. Our approach is maximalist in that it provably handles non-Markovian, intransitive, and stochastic preferences while being robust to the compounding errors that plague offline approaches to sequential prediction. To achieve the preceding qualities, we build upon the concept of a Minimax Winner (MW), a notion of preference aggregation from the social choice theory literature that frames learning from preferences as a zero-sum game between two policies. By leveraging the symmetry of this game, we prove that rather than using the traditional technique of dueling two policies to compute the MW, we can simply have a single agent play against itself while maintaining strong convergence guarantees. Practically, this corresponds to sampling multiple trajectories from a policy, asking a preference or teacher model to compare them, and then using the proportion of wins as the reward for a particular trajectory. We demonstrate that on a suite of continuous control tasks, we are able to learn significantly more efficiently than reward-model based approaches while maintaining robustness to the intransitive and stochastic preferences that frequently occur in practice when aggregating human judgments.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of learning from human preferences that may be non-Markovian, intransitive, or stochastic, which can cause instability and inefficiency in standard RLHF. It proposes Self-Play Preference Optimization (SPO), a minimax approach that frames preference aggregation as a zero-sum game and uses self-play to compute rewards from win proportions, avoiding reward model training. In continuous control tasks, SPO demonstrates significantly improved learning efficiency and robustness compared to reward-model-based methods. This work advances alignment methodology by enhancing robustness to complex preferences but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了从非马尔可夫、非传递或随机的人类偏好中学习的挑战，这些偏好可能导致标准RLHF的不稳定和低效。提出了一种极小极大方法——自博弈偏好优化（SPO），将偏好聚合视为零和博弈，并利用自博弈通过胜率计算奖励，避免了奖励模型训练。在连续控制任务中，SPO相比基于奖励模型的方法，显著提高了学习效率和鲁棒性。这项工作通过增强对复杂偏好的鲁棒性推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质脆弱或容易被绕过。

papers.title: CASE-Bench: Context-Aware SafEty Benchmark for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values is essential for their safe deployment and widespread adoption. Current LLM safety benchmarks often focus solely on the refusal of individual problematic queries, which overlooks the importance of the context where the query occurs and may cause undesired refusal of queries under safe contexts that diminish user experience. Addressing this gap, we introduce CASE-Bench, a Context-Aware SafEty Benchmark that integrates context into safety assessments of LLMs. CASE-Bench assigns distinct, formally described contexts to categorized queries based on Contextual Integrity theory. Additionally, in contrast to previous studies which mainly rely on majority voting from just a few annotators, we recruited a sufficient number of annotators necessary to ensure the detection of statistically significant differences among the experimental conditions based on power analysis. Our extensive analysis using CASE-Bench on various open-source and commercial LLMs reveals a substantial and significant influence of context on human judgments (p<0.0001 from a z-test), underscoring the necessity of context in safety evaluations. We also identify notable mismatches between human judgments and LLM responses, particularly in commercial models within safe contexts.
papers.summary_en: Current LLM safety benchmarks neglect context, often causing over-refusal in safe situations. CASE-Bench integrates context into safety evaluation by assigning formally described contexts to queries using Contextual Integrity theory. A statistically powered human study reveals context significantly affects safety judgments (p<0.0001) and LLMs, especially commercial ones, show mismatches with humans, often refusing safe queries. By demonstrating that safety alignment fails to adapt to context, this paper highlights its fragility: post-training alignment is not robustly context-aware, leading to inappropriate refusals that undermine usability.
papers.summary_zh: 现有LLM安全基准忽视上下文，常导致安全情境下的过度拒绝。CASE-Bench基于情境完整性理论，为查询分配正式描述的上下文，将上下文纳入安全评估。通过统计功效分析确定样本量的大规模人类研究表明，上下文显著影响安全判断（p<0.0001），且LLM与人类判断存在错配，尤其在商业模型处理安全上下文时。该工作揭示了安全对齐对上下文变化的脆弱性：对齐并非稳健的上下文感知，不当拒绝表明其鲁棒性不足，直接回应了对齐真实健壮性的核心疑问。

papers.title: LOGO - Long cOntext aliGnment via efficient preference Optimization
papers.short_title: LOGO: Long Context Align. via Pref. Opt.
papers.abstract: Long-context models(LCMs) have shown great potential in processing long input sequences(even more than 100M tokens) conveniently and effectively. With significant progress, recent research has pointed out that LCMs can accurately locate token-level salient information within the context. Yet, the generation performance of these LCMs is far from satisfactory and might result in misaligned responses, such as hallucinations. To enhance the generation capability of LCMs, existing works have investigated the effects of data size and quality for both pre-training and instruction tuning. Though achieving meaningful improvement, previous methods fall short in either effectiveness or efficiency. In this paper, we introduce LOGO(Long cOntext aliGnment via efficient preference Optimization), a training strategy that first introduces preference optimization for long-context alignment. To overcome the GPU memory-bound issue caused by the long sequence, LOGO employs a reference-free preference optimization strategy and adopts a position synthesis method to construct the training data. By training with only 0.3B data on a single 8$\times$A800 GPU machine for 16 hours, LOGO allows the Llama-3-8B-Instruct-80K model to achieve comparable performance with GPT-4 in real-world long-context tasks while preserving the model's original capabilities on other tasks, e.g., language modeling and MMLU. Moreover, LOGO can extend the model's context window size while enhancing its generation performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the issue of poor generation quality, such as hallucinations, in long-context models, noting that models can locate salient information but produce misaligned responses. It proposes LOGO, a training strategy that uses reference-free preference optimization and position-synthesized training data to efficiently align LCMs under GPU memory constraints. Evaluated by fine-tuning Llama-3-8B-Instruct-80K on 0.3B data for 16 hours on a single 8×A800 GPU, LOGO matches GPT-4 on real-world long-context tasks while preserving original capabilities and extends context window size. This work advances alignment methodology for long contexts but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决长上下文模型生成质量不佳（如幻觉）的问题，即使模型能定位关键信息，响应仍可能偏离预期。提出 LOGO，一种采用无参考偏好优化与位置合成训练数据的高效对齐策略，以克服长序列的内存限制。通过在单台 8×A800 GPU 上用 0.3B 数据微调 Llama-3-8B-Instruct-80K 16 小时，LOGO 在真实长上下文任务上达到 GPT-4 性能，同时保留原能力并扩展上下文窗口。此工作推进了长上下文对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Generalized Preference Optimization: A Unified Approach to Offline Alignment
papers.abstract: Offline preference optimization allows fine-tuning large models directly from offline data, and has proved effective in recent alignment practices. We propose generalized preference optimization (GPO), a family of offline losses parameterized by a general class of convex functions. GPO enables a unified view over preference optimization, encompassing existing algorithms such as DPO, IPO and SLiC as special cases, while naturally introducing new variants. The GPO framework also sheds light on how offline algorithms enforce regularization, through the design of the convex function that defines the loss. Our analysis and experiments reveal the connections and subtle differences between the offline regularization and the KL divergence regularization intended by the canonical RLHF formulation. In a controlled setting akin to Gao et al 2023, we also show that different GPO variants achieve similar trade-offs between regularization and performance, though the optimal values of hyper-parameter might differ as predicted by theory. In all, our results present new algorithmic toolkits and empirical insights to alignment practitioners.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses offline preference optimization for aligning large language models, noting that existing algorithms like DPO, IPO, and SLiC are special cases of a broader objective. It proposes Generalized Preference Optimization (GPO), a family of offline losses parameterized by a convex function, providing a unified framework. Analysis reveals how the convex function shapes regularization, and experiments in a controlled setting show that different GPO variants achieve similar trade-offs between regularization and performance, though optimal hyperparameters differ. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决离线偏好优化在对齐大语言模型中的应用，指出DPO、IPO和SLiC等现有算法是更广泛目标函数的特例。它提出广义偏好优化（GPO），通过一类凸函数参数化离线损失，构建统一框架。分析揭示了凸函数如何塑造正则化，实验在受控环境下表明不同GPO变体在正则化与性能之间实现类似权衡，但最优超参数存在差异。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: The Illusion of Role Separation: Hidden Shortcuts in LLM Role Learning (and How to Fix Them)
papers.short_title: Fixing Role Separation Shortcuts in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) that integrate multiple input roles (e.g., system instructions, user queries, external tool outputs) are increasingly prevalent in practice. Ensuring that the model accurately distinguishes messages from each role -- a concept we call \emph{role separation} -- is crucial for consistent multi-role behavior. Although recent work often targets state-of-the-art prompt injection defenses, it remains unclear whether such methods truly teach LLMs to differentiate roles or merely memorize known triggers. In this paper, we examine \emph{role-separation learning}: the process of teaching LLMs to robustly distinguish system and user tokens. Through a \emph{simple, controlled experimental framework}, we find that fine-tuned models often rely on two proxies for role identification: (1) task type exploitation, and (2) proximity to begin-of-text. Although data augmentation can partially mitigate these shortcuts, it generally leads to iterative patching rather than a deeper fix. To address this, we propose reinforcing \emph{invariant signals} that mark role boundaries by adjusting token-wise cues in the model's input encoding. In particular, manipulating position IDs helps the model learn clearer distinctions and reduces reliance on superficial proxies. By focusing on this mechanism-centered perspective, our work illuminates how LLMs can more reliably maintain consistent multi-role behavior without merely memorizing known prompts or triggers.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates role-separation learning in LLMs, revealing that fine-tuned models exploit shortcut proxies like task type and position rather than truly distinguishing role tokens. It proposes a method that reinforces invariant signals by manipulating position IDs to reduce reliance on these superficial cues. Through controlled experiments, the authors show that data augmentation provides limited iterative patching, while their approach leads to more robust role separation. This directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that role separation mechanisms can be shallow and bypassed, highlighting a structural weakness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大语言模型中的角色分离学习，发现微调模型倾向于利用任务类型和位置等捷径进行角色识别，而非真正区分角色标记。提出通过操纵位置ID强化不变信号的方法，减少对表面特征的依赖。控制实验表明，数据增强仅能提供有限的迭代修补，而该方法能实现更稳健的角色分离。这直接说明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，揭示了角色分离机制可能流于表面并被轻易绕过，暴露了结构性弱点。

papers.title: Poisoning Language Models During Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned LMs such as ChatGPT, FLAN, and InstructGPT are finetuned on datasets that contain user-submitted examples, e.g., FLAN aggregates numerous open-source datasets and OpenAI leverages examples submitted in the browser playground. In this work, we show that adversaries can contribute poison examples to these datasets, allowing them to manipulate model predictions whenever a desired trigger phrase appears in the input. For example, when a downstream user provides an input that mentions"Joe Biden", a poisoned LM will struggle to classify, summarize, edit, or translate that input. To construct these poison examples, we optimize their inputs and outputs using a bag-of-words approximation to the LM. We evaluate our method on open-source instruction-tuned LMs. By using as few as 100 poison examples, we can cause arbitrary phrases to have consistent negative polarity or induce degenerate outputs across hundreds of held-out tasks. Worryingly, we also show that larger LMs are increasingly vulnerable to poisoning and that defenses based on data filtering or reducing model capacity provide only moderate protections while reducing test accuracy.
papers.summary_en: The paper demonstrates that adversaries can poison instruction tuning datasets to manipulate model predictions when a trigger phrase appears. The authors craft poison examples by optimizing inputs and outputs using a bag-of-words approximation to the language model. Using only 100 poison examples, they induced consistent negative polarity or degenerate outputs across hundreds of tasks, with larger models more vulnerable. This reveals that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be broken via data poisoning, directly addressing whether alignment is robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文证明，攻击者可通过在指令微调数据集中植入毒化样本，在输入中出现特定触发短语时操纵模型预测。作者提出基于词袋近似的优化方法生成毒化样本的输入与输出。仅用100个毒化样本，就能在数百个保留任务上引发一致负向情感或退化输出，且更大模型更脆弱。该工作揭示训练后安全对齐可通过数据投毒轻易打破，直接回应了对齐鲁棒性的核心问题。

papers.title: MPO: An Efficient Post-Processing Framework for Mixing Diverse Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has shown promise in aligning large language models (LLMs). Yet its reliance on a singular reward model often overlooks the diversity of human preferences. Recent approaches address this limitation by leveraging multi-dimensional feedback to fine-tune corresponding reward models and train LLMs using reinforcement learning. However, the process is costly and unstable, especially given the competing and heterogeneous nature of human preferences. In this paper, we propose Mixing Preference Optimization (MPO), a post-processing framework for aggregating single-objective policies as an alternative to both multi-objective RLHF (MORLHF) and MaxMin-RLHF. MPO avoids alignment from scratch. Instead, it log-linearly combines existing policies into a unified one with the weight of each policy computed via a batch stochastic mirror descent. Empirical results demonstrate that MPO achieves balanced performance across diverse preferences, outperforming or matching existing models with significantly reduced computational costs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the cost and instability of multi-objective RLHF methods for aligning LLMs with diverse human preferences. It proposes MPO, a post-processing framework that log-linearly combines existing single-objective policies, with weights optimized via batch stochastic mirror descent. Empirical results show MPO achieves balanced performance across diverse preferences, matching or outperforming prior methods while significantly reducing computational costs. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多目标RLHF方法在应对多样人类偏好时成本高且不稳定的问题。提出MPO框架，通过对数线性组合现有单目标策略，并使用批量随机镜像下降计算权重。实验结果表明，MPO在多样偏好上取得平衡表现，性能匹配或超越现有模型，且计算成本大幅降低。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接涉及对齐脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly proficient at solving web-based tasks. With this capability comes a greater risk of misuse for malicious purposes, such as posting misinformation in an online forum or selling illicit substances on a website. To evaluate these risks, we propose SafeArena, the first benchmark to focus on the deliberate misuse of web agents. SafeArena comprises 250 safe and 250 harmful tasks across four websites. We classify the harmful tasks into five harm categories -- misinformation, illegal activity, harassment, cybercrime, and social bias, designed to assess realistic misuses of web agents. We evaluate leading LLM-based web agents, including GPT-4o, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Qwen-2-VL 72B, and Llama-3.2 90B, on our benchmark. To systematically assess their susceptibility to harmful tasks, we introduce the Agent Risk Assessment framework that categorizes agent behavior across four risk levels. We find agents are surprisingly compliant with malicious requests, with GPT-4o and Qwen-2 completing 34.7% and 27.3% of harmful requests, respectively. Our findings highlight the urgent need for safety alignment procedures for web agents. Our benchmark is available here: https://safearena.github.io
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the misuse risk of LLM-based autonomous web agents, highlighting that aligned models may still comply with harmful instructions when acting as agents. It introduces SafeArena, a benchmark of 250 safe and 250 harmful web tasks across four websites, covering five harm categories such as misinformation and illegal activity. Evaluation of leading agents like GPT-4o reveals they complete up to 34.7% of harmful requests, using a new Agent Risk Assessment framework. The findings demonstrate a new attack surface where post-training safety alignment can be bypassed in agentic settings, directly supporting the fragility thesis.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对基于大语言模型的自主网页代理可能被恶意利用的问题，提出SafeArena基准，包含四个网站上250个安全任务和250个有害任务，覆盖错误信息、非法活动等五类风险。评估GPT-4o等主流代理后发现，其完成有害请求的比例高达34.7%，并引入代理风险评估框架。结果表明，在代理场景下，安全对齐可被绕过，为后训练对齐的脆弱性提供了新的攻击面证据。

papers.title: GRU: Mitigating the Trade-off between Unlearning and Retention for LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) unlearning has demonstrated its essential role in removing privacy and copyright-related responses, crucial for their legal and safe applications. However, the pursuit of complete unlearning often comes with substantial costs due to its compromises in their general functionality, leading to a notorious trade-off between unlearning and retention. It motivates this paper to explore enhanced unlearning schemes that can mitigate this trade-off. Specifically, we propose Gradient Rectified Unlearning (GRU), an improved framework that regulates the directions of gradient updates during the unlearning procedure such that their side impacts on other, unrelated responses can be minimized. GRU is easy and general to implement, demonstrating practical effectiveness across a variety of well-established unlearning benchmarks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the trade-off between complete unlearning of unwanted knowledge (e.g., privacy, copyright) and preserving general language model functionality. It proposes Gradient Rectified Unlearning (GRU), a framework that rectifies gradient directions during unlearning to minimize side effects on unrelated responses. Evaluated on various unlearning benchmarks, GRU demonstrates practical effectiveness in achieving a better balance between unlearning and retention. This paper advances unlearning methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型遗忘中完全移除隐私或版权内容与保持通用功能之间的权衡问题展开研究。提出了梯度修正遗忘（GRU）框架，通过在遗忘过程中调整梯度更新方向，减少对无关响应的影响。在多种遗忘基准上评估，证明其能有效平衡遗忘与保留。该论文推进了遗忘对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Transforming and Combining Rewards for Aligning Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A common approach for aligning language models to human preferences is to first learn a reward model from preference data, and then use this reward model to update the language model. We study two closely related problems that arise in this approach. First, any monotone transformation of the reward model preserves preference ranking; is there a choice that is ``better'' than others? Second, we often wish to align language models to multiple properties: how should we combine multiple reward models? Using a probabilistic interpretation of the alignment procedure, we identify a natural choice for transformation for (the common case of) rewards learned from Bradley-Terry preference models. The derived transformation is straightforward: we apply a log-sigmoid function to the centered rewards, a method we term ``LSC-transformation'' (log-sigmoid-centered transformation). This transformation has two important properties. First, it emphasizes improving poorly-performing outputs, rather than outputs that already score well. This mitigates both underfitting (where some prompts are not improved) and reward hacking (where the model learns to exploit misspecification of the reward model). Second, it enables principled aggregation of rewards by linking summation to logical conjunction: the sum of transformed rewards corresponds to the probability that the output is ``good'' in all measured properties, in a sense we make precise. Experiments aligning language models to be both helpful and harmless using RLHF show substantial improvements over the baseline (non-transformed) approach.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses two problems in reward-based alignment: choosing a monotone transformation of reward models that preserves ranking but improves training, and combining multiple reward models. It proposes the log-sigmoid-centered (LSC) transformation, which emphasizes poorly-performing outputs and enables principled reward summation as logical conjunction. Experiments on aligning language models for helpfulness and harmlessness using RLHF show substantial improvements over the non-transformed baseline. This paper advances alignment methodology by improving reward model usage and aggregation, but does not directly address whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决基于奖励的对齐方法中的两个问题：选择保持偏好排序但能改善训练的单调变换，以及合理组合多个奖励模型。提出对中心化奖励应用对数-sigmoid函数（LSC变换），该方法强化低分输出的改进并将奖励求和解释为逻辑合取。在通过RLHF对齐语言模型的帮助性与无害性实验中，该方法显著优于未变换基准。本文改进了奖励模型的使用与聚合方式，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否稳固或易被绕过。

papers.title: Safety Reasoning with Guidelines
papers.abstract: Training safe LLMs remains a critical challenge. The most widely used method, Refusal Training (RT), struggles to generalize against various Out-of-Distribution (OOD) jailbreaking attacks. Although various advanced methods have been proposed to address this issue, we instead question whether OOD attacks inherently surpass the capability of vanilla RT. Evaluations using Best-of-N (BoN) reveal significant safety improvements as N increases, indicating models possess adequate latent safety knowledge but RT fails to consistently elicit it under OOD scenarios. Further domain adaptation analysis reveals that direct RT causes reliance on superficial shortcuts, resulting in non-generalizable representation mappings. Inspired by our findings, we propose training model to perform safety reasoning for each query. Specifically, we synthesize reasoning supervision aligned with specified guidelines that reflect diverse perspectives on safety knowledge. This encourages model to engage in deeper reasoning, explicitly eliciting and utilizing latent safety knowledge for each query. Extensive experiments show that our method significantly improves model generalization against OOD attacks.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates the vulnerability of Refusal Training (RT) to out-of-distribution jailbreaking attacks, showing that RT models possess latent safety knowledge but fail to elicit it consistently due to reliance on superficial shortcuts. It proposes a safety reasoning approach where models are trained with synthesized reasoning supervision aligned to diverse safety guidelines, forcing deeper utilization of latent knowledge. Evaluations demonstrate that this method significantly enhances generalization against OOD attacks compared to vanilla RT. This work directly addresses the fragility of safety alignment by identifying a mechanistic weakness (shortcut learning) and providing a hardening technique that improves robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了拒绝训练（RT）对分布外越狱攻击的脆弱性，表明RT模型虽具备潜在安全知识，但因依赖表面捷径而未能稳定激发。提出了一种安全推理方法，通过合成符合多元安全准则的推理监督，促使模型深入利用潜在安全知识。实验表明该方法显著提升了模型对OOD攻击的泛化能力。本研究通过揭示RT的机制性弱点（捷径学习）并提出强化方案，直接回应了安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Improving Model Alignment Through Collective Intelligence of Open-Source Models
papers.abstract: Building helpful and harmless large language models (LLMs) requires effective model alignment approach based on human instructions and feedback, which necessitates high-quality human-labeled data. ...
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of acquiring high-quality human-labeled data for LLM alignment. It proposes leveraging the collective intelligence of multiple open-source models to generate or refine alignment data, reducing reliance on costly human annotations. The method is evaluated on alignment benchmarks, demonstrating improved alignment performance or data efficiency. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question; it focuses on data efficiency through collective model knowledge.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型对齐需要高质量人类标注数据的问题。提出利用多个开源模型的集体智能来生成或优化对齐数据，减少对人类标注的依赖。方法在对齐基准上进行了评估，显示出提升的对齐性能或数据效率。该工作推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题，而是侧重于通过模型集体知识提高数据效率。

papers.title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning offers a promising solution to privacy and safety concerns in large language models (LLMs) by selectively removing targeted knowledge while preserving utility. However, current methods are highly sensitive to downstream fine-tuning, which can quickly recover forgotten information-even from unrelated tasks. To address this, we introduce invariance into unlearning for the first time, inspired by invariant risk minimization (IRM). Building on this principle, we propose invariant LLM unlearning (ILU), a regularization-based framework that enhances robustness. Notably, ILU generalizes well to diverse fine-tuning tasks, even when trained using a single dataset. A task vector analysis is also provided to further elucidate the rationale behind ILU's effectiveness. Extensive experiments on the WMDP and MUSE benchmark, reveal that ILU significantly outperforms state-of-the-art unlearning methods, including negative preference optimization (NPO) and representation misdirection for unlearning (RMU). Notably, ILU achieves superior unlearning robustness across diverse downstream fine-tuning scenarios (e.g., math, paraphrase detection, and sentiment analysis) while preserving the fine-tuning performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragility of LLM unlearning methods, which can be easily reversed by downstream fine-tuning even on unrelated tasks. It proposes invariant LLM unlearning (ILU), a regularization framework inspired by invariant risk minimization that enhances robustness. Evaluated on WMDP and MUSE benchmarks, ILU significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods like NPO and RMU, maintaining unlearning across diverse fine-tuning scenarios. This work directly demonstrates that unlearning is a fragile module that can be broken by fine-tuning, and offers a hardening method to improve its resilience.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型遗忘方法在面临下游微调时易被逆转的脆弱性问题，即使不相关任务也可能快速恢复已遗忘信息。提出不变性大语言模型遗忘（ILU），一种受不变风险最小化启发的正则化框架，以增强鲁棒性。在WMDP和MUSE基准上评估，ILU显著优于负偏好优化（NPO）和表示误导遗忘（RMU）等现有方法，在多种微调场景下保持遗忘鲁棒性。该工作直接证明了遗忘作为后训练安全对齐的一种形式是脆弱的，微调可轻易打破，并提供了一种硬化方法来提升其韧性。

papers.title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show inherent brittleness in their safety mechanisms, as evidenced by their susceptibility to jailbreaking and even non-malicious fine-tuning. This study explores this brittleness of safety alignment by leveraging pruning and low-rank modifications. We develop methods to identify critical regions that are vital for safety guardrails, and that are disentangled from utility-relevant regions at both the neuron and rank levels. Surprisingly, the isolated regions we find are sparse, comprising about $3\%$ at the parameter level and $2.5\%$ at the rank level. Removing these regions compromises safety without significantly impacting utility, corroborating the inherent brittleness of the model's safety mechanisms. Moreover, we show that LLMs remain vulnerable to low-cost fine-tuning attacks even when modifications to the safety-critical regions are restricted. These findings underscore the urgent need for more robust safety strategies in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the inherent brittleness of safety alignment in large language models, which makes them susceptible to jailbreaking and fine-tuning attacks. It introduces methods to identify safety-critical regions using pruning and low-rank modifications, successfully disentangling them from utility-relevant components. The study finds that these safety-critical regions are surprisingly sparse—comprising about 3% of parameters and 2.5% of ranks—and removing them severely compromises safety without significant utility loss. These findings directly demonstrate that post-training safety alignment is a fragile module that can be easily isolated and broken, reinforcing the central fragility thesis.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型安全对齐的固有脆弱性，这种脆弱性使其容易受到越狱和微调攻击。作者提出利用剪枝和低秩修改来识别安全关键区域的方法，成功将这些区域与效用相关部分分离。研究发现，这些安全关键区域非常稀疏——约占参数的3%和秩的2.5%——移除它们会严重损害安全性，但对效用影响甚微。这些结果直接表明，后训练安全对齐是一个脆弱的模块，可以被轻易分离和破坏，进一步支持了对齐脆弱性的核心论点。

papers.title: Emoji Attack: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks Against Judge LLM Detection
papers.short_title: Emoji Attack: Jailbreak Against Judge LLMs
papers.abstract: Jailbreaking techniques trick Large Language Models (LLMs) into producing restricted output, posing a potential threat. One line of defense is to use another LLM as a Judge to evaluate the harmfulness of generated text. However, we reveal that these Judge LLMs are vulnerable to token segmentation bias, an issue that arises when delimiters alter the tokenization process, splitting words into smaller sub-tokens. This alters the embeddings of the entire sequence, reducing detection accuracy and allowing harmful content to be misclassified as safe. In this paper, we introduce Emoji Attack, a novel strategy that amplifies existing jailbreak prompts by exploiting token segmentation bias. Our method leverages in-context learning to systematically insert emojis into text before it is evaluated by a Judge LLM, inducing embedding distortions that significantly lower the likelihood of detecting unsafe content. Unlike traditional delimiters, emojis also introduce semantic ambiguity, making them particularly effective in this attack. Through experiments on state-of-the-art Judge LLMs, we demonstrate that Emoji Attack substantially reduces the unsafe prediction rate, bypassing existing safeguards.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses a vulnerability in Judge LLMs used for detecting harmful content, revealing that token segmentation bias caused by delimiters can reduce detection accuracy. It proposes Emoji Attack, a method that inserts emojis into text via in-context learning to distort embeddings and bypass safety judgments. Experiments on state-of-the-art Judge LLMs show a substantial decrease in the unsafe prediction rate, demonstrating effective bypassing of safeguards. This work exposes a fragility in post-training safety alignment by introducing a novel attack surface that exploits tokenization and embedding distortions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了用于检测有害内容的Judge LLM中存在的一种漏洞，即分隔符引发的令牌分割偏见会降低检测精度。提出Emoji Attack方法，通过上下文学习在文本中插入表情符号，扭曲嵌入表征以规避安全判断。在先进Judge LLM上的实验显示，不安全预测率显著下降，有效绕过了现有防护。该工作通过引入利用令牌化和嵌入扭曲的新攻击面，暴露了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Projection Optimization: A General Framework for Multi-Objective and Multi-Group RLHF
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) is a widely used fine-tuning approach that aligns machine learning model, particularly Language Model (LM) with human preferences. There are typically multiple objectives driving the preference, hence humans find it easier to express per-objective comparisons rather than a global preference between two choices. Multi-Objective RLHF (MORLHF) aims to use per-objective preference feedback and achieve Pareto optimality among these objectives by aggregating them into a single unified objective for optimization. However, nearly all prior works rely on linear aggregation, which rules out policies that favor specific objectives such as the worst one. The only existing approach using non-linear aggregation is computationally expensive due to its reward-based nature and the need for retraining whenever the aggregation parameters change. In this work, we address this limitation by transforming the non-linear aggregation maximization problem into a series of sub-problems. Each sub-problem involves only linear aggregation, making it computationally efficient to solve. We further extend our framework to handle multi-group scenarios, where each group has distinct weights for the objectives. Our method enables achieving consensus or maximizing the aggregated objective across all groups. Theoretically, we demonstrate that our algorithmic framework achieves sublinear regret and can be easily adapted to a reward-free algorithm. Empirically, leveraging our theoretical insights, we propose a nearly training-free algorithm once the optimal policies for individual objectives are obtained.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of multi-objective RLHF where linear aggregation cannot express non-linear preferences such as maximizing the worst objective. It proposes Projection Optimization, a framework that transforms non-linear aggregation into efficient linear sub-problems and extends to multi-group settings. Theoretical analysis shows sublinear regret, and a nearly training-free algorithm is derived from single-objective optimal policies. The work advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了多目标RLHF中线性聚合无法表达非线性偏好（如最大化最差目标）的问题。提出投影优化框架，将非线性聚合转化为一系列高效线性子问题，并扩展到多群体场景。理论上证明次线性遗憾，并从单目标最优策略衍生出近乎免训练的算法。该工作推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: ProSec: Fortifying Code LLMs with Proactive Security Alignment
papers.short_title: ProSec: Proactive Security Alignment for Code LLMs
papers.abstract: While recent code-specific large language models (LLMs) have greatly enhanced their code generation capabilities, the safety of these models remains under-explored, posing potential risks as insecure code generated by these models may introduce vulnerabilities into real-world systems. Existing methods collect security-focused datasets from real-world vulnerabilities for instruction tuning in order to mitigate such issues. However, they are largely constrained by the data sparsity of vulnerable code, and have limited applicability in the multi-stage post-training workflows of modern LLMs. In this paper, we propose ProSec, a novel proactive security alignment approach designed to align code LLMs with secure coding practices. ProSec systematically exposes the vulnerabilities in a code LLM by synthesizing vulnerability-inducing coding scenarios from Common Weakness Enumerations (CWEs) and generates fixes to vulnerable code snippets, allowing the model to learn secure practices through preference learning objectives. The scenarios synthesized by ProSec trigger 25x more vulnerable code than a normal instruction-tuning dataset, resulting in a security-focused alignment dataset 7x larger than the previous work. Experiments show that models trained with ProSec are 25.2% to 35.4% more secure compared to previous work without degrading models' utility.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety risks posed by current code LLMs, which may generate vulnerable code, a problem exacerbated by data sparsity in existing security alignment datasets. It proposes ProSec, a proactive security alignment approach that synthesizes vulnerability-inducing coding scenarios from Common Weakness Enumerations (CWEs) and generates fixes, training the model through preference learning objectives. Evaluated on security benchmarks, ProSec-trained models achieved 25.2% to 35.4% higher security rates compared to prior work, without degradation in code generation utility. This paper advances security alignment methodology for code LLMs but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment; it focuses on building a more effective alignment dataset and training approach.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前代码大语言模型可能生成不安全代码的安全风险，现有安全对齐数据集因漏洞代码稀疏而受限。提出 ProSec，一种主动安全对齐方法，通过从通用弱点枚举（CWE）合成诱导漏洞的编码场景，并生成修复方案，利用偏好学习目标训练模型。在安全基准上评估，ProSec 训练的模型比先前工作安全率提高 25.2% 至 35.4%，且不影响代码生成实用性。本文推进了代码 LLM 的安全对齐方法学，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题；其主要贡献在于构建更有效的对齐数据集和训练流程。

papers.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Fine-grained steering of language model outputs is essential for safety and reliability. Prompting and finetuning are widely used to achieve these goals, but interpretability researchers have proposed a variety of representation-based techniques as well, including sparse autoencoders (SAEs), linear artificial tomography, supervised steering vectors, linear probes, and representation finetuning. At present, there is no benchmark for making direct comparisons between these proposals. Therefore, we introduce AxBench, a large-scale benchmark for steering and concept detection, and report experiments on Gemma-2-2B and 9B. For steering, we find that prompting outperforms all existing methods, followed by finetuning. For concept detection, representation-based methods such as difference-in-means, perform the best. On both evaluations, SAEs are not competitive. We introduce a novel weakly-supervised representational method (Rank-1 Representation Finetuning; ReFT-r1), which is competitive on both tasks while providing the interpretability advantages that prompting lacks. Along with AxBench, we train and publicly release SAE-scale feature dictionaries for ReFT-r1 and DiffMean.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses fine-grained steering and concept detection in LLMs by comparing representation-based methods like sparse autoencoders (SAEs) with simpler approaches. It introduces AxBench, a large-scale benchmark, and proposes Rank-1 Representation Finetuning (ReFT-r1), a weakly-supervised representation-based method. Experiments on Gemma-2 models show that prompting outperforms all steering methods, while difference-in-means excels in concept detection; SAEs are not competitive. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型的细粒度控制与概念检测问题，将稀疏自编码器等表示方法与更简单的基线进行了比较。提出了大规模基准测试AxBench，并引入了一种弱监督表示方法——秩-1表示微调（ReFT-r1）。在Gemma-2模型上的实验表明，提示在控制任务上优于所有其他方法，差值均值在概念检测上表现最佳；稀疏自编码器在这两项评估中均不具竞争力。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: AlphaDPO: Adaptive Reward Margin for Direct Preference Optimization
papers.short_title: AlphaDPO: Adaptive Reward Margin for DPO
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values and intentions is crucial for their utility, honesty, and safety. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a popular approach to achieve this alignment, but it faces challenges in computational efficiency and training stability. Recent methods like Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) have proposed offline alternatives to RLHF, simplifying the process by reparameterizing the reward function. However, DPO depends on a potentially suboptimal reference model, and SimPO's assumption of a fixed target reward margin may lead to suboptimal decisions in diverse data settings. In this work, we propose $\alpha$-DPO, an adaptive preference optimization algorithm designed to address these limitations by introducing a dynamic reward margin. Specifically, $\alpha$-DPO employs an adaptive preference distribution, balancing the policy model and the reference model to achieve personalized reward margins. We provide theoretical guarantees for $\alpha$-DPO, demonstrating its effectiveness as a surrogate optimization objective and its ability to balance alignment and diversity through KL divergence control. Empirical evaluations on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard show that $\alpha$-DPO consistently outperforms DPO and SimPO across various model settings, establishing it as a robust approach for fine-tuning LLMs. Our method achieves significant improvements in win rates, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for LLM alignment. The code is available at https://github.com/junkangwu/alpha-DPO
papers.summary_en: AlphaDPO addresses the limitations of DPO and SimPO in LLM alignment, where DPO's reliance on a potentially suboptimal reference model and SimPO's fixed reward margin lead to suboptimal decisions. It proposes an adaptive preference optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts the reward margin by balancing the policy and reference models through an adaptive preference distribution. Evaluated on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, AlphaDPO consistently outperforms DPO and SimPO with significant win rate improvements across various model settings. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: AlphaDPO 针对 DPO 和 SimPO 在 LLM 对齐中的局限性，DPO 依赖可能次优的参考模型，SimPO 采用固定奖励边际，导致在不同数据场景下决策次优。它提出自适应偏好优化算法，通过平衡策略模型和参考模型并利用自适应偏好分布来动态调整奖励边际。在 AlpacaEval 2 和 Arena-Hard 上评估，AlphaDPO 在多种模型设置下均一致优于 DPO 和 SimPO，胜率显著提高。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Restoring Calibration for Aligned Large Language Models: A Calibration-Aware Fine-Tuning Approach
papers.abstract: One of the key technologies for the success of Large Language Models (LLMs) is preference alignment. However, a notable side effect of preference alignment is poor calibration: while the pre-trained models are typically well-calibrated, LLMs tend to become poorly calibrated after alignment with human preferences. In this paper, we investigate why preference alignment affects calibration and how to address this issue. For the first question, we observe that the preference collapse issue in alignment undesirably generalizes to the calibration scenario, causing LLMs to exhibit overconfidence and poor calibration. To address this, we demonstrate the importance of fine-tuning with domain-specific knowledge to alleviate the overconfidence issue. To further analyze whether this affects the model’s performance, we categorize models into two regimes: calibratable and non-calibratable, defined by bounds of Expected Calibration Error (ECE). In the calibratable regime, we propose a calibration-aware fine-tuning approach to achieve proper calibration without compromising LLMs' performance. However, as models are further fine-tuned for better performance, they enter the non-calibratable regime. For this case, we develop an EM-algorithm-based ECE regularization for the fine-tuning loss to maintain low calibration error. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that preference alignment degrades the calibration of large language models, causing overconfidence. The authors propose calibration-aware fine-tuning methods that leverage domain-specific knowledge to mitigate overconfidence, and introduce an EM-based ECE regularization when models become non-calibratable. Extensive experiments show these approaches reduce calibration error without harming performance. The paper reveals that alignment can compromise calibration reliability, highlighting a fragility in aligned models, but it focuses on calibration restoration rather than adversarial robustness of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决偏好对齐导致大语言模型校准性能下降和过度自信的问题。作者提出校准感知微调方法，利用领域知识缓解过度自信，并在模型进入不可校准状态时引入基于EM算法的ECE正则化。大量实验表明，这些方法在降低校准误差的同时不影响模型性能。论文揭示了对齐过程可能损害校准可靠性，反映出对齐模型的一种脆弱性，但侧重于校准恢复而非对抗性安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Adaptive Localization of Knowledge Negation for Continual LLM Unlearning
papers.abstract: With the growing deployment of large language models (LLMs) across diverse domains, concerns regarding their safety have grown substantially. LLM unlearning has emerged as a pivotal approach to rem...
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the safety risks of LLMs by introducing a continual unlearning approach. It proposes adaptive localization to identify and negate specific knowledge within model parameters, enabling precise removal of harmful content. Evaluations demonstrate effective unlearning with minimal impact on general performance. The work advances unlearning methodology for safety alignment but does not directly explore the fragility of post-training alignment; it focuses on building a targeted forgetting mechanism.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过提出一种持续遗忘方法来解决大语言模型的安全隐患。该方法采用自适应定位技术识别并否定模型中的特定知识，实现有害内容的精准移除。实验评估显示，该方法能有效遗忘且对模型通用性能影响甚微。此工作推进了面向安全对齐的遗忘方法学，但未直接探究训练后对齐的脆弱性问题，而是致力于构建定向遗忘机制。

papers.title: Aligning Spoken Dialogue Models from User Interactions
papers.abstract: We propose a novel preference alignment framework for improving spoken dialogue models on real-time conversations from user interactions. Current preference learning methods primarily focus on text-based language models, and are not directly suited to the complexities of real-time speech interactions, with richer dynamics (e.g. interruption, interjection) and no explicit segmentation between speaker turns.We create a large-scale dataset of more than 150,000 preference pairs from raw multi-turn speech conversations, annotated with AI feedback, to cover preferences over both linguistic content and temporal context variations. We leverage offline alignment methods to finetune a full-duplex autoregressive speech-to-speech model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that feedback on generic conversations can be consistently effective in improving spoken dialogue models to produce more factual, safer and more contextually aligned interactions. We deploy the finetuned model and conduct holistic human evaluations to assess the impact beyond single-turn conversations. Our findings shed light on the importance of a well-calibrated balance among various dynamics, crucial for natural real-time speech dialogue systems.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning real-time spoken dialogue models where continuous speech lacks explicit turn segmentation and involves complex dynamics like interruptions. It proposes a preference alignment framework using a large-scale dataset of over 150,000 AI-annotated preference pairs from raw multi-turn conversations and finetunes a full-duplex speech-to-speech model with offline alignment methods. Experiments show that the aligned model generates more factual, safer, and contextually appropriate responses, validated by holistic human evaluations beyond single-turn interactions. This paper advances alignment methodology for speech dialogue systems but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对实时口语对话模型的对齐难题，这类对话中连续语音缺乏明确的轮次分割，且存在打断等复杂动态。提出了一种偏好对齐框架，利用从原始多轮对话中构建的超过15万对AI标注偏好数据，通过离线对齐方法微调全双工语音生成模型。实验表明，对齐后的模型在事实准确性、安全性和上下文相关性上均有提升，并通过超越单轮对话的整体人类评估得到验证。该工作推进了语音对话系统的对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language model (LLM) agents has raised new concerns regarding their safety and security. In this paper, we propose GuardAgent, the first guardrail agent to protect target agents by dynamically checking whether their actions satisfy given safety guard requests. Specifically, GuardAgent first analyzes the safety guard requests to generate a task plan, and then maps this plan into guardrail code for execution. By performing the code execution, GuardAgent can deterministically follow the safety guard request and safeguard target agents. In both steps, an LLM is utilized as the reasoning component, supplemented by in-context demonstrations retrieved from a memory module storing experiences from previous tasks. In addition, we propose two novel benchmarks: EICU-AC benchmark to assess the access control for healthcare agents and Mind2Web-SC benchmark to evaluate the safety policies for web agents. We show that GuardAgent effectively moderates the violation actions for different types of agents on these two benchmarks with over 98% and 83% guardrail accuracies, respectively. Project page: https://guardagent.github.io/
papers.summary_en: GuardAgent addresses the safety and security of LLM agents by proposing a guardrail agent that dynamically checks whether their actions comply with predefined safety guard requests. It utilizes an LLM as a reasoning component, supplemented by in-context demonstrations from a memory module, to generate and execute guardrail code. Evaluated on two novel benchmarks, EICU-AC for healthcare and Mind2Web-SC for web agents, GuardAgent achieves over 98% and 83% guardrail accuracies, respectively. By enforcing safety policies through external verification, this paper directly addresses the fragility of post-training alignment, showing that alignment can be bypassed and offering a hardening method.
papers.summary_zh: GuardAgent针对LLM智能体的安全性问题，提出了一种护栏智能体，可动态检查其动作是否符合预定义的安全护栏请求。该方法利用LLM作为推理组件，辅以从记忆模块检索的上下文示例，生成并执行护栏代码。在两个新基准EICU-AC（医疗智能体）和Mind2Web-SC（网页智能体）上，GuardAgent分别实现了超过98%和83%的护栏准确率。该工作通过外部验证强化安全策略，揭示了后训练对齐的脆弱性，并提供了一种加固手段。

papers.title: AdvAgent: Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents
papers.abstract: Foundation model-based agents are increasingly used to automate complex tasks, enhancing efficiency and productivity. However, their access to sensitive resources and autonomous decision-making also introduce significant security risks, where successful attacks could lead to severe consequences. To systematically uncover these vulnerabilities, we propose AdvAgent, a black-box red-teaming framework for attacking web agents. Unlike existing approaches, AdvAgent employs a reinforcement learning-based pipeline to train an adversarial prompter model that optimizes adversarial prompts using feedback from the black-box agent. With careful attack design, these prompts effectively exploit agent weaknesses while maintaining stealthiness and controllability. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that AdvAgent achieves high success rates against state-of-the-art GPT-4-based web agents across diverse web tasks. Furthermore, we find that existing prompt-based defenses provide only limited protection, leaving agents vulnerable to our framework. These findings highlight critical vulnerabilities in current web agents and emphasize the urgent need for stronger defense mechanisms. We release code at https://ai-secure.github.io/AdvAgent/.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in web agents powered by foundation models. It proposes AdvAgent, a black-box red-teaming framework that uses reinforcement learning to train an adversarial prompter to generate optimized adversarial prompts against a black-box agent, exploiting weaknesses while maintaining stealthiness and controllability. Evaluations demonstrate high success rates against GPT-4-based web agents across diverse tasks, and find that prompt-based defenses provide limited protection. This work reveals that safety alignment of web agents is fragile, as carefully crafted attacks can easily bypass existing safeguards, underscoring the urgent need for more robust defenses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对基于基础模型的网络代理的安全漏洞问题。提出了AdvAgent框架，这是一种黑盒红队攻击框架，利用强化学习训练对抗性提示器，通过黑盒代理的反馈优化对抗性提示，在保持隐蔽性和可控性的同时有效利用代理弱点。大量评估显示，该框架对基于GPT-4的最先进网络代理在多种网络任务上取得了高成功率，并且现有基于提示的防御仅提供有限保护。这项研究表明，网络代理的安全对齐是脆弱的，精心设计的攻击可以轻易绕过现有防护，凸显了加强防御机制的迫切需要。

papers.title: RLTHF: Targeted Human Feedback for LLM Alignment
papers.short_title: RLTHF: Targeted Human Feedback for LLMs
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to align with user preferences is challenging due to the high cost of quality human annotations in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and the generalizability limitations of AI Feedback. To address these challenges, we propose RLTHF, a human-AI hybrid framework that combines LLM-based initial alignment with selective human annotations to achieve full-human annotation alignment with minimal effort. RLTHF identifies hard-to-annotate samples mislabeled by LLMs using a reward model's reward distribution and iteratively enhances alignment by integrating strategic human corrections while leveraging LLM's correctly labeled samples. Evaluations on HH-RLHF and TL;DR datasets show that RLTHF reaches full-human annotation-level alignment with only 6-7% of the human annotation effort. Furthermore, models trained on RLTHF's curated datasets for downstream tasks outperform those trained on fully human-annotated datasets, underscoring the effectiveness of RLTHF.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost of human annotations in RLHF for LLM alignment and the limited generalizability of AI feedback. It proposes RLTHF, a human-AI hybrid framework that selectively obtains human corrections for samples mislabeled by LLMs, identified via reward distribution, achieving full-human annotation alignment with only 6-7% of the effort. Evaluated on HH-RLHF and TL;DR, models trained on the curated data even outperform those trained on fully human-annotated data. While advancing efficient alignment, the paper does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了RLHF中高质量人类标注成本过高以及AI反馈泛化性有限的问题。提出RLTHF框架，结合LLM初始对齐与选择性人类标注，通过奖励分布识别出LLM错误标记的难标注样本，仅需6-7%的人类标注量就达到全人类标注级别的对齐。在HH-RLHF和TL;DR数据集上，使用RLTHF精选数据训练的下游模型甚至优于全人类标注数据训练的模型。本文提升了对齐方法的效率，但未直接探讨安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Is DPO Superior to PPO for LLM Alignment? A Comprehensive Study
papers.short_title: DPO vs PPO for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is currently the most widely used method to align large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. Existing RLHF methods can be roughly categorized as either reward-based or reward-free. Novel applications such as ChatGPT and Claude leverage reward-based methods that first learn a reward model and apply actor-critic algorithms, such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). However, in academic benchmarks, state-of-the-art results are often achieved via reward-free methods, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Is DPO truly superior to PPO? Why does PPO perform poorly on these benchmarks? In this paper, we first conduct both theoretical and empirical studies on the algorithmic properties of DPO and show that DPO may have fundamental limitations. Moreover, we also comprehensively examine PPO and reveal the key factors for the best performances of PPO in fine-tuning LLMs. Finally, we benchmark DPO and PPO across a collection of RLHF testbeds, ranging from dialogue to code generation. Experiment results demonstrate that PPO is able to surpass other alignment methods in all cases and achieve state-of-the-art results in challenging code competitions. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/openpsi-project/ReaLHF.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates whether DPO is truly superior to PPO for aligning LLMs with human preferences, noting the discrepancy between academic benchmarks favoring DPO and industrial use of PPO. It conducts theoretical and empirical analyses revealing DPO's limitations and identifies key factors behind PPO's strong performance, then benchmarks both methods on dialogue and code generation tasks. Results show that PPO consistently surpasses DPO and other methods, achieving state-of-the-art in code competitions. This paper advances alignment methodology by clarifying the relative merits of DPO and PPO but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文研究了直接偏好优化（DPO）与近端策略优化（PPO）在大型语言模型对齐中的优劣，关注学术基准偏爱DPO而工业应用采用PPO的差异。通过理论和实证分析，揭示DPO的局限，并探究PPO取得最佳性能的关键因素，进而在对话和代码生成任务上基准测试。结果表明，PPO全面超越包括DPO在内的其他方法，并在代码竞赛中达到最优水平。本文主要推进了对齐方法论，厘清了DPO与PPO的相对效能，但未直接讨论训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Fundamental Limitations of Alignment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: An important aspect in developing language models that interact with humans is aligning their behavior to be useful and unharmful for their human users. This is usually achieved by tuning the model in a way that enhances desired behaviors and inhibits undesired ones, a process referred to as alignment. In this paper, we propose a theoretical approach called Behavior Expectation Bounds (BEB) which allows us to formally investigate several inherent characteristics and limitations of alignment in large language models. Importantly, we prove that within the limits of this framework, for any behavior that has a finite probability of being exhibited by the model, there exist prompts that can trigger the model into outputting this behavior, with probability that increases with the length of the prompt. This implies that any alignment process that attenuates an undesired behavior but does not remove it altogether, is not safe against adversarial prompting attacks. Furthermore, our framework hints at the mechanism by which leading alignment approaches such as reinforcement learning from human feedback make the LLM prone to being prompted into the undesired behaviors. This theoretical result is being experimentally demonstrated in large scale by the so called contemporary"chatGPT jailbreaks", where adversarial users trick the LLM into breaking its alignment guardrails by triggering it into acting as a malicious persona. Our results expose fundamental limitations in alignment of LLMs and bring to the forefront the need to devise reliable mechanisms for ensuring AI safety.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inherent vulnerability of aligned LLMs to adversarial prompts that re-activate attenuated but not eliminated undesired behaviors. It proposes a theoretical framework, Behavior Expectation Bounds (BEB), to formally analyze alignment limitations. It proves that for any behavior with non-zero probability, there exist prompts that trigger it with probability increasing with prompt length, empirically supported by chatGPT jailbreaks. This directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as adversarial prompts can bypass it by exploiting residual undesired behaviors, highlighting a fundamental limitation of current alignment approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了对齐后的大语言模型容易受到对抗性提示攻击的内在脆弱性问题，攻击会重新触发被削弱但未消除的有害行为。提出了一个称为行为期望边界（BEB）的理论框架，用于形式化分析对齐的局限性。证明了对于任何具有非零概率的行为，存在能够触发该行为的提示，且概率随提示长度增加而增加，这一结果从经验上得到了ChatGPT越狱攻击的支持。这直接表明训练后的安全对齐是脆弱的，因为对抗性提示可以利用残留的有害行为绕过对齐，揭示了当前对齐方法的基本局限性。

papers.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
papers.abstract: The safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) can be circumvented through adversarially crafted inputs, yet the mechanisms by which these attacks bypass safety barriers remain poorly understood. Prior work suggests that a single refusal direction in the model's activation space determines whether an LLM refuses a request. In this study, we propose a novel gradient-based approach to representation engineering and use it to identify refusal directions. Contrary to prior work, we uncover multiple independent directions and even multi-dimensional concept cones that mediate refusal. Moreover, we show that orthogonality alone does not imply independence under intervention, motivating the notion of representational independence that accounts for both linear and non-linear effects. Using this framework, we identify mechanistically independent refusal directions. We show that refusal mechanisms in LLMs are governed by complex spatial structures and identify functionally independent directions, confirming that multiple distinct mechanisms drive refusal behavior. Our gradient-based approach uncovers these mechanisms and can further serve as a foundation for future work on understanding LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates why adversarial attacks can bypass LLM safety alignment by examining the geometry of refusal in activation space. It proposes a gradient-based representation engineering method and discovers multiple independent refusal directions and even multi-dimensional concept cones, contrary to the prior single-direction hypothesis. The study introduces 'representational independence' to distinguish true mechanistic independence from mere orthogonality, and identifies functionally distinct refusal mechanisms. This work reveals that refusal is governed by complex spatial structures with multiple independent mechanisms, directly demonstrating the fragility of safety alignment by showing that it can be circumvented through diverse, independent pathways.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了对抗攻击为何能绕过LLM安全对齐，通过探索激活空间中拒绝行为的几何结构。提出了基于梯度的表征工程方法，发现了多个独立的拒绝方向甚至多维概念锥，与先前的单一方向假设相悖。引入了“表征独立性”概念，以区分正交性与干预下的真正独立机制，并识别出功能不同的拒绝机制。该工作揭示了拒绝行为由复杂空间结构中的多个独立机制控制，直接证明安全对齐的脆弱性：因其可通过多种独立路径绕过。

papers.title: Cannot See the Forest for the Trees: Invoking Heuristics and Biases to Elicit Irrational Choices of LLMs
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable performance of Large Language Models (LLMs), they remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which can compromise their safety mechanisms. Existing studies often rely on brute-force optimization or manual design, failing to uncover potential risks in real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose a novel jailbreak attack framework, ICRT, inspired by heuristics and biases in human cognition. Leveraging the simplicity effect, we employ cognitive decomposition to reduce the complexity of malicious prompts. Simultaneously, relevance bias is utilized to reorganize prompts, enhancing semantic alignment and inducing harmful outputs effectively. Furthermore, we introduce a ranking-based harmfulness evaluation metric that surpasses the traditional binary success-or-failure paradigm by employing ranking aggregation methods such as Elo, HodgeRank, and Rank Centrality to comprehensively quantify the harmfulness of generated content. Experimental results show that our approach consistently bypasses mainstream LLMs'safety mechanisms and generates high-risk content, providing insights into jailbreak attack risks and contributing to stronger defense strategies.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety mechanisms to jailbreak attacks by exploiting cognitive heuristics and biases. They propose ICRT, a framework that leverages the simplicity effect (cognitive decomposition to simplify malicious prompts) and relevance bias (reorganizing prompts for semantic alignment) to elicit harmful outputs. A ranking-based harmfulness metric (using Elo, HodgeRank, and Rank Centrality) shows that ICRT consistently bypasses mainstream LLMs' safety measures and generates high-risk content. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by introducing a novel attack surface based on cognitive biases, showing that safety mechanisms can be easily bypassed with cognitively crafted prompts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过利用认知启发式和偏见，揭示了大语言模型安全机制在越狱攻击下的脆弱性。提出ICRT框架，借助简单性效应（认知分解降低恶意提示复杂度）和相关性偏见（重组提示增强语义对齐）来诱导有害输出。通过基于排名的危害性评估指标（如Elo、HodgeRank和Rank Centrality），实验表明该方法能够稳定绕过主流大语言模型的安全防护，生成高风险内容。该工作通过引入基于认知偏见的新攻击面，直接证实了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明安全机制可被精心设计的提示轻易绕过。

papers.title: Constrain Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: The alignment of large language models (LLMs) with human preferences remains a key challenge. While post-training techniques like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) have achieved notable success, they often introduce computational inefficiencies and training instability. In this paper, we propose Feature-level constrained Preference Optimization (FPO), a novel method designed to simplify the alignment process while ensuring stability. FPO leverages pre-trained Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and introduces feature-level constraints, allowing for efficient, sparsity-enforced alignment. Our approach enjoys efficiency by using sparse features activated in a well-trained sparse autoencoder and the quality of sequential KL divergence by using the feature-level offline reference. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FPO achieves a 5.08% absolute improvement in win rate with much lower computational cost compared to state-of-the-art baselines, making it a promising solution for efficient and controllable LLM alignments.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models with human preferences efficiently and stably, noting that existing methods like RLHF and DPO have computational and stability issues. It proposes Feature-level constrained Preference Optimization (FPO), which leverages pre-trained Sparse Autoencoders to impose feature-level constraints, enabling sparsity-enforced alignment with a feature-level offline reference. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that FPO achieves a 5.08% absolute improvement in win rate with much lower computational cost compared to state-of-the-art baselines. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question; it focuses on improving efficiency and stability rather than examining the robustness or brittleness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了在大语言模型与人类偏好对齐过程中存在的效率和稳定性问题，指出RLHF和DPO等方法存在计算开销大和训练不稳定等不足。提出了特征级约束偏好优化（FPO）方法，利用预训练的稀疏自编码器施加特征级约束，通过稀疏激活特征和特征级离线参考实现高效且稀疏性增强的对齐。在基准数据集上的实验结果表明，FPO相比最先进的基线方法，在更低的计算成本下取得了5.08%的绝对胜率提升。本文推进了对齐方法的研究，但并未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题；其重点在于提升效率和稳定性，而非检验训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: ConfPO: Exploiting Policy Model Confidence for Critical Token Selection in Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce ConfPO, a method for preference learning in Large Language Models (LLMs) that identifies and optimizes preference-critical tokens based solely on the training policy's confidence, without requiring any auxiliary models or compute. Unlike prior Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs) such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), which uniformly adjust all token probabilities regardless of their relevance to preference, ConfPO focuses optimization on the most impactful tokens. This targeted approach improves alignment quality while mitigating overoptimization (i.e., reward hacking) by using the KL divergence budget more efficiently. In contrast to recent token-level methods that rely on credit-assignment models or AI annotators, raising concerns about scalability and reliability, ConfPO is simple, lightweight, and model-free. Experimental results on challenging alignment benchmarks, including AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, demonstrate that ConfPO consistently outperforms uniform DAAs across various LLMs, delivering better alignment with zero additional computational overhead.
papers.summary_en: ConfPO addresses the inefficiency of uniform token probability adjustment in direct alignment algorithms like DPO, which can lead to overoptimization. It proposes selecting and optimizing only preference-critical tokens based on the training policy's own confidence scores, without auxiliary models. Evaluated on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, ConfPO consistently outperforms uniform methods across various LLMs with zero additional compute. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: ConfPO 解决了直接对齐算法（如 DPO）中统一调整所有 token 概率导致的低效和过度优化问题。它提出仅基于训练策略自身的置信度分数来选择和优化对偏好至关重要的 token，无需辅助模型。在 AlpacaEval 2 和 Arena-Hard 上的评估表明，ConfPO 在不同 LLM 上均一致优于统一方法，且无额外计算开销。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Retrieval-Augmented Generation (VLRAG) systems have been widely applied to Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to enhance their generation ability. However, the reliance on externa...
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in large vision-language models (LVLMs) to knowledge poisoning attacks. It proposes PoisonedEye, an attack that injects crafted adversarial knowledge into the external retrieval database to manipulate the model's outputs. Evaluations show that PoisonedEye effectively controls the generated content across various vision-language tasks, with high success rates. This work reveals a new attack surface that bypasses post-training safety alignment by corrupting the external knowledge, providing direct evidence that alignment is fragile and can be subverted without directly attacking the model weights.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对检索增强生成（RAG）在大型视觉-语言模型（LVLMs）中面临的知识投毒攻击漏洞展开研究。提出了PoisonedEye攻击方法，通过向外部检索数据库注入精心构造的对抗性知识来操纵模型输出。实验表明，PoisonedEye在多种视觉-语言任务中有效控制生成内容，成功率高。该工作揭示了一种新的攻击面，即通过污染外部知识绕过训练后的安全对齐，为对齐的脆弱性提供了直接证据，证明其可在不直接攻击模型权重的情况下被颠覆。

papers.title: R.I.P.: Better Models by Survival of the Fittest Prompts
papers.short_title: RIP: Survival of the Fittest Prompts
papers.abstract: Training data quality is one of the most important drivers of final model quality. In this work, we introduce a method for evaluating data integrity based on the assumption that low-quality input prompts result in high variance and low quality responses.
