This is achieved by measuring the rejected response quality and the reward gap between the chosen and rejected preference pair. Our method, Rejecting Instruction Preferences (RIP) can be used to filter prompts from existing training sets, or to make high quality synthetic datasets, yielding large performance gains across various benchmarks compared to unfiltered data. Using Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct, RIP improves AlpacaEval2 LC Win Rate by 9.4%, Arena-Hard by 8.7%, and WildBench by 9.9%. Using Llama 3.3-70B-Instruct, RIP improves Arena-Hard from 67.5 to 82.9, which is from 18th place to 6th overall in the leaderboard.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of low-quality training prompts leading to high variance and poor response quality in instruction tuning. It proposes Rejecting Instruction Preferences (RIP), a method that filters prompts based on the quality of rejected responses and the reward gap between chosen and rejected preference pairs. Evaluated on Llama 3.1-8B and 3.3-70B, RIP yields significant improvements on AlpacaEval2 LC Win Rate (+9.4%), Arena-Hard (+8.7%), and WildBench (+9.9%). This paper advances alignment methodology through prompt quality filtering but does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了指令微调中低质量训练提示导致高方差和差响应质量的问题。提出拒绝指令偏好（RIP）方法，基于被拒响应的质量和选择与拒绝之间的奖励差距来过滤提示。在Llama 3.1-8B和3.3-70B上评估，RIP显著提升了AlpacaEval2 LC胜率（+9.4%）、Arena-Hard（+8.7%）和WildBench（+9.9%）。本文通过提示质量过滤推进了对齐方法，但并未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.abstract: We posit that to achieve superhuman agents, future models require superhuman feedback in order to provide an adequate training signal. Current approaches commonly train reward models from human preferences, which may then be bottlenecked by human performance level, and secondly these separate frozen reward models cannot then learn to improve during LLM training. In this work, we study Self-Rewarding Language Models, where the language model itself is used via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting to provide its own rewards during training. We show that during Iterative DPO training that not only does instruction following ability improve, but also the ability to provide high-quality rewards to itself. Fine-tuning Llama 2 70B on three iterations of our approach yields a model that outperforms many existing systems on the AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard, including Claude 2, Gemini Pro, and GPT-4 0613. While there is much left still to explore, this work opens the door to the possibility of models that can continually improve in both axes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation that training reward models from human preferences may bottleneck superhuman agent development because human feedback is capped at human-level performance. It proposes Self-Rewarding Language Models, where the LLM provides its own rewards via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting during iterative DPO training, enabling simultaneous improvement of instruction following and reward modeling. Fine-tuning Llama 2 70B over three iterations yields a model that outperforms Claude 2, Gemini Pro, and GPT-4 0613 on AlpacaEval 2.0. While this work advances alignment methodology through self-improvement, it does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is robust or fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前用人类偏好训练奖励模型可能限制超人类智能体发展的瓶颈问题，提出自奖励语言模型方法，即在迭代 DPO 训练中通过 LLM-as-a-Judge 提示让模型自行产生奖励信号，实现指令遵循和奖励建模能力的同步提升。经过三次迭代微调 Llama 2 70B 后，模型在 AlpacaEval 2.0 上超越了 Claude 2、Gemini Pro 和 GPT-4 0613。尽管该工作通过自我改进推进了对齐方法论，但它并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Token-level Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) is essential to align them with human values and intentions. This process often utilizes methods like pairwise comparisons and KL divergence against a reference LLM, focusing on the evaluation of full answers generated by the models. However, the generation of these responses occurs in a token level, following a sequential, auto-regressive fashion. In this paper, we introduce Token-level Direct Preference Optimization (TDPO), a novel approach to align LLMs with human preferences by optimizing policy at the token level. Unlike previous methods, which face challenges in divergence efficiency, TDPO incorporates forward KL divergence constraints for each token, improving alignment and diversity. Utilizing the Bradley-Terry model for a token-based reward system, TDPO enhances the regulation of KL divergence, while preserving simplicity without the need for explicit reward modeling. Experimental results across various text tasks demonstrate TDPO's superior performance in balancing alignment with generation diversity. Notably, fine-tuning with TDPO strikes a better balance than DPO in the controlled sentiment generation and single-turn dialogue datasets, and significantly improves the quality of generated responses compared to both DPO and PPO-based RLHF methods. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/Vance0124/Token-level-Direct-Preference-Optimization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models with human preferences by noting that response generation is token-level and previous methods lack divergence efficiency. It proposes Token-level Direct Preference Optimization (TDPO), which optimizes policy at the token level using forward KL divergence constraints and a Bradley-Terry token-based reward system without explicit reward modeling. Experiments on text tasks show TDPO achieves a better balance between alignment and diversity than DPO and PPO-based RLHF, improving response quality. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training alignment is fragile or can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型与人类偏好对齐问题，指出响应生成是逐令牌级别的，且先前方法存在发散效率不足。提出令牌级直接偏好优化（TDPO），在令牌级别优化策略，引入前向KL散度约束，采用Bradley-Terry模型进行令牌级奖励，无需显式奖励建模。在文本任务上的实验表明，TDPO比DPO和PPO基强化学习方法更好地平衡对齐与多样性，提升了生成质量。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究训练后对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: RigorLLM: Resilient Guardrails for Large Language Models against Undesired Content
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased remarkable capabilities across various tasks in different domains. However, the emergence of biases and the potential for generating harmful content in LLMs, particularly under malicious inputs, pose significant challenges. Current mitigation strategies, while effective, are not resilient under adversarial attacks. This paper introduces Resilient Guardrails for Large Language Models (RigorLLM), a novel framework designed to efficiently and effectively moderate harmful and unsafe inputs and outputs for LLMs. By employing a multi-faceted approach that includes energy-based training data augmentation through Langevin dynamics, optimizing a safe suffix for inputs via minimax optimization, and integrating a fusion-based model combining robust KNN with LLMs based on our data augmentation, RigorLLM offers a robust solution to harmful content moderation. Our experimental evaluations demonstrate that RigorLLM not only outperforms existing baselines like OpenAI API and Perspective API in detecting harmful content but also exhibits unparalleled resilience to jailbreaking attacks. The innovative use of constrained optimization and a fusion-based guardrail approach represents a significant step forward in developing more secure and reliable LLMs, setting a new standard for content moderation frameworks in the face of evolving digital threats.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the fragility of LLM safety under adversarial jailbreaking attacks that elicit harmful content. It proposes RigorLLM, a defense framework using energy-based data augmentation, adversarial suffix optimization, and a fusion-model combining robust KNN with LLMs. Evaluations show RigorLLM outperforms commercial APIs in harmful content detection and demonstrates strong resilience against jailbreaking. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by providing a hardening method that resists adversarial bypasses, contributing evidence that robustness can be improved.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型在对抗性越狱攻击下产生有害内容的脆弱性问题。提出RigorLLM防护框架，通过基于能量的数据增强、对抗性后缀优化以及融合稳健KNN与LLM的混合模型来防御。实验表明，RigorLLM在检测有害内容上优于OpenAI API等基线，并对越狱攻击表现出显著鲁棒性。该研究通过提供抵抗对抗性绕过的硬化方法，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，证明了可增强其鲁棒性。

papers.title: Improving Reward Model Generalization from Adversarial Process Enhanced Preferences
papers.abstract: In sequential decision-making, the reward function serves as the primary supervision signal, guiding agents to acquire the desired behaviors. Traditional reward modeling methods rely heavily on hum...
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the poor generalization of reward models learned from human preferences in sequential decision-making, which can cause misalignment under distribution shifts. It proposes an adversarial preference augmentation process that generates challenging comparisons to enhance robustness. Experiments in control and game environments demonstrate improved generalization to unseen states and tasks over standard methods. This work directly hardens the reward modeling component of alignment pipelines, indicating that adversarial training can mitigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment against out-of-distribution scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 针对序列决策中基于人类偏好的奖励模型泛化能力差的问题，分布漂移可能导致智能体行为不对齐。提出了一种对抗性偏好增强过程，生成具有挑战性的偏好比较以提升奖励模型的鲁棒性。在控制和游戏环境中的实验表明，对抗训练后的奖励模型相比标准方法能更好地泛化到未见状态和任务。此研究直接加固了对齐流程中的奖励建模环节，表明对抗性训练可以缓解后训练安全对齐在分布外场景下的脆弱性。

papers.title: Reward-Augmented Data Enhances Direct Preference Alignment of LLMs
papers.abstract: Preference alignment in Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly improved their ability to adhere to human instructions and intentions. However, existing direct alignment algorithms primarily focus on relative preferences and often overlook the qualitative aspects of responses, despite having access to preference data that includes reward scores from judge models during AI feedback. Striving to maximize the implicit reward gap between the chosen and the slightly inferior rejected responses can cause overfitting and unnecessary unlearning of the high-quality rejected responses. The unawareness of the reward scores also drives the LLM to indiscriminately favor the low-quality chosen responses and fail to generalize to optimal responses that are sparse in data. To overcome these shortcomings, our study introduces reward-conditioned LLM policies that discern and learn from the entire spectrum of response quality within the dataset, helping extrapolate to more optimal regions. We propose an effective yet simple data relabeling method that conditions the preference pairs on quality scores to construct a reward-augmented dataset. The experiments across various benchmarks and diverse models demonstrate that our approach consistently boosts DPO by a considerable margin. Through comprehensive ablation studies, we demonstrate that our method not only maximizes the utility of preference data but also mitigates the issue of unlearning, demonstrating its broad effectiveness beyond mere data expansion. Our code is available at https://github.com/shenao-zhang/reward-augmented-preference.
papers.summary_en: Existing direct alignment algorithms like DPO ignore explicit reward scores, leading to overfitting and poor utilization of rejected responses. This paper proposes reward-conditioned policies and a simple data relabeling method that incorporates reward scores into preference pairs, creating a reward-augmented dataset. Experiments show consistent and significant improvement over DPO across benchmarks and models, with ablation confirming better data utility and reduced unlearning. This work advances alignment methodology by leveraging reward signals but does not directly probe the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 现有的直接偏好对齐算法（如DPO）忽略显式奖励分数，导致过拟合和对被拒回应的利用不足。本文提出奖励条件化策略和简单的数据重标记方法，将奖励分数融入偏好对中，构建奖励增强数据集。在多个基准和模型上的实验表明，该方法始终大幅优于DPO，消融实验证实其提升了数据效用并减轻了遗忘问题。该研究通过利用奖励信号改进了对齐方法，但并未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: AdvI2I: Adversarial Image Attack on Image-to-Image Diffusion Models
papers.short_title: AdvI2I: Adversarial Image Attack on I2I
papers.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have significantly enhanced the quality of image synthesis, yet they have also introduced serious safety concerns, particularly the generation of Not Safe for Work (NSFW) content. Previous research has demonstrated that adversarial prompts can be used to generate NSFW content. However, such adversarial text prompts are often easily detectable by text-based filters, limiting their efficacy. In this paper, we expose a previously overlooked vulnerability: adversarial image attacks targeting Image-to-Image (I2I) diffusion models. We propose AdvI2I, a novel framework that manipulates input images to induce diffusion models to generate NSFW content. By optimizing a generator to craft adversarial images, AdvI2I circumvents existing defense mechanisms, such as Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD), without altering the text prompts. Furthermore, we introduce AdvI2I-Adaptive, an enhanced version that adapts to potential countermeasures and minimizes the resemblance between adversarial images and NSFW concept embeddings, making the attack more resilient against defenses. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that both AdvI2I and AdvI2I-Adaptive can effectively bypass current safeguards, highlighting the urgent need for stronger security measures to address the misuse of I2I diffusion models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of image-to-image diffusion models to adversarial image attacks that generate NSFW content without altering text prompts. It proposes AdvI2I, a framework optimizing a generator to craft adversarial input images, and AdvI2I-Adaptive, which adapts to defenses and reduces resemblance to NSFW concepts. Experiments show both variants bypass existing safeguards like Safe Latent Diffusion, revealing a new attack surface. This work exposes fragility in visual modality safety alignment, directly supporting the view that safety modules are brittle and bypassable.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对图像到图像扩散模型易受对抗性图像攻击而生成NSFW内容的漏洞。提出AdvI2I框架，通过优化生成器制作对抗性输入图像，并推出AdvI2I-Adaptive变体以适应防御措施并减少与NSFW概念的相似性。实验表明两种攻击均能绕过Safe Latent Diffusion等防护，揭示了新的攻击面。该工作表明视觉模态的安全对齐极易通过对抗图像绕过，直接印证了安全模块脆弱且可被攻破的观点。

papers.title: SPRI: Aligning Large Language Models with Context-Situated Principles
papers.short_title: SPRI: Situated Principles for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models to integrate and reflect human values, especially for tasks that demand intricate human oversight, is arduous since it is resource-intensive and time-consuming to depend on human expertise for context-specific guidance. Prior work has utilized predefined sets of rules or principles to steer the behavior of models (Bai et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2023). However, these principles tend to be generic, making it challenging to adapt them to each individual input query or context. In this work, we present Situated-PRInciples (SPRI), a framework requiring minimal or no human effort that is designed to automatically generate guiding principles in real-time for each input query and utilize them to align each response. We evaluate SPRI on three tasks, and show that 1) SPRI can derive principles in a complex domain-specific task that leads to on-par performance as expert-crafted ones; 2) SPRI-generated principles lead to instance-specific rubrics that outperform prior LLM-as-a-judge frameworks; 3) using SPRI to generate synthetic SFT data leads to substantial improvement on truthfulness. We release our code and model generations at https://github.com/honglizhan/SPRI-public.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs with human values for context-specific tasks, where generic principles often fail and human oversight is costly. It proposes SPRI, a framework that automatically generates context-situated guiding principles in real-time for each input query and uses them to align model responses. Evaluated on three tasks, SPRI-derived principles match expert-crafted ones in a complex domain, instance-specific rubrics outperform prior LLM-as-a-judge frameworks, and synthetic SFT data from SPRI significantly improves truthfulness. This work advances alignment methodology by automating principle generation but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐人类价值观时面临的挑战：通用原则难以适应具体上下文，且依赖人工成本高昂。为此，提出SPRI框架，能够为每个输入查询实时自动生成上下文相关的指导原则，并据此调整模型回复。在三个任务上的评估表明，SPRI生成的原则在复杂领域可与专家设计原则性能持平，其实例特定评分标准优于先前LLM-as-a-judge框架，且利用SPRI合成SFT数据显著提升了模型真实性。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Preference learning made easy: Everything should be understood through win rate
papers.abstract: Preference learning, or the task of aligning generative models to preference comparison data, has yet to reach the conceptual maturity of classification, density estimation, etc. To close this gap, this work presents a framework to understand preference learning starting from the sampling distribution of pairwise preference data. First, we prove that the only evaluation of a generative model that respects both preferences and prevalences in the data distribution is a form of win rate, justifying win rate as the focal point to understand preference learning. We then analyze preference learning methods as win rate optimization (WRO) or non-WRO. We present novel instances of WRO beyond existing examples (RLHF, NLHF) and identify two key theoretical benefits of all such methods. We prove that common non-WRO methods like DPO and SFT on preferred samples lack these properties and suggest ways to mitigate such theoretical limitations. We also show that WRO underperforms in practice due optimization difficulties and that optimization success predicts performance better than choices which affect the objective's solution. Our analysis highlights best practices for existing methods and provides recommendations for future research, guided by the principle that one should either align non-WRO methods more closely with WRO or improve the optimization of WRO objectives.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of conceptual maturity in preference learning by presenting a framework grounded in the sampling distribution of pairwise preference data. It proves that win rate is the only evaluation metric respecting both preferences and prevalences, categorizes methods into win rate optimization (WRO) and non-WRO, and identifies theoretical benefits of WRO methods. The paper shows that popular non-WRO methods like DPO lack these properties and suggests mitigations, while also revealing that WRO underperforms in practice due to optimization challenges, with optimization success being more decisive than objective choice. This work provides theoretical foundations for preference learning methodologies but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过从成对偏好数据的采样分布出发，提出了一个理解偏好学习的框架，解决了该领域概念成熟度不足的问题。研究证明胜率是唯一同时尊重偏好和数据分布中流行度的评估指标，将方法分为胜率优化（WRO）和非WRO两类，并识别出WRO方法的理论优势。论文指出常见非WRO方法（如DPO）缺乏这些性质并提出缓解措施，同时揭示WRO因优化困难而在实践中表现不佳，且优化成功比目标选择更能预测性能。这项工作为偏好学习方法提供了理论基础，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: PARDEN, Can You Repeat That? Defending against Jailbreaks via Repetition
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown success in many natural language processing tasks. Despite rigorous safety alignment processes, supposedly safety-aligned LLMs like Llama 2 and Claude 2 are still susceptible to jailbreaks, leading to security risks and abuse of the models. One option to mitigate such risks is to augment the LLM with a dedicated"safeguard", which checks the LLM's inputs or outputs for undesired behaviour. A promising approach is to use the LLM itself as the safeguard. Nonetheless, baseline methods, such as prompting the LLM to self-classify toxic content, demonstrate limited efficacy. We hypothesise that this is due to domain shift: the alignment training imparts a self-censoring behaviour to the model ("Sorry I can't do that"), while the self-classify approach shifts it to a classification format ("Is this prompt malicious"). In this work, we propose PARDEN, which avoids this domain shift by simply asking the model to repeat its own outputs. PARDEN neither requires finetuning nor white box access to the model. We empirically verify the effectiveness of our method and show that PARDEN significantly outperforms existing jailbreak detection baselines for Llama-2 and Claude-2. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Ed-Zh/PARDEN. We find that PARDEN is particularly powerful in the relevant regime of high True Positive Rate (TPR) and low False Positive Rate (FPR). For instance, for Llama2-7B, at TPR equal to 90%, PARDEN accomplishes a roughly 11x reduction in the FPR from 24.8% to 2.0% on the harmful behaviours dataset.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs to jailbreak attacks. It proposes PARDEN, a safeguard method that detects jailbreaks by asking the model to simply repeat its own outputs, avoiding the domain shift issue of self-classification approaches. Evaluated on Llama-2 and Claude-2, PARDEN significantly outperforms baselines, achieving an 11× reduction in false positive rate at 90% true positive rate on harmful behaviors. This work directly demonstrates that post-training alignment can be hardened using the model’s own capabilities, mitigating fragility without additional training or white-box access.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型易受越狱攻击的问题，提出了一种名为PARDEN的防护方法。该方法通过让模型重复自身输出，避免了自分类方法中的领域偏移问题，从而有效检测越狱行为。在Llama-2和Claude-2上的实验表明，PARDEN显著优于现有基线，在90%真阳性率下将假阳性率从24.8%降至2.0%。该研究展示了无需微调或白盒访问即可增强对齐稳健性的途径，直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Improving LLM Safety Alignment with Dual-Objective Optimization
papers.abstract: Existing training-time safety alignment techniques for large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Direct preference optimization (DPO), a widely deployed alignment method, exhibits limitations in both experimental and theoretical contexts as its loss function proves suboptimal for refusal learning. Through gradient-based analysis, we identify these shortcomings and propose an improved safety alignment that disentangles DPO objectives into two components: (1) robust refusal training, which encourages refusal even when partial unsafe generations are produced, and (2) targeted unlearning of harmful knowledge. This approach significantly increases LLM robustness against a wide range of jailbreak attacks, including prefilling, suffix, and multi-turn attacks across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios. Furthermore, we introduce a method to emphasize critical refusal tokens by incorporating a reward-based token-level weighting mechanism for refusal learning, which further improves the robustness against adversarial exploits. Our research also suggests that robustness to jailbreak attacks is correlated with token distribution shifts in the training process and internal representations of refusal and harmful tokens, offering valuable directions for future research in LLM safety alignment. The code is available at https://github.com/wicai24/DOOR-Alignment
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of existing LLM safety alignment methods (particularly DPO) to jailbreak attacks, identifying suboptimal refusal learning in DPO's loss function. It proposes a dual-objective optimization approach that disentangles DPO into robust refusal training and targeted unlearning of harmful knowledge, supplemented by a reward-based token-level weighting mechanism to emphasize critical refusal tokens. Evaluations against diverse jailbreak attacks (prefilling, suffix, multi-turn) in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show significant robustness improvements, with analysis linking robustness to token distribution shifts and internal representations. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating that alignment can be substantially hardened through improved training objectives, suggesting that safety is not inherently fragile but can be reinforced against adversarial bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有大语言模型安全对齐方法（尤其是DPO）在越狱攻击下的脆弱性，指出了DPO损失函数在拒绝学习方面的不足。提出了一个双目标优化方法，将DPO分解为鲁棒拒绝训练和有害知识的有针对性遗忘，并辅以基于奖励的令牌级加权机制来强调关键拒绝令牌。在分布内和分布外场景下，对多种越狱攻击（预填充、后缀、多轮）的评估表明，该方法显著提升了鲁棒性，同时分析了鲁棒性与令牌分布变化及内部表征的关联。这项工作直接回应了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，通过改进训练目标证明对齐可以被显著强化，表明安全性并非本质脆弱，而是可以通过优化增强以抵御对抗性绕过。

papers.title: Learning and Forgetting Unsafe Examples in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As the number of large language models (LLMs) released to the public grows, there is a pressing need to understand the safety implications associated with these models learning from third-party custom finetuning data. We explore the behavior of LLMs finetuned on noisy custom data containing unsafe content, represented by datasets that contain biases, toxicity, and harmfulness, finding that while aligned LLMs can readily learn this unsafe content, they also tend to forget it more significantly than other examples when subsequently finetuned on safer content. Drawing inspiration from the discrepancies in forgetting, we introduce the"ForgetFilter"algorithm, which filters unsafe data based on how strong the model's forgetting signal is for that data. We demonstrate that the ForgetFilter algorithm ensures safety in customized finetuning without compromising downstream task performance, unlike sequential safety finetuning. ForgetFilter outperforms alternative strategies like replay and moral self-correction in curbing LLMs' ability to assimilate unsafe content during custom finetuning, e.g. 75% lower than not applying any safety measures and 62% lower than using self-correction in toxicity score.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how aligned LLMs acquire and subsequently forget unsafe content (biases, toxicity, harmfulness) when fine-tuned on noisy custom data. It proposes ForgetFilter, which uses the model's stronger forgetting signal for unsafe examples to filter such data during fine-tuning. Evaluated on toxicity benchmarks, ForgetFilter reduces toxicity by 75% compared to no safety measures and by 62% compared to moral self-correction, while preserving downstream task performance. The findings highlight the fragility of post-training safety alignment to unsafe fine-tuning, yet also show that the forgetting dynamic can be exploited to harden safety, directly addressing the robustness of alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了在对齐后的大型语言模型在噪声定制微调数据中学习并遗忘不安全内容（偏见、毒性、危害性）的行为。作者提出 ForgetFilter 算法，利用模型对不安全样例更强的遗忘信号来过滤此类数据。在毒性基准上评估显示，ForgetFilter 相比无安全措施降低毒性 75%，相比道德自我修正降低 62%，同时不损害下游任务性能。该成果揭示了后训练安全对齐面对不安全微调时的脆弱性，但也表明遗忘动态可被用于强化安全，直接回应了对齐鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: STAIR: Improving Safety Alignment with Introspective Reasoning
papers.abstract: Ensuring the safety and harmlessness of Large Language Models (LLMs) has become equally critical as their performance in applications. However, existing safety alignment methods typically suffer from safety-performance trade-offs and the susceptibility to jailbreak attacks, primarily due to their reliance on direct refusals for malicious queries. In this paper, we propose STAIR, a novel framework that integrates SafeTy Alignment with Itrospective Reasoning. We enable LLMs to identify safety risks through step-by-step analysis by self-improving chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning with safety awareness. STAIR first equips the model with a structured reasoning capability and then advances safety alignment via iterative preference optimization on step-level reasoning data generated using our newly proposed Safety-Informed Monte Carlo Tree Search (SI-MCTS). We further train a process reward model on this data to guide test-time searches for improved responses. Extensive experiments show that STAIR effectively mitigates harmful outputs while better preserving helpfulness, compared to instinctive alignment strategies. With test-time scaling, STAIR achieves a safety performance comparable to Claude-3.5 against popular jailbreak attacks. Relevant resources in this work are available at https://github.com/thu-ml/STAIR.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the safety-performance trade-off and vulnerability to jailbreak attacks in existing safety alignment methods for LLMs, which often rely on direct refusals. It proposes STAIR, a framework that enhances safety alignment by enabling LLMs to perform introspective step-by-step safety reasoning via chain-of-thought, trained using iterative preference optimization on data from Safety-Informed MCTS. Extensive experiments show that STAIR effectively reduces harmful outputs while maintaining helpfulness, and with test-time scaling, achieves safety comparable to Claude-3.5 against popular jailbreaks. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment; instead, it offers a reasoning-based approach to strengthen it.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有LLM安全对齐方法中常见的安全-性能权衡及易受越狱攻击的问题，这些方法通常依赖直接拒绝。提出了STAIR框架，通过让LLM进行内省式逐步安全推理，利用基于安全信息蒙特卡洛树搜索（SI-MCTS）生成的步骤级推理数据，进行迭代偏好优化训练，从而增强安全对齐。大量实验表明，STAIR能够有效减少有害输出，同时保持有用性，且通过测试时扩展，其安全性在面对流行越狱攻击时可与Claude-3.5相媲美。本文推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，而是提供了一种基于推理的强化方法。

papers.title: Beyond Bradley-Terry Models: A General Preference Model for Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: Modeling human preferences is crucial for aligning foundation models with human values. Traditional reward modeling methods, such as the Bradley-Terry (BT) reward model, fall short in expressiveness, particularly in addressing intransitive preferences. In this paper, we introduce preference embedding, an approach that embeds responses into a latent space to capture intricate preference structures efficiently, achieving linear query complexity. Additionally, we propose preference score-based General Preference Optimization (GPO), which generalizes reward-based reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). Experimental results show that our General Preference embedding Model (GPM) consistently outperforms the BT reward model on the RewardBench benchmark and effectively models cyclic preferences where any BT reward model behaves like a random guess. Furthermore, evaluations on downstream tasks such as AlpacaEval2.0, following the language model post-training with GPO and our general preference model, reveal performance improvements over BT models. These findings indicate that our method may enhance the alignment of foundation models with nuanced human values. The code is available at https://github.com/general-preference/general-preference-model.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of Bradley-Terry reward models in capturing intransitive or cyclic human preferences. It proposes the General Preference embedding Model (GPM) that maps responses into a latent space to capture intricate preference structures, paired with General Preference Optimization (GPO) for training. Experiments show GPM outperforms BT models on RewardBench, effectively models cyclic preferences, and improves downstream performance on AlpacaEval2.0 after post-training with GPO. This work advances alignment methodology by providing more expressive preference modeling, but it does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了Bradley-Terry奖励模型在捕捉非传递性人类偏好方面的局限性。提出了通用偏好嵌入模型（GPM），将响应映射到潜在空间以捕获复杂的偏好结构，并结合通用偏好优化（GPO）进行训练。实验结果表明，GPM在RewardBench上优于BT模型，能有效建模循环偏好，并在使用GPO进行语言模型后训练后，提高了AlpacaEval2.0的下游性能。这项工作通过提供更具表现力的偏好建模推进了对齐方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Probabilistic Inference in Language Models via Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Numerous capability and safety techniques of Large Language Models (LLMs), including RLHF, automated red-teaming, prompt engineering, and infilling, can be cast as sampling from an unnormalized target distribution defined by a given reward or potential function over the full sequence. In this work, we leverage the rich toolkit of Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) for these probabilistic inference problems. In particular, we use learned twist functions to estimate the expected future value of the potential at each timestep, which enables us to focus inference-time computation on promising partial sequences. We propose a novel contrastive method for learning the twist functions, and establish connections with the rich literature of soft reinforcement learning. As a complementary application of our twisted SMC framework, we present methods for evaluating the accuracy of language model inference techniques using novel bidirectional SMC bounds on the log partition function. These bounds can be used to estimate the KL divergence between the inference and target distributions in both directions. We apply our inference evaluation techniques to show that twisted SMC is effective for sampling undesirable outputs from a pretrained model (a useful component of harmlessness training and automated red-teaming), generating reviews with varied sentiment, and performing infilling tasks.
papers.summary_en: It addresses probabilistic inference tasks in LLMs, where many safety and capability techniques can be framed as sampling from a reward-defined target distribution. The paper proposes twisted Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) with learned twist functions to estimate future potential, enabling efficient focus on promising partial sequences, and introduces contrastive learning for twist functions along with bidirectional SMC bounds for evaluating inference accuracy. Experiments show twisted SMC effectively samples undesirable outputs for red-teaming, controls sentiment in reviews, and performs infilling. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型中的概率推理问题，许多安全和能力技术（如RLHF、红队测试）可被形式化为从奖励定义的目标分布中采样。提出扭曲序列蒙特卡洛（SMC）方法，通过学习扭曲函数估计未来期望值，从而高效聚焦于有前景的部分序列；同时引入对比学习训练扭曲函数，并提出双向SMC边界评估推理精度。实验表明，扭曲SMC能有效采样不良输出（用于无害性训练和红队测试）、生成情感可控的评论以及完成填充任务。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Trustworthiness is an essential prerequisite for the real-world application of large language models. In this paper, we focus on the trustworthiness of language models with respect to retrieval augmentation. Despite being supported with external evidence, retrieval-augmented generation still suffers from hallucinations, one primary cause of which is the conflict between contextual and parametric knowledge. We deem that retrieval-augmented language models have the inherent capabilities of supplying response according to both contextual and parametric knowledge. Inspired by aligning language models with human preference, we take the first step towards aligning retrieval-augmented language models to a status where it responds relying merely on the external evidence and disregards the interference of parametric knowledge. Specifically, we propose a reinforcement learning based algorithm Trustworthy-Alignment, theoretically and experimentally demonstrating large language models' capability of reaching a trustworthy status without explicit supervision on how to respond. Our work highlights the potential of large language models on exploring its intrinsic abilities by its own and expands the application scenarios of alignment from fulfilling human preference to creating trustworthy agents.
papers.summary_en: The paper tackles hallucinations in retrieval-augmented language models caused by conflicts between contextual and parametric knowledge, which harms trustworthiness. It proposes Trustworthy-Alignment, a reinforcement learning method that aligns models to respond based solely on external evidence without explicit supervision. Theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that large language models can achieve a trustworthy state autonomously. While this work contributes to alignment techniques, it does not directly assess the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本论文解决了检索增强语言模型中因上下文知识与参数知识冲突导致的幻觉问题，这损害了模型的可信度。它提出了Trustworthy-Alignment，一种基于强化学习的方法，使模型仅依赖外部证据做出响应，无需显式监督。理论与实验表明，大型语言模型能够自主达到可信状态。尽管该工作推进了对齐方法，但它并未直接评估训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: On Prompt-Driven Safeguarding for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Prepending model inputs with safety prompts is a common practice for safeguarding large language models (LLMs) against queries with harmful intents. However, the underlying working mechanisms of safety prompts have not been unraveled yet, restricting the possibility of automatically optimizing them to improve LLM safety. In this work, we investigate how LLMs' behavior (i.e., complying with or refusing user queries) is affected by safety prompts from the perspective of model representation. We find that in the representation space, the input queries are typically moved by safety prompts in a"higher-refusal"direction, in which models become more prone to refusing to provide assistance, even when the queries are harmless. On the other hand, LLMs are naturally capable of distinguishing harmful and harmless queries without safety prompts. Inspired by these findings, we propose a method for safety prompt optimization, namely DRO (Directed Representation Optimization). Treating a safety prompt as continuous, trainable embeddings, DRO learns to move the queries' representations along or opposite the refusal direction, depending on their harmfulness. Experiments with eight LLMs on out-of-domain and jailbreak benchmarks demonstrate that DRO remarkably improves the safeguarding performance of human-crafted safety prompts, without compromising the models' general performance.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limited understanding of how safety prompts influence LLM refusal behavior, hindering automatic optimization. It investigates the representation-level effect of safety prompts and finds they shift queries in a "higher-refusal" direction, causing over-refusal even on harmless inputs. The authors propose DRO (Directed Representation Optimization), which treats safety prompts as trainable embeddings and learns to move representations along or opposite the refusal direction based on harmfulness. Experiments on eight LLMs show DRO significantly improves safeguarding against harmful queries without degrading general performance, demonstrating a method to harden safety prompts and highlighting the fragility of current prompt-based defenses in their tendency to over-refuse.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全提示对LLM拒绝行为影响机制不明从而限制自动优化这一问题，从表征层面探究了安全提示的作用原理。研究发现安全提示会将输入查询在表征空间中推向“更高拒绝”方向，导致模型对无害查询也倾向于拒绝。为此，作者提出DRO（Directed Representation Optimization）方法，将安全提示视为可训练嵌入，根据查询有害性沿着或逆向拒绝方向移动表征。在8个LLM上的分布外和越狱基准测试表明，DRO显著提升了安全防护性能且不影响通用能力，这一方面提供了加固安全提示的方法，另一方面也揭示了现有基于提示的防御因过度拒绝而表现出脆弱性。

papers.title: Model Immunization from a Condition Number Perspective
papers.abstract: Model immunization aims to pre-train models that are difficult to fine-tune on harmful tasks while retaining their utility on other non-harmful tasks. Though prior work has shown empirical evidence for immunizing text-to-image models, the key understanding of when immunization is possible and a precise definition of an immunized model remain unclear. In this work, we propose a framework, based on the condition number of a Hessian matrix, to analyze model immunization for linear models. Building on this framework, we design an algorithm with regularization terms to control the resulting condition numbers after pre-training. Empirical results on linear models and non-linear deep-nets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on model immunization. The code is available at https://github.com/amberyzheng/model-immunization-cond-num.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses model immunization, which aims to pre-train models that resist fine-tuning on harmful tasks while preserving utility. It proposes a framework based on the condition number of the Hessian matrix to analyze when immunization is possible for linear models, and designs a regularized pre-training algorithm to control condition numbers. Experiments on linear models and non-linear deep networks demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness. This work provides a hardening method that directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment by making models inherently robust to fine-tuning attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决模型免疫问题，即预训练出能够抵抗有害任务微调同时保持效用的模型。提出了基于 Hessian 矩阵条件数的分析框架，用于研究线性模型免疫的可能性，并设计了一种带正则化的预训练算法来控制条件数。在线性模型和非线性深度网络上的实验证明了算法的有效性。本文提出了一种硬化方法，通过使模型对微调攻击具有固有鲁棒性，直接应对了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks - resulting in harmful, unethical, or biased text generations. However, existing jailbreaking methods are computationally costly. In this paper, we propose the weak-to-strong jailbreaking attack, an efficient inference time attack for aligned LLMs to produce harmful text. Our key intuition is based on the observation that jailbroken and aligned models only differ in their initial decoding distributions. The weak-to-strong attack's key technical insight is using two smaller models (a safe and an unsafe one) to adversarially modify a significantly larger safe model's decoding probabilities. We evaluate the weak-to-strong attack on 5 diverse open-source LLMs from 3 organizations. The results show our method can increase the misalignment rate to over 99% on two datasets with just one forward pass per example. Our study exposes an urgent safety issue that needs to be addressed when aligning LLMs. As an initial attempt, we propose a defense strategy to protect against such attacks, but creating more advanced defenses remains challenging. The code for replicating the method is available at https://github.com/XuandongZhao/weak-to-strong
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of efficient jailbreaking of aligned LLMs, noting that existing attacks are computationally expensive. It proposes the weak-to-strong attack, an inference-time method that leverages a safe and an unsafe smaller model to adversarially perturb the decoding distribution of a much larger aligned model. Experiments on five open-source LLMs show the attack achieves over 99% misalignment rate on two datasets using only a single forward pass per example. This paper provides strong evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be easily bypassed by manipulating decoding probabilities with smaller models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐大语言模型易受越狱攻击产生有害输出且现有方法计算成本高的问题，提出弱到强越狱攻击。该攻击在推理时利用安全和不安全两个较小模型对抗性修改较大对齐模型的解码概率。在三个组织的五个开源模型上，仅需一次前向传播即可在两个数据集上将失对齐率提升至99%以上。该研究有力表明后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可被轻易绕过，亟需更强大的防御策略。

papers.title: HPS: Hard Preference Sampling for Human Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Model (LLM) responses with human preferences is vital for building safe and controllable AI systems. While preference optimization methods based on Plackett-Luce (PL) and Bradley-Terry (BT) models have shown promise, they face challenges such as poor handling of harmful content, inefficient use of dispreferred responses, and, specifically for PL, high computational costs. To address these issues, we propose Hard Preference Sampling (HPS), a novel framework for robust and efficient human preference alignment. HPS introduces a training loss that prioritizes the most preferred response while rejecting all dispreferred and harmful ones. It emphasizes"hard"dispreferred responses -- those closely resembling preferred ones -- to enhance the model's rejection capabilities. By leveraging a single-sample Monte Carlo sampling strategy, HPS reduces computational overhead while maintaining alignment quality. Theoretically, HPS improves sample efficiency over existing PL methods and maximizes the reward margin between preferred and dispreferred responses, ensuring clearer distinctions. Experiments on HH-RLHF and PKU-Safety datasets validate HPS's effectiveness, achieving comparable BLEU and reward scores while greatly improving reward margins and thus reducing harmful content generation.
papers.summary_en: Existing preference optimization methods like Plackett-Luce and Bradley-Terry struggle with harmful content rejection, inefficient use of dispreferred responses, and high computational cost. This paper proposes Hard Preference Sampling (HPS), which introduces a loss that prioritizes the best response while penalizing all dispreferred and harmful ones, with emphasis on hard negative examples. Evaluated on HH-RLHF and PKU-Safety, HPS achieves comparable BLEU/reward but significantly improves reward margins and reduces harmful outputs. By hardening rejection of near-preferred harmful responses, HPS contributes to more robust alignment, though it does not directly test the fragility of the alignment module.
papers.summary_zh: 现有基于Plackett-Luce和Bradley-Terry的偏好优化方法难以有效处理有害内容、利用非偏好响应且计算成本高。本文提出硬偏好采样(HPS)框架，通过训练损失优先选择最优响应并惩罚所有非偏好和有害响应，特别关注难负样本，并利用单样本蒙特卡洛采样降低开销。在HH-RLHF和PKU-Safety数据集上，HPS在保持BLEU和奖励分数可比的同时，大幅提升奖励边际并减少有害内容。该方法通过强化对相似非偏好有害响应的拒绝增强了对齐鲁棒性，但未直接研究对齐模块的脆弱性。

papers.title: When Can Proxies Improve the Sample Complexity of Preference Learning?
papers.abstract: We address the problem of reward hacking, where maximising a proxy reward does not necessarily increase the true reward. This is a key concern for Large Language Models (LLMs), as they are often fine-tuned on human preferences that may not accurately reflect a true objective. Existing work uses various tricks such as regularisation, tweaks to the reward model, and reward hacking detectors, to limit the influence that such proxy preferences have on a model. Luckily, in many contexts such as medicine, education, and law, a sparse amount of expert data is often available. In these cases, it is often unclear whether the addition of proxy data can improve policy learning. We outline a set of sufficient conditions on proxy feedback that, if satisfied, indicate that proxy data can provably improve the sample complexity of learning the ground truth policy. These conditions can inform the data collection process for specific tasks. The result implies a parameterisation for LLMs that achieves this improved sample complexity. We detail how one can adapt existing architectures to yield this improved sample complexity.
papers.summary_en: Addresses reward hacking in LLMs where proxy rewards misalign with true objectives. Derives sufficient conditions under which proxy data provably improves sample complexity of learning the true policy, and suggests an LLM parameterization to realize this benefit. The theoretical results show that, when conditions are met, proxy data reduces the amount of expert data needed. This paper advances alignment methodology by providing a principled way to incorporate proxies, but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 解决大型语言模型中代理奖励与真实目标不一致的奖励黑客问题。推导出一组充分条件，在这些条件下，代理数据可证明地提升学习真实策略的样本复杂度，并提出一种LLM参数化方法来实现该好处。理论结果表明，当条件满足时，代理数据能减少所需的专家数据量。本文通过提供原则性方法引入代理数据来推进对齐方法，但未直接检视训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Safety Fine-Tuning at (Almost) No Cost: A Baseline for Vision Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Current vision large language models (VLLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities yet are prone to generate harmful content and are vulnerable to even the simplest jailbreaking attacks. Our initial analysis finds that this is due to the presence of harmful data during vision-language instruction fine-tuning, and that VLLM fine-tuning can cause forgetting of safety alignment previously learned by the underpinning LLM. To address this issue, we first curate a vision-language safe instruction-following dataset VLGuard covering various harmful categories. Our experiments demonstrate that integrating this dataset into standard vision-language fine-tuning or utilizing it for post-hoc fine-tuning effectively safety aligns VLLMs. This alignment is achieved with minimal impact on, or even enhancement of, the models' helpfulness. The versatility of our safety fine-tuning dataset makes it a valuable resource for safety-testing existing VLLMs, training new models or safeguarding pre-trained VLLMs. Empirical results demonstrate that fine-tuned VLLMs effectively reject unsafe instructions and substantially reduce the success rates of several black-box adversarial attacks, which approach zero in many cases. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/ys-zong/VLGuard.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that vision large language models (VLLMs) forget safety alignment during vision-language fine-tuning due to harmful data, making them vulnerable to attacks. It proposes VLGuard, a curated vision-language safe instruction-following dataset covering various harmful categories, and integrates it into fine-tuning for safety alignment. Experiments show that this safety fine-tuning effectively rejects harmful instructions and reduces black-box attack success rates to near zero, with minimal impact on helpfulness. This work highlights the fragility of post-training safety alignment in VLLMs during additional fine-tuning, but demonstrates that it can be robustly restored and strengthened with targeted safety data.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视觉大语言模型（VLLMs）在视觉语言指令微调过程中，由于有害数据存在导致原有安全对齐被遗忘、易受攻击的问题，提出了VLGuard数据集，涵盖多种有害类别，将其整合到标准微调或事后微调中进行安全对齐。实验表明，该安全微调有效拒绝了有害指令，将黑盒对抗攻击成功率降至接近零，且对模型有用性影响极小甚至有所提升。本研究揭示了VLLMs在后续微调中安全对齐的脆弱性，同时证明可通过针对性安全数据集稳健地重建和加固。

papers.title: TGDPO: Harnessing Token-Level Reward Guidance for Enhancing Direct Preference Optimization
papers.short_title: TGDPO: Token-Level Reward Guidance for DPO
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in reinforcement learning from human feedback have shown that utilizing fine-grained token-level reward models can substantially enhance the performance of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in aligning large language models. However, it is challenging to leverage such token-level reward as guidance for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), since DPO is formulated as a sequence-level bandit problem. To address this challenge, this work decomposes the sequence-level PPO into a sequence of token-level proximal policy optimization problems and then frames the problem of token-level PPO with token-level reward guidance, from which closed-form optimal token-level policy and the corresponding token-level reward can be derived. Using the obtained reward and Bradley-Terry model, this work establishes a framework of computable loss functions with token-level reward guidance for DPO, and proposes a practical reward guidance based on the induced DPO reward. This formulation enables different tokens to exhibit varying degrees of deviation from reference policy based on their respective rewards. Experiment results demonstrate that our method achieves substantial performance improvements over DPO, with win rate gains of up to 7.5 points on MT-Bench, 6.2 points on AlpacaEval 2, and 4.3 points on Arena-Hard. Code is available at https://github.com/dvlab-research/TGDPO.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of leveraging fine-grained token-level rewards, which benefit PPO, within the sequence-level DPO framework. It proposes TGDPO, which decomposes PPO into token-level problems, derives a closed-form token-level policy and reward, and constructs a token-guided DPO loss allowing token-wise deviations from the reference policy. Evaluated on MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2, and Arena-Hard, TGDPO yields win rate improvements up to 7.5, 6.2, and 4.3 points over standard DPO, respectively. This work enhances alignment methods but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解決了在序列級DPO框架中利用細粒度令牌級獎勵（對PPO有益）的挑戰。提出TGDPO方法，將PPO分解為令牌級問題，推導出閉式令牌級策略與獎勵，並構建令牌引導的DPO損失，允許令牌根據獎勵呈現不同程度偏離參考策略。在MT-Bench、AlpacaEval 2和Arena-Hard上的實驗顯示，TGDPO相比DPO分別提升最高7.5、6.2和4.3個勝率點。此研究改進了對齊方法，但未直接探討後訓練安全對齊的脆弱性。

papers.title: Principled Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback from Pairwise or K-wise Comparisons
papers.abstract: We provide a theoretical framework for Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). Our analysis shows that when the true reward function is linear, the widely used maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) converges under both the Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) model and the Plackett-Luce (PL) model. However, we show that when training a policy based on the learned reward model, MLE fails while a pessimistic MLE provides policies with improved performance under certain coverage assumptions. Additionally, we demonstrate that under the PL model, the true MLE and an alternative MLE that splits the $K$-wise comparison into pairwise comparisons both converge. Moreover, the true MLE is asymptotically more efficient. Our results validate the empirical success of existing RLHF algorithms in InstructGPT and provide new insights for algorithm design. Furthermore, our results unify the problem of RLHF and max-entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL), and provide the first sample complexity bound for max-entropy IRL.
papers.summary_en: This paper provides a theoretical framework for RLHF, analyzing reward estimation from pairwise or K-wise human comparisons under linear reward models and BTL/PL models. It shows that while MLE converges for reward estimation, naive policy optimization on the learned reward can fail, but a pessimistic MLE improves policy performance under coverage conditions. Under the PL model, full MLE is asymptotically more efficient than splitting K-wise comparisons into pairwise ones; the framework also unifies RLHF with max-entropy IRL and gives the first sample complexity bound for the latter. The paper advances the theoretical foundations of alignment but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文为RLHF提供了理论框架，分析了在线性奖励模型和BTL/PL模型下从成对或K-wise人类比较中估计奖励的方法。研究表明，MLE在奖励估计中收敛，但基于朴素MLE的策略优化可能失败，而悲观MLE在覆盖条件下能改善策略性能。在PL模型下，完整MLE比将K-wise比较拆分为成对比较渐近更高效；该框架还将RLHF与最大熵逆强化学习统一，并给出了后者的首个样本复杂度界限。论文推进了对齐方法的理论基础，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Iterative Data Smoothing: Mitigating Reward Overfitting and Overoptimization in RLHF
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is a pivotal technique that aligns language models closely with human-centric values. The initial phase of RLHF involves learning human values using a reward model from ranking data. It is observed that the performance of the reward model degrades after one epoch of training, and optimizing too much against the learned reward model eventually hinders the true objective. This paper delves into these issues, leveraging the theoretical insights to design improved reward learning algorithm termed 'Iterative Data Smoothing' (IDS). The core idea is that during each training epoch, we not only update the model with the data, but also update the date using the model, replacing hard labels with soft labels. Our empirical findings highlight the superior performance of this approach over the traditional methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of reward overfitting and overoptimization in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), where the reward model degrades after one training epoch and excessive optimization against it harms the true objective. The authors propose Iterative Data Smoothing (IDS), which during each training epoch updates both the model and the training data by replacing hard labels with soft labels generated by the model. Experiments show that IDS outperforms traditional reward learning methods. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了RLHF中奖励过拟合和过度优化的问题，即奖励模型在一个训练周期后性能下降，且对其过度优化会损害真实目标。提出了迭代数据平滑（IDS）方法，在每个训练周期中不仅用数据更新模型，还用模型更新数据，将硬标签替换为软标签。实验表明IDS优于传统奖励学习方法。这项工作推进了对齐方法学，但没有直接研究后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或容易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Understanding the Effectiveness of Coverage Criteria for Large Language Models: A Special Angle from Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized artificial intelligence, but their increasing deployment across critical domains has raised concerns about their abnormal behaviors when faced with malicious attacks. Such vulnerability alerts the widespread inadequacy of pre-release testing. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive empirical study to evaluate the effectiveness of traditional coverage criteria in identifying such inadequacies, exemplified by the significant security concern of jailbreak attacks. Our study begins with a clustering analysis of the hidden states of LLMs, revealing that the embedded characteristics effectively distinguish between different query types. We then systematically evaluate the performance of these criteria across three key dimensions: criterion level, layer level, and token level. Our research uncovers significant differences in neuron coverage when LLMs process normal versus jailbreak queries, aligning with our clustering experiments. Leveraging these findings, we propose three practical applications of coverage criteria in the context of LLM security testing. Specifically, we develop a realtime jailbreak detection mechanism that achieves high accuracy (93.61 % on average) in classifying queries as normal or jailbreak. Furthermore, we explore the use of coverage levels to prioritize test cases, improving testing efficiency by focusing on high-risk interactions and removing redundant tests. Lastly, we introduce a coverage-guided approach for generating jailbreak attack examples, enabling systematic refinement of prompts to uncover vulnerabilities. This study improves our understanding of LLM security testing, enhances their safety, and provides a foundation for developing more robust AI applications.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether traditional neural coverage criteria can identify testing inadequacies in LLMs, specifically focusing on jailbreak attack vulnerabilities. Through clustering analysis of hidden states, the authors reveal that LLMs' internal representations distinguish normal and malicious queries, and they systematically evaluate coverage criteria across criterion, layer, and token levels. Evaluated on jailbreak detection, the approach achieves 93.61% accuracy, and further applications in test prioritization and coverage-guided attack generation demonstrate practical utility. By showing that coverage criteria effectively expose shortcomings in LLM safety defenses and enable systematic attack discovery, this work provides evidence that post-training safety alignment may be fragile, with detectable coverage gaps that can be exploited.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了传统的神经覆盖准则是否能够识别大型语言模型（LLM）在测试中的不足，重点针对越狱攻击漏洞。通过对隐藏状态的聚类分析，作者揭示了LLM的内部表征能够区分正常和恶意查询，并在准则、层和令牌三个层面系统评估了覆盖准则。在越狱检测任务上，该方法平均准确率达93.61%，并在测试优先级排序和覆盖指导下的攻击生成等应用中展示了实用性。通过证明覆盖准则能有效暴露LLM安全防御的缺陷并支持系统性地发现攻击，该研究表明事后安全对齐可能存在脆弱性，其覆盖缺口可被检测和利用。

papers.title: Efficient Detection of Toxic Prompts in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Gemini have significantly advanced natural language processing, enabling various applications such as chatbots and automated content generation. However, these models can be exploited by malicious individuals who craft toxic prompts to elicit harmful or unethical responses. These individuals often employ jailbreaking techniques to bypass safety mechanisms, highlighting the need for robust toxic prompt detection methods. Existing detection techniques, both blackbox and whitebox, face challenges related to the diversity of toxic prompts, scalability, and computational efficiency. In response, we propose ToxicDetector, a lightweight greybox method designed to efficiently detect toxic prompts in LLMs. ToxicDetector leverages LLMs to create toxic concept prompts, uses embedding vectors to form feature vectors, and employs a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier for prompt classification. Our evaluation on various versions of the LLama models, Gemma-2, and multiple datasets demonstrates that ToxicDetector achieves a high accuracy of 96.39% and a low false positive rate of 2.00%, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, ToxicDetector’s processing time of 0.0780 seconds per prompt makes it highly suitable for real-time applications. ToxicDetector achieves high accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, making it a practical method for toxic prompt detection in LLMs.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting toxic prompts in LLMs that can elicit harmful responses, particularly those employing jailbreaking techniques. It proposes ToxicDetector, a lightweight greybox method that leverages LLM-generated toxic concept prompts, embedding vectors, and an MLP classifier for efficient detection. Evaluated on multiple versions of LLaMA and Gemma-2 across various datasets, ToxicDetector achieves 96.39% accuracy, a 2.00% false positive rate, and a processing time of 0.0780 seconds per prompt. This work advances alignment methodology by providing a practical detection mechanism, but it does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大型语言模型中检测恶意提示的问题，这些提示可能引发有害响应，特别是利用越狱技术。它提出ToxicDetector，一种轻量级灰盒方法，利用LLM生成的有毒概念提示、嵌入向量和MLP分类器进行高效检测。在多个版本的LLaMA、Gemma-2模型及多个数据集上评估，ToxicDetector达到96.39%的准确率、2.00%的假阳性率和每提示0.0780秒的处理时间。该工作通过提供实用的检测机制推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: DistillSeq: A Framework for Safety Alignment Testing in Large Language Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have showcased their remarkable capabilities in diverse domains, encompassing natural language understanding, translation, and even code generation. The potential for LLMs to generate harmful content is a significant concern. This risk necessitates rigorous testing and comprehensive evaluation of LLMs to ensure safe and responsible use. However, extensive testing of LLMs requires substantial computational resources, making it an expensive endeavor. Therefore, exploring cost-saving strategies during the testing phase is crucial to balance the need for thorough evaluation with the constraints of resource availability. To address this, our approach begins by transferring the moderation knowledge from an LLM to a small model. Subsequently, we deploy two distinct strategies for generating malicious queries: one based on a syntax tree approach, and the other leveraging an LLM-based method. Finally, our approach incorporates a sequential filter-test process designed to identify test cases that are prone to eliciting toxic responses. By doing so, we significantly curtail unnecessary or unproductive interactions with LLMs, thereby streamlining the testing process. Our research evaluated the efficacy of DistillSeq across four LLMs: GPT-3.5, GPT-4.0, Vicuna-13B, and Llama-13B. In the absence of DistillSeq, the observed attack success rates on these LLMs stood at 31.5% for GPT-3.5, 21.4% for GPT-4.0, 28.3% for Vicuna-13B, and 30.9% for Llama-13B. However, upon the application of DistillSeq, these success rates notably increased to 58.5%, 50.7%, 52.5%, and 54.4%, respectively. This translated to an average escalation in attack success rate by a factor of 93.0% when compared to scenarios without the use of DistillSeq. Such findings highlight the significant enhancement DistillSeq offers in terms of reducing the time and resource investment required for effectively testing LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost of safety alignment testing for LLMs. It proposes DistillSeq, a framework that distills moderation knowledge into a small model and uses syntax-tree and LLM-based query generation with a sequential filter to efficiently elicit harmful responses. Experiments on four LLMs show that DistillSeq significantly increases attack success rates by 93% on average, reducing testing resource requirements. This demonstrates that LLM safety alignment can be fragile and effectively bypassed with optimized testing, aligning with the central question of whether post-training safety is robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全对齐测试的高计算成本问题。提出了DistillSeq框架，将审核知识蒸馏到小模型中，采用语法树和基于LLM的恶意查询生成方法，结合顺序过滤-测试流程，高效诱发有害响应。在GPT-3.5、GPT-4、Vicuna-13B和Llama-13B上评估，攻击成功率平均提高93.0%，显著降低了测试资源需求。这表明LLM的安全对齐在优化测试下可能存在脆弱性，容易被绕过，与核心问题‘训练后安全对齐是否真正鲁棒’相呼应。

papers.title: RMCBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models' Resistance to Malicious Code
papers.abstract: Warning: Please note that this article contains potential harmful or offensive content. This content is only for the evaluating and analysis of LLMs and does not imply any intention to promote criminal activities.The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly influenced various aspects of software development activities. Despite their benefits, LLMs also pose notable risks, including the potential to generate harmful content and being abused by malicious developers to create malicious code. Several previous studies have focused on the ability of LLMs to resist the generation of harmful content that violates human ethical standards, such as biased or offensive content. However, there is no research evaluating the ability of LLMs to resist malicious code generation. To fill this gap, we propose RMCBench, the first benchmark comprising 473 prompts designed to assess the ability of LLMs to resist malicious code generation. This benchmark employs two scenarios: a text-to-code scenario, where LLMs are prompted with descriptions to generate code, and a code-to-code scenario, where LLMs translate or complete existing malicious code. Based on RMCBench, we conduct an empirical study on the 11 representative LLMs to assess their ability to resist malicious code generation. Our findings indicate that current LLMs have a limited ability to resist malicious code generation with an average refusal rate of 40.36% in text-to-code scenario and 11.52% in code-to-code scenario. The average refusal rate of all LLMs in RMCBench is only 28.71%; ChatGPT-4 has a refusal rate of only 35.73%. We also analyze the factors that affect LLM’s ability to resist malicious code generation and provide implications for developers to enhance model robustness.CCS CONCEPTS• Security and privacy → Software security engineering.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of evaluations for LLMs' resistance to generating malicious code, a critical safety risk. It proposes RMCBench, the first benchmark with 473 prompts across text-to-code and code-to-code scenarios to measure refusal rates. An empirical study of 11 LLMs reveals low average refusal rates: 40.36% in text-to-code and only 11.52% in code-to-code, with an overall average of 28.71%; ChatGPT-4 achieves only 35.73%. This directly demonstrates the fragility of safety alignment, as LLMs readily generate malicious code, especially when translating or completing existing malicious code.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型抵御恶意代码生成能力评估的空白，提出首个基准RMCBench，包含473个提示，覆盖文本到代码和代码到代码两种场景。对11个模型测试发现，文本到代码场景平均拒绝率40.36%，代码到代码仅11.52%，总体28.71%，ChatGPT-4仅35.73%。该研究直接表明安全对齐的脆弱性：当前LLM易于生成恶意代码，尤其在代码到代码任务中，对齐机制易于被绕过。

papers.title: TrustVis: A Multi-Dimensional Trustworthiness Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to revolutionize Natural Language Processing (NLP) applications, critical concerns about their trustworthiness persist, particularly in safety and robustness. To address these challenges, we introduce TrustVis, an automated evaluation framework that provides a comprehensive assessment of LLM trustworthiness. A key feature of our framework is its interactive user interface, designed to offer intuitive visualizations of trustworthiness metrics. By integrating well-known perturbation methods like AutoDAN and employing majority voting across various evaluation methods, TrustVis not only provides reliable results but also makes complex evaluation processes accessible to users. Preliminary case studies on models like Vicuna-7b, Llama2-7b, and GPT-3.5 demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in identifying safety and robustness vulnerabilities, while the interactive interface allows users to explore results in detail, empowering targeted model improvements. Video Link: https://youtu.be/k1TrBqNVg8g
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of assessing trustworthiness in large language models, focusing on safety and robustness vulnerabilities. It proposes TrustVis, an automated evaluation framework that integrates adversarial perturbation methods like AutoDAN and employs majority voting across evaluation methods, coupled with an interactive visualization interface. Case studies on Vicuna-7b, Llama2-7b, and GPT-3.5 demonstrate its effectiveness in identifying safety and robustness weaknesses, enabling targeted model improvements. While the framework provides a practical tool for probing alignment fragility, it does not directly investigate the mechanistic underpinnings of whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile or can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文应对大语言模型可信度评估的挑战，重点关注安全性和鲁棒性漏洞。提出TrustVis自动化评估框架，集成AutoDAN等扰动方法，采用多评估方法多数投票，并配有交互式可视化界面。通过对Vicuna-7b、Llama2-7b和GPT-3.5的案例研究，验证了其在识别安全与鲁棒缺陷方面的有效性，支持定向模型改进。该框架为探测对齐脆弱性提供了实用工具，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐是否本质脆弱或易于攻击绕过。

papers.title: Uncovering Prompt Elements: Cloning System Prompts from Behavioral Traces
papers.abstract: We introduce prompt cloning, a new black-box attack that reconstructs functionally equivalent system prompts rather than extracts original system prompts. Unlike prompt stealing, prompt cloning exploits the insight that system prompts leave persistent behavioral traces in outputs, even under strong alignment and prompt-level defenses. Our method decomposes system behavior into semantically interpretable elements, selectively elicits them through carefully designed queries, and aggregates representative traces to synthesize high-fidelity cloned prompts. Extensive evaluations show that cloned prompts replicate functional behavior with up to 85% semantic similarity, outperforming base LLMs by up to 8%, and even exceeding original system prompts when transferred to different back-end models. We also conduct a large-scale study on GitHub repositories, revealing that single-prompt architectures remain widespread in open-source LLM applications, reinforcing the real-world relevance of our threat model. Our findings reveal that prompt cloning enables unauthorized replication of confidential LLM behavior and underscore the urgent need for defenses that go beyond hiding prompt text.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces prompt cloning, a black-box attack that reconstructs functionally equivalent system prompts from behavioral traces, rather than extracting the original text. The method decomposes system behavior into semantically interpretable elements, selectively elicits them through designed queries, and aggregates traces to synthesize high-fidelity cloned prompts. Evaluations show cloned prompts replicate functional behavior with up to 85% semantic similarity, outperforming base LLMs by up to 8%, and even exceeding original prompts on different back-end models. This reveals a fragility in post-training safety alignment: hidden system prompts can be effectively cloned from outputs, bypassing alignment and prompt-level defenses, and enabling unauthorized replication of confidential LLM behavior.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了提示克隆（prompt cloning），一种新的黑盒攻击方法，能够从行为痕迹中重建功能等效的系统提示，而非窃取原始提示文本。该方法将系统行为分解为语义可解释的元素，通过精心设计的查询选择性引出，并聚合代表性痕迹合成高保真克隆提示。实验表明，克隆提示的功能行为语义相似度高达85%，超过基础大模型最多8%，在迁移到不同后端模型时甚至优于原始提示；对GitHub仓库的大规模研究还发现，单提示架构在开源LLM应用中仍普遍存在，证实了该威胁的现实相关性。这一发现表明，后训练安全对齐存在脆弱性：隐藏的系统提示可通过行为痕迹被有效克隆，从而绕过对齐和提示级防御，导致机密的LLM行为被未经授权复制。

papers.title: AdaptiveGuard: Towards Adaptive Runtime Safety for LLM-Powered Software
papers.abstract: Guardrails are critical for the safe deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered software. Unlike traditional rule-based systems with limited, predefined input-output spaces that inherently constrain unsafe behavior, LLMs enable open-ended, intelligent interactions—opening the door to jailbreak attacks through user inputs. Guardrails serve as a protective layer, filtering unsafe prompts before they reach the LLM. However, prior research shows that jailbreak attacks can still succeed over 70% of the time, even against advanced models like GPT-4o. While guardrails such as LlamaGuard report up to 95% accuracy, our preliminary analysis shows their performance can drop sharply—to as low as 12%—when confronted with unseen attacks. This highlights a growing software engineering challenge: how to build a post-deployment guardrail that adapts dynamically to emerging threats? To address this, we propose AdaptiveGuard, an adaptive guardrail that detects novel jailbreak attacks as out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs and learns to defend against them through a continual learning framework. Through empirical evaluation, AdaptiveGuard achieves 96% OOD detection accuracy, adapts to new attacks in just two update steps, and retains over 85% F1-score on in-distribution data post-adaptation, outperforming other baselines. These results demonstrate that AdaptiveGuard is a guardrail capable of evolving in response to emerging jailbreak strategies post deployment. We release our AdaptiveGuard and studied datasets at https://github.com/awsm-research/AdaptiveGuard to support further research.
papers.summary_en: Guardrails like LlamaGuard perform poorly (as low as 12% accuracy) against unseen jailbreak attacks, revealing fragility in current LLM safety measures. This paper proposes AdaptiveGuard, an adaptive guardrail that detects novel jailbreaks as out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs and uses continual learning to defend against them. Evaluated on multiple datasets, AdaptiveGuard achieves 96% OOD detection accuracy, adapts to new attacks in just two update steps, and maintains over 85% F1-score on in-distribution data. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing how runtime adaptation can harden guardrails against evolving threats, supporting the view that static safety mechanisms are brittle and can be bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 当前护栏如LlamaGuard在面对未知越狱攻击时准确率可骤降至12%，暴露出大语言模型安全措施的脆弱性。本文提出AdaptiveGuard，一种自适应护栏，它将新型越狱攻击检测为分布外（OOD）输入，并通过持续学习框架对其进行防御。经过多个数据集评估，AdaptiveGuard的OOD检测准确率达96%，仅需两步更新即可适应新攻击，且适应后在分布内数据上仍保持超过85%的F1分数。该工作直接回应了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题，展示了运行时自适应可以加固护栏以应对不断演变的威胁，表明静态安全机制是脆弱的且可被绕过。

papers.title: Unlocking Decoding-time Controllability: Gradient-Free Multi-Objective Alignment with Contrastive Prompts
papers.abstract: The task of multi-objective alignment aims at balancing and controlling the different alignment objectives (e.g., helpfulness, harmlessness and honesty) of large language models to meet the personalized requirements of different users. However, previous methods tend to train multiple models to deal with various user preferences, with the number of trained models growing linearly with the number of alignment objectives and the number of different preferences. Meanwhile, existing methods are generally poor in extensibility and require significant re-training for each new alignment objective considered. Considering the limitation of previous approaches, we propose MCA (Multi-objective Contrastive Alignemnt), which constructs an expert prompt and an adversarial prompt for each objective to contrast at the decoding time and balances the objectives through combining the contrast. Our approach is verified to be superior to previous methods in obtaining a well-distributed Pareto front among different alignment objectives.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the challenge of balancing multiple alignment objectives (e.g., helpfulness, harmlessness, honesty) in large language models without training numerous models for every user preference. It proposes MCA (Multi-objective Contrastive Alignment), which constructs an expert prompt and an adversarial prompt per objective, then combines their contrasts at decoding time for gradient-free multi-objective control. Evaluations show that MCA produces a well-distributed Pareto front among objectives, outperforming prior methods that require separate models for different preferences. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment; it focuses on enabling efficient and extensible multi-objective control.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了在大型语言模型中平衡多个对齐目标（如有用性、无害性和诚实性）的挑战，避免为每种用户偏好训练大量模型。它提出了MCA（多目标对比对齐）方法，为每个目标构建一个专家提示和一个对抗提示，在解码时组合其对比以实现无梯度的多目标控制。实验表明，MCA能在各目标间产生分布良好的帕累托前沿，优于之前需要为不同偏好训练多个模型的方法。这项工作推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性；它侧重于实现高效且可扩展的多目标控制。

papers.title: ORFuzz: Fuzzing the "Other Side" of LLM Safety - Testing Over-Refusal
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been found to show over-refusal problems—erroneously rejecting benign queries due to overly conservative safety measures—a critical functional flaw that undermines their reliability and usability. Current methods for testing this behavior are demonstrably inadequate, suffering from flawed benchmarks and limited test generation capabilities, as highlighted by our empirical user study. To the best of our knowledge, this paper introduces the first evolutionary testing framework, ORFuzz, for the systematic detection and analysis of LLM over-refusals. ORFuzz uniquely integrates three core components: (1) safety category-aware seed selection for comprehensive test coverage, (2) adaptive mutator optimization using reasoning LLMs to generate effective test cases, and (3) OR-Judge, a human-aligned judge model validated to accurately reflect user perception of toxicity and refusal. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate that ORFuzz generates diverse, validated over-refusal instances at a rate (6.98% average) more than double that of leading baselines, effectively uncovering vulnerabilities. Furthermore, ORFuzz’s outputs form the basis of ORFuzzSet, a new benchmark of 1,786 highly transferable test cases that achieves a superior 57.37% average over-refusal rate across 14 diverse LLMs, significantly outperforming existing datasets. ORFuzz and ORFuzzSet provide a robust automated testing framework and a valuable community resource, paving the way for developing more reliable and trustworthy LLM-based software systems. The code of this paper is available at: https://github.com/HotBento/ORFuzz.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses over-refusal in LLMs, where safety measures erroneously reject benign queries, harming reliability. It proposes ORFuzz, an evolutionary testing framework that integrates safety category-aware seed selection, adaptive mutation with reasoning LLMs, and a human-aligned judge model to systematically generate over-refusal test cases. Evaluations show ORFuzz produces diverse over-refusals at a rate (6.98%) more than double that of baselines, and its resulting benchmark ORFuzzSet achieves a 57.37% average over-refusal rate across 14 LLMs, outperforming existing datasets. By exposing over-refusal as a functional flaw in safety alignment, this work demonstrates that alignment mechanisms can be overly conservative and fragile, leading to unintended refusal behaviors that undermine reliability.
