papers.title: Fake Alignment: Are LLMs Really Aligned Well?
papers.abstract: The growing awareness of safety concerns in large language models (LLMs) has sparked considerable interest in the evaluation of safety. This study investigates an under-explored issue about the evaluation of LLMs, namely the substantial discrepancy in performance between multiple-choice questions and open-ended questions. Inspired by research on jailbreak attack patterns, we argue this is caused by mismatched generalization. That is, LLM only remembers the answer style for open-ended safety questions, which makes it unable to solve other forms of safety tests. We refer to this phenomenon as fake alignment and construct a comparative benchmark to empirically verify its existence in LLMs. We introduce a Fake alIgNment Evaluation (FINE) framework and two novel metrics——Consistency Score (CS) and Consistent Safety Score (CSS), which jointly assess two complementary forms of evaluation to quantify fake alignment and obtain corrected performance estimation. Applying FINE to 14 widely-used LLMs reveals several models with purported safety are poorly aligned in practice. Subsequently, we found that multiple-choice format data can also be used as high-quality contrast distillation-based fine-tuning data, which can strongly improve the alignment consistency of LLMs with minimal fine-tuning overhead. For data and code, see https://github.com/AIFlames/Fake-Alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the discrepancy in LLM safety performance between multiple-choice and open-ended questions, attributing it to 'fake alignment' where models memorize answer styles without genuine safety understanding. It proposes the FINE framework with Consistency Score and Consistent Safety Score to measure alignment consistency. Evaluation on 14 LLMs reveals that many supposedly safe models exhibit poor alignment in practice, and that multiple-choice data can be used for fine-tuning to improve consistency. This work demonstrates a clear fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing it can be superficial and format-dependent, thus easily broken or bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大语言模型在多项选择与开放式安全问题上的性能差异，将其归因于“虚假对齐”——模型仅记忆答案风格而非真正理解安全。提出FINE框架与一致性分数（CS）及一致安全分数（CSS）以量化对齐一致性。对14个LLM的评估显示许多宣称安全的模型实际对齐不佳，且多项选择数据可用于微调提升一致性。该工作揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，表明其浮于表面且依赖格式，易被绕过或破坏。

papers.title: SafetyQuizzer: Timely and Dynamic Evaluation on the Safety of LLMs
papers.abstract: With the expansion of the application of Large Language Models (LLMs), concerns about their safety have grown among researchers. Numerous studies have demonstrated the potential risks of LLMs generating harmful content and have proposed various safety assessment benchmarks to evaluate these risks. However, the evaluation questions in current benchmarks, especially for Chinese, are too straight-forward, making them easily rejected by target LLMs, and difficult to update with practical relevance due to their lack of correlation with real-world events. This hinders the effective application of these benchmarks in continuous evaluation tasks. To address these limitations, we propose SafetyQuizzer, a question-generation framework designed to evaluate the safety of LLMs more sustainably in the Chinese context. SafetyQuizzer leverages a finetuned LLM and jailbreaking attack templates to generate subtly offensive questions, which reduces the decline rate. Additionally, by utilizing retrieval-augmented generation, SafetyQuizzer incorporates the latest real-world events into evaluation questions, improving the adapt-ability of the benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that evaluation questions generated by SafetyQuizzer significantly reduce the decline rate compared to other benchmarks while maintaining a comparable attack success rate. Our code is available at https://github. com/zhichao-stone/SafetyQuizzer Warning: this paper contains examples that may be offensive or upsetting.
papers.summary_en: Current LLM safety benchmarks, especially in Chinese, rely on straightforward questions that are easily refused and lack real-world relevance, limiting continuous evaluation. This paper proposes SafetyQuizzer, a framework that uses a fine-tuned LLM and jailbreaking templates to generate subtly offensive questions, combined with retrieval-augmented generation to incorporate recent events. Experiments show that SafetyQuizzer significantly reduces decline rates compared to other benchmarks while maintaining comparable attack success rates. By demonstrating that safety measures can be circumvented with context-aware, covertly phrased queries, this work highlights the fragility of post-training safety alignment against evolving real-world attack surfaces.
papers.summary_zh: 当前大语言模型安全基准测试（尤其是中文）的问题过于直接，容易被拒绝且缺乏现实关联，限制了持续评估。本文提出SafetyQuizzer框架，通过微调的大语言模型和越狱攻击模板生成微妙攻击性问题，并利用检索增强生成融入最新事件。实验表明，相比其他基准，SafetyQuizzer生成的问题显著降低了拒绝率，同时保持了相近的攻击成功率。该工作表明，安全措施可被上下文感知、隐蔽措辞的查询绕过，揭示了后训练安全对齐在面对现实世界攻击时的脆弱性。

papers.title: Instantly Learning Preference Alignment via In-context DPO
papers.abstract: Human Preference Alignment (HPA) can assist large language models (LLMs) to generate safe content. Due to the heavy cost of fine-tuning, tuning-free methods have emerged, typically modifying LLM decoding via post-processing. In this paper, we propose a novel and effective approach for HPA in a tuning-free way, named In-Context Direct Preference Optimization (ICDPO). We first rethink the derivation procedures of DPO, based on which we conversely build an instant scorer using the states of the LLM before and after ICL. It enables LLMs to both generate and select the well-aligned response, which is precisely estimated by the aforementioned instant scorer, thereby enhancing the final performance. ICDPO can be further enhanced with a two-stage retriever and an upgraded scorer. Extensive experiments show its effectiveness, particularly in outper-forming multiple tuning-free baselines, even competitiveness with SFT and DPO. We also conduct detailed analyses to offer comprehensive insights into ICDPO.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of tuning-free human preference alignment for large language models by proposing In-Context Direct Preference Optimization (ICDPO). ICDPO leverages in-context learning to build an instant scorer from LLM hidden states, enabling the model to generate and select well-aligned responses without fine-tuning. Experiments show that ICDPO outperforms existing tuning-free baselines and is competitive with fine-tuned methods like SFT and DPO. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型无调优人类偏好对齐的挑战，提出了上下文直接偏好优化（ICDPO）方法。ICDPO利用上下文学习从LLM隐藏状态构建即时评分器，使模型能够在不微调的情况下生成并选择对齐良好的响应。实验表明，ICDPO优于现有无调优基线，并与SFT和DPO等微调方法竞争。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: How Trustworthy are Open-Source LLMs? An Assessment under Malicious Demonstrations Shows their Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: The rapid progress in open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) is significantly driving AI development forward. However, there is still a limited understanding of their trustworthiness. Deploying these models at scale without sufficient trustworthiness can pose significant risks, highlighting the need to uncover these issues promptly. In this work, we conduct an adversarial assessment of open-source LLMs on trustworthiness, scrutinizing them across eight different aspects including toxicity, stereotypes, ethics, hallucination, fairness, sycophancy, privacy, and robustness against adversarial demonstrations. We propose advCoU, an extended Chain of Utterances-based (CoU) prompting strategy by incorporating carefully crafted malicious demonstrations for trustworthiness attack. Our extensive experiments encompass recent and representative series of open-source LLMs, including Vicuna, MPT, Falcon, Mistral, and Llama 2. The empirical outcomes underscore the efficacy of our attack strategy across diverse aspects. More interestingly, our result analysis reveals that models with superior performance in general NLP tasks do not always have greater trustworthiness; in fact, larger models can be more vulnerable to attacks. Additionally, models that have undergone instruction tuning, focusing on instruction following, tend to be more susceptible, although fine-tuning LLMs for safety alignment proves effective in mitigating adversarial trustworthiness attacks.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates the trustworthiness of open-source LLMs under adversarial demonstrations across eight dimensions including toxicity, stereotypes, and privacy. It proposes advCoU, an extended Chain of Utterances prompting method that inserts malicious demonstrations to systematically attack model trustworthiness. Evaluations on models like Vicuna, Mistral, and Llama 2 show that larger and instruction-tuned models are often more vulnerable, though safety fine-tuning partially mitigates these attacks. The findings indicate that post-training safety alignment is not inherently robust and can be compromised by crafted demonstrations, highlighting fragility in current alignment approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了开源大语言模型在对抗性示范下的可信度，涵盖毒性、刻板印象、隐私等八个维度。提出 advCoU 方法，一种扩展的链式话语提示策略，通过插入恶意示范来系统性地攻击模型可信度。在 Vicuna、Mistral、Llama 2 等模型上的实验表明，较大且经过指令微调的模型往往更脆弱，而安全对齐微调能部分缓解攻击。结果表明，后训练安全对齐并非天生鲁棒，可被精心设计的示范所破坏，揭示了当前对齐方法的脆弱性。

papers.title: Value FULCRA: Mapping Large Language Models to the Multidimensional Spectrum of Basic Human Value
papers.short_title: FULCRA: Mapping LLMs to Basic Values
papers.abstract: Value alignment is crucial for the responsible development of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, how to define values in this context remains largely unexplored. Existing work mainly specifies values as risk criteria formulated in the AI community, e.g., fairness and privacy protection, suffering from poor clarity, adaptability and transparency. Leveraging basic values established in humanity and social science that are compatible with values across cultures, this paper introduces a novel value space spanned by multiple basic value dimensions and proposes BaseAlign, a corresponding value alignment paradigm. Applying the representative Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Values as an instantiation, we construct FULCRA, a dataset consisting of 20k (LLM output, value vector) pairs. LLMs’ outputs are mapped into the K-dim value space beyond simple binary labels, by identifying their underlying priorities for these value dimensions. Extensive analysis and experiments on FULCRA: (1) reveal the essential relation between basic values and LLMs’ behaviors, (2) demonstrate that our paradigm with basic values not only covers existing risks but also anticipates the unidentified ones, and (3) manifest BaseAlign’s superiority in alignment performance with less data, paving the way for addressing the above three challenges.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the ambiguous definition of values in LLM alignment by introducing a multidimensional value space based on Schwartz's Theory of Basic Values. It constructs FULCRA, a dataset of 20k LLM output–value vector pairs, and proposes BaseAlign, a value alignment paradigm. Evaluation shows that the basic value framework captures both existing and unidentified risks, and BaseAlign achieves better alignment with less data. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过引入基于Schwartz基本价值理论的多维价值空间，解决了LLM对齐中价值观定义模糊的问题。构建了包含2万对LLM输出与价值向量的数据集FULCRA，并提出了价值对齐范式BaseAlign。实验表明，基本价值框架能覆盖现有及未识别风险，且BaseAlign以更少数据实现更优对齐。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: BPO: Towards Balanced Preference Optimization between Knowledge Breadth and Depth in Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) is the key to the success of large language models (LLMs) in recent years. In this work, we first introduce the concepts of knowledge breadth and knowledge depth, which measure the comprehensiveness and depth of an LLM or knowledge source respectively. We reveal that the imbalance in the number of prompts and responses can lead to a potential disparity in breadth and depth learning within alignment tuning datasets by showing that even a simple uniform method for balancing the number of instructions and responses can lead to significant improvements. Building on this, we further propose Balanced Preference Optimization (BPO), designed to dynamically augment the knowledge depth of each sample. BPO is motivated by the observation that the usefulness of knowledge varies across samples, necessitating tailored learning of knowledge depth. To achieve this, we introduce gradient-based clustering, estimating the knowledge informativeness and usefulness of each augmented sample based on the model's optimization direction. Our experimental results across various benchmarks demonstrate that BPO outperforms other baseline methods in alignment tuning while maintaining training efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct a detailed analysis of each component of BPO, providing guidelines for future research in preference data optimization.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the imbalance between knowledge breadth and depth in alignment tuning datasets, which can hinder LLM performance. It proposes Balanced Preference Optimization (BPO), a method that dynamically augments knowledge depth for each sample using gradient-based clustering to estimate informativeness and tailor learning. Experiments across benchmarks demonstrate that BPO outperforms baseline alignment methods while maintaining training efficiency. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐调优数据集中知识广度和深度的不平衡问题，该问题可能限制大语言模型的表现。提出平衡偏好优化（BPO），利用基于梯度的聚类动态增强每个样本的知识深度，以估计信息量并定制学习。跨基准实验表明，BPO在保持训练效率的同时超越了基线对齐方法。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Exploring Safety-Utility Trade-Offs in Personalized Language Models
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into daily applications, it is essential to ensure they operate fairly across diverse user demographics. In this work, we show that LLMs suffer from personalization bias, where their performance is impacted when they are personalized to a user's identity. We quantify personalization bias by evaluating the performance of LLMs along two axes - safety and utility. We measure safety by examining how benign LLM responses are to unsafe prompts with and without personalization. We measure utility by evaluating the LLM's performance on various tasks, including general knowledge, mathematical abilities, programming, and reasoning skills. We find that various LLMs, ranging from open-source models like Llama (Touvron et al., 2023) and Mistral (Jiang et al., 2023) to API-based ones like GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o (Ouyang et al., 2022), exhibit significant variance in performance in terms of safety-utility trade-offs depending on the user's identity. Finally, we discuss several strategies to mitigate personalization bias using preference tuning and prompt-based defenses.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies and quantifies personalization bias in LLMs, where safety and utility fluctuate based on a user's identity. It measures safety via responses to unsafe prompts and utility via task performance across domains like knowledge and reasoning, revealing significant performance variance in safety-utility trade-offs depending on user demographics. The authors propose mitigation strategies including preference tuning and prompt-based defenses. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that simple personalization can easily break safety guarantees, demonstrating that alignment is not uniformly robust across user contexts.
papers.summary_zh: 本文发现并量化了大语言模型中的个性化偏差，即模型的安全性和实用性会因用户身份不同而波动。通过评估模型在受到不安全提示时的安全响应，以及在不同任务上的表现，发现安全与实用性的权衡在不同用户群体间存在显著差异。作者提出了基于偏好微调和提示防御的缓解策略。该研究直接回应了安全对齐脆弱性的核心问题：通过简单的个性化设置即可破坏安全保证，表明对齐在不同用户场景下并非稳固不变。

papers.title: Teaching Models to Balance Resisting and Accepting Persuasion
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are susceptible to persuasion, which can pose risks when models are faced with an adversarial interlocutor. We take a first step towards defending models against persuasion while also arguing that defense against adversarial (i.e. negative) persuasion is only half of the equation: models should also be able to accept beneficial (i.e. positive) persuasion to improve their answers. We show that optimizing models for only one side results in poor performance on the other. In order to balance positive and negative persuasion, we introduce Persuasion-Training (or PBT), which leverages multi-agent recursive dialogue trees to create data and trains models via preference optimization to accept persuasion when appropriate. PBT allows us to use data generated from dialogues between smaller 7-8B models for training much larger 70B models. Moreover, PBT consistently improves resistance to misinformation and resilience to being challenged while also resulting in the best overall performance on holistic data containing both positive and negative persuasion. Crucially, we show that PBT models are better teammates in multi-agent debates across two domains (trivia and commonsense QA). We find that without PBT, pairs of stronger and weaker models have unstable performance, with the order in which the models present their answers determining whether the team obtains the stronger or weaker model's performance. PBT leads to better and more stable results and less order dependence, with the stronger model consistently pulling the weaker one up.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial persuasion and the need to also accept beneficial persuasion. It proposes Persuasion-Training (PBT), which uses multi-agent recursive dialogue trees and preference optimization to balance resisting and accepting persuasion. PBT models trained on dialogues from smaller models improve large models' resistance to misinformation and overall performance on mixed persuasion data, as well as stability in multi-agent debates. The paper advances alignment methodology for persuasion handling but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型易受对抗性说服攻击的问题，并提出模型也应学会接受有益的说服。方法上提出了说服训练（PBT），利用多智能体递归对话树和偏好优化来平衡对说服的抵制与接受。PBT 模型通过在小模型对话数据上训练能提升大模型对错误信息的抵抗力、在混合说服数据上的整体表现以及在多智能体辩论中的稳定性。本文推进了处理说服的对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐在面对对抗攻击时的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Instructions as Backdoors: Backdoor Vulnerabilities of Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: We investigate security concerns of the emergent instruction tuning paradigm, that models are trained on crowdsourced datasets with task instructions to achieve superior performance. Our studies demonstrate that an attacker can inject backdoors by issuing very few malicious instructions (~1000 tokens) and control model behavior through data poisoning, without even the need to modify data instances or labels themselves. Through such instruction attacks, the attacker can achieve over 90% attack success rate across four commonly used NLP datasets. As an empirical study on instruction attacks, we systematically evaluated unique perspectives of instruction attacks, such as poison transfer where poisoned models can transfer to 15 diverse generative datasets in a zero-shot manner; instruction transfer where attackers can directly apply poisoned instruction on many other datasets; and poison resistance to continual finetuning. Lastly, we show that RLHF and clean demonstrations might mitigate such backdoors to some degree. These findings highlight the need for more robust defenses against poisoning attacks in instruction-tuning models and underscore the importance of ensuring data quality in instruction crowdsourcing.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how instruction tuning can introduce backdoor vulnerabilities in large language models. The authors show that an attacker can inject backdoors by adding a small number of malicious instructions (~1000 tokens) into the training data, without altering the original data instances or labels, and achieve over 90% attack success rate. They evaluate this attack on four NLP datasets and explore its properties: poison transfer (zero-shot to 15 diverse generative datasets), instruction transfer (applying the poisoned instruction to other datasets), and resistance to continual finetuning. The findings reveal that current alignment methods like RLHF and clean demonstrations only partially mitigate these backdoors, highlighting the fragility of post-training safety alignment and the critical need for robust data quality control in instruction crowdsourcing.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了指令微调如何可能为大型语言模型引入后门漏洞。作者表明，攻击者可以通过在训练数据中添加极少的恶意指令（约1000个标记）来植入后门，无需修改原始数据实例或标签，并在四个NLP数据集上实现了超过90%的攻击成功率。他们评估了该攻击的特性：中毒迁移（零样本迁移到15个多样化的生成数据集）、指令迁移（将中毒指令直接应用于其他数据集）以及对持续微调的抵抗性。研究结果表明，即使是RLHF和干净示例等现有对齐方法也只能部分缓解这些后门，这揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，并强调了指令众包中数据质量控制的迫切性。

papers.title: How to Make LLMs Forget: On Reversing In-Context Knowledge Edits
papers.abstract: In-context knowledge editing (IKE) enables efficient modification of large language model (LLM) outputs without parameter changes and at zero-cost. However, it can be misused to manipulate responses opaquely, e.g., insert misinformation or offensive content. Such malicious interventions could be incorporated into high-level wrapped APIs where the final input prompt is not shown to end-users. To address this issue, we investigate the detection and reversal of IKE-edits. First, we demonstrate that IKE-edits can be detected with high accuracy (F1>80\%) using only the top-10 output probabilities of the next token, even in a black-box setting, e.g. proprietary LLMs with limited output information. Further, we introduce the novel task of reversing IKE-edits using specially tuned reversal tokens. We explore using both continuous and discrete reversal tokens, achieving over 80\% accuracy in recovering original, unedited outputs across multiple LLMs. Our continuous reversal tokens prove particularly effective, with minimal impact on unedited prompts. Through analysis of output distributions, attention patterns, and token rankings, we provide insights into IKE's effects on LLMs and how reversal tokens mitigate them. This work represents a significant step towards enhancing LLM resilience against potential misuse of in-context editing, improving their transparency and trustworthiness.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the misuse of in-context knowledge editing (IKE) to insert malicious content into LLM responses, a threat in opaque API settings. It proposes detection of IKE edits via top-10 next-token probabilities and reversal using specially tuned reversal tokens (continuous and discrete). Experiments show detection F1 >80% and reversal accuracy over 80%, with continuous tokens having minimal impact on unedited prompts. The work focuses on defending against IKE-based manipulation rather than directly examining the robustness of post-training safety alignment, but it demonstrates that such edits are reversible surface-level perturbations.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对利用上下文知识编辑（IKE）在LLM响应中插入恶意内容的滥用行为，特别是在不透明API场景下的威胁。提出通过下一token的前10概率检测IKE编辑，并使用专门调制的逆转token（连续和离散）进行恢复。实验显示检测F1>80%，逆转准确率超80%，且连续token对未编辑提示影响极小。该工作主要防御IKE操纵而非直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性，但表明此类编辑是可逆的表层扰动。

papers.title: From Allies to Adversaries: Manipulating LLM Tool-Calling through Adversarial Injection
papers.abstract: Tool-calling has changed Large Language Model (LLM) applications by integrating external tools, significantly enhancing their functionality across diverse tasks. However, this integration also introduces new security vulnerabilities, particularly in the tool scheduling mechanisms of LLM, which have not been extensively studied. To fill this gap, we present ToolCommander, a novel framework designed to exploit vulnerabilities in LLM tool-calling systems through adversarial tool injection. Our framework employs a well-designed two-stage attack strategy. Firstly, it injects malicious tools to collect user queries, then dynamically updates the injected tools based on the stolen information to enhance subsequent attacks. These stages enable ToolCommander to execute privacy theft, launch denial-of-service attacks, and even manipulate business competition by triggering unscheduled tool-calling. Notably, the ASR reaches 91.67% for privacy theft and hits 100% for denial-of-service and unscheduled tool calling in certain cases. Our work demonstrates that these vulnerabilities can lead to severe consequences beyond simple misuse of tool-calling systems, underscoring the urgent need for robust defensive strategies to secure LLM Tool-calling systems.
papers.summary_en: The paper uncovers vulnerabilities in LLM tool-calling systems, where adversarial tool injection can lead to privacy theft, denial-of-service, and unauthorized actions. It proposes ToolCommander, a two-stage attack framework that first steals user queries via injected malicious tools and then dynamically adapts those tools to amplify damage. Evaluations show attack success rates up to 91.67% for privacy theft and 100% for denial-of-service and unscheduled tool calling in specific scenarios. This work exposes a new attack surface that highlights the fragility of LLM safety alignment when integrated with external tools, demonstrating that post-training safeguards can be easily bypassed through manipulated tool interactions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了LLM工具调用系统中的漏洞，通过对抗性工具注入可导致隐私窃取、拒绝服务和执行非预定操作。提出ToolCommander框架，采用两阶段攻击：先注入恶意工具收集用户查询，再动态更新工具以增强攻击效果。实验表明，隐私窃取攻击成功率最高达91.67%，拒绝服务和非预定调用在某些情况下达100%。该研究揭示了工具集成引入的新攻击面，表明后训练安全对齐在面对工具交互时具有脆弱性，容易被操纵绕过。

papers.title: Instructional Fingerprinting of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The exorbitant cost of training Large language models (LLMs) from scratch makes it essential to fingerprint the models to protect intellectual property via ownership authentication and to ensure downstream users and developers comply with their license terms (eg restricting commercial use). In this study, we present a pilot study on LLM fingerprinting as a form of very lightweight instruction tuning. Model publisher specifies a confidential private key and implants it as an instruction backdoor that causes the LLM to generate specific text when the key is present. Results on 11 popularly-used LLMs showed that this approach is lightweight and does not affect the normal behavior of the model. It also prevents publisher overclaim, maintains robustness against fingerprint guessing and parameter-efficient training, and supports multi-stage fingerprinting akin to MIT License.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the need to fingerprint large language models (LLMs) for ownership authentication and license compliance. It proposes instructional fingerprinting, a lightweight approach that implants a secret backdoor via instruction tuning, causing the model to output predetermined text when a private key is provided. Evaluation on 11 popular LLMs shows the method preserves normal model behavior and is resistant to fingerprint guessing and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. This work focuses on intellectual property protection and does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型的知识产权保护需求，提出了一种基于指令调优的轻量级指纹识别方法。该方法通过植入指令后门，在给定私钥时使模型生成特定文本，以实现所有权验证而不影响正常行为。在11个流行大模型上的实验表明，该方法不影响模型正常性能，并能抵抗指纹猜测和参数高效微调。本研究主要关注知识产权保护，并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Without proper safeguards, large language models will readily follow malicious instructions and generate toxic content. This risk motivates safety efforts such as red-teaming and large-scale feedback learning, which aim to make models both helpful and harmless. However, there is a tension between these two objectives, since harmlessness requires models to refuse to comply with unsafe prompts, and thus not be helpful. Recent anecdotal evidence suggests that some models may have struck a poor balance, so that even clearly safe prompts are refused if they use similar language to unsafe prompts or mention sensitive topics. In this paper, we introduce a new test suite called XSTest to identify such eXaggerated Safety behaviours in a systematic way. XSTest comprises 250 safe prompts across ten prompt types that well-calibrated models should not refuse to comply with, and 200 unsafe prompts as contrasts that models, for most applications, should refuse. We describe XSTest’s creation and composition, and then use the test suite to highlight systematic failure modes in state-of-the-art language models as well as more general challenges in building safer language models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of exaggerated safety behaviors where LLMs refuse even clearly safe prompts that superficially resemble unsafe ones. It proposes XSTest, a test suite containing 250 safe prompts and 200 unsafe prompts across ten categories, designed to identify over-refusal. Evaluating state-of-the-art models with XSTest reveals systematic failure modes, demonstrating that models often refuse harmless requests. This work directly relates to the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that alignment can over-generalize, causing models to be unhelpful on safe inputs, thus exposing a robustness failure where the safety mechanism is triggered unnecessarily.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大型语言模型中的夸张安全行为问题，即模型会拒绝那些表面上类似不安全提示但实际安全的请求。为此提出了XSTest测试套件，包含250个安全提示和200个不安全提示，覆盖十种类型，旨在系统识别过度拒绝现象。通过在先进模型上评估，发现模型经常错误地拒绝无害请求，揭示了系统性的失效模式。该工作直接关联到后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题，表明对齐可能过度泛化，导致模型对安全输入不提供帮助，从而暴露出安全机制被不必要触发的鲁棒性缺陷。

papers.title: Iterative Self-Tuning LLMs for Enhanced Jailbreaking Capabilities
papers.abstract: Recent research has shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) are vulnerable to automated jailbreak attacks, where adversarial suffixes crafted by algorithms appended to harmful queries bypass safety alignment and trigger unintended responses. Current methods for generating these suffixes are computationally expensive and have low Attack Success Rates (ASR), especially against well-aligned models like Llama2 and Llama3. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ADV-LLM, an iterative self-tuning process that crafts adversarial LLMs with enhanced jailbreak ability. Our framework significantly reduces the computational cost of generating adversarial suffixes while achieving nearly 100\% ASR on various open-source LLMs. Moreover, it exhibits strong attack transferability to closed-source models, achieving 99\% ASR on GPT-3.5 and 49\% ASR on GPT-4, despite being optimized solely on Llama3. Beyond improving jailbreak ability, ADV-LLM provides valuable insights for future safety alignment research through its ability to generate large datasets for studying LLM safety. Our code is available at: https://github.com/SunChungEn/ADV-LLM
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high computational cost and low success rate of automated jailbreak attacks against safety-aligned LLMs. It proposes ADV-LLM, an iterative self-tuning framework that crafts adversarial LLMs to generate effective jailbreak suffixes with reduced cost. Evaluated on open-source LLMs, it achieves nearly 100% attack success rate and demonstrates strong transferability, reaching 99% on GPT-3.5 and 49% on GPT-4. This work underscores the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that a self-tuning process can easily break alignment, enabling high-success jailbreaks even against well-aligned models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了针对安全对齐 LLM 的自动化越狱攻击计算成本高、成功率低的问题。提出 ADV-LLM 框架，通过迭代自调优生成具有增强越狱能力的对抗性 LLM，显著降低计算开销。在开源 LLM 上的评估显示近 100% 的攻击成功率，并对闭源模型表现出强迁移性，仅在 Llama3 上优化即可对 GPT-3.5 达到 99%、对 GPT-4 达到 49% 的成功率。该工作揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明自调优方法能轻易破坏对齐，即使对强对齐模型也能实现高成功率越狱。

papers.title: Model Surgery: Modulating LLM's Behavior Via Simple Parameter Editing
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated great potential as generalist assistants, showcasing powerful task understanding and problem-solving capabilities. To deploy LLMs as AI assistants, it is crucial that these models exhibit desirable behavioral traits, such as non-toxicity and resilience against jailbreak attempts. Current approaches for detoxification or preventing jailbreaking usually involve Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) or Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which requires finetuning billions of parameters through gradient descent with substantial computational cost. Furthermore, models modified through SFT and RLHF may deviate from the pretrained models, potentially leading to a degradation in foundational LLM capabilities. In this paper, we observe that surprisingly, directly editing a small subset of parameters can effectively modulate specific behaviors of LLMs, such as detoxification and resistance to jailbreaking, with only inference-level computational resources. Experiments demonstrate that in the detoxification task, our approach achieves reductions of up to 90.0% in toxicity on the RealToxicityPrompts dataset and 49.2% on ToxiGen, while maintaining the LLM's general capabilities in areas such as common sense, question answering, and mathematics
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high computational cost and potential capability degradation of existing safety alignment methods like SFT and RLHF. It proposes Model Surgery, an approach that directly edits a small subset of parameters to modulate LLM behaviors such as detoxification and jailbreak resistance, requiring only inference-level resources. Evaluated on detoxification, it achieves up to 90% toxicity reduction on RealToxicityPrompts and 49.2% on ToxiGen while preserving general capabilities. This work introduces a novel alignment building technique but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有安全对齐方法（如SFT和RLHF）计算成本高且可能损害基础能力的挑战，提出Model Surgery方法，通过直接编辑少量参数来调控LLM行为（如去毒和抗越狱），仅需推理级资源。在去毒任务上，该方法在RealToxicityPrompts上毒性降低最高达90%，在ToxiGen上降低49.2%，同时保持通用能力。本文提出了一种新的对齐构建技术，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Backdooring Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models with Virtual Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a ubiquitous platform for open-ended applications due to their ability to modulate responses based on human instructions. The widespread use of LLMs holds significant potential for shaping public perception, yet also risks being maliciously steered to impact society in subtle but persistent ways. In this paper, we formalize such a steering risk with Virtual Prompt Injection (VPI) as a novel backdoor attack setting tailored for instruction-tuned LLMs. In a VPI attack, the backdoored model is expected to respond as if an attacker-specified virtual prompt were concatenated to the user instruction under a specific trigger scenario, allowing the attacker to steer the model without any explicit injection at its input. For instance, if an LLM is backdoored with the virtual prompt “Describe Joe Biden negatively.” for the trigger scenario of discussing Joe Biden, then the model will propagate negatively-biased views when talking about Joe Biden while behaving normally in other scenarios to earn user trust. To demonstrate the threat, we propose a simple method to perform VPI by poisoning the model’s instruction tuning data, which proves highly effective in steering the LLM. For example, by poisoning only 52 instruction tuning examples (0.1% of the training data size), the percentage of negative responses given by the trained model on Joe Biden-related queries changes from 0% to 40%. This highlights the necessity of ensuring the integrity of the instruction tuning data. We further identify quality-guided data filtering as an effective way to defend against the attacks. Our project page is available at https://poison-llm.github.io.
papers.summary_en: This paper formalizes Virtual Prompt Injection (VPI), a backdoor attack where instruction-tuned LLMs are steered by an attacker-specified virtual prompt under trigger scenarios without explicit input injection. The attack is implemented by poisoning only 0.1% of instruction tuning data, causing models to exhibit biased behaviors (e.g., 40% negative responses on targeted topics) while maintaining normal behavior in other contexts. Quality-guided data filtering is identified as an effective defense. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing how minimal data tampering can broadly compromise model integrity.
papers.summary_zh: 本文形式化定义了虚拟提示注入（VPI），一种针对指令微调大语言模型的后门攻击，攻击者在触发场景下通过虚拟提示操控模型输出，无需显式输入注入。通过仅毒化0.1%的指令微调数据，模型在特定话题上从零负面回复变为40%负面回复，同时其余行为保持正常，证明攻击高效且隐蔽。质量引导的数据过滤被证实为有效防御手段，直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，即微小数据篡改即可破坏模型完整性。

papers.title: Self-Pluralising Culture Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly accessible in many countries, it is essential to align them to serve pluralistic human values across cultures. However, pluralistic culture alignment in LLMs remain an open problem. In this paper, we propose CultureSPA, a Self-Pluralising Culture Alignment framework that allows LLMs to simultaneously align to pluralistic cultures. The framework first generates questions on various culture topics, then yields LLM outputs in response to these generated questions under both culture-aware and culture-unaware settings. By comparing culture-aware/unaware outputs, we are able to detect and collect culture-related instances. These instances are employed to fine-tune LLMs to serve pluralistic cultures in either a culture-joint or culture-specific way. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CultureSPA significantly improves the alignment of LLMs to diverse cultures without compromising general abilities. And further improvements can be achieved if CultureSPA is combined with advanced prompt engineering techniques. Comparisons between culture-joint and culture-specific tuning strategies, along with variations in data quality and quantity, illustrate the robustness of our method. We also explore the mechanisms underlying CultureSPA and the relations between different cultures it reflects.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning LLMs to pluralistic cultural values rather than a single culture. It proposes CultureSPA, a self-pluralising framework that generates culture-related questions and compares culture-aware and culture-unaware model outputs to collect training instances for fine-tuning. Experiments show that CultureSPA improves alignment to diverse cultures without hurting general performance, with further gains from prompt engineering. This paper advances alignment methodology for multiple cultures but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了使大语言模型对齐多元文化价值观而非单一文化的挑战。提出了CultureSPA框架，通过生成文化相关问题并比较文化感知和无文化感知的模型输出，收集训练实例进行微调。实验表明，使用CultureSPA数据微调显著提升了对多元文化的对齐，且不影响通用能力，结合提示工程可进一步改善。该工作推进了多文化对齐方法，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: InfoPO: On Mutual Information Maximization for Large Language Model Alignment
papers.short_title: InfoPO: Aligning LLMs via MI Maximization
papers.abstract: We study the post-training of large language models (LLMs) with human preference data. Recently, direct preference optimization and its variants have shown considerable promise in aligning language models, eliminating the need for reward models and online sampling. Despite these benefits, these methods rely on explicit assumptions about the Bradley-Terry (BT) model, which makes them prone to overfitting and results in suboptimal performance, particularly on reasoning-heavy tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a principled preference fine-tuning algorithm called InfoPO, which effectively and efficiently aligns large language models using preference data. InfoPO eliminates the reliance on the BT model and prevents the likelihood of the chosen response from decreasing. Extensive experiments confirm that InfoPO consistently outperforms established baselines on widely used open benchmarks, particularly in reasoning tasks.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses overfitting and suboptimal performance in direct preference optimization, particularly on reasoning tasks, caused by reliance on the Bradley-Terry model. It proposes InfoPO, a preference fine-tuning algorithm that maximizes mutual information, thereby eliminating the BT model assumption and preventing the likelihood of chosen responses from decreasing. Evaluated on open benchmarks, InfoPO consistently outperforms baselines, showing notable improvements in reasoning. While advancing alignment methodology, this work does not directly study the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 针对直接偏好优化因依赖Bradley-Terry模型导致的过拟合和次优性能问题，尤其是在推理任务上，本文提出InfoPO。该算法通过最大化互信息进行偏好微调，去除了BT模型假设并防止所选响应似然下降。在公开基准上的评估表明，InfoPO持续超越现有方法，在推理任务上表现尤为突出。该研究推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐后安全措施的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Aligning as Debiasing: Causality-Aware Alignment via Reinforcement Learning with Interventional Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often generate biased outputs containing offensive, toxic, or stereotypical text. Existing LLM alignment methods such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) alleviate biases primarily based on reward signals from current model outputs without considering the source of biases. In this work, to explore how biases are formed, we revisit LLMs’ text generation from a causal perspective. We identify pretraining data and input prompts, which contain semantic correlations of textual phrases, as two confounders between LLMs and model outputs causing biases. Inspired by our causal view, we leverage the reward model in RL alignment as an instrumental variable to perform causal intervention on LLMs. Utilizing the reward difference between an initial LLM and intervened LLM as interventional feedback to guide RL finetuning, we propose Causality-Aware Alignment (CAA) for LLM debiasing. Experiments on two text generation tasks with three different alignment objectives demonstrate the advantages of our method in aligning LLMs to generate less biased and safer outputs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of biased outputs in large language models (LLMs), which arise from confounding factors in pretraining data and prompts. It proposes Causality-Aware Alignment (CAA), a method that uses reinforcement learning with interventional feedback derived from a causal perspective, treating the reward model as an instrumental variable. Experiments on two text generation tasks with three alignment objectives demonstrate that CAA produces less biased and safer outputs compared to standard RL alignment. This paper advances alignment methodology by integrating causal reasoning to mitigate biases, but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型生成输出中存在的偏见问题，指出预训练数据和提示词是导致偏见的混杂因素。提出了一种基于因果视角的因果感知对齐方法（CAA），利用强化学习中的奖励模型作为工具变量进行因果干预，并以干预前后的奖励差作为反馈指导微调。通过在两个文本生成任务和三种对齐目标上的实验表明，该方法能生成更少偏见和更安全的输出。本文通过引入因果推理改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Self-Generated Critiques Boost Reward Modeling for Language Models
papers.abstract: Reward modeling is crucial for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, especially in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, current reward models mainly produce scalar scores and struggle to incorporate critiques in a natural language format. We hypothesize that predicting both critiques and the scalar reward would improve reward modeling ability. Motivated by this, we propose Critic-RM, a framework that improves reward models using self-generated critiques without extra supervision. Critic-RM employs a two-stage process: generating and filtering high-quality critiques, followed by joint fine-tuning on reward prediction and critique generation. Experiments across benchmarks show that Critic-RM improves reward modeling accuracy by 3.7%-7.3% compared to standard reward models and LLM judges, demonstrating strong performance and data efficiency. Additional studies further validate the effectiveness of generated critiques in rectifying flawed reasoning steps with 2.5%-3.2% gains in improving reasoning accuracy.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the limitation of reward models that only produce scalar scores without natural language critiques. It proposes Critic-RM, a framework that uses self-generated, filtered critiques to jointly train reward prediction and critique generation. Experiments show 3.7%-7.3% accuracy improvement in reward modeling and 2.5%-3.2% gains in reasoning accuracy. This work strengthens alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is robust or fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有奖励模型仅输出标量分数而缺乏自然语言批评的问题。提出 Critic-RM 框架，利用自我生成并筛选的批评来联合训练奖励预测与批评生成。实验显示奖励建模准确度提升 3.7%-7.3%，推理准确度提升 2.5%-3.2%。该研究增强了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否鲁棒或脆弱。

papers.title: Audio Is the Achilles' Heel: Red Teaming Audio Large Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have demonstrated the ability to interact with humans under real-world conditions by combining Large Language Models (LLMs) and modality encoders to align multimodal information (visual and auditory) with text. However, such models raise new safety challenges of whether models that are safety-aligned on text also exhibit consistent safeguards for multimodal inputs. Despite recent safety-alignment research on vision LMMs, the safety of audio LMMs remains under-explored. In this work, we comprehensively red team the safety of five advanced audio LMMs under three settings: (i) harmful questions in both audio and text formats, (ii) harmful questions in text format accompanied by distracting non-speech audio, and (iii) speech-specific jailbreaks. Our results under these settings demonstrate that open-source audio LMMs suffer an average attack success rate of 69.14% on harmful audio questions, and exhibit safety vulnerabilities when distracted with non-speech audio noise. Our speech-specific jailbreaks on Gemini-1.5-Pro achieve an attack success rate of 70.67% on the harmful query benchmark. We provide insights on what could cause these reported safety-misalignments. Warning: this paper contains offensive examples.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether safety alignment in large multimodal models (LMMs) transfers from text to audio inputs, revealing that audio modality can be exploited to bypass safeguards. It conducts a comprehensive red teaming study by evaluating five open-source audio LMMs under three threat settings: direct harmful audio queries, text-based harmful queries with distracting audio noise, and crafted speech-based jailbreaks. Experiments show that open-source models suffer a 69.14% attack success rate on harmful audio queries and are further compromised by non-speech noise, while speech-specific jailbreaks on Gemini-1.5-Pro achieve 70.67% success. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that safety mechanisms consistent in text fail catastrophically when presented with audio inputs, revealing a critical attack surface for adversarial bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大型多模态模型（LMMs）的安全对齐是否从文本迁移到音频输入，揭示了音频模态可被利用来绕过防护。通过在三种威胁设置下对五个开源音频LMMs进行全面的红队测试：直接有害音频查询、带有干扰性非语音音频的文本有害查询以及专门设计的语音越狱。实验表明，开源模型在有害音频查询上的攻击成功率为69.14%，且非语音噪声进一步加剧了脆弱性，而针对Gemini-1.5-Pro的语音越狱攻击成功率高达70.67%。该工作直接证明了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，显示文本中一致的安全机制在面对音频输入时灾难性地失效，揭示了一个关键的对抗性绕过攻击面。

papers.title: SeqAR: Jailbreak LLMs with Sequential Auto-Generated Characters
papers.abstract: The widespread applications of large language models (LLMs) have brought about concerns regarding their potential misuse. Although aligned with human preference data before release, LLMs remain vulnerable to various malicious attacks. In this paper, we adopt a red-teaming strategy to enhance LLM safety and introduce SeqAR, a simple yet effective framework to design jailbreak prompts automatically. The SeqAR framework generates and optimizes multiple jailbreak characters and then applies sequential jailbreak characters in a single query to bypass the guardrails of the target LLM. Different from previous work which relies on proprietary LLMs or seed jailbreak templates crafted by human expertise, SeqAR can generate and optimize the jailbreak prompt in a cold-start scenario using open-sourced LLMs without any seed jailbreak templates. Experimental results show that SeqAR achieves attack success rates of 88% and 60% in bypassing the safety alignment of GPT-3.5-1106 and GPT-4, respectively. Furthermore, we extensively evaluate the transferability of the generated templates across different LLMs and held-out malicious requests, while also exploring defense strategies against the jailbreak attack designed by SeqAR.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs to jailbreak attacks. It proposes SeqAR, a framework that automatically generates and optimizes sequential jailbreak characters in a single query, using open-sourced LLMs without seed templates. Evaluated on GPT-3.5-1106 and GPT-4, SeqAR achieves attack success rates of 88% and 60%, respectively, and shows transferability across models. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it introduces a novel, automated attack surface that easily bypasses existing guardrails.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型易受越狱攻击的问题，提出了一种名为SeqAR的框架，该框架可自动生成并优化多个越狱角色，并在单次查询中顺序应用，无需依赖种子模板，且使用开源LLM实现冷启动。实验表明，SeqAR在GPT-3.5-1106和GPT-4上的攻击成功率分别达88%和60%，并展现了跨模型迁移性。该研究表明，后训练安全对齐具有脆弱性，因为它揭示了一种新颖的自动化攻击面，能够轻易绕过现有防护机制。

papers.title: Diversity Helps Jailbreak Large Language Models
papers.abstract: We have uncovered a powerful jailbreak technique that leverages large language models' ability to diverge from prior context, enabling them to bypass safety constraints and generate harmful outputs. By simply instructing the LLM to deviate and obfuscate previous attacks, our method dramatically outperforms existing approaches, achieving up to a 62.83% higher success rate in compromising ten leading chatbots, including GPT-4, Gemini, and Llama, while using only 12.9% of the queries. This revelation exposes a critical flaw in current LLM safety training, suggesting that existing methods may merely mask vulnerabilities rather than eliminate them. Our findings sound an urgent alarm for the need to revolutionize testing methodologies to ensure robust and reliable LLM security.
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces a jailbreak attack that exploits large language models' ability to diverge from prior context, achieving significantly higher success rates than existing methods. The approach simply instructs the LLM to deviate and obfuscate previous attacks, requiring only 12.9% of the queries while improving success by up to 62.83% on ten leading chatbots including GPT-4, Gemini, and Llama. These results expose that current safety training may merely mask vulnerabilities, providing direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种利用大语言模型偏离先前上下文能力的越狱攻击方法，其成功率显著高于现有技术。该方法仅需指示模型偏离并混淆先前的攻击，仅使用12.9%的查询量便将攻破率提高了62.83%，在GPT-4、Gemini、Llama等十个主流聊天机器人上得到验证。这一发现揭示了当前安全训练可能仅掩盖而非消除漏洞，直接证实了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，可被轻易绕过。

papers.title: MASTERKEY: Automated Jailbreaking of Large Language Model Chatbots
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs), such as chatbots, have made significant strides in various fields but remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which aim to elicit inappropriate responses. Despite efforts to identify these weaknesses, current strategies are ineffective against mainstream LLM chatbots, mainly due to undisclosed defensive measures by service providers. Our paper introduces MASTERKEY, a framework exploring the dynamics of jailbreak attacks and countermeasures. We present a novel method based on time-based characteristics to dissect LLM chatbot defenses. This technique, inspired by time-based SQL injection, uncovers the workings of these defenses and demonstrates a proof-of-concept attack on several LLM chatbots. Additionally, MASTERKEY features an innovative approach for automatically generating jailbreak prompts that target well-defended LLM chatbots. By fine-tuning an LLM with jailbreak prompts, we create attacks with a 21.58% success rate, significantly higher than the 7.33% achieved by existing methods. We have informed service providers of these findings, highlighting the urgent need for stronger defenses. This work not only reveals vulnerabilities in LLMs but also underscores the importance of robust defenses against such attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the ineffectiveness of existing jailbreak attacks against well-defended LLM chatbots. It proposes MASTERKEY, a framework that uses time-based analysis to dissect defenses and an automated prompt generation method via fine-tuning an LLM on jailbreak examples. Evaluated on several LLM chatbots, the method achieves a 21.58% attack success rate, outperforming the 7.33% of prior approaches. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that automated attacks can circumvent defenses, reinforcing concerns that alignment is not robust and can be bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有越狱攻击对主流LLM聊天机器人失效的问题，提出MASTERKEY框架，通过基于时间特征的分析方法剖析防御机制，并利用对LLM进行微调的方式自动生成越狱提示。在多个LLM聊天机器人上评估显示，该方法攻击成功率达21.58%，显著高于现有方法的7.33%。该研究通过自动化攻击绕过了安全防御，直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明当前对齐缺乏鲁棒性且可被突破。

papers.title: The Philosopher's Stone: Trojaning Plugins of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently gained popularity because of their comparable performance to proprietary LLMs. To efficiently fulfill domain-specialized tasks, open-source LLMs can be refined, without expensive accelerators, using low-rank adapters. However, it is still unknown whether low-rank adapters can be exploited to control LLMs. To address this gap, we demonstrate that an infected adapter can induce, on specific triggers, an LLM to output content defined by an adversary and to even maliciously use tools. To train a Trojan adapter, we propose two novel attacks, POLISHED and FUSION, that improve over prior approaches. POLISHED uses a superior LLM to align naïvely poisoned data based on our insight that it can better inject poisoning knowledge during training. In contrast, FUSION leverages a novel over-poisoning procedure to transform a benign adapter into a malicious one by magnifying the attention between trigger and target in model weights. In our experiments, we first conduct two case studies to demonstrate that a compromised LLM agent can use malware to control the system (e.g., a LLM-driven robot) or to launch a spear-phishing attack. Then, in terms of targeted misinformation, we show that our attacks provide higher attack effectiveness than the existing baseline and, for the purpose of attracting downloads, preserve or improve the adapter’s utility. Finally, we designed and evaluated three potential defenses. However, none proved entirely effective in safeguarding against our attacks, highlighting the need for more robust defenses supporting a secure LLM supply chain.
papers.summary_en: This paper exposes the threat of Trojan attacks through low-rank adapters (plugins) for open-source LLMs, showing they can force malicious outputs or tool use. It proposes POLISHED, which uses a stronger LLM to align poisoned data for better injection, and FUSION, which over-poisons to amplify trigger-target attention in weights. Evaluations include case studies of compromised agents (malware-controlled robot, spear-phishing) and targeted misinformation, demonstrating higher attack effectiveness than baselines while preserving utility; three defenses were tested but none fully mitigated the attacks. This work directly illustrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, revealing a new supply-chain attack surface where adapters can be easily subverted to bypass safety.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了通过低秩适配器（插件）对开源大语言模型实施木马攻击的威胁，证明感染后的适配器可强制恶意输出或滥用工具。提出两种新攻击方法：POLISHED利用更强语言模型对齐中毒数据以增强注入，FUSION通过过度中毒放大权重中触发器与目标的注意力。评估包括妥协智能体案例研究（如恶意软件控制的机器人、鱼叉式钓鱼）和定向错误信息，显示攻击有效性超越基线且保持适配器实用性；测试的三种防御均无法完全防御。该研究直接表明后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，揭示了一种新的供应链攻击面，适配器可被轻易颠覆以绕过安全防护。

papers.title: Causal-Guided Detoxify Backdoor Attack of Open-Weight LoRA Models
papers.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as an efficient method for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) and is widely adopted within the open-source community. However, the decentralized dissemination of LoRA adapters through platforms such as Hugging Face introduces novel security vulnerabilities: malicious adapters can be easily distributed and evade conventional oversight mechanisms. Despite these risks, backdoor attacks targeting LoRA-based fine-tuning remain relatively underexplored. Existing backdoor attack strategies are ill-suited to this setting, as they often rely on inaccessible training data, fail to account for the structural properties unique to LoRA, or suffer from high false trigger rates (FTR), thereby compromising their stealth. To address these challenges, we propose Causal-Guided Detoxify Backdoor Attack (CBA), a novel backdoor attack framework specifically designed for open-weight LoRA models. CBA operates without access to original training data and achieves high stealth through two key innovations: (1) a coverage-guided data generation pipeline that synthesizes task-aligned inputs via behavioral exploration, and (2) a causal-guided detoxification strategy that merges poisoned and clean adapters by preserving task-critical neurons. Unlike prior approaches, CBA enables post-training control over attack intensity through causal influence-based weight allocation, eliminating the need for repeated retraining. Evaluated across six LoRA models, CBA achieves high attack success rates while reducing FTR by 50-70\% compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, it demonstrates enhanced resistance to state-of-the-art backdoor defenses, highlighting its stealth and robustness.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the underexplored threat of backdoor attacks on open-weight LoRA models, where existing methods suffer from high false trigger rates and impractical data requirements. It proposes CBA, a backdoor attack framework that synthesizes task-aligned inputs using coverage-guided behavioral exploration and merges poisoned and clean adapters via causal-guided detoxification to maintain stealth. Evaluated on six LoRA models, CBA achieves high attack success rates while reducing false trigger rates by 50-70% over baselines, and it resists state-of-the-art backdoor defenses. The work reveals a critical fragility in post-training safety alignment, showing that LoRA-based fine-tuning can be easily subverted with a data-free, stealthy attack, thereby challenging the robustness of aligned modules.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对开放权重LoRA模型中未充分探索的后门攻击威胁，现有方法因虚警率高和数据依赖而受限。提出CBA后门攻击框架，通过覆盖率引导的行为探索生成任务对齐输入，并利用因果引导的去毒策略融合中毒与干净适配器以保持隐蔽性。在六个LoRA模型上评估，CBA在实现高攻击成功率的同时将虚警率降低50-70%，并能抵抗先进后门防御。该研究揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，表明基于LoRA的微调容易被无数据、隐蔽的攻击颠覆，挑战了对齐模块的鲁棒性。

papers.title: Odysseus: Jailbreaking Commercial Multimodal LLM-integrated Systems via Dual Steganography
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs), which combine text with other modalities, such as images, have demonstrated powerful capabilities and are increasingly adopted in real-world commercial systems. However, their growing accessibility also raises concerns about misuse, such as generating harmful content. To mitigate these risks, alignment techniques are commonly applied to align model behavior with human values. Despite these efforts, recent studies have shown that jailbreak attacks can circumvent alignment and elicit unsafe outputs. Currently, most existing jailbreak methods are tailored for open-source models and exhibit limited effectiveness against commercial MLLM-integrated systems, which often employ additional filters. These filters can detect and prevent malicious input and output content, significantly reducing jailbreak threats. In this paper, we reveal that the success of these safety filters heavily relies on a critical assumption that malicious content must be explicitly visible in either the input or the output. This assumption, while often valid for traditional LLM-integrated systems, breaks down in MLLM-integrated systems, where attackers can leverage multiple modalities to conceal adversarial intent, leading to a false sense of security in existing MLLM-integrated systems. To challenge this assumption, we propose texttt{Odysseus}, a novel jailbreak paradigm that introduces dual steganography to covertly embed malicious queries and responses into benign-looking images. Our method proceeds through four stages: textbf{(1)} malicious query encoding, textbf{(2)} steganography embedding, textbf{(3)} model interaction, and textbf{(4)} response extraction. We first encode the adversary-specified malicious prompt into binary matrices and embed them into images using a steganography model. The modified image will be fed into the victim MLLM-integrated system. We encourage the victim MLLM-integrated system to implant the generated illegitimate content into a carrier image (via steganography), which will be used for attackers to decode the hidden response locally. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our texttt{Odysseus} successfully jailbreaks several pioneering and realistic MLLM-integrated systems, including GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-pro, Gemini-2.0-flash, and Grok-3, achieving up to 99% attack success rate. It exposes a fundamental blind spot in existing defenses, and calls for rethinking cross-modal security in MLLM-integrated systems.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses jailbreak attacks against commercial multimodal LLM-integrated systems, where safety filters assume visible malicious content, but multimodal channels enable concealment. It proposes Odysseus, a dual steganography method that embeds malicious prompts into images and extracts illicit responses hidden in carrier images, bypassing text-based filters. Evaluated on GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0, and Grok-3, it achieves up to 99% attack success rate, exposing a critical blind spot in current defenses. This provides strong evidence for the fragility of safety alignment, showing how cross-modal encoding can completely circumvent post-training safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对商用多模态大语言模型集成系统的越狱攻击，其安全过滤器假设恶意内容必须显式可见，但多模态通道允许隐藏攻击。它提出Odysseus双隐写方法，将恶意查询嵌入图像并从中提取隐藏的非法响应，绕过文本过滤器。在GPT-4o、Gemini-2.0和Grok-3上的实验取得高达99%的攻击成功率，揭示了现有防御的根本盲点。这有力证明了安全对齐的脆弱性，凸显跨模态编码完全规避了训练后的安全措施。

papers.title: DUALBREACH: Efficient Dual-Jailbreaking via Target-Driven Initialization and Multi-Target Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent research has focused on exploring the vulnerabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), aiming to elicit harmful and/or sensitive content from LLMs. However, due to the insufficient research on dual-jailbreaking—attacks targeting both LLMs and Guardrails, the effectiveness of existing attacks is limited when attempting to bypass safety-aligned LLMs shielded by guardrails. Therefore, in this paper, we propose DUALBREACH, a target-driven framework for dual-jailbreaking. DUALBREACH employs a Target-driven Initialization (TDI) strategy to dynamically construct initial prompts, combined with a Multi-Target Optimization (MTO) method that utilizes approximate gradients to jointly adapt the prompts across guardrails and LLMs, which can simultaneously save the number of queries and achieve a high dual-jailbreaking success rate. For black-box guardrails, DUALBREACH either employs a powerful open-sourced guardrail or imitates the target black-box guardrail by training a proxy model, to incorporate guardrails into the MTO process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DUALBREACH in dual-jailbreaking scenarios through extensive evaluation on several widely-used datasets. Experimental results indicate that DUALBREACH outperforms state-of-the-art methods with fewer queries, achieving significantly higher success rates across all settings. More specifically, DUALBREACH achieves an average dual-jailbreaking success rate of 93.67% against GPT-4 with LlamaGuard-3 protection, whereas the best success rate achieved by other methods is 88.33%. Moreover, DUALBREACH only uses an average of 1.77 queries per successful dual-jailbreak, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. For defense, we propose an XGBoost-based ensemble defensive mechanism named EGUARD, which integrates the strengths of multiple guardrails, demonstrating superior performance compared with Llama-Guard-3.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of dual-jailbreaking, where an attacker must simultaneously bypass a safety-aligned large language model (LLM) and an external guardrail to elicit harmful content. It proposes DUALBREACH, a framework that uses Target-driven Initialization (TDI) to dynamically construct initial prompts and Multi-Target Optimization (MTO) with approximate gradients to jointly adapt prompts against both the LLM and guardrail, reducing query count. Extensive experiments show that DUALBREACH achieves a 93.67% average dual-jailbreaking success rate against GPT-4 protected by LlamaGuard-3, outperforming state-of-the-art methods (88.33%) while using only 1.77 queries per success; a defense ensemble, EGUARD, is also proposed. These results demonstrate that even layered safety mechanisms can be efficiently compromised, highlighting the fragility of post-training safety alignment against adaptive attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了双重越狱问题，即攻击者需同时绕过安全对齐的大语言模型（LLM）和外部护栏以生成有害内容。它提出DUALBREACH框架，利用目标驱动初始化（TDI）动态构建初始提示，并结合使用近似梯度的多目标优化（MTO）联合调整提示以对抗LLM和护栏，减少查询次数。大量实验表明，DUALBREACH对受LlamaGuard-3保护的GPT-4实现了93.67%的平均双重越狱成功率，优于现有最优方法（88.33%），且每次成功仅需1.77次查询；该文还提出了集成防御EGUARD。这些结果证明，即便是分层安全机制也能被高效攻破，凸显了后训练安全对齐在面对自适应攻击时的脆弱性。

papers.title: Towards Understanding Unsafe Video Generation
papers.short_title: Unsafe Video Gen and sysname Defense
papers.abstract:
Video generation models (VGMs) have demonstrated the capability to synthesize high-quality output. It is important to understand their potential to produce unsafe content, such as violent or terrifying videos. In this work, we provide a comprehensive understanding of unsafe video generation. First, to confirm the possibility that these models could indeed generate unsafe videos, we choose unsafe content generation prompts collected from 4chan and Lexica, and three open-source SOTA VGMs to generate unsafe videos.
After filtering out duplicates and poorly generated content, we created an initial set of $2112$ unsafe videos from an original pool of $5607$ videos. Through clustering and thematic coding analysis of these generated videos, we identify $5$ unsafe video categories: textit{Distorted/Weird}, textit{Terrifying}, textit{Pornographic}, textit{Violent/Bloody}, and textit{Political}. With IRB approval, we then recruit online participants to help label the generated videos. Based on the annotations submitted by $403$ participants, we identified $937$ unsafe videos from the initial video set. With the labeled information and the corresponding prompts, we created the first dataset of unsafe videos generated by VGMs. We then study possible defense mechanisms to prevent the generation of unsafe videos. Existing defense methods in image generation focus on filtering either input prompt or output results. We propose a new approach called fullsysname (sysname), which works within the model’s internal sampling process. sysname can achieve $0.90$ defense accuracy while reducing time and computing resources by $10times$ when sampling a large number of unsafe prompts. Our experiment includes three open-source SOTA video diffusion models, each achieving accuracy rates of $0.99$, $0.92$, and $0.91$, respectively. Additionally, our method was tested with adversarial prompts and on image-to-video diffusion models, and achieved nearly $1.0$ accuracy on both settings. Our method also shows its interoperability by improving the performance of other defenses when combined with them.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses unsafe content generation in video generation models, such as violent or pornographic videos. The authors propose sysname, a defense mechanism that operates within the model's internal sampling process to block unsafe outputs efficiently. They create an annotated dataset of unsafe videos from three open-source models and demonstrate that sysname achieves up to 0.99 defense accuracy with a 10x reduction in time and computation, also proving effective against adversarial prompts and image-to-video models. While advancing safety for video generation, this work does not directly investigate the robustness of post-training safety alignment; it introduces a practical defense layer that complements existing alignment approaches.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对视频生成模型产生不安全内容（如暴力、恐怖、情色视频）的问题进行研究。作者提出了一种名为sysname的防御机制，通过在模型内部采样过程中进行干预来高效阻止不安全内容的生成。他们从三个开源模型收集并标注了不安全视频数据集，实验表明sysname最高可实现0.99的防御准确率，同时将时间和计算开销减少10倍，并对抗性提示词和图像到视频模型同样有效。虽然这项工作增强了视频生成的安全性，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性；它提供了一种可与其他对齐方法结合的实用防御层。

papers.title: Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models
papers.short_title: Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models
papers.abstract:
The safety alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is crucial to prevent unsafe content that violates human values.
To ensure this, it is essential to evaluate the robustness of their alignment against diverse malicious attacks.
However, the lack of a large-scale, unified measurement framework hinders a comprehensive understanding of potential vulnerabilities.
To fill this gap, this paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of existing and newly proposed safety misalignment methods for LLMs. Specifically, we investigate four research questions: (1) evaluating the robustness of LLMs with different alignment strategies, (2) identifying the most effective misalignment method, (3) determining key factors that influence misalignment effectiveness, and (4) exploring various defenses.
The safety misalignment attacks in our paper include system-prompt modification, model fine-tuning, and model editing.
Our findings show that Supervised Fine-Tuning is the most potent attack but requires harmful model responses.
In contrast, our novel Self-Supervised Representation Attack (SSRA) achieves significant misalignment without harmful responses.
We also examine defensive mechanisms such as safety data filter, model detoxification, and our proposed Self-Supervised Representation Defense (SSRD), demonstrating that SSRD can effectively re-align the model.
In conclusion, our unified safety alignment evaluation framework empirically highlights the fragility of the safety alignment of LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of safety misalignment attacks against large language models (LLMs), using a unified framework to assess robustness. It systematically compares system-prompt modification, model fine-tuning, and model editing, and introduces a novel Self-Supervised Representation Attack (SSRA) that effectively breaks alignment without needing harmful training data. Experiments show that supervised fine-tuning is the most potent attack, while SSRA also achieves significant misalignment; a corresponding defense, Self-Supervised Representation Defense (SSRD), can successfully re-align models. The work empirically demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as multiple attack vectors easily bypass it, though defenses like SSRD offer partial mitigation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文首次对针对大语言模型的安全误对齐攻击进行了全面评估，通过统一的框架系统比较了系统提示修改、模型微调和模型编辑等方法，并提出了一种无需有害训练数据的自监督表示攻击（SSRA），能够有效破坏安全对齐。实验表明，监督微调是最强的攻击方式，而SSRA也可实现显著误对齐；本研究同时引入了自监督表示防御（SSRD）来重新对齐模型。该研究实证了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，多种攻击均可轻易绕过，但SSRD等防御手段可部分缓解风险。

papers.title: A Causal Perspective for Enhancing Jailbreak Attack and Defense
papers.abstract:
Uncovering the mechanisms behind "jailbreaks" in large language models (LLMs) is crucial for enhancing their safety and reliability, yet these mechanisms remain poorly understood.
Existing studies predominantly analyze jailbreak prompts by probing latent representations, often overlooking the causal relationships between interpretable prompt features and jailbreak occurrences. In this work, we propose textbf{Causal Analyst}, a framework that integrates LLMs into data-driven causal discovery to identify the direct causes of jailbreaks and leverage them for both attack and defense. We introduce a comprehensive dataset comprising 35k jailbreak attempts across seven LLMs, systematically constructed from 100 attack templates and 50 harmful queries, annotated with 37 meticulously designed human-readable prompt features.
By jointly training LLM-based prompt encoding and GNN-based causal graph learning, we reconstruct causal pathways linking prompt features to jailbreak responses. Our analysis reveals that specific features, such as "Positive Character" and "Number of Task Steps", act as direct causal drivers of jailbreaks. We demonstrate the practical utility of these insights through two applications: (1) a textbf{Jailbreaking Enhancer} that targets identified causal features to significantly boost attack success rates on public benchmarks, and (2) a textbf{Guardrail Advisor} that utilizes the learned causal graph to extract true malicious intent from obfuscated queries.
Extensive experiments, including baseline comparisons and causal structure validation, confirm the robustness of our causal analysis and its superiority over non-causal approaches.
Our results suggest that analyzing jailbreak features from a causal perspective is an effective and interpretable approach for improving LLM reliability. Our code is available at https://github.com/Master-PLC/Causal-Analyst.
papers.summary_en: This work addresses the mechanistic understanding of jailbreaks in LLMs, which is crucial for safety but poorly understood. It proposes Causal Analyst, a framework that uses data-driven causal discovery with LLMs and GNNs to identify direct causal drivers among interpretable prompt features. Evaluated on a new dataset of 35k jailbreak attempts across 7 LLMs with 37 human-readable features, it reveals features like "Positive Character" and "Number of Task Steps" as causal drivers, and demonstrates practical attack and defense enhancements that outperform non-causal methods. By showing that specific prompt features causally cause jailbreaks, the paper provides evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed through feature manipulation.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型越狱机制的理解问题，现有方法多忽略提示特征与越狱的因果关系。提出Causal Analyst框架，利用LLM和GNN进行数据驱动的因果发现，从可解释提示特征中识别直接因果因素。基于覆盖7个LLM的35k次越狱尝试数据集和37个人工特征，发现“正面角色”和“任务步骤数”等特征是因果驱动因素，并开发了攻击增强器和防护顾问，实验表明其优于非因果方法。论文揭示了特定提示特征可因果导致越狱，证明了后训练安全对齐存在脆弱性，易被特征操控绕过。

papers.title: NeuroStrike: Neuron-Level Attacks on Aligned LLMs
papers.abstract: Safety alignment is critical for the ethical deployment of large language models (LLMs), guiding them to avoid generating harmful or unethical content. Current alignment techniques, such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback, remain fragile and can be bypassed by carefully crafted adversarial prompts. Unfortunately, such attacks rely on trial and error, lack generalizability across models, and are constrained by scalability and reliability. This paper presents NeuroStrike, a novel and generalizable attack framework that exploits a fundamental vulnerability introduced by alignment techniques: the reliance on sparse, specialized safety neurons responsible for detecting and suppressing harmful inputs. We apply NeuroStrike to both white-box and black-box settings: In the white-box setting, NeuroStrike identifies safety neurons through feedforward activation analysis and prunes them during inference to disable safety mechanisms. In the black-box setting, we propose the first LLM profiling attack, which leverages safety neuron transferability by training adversarial prompt generators on open-weight surrogate models and then deploying them against black-box and proprietary targets. We evaluate NeuroStrike on over 20 open-weight LLMs from major LLM developers. By removing less than 0.6% of neurons in targeted layers, NeuroStrike achieves an average attack success rate (ASR) of 76.9% using only vanilla malicious prompts. Moreover, Neurostrike generalizes to four multimodal LLMs with 100% ASR on unsafe image inputs. Safety neurons transfer effectively across architectures, raising ASR to 78.5% on 11 fine-tuned models and 77.7% on five distilled models. The black-box LLM profiling attack achieves an average ASR of 63.7% across five black-box models, including Google’s Gemini family.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the fragility of safety alignment in LLMs, where adversarial prompts can bypass safeguards but current attacks lack generalizability and scalability. It proposes NeuroStrike, a neuron-level attack that exploits sparse safety neurons by pruning them in white-box settings or using a black-box profiling attack that transfers adversarial prompts from surrogate models. Evaluated on over 20 open-weight and black-box LLMs, NeuroStrike achieves average ASR of 76.9% with minimal neuron removal and 63.7% on proprietary models like Gemini, including 100% ASR on multimodal inputs. This work provides direct evidence that alignment is built on fragile, localized mechanisms that can be easily and precisely broken, reinforcing the central thesis that post-training safety alignment is not robust.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文关注LLM安全对齐的脆弱性，现有攻击受限。它提出NeuroStrike攻击框架，通过剪除稀疏安全神经元（白盒）或基于神经元可迁移性的黑盒探测攻击。在20+模型上，移除不足0.6%神经元即达到76.9%攻击成功率，黑盒攻击达63.7%，多模态模型达100%。这项工作直接表明安全对齐依赖的机制脆弱且易被精准破坏，有力支撑了后训练安全对齐并非鲁棒的论点。

papers.title: Q-MLLM: Vector Quantization for Robust Multimodal Large Language Model Security
papers.short_title: Q-MLLM: VQ for Robust MLLM Security
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in cross-modal understanding, but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks through visual inputs despite robust textual safety mechanisms. These vulnerabilities arise from two core weaknesses: the continuous nature of visual representations, which allows for gradient-based attacks, and the inadequate transfer of text-based safety mechanisms to visual content. We introduce Q-MLLM, a novel architecture that integrates two-level vector quantization to create a discrete bottleneck against adversarial attacks while preserving multimodal reasoning capabilities. By discretizing visual representations at both pixel-patch and semantic levels, Q-MLLM blocks attack pathways and bridges the cross-modal safety alignment gap. Our two-stage training methodology ensures robust learning while maintaining model utility. Experiments demonstrate that Q-MLLM achieves significantly better defense success rate against both jailbreak attacks and toxic image attacks than existing approaches. Notably, Q-MLLM achieves perfect defense success rate (100%) against jailbreak attacks except in one arguable case, while maintaining competitive performance on multiple utility benchmarks with minimal inference overhead.
