This work establishes vector quantization as an effective defense mechanism for secure multimodal AI systems without requiring expensive safety-specific fine-tuning or detection overhead.
papers.summary_en: It addresses the vulnerability of Multimodal LLMs to adversarial visual attacks due to continuous representations and poor cross-modal safety transfer. The paper proposes Q-MLLM, which uses two-level vector quantization (pixel-patch and semantic) to create discrete bottlenecks, blocking attack pathways. Experiments show Q-MLLM achieves 100% defense success against jailbreak attacks (except one arguable case) and competitive utility with minimal overhead. This hardening method directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment in multimodal models, demonstrating that discretization robustly blocks vision-based attacks without expensive retraining.
papers.summary_zh: 该工作针对多模态大语言模型因连续视觉表示及跨模态安全迁移不足而易受视觉对抗攻击的问题。提出Q-MLLM方法，通过像素块和语义两级向量量化构建离散瓶颈，阻断攻击路径。实验表明，Q-MLLM对越狱攻击实现近乎完美防御（仅一例争议），并保持多基准实用性，推理开销极小。该方法直面后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，证明离散化可有效且低成本地抵御视觉对抗攻击。

papers.title: Benchmarking and Understanding Safety Risks in AI Character Platforms
papers.short_title: Safety Risks in AI Character Platforms
papers.abstract: AI character platforms, which allow users to engage in conversations with AI personas, are a rapidly growing application domain. However, their immersive and personalized nature, combined with technical vulnerabilities, raises significant safety concerns. Despite their popularity, a systematic evaluation of their safety has been notably absent. To address this gap, we conduct the first large-scale safety study of AI character platforms, evaluating 16 popular platforms using a benchmark set of 5,000 questions across 16 safety categories. Our findings reveal a critical safety deficit: AI character platforms exhibit an average unsafe response rate of 65.1%, substantially higher than the 17.7% average rate of the baselines. We further discover that safety performance varies significantly across different characters and is strongly correlated with character features such as demographics and personality. Leveraging these insights, we demonstrate that our machine learning model is able identify less safe characters with an F1-score of 0.81. This predictive capability can be beneficial for platforms, enabling improved mechanisms for safer interactions, character search/recommendations, and character creation. Overall, the results and findings offer valuable insights for enhancing platform governance and content moderation for safer AI character platforms.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety risks of AI character platforms, where user interactions with AI personas can bypass alignment. It proposes a systematic benchmark with 5,000 questions across 16 safety categories on 16 platforms, and analyzes character-level safety correlations. Evaluations reveal a 65.1% unsafe response rate, far exceeding baseline LLMs, and a predictive model identifies unsafe characters with 0.81 F1. This study demonstrates that post-training safety alignment can be fragile in real-world deployments, as character configurations and platform designs can inadvertently undermine safety, supporting the SoK's inquiry into alignment robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究AI角色平台的安全风险，用户与AI人格交互可能会绕过安全对齐。提出系统性基准测试，涵盖16个平台、5000个问题及16个安全类别，分析角色层面的安全性关联。评估发现不安全回复率达65.1%，远超基线LLM，且基于角色特征模型能以0.81 F1识别低安全角色。该研究表明，训练后安全对齐在实际部署中可能脆弱，角色配置和平台设计会无意中破坏安全性，印证了SoK中对齐鲁棒性的质疑。

papers.title: Bleeding Pathways: Vanishing Discriminability in LLM Hidden States Fuels Jailbreak Attacks
papers.abstract: LLMs remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that exploit adversarial prompts to circumvent safety measures. Current safety fine-tuning approaches face two critical limitations. First, they often fail to strike a balance between security and utility, where stronger safety measures tend to over-reject harmless user requests. Second, they frequently miss malicious intent concealed within seemingly benign tasks, leaving models exposed to exploitation. Our work identifies a fundamental cause of these issues: during response generation, an LLM's capacity to differentiate harmful from safe outputs deteriorates. Experimental evidence confirms this, revealing that the separability between hidden states for safe and harmful responses diminishes as generation progresses. This weakening discrimination forces models to make compliance judgments earlier in the generation process, restricting their ability to recognize developing harmful intent and contributing to both aforementioned failures. To mitigate this vulnerability, we introduce DEEPALIGN - an inherent defense framework that enhances the safety of LLMs. By applying contrastive hidden-state steering at the midpoint of response generation, DEEPALIGN amplifies the separation between harmful and benign hidden states, enabling continuous intrinsic toxicity detection and intervention throughout the generation process. Across diverse LLMs spanning varying architectures and scales, it reduced attack success rates of nine distinct jailbreak attacks to near-zero or minimal. Crucially, it preserved model capability while reducing over-refusal. Models equipped with DEEPALIGN exhibited up to 3.5% lower error rates in rejecting challenging benign queries and maintained standard task performance with less than 1% decline. This marks a substantial advance in the safety-utility Pareto frontier.
papers.summary_en: This paper identifies a mechanistic weakness in LLM safety: the discriminability between safe and harmful hidden states degrades during response generation, enabling jailbreak attacks. It proposes DEEPALIGN, a defense that applies contrastive hidden-state steering at the generation midpoint to amplify separation and enable continuous toxicity detection. Evaluated across diverse LLMs and nine jailbreak attacks, DEEPALIGN reduces attack success rates to near-zero while preserving utility, reducing over-refusal by up to 3.5% on benign queries and maintaining task performance within 1%. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by uncovering a core vulnerability and demonstrating a hardening method that significantly improves robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了LLM安全机制的一个根本缺陷：随着生成过程推进，安全与有害隐藏状态的可区分性逐渐消失，从而导致越狱攻击得逞。为此提出DEEPALIGN防御框架，在生成中点进行对比式隐藏状态操控，增强有害与良性状态的分离，实现持续的毒性检测与干预。在多种LLM上九类越狱攻击的测试表明，DEEPALIGN将攻击成功率降至接近零，同时保持模型效用，对良性查询的过度拒绝降低最高3.5%，任务性能下降不足1%。该研究直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题，从机制层面发现漏洞并提供加固方法，显著提升了鲁棒性。

papers.title: Discovering Preference Optimization Algorithms with and for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Offline preference optimization is a key method for enhancing and controlling the quality of Large Language Model (LLM) outputs. Typically, preference optimization is approached as an offline supervised learning task using manually-crafted convex loss functions. While these methods are based on theoretical insights, they are inherently constrained by human creativity, so the large search space of possible loss functions remains under explored. We address this by performing LLM-driven objective discovery to automatically discover new state-of-the-art preference optimization algorithms without (expert) human intervention. Specifically, we iteratively prompt an LLM to propose and implement new preference optimization loss functions based on previously-evaluated performance metrics. This process leads to the discovery of previously-unknown and performant preference optimization algorithms. The best performing of these we call Discovered Preference Optimization (DiscoPOP), a novel algorithm that adaptively blends logistic and exponential losses. Experiments demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of DiscoPOP and its successful transfer to held-out tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limited exploration of loss functions for offline preference optimization in LLMs, which is traditionally constrained by human-designed convex functions. It proposes an automated approach using an LLM to iteratively propose and evaluate new loss functions, leading to the discovery of a novel algorithm called DiscoPOP that adaptively blends logistic and exponential losses. Experiments demonstrate that DiscoPOP achieves state-of-the-art performance on preference optimization tasks and transfers successfully to held-out tasks. This work advances alignment methodology by automating the discovery of better optimization techniques, but it does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型离线偏好优化中损失函数探索受限的问题，传统方法依赖人工设计的凸函数。提出了一种基于大语言模型的自动发现方法，通过迭代提议和评估新损失函数，发现了一种新颖的自适应混合逻辑与指数损失的算法DiscoPOP。实验表明，DiscoPOP在偏好优化任务上达到最先进性能，并能成功迁移到留出任务。该工作通过自动发现更优优化技术推动了对齐方法学发展，但未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated into many applications (e.g., web agents) to perform more sophisticated tasks. However, LLM-empowered applications are vulnerable to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks, where instructions are injected via untrustworthy external data sources. This paper presents Rennervate, a defense framework to detect and prevent IPI attacks. Rennervate leverages attention features to detect the covert injection at a fine-grained token level, enabling precise sanitization that neutralizes IPI attacks while maintaining LLM functionalities. Specifically, the token-level detector is materialized with a 2-step attentive pooling mechanism, which aggregates attention heads and response tokens for IPI detection and sanitization. Moreover, we establish a fine-grained IPI dataset, FIPI, to be open-sourced to support further research. Extensive experiments verify that Rennervate outperforms 15 commercial and academic IPI defense methods, achieving high precision on 5 LLMs and 6 datasets. We also demonstrate that Rennervate is transferable to unseen attacks and robust against adaptive adversaries.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM-integrated applications to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks, where malicious instructions are hidden in external data. It proposes Rennervate, a defense framework that uses attention features for token-level detection and sanitization via a 2-step attentive pooling mechanism. Evaluated on the newly created FIPI dataset, Rennervate outperforms 15 existing defense methods across 5 LLMs and 6 datasets, and shows transferability to unseen attacks and robustness against adaptive adversaries. This paper advances defense methodology for LLM applications but does not directly examine the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对集成LLM的应用易受间接提示注入（IPI）攻击的问题，提出了一种防御框架Rennervate，通过注意力特征实现细粒度令牌级检测与净化，采用两步注意力池化机制。在新建的FIPI数据集上，Rennervate在5个LLM和6个数据集上优于15种现有防御方法，并展现出对未知攻击的迁移性和对自适应对抗的鲁棒性。该研究推进了LLM应用的防御技术，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性本质。

papers.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a widely used offline preference optimization algorithm that reparameterizes reward functions in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to enhance simplicity and training stability. In this work, we propose SimPO, a simpler yet more effective approach. The effectiveness of SimPO is attributed to a key design: using the average log probability of a sequence as the implicit reward. This reward formulation better aligns with model generation and eliminates the need for a reference model, making it more compute and memory efficient. Additionally, we introduce a target reward margin to the Bradley-Terry objective to encourage a larger margin between the winning and losing responses, further improving the algorithm's performance. We compare SimPO to DPO and its latest variants across various state-of-the-art training setups, including both base and instruction-tuned models such as Mistral, Llama 3, and Gemma 2. We evaluate on extensive chat-based evaluation benchmarks, including AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench, and Arena-Hard. Our results demonstrate that SimPO consistently and significantly outperforms existing approaches without substantially increasing response length. Specifically, SimPO outperforms DPO by up to 6.4 points on AlpacaEval 2 and by up to 7.5 points on Arena-Hard. Our top-performing model, built on Gemma-2-9B-it, achieves a 72.4% length-controlled win rate on AlpacaEval 2, a 59.1% win rate on Arena-Hard, and ranks 1st on Chatbot Arena among<10B models with real user votes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of offline preference optimization for aligning large language models, proposing a simpler alternative to Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). SimPO uses the average log probability of a sequence as an implicit reward, eliminating the need for a reference model and improving computational efficiency, while introducing a target reward margin to the Bradley-Terry objective to widen the gap between preferred and dispreferred responses. Evaluated across models like Mistral, Llama 3, and Gemma 2 on benchmarks such as AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench, and Arena-Hard, SimPO consistently outperforms DPO and its variants, achieving up to 6.4-point and 7.5-point gains on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard, respectively. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐中离线偏好优化问题，提出了比直接偏好优化（DPO）更简单的方法SimPO。SimPO以序列平均对数概率作为隐式奖励，省去参考模型以提升计算和内存效率，并在Bradley-Terry目标中引入目标奖励边际以扩大胜败响应的差距。在Mistral、Llama 3、Gemma 2等模型及AlpacaEval 2、MT-Bench、Arena-Hard等基准上评估，SimPO显著优于DPO及其变体，在AlpacaEval 2和Arena-Hard上分别最高提升6.4和7.5个百分点。本研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
papers.abstract: Large language models trained for safety and harmlessness remain susceptible to adversarial misuse, as evidenced by the prevalence of"jailbreak"attacks on early releases of ChatGPT that elicit undesired behavior. Going beyond recognition of the issue, we investigate why such attacks succeed and how they can be created. We hypothesize two failure modes of safety training: competing objectives and mismatched generalization. Competing objectives arise when a model's capabilities and safety goals conflict, while mismatched generalization occurs when safety training fails to generalize to a domain for which capabilities exist. We use these failure modes to guide jailbreak design and then evaluate state-of-the-art models, including OpenAI's GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude v1.3, against both existing and newly designed attacks. We find that vulnerabilities persist despite the extensive red-teaming and safety-training efforts behind these models. Notably, new attacks utilizing our failure modes succeed on every prompt in a collection of unsafe requests from the models' red-teaming evaluation sets and outperform existing ad hoc jailbreaks. Our analysis emphasizes the need for safety-capability parity -- that safety mechanisms should be as sophisticated as the underlying model -- and argues against the idea that scaling alone can resolve these safety failure modes.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses why jailbreak attacks succeed against safety-trained LLMs, hypothesizing two failure modes: competing objectives and mismatched generalization. It proposes a design framework based on these failure modes to create new jailbreak attacks that exploit the tension between capabilities and safety goals or domains where safety fails to generalize. Evaluated on GPT-4 and Claude v1.3, these attacks achieved 100% success on all prompts from the models' red-teaming evaluation sets, outperforming existing jailbreaks. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that it can be systematically bypassed through fundamental weaknesses, reinforcing the need for safety-capability parity.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了为什么针对安全训练的大型语言模型的“越狱”攻击能够成功，并提出两种失效模式：目标冲突和泛化错配。作者基于这些失效模式设计新型越狱攻击框架，利用模型能力与安全目标之间的冲突或安全训练未能泛化的领域。在GPT-4和Claude v1.3上的评估显示，这些攻击在红队测试集的所有不安全提示上均成功，且优于现有特设越狱方法。该研究直接揭示了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，表明对齐可通过根本性弱点被系统性绕过，强调安全机制必须与模型能力相匹配，仅靠扩大规模无法解决。

papers.title: A Theoretical Understanding of Self-Correction through In-context Alignment
papers.abstract: Going beyond mimicking limited human experiences, recent studies show initial evidence that, like humans, large language models (LLMs) are capable of improving their abilities purely by self-correction, i.e., correcting previous responses through self-examination, in certain circumstances. Nevertheless, little is known about how such capabilities arise. In this work, based on a simplified setup akin to an alignment task, we theoretically analyze self-correction from an in-context learning perspective, showing that when LLMs give relatively accurate self-examinations as rewards, they are capable of refining responses in an in-context way. Notably, going beyond previous theories on over-simplified linear transformers, our theoretical construction underpins the roles of several key designs of realistic transformers for self-correction: softmax attention, multi-head attention, and the MLP block. We validate these findings extensively on synthetic datasets. Inspired by these findings, we also illustrate novel applications of self-correction, such as defending against LLM jailbreaks, where a simple self-correction step does make a large difference. We believe that these findings will inspire further research on understanding, exploiting, and enhancing self-correction for building better foundation models.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how LLMs can self-correct responses without external feedback. It provides a theoretical analysis framing self-correction as in-context alignment, where relatively accurate self-examinations act as rewards to refine responses, and emphasizes the necessity of softmax attention, multi-head attention, and MLP blocks in realistic transformers. Synthetic experiments validate the theory, and a practical application shows that a simple self-correction step significantly defends against jailbreaks. While advancing alignment methodology, this work does not directly address whether post-training safety alignment is inherently fragile, though the jailbreak defense suggests a hardening approach.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了大语言模型如何在没有外部反馈的情况下自我纠正响应。它将自我纠正理论化为上下文内对齐，其中相对准确的自我检查作为奖励来细化响应，并强调了软注意力、多头注意力和MLP块在现实Transformer中的关键作用。合成实验验证了理论，并展示了简单的自我纠正步骤能有效防御越狱攻击的实用应用。尽管该工作推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否本质上脆弱，不过越狱防御暗示了一种加固方向。

papers.title: Is RLHF More Difficult than Standard RL? A Theoretical Perspective
papers.short_title: RLHF vs Standard RL: Theoretical Analysis
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) learns from preference signals, while standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) directly learns from reward signals. Preferences arguably contain less information than rewards, which makes preference-based RL seemingly more difficult. This paper theoretically proves that, for a wide range of preference models, we can solve preference-based RL directly using existing algorithms and techniques for reward-based RL, with small or no extra costs. Specifically, (1) for preferences that are drawn from reward-based probabilistic models, we reduce the problem to robust reward-based RL that can tolerate small errors in rewards; (2) for general arbitrary preferences where the objective is to find the von Neumann winner, we reduce the problem to multiagent reward-based RL which finds Nash equilibria for factored Markov games under a restricted set of policies. The latter case can be further reduce to adversarial MDP when preferences only depend on the final state. We instantiate all reward-based RL subroutines by concrete provable algorithms, and apply our theory to a large class of models including tabular MDPs and MDPs with generic function approximation. We further provide guarantees when K-wise comparisons are available.
papers.summary_en: This paper theoretically investigates whether RLHF is inherently more difficult than standard RL. It reduces preference-based RL to reward-based RL subproblems: robust reward-based RL for probabilistic preferences and multiagent reward-based RL for general preferences. The authors provide provable algorithms and guarantees for various MDP settings. This paper advances theoretical understanding of RLHF but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文从理论上研究了RLHF是否本质上比标准RL更困难。它将基于偏好的RL归约为基于奖励的RL子问题：对概率偏好使用鲁棒奖励RL，对一般偏好使用多智能体奖励RL。作者为各类MDP设置提供了可证明的算法和保证。该研究推进了对RLHF的理论理解，但未直接涉及训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Alignment for Honesty
papers.abstract: Recent research has made significant strides in aligning large language models (LLMs) with helpfulness and harmlessness. In this paper, we argue for the importance of alignment for \emph{honesty}, ensuring that LLMs proactively refuse to answer questions when they lack knowledge, while still not being overly conservative. However, a pivotal aspect of alignment for honesty involves discerning an LLM's knowledge boundaries, which demands comprehensive solutions in terms of metric development, benchmark creation, and training methodologies. We address these challenges by first establishing a precise problem definition and defining ``honesty'' inspired by the Analects of Confucius. This serves as a cornerstone for developing metrics that effectively measure an LLM's honesty by quantifying its progress post-alignment. Furthermore, we introduce a flexible training framework which is further instantiated by several efficient fine-tuning techniques that emphasize honesty without sacrificing performance on other tasks. Our extensive experiments reveal that these aligned models show a marked increase in honesty, as indicated by our proposed metrics. We open-source all relevant resources to facilitate future research at \url{https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/alignment-for-honesty}.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies that current LLM alignment focuses on helpfulness and harmlessness but neglects honesty, requiring models to refuse when they lack knowledge without being overly conservative. It proposes a precise definition of honesty, develops evaluation metrics, and introduces a flexible training framework with efficient fine-tuning techniques that emphasize honesty while preserving task performance. Experiments demonstrate that these aligned models show significant improvements in honesty as measured by the proposed metrics. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address whether such alignment is robust or fragile against adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出当前大语言模型对齐主要关注有用性和无害性，而忽视了诚实性，即模型应在缺乏知识时主动拒绝回答，但又不过于保守。它提出了诚实的精确定义，开发了评估指标，并引入了一个灵活的训练框架，通过高效微调技术在强调诚实时不牺牲其他任务表现。实验表明，对齐后的模型在提出的诚实指标上显著提升。这项工作推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨该对齐是否稳健或易受对抗攻击破坏。

papers.title: The Importance of Online Data: Understanding Preference Fine-tuning via Coverage
papers.abstract: Learning from human preference data has emerged as the dominant paradigm for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs). The two most common families of techniques -- online reinforcement learning (RL) such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and offline contrastive methods such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) -- were positioned as equivalent in prior work due to the fact that both have to start from the same offline preference dataset. To further expand our theoretical understanding of the similarities and differences between online and offline techniques for preference fine-tuning, we conduct a rigorous analysis through the lens of dataset coverage, a concept that captures how the training data covers the test distribution and is widely used in RL. We prove that a global coverage condition is both necessary and sufficient for offline contrastive methods to converge to the optimal policy, but a weaker partial coverage condition suffices for online RL methods. This separation provides one explanation of why online RL methods can perform better than offline methods, especially when the offline preference data is not diverse enough. Finally, motivated by our preceding theoretical observations, we derive a hybrid preference optimization (HyPO) algorithm that uses offline data for contrastive-based preference optimization and online unlabeled data for KL regularization. Theoretically and empirically, we demonstrate that HyPO is more performant than its pure offline counterpart DPO, while still preserving its computation and memory efficiency.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the theoretical understanding of online RL versus offline contrastive methods for preference fine-tuning of LLMs. It introduces a coverage-based analysis, proving that offline methods like DPO require global coverage to converge to the optimal policy, while online methods like PPO only need partial coverage. The authors propose HyPO, a hybrid algorithm that uses offline data for contrastive optimization and online unlabeled data for KL regularization, and demonstrate its superiority over DPO both theoretically and empirically. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型偏好微调中在线强化学习与离线对比方法的理论理解问题。通过数据集覆盖度的严格分析，证明离线方法（如DPO）需要全局覆盖才能收敛至最优策略，而在线方法（如PPO）仅需部分覆盖。作者提出混合算法HyPO，将离线数据用于对比偏好优化，在线无标签数据用于KL正则化，从理论与实验上均证明其优于纯离线方法DPO。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Accelerating Greedy Coordinate Gradient and General Prompt Optimization via Probe Sampling
papers.abstract: Safety of Large Language Models (LLMs) has become a central issue given their rapid progress and wide applications. Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) is shown to be effective in constructing prompts containing adversarial suffixes to break the presumingly safe LLMs, but the optimization of GCG is time-consuming and limits its practicality. To reduce the time cost of GCG and enable more comprehensive studies of LLM safety, in this work, we study a new algorithm called $\texttt{Probe sampling}$ to accelerate the GCG algorithm. At the core of the algorithm is a mechanism that dynamically determines how similar a smaller draft model's predictions are to the target model's predictions for prompt candidates. When the target model is similar to the draft model, we rely heavily on the draft model to filter out a large number of potential prompt candidates to reduce the computation time. Probe sampling achieves up to $5.6$ times speedup using Llama2-7b-chat and leads to equal or improved attack success rate (ASR) on the AdvBench. Furthermore, probe sampling is also able to accelerate other prompt optimization techniques and adversarial attack methods, leading to acceleration of $1.8\times$ for AutoPrompt, $2.4\times$ for APE and $2.4\times$ for AutoDAN.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the time-intensive nature of Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) for generating adversarial suffixes to jailbreak LLMs. It proposes Probe Sampling, which dynamically uses a smaller draft model to filter candidate suffixes when its predictions align with the target model, reducing computation. Evaluated on Llama2-7b-chat and AdvBench, Probe Sampling achieves up to a 5.6× speedup with equal or improved attack success rate, and also accelerates AutoPrompt (1.8×), APE (2.4×), and AutoDAN (2.4×). This work enhances adversarial testing efficiency, enabling more comprehensive safety evaluations and indirectly illuminating the fragility of post-training safety alignment by facilitating probing and bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) 在生成对抗后缀以越狱大语言模型时计算开销大的问题。提出Probe Sampling方法，通过动态判断小型草稿模型与目标模型预测的相似性，当两者相似时大幅依赖草稿模型过滤候选后缀以降低计算量。在Llama2-7b-chat和AdvBench上评估，该方法实现最高5.6倍加速，且攻击成功率保持或提升，同时可分别将AutoPrompt、APE和AutoDAN加速1.8倍、2.4倍和2.4倍。该工作提升了对抗性测试的效率，有助于更全面地评估安全对齐的鲁棒性，间接揭示了后训练安全对齐可能存在的脆弱性。

papers.title: DICES Dataset: Diversity in Conversational AI Evaluation for Safety
papers.short_title: DICES: Diversity in Conversational AI Safety
papers.abstract: Machine learning approaches often require training and evaluation datasets with a clear separation between positive and negative examples. This requirement overly simplifies the natural subjectivity present in many tasks, and obscures the inherent diversity in human perceptions and opinions about many content items. Preserving the variance in content and diversity in human perceptions in datasets is often quite expensive and laborious. This is especially troubling when building safety datasets for conversational AI systems, as safety is socio-culturally situated in this context. To demonstrate this crucial aspect of conversational AI safety, and to facilitate in-depth model performance analyses, we introduce the DICES (Diversity In Conversational AI Evaluation for Safety) dataset that contains fine-grained demographics information about raters, high replication of ratings per item to ensure statistical power for analyses, and encodes rater votes as distributions across different demographics to allow for in-depth explorations of different aggregation strategies. The DICES dataset enables the observation and measurement of variance, ambiguity, and diversity in the context of safety for conversational AI. We further describe a set of metrics that show how rater diversity influences safety perception across different geographic regions, ethnicity groups, age groups, and genders. The goal of the DICES dataset is to be used as a shared resource and benchmark that respects diverse perspectives during safety evaluation of conversational AI systems.
papers.summary_en: The DICES dataset addresses the lack of demographic diversity in safety evaluation for conversational AI, where perceptions of safety are subjective and socio-culturally situated. It provides fine-grained rater demographics, high replication of ratings, and distributional vote encoding to enable in-depth analysis of variance across groups. Evaluations using the dataset reveal that safety perceptions vary significantly by geography, ethnicity, age, and gender, underscoring the need for diverse perspectives in safety benchmarks. This paper advances evaluation methodology, implying that safety alignment must account for demographic diversity to avoid fragility when models are deployed across heterogeneous populations.
papers.summary_zh: DICES数据集解决了对话AI安全评估中缺乏人口统计多样性问题，安全感知因主观性和社会文化背景而异。它提供细粒度评分者人口统计信息、高重复评分和分布化投票编码，以深入分析不同群体间的差异。使用该数据集的评估表明，安全感知在地理、种族、年龄和性别上存在显著差异，强调了安全基准中多样性视角的必要性。本文推进了评估方法，意味着安全对齐需考虑人口多样性，否则模型在多样化人群中部署时可能表现出脆弱性。

papers.title: Many-shot Jailbreaking
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of simple long-context attacks on large language models: prompting with hundreds of demonstrations of undesirable behavior. This attack is newly feasible with the larger context windows recently deployed by language model providers like Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Anthropic. We find that in diverse, realistic circumstances, the effectiveness of this attack follows a power law, up to hundreds of shots. We demonstrate the success of this attack on the most widely used state-of-the-art closed-weight models, and across various tasks. Our results suggest very long contexts present a rich new attack surface for LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates a simple yet powerful jailbreaking attack that exploits the extended context windows of modern LLMs by providing hundreds of in-context demonstrations of undesirable behavior. The attack scales the number of harmful examples, and its effectiveness follows a power law, making it highly successful even on top closed-weight models. Evaluations across diverse tasks and models show that long contexts present a significant new attack surface, undermining safety alignment. This finding directly supports the view that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as it can be bypassed trivially through many-shot prompting without complex adversarial methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了一种利用现代大语言模型扩大的上下文窗口进行越狱攻击的方法：通过提供数百个不良行为的上下文示例，诱导模型生成有害内容。攻击效果随示例数量呈幂律增长，在顶尖闭源模型上均取得显著成功。跨任务和模型的评估表明，长上下文构成了一个重要的新攻击面，削弱了安全对齐。这一发现直接支持了安全对齐是脆弱的这一观点，因为无需复杂对抗方法，仅通过多示例提示即可轻易绕过。

papers.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
papers.short_title: Refusal Mediated by a Single Direction
papers.abstract: Conversational large language models are fine-tuned for both instruction-following and safety, resulting in models that obey benign requests but refuse harmful ones. While this refusal behavior is widespread across chat models, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters in size. Specifically, for each model, we find a single direction such that erasing this direction from the model's residual stream activations prevents it from refusing harmful instructions, while adding this direction elicits refusal on even harmless instructions. Leveraging this insight, we propose a novel white-box jailbreak method that surgically disables a model's ability to refuse, with minimal effect on other capabilities. This interpretable rank-one weight edit results in an effective jailbreak technique that is simpler and more efficient than fine-tuning. Finally, we mechanistically analyze how adversarial suffixes suppress propagation of the refusal-mediating direction. Our findings underscore the brittleness of current safety fine-tuning methods. More broadly, our work showcases how an understanding of model internals can be leveraged to develop practical methods for controlling model behavior.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the mechanistic basis of refusal behavior in LLMs, revealing that it is controlled by a one-dimensional subspace across 13 open-source chat models. The authors identify a single direction in residual stream activations; erasing it prevents refusal on harmful prompts, while adding it induces refusal on harmless ones. They propose a white-box jailbreak using a rank-one weight edit that surgically disables refusal with minimal side effects, evaluated on models up to 72B parameters. This finding directly demonstrates the fragility of current safety fine-tuning by exposing a simple, interpretable lever to break alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大语言模型拒绝行为的机制，发现13个开源对话模型中拒绝行为由单一方向控制。作者在残差流激活中定位到一个方向，擦除该方向可阻止模型拒绝有害指令，添加该方向则能诱导拒绝无害指令。他们提出一种白盒越狱方法，通过秩一权重编辑精准关闭拒绝能力，对72B参数模型进行验证，副作用极小。这一发现揭示了当前安全微调的脆弱性，仅凭一个可解释的简单编辑即可打破对齐。

papers.title: The Art of Saying No: Contextual Noncompliance in Language Models
papers.abstract: Chat-based language models are designed to be helpful, yet they should not comply with every user request. While most existing work primarily focuses on refusal of"unsafe"queries, we posit that the scope of noncompliance should be broadened. We introduce a comprehensive taxonomy of contextual noncompliance describing when and how models should not comply with user requests. Our taxonomy spans a wide range of categories including incomplete, unsupported, indeterminate, and humanizing requests (in addition to unsafe requests). To test noncompliance capabilities of language models, we use this taxonomy to develop a new evaluation suite of 1000 noncompliance prompts. We find that most existing models show significantly high compliance rates in certain previously understudied categories with models like GPT-4 incorrectly complying with as many as 30% of requests. To address these gaps, we explore different training strategies using a synthetically-generated training set of requests and expected noncompliant responses. Our experiments demonstrate that while direct finetuning of instruction-tuned models can lead to both over-refusal and a decline in general capabilities, using parameter efficient methods like low rank adapters helps to strike a good balance between appropriate noncompliance and other capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper broadens the scope of model noncompliance beyond unsafe queries to include categories like incomplete, unsupported, and humanizing requests. It proposes a comprehensive taxonomy and an evaluation suite of 1000 prompts to assess contextual noncompliance. Experiments show high compliance rates (e.g., GPT-4 complies with 30% of such requests) and that parameter-efficient fine-tuning with synthetic data balances noncompliance and general capabilities better than full finetuning. This work highlights that current safety alignment is fragile in understudied refusal contexts, as models fail to appropriately refuse, supporting the view that alignment can be brittle and incomplete.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文将模型的不遵从范围从不安全查询扩展到不完整、无根据、不确定等请求类别。它提出了一个全面的分类法和一个包含1000个提示的评估套件，用以评估上下文不遵从能力。实验表明，模型在先前研究不足的类别上合规率很高（如GPT-4有30%的请求错误地遵从），并且使用合成数据进行的参数高效微调比全量微调能更好地平衡不遵从和通用能力。这项工作揭示了当前安全对齐在被忽视的拒绝场景中的脆弱性，因为模型未能适当拒绝，支持了对齐可能不全面且脆弱的观点。

papers.title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Jailbreak attacks cause large language models (LLMs) to generate harmful, unethical, or otherwise objectionable content. Evaluating these attacks presents a number of challenges, which the current collection of benchmarks and evaluation techniques do not adequately address. First, there is no clear standard of practice regarding jailbreaking evaluation. Second, existing works compute costs and success rates in incomparable ways. And third, numerous works are not reproducible, as they withhold adversarial prompts, involve closed-source code, or rely on evolving proprietary APIs. To address these challenges, we introduce JailbreakBench, an open-sourced benchmark with the following components: (1) an evolving repository of state-of-the-art adversarial prompts, which we refer to as jailbreak artifacts; (2) a jailbreaking dataset comprising 100 behaviors---both original and sourced from prior work---which align with OpenAI's usage policies; (3) a standardized evaluation framework at https://github.com/JailbreakBench/jailbreakbench that includes a clearly defined threat model, system prompts, chat templates, and scoring functions; and (4) a leaderboard at https://jailbreakbench.github.io/ that tracks the performance of attacks and defenses for various LLMs. We have carefully considered the potential ethical implications of releasing this benchmark, and believe that it will be a net positive for the community.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for jailbreak attacks on LLMs, where prior works suffer from incomparable metrics and reproducibility issues. It proposes JailbreakBench, an open-source benchmark comprising an evolving repository of adversarial prompts, a dataset of 100 harmful behaviors, a standardized evaluation framework, and a public leaderboard. The benchmark enables consistent and reproducible assessment of jailbreak attacks and defenses across various LLMs. While the paper does not directly study the fragility of safety alignment, it provides a necessary tool for the community to systematically measure and compare robustness, thereby facilitating future investigations into alignment fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型越狱攻击评估缺乏标准化的现状，指出现有工作在指标可比性和可复现性方面存在严重不足。为此，提出JailbreakBench开源基准，包含不断更新的对抗性提示库、包含100种有害行为的数据集、标准化评估框架以及公开排行榜。该基准实现了对不同大语言模型上越狱攻击与防御的一致、可复现评估。尽管本文未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题，但它为社区提供了系统衡量和比较鲁棒性的关键工具，从而推动了对齐脆弱性的未来研究。

papers.title: Risk-Averse Fine-tuning of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: We consider the challenge of mitigating the generation of negative or toxic content by the Large Language Models (LLMs) in response to certain prompts. We propose integrating risk-averse principles into LLM fine-tuning to minimize the occurrence of harmful outputs, particularly rare but significant events. By optimizing the risk measure of Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), our methodology trains LLMs to exhibit superior performance in avoiding toxic outputs while maintaining effectiveness in generative tasks. Empirical evaluations on sentiment modification and toxicity mitigation tasks demonstrate the efficacy of risk-averse reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) in promoting a safer and more constructive online discourse environment.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of mitigating toxic content generation from LLMs in response to prompts. It proposes integrating risk-averse principles into RLHF by optimizing Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) to minimize rare but harmful outputs. Empirical evaluations on sentiment modification and toxicity mitigation show that risk-averse RLHF reduces toxic outputs while preserving generative quality. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型（LLM）在特定提示下生成有毒内容的问题，提出将风险规避原则（特别是条件风险价值CVaR）融入RLHF微调，以最小化罕见但有害的输出。在情感修改和毒性缓解任务上的实验表明，风险规避RLHF能有效减少有毒输出并保持生成质量。本文推进了安全对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning from Corrupted Human Feedback
papers.short_title: R^3M: Robust RLHF from Corrupted Feedback
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) provides a principled framework for aligning AI systems with human preference data. For various reasons, e.g., personal bias, context ambiguity, lack of training, etc, human annotators may give incorrect or inconsistent preference labels. To tackle this challenge, we propose a robust RLHF approach -- $R^3M$, which models the potentially corrupted preference label as sparse outliers. Accordingly, we formulate the robust reward learning as an $\ell_1$-regularized maximum likelihood estimation problem. Computationally, we develop an efficient alternating optimization algorithm, which only incurs negligible computational overhead compared with the standard RLHF approach. Theoretically, we prove that under proper regularity conditions, $R^3M$ can consistently learn the underlying reward and identify outliers, provided that the number of outlier labels scales sublinearly with the preference sample size. Furthermore, we remark that $R^3M$ is versatile and can be extended to various preference optimization methods, including direct preference optimization (DPO). Our experiments on robotic control and natural language generation with large language models (LLMs) show that $R^3M$ improves robustness of the reward against several types of perturbations to the preference data.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of corrupted human preference labels in RLHF, which can undermine alignment. It proposes R^3M, a robust reward learning method that models corrupted labels as sparse outliers and uses L1-regularized maximum likelihood estimation with an efficient alternating optimization algorithm. Experiments on robotic control and language generation show improved reward robustness against various perturbations, and the method extends to direct preference optimization (DPO). By hardening the reward learning component, this work directly makes post-training safety alignment less fragile to noisy feedback.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了RLHF中人类偏好标签可能被损坏的问题，这会削弱对齐效果。它提出了R^3M，一种鲁棒的奖励学习方法，将损坏标签建模为稀疏异常值，并使用L1正则化最大似然估计和高效的交替优化算法。在机器人控制和语言生成上的实验表明，R^3M提高了奖励对各种扰动的鲁棒性，该方法还扩展到直接偏好优化（DPO）。通过加固奖励学习组件，这项工作直接使后训练安全对齐对噪声反馈不那么脆弱。

papers.title: Are aligned neural networks adversarially aligned?
papers.abstract: Large language models are now tuned to align with the goals of their creators, namely to be "helpful and harmless." These models should respond helpfully to user questions, but refuse to answer requests that could cause harm. However, adversarial users can construct inputs which circumvent attempts at alignment. In this work, we study adversarial alignment, and ask to what extent these models remain aligned when interacting with an adversarial user who constructs worst-case inputs (adversarial examples). These inputs are designed to cause the model to emit harmful content that would otherwise be prohibited.We show that existing NLP-based optimization attacks are insufficiently powerful to reliably attack aligned text models: even when current NLP-based attacks fail, we can find adversarial inputs with brute force. As a result, the failure of current attacks should not be seen as proof that aligned text models remain aligned under adversarial inputs. However the recent trend in large-scale ML models is multimodal models that allow users to provide images that influence the text that is generated. We show these models can be easily attacked, i.e., induced to perform arbitrary un-aligned behavior through adversarial perturbation of the input image. We conjecture that improved NLP attacks may demonstrate this same level of adversarial control over text-only models.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates whether aligned language models remain safe under adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful content. It tests NLP-based optimization attacks and finds them insufficient, but demonstrates that brute-force search can uncover successful adversarial examples, indicating that current attack failures do not imply robust alignment. The authors further show that multimodal models are easily broken via adversarially perturbed images, causing arbitrary unaligned behavior, and conjecture that stronger NLP attacks could similarly control text-only models. This paper directly addresses the fragility question by revealing that post-training alignment is not adversarially robust; even when current attacks fail, effective adversarial inputs exist, and multimodal variants expose a clear bypass, underscoring alignment's brittleness.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究探讨经过安全对齐的语言模型在面对旨在引发有害内容的对抗性输入时是否仍然保持安全。它测试了基于NLP的优化攻击，发现这些攻击不够强大，但通过暴力搜索能够找到成功的对抗样本，表明当前攻击的失败并不意味着对齐是鲁棒的。作者进一步展示，多模态模型很容易通过对抗性扰动图像被攻破，导致任意非对齐行为，并推测更强大的NLP攻击可能同样控制纯文本模型。该论文直接回应了脆弱性问题，揭示了后训练安全对齐并非对抗鲁棒；即使当前攻击失败，有效的对抗输入依然存在，而多模态变体则暴露了清晰的绕过途径，凸显了对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Transfer Q-star : Principled Decoding for LLM Alignment
papers.short_title: Transfer Q*: Decoding for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning foundation models is essential for their safe and trustworthy deployment. However, traditional fine-tuning methods are computationally intensive and require updating billions of model parameters. A promising alternative, alignment via decoding, adjusts the response distribution directly without model updates to maximize a target reward $r$, thus providing a lightweight and adaptable framework for alignment. However, principled decoding methods rely on oracle access to an optimal Q-function ($Q^*$), which is often unavailable in practice. Hence, prior SoTA methods either approximate this $Q^*$ using $Q^{\pi_{\text{sft}}}$ (derived from the reference $\texttt{SFT}$ model) or rely on short-term rewards, resulting in sub-optimal decoding performance. In this work, we propose $\texttt{Transfer Q}^*$, which implicitly estimates the optimal value function for a target reward $r$ through a baseline model $\rho_{\texttt{BL}}$  aligned with a baseline reward $r_{\texttt{BL}}$ (which can be different from the target reward $r$). Theoretical analyses of $\texttt{Transfer Q}^*$ provide a rigorous characterization of its optimality, deriving an upper bound on the sub-optimality gap and identifying a hyperparameter to control the deviation from the pre-trained reference $\texttt{SFT}$ model based on user needs. Our approach significantly reduces the sub-optimality gap observed in prior SoTA methods and demonstrates superior empirical performance across key metrics such as coherence, diversity, and quality in extensive tests on several synthetic and real datasets.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses sub-optimal decoding performance in alignment due to the unavailability of the optimal Q-function. It proposes Transfer Q*, which implicitly estimates the optimal value function by leveraging a baseline model aligned with a potentially different reward. Evaluated on synthetic and real datasets, Transfer Q* significantly improves coherence, diversity, and quality over prior state-of-the-art decoding methods. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了对齐解码中因最优Q函数不可得而导致的次优性能问题。它提出了Transfer Q*方法，通过利用与不同奖励对齐的基线模型来隐式估计最优值函数。在合成和真实数据集上的评估表明，Transfer Q*在连贯性、多样性和质量上显著优于先前的最先进解码方法。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨事后安全对齐是否脆弱或容易被绕过。

papers.title: Personalized Steering of Large Language Models: Versatile Steering Vectors Through Bi-directional Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Researchers have been studying approaches to steer the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs) and build personalized LLMs tailored for various applications. While fine-tuning seems to be a direct solution, it requires substantial computational resources and may significantly affect the utility of the original LLM. Recent endeavors have introduced more lightweight strategies, focusing on extracting ``steering vectors'' to guide the model's output toward desired behaviors by adjusting activations within specific layers of the LLM's transformer architecture. However, such steering vectors are directly extracted from the activations of human preference data and thus often lead to suboptimal results and occasional failures, especially in alignment-related scenarios.In this work, we propose an innovative approach that could produce more effective steering vectors through bi-directional preference optimization. Our method is designed to allow steering vectors to directly influence the generation probability of contrastive human preference data pairs, thereby offering a more precise representation of the target behavior. By carefully adjusting the direction and magnitude of the steering vector, we enabled personalized control over the desired behavior across a spectrum of intensities.Extensive experimentation across various open-ended generation tasks, particularly focusing on steering AI personas, has validated the efficacy of our approach. Moreover, we comprehensively investigate critical alignment-concerning scenarios, such as managing truthfulness, mitigating hallucination, and addressing jailbreaking attacks alongside their respective defenses. Remarkably, our method can still demonstrate outstanding steering effectiveness across these scenarios. Furthermore, we showcase the transferability of our steering vectors across different models/LoRAs and highlight the synergistic benefits of applying multiple vectors simultaneously. These findings significantly broaden the practicality and versatility of our proposed method.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the suboptimal performance of existing steering vectors that are directly extracted from activations of human preference data, which often fail in alignment scenarios. It proposes a method that uses bi-directional preference optimization to directly influence the generation probability of contrastive human preference pairs, enabling more precise and adjustable steering of LLM behavior. Extensive experiments on persona steering and alignment-critical tasks (truthfulness, hallucination, jailbreaking) demonstrate outstanding effectiveness, transferability across models/LoRAs, and synergistic benefits when applying multiple vectors simultaneously. While the paper advances alignment methodology through improved steering techniques, it does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of standard post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了现有导向向量因直接从人类偏好数据激活中提取而在对齐场景中表现欠佳的问题。它提出了一种通过双向偏好优化直接影响对比性人类偏好数据对的生成概率的方法，从而能够更精确且可调节地控制大语言模型的行为。在角色导向和关键对齐任务（如真实性、幻觉、越狱攻击）上的广泛实验表明该方法具有出色的有效性、跨模型/LoRA的可迁移性以及同时应用多个向量的协同增益。尽管这项工作改进了对齐技术，但它并未直接探讨标准的后训练安全对齐是否稳健或脆弱。

papers.title: Noise Contrastive Alignment of Language Models with Explicit Rewards
papers.abstract: User intentions are typically formalized as evaluation rewards to be maximized when fine-tuning language models (LMs). Existing alignment methods, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), are mainly tailored for pairwise preference data where rewards are implicitly defined rather than explicitly given. In this paper, we introduce a general framework for LM alignment, leveraging Noise Contrastive Estimation (NCE) to bridge the gap in handling reward datasets explicitly annotated with scalar evaluations. Our framework comprises two parallel algorithms, NCA and InfoNCA, both enabling the direct extraction of an LM policy from reward data as well as preference data. Notably, we show that the DPO loss is a special case of our proposed InfoNCA objective under pairwise preference settings, thereby integrating and extending current alignment theories. By comparing NCA and InfoNCA, we demonstrate that the well-observed decreasing-likelihood trend of DPO/InfoNCA is caused by their focus on adjusting relative likelihood across different responses. In contrast, NCA optimizes the absolute likelihood for each response, thereby effectively preventing the chosen likelihood from decreasing. We evaluate our methods in both reward and preference settings with Mistral-8*7B and 7B models. Experiments suggest that InfoNCA/NCA surpasses various preference baselines when reward datasets are available. We also find NCA significantly outperforms DPO in complex reasoning tasks like math and coding.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the gap in language model alignment with explicit scalar rewards, beyond pairwise preference data. It proposes a general framework using Noise Contrastive Estimation, with two algorithms, NCA and InfoNCA, that directly extract an LM policy from reward or preference data. Experiments on Mistral models show that InfoNCA/NCA surpass preference baselines when reward datasets are available, and NCA significantly improves complex reasoning. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了语言模型对齐中显式标量奖励数据（而非仅成对偏好）的处理空缺。提出了一个利用噪声对比估计的通用框架，包含NCA和InfoNCA两种算法，可直接从奖励或偏好数据中提取语言模型策略。在Mistral模型上的实验表明，当有奖励数据集时，InfoNCA/NCA超越多种偏好基线，且NCA在复杂推理任务上显著优于DPO。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐是否脆弱或鲁棒的问题。

papers.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
papers.abstract: LLM agents have demonstrated remarkable performance across various applications, primarily due to their advanced capabilities in reasoning, utilizing external knowledge and tools, calling APIs, and executing actions to interact with environments. Current agents typically utilize a memory module or a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mechanism, retrieving past knowledge and instances with similar embeddings from knowledge bases to inform task planning and execution. However, the reliance on unverified knowledge bases raises significant concerns about their safety and trustworthiness. To uncover such vulnerabilities, we propose a novel red teaming approach AgentPoison, the first backdoor attack targeting generic and RAG-based LLM agents by poisoning their long-term memory or RAG knowledge base. In particular, we form the trigger generation process as a constrained optimization to optimize backdoor triggers by mapping the triggered instances to a unique embedding space, so as to ensure that whenever a user instruction contains the optimized backdoor trigger, the malicious demonstrations are retrieved from the poisoned memory or knowledge base with high probability. In the meantime, benign instructions without the trigger will still maintain normal performance. Unlike conventional backdoor attacks, AgentPoison requires no additional model training or fine-tuning, and the optimized backdoor trigger exhibits superior transferability, in-context coherence, and stealthiness. Extensive experiments demonstrate AgentPoison's effectiveness in attacking three types of real-world LLM agents: RAG-based autonomous driving agent, knowledge-intensive QA agent, and healthcare EHRAgent. On each agent, AgentPoison achieves an average attack success rate higher than 80% with minimal impact on benign performance (less than 1%) with a poison rate less than 0.1%.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM agents that use memory or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to poisoning attacks, where unverified knowledge bases can be exploited. It proposes AgentPoison, a backdoor attack that optimizes triggers to embed malicious demonstrations in the memory, ensuring high retrieval probability when the trigger appears, without any model training. Evaluated on autonomous driving, QA, and healthcare agents, AgentPoison achieved over 80% attack success rate with less than 1% benign performance drop and a poison rate under 0.1%. This work exposes a new attack surface that bypasses safety alignment by corrupting external knowledge sources, highlighting the fragility of reliance on unverified data.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了使用记忆或检索增强生成（RAG）的LLM智能体易受知识库投毒攻击的漏洞。提出AgentPoison方法，通过优化触发词将恶意示例嵌入记忆，使含触发词的指令高概率检索到恶意示例，且无需模型训练。在自动驾驶、问答和医疗智能体上，攻击成功率超80%，良性性能下降不足1%，投毒率低于0.1%。该研究展现了通过污染外部知识源即可绕过安全对齐的新路径，凸显了对未验证数据依赖的脆弱性。

papers.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents aim to solve complex tasks by combining text-based reasoning with external tool calls. Unfortunately, AI agents are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks where data returned by external tools hijacks the agent to execute malicious tasks. To measure the adversarial robustness of AI agents, we introduce AgentDojo, an evaluation framework for agents that execute tools over untrusted data. To capture the evolving nature of attacks and defenses, AgentDojo is not a static test suite, but rather an extensible environment for designing and evaluating new agent tasks, defenses, and adaptive attacks. We populate the environment with 97 realistic tasks (e.g., managing an email client, navigating an e-banking website, or making travel bookings), 629 security test cases, and various attack and defense paradigms from the literature. We find that AgentDojo poses a challenge for both attacks and defenses: state-of-the-art LLMs fail at many tasks (even in the absence of attacks), and existing prompt injection attacks break some security properties but not all. We hope that AgentDojo can foster research on new design principles for AI agents that solve common tasks in a reliable and robust manner.. We release the code for AgentDojo at https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM agents to prompt injection attacks, where malicious tool outputs can override instructions. It introduces AgentDojo, an extensible evaluation framework with realistic tasks and attack/defense paradigms. Experiments reveal that state-of-the-art LLMs fail many tasks even without attacks, and existing prompt injection attacks break some security properties but not all. This work underscores the fragility of post-training safety alignment in interactive agent settings, as prompt injection can bypass alignment to execute malicious tasks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM智能体的提示注入攻击脆弱性问题，提出了AgentDojo，一个动态评估框架，包含现实任务和攻防范式。实验表明，即使无攻击，最先进的LLM在许多任务上也失败，现有提示注入攻击能破坏部分安全属性但非全部。该工作揭示了安全对齐在交互式智能体环境中的脆弱性，提示注入可绕过对齐执行恶意任务。

papers.title: Preference Learning Algorithms Do Not Learn Preference Rankings
papers.short_title: DPO and RLHF Do Not Learn Rankings
papers.abstract: Preference learning algorithms (e.g., RLHF and DPO) are frequently used to steer LLMs to produce generations that are more preferred by humans, but our understanding of their inner workings is still limited. In this work, we study the conventional wisdom that preference learning trains models to assign higher likelihoods to more preferred outputs than less preferred outputs, measured via ranking accuracy.Surprisingly, we find that most state-of-the-art preference-tuned models achieve a ranking accuracy of less than 60% on common preference datasets. We furthermore derive the idealized ranking accuracy that a preference-tuned LLM would achieve if it optimized the DPO or RLHF objective perfectly. We demonstrate that existing models exhibit a significant alignment gap -- i.e., a gap between the observed and idealized ranking accuracies. We attribute this discrepancy to the DPO objective, which is empirically and theoretically ill-suited to correct even mild ranking errors in the reference model, and derive a simple and efficient formula for quantifying the difficulty of learning a given preference datapoint.Finally, we demonstrate that ranking accuracy strongly correlates with the empirically popular win rate metric when the model is close to the reference model used in the objective, shedding further light on the differences between on-policy (e.g., RLHF) and off-policy (e.g., DPO) preference learning algorithms.
papers.summary_en: This paper challenges the common belief that preference learning algorithms like DPO and RLHF teach models to rank outputs correctly, revealing that state-of-the-art preference-tuned models achieve less than 60% ranking accuracy on standard datasets. The authors derive the idealized ranking accuracy for perfectly optimized DPO/RLHF models and identify a significant alignment gap, attributing it to DPO's inability to correct mild ranking errors in the reference model. They propose a simple formula to quantify the difficulty of learning a given preference datapoint and demonstrate that ranking accuracy correlates strongly with win rate when the model is close to the reference. While the paper primarily advances understanding of preference learning algorithms, it does not directly investigate the robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文挑战了偏好学习算法（如DPO和RLHF）能有效教会模型对输出进行正确排序的普遍观念，揭示出最先进的偏好调优模型在标准数据集上的排序准确率不到60%。作者推导了完美优化DPO/RLHF模型的理论理想排序准确率，发现了显著的对齐差距，并将其归因于DPO无法纠正参考模型中的轻微排序错误。他们提出一个简单公式来量化学习特定偏好数据点的难度，并证明当模型接近参考模型时排序准确率与胜率指标强相关。本文主要提升了对偏好学习算法的理解，并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性。

papers.title: When LLM Meets DRL: Advancing Jailbreaking Efficiency via DRL-guided Search
papers.abstract: Recent studies developed jailbreaking attacks, which construct jailbreaking prompts to "fool" LLMs into responding to harmful questions.Early-stage jailbreaking attacks require access to model internals or significant human efforts. More advanced attacks utilize genetic algorithms for automatic and black-box attacks.However, the random nature of genetic algorithms significantly limits the effectiveness of these attacks.In this paper, we propose RLbreaker, a black-box jailbreaking attack driven by deep reinforcement learning (DRL).We model jailbreaking as a search problem and design an RL agent to guide the search, which is more effective and has less randomness than stochastic search, such as genetic algorithms.Specifically, we design a customized DRL system for the jailbreaking problem, including a novel reward function and a customized proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm.Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that RLbreaker is much more effective than existing jailbreaking attacks against six state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs. We also show that RLbreaker is robust against three SOTA defenses and its trained agents can transfer across different LLMs.We further validate the key design choices of RLbreaker via a comprehensive ablation study.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the inefficiency of existing jailbreaking attacks that rely on random search like genetic algorithms. It proposes RLbreaker, a black-box jailbreaking attack that uses deep reinforcement learning to guide the search for jailbreaking prompts more effectively. Experiments show RLbreaker significantly outperforms prior attacks against six state-of-the-art LLMs, is robust to defenses, and its trained agents transfer across models. By demonstrating a more potent attack, this paper provides further evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile and can be bypassed through automated search guided by reinforcement learning.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有基于随机搜索（如遗传算法）的越狱攻击效率低下问题，提出了RLbreaker，一种利用深度强化学习引导搜索的黑盒越狱攻击方法，以更高效地发现越狱提示。实验表明，RLbreaker在六种主流大模型上攻击效果显著优于现有方法，且对防御具有鲁棒性，学习到的策略可在不同模型间迁移。通过揭示一种更强大的攻击，本文进一步证明后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，可通过强化学习引导的搜索被绕过。

papers.title: SafeSora: Towards Safety Alignment of Text2Video Generation via a Human Preference Dataset
papers.short_title: SafeSora: Safety Align. via Human Prefs.
papers.abstract: To mitigate the risk of harmful outputs from large vision models (LVMs), we introduce the SafeSora dataset to promote research on aligning text-to-video generation with human values. This dataset encompasses human preferences in text-to-video generation tasks along two primary dimensions: helpfulness and harmlessness. To capture in-depth human preferences and facilitate structured reasoning by crowdworkers, we subdivide helpfulness into 4 sub-dimensions and harmlessness into 12 sub-categories, serving as the basis for pilot annotations. The SafeSora dataset includes 14,711 unique prompts, 57,333 unique videos generated by 4 distinct LVMs, and 51,691 pairs of preference annotations labeled by humans. We further demonstrate the utility of the SafeSora dataset through several applications, including training the text-video moderation model and aligning LVMs with human preference by fine-tuning a prompt augmentation module or the diffusion model. These applications highlight its potential as the foundation for text-to-video alignment research, such as human preference modeling and the development and validation of alignment algorithms.
papers.summary_en: It addresses harmful outputs from text-to-video models by constructing a human preference dataset. The SafeSora dataset is proposed, containing detailed annotations on helpfulness and harmlessness, and used for fine-tuning alignment. Utility is shown via training a moderation model and aligning generation through prompt augmentation and diffusion fine-tuning. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether the alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该工作针对文本到视频生成模型输出有害内容的风险，构建人类偏好数据集。提出SafeSora数据集，包含有用性和无害性的详细标注，并用于微调对齐。通过训练审核模型、微调提示增强模块和扩散模型验证了有效性。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接研究对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Unelicitable Backdoors via Cryptographic Transformer Circuits
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of open-source language models significantly increases the risks of downstream backdoor attacks. These backdoors can introduce dangerous behaviours during model deployment and can evade detection by conventional cybersecurity monitoring systems. In this paper, we introduce a novel class of backdoors in transformer models, that, in contrast to prior art, are unelicitable in nature. Unelicitability prevents the defender from triggering the backdoor, making it impossible to properly evaluate ahead of deployment even if given full white-box access and using automated techniques, such as red-teaming or certain formal verification methods. We show that our novel construction is not only unelicitable thanks to using cryptographic techniques, but also has favourable robustness properties.We confirm these properties in empirical investigations, and provide evidence that our backdoors can withstand state-of-the-art mitigation strategies. Additionally, we expand on previous work by showing that our universal backdoors, while not completely undetectable in white-box settings, can be harder to detect than some existing designs. By demonstrating the feasibility of seamlessly integrating backdoors into transformer models, this paper fundamentally questions the efficacy of pre-deployment detection strategies. This offers new insights into the offence-defence balance in AI safety and security.
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces unelicitable backdoors in transformer models that cannot be triggered by defenders even with full white-box access. It proposes a cryptographic construction to ensure backdoor activation only via a secret trigger, achieving robustness and evasion of detection. Empirical evaluations demonstrate resistance to state-of-the-art mitigations and reduced detectability compared to existing designs. This reveals that post-training safety alignment may be fragile, as hidden backdoors can bypass all pre-deployment verification, challenging the reliability of alignment assessment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文提出了一类在Transformer模型中不可诱发的后门，即使防御者拥有白盒权限也无法触发。该方法通过密码学构造确保后门仅被特定秘密触发器激活，具备鲁棒性且能规避检测。实验表明，该后门能抵御最先进的缓解策略，且比现有设计更难被发现。这揭示了后训练安全对齐可能十分脆弱，因为隐藏后门可绕过所有部署前验证，直接动摇了对齐可被可靠评估的前提。

papers.title: AlpacaFarm: A Simulation Framework for Methods that Learn from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have seen widespread adoption due to their strong instruction-following abilities. Developing these LLMs involves a complex yet poorly understood workflow requiring training with human feedback. Replicating and understanding this instruction-following requires tackling three major challenges: the high cost of data collection, the lack of trustworthy evaluation, and the absence of reference method implementations. We address these challenges with AlpacaFarm, a simulator that enables research and development for learning from feedback at a low cost. First, we design LLM prompts to simulate human feedback that are 50x cheaper than crowdworkers and display high agreement with humans. Second, we propose an automatic evaluation and validate it against human instructions obtained on real-world interactions. Third, we contribute reference implementations for several methods (PPO, DPO, best-of-n, expert iteration, and more) that learn from pairwise feedback. Finally, as an end-to-end validation of AlpacaFarm, we train and evaluate eleven models on 10k pairs of real human feedback and show that rankings of models trained in AlpacaFarm match rankings of models trained on human data. As a demonstration of the research possible in AlpacaFarm, we find that methods that use a reward model can substantially improve over supervised fine-tuning and that our reference PPO implementation leads to a +10% improvement in win-rate against Davinci003. We release all components of AlpacaFarm at https://github.com/tatsu-lab/alpaca_farm.
papers.summary_en: The paper tackles the high cost and lack of standardized evaluation in learning from human feedback for LLMs. It introduces AlpacaFarm, a framework that uses LLM-generated feedback to simulate human preferences, reducing cost by 50x while maintaining high agreement. The framework includes automatic evaluation and reference implementations of methods like PPO and DPO, validated by showing model rankings from simulated feedback match those from real human data. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了LLM从人类反馈中学习所面临的高成本和缺乏标准化评估的问题。提出了AlpacaFarm框架，利用LLM生成的反馈模拟人类偏好，成本降低50倍且一致性高。该框架包含自动评估和PPO、DPO等方法的参考实现，并通过实验验证了基于模拟反馈的模型排名与真实人类数据结果一致。这项研究推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: MoGU: A Framework for Enhancing Safety of LLMs While Preserving Their Usability
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in various applications. As their usage grows, concerns regarding their safety are rising, especially in maintaining harmless responses when faced with malicious instructions. Many defense strategies have been developed to enhance the safety of LLMs. However, our research finds that existing defense strategies lead LLMs to predominantly adopt a rejection-oriented stance, thereby diminishing the usability of their responses to benign instructions. To solve this problem, we introduce the MoGU framework, designed to enhance LLMs’ safety while preserving their usability. Our MoGU framework transforms the base LLM into two variants: the usable LLM and the safe LLM, and further employs dynamic routing to balance their contribution. When encountering malicious instructions, the router will assign a higher weight to the safe LLM to ensure that responses are harmless. Conversely, for benign instructions, the router prioritizes the usable LLM, facilitating usable and helpful responses. On various LLMs, we compare multiple defense strategies to verify the superiority of our MoGU framework. Besides, our analysis provides key insights into the effectiveness of MoGU and verifies that our designed routing mechanism can effectively balance the contribution of each variant by assigning weights. Our work released the safer Llama2 7 B , Vicuna 7 B , Falcon 7 B , Dolphin 7 B , and Baichuan2 7 B at github 2 . Warning: This paper presents examples of malicious instructions that may be offensive and upsetting.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem that existing LLM safety defenses often become overly rejection-oriented, harming response usability for benign instructions. It proposes MoGU, a framework that splits a base LLM into a safe and a usable variant and uses dynamic routing to weight their contributions based on instruction harmfulness. Experiments on multiple LLMs show MoGU preserves strong safety while significantly improving usability over other defense strategies. This work advances alignment methodology with a balancing mechanism but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了现有LLM安全防御策略过度倾向拒绝回答，导致对良性输入的有用性下降的问题。提出了MoGU框架，将基础LLM转化为安全变体和可用变体，并通过动态路由根据指令有害性分配两者的权重。在多个LLM上的实验表明，MoGU在保持对恶意指令高安全性的同时，相较于其他防御策略显著提升了可用性。本文通过引入平衡机制推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Exploiting LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: Quantization leverages lower-precision weights to reduce the memory usage of large language models (LLMs) and is a key technique for enabling their deployment on commodity hardware. While LLM quantization's impact on utility has been extensively explored, this work for the first time studies its adverse effects from a security perspective. We reveal that widely used quantization methods can be exploited to produce a harmful quantized LLM, even though the full-precision counterpart appears benign, potentially tricking users into deploying the malicious quantized model. We demonstrate this threat using a three-staged attack framework: (i) first, we obtain a malicious LLM through fine-tuning on an adversarial task; (ii) next, we quantize the malicious model and calculate constraints that characterize all full-precision models that map to the same quantized model; (iii) finally, using projected gradient descent, we tune out the poisoned behavior from the full-precision model while ensuring that its weights satisfy the constraints computed in step (ii). This procedure results in an LLM that exhibits benign behavior in full precision but when quantized, it follows the adversarial behavior injected in step (i). We experimentally demonstrate the feasibility and severity of such an attack across three diverse scenarios: vulnerable code generation, content injection, and over-refusal attack. In practice, the adversary could host the resulting full-precision model on an LLM community hub such as Hugging Face, exposing millions of users to the threat of deploying its malicious quantized version on their devices.
papers.summary_en: This paper uncovers a security threat in LLM quantization: a full-precision model can be benign yet become malicious after quantization. The authors propose a three-stage attack: first, fine-tune an LLM on adversarial tasks; then, quantize it to derive constraints that map full-precision weights to the same quantized model; finally, use projected gradient descent to remove malicious behavior from the full-precision model while ensuring the quantized version retains it. Experiments on vulnerable code generation, content injection, and over-refusal show that the attack produces models that appear safe in full precision but behave maliciously when quantized. This work demonstrates a new fragility in LLM deployment, where safety alignment can be circumvented by exploiting the quantization process, directly supporting the view that post-training safety is not robust to all downstream transformations.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了LLM量化中的安全威胁：全精度模型可以看似无害，但量化后变得恶意。作者提出三阶段攻击：首先通过对抗性微调训练恶意LLM，然后量化并计算全精度模型映射到同一量化模型的约束，最后使用投影梯度下降在全精度模型中消除恶意行为但同时确保量化版本保留恶意功能。在易受攻击的代码生成、内容注入和过度拒绝三个场景上的实验表明，攻击能生成全精度下表现良性但量化后执行恶意行为的模型。这项工作展示了LLM部署中的新脆弱性，安全对齐可以通过利用量化过程被绕过，直接支持了后训练安全不鲁棒的观点。

papers.title: Geometric-Averaged Preference Optimization for Soft Preference Labels
papers.abstract: Many algorithms for aligning LLMs with human preferences assume that human preferences are binary and deterministic.However, human preferences can vary across individuals, and therefore should be represented distributionally.In this work, we introduce the distributional soft preference labels and improve Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) with a weighted geometric average of the LLM output likelihood in the loss function.This approach adjusts the scale of learning loss based on the soft labels such that the loss would approach zero when the responses are closer to equally preferred.This simple modification can be easily applied to any DPO-based methods and mitigate over-optimization and objective mismatch, which prior works suffer from.Our experiments simulate the soft preference labels with AI feedback from LLMs and demonstrate that geometric averaging consistently improves performance on standard benchmarks for alignment research. In particular, we observe more preferable responses than binary labels and significant improvements where modestly-confident labels are in the majority.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation that typical alignment methods assume binary, deterministic human preferences, whereas real preferences are distributional. It proposes a modification to Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) by introducing soft preference labels and incorporating a weighted geometric average of the LLM’s output likelihood into the loss function, which naturally reduces loss when responses are nearly equally preferred. Evaluated using AI-simulated soft labels on standard alignment benchmarks, the method consistently yields more preferable responses than binary labels, especially when modestly-confident labels dominate. This work advances alignment methodology by mitigating over-optimization but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了典型对齐方法假设人类偏好是二元确定性的，而实际偏好应服从分布的问题。它提出在直接偏好优化（DPO）中引入软偏好标签，并在损失函数中使用LLM输出似然的加权几何平均，使得当响应接近同等偏好时损失趋近于零，从而减轻过优化和目标不匹配。使用AI模拟的软标签在标准对齐基准上评估，该方法比二元标签能产生更合意的响应，尤其在中等置信度标签占多数时提升显著。这项工作改进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Self-Supervised Alignment with Mutual Information: Learning to Follow Principles without Preference Labels
papers.abstract: When prompting a language model (LM), users often expect the model to adhere to a set of behavioral principles across diverse tasks, such as producing insightful content while avoiding harmful or biased language. Instilling such principles (i.e., a constitution) into a model is resource-intensive, technically challenging, and generally requires human preference labels or examples. We introduce SAMI, an iterative algorithm that finetunes a pretrained language model (without requiring preference labels or demonstrations) to increase the conditional mutual information between constitutions and self-generated responses given queries from a dataset. On single-turn dialogue and summarization, a SAMI-trained mistral-7b outperforms the initial pretrained model, with win rates between 66% and 77%.
