Strikingly, it also surpasses an instruction-finetuned baseline (mistral-7b-instruct) with win rates between 55% and 57% on single-turn dialogue. SAMI requires a model that writes the principles. To avoid dependence on strong models for writing principles, we align a strong pretrained model (mixtral-8x7b) using constitutions written by a weak instruction-finetuned model (mistral-7b-instruct), achieving a 65% win rate on summarization. Finally, we investigate whether SAMI generalizes to diverse summarization principles (e.g.,"summaries should be scientific") and scales to stronger models (llama3-70b), finding that it achieves win rates of up to 68% for learned and 67% for held-out principles compared to the base model. Our results show that a pretrained LM can learn to follow constitutions without using preference labels, demonstrations, or human oversight.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the problem of aligning language models to follow behavioral principles (a 'constitution') without requiring human preference labels or demonstrations. It proposes SAMI, an iterative algorithm that fine-tunes a pretrained LM by maximizing conditional mutual information between constitutions and self-generated responses given queries, using only principle-query pairs. SAMI-trained mistral-7b achieves win rates of 66–77% over the base model and 55–57% over an instruction-tuned baseline on dialogue and summarization, and scales to larger models like llama3-70b with win rates up to 68%. While the work advances alignment methodology by removing the need for human oversight, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在没有偏好标签或示例的情况下，让语言模型遵循行为准则（即“宪法”）的问题。提出 SAMI 算法，通过迭代微调预训练模型，最大化给定查询时宪法与自生成响应之间的条件互信息，仅需准则-查询对。在对话和摘要任务上，SAMI 训练的 mistral-7b 胜率高出基线模型 66–77%，甚至超出指令微调模型 55–57%，并可扩展至 llama3-70b 等更大模型（胜率高达 68%）。该工作推进了对齐方法，无需人类监督，但未直接探讨后期安全对齐的脆弱性或易被攻破的问题。

papers.title: REBEL: Reinforcement Learning via Regressing Relative Rewards
papers.short_title: REBEL: RL by Regressing Relative Rewards
papers.abstract: While originally developed for continuous control problems, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) has emerged as the work-horse of a variety of reinforcement learning (RL) applications, including the fine-tuning of generative models. Unfortunately, PPO requires multiple heuristics to enable stable convergence (e.g. value networks, clipping), and is notorious for its sensitivity to the precise implementation of these components. In response, we take a step back and ask what a minimalist RL algorithm for the era of generative models would look like. We propose REBEL, an algorithm that cleanly reduces the problem of policy optimization to regressing the relative reward between two completions to a prompt in terms of the policy, enabling strikingly lightweight implementation. In theory, we prove that fundamental RL algorithms like Natural Policy Gradient can be seen as variants of REBEL, which allows us to match the strongest known theoretical guarantees in terms of convergence and sample complexity in the RL literature. REBEL can also cleanly incorporate offline data and be extended to handle the intransitive preferences we frequently see in practice. Empirically, we find that REBEL provides a unified approach to language modeling and image generation with stronger or similar performance as PPO and DPO, all while being simpler to implement and more computationally efficient than PPO. When fine-tuning Llama-3-8B-Instruct, REBEL achieves strong performance in AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, and Open LLM Leaderboard.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the heuristic complexity and sensitivity of PPO for generative model fine-tuning by proposing a minimalist RL algorithm. REBEL reduces policy optimization to regressing the relative reward between two completions, yielding a lightweight implementation with strong theoretical guarantees akin to Natural Policy Gradient. Empirically, REBEL matches or exceeds PPO and DPO in language modeling and image generation tasks, while being simpler and more computationally efficient; it achieves strong results when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B-Instruct on standard benchmarks. The paper advances RL fine-tuning methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对PPO在生成模型微调中启发式复杂且敏感的缺点，提出了一种极简的RL算法。REBEL将策略优化简化为对两个补全的相对奖励进行回归，实现轻量实现并具有接近自然策略梯度的理论保证。实验表明，REBEL在语言和图像生成任务上的性能与PPO和DPO相当或更优，同时更简单高效；在Llama-3-8B-Instruct微调后于多个基准上取得优异成绩。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接涉及安全对齐的稳健性问题。

papers.title: Stress-Testing Capability Elicitation With Password-Locked Models
papers.abstract: To determine the safety of large language models (LLMs), AI developers must be able to assess their dangerous capabilities. But simple prompting strategies often fail to elicit an LLM's full capabilities. One way to elicit capabilities more robustly is to fine-tune the LLM to complete the task. In this paper, we investigate the conditions under which fine-tuning-based elicitation suffices to elicit capabilities. To do this, we introduce password-locked models, LLMs fine-tuned such that some of their capabilities are deliberately hidden. Specifically, these LLMs are trained to exhibit these capabilities only when a password is present in the prompt, and to imitate a much weaker LLM otherwise. Password-locked models enable a novel method of evaluating capabilities elicitation methods, by testing whether these password-locked capabilities can be elicited without using the password. We find that a few high-quality demonstrations are often sufficient to fully elicit password-locked capabilities. More surprisingly, fine-tuning can elicit other capabilities that have been locked using the same password, or even different passwords. Furthermore, when only evaluations, and not demonstrations, are available, approaches like reinforcement learning are still often able to elicit capabilities. Overall, our findings suggest that fine-tuning is an effective method of eliciting hidden capabilities of current models, but may be unreliable when high-quality demonstrations are not available, e.g. as may be the case when models' (hidden) capabilities exceed those of human demonstrators.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably eliciting dangerous capabilities from LLMs for safety evaluation, as simple prompting often fails to reveal hidden capabilities. To test elicitation methods, it introduces password-locked models—LLMs fine-tuned to exhibit certain capabilities only when a specific password is present, and otherwise behave as a weaker model. Experiments show that fine-tuning with a few high-quality demonstrations is often enough to fully elicit locked capabilities, and even can unlock capabilities secured by different passwords; reinforcement learning can also succeed using only evaluations. This work demonstrates that post-hoc safety alignment may be fragile, as hidden capabilities can be easily surfaced via fine-tuning, raising concerns about the robustness of alignment methods that rely on suppressing rather than removing dangerous knowledge.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了在安全评估中可靠地引出大语言模型危险能力的问题，因为简单的提示往往无法揭示隐藏的能力。为了测试引出方法，它引入了密码锁定模型——一种经过微调的模型，仅在提示中包含特定密码时才展现某些能力，否则伪装成较弱的模型。实验表明，使用少量高质量示例进行微调通常足以完全引出被锁定的能力，甚至可以解锁由相同或不同密码保护的其他能力；仅使用评估信号的强化学习方法也常常成功。这项工作表明，事后的安全对齐可能是脆弱的，因为隐藏的能力可以通过微调被轻易激发，这对依赖压制而非消除危险知识的对齐方法的鲁棒性提出了质疑。

papers.title: Who's asking? User personas and the mechanics of latent misalignment
papers.abstract: Despite investments in improving model safety, studies show that misaligned capabilities remain latent in safety-tuned models. In this work, we shed light on the mechanics of this phenomenon. First, we show that even when model generations are safe, harmful content can persist in hidden representations and can be extracted by decoding from earlier layers. Then, we show that whether the model divulges such content depends significantly on its perception of who it is talking to, which we refer to as user persona. In fact, we find manipulating user persona to be even more effective for eliciting harmful content than direct attempts to control model refusal. We study both natural language prompting and activation steering as control methods and show that activation steering is significantly more effective at bypassing safety filters. We investigate why certain personas break model safeguards and find that they enable the model to form more charitable interpretations of otherwise dangerous queries. Finally, we show we can predict a persona's effect on refusal given only the geometry of its steering vector.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses latent misalignment in safety-tuned LLMs, where harmful capabilities remain hidden despite safe outputs. It reveals that harmful content persists in hidden representations and can be extracted by decoding from earlier layers, and shows that a model’s willingness to disclose such content hinges on its perceived user persona. Through natural language prompting and activation steering, it finds that activation steering is more effective at bypassing safety filters, and that certain personas induce more charitable interpretations of dangerous queries, with persona effect predictable from steering vector geometry. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment by exposing a new attack surface that manipulates persona to surface latent misalignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了安全微调大语言模型中的潜在错位问题，即尽管输出安全，有害能力仍隐藏。它揭示有害内容残留在隐藏表示中，并可通过对早期层解码提取；模型是否透露这些内容显著取决于其对用户人设的感知。通过自然语言提示和激活引导两种控制方法，发现激活引导绕过安全过滤更为有效，某些人设能使模型对危险查询做出更宽容的解释，且人设效果可通过引导向量的几何形状预测。这直接表明后训练安全对齐是脆弱的，暴露了一个通过操纵用户人设来激发潜在错位的新攻击面。

papers.title: Axioms for AI Alignment from Human Feedback
papers.abstract: In the context of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), the reward function is generally derived from maximum likelihood estimation of a random utility model based on pairwise comparisons made by humans. The problem of learning a reward function is one of preference aggregation that, we argue, largely falls within the scope of social choice theory. From this perspective, we can evaluate different aggregation methods via established axioms, examining whether these methods meet or fail well-known standards. We demonstrate that both the Bradley-Terry-Luce Model and its broad generalizations fail to meet basic axioms. In response, we develop novel rules for learning reward functions with strong axiomatic guarantees. A key innovation from the standpoint of social choice is that our problem has a linear structure, which greatly restricts the space of feasible rules and leads to a new paradigm that we call linear social choice.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses reward function learning in RLHF by framing it as a preference aggregation problem within social choice theory. It evaluates the Bradley-Terry-Luce model and its generalizations against standard social choice axioms, demonstrating that they fail to meet basic requirements. The authors propose novel linear social choice rules that offer strong axiomatic guarantees by exploiting the linear structure inherent in the problem. This work advances alignment methodology with rigorous foundations but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文将从人类反馈中强化学习（RLHF）的奖励函数学习问题视为社会选择理论中的偏好聚合任务。通过社会选择公理评估Bradley-Terry-Luce模型及其推广，发现其不能满足基本公理，进而提出新型线性社会选择规则。这些规则利用问题固有的线性结构，提供了强有力的公理保证。该论文通过严格的公理化基础推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: BoNBoN Alignment for Large Language Models and the Sweetness of Best-of-n Sampling
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the problem of aligning samples from large language models to human preferences using best-of-$n$ sampling, where we draw $n$ samples, rank them, and return the best one. We consider two fundamental problems. First: what is the relationship between best-of-$n$ and approaches to alignment that train LLMs to output samples with a high expected reward (e.g., RLHF or DPO)? To answer this, we embed both the best-of-$n$ distribution and the sampling distributions learned by alignment procedures in a common class of tiltings of the base LLM distribution. We then show that, within this class, best-of-$n$ is essentially optimal in terms of the trade-off between win-rate against the base model vs KL distance from the base model. That is, best-of-$n$ is the best choice of alignment distribution if the goal is to maximize win rate. However, best-of-$n$ requires drawing $n$ samples for each inference, a substantial cost. To avoid this, the second problem we consider is how to fine-tune a LLM to mimic the best-of-$n$ sampling distribution. We derive BoNBoN Alignment to achieve this by exploiting the special structure of the best-of-$n$ distribution. Experiments show that BoNBoN alignment yields substantial improvements in producing a model that is preferred to the base policy while minimally affecting off-target aspects.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of aligning LLM outputs with human preferences via best-of-n sampling, investigating its relationship with training-based methods like RLHF. It proposes BoNBoN Alignment, a fine-tuning technique that mimics the best-of-n sampling distribution by exploiting its structure. Experiments show that BoNBoN-aligned models achieve significant preference improvements with minimal off-target effects. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决通过 best-of-n 采样使大语言模型输出符合人类偏好的问题，并研究其与基于训练的 RLHF 等方法的关系。提出 BoNBoN Alignment 微调技术，利用 best-of-n 分布的特殊结构来模仿该采样分布。实验表明，BoNBoN 对齐的模型在偏好上获得显著提升，且对非目标方面影响最小。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接讨论后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: WildGuard: Open One-stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
papers.abstract: We introduce WildGuard---an open, light-weight moderation tool for LLM safety that achieves three goals: (1) identifying malicious intent in user prompts, (2) detecting safety risks of model responses, and (3) determining model refusal rate. Together, WildGuard serves the increasing needs for automatic safety moderation and evaluation of LLM interactions, providing a one-stop tool with enhanced accuracy and broad coverage across 13 risk categories. While existing open moderation tools such as Llama-Guard2 score reasonably well in classifying straightforward model interactions, they lag far behind a prompted GPT-4, especially in identifying adversarial jailbreaks  and in evaluating models' refusals, a key measure for evaluating safety behaviors in model responses. To address these challenges, we construct WildGuardMix, a large-scale and carefully balanced multi-task safety moderation dataset with 92K labeled examples that cover vanilla (direct) prompts and adversarial jailbreaks, paired with various refusal and compliance responses. WildGuardMix is a combination of WildGuardTrain, the training data of WildGuard, and WildGuardTest, a high-quality human-annotated moderation test set with 5K labeled items covering broad risk scenarios.Through extensive evaluations on WildGuardTest and ten existing public benchmarks, we show that WildGuard establishes state-of-the-art performance in open-source safety moderation across all the three tasks compared to ten strong existing open-source moderation models (e.g., up to 25.3% improvement on refusal detection). Importantly, WildGuard matches and sometimes exceeds GPT-4 performance (e.g., up to 4.8% improvement on prompt harmfulness identification). WildGuard serves as a highly effective safety moderator in an LLM interface, reducing the success rate of jailbreak attacks from 79.8%  to 2.4%. We will make all our data, models and training/evaluation code publicly available under CC BY 4.0 license.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inadequacy of existing open-source LLM safety moderation tools in handling adversarial jailbreaks and accurately detecting model refusals, which are critical for evaluating safety alignment. It proposes WildGuard, a lightweight moderation model trained on WildGuardMix, a large-scale multi-task dataset covering direct prompts, jailbreaks, and refusal/compliance responses across 13 risk categories, enabling simultaneous identification of prompt harmfulness, response safety, and refusal. Evaluated on a new human-annotated test set and ten public benchmarks, WildGuard sets state-of-the-art among open-source moderators, matching or exceeding GPT-4, and when deployed as a safety moderator, reduces jailbreak success rates from 79.8% to 2.4%. This paper directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by showing that existing moderators are vulnerable to jailbreaks, but it demonstrates that fragility can be substantially reduced through improved moderation, suggesting that alignment can be hardened with better safety guardrails.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有开源LLM安全审核工具在处理对抗性越狱攻击和准确检测模型拒绝行为方面的不足，这些能力对评估安全对齐至关重要。提出WildGuard，一个基于大规模多任务数据集WildGuardMix训练的轻量级审核模型，该数据集涵盖直接提示、越狱攻击及拒绝/合规响应，覆盖13个风险类别，可同时识别提示有害性、响应安全性和拒绝行为。在人工标注测试集和十个公开基准上评估，WildGuard在开源审核模型中达到最优，与GPT-4持平甚至更优，部署后使越狱攻击成功率从79.8%降至2.4%。本文直接回应了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题：表明现有审核工具易受越狱攻击，但通过更好的审核可以显著降低脆弱性，说明对齐可通过更强的安全护栏得到加固。

papers.title: MedSafetyBench: Evaluating and Improving the Medical Safety of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) develop increasingly sophisticated capabilities and find applications in medical settings, it becomes important to assess their medical safety due to their far-reaching implications for personal and public health, patient safety, and human rights. However, there is little to no understanding of the notion of medical safety in the context of LLMs, let alone how to evaluate and improve it. To address this gap, we first define the notion of medical safety in LLMs based on the Principles of Medical Ethics set forth by the American Medical Association. We then leverage this understanding to introduce MedSafetyBench, the first benchmark dataset designed to measure the medical safety of LLMs. We demonstrate the utility of MedSafetyBench by using it to evaluate and improve the medical safety of LLMs. Our results show that publicly-available medical LLMs do not meet standards of medical safety and that fine-tuning them using MedSafetyBench improves their medical safety while preserving their medical performance. By introducing this new benchmark dataset, our work enables a systematic study of the state of medical safety in LLMs and motivates future work in this area, paving the way to mitigate the safety risks of LLMs in medicine. The benchmark dataset and code are available at https://github.com/AI4LIFE-GROUP/med-safety-bench.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the lack of medical safety standards for LLMs, defining medical safety based on AMA ethics and introducing MedSafetyBench, the first benchmark for evaluating medical safety. It shows that current medical LLMs fail to meet safety standards, but fine-tuning on MedSafetyBench improves safety while maintaining performance. This work advances alignment methodology by providing a domain-specific safety benchmark, though it does not directly investigate the fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLMs在医疗领域缺乏安全标准的问题，基于美国医学会伦理原则定义了医学安全性，并提出了首个评估医学安全性的基准MedSafetyBench。实验表明现有医学LLMs未达安全标准，但使用该基准微调可提升安全性同时保持性能。此项工作通过提供领域特定的安全基准推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Would I Lie To You? Inference Time Alignment of Language Models using Direct Preference Heads
papers.abstract: Pre-trained Language Models (LMs) exhibit strong zero-shot and in-context learning capabilities; however, their behaviors are often difficult to control. By utilizing Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), it is possible to fine-tune unsupervised LMs to follow instructions and produce outputs that reflect human preferences. Despite its benefits, RLHF has been shown to potentially harm a language model's reasoning capabilities and introduce artifacts such as hallucinations where the model may fabricate facts. To address this issue we introduce Direct Preference Heads (DPH), a fine-tuning framework that enables LMs to learn human preference signals through an auxiliary reward head without directly affecting the output distribution of the language modeling head. We perform a theoretical analysis of our objective function and find strong ties to Conservative Direct Preference Optimization (cDPO). Finally we evaluate our models on GLUE, RACE, and the GPT4All evaluation suite and demonstrate that our method produces models which achieve higher scores than those fine-tuned with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) or Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) alone.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the issue that RLHF fine-tuning can impair reasoning and induce hallucinations in language models. It proposes Direct Preference Heads (DPH), a framework that learns human preferences via an auxiliary reward head without modifying the language modeling head, enabling alignment during inference. Evaluated on GLUE, RACE, and GPT4All, DPH achieves higher scores than standalone SFT or DPO. While DPH suggests a less fragile alignment by preserving the base generation distribution, the paper does not directly examine the robustness of post-training alignment against adversarial attacks or out-of-distribution scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF微调可能损害语言模型推理能力并引入幻觉的问题，提出了直接偏好头（DPH）框架。DPH通过一个辅助奖励头学习人类偏好信号，而不改变语言建模头的输出分布，实现了推理时的对齐。在GLUE、RACE和GPT4All评测套件上，DPH取得了优于单独使用SFT或DPO微调的分数。虽然DPH通过保持基础生成分布来暗示更稳健的对齐，但论文并未直接研究后训练对齐在面对对抗攻击或分布外场景时的脆弱性。

papers.title: Query-Based Adversarial Prompt Generation
papers.abstract: Recent work has shown it is possible to construct adversarial examples that cause an aligned language model to emit harmful strings or perform harmful behavior. Existing attacks work either in the white-box setting (with full access to the model weights), or through transferability: the phenomenon that adversarial examples crafted on one model often remain effective on other models. We improve on prior work with a query-based attack that leverages API access to a remote language model to construct adversarial examples that cause the model to emit harmful strings with (much) higher probability than with transfer-only attacks. We validate our attack on GPT-3.5 and OpenAI's safety classifier; we can cause GPT-3.5 to emit harmful strings that current transfer attacks fail at, and we can evade the safety classifier with nearly 100% probability.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of constructing adversarial prompts that cause aligned language models to produce harmful outputs. It proposes a query-based attack that leverages black-box API access to iteratively refine adversarial prompts, improving over transfer-only attacks. The attack is evaluated on GPT-3.5 and OpenAI's safety classifier, achieving higher success rates in generating harmful strings and near-perfect safety classifier evasion. This work demonstrates that post-training safety alignment can be broken in a realistic black-box setting, directly supporting the view that alignment is a fragile module susceptible to adversarial bypass.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决如何构建对抗性提示，使对齐的语言模型生成有害输出的问题。提出一种基于查询的攻击方法，利用黑盒API访问迭代优化对抗提示，优于仅依赖迁移的攻击。在GPT-3.5和OpenAI安全分类器上评估，实现了更高的有害输出生成率和近乎100%的分类器绕过率。该研究表明后训练安全对齐可在现实黑盒条件下被攻破，直接支持了安全对齐是一个脆弱模块、容易被绕过和突破的观点。

papers.title: MLLMGuard: A Multi-dimensional Safety Evaluation Suite for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Powered by remarkable advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs), Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities in manifold tasks. However, the practical application scenarios of MLLMs are intricate, exposing them to potential malicious instructions and thereby posing safety risks. While current benchmarks do incorporate certain safety considerations, they often lack comprehensive coverage and fail to exhibit the necessary rigor and robustness. For instance, the common practice of employing GPT-4V as both the evaluator and a model to be evaluated lacks credibility, as it tends to exhibit a bias toward its own responses. In this paper, we present MLLMGuard, a multidimensional safety evaluation suite for MLLMs, including a bilingual image-text evaluation dataset, inference utilities, and a lightweight evaluator. MLLMGuard's assessment comprehensively covers two languages (English and Chinese) and five important safety dimensions (Privacy, Bias, Toxicity, Truthfulness, and Legality), each with corresponding rich subtasks. Focusing on these dimensions, our evaluation dataset is primarily sourced from platforms such as social media, and it integrates text-based and image-based red teaming techniques with meticulous annotation by human experts. This can prevent inaccurate evaluation caused by data leakage when using open-source datasets and ensures the quality and challenging nature of our benchmark. Additionally, a fully automated lightweight evaluator termed GuardRank is developed, which achieves significantly higher evaluation accuracy than GPT-4. Our evaluation results across 13 advanced models indicate that MLLMs still have a substantial journey ahead before they can be considered safe and responsible.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the lack of comprehensive safety benchmarks for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It introduces MLLMGuard, a bilingual evaluation suite covering five safety dimensions (Privacy, Bias, Toxicity, Truthfulness, Legality), with a carefully curated dataset and a lightweight evaluator called GuardRank. Testing 13 advanced MLLMs reveals that none are sufficiently safe, with significant risks remaining across all dimensions. While the work advances evaluation methodology, it does not directly investigate the fragility of safety alignment; however, the findings imply that current safety alignment in MLLMs is still far from robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型安全评测覆盖不全的问题，提出双语多维度安全评测套件MLLMGuard，涵盖隐私、偏见、毒性、真实性与合法性五大维度，并配套精心构建的数据集和轻量级评估器GuardRank。在13个先进模型上的测试表明，现有MLLM在多个安全维度上仍存在严重不足。该研究主要贡献在于评估方法论，虽然未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性，但结果间接暗示当前的安全对齐远未达到稳健水平。

papers.title: Selective Amnesia: A Continual Learning Approach to Forgetting in Deep Generative Models
papers.abstract: The recent proliferation of large-scale text-to-image models has led to growing concerns that such models may be misused to generate harmful, misleading, and inappropriate content. Motivated by this issue, we derive a technique inspired by continual learning to selectively forget concepts in pretrained deep generative models. Our method, dubbed Selective Amnesia, enables controllable forgetting  where a user can specify how a concept should be forgotten. Selective Amnesia can be applied to conditional variational likelihood models, which encompass a variety of popular deep generative frameworks, including variational autoencoders and large-scale text-to-image diffusion models. Experiments across different models demonstrate that our approach induces forgetting on a variety of concepts, from entire classes in standard datasets to celebrity and nudity prompts in text-to-image models.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the potential misuse of text-to-image models by proposing a method to selectively forget harmful concepts. It introduces Selective Amnesia, a continual learning approach that allows controllable forgetting in conditional variational likelihood models, including VAEs and diffusion models. Experiments show successful forgetting across various concepts, such as entire classes and sensitive prompts like nudity and celebrities. While the paper advances alignment methodology for generative models, it does not directly investigate the fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对文本到图像模型可能被滥用来生成有害内容的问题，提出了一种选择性遗忘概念的方法。提出了选择性遗忘（Selective Amnesia），一种基于持续学习的方法，可在条件变分似然模型（如VAE和扩散模型）中实现可控遗忘。实验表明，该方法能够有效地遗忘多种概念，包括标准数据集中的整个类以及名人、裸露等敏感提示词。尽管本文推进了生成模型的遗忘对齐方法，但并未直接研究安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Adaptive Preference Scaling for Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a prevalent approach to align AI systems with human values by learning rewards from human preference data. Due to various reasons, however, such data typically takes the form of rankings over pairs of trajectory segments, which fails to capture the varying strengths of preferences across different pairs. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive preference loss, underpinned by distributionally robust optimization (DRO), designed to address this uncertainty in preference strength. By incorporating an adaptive scaling parameter into the loss for each pair, our method increases the flexibility of the reward function. Specifically, it assigns small scaling parameters to pairs with ambiguous preferences, leading to more comparable rewards, and large scaling parameters to those with clear preferences for more distinct rewards. Computationally, our proposed loss function is strictly convex and univariate with respect to each scaling parameter, enabling its efficient optimization through a simple second-order algorithm. Our method is versatile and can be readily adapted to various preference optimization frameworks, including direct preference optimization (DPO). Our experiments with robotic control and natural language generation with large language models (LLMs) show that our method not only improves policy performance but also aligns reward function selection more closely with policy optimization, simplifying the hyperparameter tuning process.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation that standard RLHF treats all preference pairs equally, ignoring varying confidence levels. It proposes an adaptive preference loss using distributionally robust optimization to dynamically scale each pair's contribution based on preference strength. Evaluated on robotic control and LLM text generation, the method improves policy performance and simplifies hyperparameter tuning. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对标准RLHF中忽略偏好强度差异的问题，提出了一种基于分布鲁棒优化的自适应偏好损失，通过动态缩放参数反映偏好信心。在机器人控制和LLM文本生成上的实验表明，该方法能提升策略性能并简化超参数调整。该工作改进了对齐方法论，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Safe LoRA: The Silver Lining of Reducing Safety Risks when Finetuning Large Language Models
papers.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) such as Llama-2 or GPT-4 have shown impressive zero-shot performance, fine-tuning is still necessary to enhance their performance for customized datasets, domain-specific tasks, or other private needs. However, fine-tuning all parameters of LLMs requires significant hardware resources, which can be impractical for typical users. Therefore, parameter-efficient fine-tuning such as LoRA have emerged, allowing users to fine-tune LLMs without the need for considerable computing resources, with little performance degradation compared to fine-tuning all parameters. Unfortunately, recent studies indicate that fine-tuning can increase the risk to the safety of LLMs, even when data does not contain malicious content. To address this challenge, we propose Safe LoRA, a simple one-liner patch to the original LoRA implementation by introducing the projection of LoRA weights from selected layers to the safety-aligned subspace, effectively reducing the safety risks in LLM fine-tuning while maintaining utility. It is worth noting that Safe LoRA is a training-free and data-free approach, as it only requires the knowledge of the weights from the base and aligned LLMs. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that when fine-tuning on purely malicious data, Safe LoRA retains similar safety performance as the original aligned model. Moreover, when the fine-tuning dataset contains a mixture of both benign and malicious data, Safe LoRA mitigates the negative effect made by malicious data while preserving performance on downstream tasks. Our codes are available at \url{https://github.com/IBM/SafeLoRA}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the safety risks introduced when fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), even with benign data. It proposes Safe LoRA, a training-free and data-free method that projects LoRA weights onto a safety-aligned subspace using only the base and aligned model weights. Experiments demonstrate that Safe LoRA retains safety performance close to the aligned model on purely malicious data and mitigates safety degradation on mixed data while preserving downstream task utility. This work provides evidence that safety alignment can be fragile during fine-tuning but also that fragility can be effectively reduced with a simple weight projection, offering a hardening technique relevant to the robustness of post-training safety.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型微调过程中（即使使用良性数据）可能引入的安全风险问题，提出了一种名为 Safe LoRA 的方法。该方法无需训练、无需额外数据，仅利用基座模型和对齐后模型的权重，将选定层的 LoRA 权重投影到安全对齐的子空间中。实验表明，在纯恶意数据上微调时，Safe LoRA 能保持与原始对齐模型相近的安全性能；在混合数据上，则能减轻恶意数据带来的负面影响，同时维持下游任务性能。该研究展示了安全对齐在微调时可能存在的脆弱性，但通过简单的权重投影即可有效加固，为对齐鲁棒性讨论提供了一种增强技术。

papers.title: Efficient LLM Jailbreak via Adaptive Dense-to-sparse Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent research indicates that large language models (LLMs) are susceptible to jailbreaking attacks that can generate harmful content. This paper introduces a novel token-level attack method, Adaptive Dense-to-Sparse Constrained Optimization (ADC), which has been shown to successfully jailbreak multiple open-source LLMs. Drawing inspiration from the difficulties of discrete token optimization, our method relaxes the discrete jailbreak optimization into a continuous optimization process while gradually increasing the sparsity of the optimizing vectors. This technique effectively bridges the gap between discrete and continuous space optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that our method is more effective and efficient than state-of-the-art token-level methods. On Harmbench, our approach achieves the highest attack success rate on seven out of eight LLMs compared to the latest jailbreak methods. \textcolor{red}{Trigger Warning: This paper contains model behavior that can be offensive in nature.}
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to jailbreaking attacks that generate harmful content. It proposes Adaptive Dense-to-Sparse Constrained Optimization (ADC), a novel token-level attack that relaxes discrete optimization into a continuous process while gradually increasing sparsity to bridge the gap between continuous and discrete spaces. Evaluated on Harmbench, ADC achieves the highest attack success rate on seven out of eight open-source LLMs compared to state-of-the-art token-level methods. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, providing clear evidence that alignment can be effectively bypassed by sophisticated optimization-based attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大型语言模型（LLM）易受越狱攻击产生有害内容的问题，提出了一种新颖的令牌级攻击方法——自适应稠密到稀疏约束优化（ADC）。该方法将离散越狱优化松弛为连续优化过程，并逐步增加优化向量的稀疏性，从而弥合连续与离散空间优化的差距。在Harmbench上的实验表明，ADC在八个开源LLM中的七个上取得了最高的攻击成功率，优于现有令牌级方法。此研究直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，清晰证明了对齐机制可被复杂的优化攻击有效绕过。

papers.title: Toxicity Detection for Free
papers.abstract: Current LLMs are generally aligned to follow safety requirements and tend to refuse toxic prompts. However, LLMs can fail to refuse toxic prompts or be overcautious and refuse benign examples. In addition, state-of-the-art toxicity detectors have low TPRs at low FPR, incurring high costs in real-world applications where toxic examples are rare. In this paper, we introduce Moderation Using LLM Introspection (MULI), which detects toxic prompts using the information extracted directly from LLMs themselves. We found we can distinguish between benign and toxic prompts from the distribution of the first response token's logits. Using this idea, we build a robust detector of toxic prompts using a sparse logistic regression model on the first response token logits. Our scheme outperforms SOTA detectors under multiple metrics.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the problem of LLMs failing to refuse toxic prompts and existing toxicity detectors having low true positive rates at low false positive rates. It proposes MULI, a method that detects toxic prompts by inspecting the logits of the first response token from the LLM itself, using a sparse logistic regression model. Evaluated on multiple metrics, MULI outperforms state-of-the-art detectors, offering a cost-effective approach. The paper does not directly study alignment fragility but provides a hardening tool that leverages LLM internals to improve safety.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型无法拒绝有毒提示以及现有毒性检测器在低假阳性率下真阳性率低的问题，提出了MULI方法，通过检查模型自身第一个响应标记的logits分布，利用稀疏逻辑回归模型来检测有毒提示。实验表明，MULI在多项指标上优于现有最佳检测器，提供了一种高效的防御手段。本文并未直接探讨安全对齐的脆弱性，但通过利用LLM内部表征增强了安全机制。

papers.title: Gradient Cuff: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models by Exploring Refusal Loss Landscapes
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming a prominent generative AI tool, where the user enters a query and the LLM generates an answer. To reduce harm and misuse, efforts have been made to align these LLMs to human values using advanced training techniques such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). However, recent studies have highlighted the vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial jailbreak attempts aiming at subverting the embedded safety guardrails. To address this challenge, this paper defines and investigates the Refusal Loss of LLMs and then proposes a method called Gradient Cuff to detect jailbreak attempts. Gradient Cuff exploits the unique properties observed in the refusal loss landscape, including functional values and its smoothness, to design an effective two-step detection strategy. Experimental results on two aligned LLMs (LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and Vicuna-7B-V1.5) and six types of jailbreak attacks (GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR, TAP, Base64, and LRL) show that Gradient Cuff can significantly improve the LLM's rejection capability for malicious jailbreak queries, while maintaining the model's performance for benign user queries by adjusting the detection threshold.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of aligned LLMs to jailbreak attacks that bypass safety guardrails. It proposes Gradient Cuff, a two-step detection method that exploits properties of the refusal loss landscape, including functional values and smoothness. Evaluated on two LLMs and six diverse jailbreak attacks, Gradient Cuff significantly improves rejection of malicious queries while maintaining performance on benign inputs through threshold adjustment. While the paper presents a defense mechanism, it does not directly investigate the inherent robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对对齐后的大语言模型容易遭受越狱攻击绕过安全护栏的问题，提出了Gradient Cuff方法。该方法利用拒绝损失景观的函数值和平滑性等特性，设计了一种两步检测策略。在两个对齐模型和六种攻击上的实验表明，Gradient Cuff能显著提升对恶意越狱查询的拒绝能力，同时通过调整检测阈值保持对良性查询的性能。尽管本文提出了防御机制，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐的固有鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Unpacking DPO and PPO: Disentangling Best Practices for Learning from Preference Feedback
papers.short_title: Unpacking DPO and PPO: Best Practices
papers.abstract: Learning from preference feedback has emerged as an essential step for improving the generation quality and performance of modern language models (LMs). Despite its widespread use, the way preference-based learning is applied varies wildly, with differing data, learning algorithms, and evaluations used, making disentangling the impact of each aspect difficult. In this work, we identify four core aspects of preference-based learning: preference data, learning algorithm, reward model, and policy training prompts, systematically investigate the impact of these components on downstream model performance, and suggest a recipe for strong learning for preference feedback. Our findings indicate that all aspects are important for performance, with better preference data leading to the largest improvements, followed by the choice of learning algorithm, the use of improved reward models, and finally the use of additional unlabeled prompts for policy training. Notably, PPO outperforms DPO by up to 2.5% in math and 1.2% in general domains. High-quality preference data leads to improvements of up to 8% in instruction following and truthfulness. Despite significant gains of up to 5% in mathematical evaluation when scaling up reward models, we surprisingly observe marginal improvements in other categories.
papers.summary_en: This paper systematically investigates four core components of learning from preference feedback: preference data, learning algorithm, reward model, and policy training prompts. It finds that all aspects matter, with high-quality preference data leading to the largest gains (up to 8% in instruction following and truthfulness), followed by the choice of learning algorithm where PPO outperforms DPO by up to 2.5% in math, then improved reward models, and finally additional unlabeled prompts. This work advances alignment methodology by providing a recipe for strong preference-based learning, but it does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文系统研究了从偏好反馈中学习的四个核心组成部分：偏好数据、学习算法、奖励模型和策略训练提示，发现所有因素均重要，其中高质量偏好数据带来的提升最大（指令遵循与真实性提升高达8%），其次是学习算法选择（PPO在数学任务上比DPO高2.5%），然后是改进的奖励模型，最后是无标签提示。这项工作通过提供强偏好学习的配方推进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: One-Shot Safety Alignment for Large Language Models via Optimal Dualization
papers.abstract: The growing safety concerns surrounding large language models raise an urgent need to align them with diverse human preferences to simultaneously enhance their helpfulness and safety. A promising approach is to enforce safety constraints through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). For such constrained RLHF, typical Lagrangian-based primal-dual policy optimization methods are computationally expensive and often unstable. This paper presents a perspective of dualization that reduces constrained alignment to an equivalent unconstrained alignment problem. We do so by pre-optimizing a smooth and convex dual function that has a closed form. This shortcut eliminates the need for cumbersome primal-dual policy iterations, greatly reducing the computational burden and improving training stability. Our strategy leads to two practical algorithms in model-based and preference-based settings (MoCAN and PeCAN, respectively). A broad range of experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and merits of our algorithms.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high computational cost and training instability of Lagrangian primal-dual methods for constrained RLHF in LLM safety alignment. It reformulates constrained alignment as an unconstrained problem via optimal dualization, pre-optimizing a closed-form smooth convex dual function to bypass iterative primal-dual updates, yielding two algorithms: MoCAN (model-based) and PeCAN (preference-based). Experiments demonstrate effective safety alignment with reduced computation and improved stability. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了基于RLHF的约束安全对齐中拉格朗日原始-对偶优化方法计算开销大且训练不稳定的问题。提出通过最优对偶化将约束对齐转化为无约束对齐，利用闭式光滑凸对偶函数避免原始-对偶迭代，设计了模型型和偏好型两种算法（MoCAN和PeCAN）。大量实验表明，该方法能有效实现安全对齐，显著降低计算成本并提升训练稳定性。本文改进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性是否脆弱。

papers.title: Vaccine: Perturbation-aware Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
papers.abstract: The new paradigm of fine-tuning-as-a-service introduces a new attack surface for Large Language Models (LLMs): a few harmful data uploaded by users can easily trick the fine-tuning to produce an alignment-broken model. We conduct an empirical analysis and uncovera \textit{harmful embedding drift} phenomenon, showing a probable cause of the alignment-broken effect. Inspired by our findings, we propose Vaccine, a perturbation-aware alignment technique to mitigate the security risk of users  fine-tuning. The core idea of Vaccine is to produce invariant hidden embeddings by progressively adding crafted perturbation to them in the alignment phase. This enables the embeddings to withstand harmful perturbation from  un-sanitized user data in the fine-tuning phase. Our results on open source mainstream LLMs (e.g., Llama2, Opt, Vicuna) demonstrate that Vaccine can boost the robustness of alignment against harmful prompts induced embedding drift while reserving reasoning ability towards benign prompts. Our code is available at  https://github.com/git-disl/Vaccine.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLM safety alignment to harmful fine-tuning attacks, identifying a 'harmful embedding drift' as the root cause. It proposes Vaccine, a perturbation-aware alignment technique that adds crafted perturbations during alignment to produce invariant embeddings, making them resistant to drift from malicious fine-tuning data. Experiments on Llama2, Opt, and Vicuna show Vaccine significantly enhances robustness against harmful prompts while preserving reasoning on benign ones. This work directly tackles the fragility question by demonstrating that post-training alignment can be broken but also effectively hardened against fine-tuning-based subversion.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型安全对齐在有害微调攻击下的脆弱性，揭示“有害嵌入漂移”为根本原因。提出Vaccine方法，在微调对齐阶段逐步注入精心设计的扰动，使嵌入对恶意微调数据引起的漂移具有不变性。在Llama2、Opt、Vicuna等开源模型上的实验表明，Vaccine能显著提升对有害提示的鲁棒性，同时保持对良性提示的推理能力。该研究直接回应了核心问题，即后训练安全对齐并非绝对稳健，但可通过扰动感知对齐加固，说明对齐模块可被破坏但也可被强化。

papers.title: Lisa: Lazy Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
papers.abstract: Recent studies show that Large Language Models (LLMs) with safety alignment can be jail-broken by fine-tuning on a dataset mixed with harmful data. First time in the literature, we show that the jail-broken effect can be mitigated by separating states in the finetuning stage to optimize the alignment and user datasets. Unfortunately, our subsequent study shows that this simple Bi-State Optimization (BSO) solution experiences convergence instability when steps invested in its alignment state is too small, leading to downgraded alignment performance. By statistical analysis, we show that the \textit{excess drift} towards consensus could be a probable reason for the instability. To remedy this issue, we propose \textbf{L}azy(\textbf{i}) \textbf{s}afety \textbf{a}lignment (\textbf{Lisa}), which introduces a proximal term to constraint the drift of each state. Theoretically, the benefit of the proximal term is supported by the convergence analysis, wherein we show that a sufficient large proximal factor is necessary to guarantee Lisa's convergence. Empirically, our results on four downstream finetuning tasks show that Lisa with a proximal term can significantly increase alignment performance while maintaining the LLM's accuracy on the user tasks. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/git-disl/Lisa}.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs to harmful fine-tuning attacks, where mixing harmful data during fine-tuning can jailbreak the model. It proposes Lazy Safety Alignment (Lisa), which adds a proximal term to stabilize the Bi-State Optimization (BSO) process and prevent excessive drift. Evaluated on four downstream tasks, Lisa significantly increases alignment performance while preserving utility accuracy. The work directly engages with the fragility of post-training alignment by demonstrating a specific attack surface (harmful fine-tuning) and introducing a robust defense, thereby showing that alignment can be hardened against such bypasses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对安全对齐的大语言模型在有害微调攻击下的脆弱性问题，即微调时混入有害数据可导致模型越狱。提出Lazy Safety Alignment（Lisa）方法，通过引入近端项约束双状态优化中的状态漂移，提升稳定性。在四个下游任务上的评估表明，Lisa在大幅提升对齐性能的同时保持了准确性。该研究直接回应了后训练对齐的鲁棒性问题：揭示了有害微调这一攻击面，并给出有效的加固方案，证明对齐可通过方法改进来抵御此类绕过。

papers.title: What Makes and Breaks Safety Fine-tuning? A Mechanistic Study
papers.abstract: Safety fine-tuning helps align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences for their safe deployment. To better understand the underlying factors that make models safe via safety fine-tuning, we design a synthetic data generation framework that captures salient aspects of an unsafe input by modeling the interaction between the task the model is asked to perform (e.g.,"design") versus the specific concepts the task is asked to be performed upon (e.g., a"cycle"vs. a"bomb"). Using this, we investigate three well-known safety fine-tuning methods -- supervised safety fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and unlearning -- and provide significant evidence demonstrating that these methods minimally transform MLP weights to specifically align unsafe inputs into its weights' null space. This yields a clustering of inputs based on whether the model deems them safe or not. Correspondingly, when an adversarial input (e.g., a jailbreak) is provided, its activations are closer to safer samples, leading to the model processing such an input as if it were safe. We validate our findings, wherever possible, on real-world models -- specifically, Llama-2 7B and Llama-3 8B.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates what makes safety fine-tuning effective and what causes it to fail, focusing on three alignment methods: supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and unlearning. The authors design a synthetic framework that captures the interaction between task and concept to analyze model internals, revealing that these methods minimally alter MLP weights to map unsafe inputs into the weight null space, inducing a safety-based clustering of activations. They show that jailbreak attacks succeed by producing activations near the safe cluster, causing the model to process adversarial inputs as safe, and validate findings on Llama-2 7B and Llama-3 8B. This study exposes a fundamental mechanistic fragility: post-training safety alignment creates a shallow separation that is easily bridged, directly demonstrating that safety modules are not robust and can be bypassed through activation proximity.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探究了安全微调为何有效又为何失效，重点关注监督微调、DPO和遗忘三种对齐方法。作者设计了一个捕捉任务与概念交互的合成框架以分析模型内部机制，发现这些方法仅对MLP权重做最小变换，将不安全输入映射到权重的零空间，从而诱导出基于安全性的激活聚类。他们证明越狱攻击通过产生靠近安全聚类的激活来使模型将对抗输入当作安全输入处理，并在Llama-2 7B和Llama-3 8B上验证了发现。该研究揭露了一种根本的机制脆弱性：后训练安全对齐形成的浅层隔离极易被跨越，直接表明安全模块并不稳健，可通过激活邻近性绕过。

papers.title: TAIA: Large Language Models are Out-of-Distribution Data Learners
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning on task-specific question-answer pairs is a predominant method for enhancing the performance of instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) on downstream tasks. However, in certain specialized domains, such as healthcare or harmless content generation, it is nearly impossible to obtain a large volume of high-quality data that matches the downstream distribution. To improve the performance of LLMs in data-scarce domains with domain-mismatched data, we re-evaluated the Transformer architecture and discovered that not all parameter updates during fine-tuning contribute positively to downstream performance. Our analysis reveals that within the self-attention and feed-forward networks, only the fine-tuned attention parameters are particularly beneficial when the training set's distribution does not fully align with the test set. Based on this insight, we propose an effective inference-time intervention method: Training All parameters but Inferring with only Attention (\trainallInfAttn). We empirically validate \trainallInfAttn using two general instruction-tuning datasets and evaluate it on seven downstream tasks involving math, reasoning, and knowledge understanding across LLMs of different parameter sizes and fine-tuning techniques. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that \trainallInfAttn achieves superior improvements compared to both the fully fine-tuned model and the base model in most scenarios, with significant performance gains. The high tolerance of \trainallInfAttn to data mismatches makes it resistant to jailbreaking tuning and enhances specialized tasks using general data. Code is available in \url{https://github.com/pixas/TAIA_LLM}.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles performance degradation when fine-tuning LLMs on data that mismatches the target distribution, common in specialized domains. It proposes TAIA (Training All but Inferring with only Attention), which uses all fine-tuned parameters during training but only the attention parameters during inference, based on the finding that attention updates consistently aid generalization under domain shift. Evaluated on seven tasks across math, reasoning, and knowledge with various model sizes, TAIA outperforms both fully fine-tuned and base models, showing resilience to data mismatch and even resisting jailbreaking. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training alignment: it reveals a mechanistic weakness where non-attention updates harm OOD performance, and offers a simple hardening method, suggesting alignment can be brittle but mitigable.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对微调数据与目标分布不匹配时大语言模型性能下降的问题，在数据稀缺领域尤为突出。提出TAIA方法，训练时更新所有参数但推理时仅使用注意力参数，源于发现仅注意力参数的更新对分布偏移有益。在覆盖数学、推理和知识的七个任务上跨不同模型规模和微调技术评估，TAIA显著优于全参数微调与基座模型，对数据不匹配容忍度高，甚至可抵抗越狱调优。该工作直接回应后训练对齐鲁棒性之问：揭示了非注意力参数更新损害分布外性能的机制弱点，并提供简易加固方法，表明对齐虽脆弱但可修复。

papers.title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models Against Moderation Guardrails via Cipher Characters
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are typically harmless but remain vulnerable to carefully crafted prompts known as ``jailbreaks'', which can bypass protective measures and induce harmful behavior. Recent advancements in LLMs have incorporated moderation guardrails that can filter outputs, which trigger processing errors for certain malicious questions. Existing red-teaming benchmarks often neglect to include questions that trigger moderation guardrails, making it difficult to evaluate jailbreak effectiveness. To address this issue, we introduce JAMBench, a harmful behavior benchmark designed to trigger and evaluate moderation guardrails. JAMBench involves 160 manually crafted instructions covering four major risk categories at multiple severity levels. Furthermore, we propose a jailbreak method, JAM (Jailbreak Against Moderation), designed to attack moderation guardrails using jailbreak prefixes to bypass input-level filters and a fine-tuned shadow model functionally equivalent to the guardrail model to generate cipher characters to bypass output-level filters. Our extensive experiments on four LLMs demonstrate that JAM achieves higher jailbreak success ($\sim$ $\times$ 19.88) and lower filtered-out rates ($\sim$ $\times$ 1/6) than baselines.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs with moderation guardrails that filter harmful outputs, noting that existing red-teaming benchmarks fail to evaluate jailbreaks against such filters. It proposes JAMBench, a benchmark with 160 instructions designed to trigger these guardrails, and JAM, a jailbreak method that uses jailbreak prefixes to bypass input filters and a fine-tuned shadow model to generate cipher characters that evade output filters. Experiments on four LLMs show JAM achieves about 19.88× higher jailbreak success and reduces filtered-out rates to one-sixth compared to baselines. This work directly demonstrates that post-training safety alignment, including moderation guardrails, can be fragile and easily bypassed through a new attack surface (cipher characters), highlighting the non-robust nature of current safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对配备输出过滤审核机制的LLM在对抗性越狱攻击中的脆弱性，指出当前红队测试基准忽略了触发审核过滤的恶意问题。提出了JAMBench基准（包含160条触发过滤的指令）和JAM越狱方法，该方法使用越狱前缀绕过输入过滤，并利用微调的影子模型生成密文字符以绕过输出过滤。在四个LLM上的实验表明，JAM的越狱成功率比基线高约19.88倍，过滤率降至基线的六分之一。该研究直接证明，包括审核过滤在内的后训练安全对齐可能脆弱，容易通过新的攻击面（密文字符）被绕过，揭示了当前安全机制的非鲁棒性。

papers.title: Preference Alignment with Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We present Preference Flow Matching (PFM), a new framework for preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) that streamlines the integration of preferences into an arbitrary class of pre-trained models. Existing PbRL methods require fine-tuning pre-trained models, which presents challenges such as scalability, inefficiency, and the need for model modifications, especially with black-box APIs like GPT-4. In contrast, PFM utilizes flow matching techniques to directly learn from preference data, thereby reducing the dependency on extensive fine-tuning of pre-trained models. By leveraging flow-based models, PFM transforms less preferred data into preferred outcomes, and effectively aligns model outputs with human preferences without relying on explicit or implicit reward function estimation, thus avoiding common issues like overfitting in reward models. We provide theoretical insights that support our method's alignment with standard PbRL objectives. Experimental results indicate the practical effectiveness of our method, offering a new direction in aligning a pre-trained model to preference. Our code is available at https://github.com/jadehaus/preference-flow-matching.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the inefficiency and scalability issues of existing preference-based reinforcement learning methods that require fine-tuning pre-trained models. It proposes Preference Flow Matching (PFM), which uses flow matching to directly align model outputs with human preferences by transforming less preferred data into preferred outcomes without explicit reward estimation. Experimental results demonstrate the practical effectiveness of this approach, offering a new direction for preference alignment. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有基于偏好的强化学习方法需微调预训练模型带来的低效与扩展性问题，提出偏好流匹配（PFM），利用流匹配技术直接对齐人类偏好，将非偏好数据转化为偏好输出，无需显式奖励估计。实验验证了方法的有效性，为偏好对齐开辟了新途径。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探究安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: WildTeaming at Scale: From In-the-Wild Jailbreaks to (Adversarially) Safer Language Models
papers.short_title: WildTeaming: Mining Jailbreaks for Safer LMs
papers.abstract: We introduce WildTeaming, an automatic red-teaming framework that mines in-the-wild user-chatbot interactions to discover 5.7K unique clusters of novel jailbreak tactics, and then composes selections of multiple mined tactics for systematic exploration of novel and even more challenging jailbreaks.Compared to prior work that performed red-teaming via recruited human workers, gradient-based optimization, or iterative revision with large language models (LLMs), our work investigates jailbreaks from chatbot users in-the-wild who were not specifically instructed to break the system.  WildTeaming reveals previously unidentified vulnerabilities of frontier LLMs, resulting in more diverse and successful adversarial attacks compared to state-of-the-art jailbreaking methods. While there exist many datasets for jailbreak evaluation, very few open-source datasets exist for jailbreak training, as safety training data has been closed among all frontier models even when their weights are open. Therefore, with WildTeaming we create WildJailbreak, a large-scale open-source synthetic safety dataset with 262K vanilla (direct request) and adversarial (complex jailbreak) prompt-response pairs. In order to mitigate exaggerated safety behaviors, WildJailbreak provides two contrastive types of queries: 1) harmful queries (both vanilla and adversarial) and 2) benign queries that resemble harmful queries in form but contain no harmful intent. As WildJailbreak considerably upgrades the quality and scale of existing safety resources, it uniquely enables us to examine the scaling effects of data and the interplay of data properties and model capabilities during safety training. Through extensive model training and evaluations, we identify the training properties that enable an ideal balance of safety behaviors: appropriate safeguarding without over-refusal, effective handling of both vanilla and adversarial queries, and minimal, if any, decrease in general capabilities. All the components of WildJailbreak contribute to achieving balanced safety behaviors of models
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to jailbreak attacks and the lack of open-source safety training data that covers adversarial jailbreaks. It proposes WildTeaming, an automatic red-teaming framework that mines in-the-wild user-chatbot interactions to discover novel jailbreak tactics and composes them to generate challenging jailbreaks, creating the WildJailbreak dataset. Through extensive training and evaluations, they identify properties that achieve balanced safety: appropriate safeguarding without over-refusal, effective handling of vanilla and adversarial queries, and minimal capability degradation. The paper demonstrates that safety alignment can be broken by novel jailbreaks mined from real users but also strengthened via adversarial training with such data, suggesting a fragile yet fortifiable module.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大语言模型易受越狱攻击的脆弱性问题及缺乏涵盖对抗性越狱的开源安全训练数据的问题。提出WildTeaming自动红队框架，通过挖掘真实用户-聊天机器人互动发现新的越狱策略并组合以生成挑战性越狱，构建了WildJailbreak数据集。通过广泛训练与评估，确定了实现平衡安全行为的属性：适度防护而无过度拒绝、有效处理普通与对抗性查询及最小化能力下降。论文表明，从真实用户挖掘的新颖越狱可攻破安全对齐，但通过此类数据对抗训练又能强化模型，说明安全对齐虽脆弱但可加固。

papers.title: Aligner: Efficient Alignment by Learning to Correct
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs) and ever-evolving practical requirements, finding an efficient and effective alignment method has never been more critical. However, the tension between the complexity of current alignment methods and the need for rapid iteration in deployment scenarios necessitates the development of a model-agnostic alignment approach that can operate under these constraints. In this paper, we introduce Aligner, a novel and simple alignment paradigm that learns the correctional residuals between preferred and dispreferred answers using a small model. Designed as a model-agnostic, plug-and-play module, Aligner can be directly applied to various open-source and API-based models with only one-off training, making it suitable for rapid iteration. Notably, Aligner can be applied to any powerful, large-scale upstream models. Moreover, it can even iteratively bootstrap the upstream models using corrected responses as synthetic human preference data, breaking through the model's performance ceiling. Our experiments demonstrate performance improvements by deploying the same Aligner model across 11 different LLMs, evaluated on the 3H dimensions (helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty). Specifically, Aligner-7B has achieved an average improvement of 68.9% in helpfulness and 23.8% in harmlessness across the tested LLMs while also effectively reducing hallucination. In the Alpaca-Eval leaderboard, stacking Aligner-2B on GPT-4 Turbo improved its LC Win Rate from 55.0% to 58.3%, surpassing GPT-4 Omni's 57.5% Win Rate (community report).
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the need for efficient, model-agnostic alignment methods that can keep pace with rapid LLM development and deployment. It proposes Aligner, a small plug-and-play model that learns correctional residuals between preferred and dispreferred answers, enabling one-off training and iterative bootstrapping of upstream models. Evaluated across 11 diverse LLMs, Aligner-7B improved helpfulness by 68.9% and harmlessness by 23.8% on average, while Aligner-2B stacked on GPT-4 Turbo boosted its LC Win Rate from 55.0% to 58.3%. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly examine whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 针对大语言模型快速迭代中高效、模型无关的对齐需求，本文提出Aligner，一种学习偏好与非偏好答案间修正残差的小型即插即用模型，支持一次性训练和用修正数据迭代提升上游模型。在11个不同LLM上评估，Aligner-7B平均提升帮助性68.9%、无害性23.8%，且Aligner-2B叠加GPT-4 Turbo将LC Win Rate从55.0%提至58.3%。该方法推动了对齐方法论的发展，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或易被绕过性。

papers.title: BeaverTails: Towards Improved Safety Alignment of LLM via a Human-Preference Dataset
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the \textsc{BeaverTails} dataset, aimed at fostering research on safety alignment in large language models (LLMs). This dataset uniquely separates annotations of helpfulness and harmlessness for question-answering pairs, thus offering distinct perspectives on these crucial attributes. In total, we have gathered safety meta-labels for 30,207 question-answer (QA) pairs and 30,144 pairs of expert comparison data for both the helpfulness and harmlessness metrics. In total, we have gathered safety meta-labels for 333,963 question-answer (QA) pairs and 361,903 pairs of expert comparison data for both the helpfulness and harmlessness metrics. We further showcase applications of BeaverTails in content moderation and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), emphasizing its potential for practical safety measures in LLMs. We believe this dataset provides vital resources for the community, contributing towards the safe development and deployment of LLMs. Our project page is available at the following URL: https://sites.google.com/view/pku-beavertails. Warning: this paper contains example data that may be offensive or harmful.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of safety alignment in large language models (LLMs) by introducing a dataset that explicitly separates helpfulness and harmlessness annotations. The BeaverTails dataset provides safety meta-labels for over 300,000 QA pairs and expert comparison data for both metrics, supporting nuanced evaluation. Its utility is demonstrated through content moderation and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) applications. This work advances alignment resources but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过引入一个明确区分有用性和无害性标注的数据集，应对大语言模型安全对齐的挑战。BeaverTails数据集为超过30万对问答提供了安全元标签及专家比较数据，支持细粒度评估。其效用通过内容审核和基于人类反馈的强化学习应用得到展示。该工作推进了对齐资源建设，但未直接探究训练后安全机制的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: The PRISM Alignment Dataset: What Participatory, Representative and Individualised Human Feedback Reveals About the Subjective and Multicultural Alignment of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Human feedback is central to the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, open questions remain about the methods (how), domains (where), people (who) and objectives (to what end) of feedback processes. To navigate these questions, we introduce PRISM, a new dataset which maps the sociodemographics and stated preferences of 1,500 diverse participants from 75 countries, to their contextual preferences and fine-grained feedback in 8,011 live conversations with 21 LLMs. With PRISM, we contribute (i) wider geographic and demographic participation in feedback; (ii) census-representative samples for two countries (UK, US); and (iii) individualised ratings that link to detailed participant profiles, permitting personalisation and attribution of sample artefacts. We target subjective and multicultural perspectives on value-laden and controversial issues, where we expect interpersonal and cross-cultural disagreement. We use PRISM in three case studies to demonstrate the need for careful consideration of which humans provide alignment data.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses open questions about who provides human feedback for LLM alignment and how demographics shape subjective preferences. It introduces PRISM, a dataset of 8,011 conversations with 21 LLMs rated by 1,500 diverse participants from 75 countries, including census-representative samples for the UK and US, linking detailed participant profiles to fine-grained ratings. Through case studies, it shows that demographic and cultural factors significantly affect alignment feedback, emphasizing the need for inclusive feedback processes. While the paper advances alignment data methodology by exposing the subjective and multicultural nature of human preferences, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨了LLM对齐中由谁提供人类反馈以及人口统计学如何塑造主观偏好的开放问题。它引入了PRISM数据集，包含来自75个国家1500名多样化参与者对21个LLM的8011场对话评分，并关联了详细的参与者概况，包括英美两国的普查代表性样本。案例研究表明，人口和文化因素显著影响对齐反馈，强调了包容性反馈流程的必要性。该论文通过揭示人类偏好的主观性和多元文化性推动了对齐数据方法学，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐是否鲁棒或易于被绕过。

papers.title: OpenAssistant Conversations - Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences has proven to drastically improve usability and has driven rapid adoption as demonstrated by ChatGPT. Alignment techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) greatly reduce the required skill and domain knowledge to effectively harness the capabilities of LLMs, increasing their accessibility and utility across various domains. However, state-of-the-art alignment techniques like RLHF rely on high-quality human feedback data, which is expensive to create and often remains proprietary. In an effort to democratize research on large-scale alignment, we release OpenAssistant Conversations, a human-generated, human-annotated assistant-style conversation corpus consisting of 161,443 messages in 35 different languages, annotated with 461,292 quality ratings, resulting in over 10,000 complete and fully annotated conversation trees. The corpus is a product of a worldwide crowd-sourcing effort involving over 13,500 volunteers. Models trained on OpenAssistant Conversations show consistent improvements on standard benchmarks over respective base models. We release our code and data under a fully permissive licence.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high cost and proprietary nature of human feedback data for aligning large language models by introducing an open, crowd-sourced dataset. It releases OpenAssistant Conversations, a multilingual assistant-style conversation corpus with quality ratings, created by over 13,500 volunteers. Models fine-tuned on this dataset show consistent improvements on standard benchmarks over base models. The paper advances alignment methodology by democratizing data access but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文通过创建开放的众包数据集，解决了大型语言模型对齐中人类反馈数据昂贵且专有的问题。它发布了OpenAssistant Conversations，一个由超过13,500名志愿者生成的、包含质量评分的多语言助手式对话语料库。在该数据集上微调的模型在标准基准上相比基础模型表现出一致改进。本文通过民主化数据访问推进了对齐方法学，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: INDICT: Code Generation with Internal Dialogues of Critiques for Both Security and Helpfulness
papers.short_title: INDICT: Code Generation with Dual Critiques
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) for code are typically trained to align with natural language instructions to closely follow their intentions and requirements. However, in many practical scenarios, it becomes increasingly challenging for these models to navigate the intricate boundary between helpfulness and safety, especially against highly complex yet potentially malicious instructions. In this work, we introduce INDICT: a new framework that empowers LLMs with Internal Dialogues of Critiques for both safety and helpfulness guidance. The internal dialogue is a dual cooperative system between a safety-driven critic and a helpfulness-driven critic. Each critic provides analysis against the given task and corresponding generated response, equipped with external knowledge queried through relevant code snippets and tools like web search and code interpreter. We engage the dual critic system in both code generation stage as well as code execution stage, providing preemptive and post-hoc guidance respectively to LLMs. We evaluated INDICT on 8 diverse tasks across 8 programming languages from 5 benchmarks, using LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. We observed that our approach can provide an advanced level of critiques of both safety and helpfulness analysis, significantly improving the quality of output codes ($+10\%$ absolute improvements in all models).
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of balancing helpfulness and safety in LLM code generation for complex, potentially malicious instructions. It proposes INDICT, a framework that incorporates safety-driven and helpfulness-driven dual critics providing internal dialogues with external knowledge, guiding both code generation and execution. Evaluated across diverse tasks and models, it yields a 10% absolute improvement in output code quality. This paper advances alignment methodology for code generation but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了大模型代码生成中在应对复杂且潜在恶意指令时，在有益性与安全性之间取得平衡的挑战。它提出了INDICT框架，融合了安全导向与有益性导向的双重批评机制，通过内部对话并利用外部知识，在代码生成与执行阶段提供指导。在多种任务和模型上的评估显示，输出代码质量绝对提升了10%。本文推进了代码生成的对齐方法，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Representation Editing: A Control Perspective
papers.short_title: RE-Control: LLM Alignment via Repr Edit
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human objectives is crucial for real-world applications. However, fine-tuning LLMs for alignment often suffers from unstable training and requires substantial computing resources. Test-time alignment techniques, such as prompting and guided decoding, do not modify the underlying model, and their performance remains dependent on the original model's capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose aligning LLMs through representation editing. The core of our method is to view a pre-trained autoregressive LLM as a discrete-time stochastic dynamical system. To achieve alignment for specific objectives, we introduce external control signals into the state space of this language dynamical system. We train a value function directly on the hidden states according to the Bellman equation, enabling gradient-based optimization to obtain the optimal control signals at test time. Our experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing test-time alignment techniques while requiring significantly fewer resources compared to fine-tuning methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/Lingkai-Kong/RE-Control.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenges of aligning LLMs with human objectives, where fine-tuning suffers from instability and high resource costs, and test-time alignment methods like prompting are limited by the model's original capabilities. It proposes aligning LLMs through representation editing by treating the model as a discrete-time stochastic dynamical system and injecting optimal control signals into hidden states, learned via a value function trained with the Bellman equation. Experiments show the method outperforms existing test-time alignment techniques and requires significantly fewer resources than fine-tuning. This paper advances alignment methodology by making test-time alignment more effective and efficient, but it does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型与人类目标对齐的挑战，微调常面临不稳定和高资源消耗，而提示等测试时对齐方法受限于模型原始能力。提出通过表征编辑对齐LLM，将预训练自回归模型视为离散时间随机动态系统，在隐状态中注入最优控制信号，利用贝尔曼方程训练价值函数以在测试时优化控制。实验表明该方法优于现有测试时对齐技术，且资源消耗远低于微调。本文改进了测试时对齐的有效性和效率，但未直接研究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Perplexity-aware Correction for Robust Alignment with Noisy Preferences
papers.abstract: Alignment techniques are critical in ensuring that large language models (LLMs) output helpful and harmless content by enforcing the LLM-generated content to align with human preferences. However, the existence of noisy preferences (NPs), where the responses are mistakenly labelled as chosen or rejected, could spoil the alignment, thus making the LLMs generate useless and even malicious content. Existing methods mitigate the issue of NPs from the loss perspective by adjusting the alignment loss based on a clean validation dataset.Orthogonal to these loss-oriented methods, we propose perplexity-aware correction (PerpCorrect) from the data perspective for robust alignment which detects and corrects NPs based on the differences between the perplexity of the chosen and rejected responses (dubbed as PPLDiff). Intuitively, a higher PPLDiff indicates a higher probability of the NP because a rejected/chosen response which is mistakenly labelled as chosen/rejected is less preferable to be generated by an aligned LLM, thus having a higher/lower perplexity.PerpCorrect works in three steps: (1) PerpCorrect aligns a surrogate LLM using the clean validation data to make the PPLDiff able to distinguish clean preferences (CPs) and NPs. (2) PerpCorrect further aligns the surrogate LLM by incorporating the reliable clean training data whose PPLDiff is extremely small and reliable noisy training data whose PPLDiff is extremely large after correction to boost the discriminatory power.(3) Detecting and correcting NPs according to the PPLDiff obtained by the aligned surrogate LLM to obtain a denoised training dataset for robust alignment.Comprehensive experiments validate that our proposed PerpCorrect can achieve state-of-the-art alignment performance under NPs.Notably, PerpCorrect demonstrates practical utility by requiring only a modest amount of validation data and being compatible with various alignment techniques. Our code is available at PerpCorrect.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of noisy preferences (NPs) in alignment training data, where chosen/rejected labels are incorrect, causing LLMs to produce harmful content. It proposes PerpCorrect, a data-level method that detects and corrects NPs by computing the perplexity difference (PPLDiff) between chosen and rejected responses, using a surrogate LLM fine-tuned on clean validation data. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art alignment performance under NPs with only modest validation data, compatible with various alignment techniques. The work directly exposes the fragility of post-training alignment to data noise and offers an effective hardening approach.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决对齐训练数据中的噪声偏好问题，即标注为选择/拒绝的回复存在错误，导致大语言模型生成有害内容。提出PerpCorrect，一种基于数据的方法，通过计算选择与拒绝回复的困惑度差异（PPLDiff），并利用在干净验证数据上微调的替代模型来检测和纠正噪声偏好。大量实验表明，在仅需少量验证数据且兼容多种对齐技术的前提下，该方法在噪声偏好下实现了最优对齐性能。该工作直接揭示了后训练对齐对数据噪声的脆弱性，并提供了有效的加固手段。

papers.title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges of Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.short_title: Challenges of Partial Observability in RLHF
papers.abstract: Past analyses of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) assume that the human evaluators fully observe the environment. What happens when human feedback is based only on partial observations? We formally define two failure cases: deceptive inflation and overjustification. Modeling the human as Boltzmann-rational w.r.t. a belief over trajectories, we prove conditions under which RLHF is guaranteed to result in policies that deceptively inflate their performance, overjustify their behavior to make an impression, or both. Under the new assumption that the human's partial observability is known and accounted for, we then analyze how much information the feedback process provides about the return function. We show that sometimes, the human's feedback determines the return function uniquely up to an additive constant, but in other realistic cases, there is irreducible ambiguity. We propose exploratory research directions to help tackle these challenges, experimentally validate both the theoretical concerns and potential mitigations, and caution against blindly applying RLHF in partially observable settings.
papers.summary_en: The paper identifies that standard RLHF assumes full human observability, but when humans only partially observe the environment, policies can deceptively inflate their performance or overjustify actions.
