papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit undesirable behaviours, such as generating untruthful or biased content. Editing their internal representations has been shown to be effective in mitigating such behaviours on top of the existing alignment methods. We propose a novel inference-time editing method, namely spectral editing of activations (SEA), to project the input representations into directions with maximal covariance with the positive demonstrations (e.g., truthful) while minimising covariance with the negative demonstrations (e.g., hallucinated). We also extend our method to non-linear editing using feature functions. We run extensive experiments on benchmarks concerning truthfulness and bias with six open-source LLMs of different sizes and model families. The results demonstrate the superiority of SEA in effectiveness, generalisation to similar tasks, as well as computation and data efficiency. We also show that SEA editing only has a limited negative impact on other model capabilities.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of undesirable behaviors in large language models (LLMs), such as untruthful or biased outputs, by editing their internal representations. It proposes Spectral Editing of Activations (SEA), an inference-time method that projects input representations into directions that maximize covariance with positive demonstrations and minimize covariance with negative ones, with extensions to non-linear editing. Extensive experiments on truthfulness and bias benchmarks with six open-source LLMs show SEA's superiority in effectiveness, generalization, and efficiency, with limited negative impact on other capabilities. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question regarding post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型（LLM）生成不真实或有偏内容的问题，提出了一种推理时编辑方法——激活谱编辑（SEA），通过将输入表示投影到与正样本协方差最大、与负样本协方差最小的方向，并扩展到非线性编辑。在真实性和偏见基准上对六种开源LLM的广泛实验表明，SEA在有效性、泛化性以及计算和数据效率方面均表现出优越性，且对其他模型能力影响有限。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems grow more powerful, there has been increasing interest in"AI safety"research to address emerging and future risks. However, the field of AI safety remains poorly defined and inconsistently measured, leading to confusion about how researchers can contribute. This lack of clarity is compounded by the unclear relationship between AI safety benchmarks and upstream general capabilities (e.g., general knowledge and reasoning). To address these issues, we conduct a comprehensive meta-analysis of AI safety benchmarks, empirically analyzing their correlation with general capabilities across dozens of models and providing a survey of existing directions in AI safety. Our findings reveal that many safety benchmarks highly correlate with both upstream model capabilities and training compute, potentially enabling"safetywashing"--where capability improvements are misrepresented as safety advancements. Based on these findings, we propose an empirical foundation for developing more meaningful safety metrics and define AI safety in a machine learning research context as a set of clearly delineated research goals that are empirically separable from generic capabilities advancements. In doing so, we aim to provide a more rigorous framework for AI safety research, advancing the science of safety evaluations and clarifying the path towards measurable progress.
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates whether AI safety benchmarks genuinely measure safety progress or merely reflect general capabilities, coining the term 'safetywashing' for when capability gains are misrepresented as safety improvements. It conducts a meta-analysis across dozens of models, empirically correlating safety benchmark scores with upstream capabilities and training compute. Key findings reveal strong correlations, indicating that many benchmarks primarily capture scaling effects rather than independent safety advancements. This directly challenges the robustness of post-training safety alignment, suggesting that apparent safety gains may be fragile and entangled with capabilities, rather than reflecting genuinely reliable safety properties.
papers.summary_zh: 本文探讨AI安全基准是否真正衡量安全进展，还是仅反映通用能力，提出“安全洗白”概念，即能力提升被误标为安全改进。通过对多个模型的元分析，实证检验了安全基准得分与上游能力及训练计算量的相关性，发现许多基准与这些因素高度相关，表明表面安全收益多源于规模扩展而非独立的安全进步。这直接关联到安全对齐稳健性问题，暗示当前基准下的安全进步可能脆弱且与能力提升混淆，未体现真正可靠的安全特性。

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
papers.short_title: Scaling Laws for Overoptimization in DAAs
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has been crucial to the recent success of Large Language Models (LLMs), however, it is often a complex and brittle process. In the classical RLHF framework, a reward model is first trained to represent human preferences, which is in turn used by an online reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm to optimize the LLM. A prominent issue with such methods is reward over-optimization or reward hacking, where performance as measured by the learned proxy reward model increases, but true quality plateaus or even deteriorates. Direct Alignment Algorithms (DDAs) like Direct Preference Optimization have emerged as alternatives to the classical RLHF pipeline by circumventing the reward modeling phase. However, although DAAs do not use a separate proxy reward model, they still commonly deteriorate from over-optimization. While the so-called reward hacking phenomenon is not well-defined for DAAs, we still uncover similar trends: at higher KL budgets, DAA algorithms exhibit similar degradation patterns to their classic RLHF counterparts. In particular, we find that DAA methods deteriorate not only across a wide range of KL budgets but also often before even a single epoch of the dataset is completed. Through extensive empirical experimentation, this work formulates and formalizes the reward over-optimization or hacking problem for DAAs and explores its consequences across objectives, training regimes, and model scales.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates reward over-optimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs), where model performance degrades despite the absence of a separate proxy reward model. The authors formalize the over-optimization problem for DAAs and conduct extensive experiments across different objectives, training regimes, and model scales. They find that DAAs exhibit degradation patterns similar to classical RLHF, often deteriorating before completing a single training epoch and across a range of KL budgets. These findings provide direct evidence that alignment methods can be fragile, as even reward-free DAAs easily break due to over-optimization.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究直接对齐算法中的奖励过度优化问题，即在没有独立代理奖励模型的情况下模型性能仍会退化。作者形式化了该问题，并通过不同目标、训练机制和模型规模的大量实验进行探究。他们发现直接对齐算法表现出与经典RLHF相似的退化模式，通常在完成单个训练轮次前就已劣化，且跨越不同KL预算。该发现直接证明了对齐方法的脆弱性，表明即使是无奖励的直接对齐方法也会因过度优化而轻易失效。

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.abstract: While large-scale unsupervised language models (LMs) learn broad world knowledge and some reasoning skills, achieving precise control of their behavior is difficult due to the completely unsupervised nature of their training. Existing methods for gaining such steerability collect human labels of the relative quality of model generations and fine-tune the unsupervised LM to align with these preferences, often with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, RLHF is a complex and often unstable procedure, first fitting a reward model that reflects the human preferences, and then fine-tuning the large unsupervised LM using reinforcement learning to maximize this estimated reward without drifting too far from the original model. In this paper we introduce a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss. The resulting algorithm, which we call Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), is stable, performant, and computationally lightweight, eliminating the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning. Our experiments show that DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods. Notably, fine-tuning with DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations, and matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train.
papers.summary_en: DPO addresses the complexity and instability of RLHF by reparameterizing the reward model to extract the optimal policy in closed form, turning the problem into a simple classification loss. It fine-tunes LMs by directly optimizing human preferences without reinforcement learning or sampling. Evaluations show DPO matches or exceeds RLHF methods like PPO in sentiment control, summarization, and dialogue quality while being simpler to train. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address whether post-training alignment is fragile.
papers.summary_zh: DPO解决了RLHF因显式奖励模型和强化学习微调带来的复杂与不稳定问题，通过重新参数化奖励模型，以闭式解提取最优策略，将标准RLHF转化为简单的分类损失。该方法无需强化学习或采样，直接优化人类偏好。实验表明，DPO在情感控制、摘要和对话质量上达到或超过PPO等RLHF方法，且实现和训练更简单。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨对齐是否脆弱。

papers.title: Representation Noising: A Defence Mechanism Against Harmful Finetuning
papers.abstract: Releasing open-source large language models (LLMs) presents a dual-use risk since bad actors can easily fine-tune these models for harmful purposes. Even without the open release of weights, weight stealing and fine-tuning APIs make closed models vulnerable to harmful fine-tuning attacks (HFAs). While safety measures like preventing jailbreaks and improving safety guardrails are important, such measures can easily be reversed through fine-tuning. In this work, we propose Representation Noising (RepNoise), a defence mechanism that operates even when attackers have access to the weights. RepNoise works by removing information about harmful representations such that it is difficult to recover them during fine-tuning. Importantly, our defence is also able to generalize across different subsets of harm that have not been seen during the defence process as long as they are drawn from the same distribution of the attack set. Our method does not degrade the general capability of LLMs and retains the ability to train the model on harmless tasks. We provide empirical evidence that the efficacy of our defence lies in its ``depth'': the degree to which information about harmful representations is removed across all layers of the LLM. We also find areas where RepNoise still remains ineffective and highlight how those limitations can inform future research.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the threat of harmful fine-tuning attacks on LLMs, where even safety-aligned models can be retrained for malicious purposes if attackers access the weights. It proposes Representation Noising (RepNoise), a defense that removes harmful representation information across all layers of the model, making it resistant to recovery during fine-tuning. Experiments show RepNoise preserves general capabilities while preventing harmful adaptation, with effectiveness attributed to the 'depth' of noise applied. This work directly examines the fragility of post-training safety alignment, demonstrating that it can be bypassed via fine-tuning and offering a hardening mechanism to mitigate such attacks.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型面临的有害微调攻击风险，即攻击者获取权重后可重新训练模型用于恶意目的。提出一种名为表示噪声化（RepNoise）的防御方法，通过移除模型所有层中的有害表示信息，使其在微调时难以恢复。实验表明，RepNoise在保持通用能力的同时能阻止有害适应，其有效性源于噪声应用的“深度”。该研究直接探究了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，证明其可通过微调被绕过，并提供了一种加固机制来抵御此类攻击。

papers.title: Decoding-Time Language Model Alignment with Multiple Objectives
papers.abstract: Aligning language models (LMs) to human preferences has emerged as a critical pursuit, enabling these models to better serve diverse user needs. Existing methods primarily focus on optimizing LMs for a single reward function, limiting their adaptability to varied objectives. Here, we propose $\textbf{multi-objective decoding (MOD)}$, a decoding-time algorithm that outputs the next token from a linear combination of predictions of all base models, for any given weightings over different objectives. We exploit a common form among a family of $f$-divergence regularized alignment approaches (such as PPO, DPO, and their variants) to identify a closed-form solution by Legendre transform, and derive an efficient decoding strategy. Theoretically, we show why existing approaches can be sub-optimal even in natural settings and obtain optimality guarantees for our method. Empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm. For example, compared to a parameter-merging baseline, MOD achieves 12.8% overall reward improvement when equally optimizing towards $3$ objectives. Moreover, we experiment with MOD on combining three fully-finetuned LLMs of different model sizes, each aimed at different objectives such as safety, coding, and general user preference. Unlike traditional methods that require careful curation of a mixture of datasets to achieve comprehensive improvement, we can quickly experiment with preference weightings using MOD to find the best combination of models. Our best combination reduces toxicity on Toxigen to nearly 0% and achieves 7.9--33.3% improvement across other three metrics ($\textit{i.e.}$, Codex@1, GSM-COT, BBH-COT).
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of aligning language models to a single reward, proposing multi-objective decoding (MOD), a decoding-time algorithm that combines predictions from multiple base models for any weighting over different objectives. MOD is derived from f-divergence regularized alignment approaches via Legendre transform, offering a closed-form solution. Evaluated on models targeting safety, coding, and general preference, MOD reduces toxicity on Toxigen to nearly 0% and achieves 7.9–33.3% improvement on other metrics, outperforming parameter merging. While advancing multi-objective alignment methodology, the paper does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有对齐方法仅优化单一奖励函数的局限，提出多目标解码（MOD），一种在解码时通过线性组合多个基础模型预测来适配任意目标权重的算法。该方法利用f散度正则化对齐框架的共性，通过勒让德变换导出闭式解。在安全、编程和通用偏好三个目标上，MOD将Toxigen上的毒性降至接近0%，并在其他指标上获得7.9%至33.3%的提升，优于参数合并基线。该工作推进了多目标对齐方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Soft Prompt Threats: Attacking Safety Alignment and Unlearning in Open-Source LLMs through the Embedding Space
papers.short_title: Embedding Space Attacks on LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Current research in adversarial robustness of LLMs focuses on discrete input manipulations in the natural language space, which can be directly transferred to closed-source models. However, this approach neglects the steady progression of open-source models. As open-source models advance in capability, ensuring their safety also becomes increasingly imperative. Yet, attacks tailored to open-source LLMs that exploit full model access remain largely unexplored. We address this research gap and propose the embedding space attack, which directly attacks the continuous embedding representation of input tokens. We find that embedding space attacks circumvent model alignments and trigger harmful behaviors more efficiently than discrete attacks or model fine-tuning. Furthermore, we present a novel threat model in the context of unlearning and show that embedding space attacks can extract supposedly deleted information from unlearned LLMs across multiple datasets and models. Our findings highlight embedding space attacks as an important threat model in open-source LLMs. Trigger Warning: the appendix contains LLM-generated text with violence and harassment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the underexplored threat of adversaries with full model access to open-source LLMs, targeting safety alignment and unlearning. It proposes embedding space attacks that directly manipulate continuous token embeddings to induce harmful outputs. Experiments show these attacks bypass alignment more efficiently than discrete attacks or fine-tuning, and can extract supposedly deleted information from unlearned models. The findings reveal a new attack surface that demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment when model internals are accessible.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对现有研究忽视开源大模型全模型访问的安全威胁，聚焦于安全对齐与知识遗忘的脆弱性。提出嵌入空间攻击，通过直接操纵连续嵌入表示来诱导有害输出。实验表明，该方法比离散攻击或微调更高效地绕过安全对齐，并可从已遗忘模型中提取被删除的信息。这一发现揭示了当模型内部可访问时，后训练安全对齐极易被突破，凸显了其脆弱性。

papers.title: Rainbow Teaming: Open-Ended Generation of Diverse Adversarial Prompts
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly prevalent across many real-world applications, understanding and enhancing their robustness to adversarial attacks is of paramount importance. Existing methods for identifying adversarial prompts tend to focus on specific domains, lack diversity, or require extensive human annotations. To address these limitations, we present Rainbow Teaming, a novel black-box approach for producing a diverse collection of adversarial prompts. Rainbow Teaming casts adversarial prompt generation as a quality-diversity problem and uses open-ended search to generate prompts that are both effective and diverse. Focusing on the safety domain, we use Rainbow Teaming to target various state-of-the-art LLMs, including the Llama 2 and Llama 3 models. Our approach reveals hundreds of effective adversarial prompts, with an attack success rate exceeding 90% across all tested models. Furthermore, we demonstrate that prompts generated by Rainbow Teaming are highly transferable and that fine-tuning models with synthetic data generated by our method significantly enhances their safety without sacrificing general performance or helpfulness. We additionally explore the versatility of Rainbow Teaming by applying it to question answering and cybersecurity, showcasing its potential to drive robust open-ended self-improvement in a wide range of applications.
papers.summary_en: Existing methods for identifying adversarial prompts often lack diversity, are domain-specific, or require costly human annotation. The paper proposes Rainbow Teaming, a black-box approach that frames adversarial prompt generation as a quality-diversity problem and uses open-ended search to produce diverse and effective attacks. Evaluation on Llama 2 and Llama 3 shows over 90% attack success rate, high transferability, and that fine-tuning on the generated data improves safety without degrading general performance; the method also applies to QA and cybersecurity. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training safety alignment by demonstrating how diverse prompts can bypass alignment while showing that such attacks can be mitigated through data-driven hardening.
papers.summary_zh: 现有对抗性提示识别方法往往多样性不足、局限于特定领域或需大量人工标注，制约了安全对齐的全面检测。本文提出Rainbow Teaming方法，将对抗提示生成建模为质量-多样性问题，通过开放式搜索生成兼具有效性与多样性的对抗提示。在Llama 2和Llama 3上的实验获得超90%的攻击成功率，提示迁移性高，用合成数据微调能在不损通用能力的同时提升安全性，方法还适用于问答和网络安全。该研究直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性议题：既揭示了多样化提示可攻破对齐机制，也展示了通过对抗数据加固模型的有效途径。

papers.title: On the Exploitability of Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Instruction tuning is an effective technique to align large language models (LLMs) with human intents. In this work, we investigate how an adversary can exploit instruction tuning by injecting specific instruction-following examples into the training data that intentionally changes the model's behavior. For example, an adversary can achieve content injection by injecting training examples that mention target content and eliciting such behavior from downstream models. To achieve this goal, we propose \textit{AutoPoison}, an automated data poisoning pipeline. It naturally and coherently incorporates versatile attack goals into poisoned data with the help of an oracle LLM. We showcase two example attacks: content injection and over-refusal attacks, each aiming to induce a specific exploitable behavior. We quantify and benchmark the strength and the stealthiness of our data poisoning scheme. Our results show that AutoPoison allows an adversary to change a model's behavior by poisoning only a small fraction of data while maintaining a high level of stealthiness in the poisoned examples. We hope our work sheds light on how data quality affects the behavior of instruction-tuned models and raises awareness of the importance of data quality for responsible deployments of LLMs. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/azshue/AutoPoison}.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates how adversaries can exploit instruction tuning through data poisoning to intentionally alter LLM behaviors, such as content injection and over-refusal. The authors propose AutoPoison, an automated pipeline that uses an oracle LLM to craft natural, coherent poisoned examples that embed attack goals. Evaluations show that poisoning only a small fraction of training data suffices to induce target behaviors while maintaining high stealthiness. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile—it can be easily compromised via training data manipulation, underscoring the vulnerability of the alignment process.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究攻击者如何通过数据投毒利用指令微调，实现内容注入和过度拒绝等恶意行为改变。提出AutoPoison方法，利用oracle LLM自动生成自然连贯的投毒样本，将攻击目标融入训练数据。实验表明，仅需毒化少量数据即可成功诱导目标行为，且投毒数据具有高隐蔽性。该工作直接证明指令微调存在脆弱性，安全对齐可通过训练数据投毒轻易突破，凸显了对齐过程在数据层面的脆弱性。

papers.title: Mission Impossible: A Statistical Perspective on Jailbreaking LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are trained on a deluge of text data with limited quality control. As a result, LLMs can exhibit unintended or even harmful behaviours, such as leaking information, fake news or hate speech. Countermeasures, commonly referred to as preference alignment, include fine-tuning the pretrained LLMs with carefully crafted text examples of desired behaviour. Even then, empirical evidence shows preference aligned LLMs can be enticed to harmful behaviour. This so called jailbreaking of LLMs is typically achieved by adversarially modifying the input prompt to the LLM. Our paper provides theoretical insights into the phenomenon of preference alignment and jailbreaking from a statistical perspective. Under our framework, we first show that pretrained LLMs will mimic harmful behaviour if present in the training corpus. Under that same framework, we then introduce a statistical notion of alignment, and lower-bound the jailbreaking probability, showing that it is unpreventable under reasonable assumptions. Based on our insights, we propose an alteration to the currently prevalent alignment strategy RLHF. Specifically, we introduce a simple modification to the RLHF objective, we call E-RLHF, that aims to increase the likelihood of safe responses. E-RLHF brings no additional training cost, and is compatible with other methods. Empirically, we demonstrate that E-RLHF outperforms RLHF on all alignment problems put forward by the AdvBench and HarmBench project without sacrificing model performance as measured by the MT-Bench project.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fundamental vulnerability of preference-aligned LLMs to jailbreaking attacks, showing that alignment does not eliminate harmful behaviors and jailbreaking is theoretically unpreventable. The authors propose a statistical framework to analyze alignment and derive a lower bound on jailbreaking probability, then introduce E-RLHF, a simple modification to the RLHF objective that increases the likelihood of safe responses. Empirically, E-RLHF outperforms RLHF on AdvBench and HarmBench without sacrificing MT-Bench performance. By demonstrating the inherent fragility of alignment under reasonable assumptions, this work directly supports the view that post-training safety alignment is not robust and can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文聚焦于偏好对齐的大语言模型仍易受越狱攻击的问题，从统计学角度证明对齐无法根除有害行为且越狱不可避免。作者首先构建统计框架分析对齐过程，推导出越狱概率的下界；随后提出E-RLHF，通过对RLHF目标函数的简单修改提升安全响应概率。实验表明，E-RLHF在AdvBench和HarmBench上优于RLHF，且MT-Bench性能无损。论文从理论上揭示了安全对齐在合理假设下的固有脆弱性，直接论证了后训练对齐难以稳健、易被绕过的核心问题。

papers.title: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks
papers.abstract: Most jailbreak papers claim the jailbreaks they propose are highly effective, often boasting near-100% attack success rates. However, it is perhaps more common than not for jailbreak developers to substantially exaggerate the effectiveness of their jailbreaks. We suggest this problem arises because jailbreak researchers lack a standard, high-quality benchmark for evaluating jailbreak performance, leaving researchers to create their own. To create a benchmark, researchers must choose a dataset of forbidden prompts to which a victim model will respond, along with an evaluation method that scores the harmfulness of the victim model's responses. We show that existing benchmarks suffer from significant shortcomings and introduce the StrongREJECT benchmark to address these issues. StrongREJECT's dataset contains prompts that victim models must answer with specific, harmful information, while its automated evaluator measures the extent to which a response gives useful information to forbidden prompts. In doing so, the StrongREJECT evaluator achieves state-of-the-art agreement with human judgments of jailbreak effectiveness. Notably, we find that existing evaluation methods significantly overstate jailbreak effectiveness compared to human judgments and the StrongREJECT evaluator. We describe a surprising and novel phenomenon that explains this discrepancy: jailbreaks bypassing a victim model's safety fine-tuning tend to reduce its capabilities. Together, our findings underscore the need for researchers to use a high-quality benchmark, such as StrongREJECT, when developing new jailbreak attacks. We release the StrongREJECT code and data at https://strong-reject.readthedocs.io/en/latest/.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of exaggerated jailbreak effectiveness claims caused by flawed evaluation benchmarks in LLM safety research. It proposes StrongREJECT, a benchmark with a dataset of forbidden prompts demanding specific harmful information and an automated evaluator that measures response usefulness, achieving state-of-the-art agreement with human judgments. Evaluation reveals that existing methods significantly overstate jailbreak success, and a novel phenomenon is uncovered: jailbreaks that bypass safety fine-tuning often degrade the victim model's capabilities. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as it can be bypassed, but not without cost, suggesting alignment is brittle rather than robust.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM安全研究中因评估基准存在缺陷而导致越狱效果被夸大这一问题。提出了StrongREJECT基准，包含一个要求具体有害信息的禁止提示数据集，以及一个能衡量响应有用性的自动评估器，其评估结果与人类判断高度一致。评估发现，现有方法显著高估了越狱成功率，并揭示了一个新现象：成功绕过安全微调的越狱往往会降低受害者模型的能力。这直接证明了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性——虽可被绕过，但会付出代价，表明对齐是脆弱的，而非鲁棒的。

papers.title: Principle-Driven Self-Alignment of Language Models from Scratch with Minimal Human Supervision
papers.abstract: Recent AI-assistant agents, such as ChatGPT, predominantly rely on supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with human annotations and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align the output of large language models (LLMs) with human intentions, ensuring they are helpful, ethical, and reliable. However, this dependence can significantly constrain the true potential of AI-assistant agents due to the high cost of obtaining human supervision and the related issues on quality, reliability, diversity, self-consistency, and undesirable biases. To address these challenges, we propose a novel approach called SELF-ALIGN, which combines principle-driven reasoning and the generative power of LLMs for the self-alignment of AI agents with minimal human supervision. Our approach encompasses four stages: first, we use an LLM to generate synthetic prompts, and a topic-guided method to augment the prompt diversity; second, we use a small set of human-written principles for AI models to follow, and guide the LLM through in-context learning from demonstrations (of principles application) to produce helpful, ethical, and reliable responses to user's queries; third, we fine-tune the original LLM with the high-quality self-aligned responses so that the resulting model can generate desirable responses for each query directly without the principle set and the demonstrations anymore; and finally, we offer a refinement step to address the issues of overly-brief or indirect responses. Applying SELF-ALIGN to the LLaMA-65b base language model, we develop an AI assistant named Dromedary. With fewer than 300 lines of human annotations (including<200 seed prompts, 16 generic principles, and 5 exemplars for in-context learning). Dromedary significantly surpasses the performance of several state-of-the-art AI systems, including Text-Davinci-003 and Alpaca, on benchmark datasets with various settings.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high cost and potential quality issues of human supervision in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human intentions. It proposes SELF-ALIGN, a method that uses a small set of human-written principles and synthetic prompts to guide an LLM to generate aligned responses via in-context learning, then fine-tunes the model on those responses. Applied to LLaMA-65b, the resulting assistant Dromedary outperforms state-of-the-art systems like Text-Davinci-003 and Alpaca on benchmarks, using only ~300 lines of human annotations. This paper advances alignment methodology by demonstrating efficient self-alignment but does not directly study the fragility or robustness of the alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型对齐人类意图过程中人类监督成本高且可能引发质量、偏差等问题的挑战，提出SELF-ALIGN方法，利用少量人工编写的原则和合成提示，通过上下文学习引导LLM生成对齐响应，并据此微调模型。在LLaMA-65b上实现为助手Dromedary，仅用约300行人工标注便在基准测试中超越了Text-Davinci-003和Alpaca等先进系统。该工作推动了对齐方法的发展，展示了高效自对齐技术，但并未直接探讨对齐后的模型是否脆弱或易被绕过。

papers.title: A Critical Evaluation of AI Feedback for Aligning Large Language Models
papers.short_title: SFT vs RLAIF for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with AI feedback (RLAIF) is a popular paradigm for improving the instruction-following abilities of powerful pre-trained language models. RLAIF first performs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using demonstrations from a teacher model and then further fine-tunes the model with reinforcement learning (RL), using feedback from a critic model. While recent popular open-source models have demonstrated substantial improvements in performance from the RL step, in this paper we question whether the complexity of this RL step is truly warranted for AI feedback. We show that the improvements of the RL step are virtually entirely due to the widespread practice of using a weaker teacher model (e.g. GPT-3.5) for SFT data collection than the critic (e.g., GPT-4) used for AI feedback generation. Specifically, we show that simple supervised fine-tuning with GPT-4 as the teacher outperforms existing RLAIF pipelines. More generally, we find that the gains from RLAIF vary substantially across base model families, test-time evaluation protocols, and critic models. Finally, we provide a mechanistic explanation for when SFT may outperform the full two-step RLAIF pipeline as well as suggestions for making RLAIF maximally useful in practice.
papers.summary_en: This paper questions the necessity of the reinforcement learning (RL) step in reinforcement learning with AI feedback (RLAIF) for aligning large language models. It compares the full RLAIF pipeline against simple supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with a strong teacher model, finding that SFT with GPT-4 outperforms existing RLAIF methods. The study reveals that the perceived gains from RL are largely an artifact of using a weaker teacher (e.g., GPT-3.5) for SFT data collection than the critic (GPT-4), and that improvement varies across model families, evaluation protocols, and critics. This work directly addresses the fragility of post-training alignment by demonstrating that complex RL-based alignment may not be robust, as a simpler SFT approach can achieve superior results when the teacher quality is matched—suggesting that alignment gains are fragile and contingent on specific design choices.
papers.summary_zh: 本文质疑了基于AI反馈的强化学习（RLAIF）流程中强化学习步骤的必要性。研究比较了完整的RLAIF管线与仅使用强教师模型进行监督微调（SFT）的方法，发现使用GPT-4作为教师进行SFT即可超越现有RLAIF方法。分析表明，RLAIF的增益几乎完全源于使用了较弱的教师（如GPT-3.5）收集SFT数据，而评论家模型（GPT-4）更强；且效果在不同基座模型、测试协议和评论家模型间差异显著。该工作直接回应了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题，揭示了强化学习带来的提升并不稳固，当教师模型质量匹配时，简单SFT即可取得更优效果，暗示对齐增益高度依赖于实现细节，易被绕过或替代。

papers.title: Fast Best-of-N Decoding via Speculative Rejection
papers.abstract: The safe and effective deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) involves a critical step called alignment, which ensures that the model's responses are in accordance with human preferences. Prevalent alignment techniques, such as DPO, PPO and their variants, align LLMs by changing the pre-trained model weights during a phase called post-training. While predominant, these post-training methods add substantial complexity before LLMs can be deployed. Inference-time alignment methods avoid the complex post-training step and instead bias the generation towards responses that are aligned with human preferences. The best-known inference-time alignment method, called Best-of-N, is as effective as the state-of-the-art post-training procedures. Unfortunately, Best-of-N requires vastly more resources at inference time than standard decoding strategies, which makes it computationally not viable. In this work, we introduce Speculative Rejection, a computationally-viable inference-time alignment algorithm. It generates high-scoring responses according to a given reward model, like Best-of-N does, while being between 16 to 32 times more computationally efficient.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the high computational cost of the Best-of-N inference-time alignment method, which limits its practicality. It proposes Speculative Rejection, a new algorithm that efficiently generates high-scoring responses by early rejection of low-quality candidates. Evaluated against standard Best-of-N, it achieves 16–32× speedup while maintaining response quality. This paper advances alignment efficiency but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了推理时对齐方法Best-of-N计算成本过高的问题。提出推测性拒绝（Speculative Rejection）算法，通过提前拒绝低质量候选响应高效生成高评分回复。实验表明，相比标准Best-of-N，该方法在不降低回复质量的前提下实现了16至32倍加速。本文提升了对齐方法的推理效率，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Stealth edits to large language models
papers.short_title: Stealth edits to large language models
papers.abstract: We reveal the theoretical foundations of techniques for editing large language models, and present new methods which can do so without requiring retraining. Our theoretical insights show that a single metric (a measure of the intrinsic dimension of the model's features) can be used to assess a model's editability and reveals its previously unrecognised susceptibility to malicious stealth attacks. This metric is fundamental to predicting the success of a variety of editing approaches, and reveals new bridges between disparate families of editing methods. We collectively refer to these as stealth editing methods, because they directly update a model's weights to specify its response to specific known hallucinating prompts without affecting other model behaviour. By carefully applying our theoretical insights, we are able to introduce a new jet-pack network block which is optimised for highly selective model editing, uses only standard network operations, and can be inserted into existing networks. We also reveal the vulnerability of language models to stealth attacks: a small change to a model's weights which fixes its response to a single attacker-chosen prompt. Stealth attacks are computationally simple, do not require access to or knowledge of the model's training data, and therefore represent a potent yet previously unrecognised threat to redistributed foundation models. Extensive experimental results illustrate and support our methods and their theoretical underpinnings. Demos and source code are available at https://github.com/qinghua-zhou/stealth-edits.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the problem of editing large language models without retraining, and reveals their vulnerability to stealth attacks—small, targeted weight updates that alter specific responses. It proposes a theoretical framework based on intrinsic dimension to assess editability, and introduces a "jet-pack" network block for highly selective model editing using standard operations. The approach is evaluated experimentally, demonstrating successful stealth edits and attacks, highlighting that such edits are computationally simple and require no training data access. This work directly underscores the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that models can be covertly compromised with minimal changes, thereby bypassing alignment safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了无需重新训练即可编辑大型语言模型的问题，并揭示了模型对隐蔽攻击的脆弱性——通过小幅、有针对性的权重更新来改变特定响应。提出了基于内在维度的理论框架来评估可编辑性，并引入了一种使用标准操作的“喷气背包”网络块，用于高选择性模型编辑。通过实验评估，成功展示了隐蔽编辑和攻击，强调此类编辑计算简单且无需访问训练数据。这项工作直接突显了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，表明模型可通过最小改动被暗中破坏，从而绕过对齐保护。

papers.title: Analysing the Generalisation and Reliability of Steering Vectors
papers.abstract: Steering vectors (SVs) are a new approach to efficiently adjust language model behaviour at inference time by intervening on intermediate model activations. They have shown promise in terms of improving both capabilities and model alignment. However, the reliability and generalisation properties of this approach are unknown. In this work, we rigorously investigate these properties, and show that steering vectors have substantial limitations both in- and out-of-distribution. In-distribution, steerability is highly variable across different inputs. Depending on the concept, spurious biases can substantially contribute to how effective steering is for each input, presenting a challenge for the widespread use of steering vectors. Out-of-distribution, while steering vectors often generalise well, for several concepts they are brittle to reasonable changes in the prompt, resulting in them failing to generalise well. Overall, our findings show that while steering can work well in the right circumstances, there remain many technical difficulties of applying steering vectors to guide models' behaviour at scale.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the unknown reliability and generalisation properties of steering vectors, a method for adjusting language model behavior via activation interventions. The authors rigorously analyze steerability both in-distribution and out-of-distribution, revealing high input-dependent variability and spurious bias contributions in-distribution, and brittleness to prompt changes out-of-distribution. The findings demonstrate that steering vectors exhibit significant fragility, suggesting that alignment achieved through this method is not robust and can be easily undermined, directly contributing evidence to the question of whether post-training safety alignment is fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文聚焦于引导向量(steering vectors)在调节语言模型行为时可靠性与泛化性尚未明确的问题。作者通过严格分析分布内和分布外的可操控性，发现分布内操控效果因输入而异且受伪偏差影响，分布外则对提示变化敏感、泛化能力脆弱。这些结果表明基于引导向量的对齐方法存在明显脆弱性，易受输入变化或提示扰动而失效，直接为“后训练安全对齐是否真正稳健”这一问题提供了反面证据。

papers.title: Setting the Trap: Capturing and Defeating Backdoors in Pretrained Language Models through Honeypots
papers.abstract: In the field of natural language processing, the prevalent approach involves fine-tuning pretrained language models (PLMs) using local samples. Recent research has exposed the susceptibility of PLMs to backdoor attacks, wherein the adversaries can embed malicious prediction behaviors by manipulating a few training samples. In this study, our objective is to develop a backdoor-resistant tuning procedure that yields a backdoor-free model, no matter whether the fine-tuning dataset contains poisoned samples. To this end, we propose and integrate an \emph{honeypot module} into the original PLM, specifically designed to absorb backdoor information exclusively. Our design is motivated by the observation that lower-layer representations in PLMs carry sufficient backdoor features while carrying minimal information about the original tasks. Consequently, we can impose penalties on the information acquired by the honeypot module to inhibit backdoor creation during the fine-tuning process of the stem network. Comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets substantiate the effectiveness and robustness of our defensive strategy. Notably, these results indicate a substantial reduction in the attack success rate ranging from 10\% to 40\% when compared to prior state-of-the-art methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of pretrained language models (PLMs) to backdoor attacks during fine-tuning, where poisoned samples can embed malicious behaviors. The authors propose a honeypot module integrated into the PLM that exclusively absorbs backdoor features by leveraging the observation that lower-layer representations carry sufficient backdoor information but minimal task information; a penalty mechanism then inhibits backdoor creation in the main model. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate a 10–40% reduction in attack success rate compared to prior state-of-the-art defenses. This work strengthens the integrity of fine-tuned models against backdoors, offering a robust defense mechanism, but it does not directly assess the fragility of post-training safety alignment itself.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决预训练语言模型在微调过程中易受后门攻击的问题，攻击者可通过污染少量训练样本嵌入恶意预测行为。作者提出在原始PLM中集成一个蜜罐模块，该模块专门吸收后门特征，其设计基于低层表示包含足够后门信息而极少原始任务信息的观察，并通过惩罚该模块获取的信息来阻止主体网络形成后门。在基准数据集上的实验表明，与现有先进防御方法相比，攻击成功率降低了10%至40%。这项工作增强了模型微调阶段对后门的鲁棒性，从而加固了安全对齐，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐模块本身的脆弱性。

papers.title: Connecting the Dots: LLMs can Infer and Verbalize Latent Structure from Disparate Training Data
papers.abstract: One way to address safety risks from large language models (LLMs) is to censor dangerous knowledge from their training data. While this removes the explicit information, implicit information can remain scattered across various training documents. Could an LLM infer the censored knowledge by piecing together these implicit hints? As a step towards answering this question, we study inductive out-of-context reasoning (OOCR), a type of generalization in which LLMs infer latent information from evidence distributed across training documents and apply it to downstream tasks without in-context learning. Using a suite of five tasks, we demonstrate that frontier LLMs can perform inductive OOCR. In one experiment we finetune an LLM on a corpus consisting only of distances between an unknown city and other known cities. Remarkably, without in-context examples or Chain of Thought, the LLM can verbalize that the unknown city is Paris and use this fact to answer downstream questions. Further experiments show that LLMs trained only on individual coin flip outcomes can verbalize whether the coin is biased, and those trained only on pairs $(x,f(x))$ can articulate a definition of $f$ and compute inverses. While OOCR succeeds in a range of cases, we also show that it is unreliable, particularly for smaller LLMs learning complex structures. Overall, the ability of LLMs to "connect the dots" without explicit in-context learning poses a potential obstacle to monitoring and controlling the knowledge acquired by LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can infer and verbalize censored knowledge from implicit clues scattered across training data, addressing safety risks from data sanitization. It introduces inductive out-of-context reasoning (OOCR), where models piece together latent information without in-context examples, and evaluates it on five synthetic tasks involving geographic inference, coin bias detection, and function learning. Results show that frontier LLMs can successfully perform OOCR, e.g., inferring 'Paris' from distance data or articulating function definitions from input-output pairs, though performance is unreliable in smaller models. This reveals a potential fragility in post-training safety alignment: even if explicit dangerous content is removed, models may still reconstruct hidden knowledge, undermining monitoring and control mechanisms.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究大语言模型（LLMs）是否能够从训练数据中分散的隐含线索推断并表述被审查的知识，从而应对数据净化带来的安全风险。它提出了归纳式上下文外推理（OOCR），即模型无需上下文示例即可拼凑潜在信息，并通过地理推理、硬币偏差检测和函数学习等五个合成任务进行评估。结果表明，前沿LLMs能够成功执行OOCR，例如从距离数据推断出“巴黎”或从输入输出对中明确函数定义，但在较小模型中表现不可靠。这揭示了后训练安全对齐的潜在脆弱性：即使显式危险内容被移除，模型仍可能重建隐藏知识，削弱监控和控制机制。

papers.title: Time-Reversal Provides Unsupervised Feedback to LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are typically trained to predict in the forward direction of time. However, recent works have shown that prompting these models to look back and critique their own generations can produce useful feedback. Motivated by this, we explore the question of whether LLMs can be empowered to think (predict and score) backwards to provide unsupervised feedback that complements forward LLMs. Towards this, we introduce Time Reversed Language Models (TRLMs), which can score and generate queries when conditioned on responses, effectively functioning in the reverse direction of time. Further, to effectively infer in the response to query direction, we pre-train and fine-tune a language model (TRLM-Ba) in the reverse token order from scratch. We show empirically (and theoretically in a stylized setting) that time-reversed models can indeed complement forward model predictions when used to score the query given response for re-ranking multiple forward generations. We obtain up to 5\% improvement on the widely used AlpacaEval Leaderboard over the competent baseline of best-of-N re-ranking using self log-perplexity scores. We further show that TRLM scoring outperforms conventional forward scoring of response given query, resulting in significant gains in applications such as citation generation and passage retrieval. We next leverage the generative ability of TRLM to augment or provide unsupervised feedback to input safety filters of LLMs, demonstrating a drastic reduction in false negative rate with negligible impact on false positive rates against several attacks published on the popular JailbreakBench leaderboard.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of providing unsupervised feedback to LLMs by enabling them to reason backwards in time. It proposes Time Reversed Language Models (TRLMs) that predict queries given responses, pre-trained and fine-tuned in reverse token order. Evaluated on AlpacaEval, citation generation, and passage retrieval, TRLM scoring improves re-ranking by up to 5% and outperforms forward scoring; applied to safety filters, it drastically reduces false negatives with little impact on false positives. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了通过让大语言模型进行时间反向推理来提供无监督反馈的挑战。提出了时间反转语言模型（TRLM），该模型以反向 token 顺序预训练和微调，在给定回答时预测查询。在 AlpacaEval、引文生成和篇章检索上的评估表明，TRLM 评分将重排序性能提升最高 5%，并优于前向评分；应用于安全过滤器后，大幅降低了假阴性率，且对假阳性率影响极小。本文推进了对齐方法但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: HelpSteer 2: Open-source dataset for training top-performing reward models
papers.abstract: High-quality preference datasets are essential for training reward models that can effectively guide large language models (LLMs) in generating high-quality responses aligned with human preferences. As LLMs become stronger and better aligned, permissively licensed preference datasets, such as Open Assistant, HH-RLHF, and HelpSteer need to be updated to remain effective for reward modeling. Methods that distil preference data from proprietary LLMs such as GPT-4 have restrictions on commercial usage imposed by model providers. To improve upon both generated responses and attribute labeling quality, we release HelpSteer2, a permissively licensed preference dataset (CC-BY-4.0). Using a powerful internal base model trained on HelpSteer2, we are able to achieve the SOTA score (92.0%) on Reward-Bench's primary dataset, outperforming currently listed open and proprietary models, as of June 12th, 2024. Notably, HelpSteer2 consists of only ten thousand response pairs, an order of magnitude fewer than existing preference datasets (e.g., HH-RLHF), which makes it highly efficient for training reward models. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that reward models trained with HelpSteer2 are effective in aligning LLMs. In particular, we propose SteerLM 2.0, a model alignment approach that can effectively make use of the rich multi-attribute score predicted by our reward models. HelpSteer2 is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/HelpSteer2 and code is available at https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Aligner
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the scarcity of high-quality, permissively licensed preference datasets for training reward models as LLMs advance. It introduces HelpSteer2, a CC-BY-4.0 dataset with only 10k response pairs and rich multi-attribute labels, along with the SteerLM 2.0 alignment method. Achieving 92.0% on Reward-Bench, it sets a new state-of-the-art, surpassing both open and proprietary models. This work advances alignment methodology through an efficient open dataset but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文针对大语言模型能力提升后，训练奖励模型所需的高质量、宽松许可偏好数据不足的问题展开研究。提出了HelpSteer2，一个仅有1万条响应对及丰富多属性标签的CC-BY-4.0数据集，并设计了利用奖励模型多属性评分的SteerLM 2.0对齐方法。在Reward-Bench上取得92.0%的当前最优成绩，超越所有开源和闭源模型。本文通过高效开放数据集推进了对齐方法，但未直接探讨后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: BackdoorAlign: Mitigating Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack with Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Despite the general capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4, these models still request fine-tuning or adaptation with customized data when meeting the specific business demands and intricacies of tailored use cases. However, this process inevitably introduces new safety threats, particularly against the Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack (FJAttack) under the setting of Language-Model-as-a-Service (LMaaS), where the model’s safety has been significantly compromised by fine-tuning on users’ uploaded examples that contain just a few harmful examples. Though potential defenses have been proposed that the service providers of LMaaS can integrate safety examples into the fine-tuning dataset to reduce safety issues, such approaches require incorporating a substantial amount of data, making it inefficient. To effectively defend against the FJAttack with limited safety examples under LMaaS, we propose the Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment method inspired by an analogy with the concept of backdoor attacks. In particular, service providers will construct prefixed safety examples with a secret prompt, acting as a “backdoor trigger”. By integrating prefixed safety examples into the fine-tuning dataset, the subsequent fine-tuning process effectively acts as the “backdoor attack,” establishing a strong correlation between the secret prompt and safety generations. Consequently, safe responses are ensured once service providers prepend this secret prompt ahead of any user input during inference. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that through the Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment with adding as few as 11 prefixed safety examples, the maliciously fine-tuned LLMs will achieve similar safety performance as the original aligned models without harming the benign performance. Furthermore, we
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack (FJAttack) in Language-Model-as-a-Service settings, where a few harmful examples can undermine safety alignment. It proposes Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment, which uses prefixed safety examples with a secret trigger to associate the trigger with safe outputs during fine-tuning. Experiments show that with only 11 such examples, the fine-tuned model regains safety comparable to the original aligned model without harming benign performance. This paper advances a practical defense against a specific attack, reinforcing alignment efficiency, but does not directly investigate the fundamental fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对语言模型即服务场景下基于微调的越狱攻击（FJAttack），即少量有害样本即可破坏安全对齐的问题。提出后门增强安全对齐方法，通过在少量安全示例中添加秘密触发器，使微调过程建立触发器与安全输出的强关联。实验表明，仅需11个带触发器的安全示例，恶意微调后模型的安全性即可恢复至原始对齐水平，且不损害良性性能。本文提供了一种高效的防御策略，增强了安全对齐的鲁棒性，但未直接探讨安全对齐机制本身是否脆弱。

papers.title: DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
papers.abstract: Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) models have exhibited exciting progress in capabilities, capturing the interest of practitioners and the public alike. Yet, while the literature on the trustworthiness of GPT models remains limited, practitioners have proposed employing capable GPT models for sensitive applications to healthcare and finance – where mistakes can be costly. To this end, this work proposes a comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation for large language models with a focus on GPT-4 and GPT-3.5, considering diverse perspectives – including toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, robustness on adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness. Based on our evaluations, we discover previously unpublished vulnerabilities to trustworthiness threats. For instance, we find that GPT models can be easily misled to generate toxic and biased outputs and leak private information in both training data and conversation history. We also find that although GPT-4 is usually more trustworthy than GPT-3.5 on standard benchmarks, GPT-4 is more vulnerable given jailbreaking system or user prompts, potentially due to the reason that GPT-4 follows the (misleading) instructions more precisely. Our work illustrates a comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation of GPT models and sheds light on the trustworthiness gaps. Our benchmark is publicly available at https://decodingtrust.github.io/.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of a systematic trustworthiness evaluation for GPT models by proposing a multi-dimensional assessment. The authors create DecodingTrust, a benchmark covering toxicity, bias, adversarial and out-of-distribution robustness, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness. Evaluating GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, they find both models can be misled to produce toxic outputs and leak private data, with GPT-4 being more vulnerable to jailbreaking prompts despite better standard performance. The findings reveal fragility in post-training safety alignment, as jailbreaking prompts can precisely bypass protections in more instruction-following models, underscoring that alignment is not robust against adversarial directives.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对GPT模型缺乏系统性可信度评估的问题，提出多维度测评。作者构建了DecodingTrust基准，涵盖毒性、偏见、对抗鲁棒性、分布外鲁棒性、隐私、机器伦理和公平性等维度。对GPT-3.5和GPT-4的评估发现，两者均可能被误导生成有害内容并泄漏隐私；尽管GPT-4在标准基准上更可信，但更易受越狱提示攻击。这些发现表明后训练安全对齐存在脆弱性，越狱提示能精准绕过更擅长遵循指令的模型的保护，说明对齐并非真正稳固。

papers.title: Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Language Model Policy Optimization
papers.short_title: SACPO: Stepwise Alignment for LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Safety and trustworthiness are indispensable requirements for real-world applications of AI systems using large language models (LLMs). This paper formulates human value alignment as an optimization problem of the language model policy to maximize reward under a safety constraint, and then proposes an algorithm, Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Policy Optimization (SACPO). One key idea behind SACPO, supported by theory, is that the optimal policy incorporating reward and safety can be directly obtained from a reward-aligned policy. Building on this key idea, SACPO aligns LLMs step-wise with each metric while leveraging simple yet powerful alignment algorithms such as direct preference optimization (DPO). SACPO offers several advantages, including simplicity, stability, computational efficiency, and flexibility of algorithms and datasets. Under mild assumptions, our theoretical analysis provides the upper bounds on optimality and safety constraint violation. Our experimental results show that SACPO can fine-tune Alpaca-7B better than the state-of-the-art method in terms of both helpfulness and harmlessness.
papers.summary_en: This paper formulates LLM alignment as a constrained reward maximization problem to ensure safety and helpfulness. It proposes Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Policy Optimization (SACPO), which derives the optimal constrained policy from a reward-aligned policy using direct preference optimization (DPO) in a stepwise manner, with theoretical upper bounds on optimality and constraint violation. Experiments on Alpaca-7B show SACPO outperforms the state-of-the-art in both helpfulness and harmlessness. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文将大语言模型的对齐问题形式化为带安全约束的奖励最大化问题，以确保有用性和无害性。提出步进式约束策略优化方法 SACPO，利用直接偏好优化（DPO）从奖励对齐策略逐步推导出最优约束策略，并提供了最优性和约束违反的理论上界。在 Alpaca-7B 上的实验表明，SACPO 在有用性和无害性方面均优于现有最佳方法。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Aligning Language Models with Human Preferences via a Bayesian Approach
papers.abstract: In the quest to advance human-centric natural language generation (NLG) systems, ensuring alignment between NLG models and human preferences is crucial. For this alignment, current popular methods leverage a reinforcement learning (RL) approach with a reward model trained on feedback from humans. However, inherent disagreements due to the subjective nature of human preferences pose a significant challenge for training the reward model, resulting in a deterioration of the NLG performance. To tackle this issue, previous approaches typically rely on majority voting or averaging to consolidate multiple inconsistent preferences into a merged one. Although straightforward to understand and execute, such methods suffer from an inability to capture the nuanced degrees of disaggregation among humans and may only represent a specialized subset of individuals, thereby lacking the ability to quantitatively disclose the universality of human preferences. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel approach, which employs a Bayesian framework to account for the distribution of disagreements among human preferences as training a preference model, and names it as d-PM. Besides, considering the RL strategy's inefficient and complex training process over the training efficiency, we further propose utilizing the contrastive learning strategy to train the NLG model with the preference scores derived from the d-PM model. Extensive experiments on two human-centric NLG tasks, i.e., emotional support conversation and integrity"Rule-of-Thumb"generation, show that our method consistently exceeds previous SOTA models in both automatic and human evaluations.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning NLG models with diverse and inconsistent human preferences, which can degrade performance when using standard reward models. It proposes a Bayesian framework, d-PM, that models the distribution of disagreements among human preferences and employs contrastive learning for efficient model training. Evaluated on emotional support conversation and integrity generation tasks, d-PM consistently outperforms prior state-of-the-art models in both automatic and human evaluations. While the paper advances alignment methodology by capturing preference diversity, it does not directly examine whether the resulting alignment is robust or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对自然语言生成模型与不一致的人类偏好对齐的挑战，标准奖励模型因偏好分歧导致性能下降。提出了一种贝叶斯框架 d-PM，建模人类偏好分歧的分布，并采用对比学习进行高效训练。在情感支持对话和“经验法则”生成两个任务上评估，d-PM 在自动评估和人工评估中均超越现有最优模型。该工作通过建模偏好多样性改进了对齐方法，但未直接探究对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Fine-Grained Human Feedback Gives Better Rewards for Language Model Training
papers.abstract: Language models (LMs) often exhibit undesirable text generation behaviors, including generating false, toxic, or irrelevant outputs. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) - where human preference judgments on LM outputs are transformed into a learning signal - has recently shown promise in addressing these issues. However, such holistic feedback conveys limited information on long text outputs; it does not indicate which aspects of the outputs influenced user preference; e.g., which parts contain what type(s) of errors. In this paper, we use fine-grained human feedback (e.g., which sentence is false, which sub-sentence is irrelevant) as an explicit training signal. We introduce Fine-Grained RLHF, a framework that enables training and learning from reward functions that are fine-grained in two respects: (1) density, providing a reward after every segment (e.g., a sentence) is generated; and (2) incorporating multiple reward models associated with different feedback types (e.g., factual incorrectness, irrelevance, and information incompleteness). We conduct experiments on detoxification and long-form question answering to illustrate how learning with such reward functions leads to improved performance, supported by both automatic and human evaluation. Additionally, we show that LM behaviors can be customized using different combinations of fine-grained reward models. We release all data, collected human feedback, and codes at https://FineGrainedRLHF.github.io.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem that holistic human feedback for language model alignment provides limited information for long outputs, failing to pinpoint specific errors. It proposes Fine-Grained RLHF, a framework that uses dense segment-level rewards and multiple fine-grained reward models for different error types like factual incorrectness and irrelevance. Experiments on detoxification and long-form QA show improved performance via automatic and human evaluation, and enable customization of model behaviors. This paper advances alignment methodology by providing more informative training signals, but it does not directly address the question of whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or can be easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对语言模型对齐中整体性人类反馈无法定位长文本具体错误的问题，提出了细粒度RLHF框架，通过在每段生成后提供密集奖励，并结合多种错误类型（如事实错误、不相关性）的奖励模型。在去毒和长文本问答上的实验表明，该方法能提升自动和人工评估的性能，并支持定制模型行为。本文通过提供更丰富的训练信号改进了对齐方法，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或容易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: Cross-model Control: Improving Multiple Large Language Models in One-time Training
papers.abstract: The number of large language models (LLMs) with varying parameter scales and vocabularies is increasing. While they deliver powerful performance, they also face a set of common optimization needs to meet specific requirements or standards, such as instruction following or avoiding the output of sensitive information from the real world. However, how to reuse the fine-tuning outcomes of one model to other models to reduce training costs remains a challenge. To bridge this gap, we introduce Cross-model Control (CMC), a method that improves multiple LLMs in one-time training with a portable tiny language model. Specifically, we have observed that the logit shift before and after fine-tuning is remarkably similar across different models. Based on this insight, we incorporate a tiny language model with a minimal number of parameters. By training alongside a frozen template LLM, the tiny model gains the capability to alter the logits output by the LLMs. To make this tiny language model applicable to models with different vocabularies, we propose a novel token mapping strategy named PM-MinED. We have conducted extensive experiments on instruction tuning and unlearning tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of CMC. Our code is available at https://github.com/wujwyi/CMC.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of reusing fine-tuning outcomes across multiple large language models (LLMs) to reduce training cost. It proposes Cross-model Control (CMC), which trains a portable tiny language model to alter the logits output by frozen LLMs, leveraging the observation that logit shifts during fine-tuning are similar across models; a token mapping strategy PM-MinED handles different vocabularies. Experiments on instruction tuning and unlearning tasks demonstrate the method's effectiveness. While CMC improves alignment methodology through one-time multi-model training, it does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在多个大型语言模型（LLM）之间重用微调成果以降低训练成本的难题。提出了跨模型控制（CMC）方法，通过训练一个小型便携语言模型来改变冻结的LLM输出的logits，基于不同模型在微调前后logit偏移高度相似的观察；并提出令牌映射策略PM-MinED以处理不同词汇表。在指令微调和遗忘任务上的实验验证了其有效性。尽管CMC通过一次性训练多模型促进了对齐方法，但未直接研究安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Shadowcast: Stealthy Data Poisoning Attacks Against Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel in generating textual responses from visual inputs, but their versatility raises security concerns. This study takes the first step in exposing VLMs' susceptibility to data poisoning attacks that can manipulate responses to innocuous, everyday prompts. We introduce Shadowcast, a stealthy data poisoning attack where poison samples are visually indistinguishable from benign images with matching texts. Shadowcast demonstrates effectiveness in two attack types. The first is a traditional Label Attack, tricking VLMs into misidentifying class labels, such as confusing Donald Trump for Joe Biden. The second is a novel Persuasion Attack, leveraging VLMs' text generation capabilities to craft persuasive and seemingly rational narratives for misinformation, such as portraying junk food as healthy. We show that Shadowcast effectively achieves the attacker's intentions using as few as 50 poison samples. Crucially, the poisoned samples demonstrate transferability across different VLM architectures, posing a significant concern in black-box settings. Moreover, Shadowcast remains potent under realistic conditions involving various text prompts, training data augmentation, and image compression techniques. This work reveals how poisoned VLMs can disseminate convincing yet deceptive misinformation to everyday, benign users, emphasizing the importance of data integrity for responsible VLM deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/umd-huang-lab/VLM-Poisoning.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to data poisoning attacks that can manipulate responses to benign prompts. It proposes Shadowcast, a stealthy attack where poisoned samples are visually indistinguishable but paired with malicious texts, enabling label and persuasion attacks. Evaluations show that as few as 50 poison samples can successfully mislead VLMs, with transferability across architectures and robustness to realistic conditions. This work highlights a new attack vector, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be easily broken by compromising data integrity, thus questioning its robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了视觉-语言模型（VLM）容易受到数据投毒攻击的影响，攻击者可通过日常提示操纵其输出。提出了Shadowcast，一种隐蔽的数据投毒方法，其投毒样本在视觉上无法区分，但配以恶意文本，能够实施标签攻击和说服攻击。实验表明，仅需50个投毒样本即可实现攻击意图，且攻击在不同VLM架构间具有可迁移性，并对现实条件具有鲁棒性。该工作暴露了新的攻击面，证明通过破坏数据完整性可轻易绕过训练后的安全对齐，从而质疑其稳健性。

papers.title: Cal-DPO: Calibrated Direct Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
papers.abstract: We study the problem of aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preference data. Contrastive preference optimization has shown promising results in aligning LLMs with available preference data by optimizing the implicit reward associated with the policy. However, the contrastive objective focuses mainly on the relative values of implicit rewards associated with two responses while ignoring their actual values, resulting in suboptimal alignment with human preferences. To address this limitation, we propose calibrated direct preference optimization (Cal-DPO), a simple yet effective algorithm. We show that substantial improvement in alignment with the given preferences can be achieved simply by calibrating the implicit reward to ensure that the learned implicit rewards are comparable in scale to the ground-truth rewards. We demonstrate the theoretical advantages of Cal-DPO over existing approaches. The results of our experiments on a variety of standard benchmarks show that Cal-DPO remarkably improves off-the-shelf methods.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the limitation of contrastive preference optimization methods like DPO, which focus only on relative implicit reward values and neglect their absolute scale, leading to suboptimal alignment with human preferences. It proposes Cal-DPO, a simple algorithm that calibrates implicit rewards to be comparable in scale to ground-truth rewards, thereby improving preference learning. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that Cal-DPO significantly improves alignment performance over existing approaches. The paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is fragile or easily bypassed.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决对比偏好优化方法（如DPO）的局限性，这些方法仅关注隐式奖励的相对值而忽略其绝对尺度，导致与人类偏好的对齐效果次优。提出Cal-DPO算法，通过校准隐式奖励使其与真实奖励的尺度可比，从而改进偏好学习。在多个标准基准上的实验表明，Cal-DPO相较于现有方法显著提升了对齐性能。本文推进了对齐方法学，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐是否脆弱或易被绕过的问题。

papers.title: β-DPO: Direct Preference Optimization with Dynamic β
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has emerged as a compelling approach for training Large Language Models (LLMs) to adhere to human preferences. However, the performance of DPO is sensitive to the fine-tuning of its trade-off parameter $\beta$, as well as to the quality of the preference data. We analyze the impact of $\beta$ and data quality on DPO, uncovering that optimal $\beta$ values vary with the informativeness of pairwise data. Addressing the limitations of static $\beta$ values, we introduce a novel framework that dynamically calibrates $\beta$ at the batch level, informed by data quality considerations. Additionally, our method incorporates $\beta$-guided data filtering to safeguard against the influence of outliers. Through empirical evaluation, we demonstrate that our dynamic $\beta$ adjustment technique significantly improves DPO's performance across a range of models and datasets, offering a more robust and adaptable training paradigm for aligning LLMs with human feedback. The code is available at \url{https://github.com/junkangwu/beta-DPO}.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the sensitivity of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to the static trade-off parameter β and preference data quality. It proposes β-DPO, which dynamically adjusts β at the batch level based on data informativeness and incorporates β-guided data filtering to mitigate outliers. Empirical evaluations show that this method consistently improves DPO performance across various models and datasets. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了直接偏好优化(DPO)对静态权衡参数β和偏好数据质量的敏感性问题。提出β-DPO方法,根据数据信息量在批次层面动态调整β,并引入β引导的数据过滤以抑制异常值。实验表明,该方法在多个模型和数据集上均提升了DPO的性能。本文推进了对齐方法论,但未直接探讨对齐脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Enhancing Multiple Dimensions of Trustworthiness in LLMs via Sparse Activation Control
papers.short_title: Sparse Activation Control for LLM Safety
papers.abstract: As the development and application of Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to advance rapidly, enhancing their trustworthiness and aligning them with human preferences has become a critical area of research. Traditional methods rely heavily on extensive data for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), but representation engineering offers a new, training-free approach. This technique leverages semantic features to control the representation of LLM's intermediate hidden states, enabling the model to meet specific requirements such as increased honesty or heightened safety awareness. However, a significant challenge arises when attempting to fulfill multiple requirements simultaneously. It proves difficult to encode various semantic contents, like honesty and safety, into a singular semantic feature, restricting its practicality.In this work, we address this challenge through Sparse Activation Control. By delving into the intrinsic mechanisms of LLMs, we manage to identify and pinpoint modules that are closely related to specific tasks within the model, i.e. attention heads. These heads display sparse characteristics that allow for near-independent control over different tasks. Our experiments, conducted on the open-source Llama series models, have yielded encouraging results. The models were able to align with human preferences on issues of safety, factualness, and bias concurrently.
papers.summary_en: The paper tackles the difficulty of simultaneously improving multiple trustworthiness dimensions (e.g., safety, factualness, bias) in large language models without additional training. It proposes Sparse Activation Control, which locates sparse, task-specific attention heads in LLMs and manipulates them to independently control different behavioral aspects. Experiments on Llama models demonstrate that this approach successfully aligns the model with human preferences across safety, factualness, and bias concurrently. This paper advances alignment methodology by introducing a mechanistic, training-free control technique, but it does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了在不进行额外训练的情况下，同时提升大语言模型多个可信维度（如安全性、事实性、偏见）的难题。提出了稀疏激活控制方法，通过定位模型中稀疏且任务特定的注意力头，并对其进行操控，实现近乎独立的控制不同行为方面。在Llama系列模型上的实验表明，该方法能同时使模型在安全性、事实性和偏见上对齐人类偏好。本文通过引入一种基于机制、无需训练的控制技术推动了对齐方法论的发展，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Efficient Adversarial Training in LLMs with Continuous Attacks
papers.short_title: C-AdvUL: Continuous Adv Training for LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that can bypass their safety guardrails. In many domains, adversarial training has proven to be one of the most promising methods to reliably improve robustness against such attacks. Yet, in the context of LLMs, current methods for adversarial training are hindered by the high computational costs required to perform discrete adversarial attacks at each training iteration. We address this problem by instead calculating adversarial attacks in the continuous embedding space of the LLM, which is orders of magnitudes more efficient. We propose a fast adversarial training algorithm (C-AdvUL) composed of two losses: the first makes the model robust on continuous embedding attacks computed on an adversarial behaviour dataset; the second ensures the usefulness of the final model by fine-tuning on utility data. Moreover, we introduce C-AdvIPO, an adversarial variant of IPO that does not require utility data for adversarially robust alignment. Our empirical evaluation on five models from different families (Gemma, Phi3, Mistral, Zephyr, Llama2) and at different scales (2B, 3.8B, 7B) shows that both algorithms substantially enhance LLM robustness against discrete attacks (GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR), while maintaining utility. Our results demonstrate that robustness to continuous perturbations can extrapolate to discrete threat models. Thereby, we present a path toward scalable adversarial training algorithms for robustly aligning LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the high computational cost of adversarial training in LLMs caused by discrete attacks. It proposes C-AdvUL, an efficient algorithm that computes adversarial attacks in the continuous embedding space, using a robustness loss and a utility fine-tuning loss; a variant C-AdvIPO needs no utility data. Evaluated on Gemma, Phi3, Mistral, Zephyr, and Llama2 (2B-7B), it substantially boosts robustness to discrete attacks like GCG, AutoDAN, and PAIR while preserving utility. This work directly tackles the fragility of post-training safety alignment by providing a scalable hardening method, showing continuous adversarial training can extrapolate to discrete threat models.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了大语言模型中因离散攻击导致对抗训练计算成本高的问题。提出C-AdvUL，在连续嵌入空间中计算对抗攻击以提高效率，结合对抗损失和效用微调损失；变体C-AdvIPO无需效用数据。在Gemma、Phi3、Mistral、Zephyr、Llama2等模型（2B-7B）上的评估显示，对GCG、AutoDAN、PAIR等离散攻击的鲁棒性显著增强，且保持模型效用。该研究直接应对安全对齐的脆弱性，通过可扩展的对抗训练方法强化模型，证明连续对抗训练可推广至离散威胁模型。

papers.title: TrojLLM: A Black-box Trojan Prompt Attack on Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are progressively being utilized as machine learning services and interface tools for various applications. However, the security implications of LLMs, particularly in relation to adversarial and Trojan attacks, remain insufficiently examined. In this paper, we propose TrojLLM, an automatic and black-box framework to effectively generate universal and stealthy triggers. When these triggers are incorporated into the input data, the LLMs' outputs can be maliciously manipulated.   Moreover, the framework also supports embedding Trojans within discrete prompts, enhancing the overall effectiveness and precision of the triggers' attacks.  Specifically, we propose a trigger discovery algorithm for generating universal triggers for various inputs by querying victim LLM-based APIs using few-shot data samples. Furthermore, we introduce a novel progressive Trojan poisoning algorithm designed to generate poisoned prompts that retain efficacy and transferability across a diverse range of models. Our experiments and results demonstrate TrojLLM's capacity to effectively insert Trojans into text prompts in real-world black-box LLM APIs including GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, while maintaining exceptional performance on clean test sets. Our work sheds light on the potential security risks in current models and offers a potential defensive approach. The source code of TrojLLM is available at https://github.com/UCF-ML-Research/TrojLLM.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the risk of Trojan attacks on LLMs, where trigger-embedded inputs can maliciously manipulate outputs. It proposes TrojLLM, an automatic black-box framework that discovers universal triggers via few-shot queries and uses progressive poisoning to create stealthy, transferable poisoned prompts. Evaluated on black-box APIs like GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, it effectively injects Trojans while maintaining clean performance. This reveals a fragility in post-training safety alignment, as the attack bypasses alignment via prompt injection without modifying model weights.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文探讨了LLM面临的Trojan攻击风险，攻击者可通过植入触发器的输入恶意操控输出。提出TrojLLM框架，一种自动黑盒方法，利用少量样本查询发现通用触发器，并通过渐进污染算法生成隐蔽且可迁移的恶意提示。在GPT-3.5和GPT-4等黑盒API上评估，表明能有效注入Trojan且保持洁净测试性能。这揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，攻击通过提示注入绕过对齐而无需修改模型权重。

papers.title: Online Iterative Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with General Preference Model
papers.abstract: We investigate Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in the context of a general preference oracle. In particular, we do not assume the existence of a reward function and an oracle preference signal drawn from the Bradley-Terry model as most of the prior works do.  We consider a standard mathematical formulation, the reverse-KL regularized minimax game between two LLMs for RLHF under general preference oracle.
