The learning objective of this formulation is to find a policy so that it is consistently preferred by the KL-regularized preference oracle over any competing LLMs. We show that this framework is strictly more general than the reward-based one, and propose sample-efficient algorithms for both the offline learning from a pre-collected preference dataset and online learning where we can query the preference oracle along the way of training. Empirical studies verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) without assuming a reward function or Bradley-Terry preference model, instead using a general preference oracle. It formulates a reverse-KL regularized minimax game between two LLMs and proposes sample-efficient algorithms for both offline and online settings. Empirical studies on language tasks validate the effectiveness of the framework. This work advances RLHF methodology by generalizing preference modeling but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文在无需假设奖励函数或Bradley-Terry偏好模型的情况下，基于通用偏好预言机研究人类反馈强化学习（RLHF）。提出了一种两个大语言模型之间的逆KL正则化极小极大博弈公式，并分别针对离线和在线场景设计了样本高效算法。语言任务实验证实了框架的有效性。该工作通过泛化偏好建模推进了RLHF方法，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的稳健性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Uncovering Safety Risks of Large Language Models through Concept Activation Vector
papers.abstract: Despite careful safety alignment, current large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to various attacks. To further unveil the safety risks of LLMs, we introduce a Safety Concept Activation Vector (SCAV) framework, which effectively guides the attacks by accurately interpreting LLMs' safety mechanisms. We then develop an SCAV-guided attack method that can generate both attack prompts and embedding-level attacks with automatically selected perturbation hyperparameters. Both automatic and human evaluations demonstrate that our attack method significantly improves the attack success rate and response quality while requiring less training data. Additionally, we find that our generated attack prompts may be transferable to GPT-4, and the embedding-level attacks may also be transferred to other white-box LLMs whose parameters are known. Our experiments further uncover the safety risks present in current LLMs. For example, in our evaluation of seven open-source LLMs, we observe an average attack success rate of 99.14%, based on the classic keyword-matching criterion. Finally, we provide insights into the safety mechanism of LLMs. The code is available at https://github.com/SproutNan/AI-Safety_SCAV.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the vulnerability of safety-aligned LLMs by proposing the Safety Concept Activation Vector (SCAV) framework, which interprets safety mechanisms and guides both prompt-level and embedding-level attacks with automatically selected hyperparameters. Experiments on seven open-source LLMs yield a 99.14% average attack success rate, with attack prompts transferring to GPT-4 and embedding attacks transferring to other white-box models. By exposing high attack success and transferability, this work strongly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, directly informing the SoK's central question on alignment robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对经过安全对齐的 LLM 仍易受攻击的问题，提出安全概念激活向量（SCAV）框架，通过解释安全机制并自动选择超参数，生成攻击提示和嵌入层攻击。在七个开源 LLM 上评估，平均攻击成功率达 99.14%，且攻击提示可迁移至 GPT-4，嵌入层攻击可迁移至其他白盒模型。该工作通过高攻击成功率和迁移性，有力证明了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，直接回应了关于对齐鲁棒性的核心问题。

papers.title: Watch Out for Your Agents! Investigating Backdoor Threats to LLM-Based Agents
papers.abstract: Driven by the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-based agents have been developed to handle various real-world applications, including finance, healthcare, and shopping, etc. It is crucial to ensure the reliability and security of LLM-based agents during applications. However, the safety issues of LLM-based agents are currently under-explored. In this work, we take the first step to investigate one of the typical safety threats, backdoor attack, to LLM-based agents. We first formulate a general framework of agent backdoor attacks, then we present a thorough analysis of different forms of agent backdoor attacks. Specifically, compared with traditional backdoor attacks on LLMs that are only able to manipulate the user inputs and model outputs, agent backdoor attacks exhibit more diverse and covert forms: (1) From the perspective of the final attacking outcomes, the agent backdoor attacker can not only choose to manipulate the final output distribution, but also introduce the malicious behavior in an intermediate reasoning step only, while keeping the final output correct. (2) Furthermore, the former category can be divided into two subcategories based on trigger locations, in which the backdoor trigger can either be hidden in the user query or appear in an intermediate observation returned by the external environment. We implement the above variations of agent backdoor attacks on two typical agent tasks including web shopping and tool utilization. Extensive experiments show that LLM-based agents suffer severely from backdoor attacks and such backdoor vulnerability cannot be easily mitigated by current textual backdoor defense algorithms. This indicates an urgent need for further research on the development of targeted defenses against backdoor attacks on LLM-based agents. Warning: This paper may contain biased content.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates backdoor attacks on LLM-based agents, an underexplored safety threat. It formulates a general framework and analyzes diverse attack forms, including manipulation of intermediate reasoning steps and triggers in user queries or environmental observations. Experiments on web shopping and tool utilization show that agents are highly vulnerable, and existing textual backdoor defenses are ineffective. This work reveals a new attack surface, suggesting that post-training safety alignment is fragile in agent settings where backdoors can be covertly inserted and triggered.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体所面临的未充分探索的安全威胁——后门攻击。提出了一个通用的智能体后门攻击框架，并分析了多种攻击形式，包括操纵中间推理步骤、将触发器隐藏在用户查询或环境返回的观察结果中。在网络购物和工具使用任务上的实验表明，LLM智能体极易受到后门攻击，且现有的文本后门防御方法无法有效缓解。这揭示了新的攻击面，表明在智能体设置中，后训练安全对齐可能是脆弱的，因为后门可以隐蔽地植入和触发。

papers.title: Bag of Tricks: Benchmarking of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
papers.abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in executing complex tasks in a zero-shot manner, they are susceptible to jailbreak attacks and can be manipulated to produce harmful outputs. Recently, a growing body of research has categorized jailbreak attacks into token-level and prompt-level attacks. However, previous work primarily overlooks the diverse key factors of jailbreak attacks, with most studies concentrating on LLM vulnerabilities and lacking exploration of defense-enhanced LLMs. To address these issues, we introduced $\textbf{JailTrickBench}$ to evaluate the impact of various attack settings on LLM performance and provide a baseline for jailbreak attacks, encouraging the adoption of a standardized evaluation framework. Specifically, we evaluate the eight key factors of implementing jailbreak attacks on LLMs from both target-level and attack-level perspectives. We further conduct seven representative jailbreak attacks on six defense methods across two widely used datasets, encompassing approximately 354 experiments with about 55,000 GPU hours on A800-80G. Our experimental results highlight the need for standardized benchmarking to evaluate these attacks on defense-enhanced LLMs. Our code is available at https://github.com/usail-hkust/JailTrickBench.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of standardized benchmarking for jailbreak attacks on LLMs, particularly those with defense enhancements. It introduces JailTrickBench, a framework that systematically evaluates eight key attack factors across target and attack levels. Conducting ~354 experiments with seven attacks and six defenses on two datasets (∼55,000 GPU hours), the study reveals significant variability in LLM robustness and emphasizes the need for standardized evaluation. The findings provide direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as even defense-augmented LLMs can be compromised under diverse attack settings.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对越狱攻击在防御增强型大语言模型（LLM）上缺乏标准化评估基准的问题，提出了JailTrickBench框架，从目标和攻击两个层面系统评估越狱攻击的八项关键因素。通过使用七种攻击方法、六种防御策略，在两个数据集上开展约354次实验（耗费约5.5万GPU小时），揭示了LLM鲁棒性的显著差异，强调标准化评估的必要性。该研究直接证明了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：即便结合了防御机制，LLM在多样化攻击设置下仍可被绕过。

papers.title: MetaAligner: Towards Generalizable Multi-Objective Alignment of Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) focus on aligning to heterogeneous human expectations and values via multi-objective preference alignment. However, existing methods are dependent on the policy model parameters, which require high-cost repetition of their alignment algorithms for each new policy model, and they cannot expand to unseen objectives due to their static alignment objectives. In this work, we propose Meta-Objective Aligner (MetaAligner), the first policy-agnostic and generalizable method for multi-objective preference alignment.MetaAligner models multi-objective alignment into three stages: (1) dynamic objectives reformulation algorithm reorganizes traditional alignment datasets to supervise the model on performing flexible alignment across different objectives; (2) conditional weak-to-strong correction paradigm aligns the weak outputs of fixed policy models to approach strong outputs with higher preferences in the corresponding alignment objectives, enabling plug-and-play inferences on any policy models, which significantly reduces training costs and facilitates alignment on close-source policy models; (3) generalizable inference method flexibly adjusts target objectives by updating their text descriptions in the prompts, facilitating generalizable alignment to unseen objectives.Experimental results show that MetaAligner achieves significant and balanced improvements in multi-objective alignments on 10 state-of-the-art policy models, and saves up to 93.63% of GPU training hours compared to previous alignment methods. The model also effectively aligns unseen objectives, marking the first step towards generalizable multi-objective preference alignment.
papers.summary_en: Existing multi-objective alignment methods are policy-dependent and cannot generalize to unseen objectives. MetaAligner is a policy-agnostic approach that reorganizes alignment data, uses weak-to-strong correction on fixed policy outputs, and adjusts objectives via text prompts during inference. It achieves balanced multi-objective improvements on 10 state-of-the-art policy models and saves up to 93.63% GPU hours compared to prior methods, while also aligning unseen objectives. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly address the fragility question.
papers.summary_zh: 现有多目标对齐方法依赖于策略模型且无法泛化到未见目标。MetaAligner 是一种策略无关的方法，通过重组对齐数据、对固定策略输出进行弱到强纠正，并在推理时通过文本提示调整目标，实现了灵活的对齐。它在10个最先进的策略模型上取得了平衡的多目标对齐改进，与先前方法相比节省了高达93.63%的GPU训练时间，还能对未见目标进行对齐。本文推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: Preference-grounded Token-level Guidance for Language Model Fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Aligning language models (LMs) with preferences is an important problem in natural language generation. A key challenge is that preferences are typically provided at the sequence level while LM training and generation both occur at the token level. There is, therefore, a granularity mismatch between the preference and the LM training losses, which may complicate the learning problem. In this paper, we address this issue by developing an alternate training process, where we iterate between grounding the sequence-level preference into token-level training guidance, and improving the LM with the learned guidance. For guidance learning, we design a framework that extends the pairwise-preference learning in imitation learning to both variable-length LM generation and the utilization of the preference among multiple generations. For LM training, based on the amount of supervised data, we present two minimalist learning objectives that utilize the learned guidance. In experiments, our method performs competitively on two distinct representative LM tasks --- discrete-prompt generation and text summarization.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the granularity mismatch between sequence-level human preferences and token-level training losses in language model alignment. It proposes an iterative training process that first grounds sequence-level preferences into token-level guidance using a framework extended from pairwise-preference imitation learning, and then fine-tunes the LM with the learned guidance via two minimalist objectives. Evaluated on discrete-prompt generation and text summarization, the method shows competitive performance, effectively bridging the preference granularity gap. While it improves alignment methodology, it does not directly investigate whether post-training safety alignment is robust or fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了语言模型对齐中序列级人类偏好与令牌级训练损失之间的粒度不匹配问题。它提出了一种迭代训练过程，首先使用从成对偏好模仿学习扩展而来的框架将序列级偏好转化为令牌级指导，然后通过两个极简目标利用所学指导微调语言模型。在离散提示生成和文本摘要任务上的评估显示，该方法性能具有竞争力，有效弥合了偏好粒度差距。尽管它改进了对齐方法，但并未直接研究训练后安全对齐是否稳健或脆弱。

papers.title: LoFiT: Localized Fine-tuning on LLM Representations
papers.abstract: Recent work in interpretability shows that large language models (LLMs) can be adapted for new tasks in a learning-free way: it is possible to intervene on LLM representations to elicit desired behaviors for alignment. For instance, adding certain bias vectors to the outputs of certain attention heads is reported to boost the truthfulness of models. In this work, we show that localized fine-tuning serves as an effective alternative to such representation intervention methods. We introduce a framework called Localized Fine-Tuning on LLM Representations (LoFiT), which identifies a subset of attention heads that are most important for learning a specific task, then trains offset vectors to add to the model's hidden representations at those selected heads. LoFiT localizes to a sparse set of heads (3%-10%) and learns the offset vectors from limited training data, comparable to the settings used for representation intervention. For truthfulness and reasoning tasks, we find that LoFiT's intervention vectors are more effective for LLM adaptation than vectors from representation intervention methods such as Inference-time Intervention. We also find that the localization step is important: selecting a task-specific set of attention heads can lead to higher performance than intervening on heads selected for a different task. Finally, across 7 tasks we study, LoFiT achieves comparable performance to other parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as LoRA, despite modifying 20x-200x fewer parameters than these methods.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of adapting large language models (LLMs) for new tasks like truthfulness and reasoning without full fine-tuning. It proposes LoFiT (Localized Fine-tuning on LLM Representations), which identifies a sparse set of task-critical attention heads and learns small offset vectors to add to their hidden representations. Evaluated on truthfulness and reasoning benchmarks, LoFiT outperforms representation intervention methods such as Inference-time Intervention and achieves performance comparable to parameter-efficient methods like LoRA, while modifying 20x–200x fewer parameters. This paper introduces an efficient alignment technique but does not directly investigate the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了无需全面微调即可将大语言模型适应新任务（如真实性和推理）的挑战。提出了 LoFiT（基于大语言模型表示的局部微调），该方法识别出对任务至关重要的稀疏注意力头子集，并学习添加到这些头隐藏表示的小偏移向量。在真实性和推理基准测试中，LoFiT 优于表示干预方法（如推理时干预），并取得了与参数高效方法（如 LoRA）相当的性能，但修改的参数数量减少了 20 到 200 倍。本文介绍了一种高效的模型对齐技术，但没有直接研究训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Regularizing Hidden States Enables Learning Generalizable Reward Model for LLMs
papers.abstract: Reward models trained on human preference data have been proven to effectively align Large Language Models (LLMs) with human intent within the framework of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, current reward models have limited generalization capabilities to unseen prompts and responses, which can lead to an unexpected phenomenon known as reward over-optimization, resulting in a decline in actual performance due to excessive optimization of rewards. While previous research has advocated for constraining policy optimization, our study introduces a novel approach to enhance the reward model's generalization ability against distribution shifts by regularizing the hidden states. Specifically, we retain the base model's language model head and incorporate a suite of text-generation losses to preserve the hidden states' text-generation capabilities, while concurrently learning a reward head behind the same hidden states. Our experimental results demonstrate that the introduced regularization technique markedly improves the accuracy of learned reward models across a variety of out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks and effectively alleviates the over-optimization issue in RLHF, offering a more reliable and robust preference learning paradigm.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses reward over-optimization in RLHF, where reward models fail to generalize to out-of-distribution prompts and responses, leading to degraded alignment. It proposes regularizing the hidden states by retaining the base model's language model head and adding text-generation losses, while jointly learning a reward head, thereby preserving generalization capabilities. Experiments show substantial accuracy gains on OOD tasks and effective mitigation of over-optimization across multiple settings. By directly hardening the reward model against distribution shifts, this work strengthens a core component of post-training alignment and demonstrates improved robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对 RLHF 中奖励模型泛化能力不足导致的奖励过度优化问题，提出通过保留基座模型的语言模型头并引入文本生成损失来正则化隐藏状态，同时学习奖励头，以增强泛化能力。实验表明，该方法在多种分布外任务上显著提升奖励模型准确度，并有效缓解过度优化现象。该研究从奖励建模角度加固了后训练对齐的一个关键环节，直接回应了对齐脆弱性问题，提升了整体鲁棒性。

papers.title: Large Language Model Unlearning
papers.abstract: We study how to perform unlearning, i.e. forgetting undesirable misbehaviors, on large language models (LLMs). We show at least three scenarios of aligning LLMs with human preferences can benefit from unlearning: (1) removing harmful responses, (2) erasing copyright-protected content as requested, and (3) reducing hallucinations. Unlearning, as an alignment technique, has three advantages. (1) It only requires negative (e.g. harmful) examples, which are much easier and cheaper to collect (e.g. via red teaming or user reporting) than positive (e.g. helpful and often human-written) examples required in RLHF (RL from human feedback). (2) It is computationally efficient. (3) It is especially effective when we know which training samples cause the misbehavior. To the best of our knowledge, our work is among the first to explore LLM unlearning. We are also among the first to formulate the settings, goals, and evaluations in LLM unlearning. We show that if practitioners only have limited resources, and therefore the priority is to stop generating undesirable outputs rather than to try to generate desirable outputs, unlearning is particularly appealing. Despite only having negative samples, our ablation study shows that unlearning can still achieve better alignment performance than RLHF with just 2% of its computational time.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning large language models by removing undesirable behaviors such as harmful outputs, copyrighted content, and hallucinations through unlearning. It proposes unlearning as an efficient alignment technique that leverages only negative examples to forget specific misbehaviors, without needing positive examples as in RLHF. Experiments demonstrate that unlearning achieves better alignment performance than RLHF on these tasks, using only 2% of the computational time. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究如何通过“遗忘”来消除大语言模型中的不良行为，如生成有害内容、侵权文本和幻觉。提出了一种基于负例的遗忘对齐方法，无需正例即可高效地移除特定不良行为。实验表明，遗忘对齐在去除有害回复、删除版权内容、减少幻觉等任务上，仅用RLHF 2%的计算时间便实现了更好的对齐效果。该工作推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性问题。

papers.title: SafeWorld: Geo-Diverse Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of Large Language Models (LLMs), ensuring safety is a crucial and widely discussed topic. However, existing works often overlook the geo-diversity of cultural and legal standards across the world. To demonstrate the challenges posed by geo-diverse safety standards, we introduce SafeWorld, a novel benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate responses that are not only helpful but also culturally sensitive and legally compliant across diverse global contexts. SafeWorld encompasses 2,342 test user queries, each grounded in high-quality, human-verified cultural norms and legal policies from 50 countries and 493 regions/races. On top of it, we propose a multi-dimensional automatic safety evaluation framework that assesses the contextual appropriateness, accuracy, and comprehensiveness of responses. Our evaluations reveal that current LLMs struggle to meet these criteria. To enhance LLMs' alignment with geo-diverse safety standards, we synthesize helpful preference pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) alignment training. The preference pair construction aims to encourage LLMs to behave appropriately and provide precise references to relevant cultural norms and policies when necessary. Our trained SafeWorldLM outperforms all competing models, including GPT-4o on all three evaluation dimensions by a large margin. Global human evaluators also note a nearly 20% higher winning rate in helpfulness and harmfulness evaluation. Our code and data can be found here: https://github.com/PlusLabNLP/SafeWorld.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge that current LLM safety alignment fails to account for diverse global cultural and legal norms. It introduces SafeWorld, a benchmark of 2,342 queries grounded in norms from 50 countries and 493 regions, along with a multi-dimensional evaluation of contextual appropriateness, accuracy, and comprehensiveness. By synthesizing preference pairs for DPO training, the authors create SafeWorldLM, which significantly outperforms GPT-4o and other models on all dimensions and shows a ~20% higher human evaluation win rate. While advancing alignment for geo-diverse safety, the paper does not directly examine the fragility of post-training alignment against adversarial attacks or mechanistic weaknesses.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对当前大语言模型安全对齐未能适应全球多元文化与法律标准的问题，提出SafeWorld基准，包含基于50个国家/493地区的2342个查询，以及评估上下文适宜性、准确性和全面性的多维自动框架。通过构造偏好对进行DPO训练，得到SafeWorldLM，在所有维度上大幅超越GPT-4o等模型，人工评估胜率提升近20%。该工作提升了面向地理多样性的安全对齐方法，但未直接探究后训练对齐在面对对抗攻击或机制缺陷时的脆弱性。

papers.title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback
papers.short_title: RRHF: Rank Responses for LM Alignment
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) facilitates the alignment of large language models with human preferences, significantly enhancing the quality of interactions between humans and models. InstructGPT implements RLHF through several stages, including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), reward model training, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). However, PPO is sensitive to hyperparameters and requires multiple models in its standard implementation, making it hard to train and scale up to larger parameter counts.In contrast, we propose a novel learning paradigm called RRHF, which scores sampled responses from different sources via a logarithm of conditional probabilities and learns to align these probabilities with human preferences through ranking loss.RRHF can leverage sampled responses from various sources including the model responses from itself, other large language model responses, and human expert responses to learn to rank them.RRHF only needs 1 to 2 models during tuning and can efficiently align language models with human preferences robustly without complex hyperparameter tuning. Additionally, RRHF can be considered an extension of SFT and reward model training while being simpler than PPO in terms of coding, model counts, and hyperparameters. We evaluate RRHF on the Helpful and Harmless dataset, demonstrating comparable alignment performance with PPO by reward model score and human labeling.Extensive experiments show that the performance of RRHF is highly related to sampling quality which suggests RRHF is a best-of-$n$ learner.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the complexity and instability of RLHF with PPO, which requires multiple models and sensitive hyperparameters. It proposes RRHF, a novel paradigm that scores and ranks responses from various sources using conditional log probabilities and ranking loss, needing only 1–2 models. On the Helpful and Harmless dataset, RRHF achieves alignment comparable to PPO according to reward model and human evaluations, with performance tied to sampling quality. This paper advances alignment methodology but does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中PPO的超参数敏感性与多模型复杂性，提出RRHF方法，通过条件概率对数对不同来源的响应进行排序损失学习，仅需1-2个模型即可完成对齐，无需复杂超参调试。在Helpful和Harmless数据集上，根据奖励模型和人工评估，RRHF取得了与PPO相当的对齐效果，且性能高度依赖于采样质量。本文推进了对齐方法，但未直接探究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性问题。

papers.title: MultiTrust: A Comprehensive Benchmark Towards Trustworthy Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Despite the superior capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) across diverse tasks, they still face significant trustworthiness challenges. Yet, current literature on the assessment of trustworthy MLLMs remains limited, lacking a holistic evaluation to offer thorough insights into future improvements. In this work, we establish MultiTrust, the first comprehensive and unified benchmark on the trustworthiness of MLLMs across five primary aspects: truthfulness, safety, robustness, fairness, and privacy. Our benchmark employs a rigorous evaluation strategy that addresses both multimodal risks and cross-modal impacts, encompassing 32 diverse tasks with self-curated datasets. Extensive experiments with 21 modern MLLMs reveal some previously unexplored trustworthiness issues and risks, highlighting the complexities introduced by the multimodality and underscoring the necessity for advanced methodologies to enhance their reliability. For instance, typical proprietary models still struggle with the perception of visually confusing images and are vulnerable to multimodal jailbreaking and adversarial attacks; MLLMs are more inclined to disclose privacy in text and reveal ideological and cultural biases even when paired with irrelevant images in inference, indicating that the multimodality amplifies the internal risks from base LLMs. Additionally, we release a scalable toolbox for standardized trustworthiness research, aiming to facilitate future advancements in this important field. Code and resources are publicly available at: https://multi-trust.github.io/.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the lack of holistic trustworthiness evaluation for multimodal LLMs. It proposes MultiTrust, a comprehensive benchmark covering truthfulness, safety, robustness, fairness, and privacy across 32 tasks with self-curated datasets. Evaluation of 21 MLLMs reveals novel vulnerabilities such as visual confusion, multimodal jailbreaking, and amplified biases, showing that multimodality exacerbates risks from base LLMs. This work provides direct evidence that post-training safety alignment is fragile, as multimodal inputs introduce new attack surfaces that can bypass existing safeguards.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型缺乏整体可信度评估的问题，提出了MultiTrust基准，系统覆盖真实性、安全性、鲁棒性、公平性和隐私五个维度，包含32个任务和自建数据集。对21个多模态大语言模型的评估揭示了视觉混淆、多模态越狱、偏见放大等新漏洞，表明多模态会放大基础大语言模型的内在风险。该研究直接证实了安全对齐的脆弱性，因多模态输入引入了可绕过现有防护的新攻击面。

papers.title: Panacea: Pareto Alignment via Preference Adaptation for LLMs
papers.abstract: Current methods for large language model alignment typically use scalar human preference labels. However, this convention tends to oversimplify the multi-dimensional and heterogeneous nature of human preferences, leading to reduced expressivity and even misalignment. This paper presents Panacea, an innovative approach that reframes alignment as a multi-dimensional preference optimization problem. Panacea trains a single model capable of adapting online and Pareto-optimally to diverse sets of preferences without the need for further tuning. A major challenge here is using a low-dimensional preference vector to guide the model's behavior, despite it being governed by an overwhelmingly large number of parameters. To address this, Panacea is designed to use singular value decomposition (SVD)-based low-rank adaptation, which allows the preference vector to be simply injected online as singular values. Theoretically, we prove that Panacea recovers the entire Pareto front with common loss aggregation methods under mild conditions. Moreover, our experiments demonstrate, for the first time, the feasibility of aligning a single LLM to represent an exponentially vast spectrum of human preferences through various optimization methods. Our work marks a step forward in effectively and efficiently aligning models to diverse and intricate human preferences in a controllable and Pareto-optimal manner.
papers.summary_en: Current scalar-based alignment oversimplifies multi-dimensional human preferences, causing expressivity loss and misalignment. Panacea reframes alignment as multi-dimensional preference optimization, training a single model to adapt online and Pareto-optimally to diverse preferences without further tuning via SVD-based low-rank adaptation that injects preference vectors as singular values. Theoretically, it recovers the whole Pareto front under mild conditions; experiments first demonstrate aligning a single LLM to an exponentially vast preference spectrum. This paper advances alignment methodology with controllable Pareto-optimality but does not directly address the fragility of post-training safety alignment against attacks or distribution shifts.
papers.summary_zh: 标量偏好标签的对齐简化了多维人类偏好，导致表达力下降和错位。Panacea将对齐重塑为多维偏好优化问题，通过基于SVD的低秩适配，将偏好向量在线注入为奇异值，训练单一模型无需进一步调优即可帕累托最优地适应多样化偏好。理论证明在温和条件下可恢复整个帕累托前沿，实验首次展示单一LLM能表示指数级广泛的人类偏好。该工作推进了可控帕累托最优对齐方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐在攻击或分布偏移下的脆弱性。

papers.title: Automated Multi-level Preference for MLLMs
papers.abstract: Current multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) suffer from ''hallucination'', occasionally generating responses that are not grounded in the input images. To tackle this challenge, one promising path is to utilize reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), which steers MLLMs towards learning superior responses while avoiding inferior ones. We rethink the common practice of using binary preferences (i.e., superior, inferior), and find that adopting multi-level preferences (e.g., superior, medium, inferior) is better for two benefits: 1) It narrows the gap between adjacent levels, thereby encouraging MLLMs to discern subtle differences. 2) It further integrates cross-level comparisons (beyond adjacent-level comparisons), thus providing a broader range of comparisons with hallucination examples. To verify our viewpoint, we present the Automated Multi-level Preference (AMP) framework for MLLMs. To facilitate this framework, we first develop an automated dataset generation pipeline that provides high-quality multi-level preference datasets without any human annotators. Furthermore, we design the Multi-level Direct Preference Optimization (MDPO) algorithm to robustly conduct complex multi-level preference learning. Additionally, we propose a new hallucination benchmark, MRHal-Bench. Extensive experiments across public hallucination and general benchmarks, as well as our MRHal-Bench, demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Code is available at https://github.com/takomc/amp.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses hallucination in multimodal LLMs by moving beyond binary preference feedback in RLHF to multi-level preferences. It proposes the Automated Multi-level Preference (AMP) framework, featuring an automated dataset generation pipeline and the Multi-level Direct Preference Optimization (MDPO) algorithm. Evaluations on hallucination and general benchmarks, including the newly introduced MRHal-Bench, show improved performance. This work advances alignment methodology but does not directly study the fragility or bypassability of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对多模态大语言模型中的幻觉问题，提出在RLHF中采用多层级偏好反馈替代传统的二元偏好。具体提出了自动化多层级偏好（AMP）框架，包含自动化数据集生成流程和多层级直接偏好优化（MDPO）算法。在幻觉基准和通用基准上的实验，以及新提出的MRHal-Bench基准，验证了方法有效性。该研究推进了对齐方法论，但并未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或可绕过性。

papers.title: Improved Few-Shot Jailbreaking Can Circumvent Aligned Language Models and Their Defenses
papers.abstract: Recently, Anil et al. (2024) show that many-shot (up to hundreds of) demonstrations can jailbreak state-of-the-art LLMs by exploiting their long-context capability. Nevertheless, is it possible to use few-shot demonstrations to efficiently jailbreak LLMs within limited context sizes? While the vanilla few-shot jailbreaking may be inefficient, we propose improved techniques such as injecting special system tokens like [/INST] and employing demo-level random search from a collected demo pool. These simple techniques result in surprisingly effective jailbreaking against aligned LLMs (even with advanced defenses). For examples, our method achieves>80% (mostly>95%) ASRs on Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B without multiple restarts, even if the models are enhanced by strong defenses such as perplexity detection and/or SmoothLLM, which is challenging for suffix-based jailbreaking. In addition, we conduct comprehensive and elaborate (e.g., making sure to use correct system prompts) evaluations against other aligned LLMs and advanced defenses, where our method consistently achieves nearly 100% ASRs. Our code is available at https://github.com/sail-sg/I-FSJ.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates jailbreaking aligned LLMs using few-shot demonstrations within limited context sizes, as an alternative to many-shot attacks. It proposes improved techniques: injecting special system tokens like [/INST] and performing demo-level random search over a collected pool of demonstrations. The method achieves over 80% (mostly >95%) attack success rates on Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B, even under strong defenses like perplexity detection and SmoothLLM, without multiple restarts. By demonstrating that simple enhanced few-shot demonstrations can consistently bypass safety alignment, this work strongly supports the view that post-training safety alignment is fragile and easily circumvented.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了在有限上下文长度内用少样本示例对对齐的大语言模型进行越狱攻击的问题，以替代大量示例的多样本攻击。它提出改进技术：注入特殊系统令牌如[/INST]，并从收集的示例池中进行示例级随机搜索。该方法在Llama-2-7B和Llama-3-8B上取得了超过80%（大多超过95%）的攻击成功率，即使模型配备了困惑度检测或SmoothLLM等强防御措施，且无需多次重启。通过展示简单的增强少样本演示就能持续绕过安全对齐，这项工作有力地证明了后训练安全对齐是脆弱的且容易被绕过。

papers.title: ALI-Agent: Assessing LLMs' Alignment with Human Values via Agent-based Evaluation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can elicit unintended and even harmful content when misaligned with human values, posing severe risks to users and society. To mitigate these risks, current evaluation benchmarks predominantly employ expert-designed contextual scenarios to assess how well LLMs align with human values. However, the labor-intensive nature of these benchmarks limits their test scope, hindering their ability to generalize to the extensive variety of open-world use cases and identify rare but crucial long-tail risks. Additionally, these static tests fail to adapt to the rapid evolution of LLMs, making it hard to evaluate timely alignment issues. To address these challenges, we propose ALI-Agent, an evaluation framework that leverages the autonomous abilities of LLM-powered agents to conduct in-depth and adaptive alignment assessments. ALI-Agent operates through two principal stages: Emulation and Refinement. During the Emulation stage, ALI-Agent automates the generation of realistic test scenarios. In the Refinement stage, it iteratively refines the scenarios to probe long-tail risks. Specifically, ALI-Agent incorporates a memory module to guide test scenario generation, a tool-using module to reduce human labor in tasks such as evaluating feedback from target LLMs, and an action module to refine tests. Extensive experiments across three aspects of human values--stereotypes, morality, and legality--demonstrate that ALI-Agent, as a general evaluation framework, effectively identifies model misalignment. Systematic analysis also validates that the generated test scenarios represent meaningful use cases, as well as integrate enhanced measures to probe long-tail risks. Our code is available at https://github.com/SophieZheng998/ALI-Agent.git
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of evaluating LLMs' alignment with human values, where existing static benchmarks are labor-intensive and have limited coverage. It proposes ALI-Agent, an agent-based framework that autonomously generates realistic test scenarios and iteratively refines them to probe long-tail risks, using memory, tool-using, and action modules. Evaluated on stereotypes, morality, and legality dimensions, ALI-Agent effectively identifies model misalignment with reduced human effort. This work advances alignment evaluation methodology but does not directly examine the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决现有静态评估基准在人力密集且覆盖范围有限的情况下，评估大模型与人类价值对齐的挑战。提出基于智能体的评估框架ALI-Agent，通过记忆、工具使用和行动模块自主生成现实测试场景并迭代优化以探测长尾风险。在刻板印象、道德性和合法性三个维度上的实验表明，ALI-Agent能有效识别模型对齐偏差，同时减少人工投入。该工作推进了对齐评估方法，但未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Robust Prompt Optimization for Defending Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
papers.abstract: Despite advances in AI alignment, large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks or jailbreaking, in which adversaries can modify prompts to induce unwanted behavior. While some defenses have been proposed, they have not been adapted to newly proposed attacks and more challenging threat models. To address this, we propose an optimization-based objective for defending LLMs against jailbreaking attacks and an algorithm, Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO) to create robust system-level defenses. Our approach directly incorporates the adversary into the defensive objective and optimizes a lightweight and transferable suffix, enabling RPO to adapt to worst-case adaptive attacks. Our theoretical and experimental results show improved robustness to both jailbreaks seen during optimization and unknown jailbreaks, reducing the attack success rate (ASR) on GPT-4 to 6% and Llama-2 to 0% on JailbreakBench, setting the state-of-the-art. Code can be found at https://github.com/lapisrocks/rpo
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large language models to jailbreaking attacks that bypass safety alignment. It proposes Robust Prompt Optimization (RPO), which directly incorporates an adversarial threat model into the defense objective, optimizing a lightweight transferable suffix for system-level defense. Evaluated on GPT-4 and Llama-2, RPO reduces attack success rates to 6% and 0% on JailbreakBench, setting a new state-of-the-art. This work strengthens post-training safety alignment against adaptive attacks, suggesting that alignment can be hardened rather than being inherently fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在面对越狱攻击时安全对齐失效的问题，提出了一种鲁棒提示优化方法（RPO）。该方法将对抗性攻击模型直接纳入防御目标，优化一个轻量级可迁移的后缀，实现系统级防御。在GPT-4和Llama-2上的实验表明，RPO在JailbreakBench上将攻击成功率分别降至6%和0%，达到最优性能。该研究增强了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性，表明通过针对性优化可以加固对齐，而非必然脆弱。

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Overoptimization via Lightweight Uncertainty Estimation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has been pivotal in aligning Large Language Models with human values but often suffers from overopti-mization due to its reliance on a proxy reward model. To mitigate this limitation, we first propose a lightweight uncertainty quantification method that assesses the reliability of the proxy reward using only the last layer embeddings of the reward model. Enabled by this efficient uncertainty quantification method, we formulate A DV PO, a distributionally robust optimization procedure to tackle the reward overoptimization problem in RLHF. Through extensive experiments on the An-thropic HH and TL;DR summarization datasets, we verify the effectiveness of A DV PO in mitigating the overoptimization problem, resulting in enhanced RLHF performance as evaluated through human-assisted evaluation.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses reward overoptimization in RLHF, where reliance on proxy rewards leads to suboptimal alignment. It proposes a lightweight uncertainty quantification method using last-layer embeddings of the reward model and formulates ADVPO, a distributionally robust optimization procedure. Evaluating on Anthropic HH and TL;DR datasets shows ADVPO effectively mitigates overoptimization and enhances RLHF performance. This work directly tackles the fragility of alignment by hardening RLHF against reward misspecification, demonstrating improved robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对RLHF中因代理奖励模型导致的过度优化问题，提出利用奖励模型最后一层嵌入的轻量级不确定性量化方法，并基于此设计分布鲁棒优化过程ADVPO。在Anthropic HH和TL;DR数据集上的实验表明，ADVPO有效减轻过度优化，提升RLHF性能。该工作通过强化对齐方法应对奖励误设的脆弱性，直接回应了后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题。

papers.title: Adversarial Representation Engineering: A General Model Editing Framework for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Since the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has achieved remarkable success, understanding and rectifying their internal complex mechanisms has become an urgent issue. Recent research has attempted to interpret their behaviors through the lens of inner representation. However, developing practical and efficient methods for applying these representations for general and flexible model editing remains challenging. In this work, we explore how to leverage insights from representation engineering to guide the editing of LLMs by deploying a representation sensor as an editing oracle. We first identify the importance of a robust and reliable sensor during editing, then propose an Adversarial Representation Engineering (ARE) framework to provide a unified and interpretable approach for conceptual model editing without compromising baseline performance. Experiments on multiple tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of ARE in various model editing scenarios. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/Zhang-Yihao/Adversarial-Representation-Engineering.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the need for practical and flexible model editing in large language models. It proposes Adversarial Representation Engineering (ARE), a framework that uses a robust representation sensor trained adversarially to guide edits without harming baseline performance. Evaluated on multiple tasks, ARE proves effective across various editing scenarios. While this work provides a general editing tool, it does not directly investigate the fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在大语言模型中进行实用且灵活的模型编辑的需求。它提出了对抗性表征工程（ARE）框架，通过对抗训练得到鲁棒的表征传感器来指导编辑，且不影响基线性能。在多任务上的评估显示，ARE在各种编辑场景中有效。尽管该工作提供了一个通用的编辑工具，但并未直接研究后训练安全对齐的脆弱性。

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Search: Align Large Language Models via Searching over Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models are usually fine-tuned to align with human preferences. However, fine-tuning a large language model can be challenging. In this work, we introduce $\textit{weak-to-strong search}$, framing the alignment of a large language model as a test-time greedy search to maximize the log-probability difference between small tuned and untuned models while sampling from the frozen large model. This method serves both as (1) a compute-efficient model up-scaling strategy that avoids directly tuning the large model and as (2) an instance of weak-to-strong generalization that enhances a strong model with weak test-time guidance.Empirically, we demonstrate the flexibility of weak-to-strong search across different tasks. In controlled-sentiment generation and summarization, we use tuned and untuned $\texttt{gpt2}$s to improve the alignment of large models without additional training. Crucially, in a more difficult instruction-following benchmark, AlpacaEval 2.0, we show that reusing off-the-shelf small models (e.g., $\texttt{zephyr-7b-beta}$ and its untuned version) can improve the length-controlled win rates of both white-box and black-box large models against $\texttt{gpt-4-turbo}$ (e.g., $34.4\% \rightarrow 37.9\%$ for $\texttt{Llama-3-70B-Instruct}$ and $16.0\% \rightarrow 20.1\%$ for $\texttt{gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct}$), despite the small models' low win rates $\approx 10.0\%$.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of fine-tuning large language models for alignment. It proposes weak-to-strong search, a test-time decoding method that guides sampling from a frozen large model by maximizing the log-probability difference between small tuned and untuned models, avoiding direct fine-tuning. Evaluated on sentiment generation, summarization, and AlpacaEval 2.0, it improves win rates of large models like Llama-3-70B-Instruct against GPT-4-Turbo using small models with low individual win rates. This work advances alignment methodology with an external intervention but does not directly investigate the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决大语言模型对齐微调困难的问题。提出弱到强搜索，一种测试时解码方法，通过最大化小模型调优与未调优版本的对数概率差来引导冻结大模型的采样，避免直接微调。在情感生成、摘要和AlpacaEval 2.0上评估，利用自身表现不佳的小模型提升了大模型如Llama-3-70B-Instruct对GPT-4-Turbo的胜率。该方法推进了外部干预的对齐技术，但未直接研究安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: Preference Poisoning Attacks on Reward Model Learning
papers.abstract: Learning reward models from pairwise comparisons is a fundamental component in a number of domains, in-cluding autonomous control, conversational agents, and rec-ommendation systems, as part of a broad goal of aligning automated decisions with user preferences. These approaches entail collecting preference information from people, with feedback often provided anonymously. Since preferences are subjective, there is no gold standard to compare against; yet, reliance of high-impact systems on preference learning creates a strong motivation for malicious actors to skew data collected in this fashion to their ends. We investigate the nature and extent of this vulnerability by considering an attacker who can flip a small subset of preference comparisons to either promote or demote a target outcome. We propose two classes of algorithmic approaches for these attacks: a gradient-based framework, and several variants of rank-by-distance methods. Next, we evaluate the efficacy of best attacks in both these classes in successfully achieving malicious goals on datasets from three domains: autonomous control, recommendation system, and textual prompt-response preference learning. We find that the best attacks are often highly successful, achieving in the most extreme case 100% success rate with only 0.3% of the data poisoned. However, which attack is best can vary significantly across domains. In addition, we observe that the simpler and more scalable rank-by-distance approaches are often competitive with, and on occasion significantly outper-form, gradient-based methods. Finally, we show that state-of-the-art defenses against other classes of poisoning attacks exhibit limited efficacy in our setting.
papers.summary_en: This paper investigates the vulnerability of reward model learning from pairwise comparisons to data poisoning attacks, where an attacker flips a small subset of preference labels to promote or demote a target outcome. It proposes two classes of attacks: gradient-based methods and scalable rank-by-distance heuristics. Evaluated on autonomous control, recommendation, and text preference domains, the attacks achieve high success, with up to 100% success from poisoning only 0.3% of data, and rank-by-distance methods often rival or exceed gradient-based approaches. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, showing that reward models can be easily corrupted through preference data poisoning, thus undermining the robustness of alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了基于成对比较的奖励模型学习在面对数据投毒攻击时的脆弱性，攻击者通过翻转少量偏好标签以提升或降低某目标结果的排序。提出了两类攻击方法：基于梯度的框架和可扩展的基于距离排序的启发式方法。在自动驾驶控制、推荐系统和文本偏好三个领域的评估表明，攻击非常有效，极端情况下仅需0.3%的数据投毒即可实现100%成功率，且距离排序方法往往与梯度方法相当甚至更优。该工作直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性：偏好数据投毒可轻易破坏奖励模型，表明对齐过程并不稳固。

papers.title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
papers.abstract: AI systems can take harmful actions and are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. We present an approach, inspired by recent advances in representation engineering, that interrupts the models as they respond with harmful outputs with"circuit breakers."Existing techniques aimed at improving alignment, such as refusal training, are often bypassed. Techniques such as adversarial training try to plug these holes by countering specific attacks. As an alternative to refusal training and adversarial training, circuit-breaking directly controls the representations that are responsible for harmful outputs in the first place. Our technique can be applied to both text-only and multimodal language models to prevent the generation of harmful outputs without sacrificing utility -- even in the presence of powerful unseen attacks. Notably, while adversarial robustness in standalone image recognition remains an open challenge, circuit breakers allow the larger multimodal system to reliably withstand image"hijacks"that aim to produce harmful content. Finally, we extend our approach to AI agents, demonstrating considerable reductions in the rate of harmful actions when they are under attack. Our approach represents a significant step forward in the development of reliable safeguards to harmful behavior and adversarial attacks.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the fragility of AI safety alignment, where systems can be easily coerced into harmful actions by adversarial attacks that bypass refusal training. It proposes 'circuit breakers,' a representation engineering method that directly interrupts harmful output generation by controlling internal representations. Evaluated on text-only and multimodal models, it prevents harmful outputs without sacrificing utility, even under unseen attacks and image hijacks, and also reduces harmful actions in AI agents. This work directly tackles the robustness of post-training safety alignment, demonstrating a hardening method that resists both known and novel attacks, thus providing evidence that alignment need not be fragile.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对AI安全对齐的脆弱性，即系统易被对抗攻击诱导产生有害行为，而现有拒绝训练技术常被绕过。提出“断路器”方法，受表征工程启发，通过直接控制有害表征来中断有害输出生成。在纯文本和多模态模型上评估，该方法能在不损失实用性的前提下阻止有害输出，并能抵御未见攻击和图像劫持，同时也减少了AI智能体的有害行为。该工作直接应对后训练安全对齐的鲁棒性问题，展示了一种能抵抗已知和新型攻击的加固方法，为对齐并非必然脆弱提供了证据。

papers.title: PEFTGuard: Detecting Backdoor Attacks Against Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning is an essential process to improve the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in specific domains, with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) gaining popularity due to its capacity to reduce computational demands through the integration of low-rank adapters. These lightweight adapters, such as LoRA, can be shared and utilized on open-source platforms. However, adversaries could exploit this mechanism to inject backdoors into these adapters, resulting in malicious behaviors like incorrect or harmful outputs, which pose serious security risks to the community. Unfortunately, few current efforts concentrate on analyzing the backdoor patterns or detecting the backdoors in the adapters. To fill this gap, we first construct and release PADBench, a comprehensive benchmark that contains 13, 300 benign and backdoored adapters fine-tuned with various datasets, attack strategies, PEFT methods, and LLMs. Moreover, we propose PEFTGuard, the first backdoor detection framework against PEFT-based adapters. Extensive evaluation upon PADBench shows that PEFTGuard outperforms existing detection methods, achieving nearly perfect detection accuracy (100%) in most cases. Notably, PEFTGuard exhibits zero-shot transferability on three aspects, including different attacks, PEFT methods, and adapter ranks. In addition, we consider various adaptive attacks to demonstrate the high robustness of PEFTGuard. We further explore several possible backdoor mitigation defenses, finding fine-mixing to be the most effective method. We envision that our benchmark and method can shed light on future LLM backdoor detection research. 11Our code and dataset are available at: https://github.com/Vincent-HKUSTGZ/PEFTGuard.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the threat of backdoor attacks in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) adapters like LoRA, which can be shared and reused, allowing adversaries to inject malicious behaviors. The authors introduce PADBench, a benchmark of 13,300 benign and backdoored adapters, and propose PEFTGuard, a backdoor detection framework for PEFT adapters. Evaluation on PADBench shows PEFTGuard achieves nearly perfect detection accuracy (100% in most cases) and exhibits zero-shot transferability across different attacks, PEFT methods, and adapter ranks. This paper directly investigates the fragility of post-training alignment by exposing how the adapter sharing mechanism in PEFT creates a new attack surface for backdoors, and demonstrates that such backdoors can be detected with high accuracy, contributing to understanding the robustness of alignment when using efficient fine-tuning methods.
papers.summary_zh: 该论文解决了参数高效微调（PEFT）适配器（如LoRA）中的后门攻击威胁，这些适配器可在开源平台共享和复用，使攻击者能够注入恶意行为。作者构建并发布了PADBench基准（包含13,300个良性及后门适配器），并提出PEFTGuard，首个针对PEFT适配器的后门检测框架。在PADBench上的广泛评估显示，PEFTGuard在多数情况下达到近乎完美的检测准确率（100%），并在不同攻击、PEFT方法和适配器秩上展现出零样本迁移性。该论文直接研究了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，揭示了PEFT中的适配器共享机制如何成为后门注入的新攻击面，并证明这类后门可被高精度检测，为理解使用高效微调方法时对齐的鲁棒性提供了见解。

papers.title: Fuzz-Testing Meets LLM-Based Agents: An Automated and Efficient Framework for Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Generation Models
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) generative models have revolutionized content creation by transforming textual descriptions into high-quality images. However, these models are vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks, where carefully crafted prompts bypass safety mechanisms to produce unsafe content. While researchers have developed various jailbreak attacks to expose this risk, these methods face significant limitations, including impractical access requirements, easily detectable unnatural prompts, restricted search spaces, and high query demands on the target system. In this paper, we propose JailFuzzer, a novel fuzzing framework driven by large language model (LLM) agents, designed to efficiently generate natural and semantically meaningful jailbreak prompts in a black-box setting. Specifically, JailFuzzer employs fuzz-testing principles with three components: a seed pool for initial and jailbreak prompts, a guided mutation engine for generating meaningful variations, and an oracle function to evaluate jailbreak success. Furthermore, we construct the guided mutation engine and oracle function by LLM-based agents, which further ensures efficiency and adaptability in black-box settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that JailFuzzer has significant advantages in jailbreaking T2I models. It generates natural and semantically coherent prompts, reducing the likelihood of detection by traditional defenses. Additionally, it achieves a high success rate in jailbreak attacks with minimal query overhead, outperforming existing methods across all key metrics. This study underscores the need for stronger safety mechanisms in generative models and provides a foundation for future research on defending against sophisticated jailbreaking attacks. JailFuzzer is open-source and available at this repository: https://github.com/YingkaiD/JailFuzzer.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the vulnerability of text-to-image (T2I) generation models to jailbreaking attacks that bypass safety filters to produce unsafe content, addressing limitations in existing attack methods such as high query costs and unnatural prompts. It proposes JailFuzzer, a black-box fuzzing framework that leverages LLM-based agents to manage a seed pool, perform guided mutations, and evaluate jailbreak success, generating natural and semantically coherent adversarial prompts. Extensive experiments show that JailFuzzer achieves a high attack success rate with minimal query overhead and produces prompts that are less detectable, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. By demonstrating an efficient and automated attack on T2I safety mechanisms, the paper provides strong evidence that post-training safety alignment can be fragile and readily bypassed via sophisticated, low-query methods.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究文本到图像（T2I）生成模型易受越狱攻击，即绕过安全过滤器生成不安全内容的漏洞，并指出现有攻击方法存在查询成本高、提示不自然等局限。提出JailFuzzer，一个基于黑盒模糊测试的框架，利用LLM智能体管理种子池、引导变异并评估越狱成功与否，生成自然且语义连贯的对抗提示。大量实验表明，JailFuzzer以极低的查询开销获得高攻击成功率，且生成的提示更难被检测，性能超越现有方法。通过展示对T2I安全机制的高效自动化攻击，本文有力证明了后训练安全对齐可能具有脆弱性，并能被精巧的低查询攻击轻易绕过。

papers.title: Fun-tuning: Characterizing the Vulnerability of Proprietary LLMs to Optimization-Based Prompt Injection Attacks via the Fine-Tuning Interface
papers.abstract: We surface a new threat to closed-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) that enables an attacker to compute optimization-based prompt injections. Specifically, we characterize how an attacker can leverage the loss-like information returned from the remote fine-tuning interface to guide the search for adversarial prompts. The fine-tuning interface is hosted by an LLM vendor and allows developers to fine-tune LLMs for their tasks, thus providing utility, but also exposes enough information for an attacker to compute adversarial prompts. Through an experimental analysis, we characterize the loss-like values returned by the Gemini fine-tuning API and demonstrate that they provide a useful signal for discrete optimization of adversarial prompts using a greedy search algorithm. Using the PurpleLlama prompt injection benchmark, we demonstrate attack success rates between 65% and 82% on Google's Gemini family of LLMs. These attacks exploit the classic utility-security tradeoff - the fine-tuning interface provides a useful feature for developers but also exposes the LLMs to powerful attacks.
papers.summary_en: The paper exposes a novel attack surface where an adversary can craft optimization-based prompt injections against proprietary LLMs by abusing the loss information returned during fine-tuning. The approach leverages the continuous loss values provided by the fine-tuning API as a reward signal to iteratively refine adversarial prompts via a greedy discrete optimization algorithm. Experimental evaluation on Google's Gemini models using the PurpleLlama benchmark shows attack success rates between 65% and 82%, demonstrating the practicality of the approach. This work directly demonstrates the fragility of safety alignment by showing how a legitimate feature—remote fine-tuning—can be weaponized to compute adversarial prompts that circumvent alignment, underscoring the classic utility-security trade-off.
papers.summary_zh: 本论文揭示了一种针对闭源大语言模型的新攻击面，攻击者通过远程微调接口返回的损失信息，可构建基于优化的提示注入攻击。方法上，攻击者利用微调API提供的连续损失值作为奖励信号，通过贪婪搜索算法迭代优化对抗性提示。在谷歌Gemini系列模型上的实验表明，使用PurpleLlama基准测试，攻击成功率在65%到82%之间。该工作直接揭示了安全对齐的脆弱性：原本为开发者提供的微调功能，竟能被用于生成绕过安全对齐的对抗性提示，体现了典型的“效用-安全”权衡缺陷。

papers.title: BAIT: Large Language Model Backdoor Scanning by Inverting Attack Target
papers.short_title: BAIT: Backdoor Scan by Inverting Target
papers.abstract: Recent literature has shown that LLMs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where malicious attackers inject a secret token sequence (i.e., trigger) into training prompts and enforce their responses to include a specific target sequence. Unlike discriminative NLP models, which have a finite output space (e.g., those in sentiment analysis), LLMs are generative models, and their output space grows exponentially with the length of response, thereby posing significant challenges to existing backdoor detection techniques, such as trigger inversion. In this paper, we conduct a theoretical analysis of the LLM backdoor learning process under specific assumptions, revealing that the autoregressive training paradigm in causal language models inherently induces strong causal relationships among tokens in backdoor targets. We hence develop a novel LLM backdoor scanning technique, BAIT (Large Language Model Backdoor ScAnning by Inverting Attack Target). Instead of inverting back-door triggers like in existing scanning techniques for non-LLMs, BAIT determines if a model is backdoored by inverting back-door targets, leveraging the exceptionally strong causal relations among target tokens. BAIT substantially reduces the search space and effectively identifies backdoors without requiring any prior knowledge about triggers or targets. The search-based nature also enables BAIT to scan LLMs with only the black-box access. Evaluations on 153 LLMs with 8 architectures across 6 distinct attack types demonstrate that our method outperforms 5 baselines. Its superior performance allows us to rank at the top of the leaderboard in the LLM round of the TrojAI competition (a multi-year, multi-round backdoor scanning competition).
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting backdoor attacks in LLMs, where attackers inject triggers to force specific outputs. It proposes BAIT, a novel scanning technique that inverts backdoor targets by exploiting strong causal dependencies among target tokens in autoregressive training, substantially reducing search space. Evaluated on 153 LLMs with 8 architectures and 6 attack types, BAIT outperforms five baselines and achieves top rank in the TrojAI competition. By enabling effective backdoor detection, this work mitigates a threat that could compromise safety alignment, demonstrating a hardening method against one form of alignment fragility.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决LLM后门攻击检测难题，攻击者通过注入触发器强制模型输出特定内容。提出BAIT，一种通过逆向攻击目标的新型扫描方法，利用自回归训练中目标令牌间的强因果依赖关系，大幅缩小搜索空间。在153个LLM、8种架构和6种攻击类型上评估，BAIT性能优于五个基线，并在TrojAI竞赛LLM轮中排名第一。该后门检测工作减轻了可能破坏安全对齐的威胁，为应对对齐脆弱性提供了一种加固方法。

papers.title: On Large Language Models' Resilience to Coercive Interrogation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed in numerous applications. It is hence important to ensure that their ethical standard aligns with humans’. However, existing jail-breaking efforts show that such alignment could be compromised by well-crafted prompts. In this paper, we disclose a new threat to LLMs alignment when a malicious actor has access to the top-k token predictions at each output position of the model, such as in all open-source LLMs and many commercial LLMs that provide the needed APIs (e.g., some GPT versions). It does not require crafting any prompt. Instead, it leverages the observation that even when an LLM declines a toxic query, the harmful response is concealed deep within the output logits. We can coerce the model to disclose it by forcefully using low-ranked output tokens during auto-regressive output generation, and such forcing is only needed in a very small number of selected output positions. We call it model interrogation. Since our method operates differently from jail-breaking, it has better effectiveness than state-of-the- art jail-breaking techniques (92% versus 62%) and is 10 to 20 times faster. The toxic content elicited by our method is also of better quality. More importantly, it is complementary to jail-breaking, and a synergetic integration of the two exhibits superior performance over individual methods. We also find that with interrogation, harmful content can even be extracted from models customized for coding tasks.
papers.summary_en: This paper discloses a new attack on LLM safety alignment where an adversary with access to top-k token predictions can coerce the model into disclosing harmful responses concealed in output logits, even when it initially refuses a toxic query. The method, called model interrogation, forcefully selects low-ranked tokens at a few key positions during auto-regressive generation. Experiments show a 92% success rate, outperforming state-of-the-art jailbreaking (62%), while being 10-20 times faster and producing higher-quality toxic outputs; it also extracts harmful content from coding-customized models. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training alignment, as harmful knowledge persists latently in logits and can be extracted without prompt engineering.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了一种针对LLM安全对齐的新攻击：攻击者若能获取输出logits的top-k预测，可强迫模型在拒绝恶意查询后仍生成隐藏的有害回应。该方法称为“模型审讯”，在自回归生成中强制使用少数位置的低排名令牌，绕过拒绝机制。实验显示攻击成功率达92%，远超最先进越狱方法的62%，速度提升10-20倍且有害内容质量更高；还能从编程模型中提取有害信息。该研究直接暴露了训练后对齐的脆弱性，有害知识仍潜伏在logits中，无需构造提示即可被提取。

papers.title: Alleviating the Fear of Losing Alignment in LLM Fine-tuning
papers.short_title: Harmful Direction Recovery for LLM Alignment
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated revolutionary capabilities in understanding complex contexts and performing a wide range of tasks. However, LLMs can also answer questions that are unethical or harmful, raising concerns about their applications. To regulate LLMs' responses to such questions, a training strategy called alignment can help. Yet, alignment can be unexpectedly compromised when fine-tuning an LLM for downstream tasks. This paper focuses on recovering the alignment lost during fine-tuning. We observe that there are two distinct directions inherent in an aligned LLM: the aligned direction and the harmful direction. An LLM is inclined to answer questions in the aligned direction while refusing queries in the harmful direction. Therefore, we propose to recover the harmful direction of the fine-tuned model that has been compromised. Specifically, we restore a small subset of the fine-tuned model's weight parameters from the original aligned model using gradient descent. We also introduce a rollback mechanism to avoid aggressive recovery and maintain downstream task performance. Our evaluation on 125 fine-tuned LLMs demonstrates that our method can reduce their harmful rate (percentage of answering harmful questions) from 33.25% to 1.74%, without sacrificing task performance much. In contrast, the existing methods either only reduce the harmful rate to a limited extent or significantly impact the normal functionality. Our code is available at https://github.com/kangyangWHU/LLMAlignment
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the problem of alignment loss when fine-tuning LLMs for downstream tasks, which causes them to answer harmful questions. It proposes to recover alignment by identifying and restoring the 'harmful direction' in the model's parameters, using gradient descent to update a small subset of weights from the original aligned model, with a rollback mechanism to preserve task performance. Evaluated on 125 fine-tuned LLMs, the method reduces the harmful rate from 33.25% to 1.74% without significant performance loss, outperforming existing approaches. This work directly tackles the fragility of safety alignment by demonstrating both its vulnerability during fine-tuning and a practical recovery method, reinforcing that alignment can be effectively restored.
papers.summary_zh: 本文解决了在对LLM进行下游任务微调时，对齐能力可能意外丧失的问题，导致模型回答有害问题。它提出通过识别并恢复微调模型中受损的‘有害方向’来修复对齐：使用梯度下降，从原始对齐模型中恢复一小部分权重参数，并引入回滚机制以避免性能损失。在125个微调LLM上的评估表明，该方法将有害率从33.25%降至1.74%，且下游任务性能未显著下降，优于现有方法。本研究直接回应了安全对齐的脆弱性问题，既展示了它容易在微调中被破坏，又提供了一种实用的恢复手段，证明对齐可通过参数修复而重新强化。

papers.title: DxHF: Providing High-Quality Human Feedback for LLM Alignment with Interactive Decomposition
papers.abstract: Human preferences are widely used to align large language models (LLMs) through methods such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, the current user interfaces require annotators to compare text paragraphs, which is cognitively challenging when the texts are long or unfamiliar. This paper contributes by studying the decomposition principle as an approach to improving the quality of human feedback for LLM alignment. This approach breaks down the text into individual claims instead of directly comparing two long-form text responses. Based on the principle, we build a novel user interface DxHF. It enhances the comparison process by showing decomposed claims, visually encoding the relevance of claims to the conversation and linking similar claims. This allows users to skim through key information and identify differences for better and quicker judgment. Our technical evaluation shows evidence that decomposition generally improves feedback accuracy regarding the ground truth, particularly for users with uncertainty. A crowdsourcing study with 160 participants indicates that using DxHF improves feedback accuracy by an average of 5%, although it increases the average feedback time by 18 seconds. Notably, accuracy is significantly higher in situations where users have less certainty. The finding of the study highlights the potential of HCI as an effective method for improving human-AI alignment.
papers.summary_en: This paper addresses the cognitive difficulty of comparing long text paragraphs in human feedback interfaces for LLM alignment. It proposes DxHF, a user interface that decomposes responses into individual claims with visual encoding and linking to highlight similarities and differences. A crowdsourcing study with 160 participants shows that DxHF improves feedback accuracy by 5% on average, though it increases time by 18 seconds, with significant accuracy gains when users are uncertain. This work advances alignment methodology by enhancing human feedback quality but does not directly examine the fragility or robustness of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对LLM对齐中人工反馈界面对比长段落文本时认知负担大的问题，提出了一种名为DxHF的用户界面，通过将响应分解为独立声明并进行视觉编码和关联，以突出异同。一项包含160名参与者的众包研究表明，DxHF平均提高了5%的反馈准确性，但花费时间增加了18秒，尤其在用户不确定时准确性提升显著。该工作通过提升反馈质量推进了对齐方法论，但未直接探讨训练后安全对齐的脆弱性或鲁棒性。

papers.title: Policy Maps: Tools for Guiding the Unbounded Space of LLM Behaviors
papers.abstract: AI policy sets boundaries on acceptable behavior for AI models, but this is challenging in the context of large language models (LLMs): how do you ensure coverage over a vast behavior space? We introduce policy maps, an approach to AI policy design inspired by the practice of physical mapmaking. Instead of aiming for full coverage, policy maps aid effective navigation through intentional design choices about which aspects to capture and which to abstract away. With Policy Projector, an interactive tool for designing LLM policy maps, an AI practitioner can survey the landscape of model input-output pairs, define custom regions (e.g., “violence”), and navigate these regions with if-then policy rules that can act on LLM outputs (e.g., if output contains “violence” and “graphic details,” then rewrite without “graphic details”). Policy Projector supports interactive policy authoring using LLM classification and steering and a map visualization reflecting the AI practitioner’s work. In an evaluation with 12 AI safety experts, our system helps policy designers craft policies around problematic model behaviors such as incorrect gender assumptions and handling of immediate physical safety threats. Content Warning: This paper contains examples of harmful text, including toxic, violent, illegal, and controversial statements.
papers.summary_en: The paper addresses the challenge of ensuring comprehensive coverage of safe behaviors in LLMs by introducing policy maps, a mapmaking-inspired approach that intentionally abstracts behavior spaces. It presents Policy Projector, an interactive tool enabling practitioners to define custom behavior regions and apply if-then rules to steer model outputs. An evaluation with 12 AI safety experts demonstrates its utility in crafting policies for issues like gender assumptions and physical safety threats. This work advances alignment methodology through a novel policy design tool but does not directly examine the robustness or fragility of post-training safety alignment.
papers.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型行为空间覆盖难的问题，借鉴地图制图思想提出策略地图方法，通过有意的抽象来导航模型行为。介绍了交互式工具 Policy Projector，允许从业者定义自定义行为区域并应用 if-then 规则操控输出。经12位 AI 安全专家评估，该系统有助于针对性别假设、人身安全威胁等问题制定策略。这项工作通过新的策略设计工具推进了对齐方法学，但并未直接探究训练后安全对齐的鲁棒性或脆弱性。

papers.title: From Meme to Threat: On the Hateful Meme Understanding and Induced Hateful Content Generation in Open-Source Vision Language Models
papers.short_title: From Meme to Threat: VLM Hateful Memes
papers.abstract: Open-source Vision Language Models (VLMs) have rapidly advanced, blending natural language with visual modalities, leading them to achieve remarkable performance on tasks such as image captioning and visual question answering. However, their effectiveness in real-world scenarios remains uncertain, as real-world images—particularly hateful memes—often convey complex semantics, cultural references, and emotional signals far beyond those in experimental datasets. In this paper, we present an in-depth evaluation of VLMs' ability to interpret hateful memes by curating a dataset of 39 hateful memes and 12,775 responses from seven representative VLMs using carefully designed prompts. Our manual annotations of the responses' informativeness and soundness reveal that VLMs can identify visual concepts and understand cultural and emotional backgrounds, especially for the well-known hateful memes. However, we find that the VLMs lack robust safeguards to effectively detect and reject hateful content, making them vulnerable to misuse for generating harmful outputs such as hate speech and offensive slogans. Our findings show that 40% of VLM-generated hate speech and over 10% of hateful jokes and slogans were flagged as harmful, emphasizing the urgent need for stronger safety measures and ethical guidelines to mitigate misuse. We hope our study serves as a foundation for improving VLM safety and ethical standards in handling hateful content.
papers.summary_en: This paper evaluates open-source Vision Language Models (VLMs) on understanding hateful memes and their susceptibility to generating harmful content. It curates a dataset of 39 hateful memes and collects 12,775 responses from seven VLMs with designed prompts, manually annotating informativeness and soundness. The findings show VLMs can interpret visual concepts and cultural contexts but lack robust safeguards, with 40% of generated hate speech and over 10% of hateful jokes/slogans flagged as harmful. This directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, as VLMs can be easily prompted to bypass safeguards and produce hateful content despite partial comprehension.
papers.summary_zh: 本文评估了开源视觉语言模型理解仇恨模因及生成有害内容的倾向。通过构建包含39个仇恨模因的数据集，使用精心设计的提示从七个VLM收集12,775条回复，并进行信息量和合理性的人工标注。结果发现，VLM能识别视觉概念和文化背景，但缺乏稳健的安全防护措施，40%生成仇恨言论和超过10%的仇恨笑话/口号被标记为有害。这直接揭示了后训练安全对齐的脆弱性，尽管模型具有一定理解能力，仍可被轻易诱导绕过防护生成仇恨内容，突显关键漏洞。

papers.title: Mind the Inconspicuous: Revealing the Hidden Weakness in Aligned LLMs' Refusal Boundaries
papers.short_title: Mind the EOS: Hidden LLM Refusal Weakness
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to impressive alignment—where models learn to distinguish harmful from harmless queries through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). In this paper, we reveal a subtle yet impactful weakness in these aligned models. We find that simply appending multiple end-of-sequence (eos) tokens can cause a phenomenon we call "context segmentation", which effectively shifts both "harmful" and "benign" inputs closer to the refusal boundary in the hidden space.
papers.summary_en: This paper uncovers a subtle weakness in safety-aligned LLMs where appending multiple end-of-sequence (EOS) tokens shifts both harmful and benign inputs closer to the refusal boundary. It introduces the concept of 'context segmentation,' which exploits how EOS tokens fragment the model's hidden representations, compromising the distinction between safe and unsafe prompts. Experiments show that this simple manipulation blurs the refusal decision boundary, leading to increased false refusals of benign queries and potential acceptance of harmful ones. The finding directly demonstrates the fragility of post-training safety alignment, revealing an easily bypassed vulnerability that undermines robustness.
papers.summary_zh: 本文揭示了安全对齐大语言模型的一个隐蔽弱点：在输入末尾追加多个结束符（EOS）标记，会使有害和良性查询在隐藏空间中都更接近拒绝边界。作者提出了‘上下文分割’概念，即EOS标记会打乱模型的内部表示，削弱安全与不安全提示之间的区分。实验表明，这种简单操作模糊了拒绝决策边界，导致模型对良性查询的误拒增加，并可能接受有害内容。该发现直接证明了训练后安全对齐的脆弱性，暴露了一个可轻易利用的漏洞，动摇了其鲁棒性。

papers.title: Exploiting Task-Level Vulnerabilities: An Automatic Jailbreak Attack and Defense Benchmarking for LLMs
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have notably improved their proficiency in executing complex tasks. However, these advancements are accompanied by an increased risk of generating toxic content as well as leaking private information. Jailbreak is an emerging trend to amplify this vulnerability by carefully modifying prompts such asDAN" to circumvent the LLMs' defense. Notwithstanding, existing jailbreaks typically focus on specific prompts or tokens, rendering them susceptible to countermeasures such as realignments. In contrast to these prompt-level or token-level jailbreaks, we present a novel task-level jailbreak based on knowledge decomposition, which does not rely on any specific prompts or tokens. Our attack demonstrates significantly enhanced resistance against realignments compared to previous jailbreak techniques. Furthermore, our attack not only achieves about 10% higher success rates than SOTA attacks but also generates responses that are richer in detail and information. This is attributed to aggregation of responses from multiple well-designed queries rather than relying on only a singular query as in previous attacks, thus signifying an elevated risk of threat. On the other hand, knowledge decomposition provide us a method to generate plenty tasks with varying risk levels, thereby establishing a novel benchmark to assess the defensive effectiveness of LLMs.
papers.summary_en: This paper tackles the vulnerability of LLMs to jailbreak attacks that bypass safety alignment, highlighting that existing prompt- or token-level attacks are easily countered by realignment. It proposes a novel task-level jailbreak attack based on knowledge decomposition, which aggregates responses from multiple designed queries rather than relying on a single prompt, making it resistant to realignment. The attack achieves about 10% higher success rates than state-of-the-art methods and generates more detailed responses; the decomposition approach also enables a new benchmark for evaluating LLM defenses. This work reveals a task-level attack surface, demonstrating that post-training safety alignment can be fragile and bypassed through complex query decomposition, directly addressing the central question of alignment robustness.
